messages.content: is honey good for coughs? my 10 month old has one

Honey does help coughs in older kids, but never give it to a baby under 12 months because it can cause infant botulism, a serious illness. For your 10-month-old, try a cool-mist humidifier, saline drops with gentle suction for a stuffy nose, and plenty of breast milk or formula. Call the pediatrician if they're breathing fast, wheezing, not feeding well, have fewer wet diapers or develop a fever. Honey is safe once they turn one.
quick q, is it bad to let my mom stay in bed most of the day after her hip surgery? she's tired

Some rest is fine, but staying in bed most of the day after hip surgery raises the risk of blood clots, pneumonia, bedsores and losing muscle strength fast. Her surgical team almost certainly wants her up and walking several times a day, even briefly with help. Follow the physical therapist's plan closely. If she's too exhausted or in too much pain to move, call the surgeon's office, because that can mean her pain control needs adjusting.
My 4 year old is the pickiest eater alive, basically lives on pasta and crackers. Should I give him a multivitamin?

A children's multivitamin is a reasonable safety net for a very picky eater. It can cover gaps in things like iron, vitamin D and zinc while you keep offering other foods without pressure. Store it somewhere he truly can't reach, because gummy vitamins look like candy and an iron overdose is one of the more dangerous poisonings in young kids. Mention his diet at his next checkup, too, since the pediatrician can check his growth and iron levels.
got metal shavings in my eye grinding, can i dig it out with tweezers

Please don't put tweezers near your eye. You could scratch the cornea or push the metal in deeper. Try flushing the eye gently with clean water or saline, but don't rub it. Metal from grinding often embeds in the eye and can leave a rust ring within hours, so if it doesn't rinse out easily, see urgent care or an eye doctor today. If the fragment came off at high speed and the pain is severe, go to an ER, because it may have gone into the eye.
my 4 month old has a stuffy nose and is fussy, can I give her some of my sudafed if I crush a tiny bit?

Please don't. Decongestants like Sudafed aren't safe for babies, and even a small piece can cause a dangerously fast heart rate or seizures. Saline drops and gentle suction with a bulb or nasal aspirator before feeds work well, and a cool-mist humidifier in her room helps too. If she's struggling to feed, breathing fast, or has any fever at her age, call her pediatrician today.
28 weeks pregnant and my heart feels like it's racing a lot, is this just pregnancy?

Your heart rate naturally rises in pregnancy because you're pumping much more blood, so mild racing or palpitations are common in the third trimester. Mention it to your midwife or OB at your next visit, or call sooner if it's happening often. Get urgent care for chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness, a cough with blood, or racing that won't settle.
flu shot or nasal spray for my 6yo who screams at needles

If your 6-year-old is healthy, the nasal spray (FluMist) is a perfectly good option and is approved from age 2 to 49. It isn't recommended for kids with asthma or recent wheezing, a weakened immune system, or certain other conditions, so mention any health issues when you book. If the pharmacy or pediatrician has it in stock, it's a much easier visit for a needle-phobic kid.
fever and a rash of tiny purple dots that don't fade when I press a glass on them. 19yo

Call emergency services or get to an ER immediately. A fever with a rash that doesn't fade under pressure can be a sign of meningococcal infection, which can become life-threatening within hours. Every minute matters here, so go now rather than waiting to see if it spreads.
forehead thermometer vs oral, which do i trust

Oral readings are generally more accurate than forehead scans for older kids and adults, as long as the person hasn't just had something hot or cold to drink. Forehead thermometers are handy for quick checks but can be thrown off by sweat or the room temperature. For babies under 3 months, rectal is the gold standard. If a forehead reading seems borderline, confirm it with a better method.
I have leftover amoxicillin from last year. My cold has been going for 5 days, should I just start taking it to knock it out faster?

Don't take it, because colds are caused by viruses and amoxicillin does nothing against them. It can still cause side effects like diarrhea or an allergic reaction, and a partial old course feeds antibiotic resistance. Five days is right in the normal range for a cold, which typically runs 7 to 10 days. See a doctor if you're getting worse after starting to improve, run a high fever, or have sinus pain lasting past 10 days, since those can signal a bacterial infection that actually needs treatment.
Can I just skip my kid's 12-month shots and catch up later? We're traveling a lot this year.

I'd strongly avoid delaying them, especially with travel, because the 12-month vaccines include MMR and varicella and measles is circulating in many places right now. Toddlers are at the age where these infections hit hardest, and airports and planes are exactly where exposure happens. Most pediatric offices can fit the visit in before you leave, and if timing is truly impossible, ask your pediatrician about a travel clinic so you can stay on schedule.
can i have one glass of wine at my sisters wedding im 30 weeks

No amount of alcohol has been shown to be safe in pregnancy, so the advice from obstetric bodies is to skip it entirely, even at a special occasion. A single glass is unlikely to cause harm, so don't panic if it's already happened, but there's no reason to take the chance. A nice alcohol-free sparkling wine in a champagne glass lets you join the toast without anyone asking questions.
Are there natural supplements that prevent migraines?

A few have decent evidence: magnesium (often around 400 to 600 mg daily), riboflavin (vitamin B2, 400 mg daily) and coenzyme Q10. They take two to three months to show a benefit. Magnesium can loosen your stools and isn't suitable for everyone with kidney problems, so check with your doctor or pharmacist first, especially if you're pregnant or take other medications.
Took my metformin twice by accident this morning. Panic?

No need to panic. An extra dose of metformin rarely causes dangerous low blood sugar on its own, though you might get some stomach upset. Eat regular meals today and skip your next dose if it's due soon, then get back on schedule. If you also take insulin or a sulfonylurea like glipizide, watch for shakiness, sweating or confusion, and call your pharmacist or poison control (1-800-222-1222 in the US) if you're unsure.
hives all over after a new laundry detergent, no breathing problems. what do i do

Rewash your clothes and sheets in your old detergent, or run them through an extra rinse, and take a non-drowsy antihistamine like cetirizine to calm the hives. Cool showers and loose clothing help with the itch. Hives from a contact or irritant trigger usually fade within a day or two once the trigger is gone. Get emergency help if you develop lip or tongue swelling, trouble breathing, or dizziness, and see a doctor if the hives last beyond a few days.
can i drink alcohol to numb a toothache? swishing whiskey is what my dad did

Swishing whiskey barely numbs anything and can sting irritated tissue, and drinking enough to dull the pain is a bad idea, especially if you're also taking painkillers. Acetaminophen and alcohol together are hard on the liver. Stick with ibuprofen or acetaminophen at label doses, use a cold compress on your cheek, and get the tooth looked at.
my back tooth has been throbbing for 3 days and now my cheek is swelling up. can i just wait it out till my dentist opens monday?

Swelling in your cheek alongside a throbbing tooth usually means an infection is spreading beyond the tooth, so this isn't one to sit on until Monday. Call an emergency dentist or urgent care today, because you may need antibiotics and drainage sooner rather than later. If the swelling spreads toward your eye or neck, or you get a fever or trouble swallowing or breathing, go to the ER right away.
my lower back has been killing me for 3 days after moving furniture. should i just stay in bed till it passes?

Skip the bed rest, because staying still for days tends to make back strains stiffer and slower to heal. Keep moving gently with short walks and normal light activity, use heat or an over-the-counter anti-inflammatory if it suits you, and avoid heavy lifting for a week or two. Most strains like this improve noticeably within a couple of weeks. Get checked sooner if you develop leg numbness, weakness, or any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and I think I have the flu. Fever, body aches, the works. I don't want to bother my OB over the weekend.

Please call your OB's on-call line or urgent care today, because this is exactly what weekend coverage is for. Pregnant people are at higher risk of serious flu complications, and early antiviral treatment with Tamiflu is recommended and safe in pregnancy. Acetaminophen is the preferred fever reducer in the meantime, and fever is worth bringing down because high temperatures aren't great for the baby. Go to the ER if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or notice the baby is moving less.
Never really exercised, but after recovering from a stomach bug I want to start running. Any tips?

That's a great goal, and the key is starting easy so your body has time to recover from being sick and adjust to running. Give yourself a few days of eating and drinking normally first, then start with walk-run intervals, like one minute jogging and two minutes walking for about 20 minutes, three times a week. Gradually increase the running parts over several weeks, and keep the pace slow enough that you can chat. If you have health conditions or any chest pain or dizziness, check with a doctor first.
Does vitamin C actually do anything for colds

Mostly not once you're already sick, since taking vitamin C after symptoms start doesn't reliably shorten a cold. Taking it regularly beforehand may trim a cold's length slightly, and it helps more in people under heavy physical stress, like marathon runners. Very high doses can cause stomach upset and diarrhea, so megadosing isn't worth it. Rest, fluids and time do most of the work.
What's the fastest way to calm down when I'm about to snap at my kids?

Put physical distance between you first. Step into another room for a minute if the kids are safe, because it's hard to calm down while you're still in the middle of it. Breathe out slowly, longer than you breathe in, a few times, and run cold water over your hands or splash your face, which can take the edge off quickly. Then come back and speak more quietly than you feel like speaking. If you're hitting this point every day, it's worth looking at the root causes, like sleep, support and your own stress, and talking to your doctor if you feel constantly on edge.
My dog bit a stranger at the park and they're freaking out about rabies. He's vaccinated. What should I tell them?

Give them your contact info and proof of your dog's current rabies vaccination, which is the most reassuring thing you can offer. Encourage them to wash the bite well and get it checked, especially if it's a puncture or on the hand. Many places require dog bites to be reported, so expect local animal control to have your dog observed for about 10 days, often at home. That's routine and not a punishment.
I'm 7 months pregnant and have a horrible toothache. Is it even safe to go to the dentist right now?

Yes, dental care is safe during pregnancy, and treating a painful or infected tooth is much better for you and the baby than leaving it alone. Tell the dentist how far along you are so they can position you comfortably and choose pregnancy-safe anesthetic and X-ray precautions. For pain in the meantime, acetaminophen is generally the go-to, but avoid ibuprofen in the third trimester unless your doctor says otherwise.
Hey, 45F, both hands stiff for hours every morning, knuckles puffy, getting worse for like 2 months. Just aging I guess?

Hours of morning stiffness with swollen knuckles in both hands is more typical of an inflammatory arthritis like rheumatoid arthritis than ordinary wear and tear. Make an appointment with your doctor soon and ask about blood tests and a rheumatology referral. Starting treatment early can prevent permanent joint damage, so this is worth chasing now rather than waiting it out.
how long can insulin stay out of the fridge

Most insulin pens and vials are good for about 28 days at room temperature, up to around 86°F (30°C), once you start using them. Some types are rated for 42 or 56 days, so check the label for yours. Keep it out of direct sun, hot cars, and freezing temperatures, because heat and freezing both break it down. If it's been frozen, looks cloudy when it should be clear, or has clumps, throw it out.
My 2 year old has a fever of 102 and is pulling at her ear. Should I wait it out or go in?

A toddler with a fever and ear-pulling likely has an ear infection, and it's reasonable to have her seen within a day or so. Many mild ear infections clear on their own, but a doctor can look at the eardrum and decide whether she needs antibiotics or can safely wait. In the meantime, give children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen dosed by her weight for comfort. Go in sooner if she's very lethargic, won't drink, has fluid draining from the ear, or the fever goes above 104°F.
Had back surgery 10 days ago, now the wound is red and leaking and I feel feverish

Contact your surgical team or go to the emergency department today. Redness, discharge and fever after spinal surgery suggest a wound infection that needs prompt assessment and probably antibiotics. Don't wait for your scheduled follow-up, and avoid putting creams on the wound in the meantime.
My son (8) has a rash with little red dots that don't fade when I press a glass on them, and he has a fever.

Take him to the emergency room now. A rash that doesn't fade under pressure, combined with a fever, can be a sign of meningococcal infection or another serious condition that needs treatment within hours. Call emergency services if he's very drowsy, confused, or getting worse quickly. It may turn out to be something mild, but this is not something to wait on.
My 6 year old fell off the monkey bars and her wrist is swollen but she can move her fingers. Probably just a sprain right?

Moving her fingers doesn't rule out a fracture, and wrist injuries from falling on an outstretched hand in kids are very often small breaks near the growth plate that look like sprains. Put a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on it, support the arm in a sling or on a pillow, and give children's ibuprofen or acetaminophen at her weight-based dose. If she's still tender right over the bone, guarding the arm, or the swelling hasn't eased by tomorrow, get it X-rayed, and go sooner if it looks bent or she's in a lot of pain.
wisdom tooth coming in, gums hurt at the back. normal?

Some soreness and tender gums are normal while a wisdom tooth pushes through, and warm salt-water rinses a few times a day plus ibuprofen usually take the edge off. The flap of gum over a partly erupted tooth can trap food and get infected, which is called pericoronitis. If you notice a bad taste, pus, swelling, or trouble opening your mouth, get it looked at by a dentist soon.
Dad is 80 and wants to start lifting weights at the gym. Too risky?

It's actually one of the best things he can do. Strength training at his age builds muscle and bone and cuts fall risk. Have him check with his doctor first if he has heart, blood pressure, or joint issues. He should start light, focus on form, and ideally get a few sessions with a trainer experienced with older adults. Sharp pain, chest discomfort, or dizziness are signals to stop.
Does stress cause permanent high blood pressure or just temporary spikes?

Acute stress causes temporary spikes, but long-term stress can contribute to lasting high blood pressure, partly through habits like poor sleep, drinking, overeating and inactivity. Managing it with exercise, better sleep and relaxation techniques can noticeably improve your numbers. If your readings stay high even on calm days, that's real hypertension worth treating, not just stress.
adult, fever 103.5 not budging with tylenol, feel awful and a bit short of breath

Get seen now. A high fever that isn't responding to medicine plus shortness of breath needs prompt evaluation, so go to urgent care or the ER. It could be pneumonia or another serious infection. Call emergency services if your breathing gets worse, your lips look bluish, or you feel faint or confused.
My mom is 82 and keeps forgetting whether she took her pills, so sometimes she takes them twice. What should I do?

Get her a weekly pill organizer with separate morning and evening compartments, so she can see at a glance whether a dose is gone. Ask her pharmacist about blister packs, which many pharmacies prepare for free, and consider a simple alarm or an automatic dispenser that locks between doses. Since double-dosing some drugs, like blood thinners or blood pressure pills, can be dangerous, tell her doctor this is happening so they can review which medications matter most.
Does melatonin interact with anything? I take lisinopril and metformin.

Melatonin is generally fine alongside both lisinopril and metformin. It can lower blood pressure slightly and occasionally affects blood sugar, so watch your readings for the first week or so. Start low, around 0.5 to 3 mg, about an hour before bed, since higher doses often work no better. Let your doctor know you're taking it so it's on your list.
How do I take my blood pressure correctly at home?

Sit with your back supported and feet flat for five minutes beforehand, and avoid caffeine, exercise or smoking for 30 minutes before. Put the cuff on bare skin of your upper arm, rest the arm on a table at heart level, and don't talk during the reading. Take two readings a minute apart, morning and evening, and keep a log to show your doctor. A validated upper-arm cuff in the right size makes a big difference.
ok so my water might have broken? its like a trickle not a gush. 37 wks

A steady trickle can be your waters breaking, so call labor and delivery now even if you aren't having contractions. Put on a pad instead of a tampon and note the time, the color and any smell. If the fluid is green, brown or bloody, or you feel something in your vagina, go in straight away.
how long after an allergic reaction can it come back? the swelling went down after the epi shot

A second wave, called a biphasic reaction, can happen hours later even without new exposure, which is why using epinephrine always means going to the emergency department. Stay there for observation as advised, usually at least several hours. Make sure you leave with replacement auto-injectors and a follow-up plan with an allergist.
I had covid a month ago and I'm still super tired and get winded climbing stairs. Should I push through it with workouts to get my fitness back?

Please don't push through it, because with lingering fatigue after covid, forcing hard workouts can make the exhaustion worse and drag out your recovery. Getting winded on stairs a month later is worth mentioning to your doctor, who may want to check your heart and lungs before you ramp up. In the meantime, keep activity gentle and short, like easy walks, and pay attention to how you feel the next day, not just during. If you crash after doing more, that means scale back further.
Is it bad to drink a few glasses of wine every night to unwind after the kids go to bed?

It's a really common habit, but nightly drinking to manage stress tends to backfire. Alcohol disrupts deep sleep and can worsen anxiety the next day, and tolerance creeps up so 'a few' becomes more. Try a few alcohol-free nights a week and swap in another wind-down ritual like a bath, a walk or a show with tea. If cutting back feels harder than you expected, mention it to your doctor without embarrassment, because it's a common conversation for them.
my bp is 190/115 and i have a pounding headache and some chest tightness. should i just take an extra dose of my bp pill

Don't double up on your pills; this combination needs emergency care now, so call 911 or get to an ER. A reading that high with chest tightness and a severe headache can mean the pressure is damaging your heart, brain or kidneys, and it needs to be lowered in a controlled way with monitoring, not with an extra dose at home that could drop it erratically. Sit down and stay calm while you wait for help.
how long should I ice an injury

About 15 to 20 minutes at a time, with a cloth between the ice and your skin, repeated every 2 to 3 hours for the first day or two. Going longer or putting ice directly on the skin can cause frostbite-like damage. Take extra care if you have poor circulation or diabetes, since you may not feel when it's getting too cold.
Found an old steroid inhaler from 2019 in a drawer. Asthma's been acting up. Use it?

Expired inhalers can lose potency, and a preventer from five years ago may no longer be the right medication or dose for you. Asthma flaring up again is a good reason to see your doctor now, rather than restarting an old prescription on your own. If you're getting short of breath, use your current rescue inhaler. If that isn't helping, seek urgent care.
I'm 16 and can't fall asleep before 2am even though I have school at 7:30. Am I broken?

You're not broken. Teenagers' body clocks naturally shift later, so feeling wide awake late at night is really common at your age. You can nudge your clock earlier by getting bright light, ideally outdoors, soon after you wake up and by dimming screens and lights for an hour before bed. Try to keep weekend wake-up times within an hour or two of school days too. If you're still exhausted or struggling at school after a few weeks of this, tell a parent and see your doctor, because there are other things they can help with.
Can I just drink coffee all day to make up for bad sleep this week? Finals.

Caffeine will help you stay alert, but it can't replace sleep, and studying while exhausted hurts memory, since your brain consolidates what you learned while you sleep. Keep it to about 400 mg a day for adults, roughly four cups of brewed coffee, and stop by mid-afternoon so you can actually sleep that night. Even 6 to 7 hours will help your exam performance more than an extra hour of cramming. Skip the energy drink stacking and caffeine pills, because heart palpitations and anxiety won't help either.
Detailed question: I'm on warfarin and just got prescribed ciprofloxacin for a UTI. My INR has been stable. Anything I should know?

Cipro can raise your INR and increase bleeding risk while you're on warfarin, so make sure both your prescriber and the clinic managing your warfarin know about the combination. They'll often check your INR within a few days of starting. In the meantime, watch for unusual bruising, bleeding gums, dark stools or blood in your urine, and report it promptly if any appear.
Can I use superglue to close a dog bite? Saw it online.

Don't glue a bite shut, because sealing it traps bacteria from the dog's mouth inside and greatly raises the chance of a nasty infection or abscess. Bite wounds are usually left open or only loosely closed by doctors for exactly that reason. Wash it thoroughly with soap and water, cover it loosely, and get it seen if it's deep, gaping or on your hand or face.
Is benzocaine gel safe to use on my 1 year old's teething gums?

No, the FDA advises against benzocaine for children under two because it can cause a rare but serious blood condition called methemoglobinemia. A chilled, not frozen, teething ring, gentle gum rubbing with a clean finger, or a weight-based dose of infant acetaminophen are the safer options. Check with your pediatrician if your baby has a fever over 100.4°F or seems truly unwell, because teething alone doesn't usually cause that.
Slammed my finger in the car door and now there's dark blood under the nail and it's throbbing like crazy

That pressure from trapped blood is what makes it throb so badly, and a doctor or urgent care can relieve it quickly by making a tiny hole in the nail, so don't try the hot-paperclip trick at home. Ice it and keep your hand raised in the meantime. Get it looked at soon, especially if the blood covers a large part of the nail or the finger looks bent or is hard to move, since the bone underneath can be broken.
I'm 52 and I've noticed my stools have been black and tarry for the last couple days. No pain really. Probably the iron pills?

Iron can turn stool dark, but it's usually dark green-black and formed. Sticky, tarry black stool can mean bleeding higher up in the gut. Since you can't be sure which it is, call your doctor today. Go to the emergency department right away if you feel dizzy, weak, short of breath or look pale.
I was in a long car trip yesterday and now I have chest pain when I breathe in and I'm kind of short of breath. My calf has been sore too. Can I sleep it off?

Please don't sleep on this. A sore calf after a long trip, followed by pain on breathing in and breathlessness, is a textbook picture of a blood clot that may have travelled to your lungs (pulmonary embolism). That can turn dangerous quickly. Go to an emergency department now, or call an ambulance if you're very breathless or lightheaded.
Ice bath for a 104 fever in my 6 year old?

No ice baths or rubbing alcohol. They can cause shivering that actually raises body temperature, and alcohol can be absorbed through the skin. Give a weight-appropriate dose of ibuprofen or acetaminophen, dress your child lightly, and offer fluids. At 104°F it's worth calling the pediatrician, and get seen urgently if they're very lethargic, struggling to breathe, or not drinking.
Can I mix DayQuil with my Sudafed? Super congested.

Check the label first, because many DayQuil versions already contain phenylephrine, a decongestant, and adding Sudafed means doubling up on decongestants. That can raise your heart rate and blood pressure and leave you jittery. A safer combo is a single decongestant plus a saline rinse, a steamy shower and extra pillows at night. If you have high blood pressure or heart issues, ask a pharmacist before using any decongestant.
should I starve a fever? my grandma swears by it

No, that's an old myth. When you have a fever, your body needs more fluids and energy, not less. You don't have to force big meals if you're not hungry, but keep drinking water, broth, or electrolyte drinks, and eat light foods when you can. Dehydration is the bigger risk with fever.
Is it fine to keep running on a knee that's been sore for 3 weeks? Marathon is in a month and I can't miss training.

Three weeks of persistent pain is your knee telling you something, and running through it is a classic way to turn a manageable overuse injury into one that takes you out of the race completely. Cut back now: drop the mileage, cross-train on a bike or in the pool to keep your fitness, and see a sports physio this week for a diagnosis. Many common runner's knee problems settle quickly with the right adjustments, which gives you a much better shot at reaching the start line.
My husband snaps at everyone and drinks more since he got back from deployment. He says he's fine.

Irritability and heavier drinking after deployment are common signs of PTSD or trouble adjusting, and 'I'm fine' is a very typical response. Raise it calmly by focusing on specific changes you've noticed rather than labels, and point him toward resources built for veterans, like the VA or the Veterans Crisis Line (988, then press 1 in the US), which also supports families. If he ever becomes threatening, or you feel unsafe at home, put your own safety first and reach out for help.
Stepped on a rusty nail in my garden shed. Went in maybe half a cm. Last tetanus shot... no idea honestly.

Clean the wound with plenty of running water and soap, then cover it. You should also contact your GP or an urgent care clinic today about a tetanus booster. Puncture wounds from garden or soil objects are classic tetanus risks, and if you can't remember your last shot, you almost certainly need one. Keep an eye on it over the next few days for increasing pain, swelling, redness, or fever, which could mean infection.
dementia mom keeps trying to leave the house at night. help

Night wandering is dangerous, so secure the house first. Put door alarms or chimes on the exits, add a latch placed high or low where she won't think to look, and make sure she wears an ID bracelet or GPS device with your number on it. Look for triggers like needing the bathroom, pain, boredom or too much daytime napping, and a calm evening routine with soft lighting often helps. Tell her doctor about it, since sleep problems and agitation can sometimes be treated. Ask about respite care too, because you need sleep to keep doing this.
my 9 year old got a high bp reading at the school nurse, 125/82. is that a thing in kids?

It can be. Kids' blood pressure is judged against charts based on age, sex and height, so for many 9-year-olds that reading would count as high. A single reading at school isn't a diagnosis, but book a visit with their pediatrician to recheck it with a child-sized cuff. In children, high readings sometimes have an underlying cause worth looking for.
I'm 52 and I've had a crushing pressure in my chest for about 20 minutes, it's going into my left arm. Probably just indigestion right? Should I just take an antacid and lie down?

Please don't wait this out, because crushing chest pressure spreading to your arm for 20 minutes is a classic heart attack pattern and needs an ambulance right now. Call emergency services immediately rather than driving yourself. If you aren't allergic to aspirin and no doctor has told you to avoid it, chew one regular 325 mg aspirin while you wait. Unlock your door and sit down somewhere the paramedics can reach you easily.
can stress alone give you high blood pressure

Stress raises blood pressure temporarily, and chronic stress contributes over time, often through poor sleep, drinking and eating habits. It's rarely the whole story, though, so consistently high readings shouldn't be written off as just stress. Get them checked, and treat stress management as one part of the plan.
my sister has some leftover zofran from her pregnancy, can I just take hers for my morning sickness

Don't take hers. The dose may not be right for you, and your provider should know what you're taking. Call your OB or midwife, because Zofran and other good options like vitamin B6 with doxylamine can be prescribed for you quickly, often the same day. If you can't keep any fluids down for a day, or you're peeing very little, get seen promptly, since that can turn into dehydration that needs IV fluids.
rolled my ankle playing pickup basketball, can i just tape it up and keep playing

Playing on a fresh sprain is how a minor one turns into a months-long problem, so sit out the rest of today. Ice it for 15 to 20 minutes every couple of hours, compress it with an elastic wrap, and keep it elevated tonight. If you couldn't take four steps right after it happened or the bony knobs on either side of the ankle are tender to press, get an X-ray. Otherwise, start gentle walking once it's bearable and save the tape or brace for when you return to playing in a week or two.
My 4 year old says her tooth hurts when she eats candy. Baby teeth fall out anyway so does it matter?

It does matter, because a cavity in a baby tooth can turn into a painful infection, and many baby molars stay in until around age 10 or 12. Those teeth also hold space for the adult teeth, so losing them early can cause crowding later. Book her in with a dentist soon, and cut back on sticky sweets while brushing twice a day with a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste.
Does drinking alcohol raise blood pressure or is red wine actually good for you

Regular drinking raises blood pressure, and red wine is no exception. The heart benefits once claimed for wine haven't held up well. If you have high blood pressure, cutting back to well under one or two drinks a day, or stopping, often brings your numbers down noticeably within a few weeks.
had covid 2 weeks ago, feel fine now. can i go back to my usual 10k runs?

Don't jump straight back to 10k. Start with an easy 20 to 30 minute run at conversational pace and build back over a week or two. If you get chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, unusual breathlessness or dizziness, stop and see a doctor before running again, because covid can occasionally affect the heart. If you just feel more tired than usual, that's common and simply means you should slow the ramp-up.
I'm pregnant and my cat scratched me. Should I be worried about toxoplasmosis?

A scratch is a very unlikely route for toxoplasmosis, which mainly spreads through contact with cat feces or eating undercooked meat. Just wash the scratch well and watch for signs of infection. To stay safe, have someone else clean the litter box during your pregnancy, or wear gloves and wash your hands well if you have to do it yourself. Mention the scratch at your next prenatal visit if you'd like reassurance.
My 10 year old had strep throat, on antibiotics for 3 days now and bouncing off the walls. Can she go to soccer practice?

If she's been fever-free for a day and has been on antibiotics for at least 24 hours, she's generally no longer contagious and light practice is usually fine. Keep her water bottle handy and let the coach know she's coming back from being sick. If she gets tired quickly, it's fine to pull her early. Make sure she finishes the full course of antibiotics even though she feels great.
Got some bleach splashed in my eye while cleaning

Rinse it right now with lukewarm running water for at least 15 to 20 minutes, holding the eyelid open and rolling your eye around. Take out contact lenses if you're wearing them. After that, get to urgent care or an ER, or call poison control, because chemical eye injuries can keep doing damage even after the pain eases. Don't rub it.
found out im pregnant, 19, dont want my parents to know. where do i even start

Start with a confidential appointment at a doctor's office, a community health center, or a Planned Parenthood clinic. They can confirm the pregnancy, check how far along you are, and talk through all your options without judgment. At 19 your medical information is private, so they won't contact your parents. If you're able to, start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid now while you figure out next steps, and lean on one trusted person for support if you have someone.
can i take melatonin and my anxiety meds together

It depends on the anxiety medication, because melatonin can add to drowsiness with some drugs, especially benzodiazepines and certain antidepressants like fluvoxamine. Ask your pharmacist with the exact names of what you take, since they can tell you in about a minute whether the combination is safe. If you get the go-ahead, start with a low dose like 0.5 to 1 mg about an hour before bed.
eyes are SO itchy and red, can i use redness relief drops every day?

Skip daily redness-relief drops like Visine Original. They constrict blood vessels and cause rebound redness when used for more than a few days. For allergies, antihistamine eye drops like ketotifen (Zaditor or Alaway) or olopatadine (Pataday) work much better and are fine for daily use. Cool compresses and not rubbing your eyes help too. If you have pain, light sensitivity, blurry vision, or thick discharge, see a doctor, because that's not typical allergy.
stepped on a rusty nail lol last tetanus shot was like high school, im 34

Get a tetanus booster. For a puncture wound like that it's recommended if it's been more than five years, and you're well past that. Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water, and urgent care or a pharmacy can usually give the shot today. Watch it closely too, because nail punctures through shoes can get infected deep down.
what's the fastest way to get rid of a cold sore before a wedding saturday

Start an antiviral as early as possible, ideally at the first tingle, since timing matters more than anything else. Over-the-counter docosanol cream helps a little, but a prescription antiviral like valacyclovir from a doctor or pharmacist is the most effective option and can shorten an outbreak noticeably. Don't pick or squeeze it, wash your hands after touching it, and avoid kissing anyone until it's fully healed. A matte concealer applied with a disposable applicator can cover it on the day once it has crusted.
Is walking OK when I have a sinus infection?

Yes, easy walking is usually fine with a sinus infection and can help you feel less stuffy. Keep it gentle, drink plenty of water, and skip anything that makes your head pound, like bending over a lot or hard efforts. If you also have a fever or feel wiped out, rest instead.
I'm 68 and my doctor said my bones are thinning. Should I just load up on calcium pills?

Don't overdo it. Aim for about 1,200 mg of calcium a day in total, getting as much as you can from food like dairy, fortified milks, canned fish with bones, and leafy greens, and only use a supplement to cover the gap. Very high doses from pills are linked to kidney stones and possibly heart risks. Make sure your vitamin D is adequate too, keep up weight-bearing exercise, and ask your doctor whether you'd benefit from medication, since supplements alone often aren't enough for osteoporosis.
can you get a fever from teething

Teething can cause a slight temperature rise, but not a true fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher. If your baby has a real fever, look for another cause, like a virus or an ear infection, rather than blaming the teeth. Judge how sick he seems the same way you would for any other fever.
got a sunburn so bad my shoulders blistered and i have chills. sleeping it off tonight

Blistering plus chills suggests sun poisoning, and that's worth more than sleeping it off. Drink plenty of fluids, take ibuprofen, cool your skin with damp cloths, and leave the blisters intact. If you develop a fever, vomiting, confusion, dizziness or severe headache, or the blistered area is large, get seen tonight at urgent care because you could be getting dehydrated or developing heat illness.
I think I have lactose intolerance. Can I just diagnose myself and cut out dairy?

You can reasonably test it yourself by cutting out dairy for two weeks and seeing whether the bloating, gas or diarrhea settles, then reintroducing it. If you go dairy-free long term, make sure you still get calcium and vitamin D from fortified foods or supplements. Don't stop at self-diagnosis if cutting dairy doesn't clearly help, or if you have weight loss, blood in your stool or ongoing diarrhea, since celiac disease and IBD can look similar.
I take ashwagandha for stress. My friend said it can mess with your liver?? Freaking out a bit

There are rare but real reported cases of liver injury linked to ashwagandha, so your friend isn't wrong, but serious problems are uncommon. Watch for warning signs like yellowing skin or eyes, dark urine, itching, or upper-right belly pain, and stop taking it and see a doctor if any of those show up. It's also worth avoiding if you have thyroid disease, are pregnant, or take sedatives, and you can ask your doctor about a quick liver test if you plan to keep using it long-term.
Ran out of my seizure meds, pharmacy closed til monday. Should I just skip till then?

Please don't skip them. Suddenly stopping seizure medication can trigger breakthrough seizures, sometimes severe ones. Call your prescriber's after-hours line or an urgent care clinic, as many pharmacists and doctors can arrange an emergency supply, and some 24-hour pharmacies can transfer a prescription. If you can't reach anyone, go to an emergency department, which can give you enough to bridge the weekend.
is 5 hours enough if i feel fine

For the vast majority of adults it isn't, even if you feel okay. Chronic short sleep tends to mask its own effects, so people underestimate how impaired they are. Over time it's linked to worse mood, weight gain, blood sugar problems and higher accident risk. Aim for seven to nine hours. If you truly can't sleep longer even when given the chance, that's worth mentioning to a doctor.
Husband has COPD and is using his oxygen and still seems more out of breath than usual and kinda confused. Wait till tomorrow's appointment?

Don't wait. Worsening shortness of breath plus new confusion in someone with COPD can mean dangerously low oxygen or a buildup of carbon dioxide, and he needs to be checked now. Call emergency services or get him to an ER tonight. Also, don't turn his oxygen up beyond what was prescribed while you wait, because in some COPD patients too much oxygen can make the carbon dioxide problem worse.
my left arm reads 150/90 and my right arm reads 130/80, which one is right??

Both readings count, so go by the higher arm. A small difference between arms is common, but a gap of more than about 10 to 15 points can point to narrowing in an artery and is worth mentioning to your doctor. Recheck both arms carefully a couple more times to confirm it before your appointment.
Can I give my dog's leftover antibiotics to my cat? Same drug, amoxicillin.

Don't do it without asking your vet. Doses are based on species and weight, so the dog tablets could easily be the wrong amount for a cat. A leftover partial course also won't be enough to treat an infection properly. Your vet can tell you quickly whether the cat even needs antibiotics and what dose to use.
I'm 67 and nobody ever told me about a pneumonia vaccine. Do I need one?

Yes, pneumococcal vaccination is recommended for everyone 50 and older, so it's well worth getting now. Usually it's a single dose of PCV20 or PCV21, though your pharmacist or doctor will check whether you've had any earlier pneumococcal shots. Pneumococcal disease can cause serious pneumonia, bloodstream infections, and meningitis, and the risk rises with age, so ask about it at your next pharmacy visit or checkup.
Mom (83) has a bruise on her arm that keeps getting bigger, she's on warfarin. Normal?

A bruise that keeps spreading on warfarin needs a call to her doctor or anticoagulation clinic today, because her INR may be too high. They'll likely want a blood test. Go to the ER if she has blood in her urine or stool, vomits blood, has a severe headache or is bleeding that won't stop. Don't skip or change her warfarin dose unless her clinic tells you to.
toddler pulled a mug of tea onto his chest, skin looks red and some is peeling. he's screaming. what do i do RIGHT NOW

Get him under cool running water straight away and keep it going for 20 minutes. Take off any clothing that isn't stuck to the skin, and keep the rest of him warm so he doesn't get chilled. Call emergency services or head to the ER now, because a scald on a toddler's chest with peeling skin needs urgent assessment. Cover it loosely with cling film or a clean sheet for the trip, and don't put any creams on it.
my 12 yo wants to start using his older brothers acne cream (benzoyl peroxide 10%). fine?

Benzoyl peroxide is safe for a 12-year-old, but 10% is stronger than needed and tends to cause dryness and irritation. A 2.5% to 5% product works about as well with fewer side effects. Have him apply a thin layer once a day at first, use a gentle moisturizer, and keep it away from towels and pillowcases because it bleaches fabric. If his acne is painful, cystic or not improving after 8 to 12 weeks, see a doctor.
I'm 50, diabetic, high BP. My chest feels heavy for a few minutes when I'm stressed at work, then fine. Probably stress, yeah?

Stress can trigger it, but stress also raises your heart's oxygen demand, and with diabetes and high blood pressure, short episodes of chest heaviness could be angina. Book a doctor's appointment within the next few days and describe exactly what happens, so they can check your heart with an ECG and likely a stress test. If an episode lasts more than about 10 minutes, happens at rest without a trigger, or comes with sweating or breathlessness, call emergency services.
Is it true that you should starve a fever and feed a cold?

No, that's an old myth. Your body needs fuel and especially fluids whether you have a fever or a cold, and fever actually raises your fluid needs because you lose more through sweating. Eat what you can stomach, even if it's just broth, toast or fruit, and keep drinking water steadily throughout the day.
teen daughter has stomach pain most mornings before school for weeks. is she faking?

Probably not, as anxiety and stress often cause very real stomach pain, especially in the morning before school. It's worth a pediatrician visit to rule out physical causes like constipation, reflux or celiac disease. Then gently talk with her about how school is going, including friends, bullying or academic pressure. Get her seen sooner if she's losing weight, has blood in her stool, or wakes up at night with pain.
can i use my hot tub if i keep it short

It's best to skip hot tubs, especially in the first trimester, because raising your core temperature above about 102°F is linked to neural tube defects. Even short soaks can heat you up faster than you'd expect. A warm, not hot, bath is a safe alternative.
I'm diabetic and have the flu, can barely eat. Anything I should watch?

Yes. Illness can push your blood sugar up even when you're not eating, so check it every 3 to 4 hours and keep taking your insulin or meds unless your doctor has told you otherwise. Sip fluids constantly and use small amounts of juice or crackers if you can't eat meals. If you use insulin, check for ketones. Call your doctor if your readings stay above 250 mg/dL, you're vomiting and can't keep fluids down, or you test positive for ketones.
I'm 28 and my big toe joint suddenly got red, hot and super swollen overnight. Hurts to even have a sheet on it. What is this??

That pattern of sudden, intensely painful, red, hot swelling in the big toe is classic gout, though an infected joint can look similar. See a doctor in the next day or so, because they can confirm it and prescribe medication that calms an attack quickly. If you also have a fever or feel generally unwell, go to urgent care today to rule out infection. In the meantime, rest it, elevate it, ice it in short sessions, and drink plenty of water while avoiding alcohol.
is it ok to give tylenol before my baby's shots so he doesn't get a fever

It's better not to give it in advance, because some research suggests that giving fever reducers before vaccination may slightly weaken the immune response. Instead, if he becomes fussy or feverish afterward, you can treat that, after checking the right dose for his weight with the pediatrician. Feeding, cuddling or skin-to-skin contact during and right after the shots works surprisingly well for the pain.
Coughing up a little yellow-green mucus. Does that mean bacterial infection?

Not necessarily. Colored mucus is common in ordinary viral colds and doesn't by itself mean you need antibiotics. What matters more is the pattern. See a doctor if you've had symptoms for more than 10 days, if a fever comes back after you started improving, or if you're short of breath. Coughing up blood or having chest pain warrants a visit right away.
Gout flare in my big toe AGAIN. How do I stop these?

For the current flare, rest and raise the foot, ice it, and use the anti-inflammatory or colchicine your doctor has advised. If you keep getting flares, ask your GP about a urate-lowering medicine like allopurinol, because that's what actually stops repeat attacks. Cutting back on beer, spirits, sugary drinks, red meat and shellfish and drinking plenty of water helps too, but medication is usually key once flares are frequent.
chickenpox vaccine for adult who never had it, do I bother? 34 and healthy

Yes, it's worth getting, since chickenpox tends to be much more severe in adults, with a higher risk of pneumonia and hospitalization. Adults need two doses at least four weeks apart. Because it's a live vaccine, don't get it if you're pregnant, and avoid getting pregnant for a month after each dose. If you're not sure whether you had chickenpox as a kid, a blood test can check, but getting vaccinated without the test is also fine.
is clove oil legit for toothache or is that a myth

It's legit as a short-term fix, because clove oil contains eugenol, which numbs and calms the area. Dab a small amount on a cotton ball and hold it against the tooth, keeping it mostly off your gums, since too much can irritate the tissue. It won't treat whatever is causing the pain, so use it to get you to a dental appointment, not instead of one.
There's a little skin tag on my neck. Can I just snip it off with nail clippers?

I wouldn't, because even small skin tags have a blood supply and can bleed a surprising amount, and home tools raise the risk of infection. A GP or dermatologist can remove one in a couple of minutes by freezing or snipping it with sterile equipment. That also lets them confirm it really is a skin tag and not something else. If it isn't bothering you, it's completely fine to leave alone.
My chiropractor wants me to come in 3x a week for 6 months for my back. That seems like a lot?

Your instinct is reasonable, because that's a big commitment, and the evidence doesn't support long, open-ended adjustment plans for most back pain. Spinal manipulation can help some people in the short term, but the benefit usually shows up within a few sessions if it's going to show up at all. Ask what specific improvement you should expect and by when. You could also get an opinion from your doctor or a physical therapist, who can build an exercise plan you can eventually do on your own.
ugh my chest burns after big meals and when I lie down. Heartburn obviously. but how do I know it's not my heart lol

Burning that reliably follows big meals or lying down, and eases with antacids, points strongly to reflux. Heart pain is more often a pressure or squeezing, typically triggered by exertion or stress and relieved by rest. The two can overlap, though, especially in older people, diabetics and women. Get checked if you have heart risk factors, if it ever comes on during activity, or if it isn't clearly improving with reflux treatment.
We think Mom (80) might have had a mini stroke. Her face drooped for like 10 minutes then went back to normal. She's fine now.

Take her to the ER now, even though she's back to normal. Those symptoms sound like a transient ischemic attack, a warning sign that a major stroke may follow, often within days. Doctors can find the cause and start treatment that greatly lowers that risk. If the symptoms come back on the way, call 911.
I've had a cold for 4 days, can I just take some leftover amoxicillin from last year to knock it out faster?

Don't take it. Colds are caused by viruses and antibiotics do nothing against them, so you'd get the side effects like diarrhea and rash without any benefit, plus you'd be helping breed resistant bacteria. Old leftovers are also often an incomplete course or the wrong drug entirely. Rest, fluids and something for symptoms will serve you better, and if you're still getting worse after 10 days or develop a high fever, see a doctor rather than self-prescribing.
can you get the chickenpox vaccine if you already had chickenpox as a kid

If you've definitely had chickenpox, you're already immune and don't need the varicella vaccine. If you're not sure, a blood test can check your immunity, and getting the vaccine anyway is safe. The more relevant shot for you later is Shingrix at age 50, because the chickenpox virus stays dormant in your body and can reactivate as shingles.
I've been taking my mom's zolpidem when I can't sleep. She doesn't mind. Is that fine?

Please stop doing that, because zolpidem is a prescription sedative with real risks, including next-morning impairment, sleepwalking or sleep-driving, and dangerous interactions with alcohol and other drugs. The right dose depends on the person, and women are usually given lower doses because the drug clears more slowly. If your sleep is bad enough that you're reaching for her pills, it's worth seeing your own doctor. They can look at the cause and offer options like CBT for insomnia, or a safer prescription if one is truly needed.
My husband got bitten by a cat yesterday, it's just two little punctures. He says it's nothing.

Cat bites deserve more respect than they get, because those small deep punctures infect easily, sometimes within a day. He should see a doctor today, since antibiotics are often given preventively for cat bites, especially on the hand. Also check when he last had a tetanus shot. If redness, swelling or pain is spreading, or he can't move a finger well, he needs prompt care.
Is it ok to drink coffee at 5pm if it doesn't keep me awake?

Even if you fall asleep fine, caffeine has a half-life of about five to six hours, so a 5 pm coffee is still in your system at midnight and can reduce your deep sleep without you noticing. Many people find they wake up more refreshed once they cut caffeine after early afternoon. Try switching to decaf in the afternoon for a week and see if your mornings feel different.
what gets rid of warts fastest. i have one on my finger

Over-the-counter salicylic acid is the most reliable home option: soak the wart, file off the dead top layer with a disposable emery board, then apply the treatment daily, and expect it to take several weeks. Freezing kits from the pharmacy can also work, though a doctor's cryotherapy is stronger and usually faster. Skip cutting or burning it yourself, and see a doctor if it's spreading, painful, bleeding, or you have diabetes or poor circulation.
best supplement for anxiety? don't want meds

The evidence for supplements is fairly modest. Magnesium and L-theanine are gentle and generally safe for most people, and chamomile has some small studies behind it. Be careful with kava, which has been linked to liver damage, and St John's wort, which interacts with lots of medications including birth control. Regular exercise and CBT, which you can do without medication, have far stronger evidence, so they're worth pairing with anything you try. Check with a pharmacist if you take other medicines.
I've been feeling exhausted for months and I think I need an energy supplement, which one is best?

Months of exhaustion is worth getting checked before you buy anything. Common causes like anemia, thyroid problems, low B12 or vitamin D, sleep apnea and depression are all easy to test for and treat properly. Energy supplements mostly rely on caffeine and would just cover up the problem. See your doctor and ask for basic bloodwork; it's a quick visit and could actually fix this.
is it okay to take my sleeping pill and then drive in like 5 hours

Probably not, depending on the pill. Many sleep medications, including extended-release zolpidem and some others, can still impair driving the next morning even when you feel fine, especially after less than a full 7 to 8 hours of sleep. Only take it if you can stay in bed for the full time recommended on the label. Check with your pharmacist about your specific medication.
cut my thumb slicing bagels. bleeding a lot. how long do i press before worrying

Press firmly with a clean cloth for a full 10 minutes without peeking, because lifting it to check restarts the bleeding. Keep your hand raised above your heart while you press. If it's still bleeding steadily after 10 to 15 minutes of real pressure, or the cut gapes open, go to urgent care, because it likely needs stitches or glue. Also get seen if your thumb feels numb or won't bend properly, since that can mean nerve or tendon damage.
Recovering from a stomach bug, still kind of weak. Yoga ok?

Gentle yoga is a nice choice while you're getting your strength back, as long as you're keeping fluids down. Stick with restorative or slow flow poses. Skip hot yoga and intense inversions for now, because dehydration and low blood sugar can make you dizzy. Have a small snack and some water beforehand, and stop if you feel faint.
i'm 19 and have a fever of 103.5 and my neck is super stiff and the light hurts my eyes. probably just flu?

Please get to an emergency room right now, don't wait this out. High fever with a stiff neck and sensitivity to light can be signs of meningitis, which can become life-threatening within hours but is very treatable when caught early. Call 911 if you notice a rash that doesn't fade when you press a glass against it, or if you're getting confused or very drowsy.
Can anxiety cause chest pain? I get it during panic attacks and the ER already cleared my heart twice.

Yes. Panic attacks commonly cause chest tightness, a racing heart, tingling and breathlessness, and two clear ER workups are genuinely reassuring. The most useful next step is treating the anxiety itself, since therapy like CBT and sometimes medication work well for panic disorder. Get rechecked if the pain feels different from your usual pattern, comes with exertion, or you develop new risk factors as you age.
is it safe to keep going with my marathon training if I sometimes feel my heart flutter on runs

It's worth pausing the hard sessions until you've been checked, because palpitations during exercise warrant a look in a way that ones at rest often don't. Endurance athletes can develop rhythm problems, and occasionally there's an underlying structural issue. See your doctor and ask about an ECG, an echocardiogram and possibly an exercise test. Stop immediately and get help if you ever feel faint, get chest pain or have a prolonged racing heartbeat while running.
pregnant, 30 weeks, have a fever of 101. can i take something

Acetaminophen is generally considered the preferred fever reducer during pregnancy, so take it as directed. Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Call your OB or midwife today, because a fever in pregnancy should be evaluated to find its cause. Go in right away if you also have contractions, fluid leaking, reduced fetal movement, or abdominal pain.
how do i know if a cut is infected

Look for redness spreading out from the cut, warmth, swelling, throbbing pain that gets worse after the first day or two, pus, or a bad smell. Red streaks running up from the wound or a fever mean the infection may be spreading, and you should be seen the same day. Mild pinkness right at the edges in the first couple of days is normal healing.
I'm 68 and just got over pneumonia, finished antibiotics 5 days ago. I'm so weak. What exercise should I even do?

Start very gently with short walks around the house or down the street, maybe five to ten minutes a couple of times a day, and add a few minutes every few days as your energy allows. Sit-to-stand from a chair and slow deep breathing are great for rebuilding strength and lung capacity. Feeling weak for several weeks after pneumonia is very normal at your age. Still, let your doctor know if you're getting breathless doing very little, have chest pain, or still have a cough or fever, and ask them whether a pulmonary rehab program would help.
I have heart failure and my ankles swelled up overnight and I gained 4 lbs. Wait it out?

Don't wait it out. A gain of 2–3 pounds in a day or 5 in a week, along with new swelling, usually means you're retaining fluid, and that's an early warning sign of worsening heart failure. Call your cardiologist or heart failure nurse today, since they may adjust your diuretic. If you get short of breath, especially lying down, go to the ER.
I'm pregnant and was down with a bad cold for a week. Is it okay to go back to my prenatal yoga?

Prenatal yoga is usually fine to return to once you're over a cold, especially since it's gentle. Make sure any fever is gone, you're drinking plenty, and take it easier than normal for the first class or two. If you had a high fever or are still feeling run down or short of breath, check in with your midwife or OB first.
I'm a welder, forgot my mask for a quick job, now hours later my eyes are killing me and watering nonstop

That's likely welder's flash, a UV burn of the cornea that typically shows up hours later and feels like sand in your eyes. It usually heals in a day or two. You should still see a doctor or ER, who can confirm there's no metal fragment and give you proper pain relief. Don't rub your eyes or use numbing drops repeatedly, as those slow healing.
Chemo patient here, last infusion 8 days ago, temp just hit 100.6. Wait till morning?

Don't wait. A fever around a week after chemo can mean neutropenic fever, which is a medical emergency because your immune defenses are at their lowest. Call your oncology team's after-hours number right now, or go to the ER if you can't reach them. Hold off on fever reducers until they tell you otherwise, since those can hide what's happening.
Hiking and my buddy got a deep gash on his shin from a rock, we're 3 miles from the car. Pour whiskey on it?

Skip the whiskey. It damages tissue and doesn't clean well. Press firmly to stop the bleeding, then flush the wound with as much clean drinking water as you can spare, cover it with the cleanest dressing you have, and wrap it snugly. Hike out at a steady pace and get it seen today. A deep gash with possible dirt in it may need stitches and a tetanus shot.
I have asthma and I'm getting a chest cold. Anything I should do differently?

Colds are a common asthma trigger, so start paying closer attention now rather than waiting to see how it goes. Follow your asthma action plan, keep your rescue inhaler with you, and check with your doctor about stepping up your controller medication if you're needing the rescue inhaler more than usual. If your inhaler isn't giving relief, you're too short of breath to talk in full sentences, or your lips look bluish, get emergency care. If you get flu rather than a cold, call your doctor early, since you qualify for antivirals.
do vaccines cause autism yes or no

No. This has been studied in millions of children across many countries, and no link has been found between vaccines, including MMR, and autism. The study that started the claim was retracted, and its author lost his medical license over it. Autism signs often become noticeable around the same age kids get some routine shots, which is why the timing can look suspicious even though there's no connection.
ok so I've been vegan for 2 years and never taken B12. am I screwed

You're probably not screwed, but start B12 today and get your levels checked. Your body can store B12 for a while, but two years is long enough that some people become deficient, which can cause fatigue, numbness or tingling, and memory problems. Nerve-related symptoms in particular should be checked promptly. A common routine is 250 mcg cyanocobalamin daily or 2,500 mcg weekly, and your doctor may give injections if your levels are very low.
how many puffs of ventolin is too many in a day

There's no hard daily ceiling, but needing your reliever more than about twice a week means your asthma isn't controlled and you need a review. If you're needing it every few hours, or it isn't lasting even four hours, that's a flare and you should be seen today. If you're using it constantly with little relief or struggling to speak, call emergency services. During an attack you can take up to 10 puffs while you wait.
Pregnant (34 weeks) and I've got a fluttering heartbeat and get breathless lying flat. Normal pregnancy stuff?

Some palpitations and breathlessness are common late in pregnancy, but needing to sit up to breathe isn't something to brush off. It can be a sign of heart strain, including a pregnancy-related heart weakness called peripartum cardiomyopathy. Call your midwife or obstetrician today to get checked. Go to labour and delivery or the ER right away if you have chest pain, fainting, a cough with frothy sputum, or worsening breathlessness.
I fell asleep with my contacts in again lol. eye is a bit sore and light sensitive now, is that normal

Soreness plus light sensitivity after sleeping in contacts is a warning sign rather than a normal hangover, because it can mean a corneal ulcer or infection is starting. Take the lenses out, leave them out, and don't patch the eye. If the pain, redness or light sensitivity hasn't clearly improved within a few hours, or you notice blurry vision or a white spot on the eye, see an eye doctor today, since these infections can scar the cornea quickly.
I keep getting painful lumps in my armpits that drain and scar. Been happening for years. Embarrassing tbh.

Recurrent painful lumps in the armpits that drain and scar are often hidradenitis suppurativa, a chronic inflammatory condition that's more common than people think and nothing to be embarrassed about. Please see a doctor or dermatologist, because there are real treatments, from antibiotics and other medicines to newer biologic drugs. Early treatment can reduce flares and prevent more scarring. Loose clothing, avoiding shaving irritation and not smoking can help in the meantime.
Marathon in 9 days. Got a bad chest cold with fever 3 days ago. I've trained 5 months for this. I'm running it no matter what, how do I make it work?

I get how gutting this is after five months, but running a marathon soon after a feverish chest infection is genuinely risky for your heart and lungs, not just your finish time. The bare minimum is to be fever-free with no chest symptoms for several days before race day, and ideally to get checked by a doctor first. If you're still coughing or feeling run down the week of the race, the safer move is to drop to a shorter distance, run it as a gentle jog, or defer. Any chest pain, racing heart or dizziness on the course means stop immediately, no matter how close the finish is.
Marathon in 10 days. Got a nasty chest cold now. I've trained 4 months for this, I'm running it no matter what, just tell me how.

Running a marathon with an active chest infection, fever or body aches is genuinely risky, because it raises the chance of heart complications, so that's the one non-negotiable line. If you're symptom-free and fever-free for several days before race day, you can likely still run, just at a slower goal pace than planned. Rest completely while you're sick, then do a few easy short runs before the race to see how you feel. If you're still coughing up stuff or feel feverish on the morning, defer or drop out, and see a doctor if you're unsure, because there will be other marathons.
sudden ripping pain in my chest going through to my back, worst pain ever. 61, high blood pressure

Call emergency services immediately. A sudden tearing pain that goes through to your back, in someone with high blood pressure, can be an aortic dissection, which is life-threatening and needs a hospital within minutes. Don't take aspirin, since it could make bleeding worse if that's what this is. Stay as still and calm as you can until help arrives.
got hit in the eye with a tennis ball, it's swollen and vision is a little blurry

Blurry vision after a blow to the eye needs same-day evaluation, ideally at an ER or by an eye doctor, because it can mean bleeding inside the eye, a retinal injury or a fracture around the socket. In the meantime, use a cold pack gently over the closed lid without pressing on the eye. Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen, which can increase bleeding, and don't blow your nose. Go immediately if you see blood in the colored part, have double vision, or the pain is severe.
quick q: can i eat after food poisoning or should i fast

You don't need to fast. Focus on fluids first, then add bland foods like toast, rice, bananas, crackers or broth as soon as you feel up to it. Hold off on greasy food, alcohol and lots of dairy for a day or two. See a doctor if you can't keep fluids down, have bloody stools or a high fever, or symptoms last more than three days.
I got bit by a stray cat yesterday, hand is a bit puffy. It's just a little bite.

Cat bites are deceptively risky because their teeth make deep punctures that often get infected fast, especially on the hand. Get seen today, since you'll likely need antibiotics and a check on your tetanus status. Because it was a stray, the doctor also needs to assess rabies risk, which is a serious concern that can't wait. Wash it well with soap and water on the way.
is it safe to drive with a migraine

Usually not, especially if you have aura, blurred vision, nausea or have taken a triptan or anything sedating. Migraine slows your reaction time and concentration more than people realize. Pull over, take your medication, and wait until the symptoms clear or get someone else to drive.
my stomach has been hurting on the lower right side since last night and now it hurts more when i walk. probably just gas right?

Pain that settles in the lower right and gets worse when you walk or move is a classic pattern for appendicitis, so this isn't one to wait out. Get seen today at urgent care or the ER, especially if you also have fever, nausea or loss of appetite. Don't take strong painkillers or laxatives beforehand, since they can mask symptoms or make things worse. If it turns out to be gas, great, but this is worth ruling out quickly.
I have leftover amoxicillin from last year, can I just take that for my tooth infection??

I wouldn't, because a partial leftover supply probably isn't a full course, and it might not be the right drug or dose for this infection. Antibiotics alone also don't fix a dental abscess. The source usually needs a dentist to drain it, do a root canal, or pull the tooth, and otherwise the infection comes back. Call a dentist or urgent care today, and go to the ER if you develop facial swelling, fever, or trouble swallowing.
Back pain for 3 weeks, now I've got shooting pain down my left leg to my foot and some tingling. 45M. Is this sciatica and can I just stretch it out?

That sounds like sciatica, most often from a disc irritating a nerve root. Many cases do improve over weeks with gentle movement, walking, and anti-inflammatories. Because you've got tingling down to the foot, book an appointment with a doctor or physiotherapist so they can check your strength and reflexes and guide which stretches to do, since some can aggravate it. Go to the ER right away if you notice foot drop, worsening leg weakness, numbness in the groin area, or bladder or bowel changes.
ice bath to bring down a high fever fast, good idea?

No, skip the ice bath. Very cold water causes shivering, which can actually raise your core temperature, and it's miserable and risky, especially for kids. Instead, use fever medicine like acetaminophen or ibuprofen at the correct dose, wear light clothing, and try a lukewarm sponge bath if you want extra comfort. If a fever is extremely high or isn't coming down with medicine, call a doctor.
my friend has extra sumatriptan, can i try one for my migraine? never been diagnosed

Don't take someone else's sumatriptan. Triptans narrow blood vessels and can be risky if you have heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure or certain other conditions, and an undiagnosed headache might not be a migraine at all. See your doctor, because if it is migraine they can prescribe a triptan that's safe for you. Ibuprofen or naproxen is a reasonable choice in the meantime if you tolerate it.
is 5 hours of sleep enough if i feel fine

For the vast majority of adults, no. Research consistently shows people need 7 to 9 hours, and chronically sleep-restricted people tend to underestimate how impaired they are because they get used to feeling that way. Ongoing short sleep is linked to weaker immunity, weight gain, worse mood and slower reaction times. Try getting 7 or more hours for two weeks and see whether your focus and energy change.
I'm on warfarin and my back is killing me. What can I take that won't mess with it?

Acetaminophen is the usual choice for people on warfarin, but even it can raise your INR if you take it regularly at higher doses, so stick to modest amounts and tell your anticoagulation clinic if you're using it daily. Avoid ibuprofen, naproxen and aspirin, because they increase bleeding risk on top of warfarin. Heat, gentle movement and topical options like a lidocaine patch are also reasonable. If the pain is severe, came on after a fall, or comes with numbness or trouble controlling your bladder, get seen promptly.
Does vitamin C actually do anything once you're sick

Not much. Taking vitamin C after symptoms start hasn't been shown to shorten colds in any meaningful way, though regular daily use might trim them slightly for some people. Zinc lozenges started within a day of symptoms have somewhat better evidence. Rest, fluids, and time are still the real cure.
I'm diabetic and my cat scratched my foot yesterday. It's a little red now. Should I wait and see?

With diabetes I wouldn't wait on this, because reduced circulation and slower healing in the feet make infections more likely to escalate. Clean it gently, keep it covered, and call your doctor today to have it looked at, since redness a day later can be the start of an infection. Get care urgently if the redness spreads, you develop a fever, or the foot becomes hot or painful.
Can I take double my ibuprofen dose for a really bad back day? Regular dose isn't touching it.

Don't double it, because higher doses sharply raise the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain without adding much pain relief. A safer move is pairing the normal ibuprofen dose with paracetamol, which works differently and can be combined if you have no conditions that rule either out. Add heat and gentle movement too. If standard doses aren't touching the pain after a few days, see a doctor, since that's a sign it needs proper assessment rather than more pills.
My eyes are so itchy and red from pollen I want to rip them out. Any fast relief?

Antihistamine eye drops like ketotifen, sold over the counter, work within minutes and are the best quick fix. Cold compresses and refrigerated artificial tears also soothe and rinse out pollen. Avoid rubbing, which makes it worse, and wear sunglasses outside. If you get eye pain, vision changes, or thick discharge, see a doctor, since that's not typical allergy.
Deep cut on my thumb from a box cutter, I can see like yellowish stuff inside. It stopped bleeding. Can I just superglue it shut?

That yellowish tissue means the cut has gone through the skin into the fat layer, so this needs a clinic or urgent care rather than home glue. A deep thumb cut can involve tendons or nerves, and it needs proper cleaning to avoid infection, which household superglue won't do. Cover it with a clean dressing and try to be seen within the next few hours, since wounds are best closed early.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and so tired. Can I take extra iron on top of my prenatal? My friend said it fixed her exhaustion.

Don't add iron on your own. Your prenatal already contains some, extra iron can cause constipation and nausea, and too much isn't good for you or the baby. Ask your midwife or OB for a quick blood test to check your iron and ferritin levels. If you're low, they'll prescribe the right dose, and fatigue at 34 weeks can have other causes worth ruling out too.
I've been feeling down for like 2 weeks after my breakup. Is that depression?

Two weeks of feeling low after a breakup is a normal grief response, not necessarily depression. Keep up the basics: see friends, move your body, eat and sleep regularly, and go easy on drinking and late-night scrolling. Watch out if it's getting worse rather than slowly lifting, if you lose interest in everything, or if you can't function at work or school after a month or so. If that happens, or if you have any thoughts of hurting yourself, talk to a doctor or counselor.
My friend has leftover oxycodone from his surgery, says I can have some for my back. Good idea?

Please skip it. Taking someone else's opioid prescription is risky because the dose wasn't chosen for you, it can interact badly with other medications or alcohol, and it's illegal to share. Opioids also don't actually help most back pain recover any faster. If over-the-counter options aren't cutting it, a doctor can assess you and offer something appropriate, including stronger short-term options if you genuinely need them.
is it ok to put my 3 month old to sleep on her tummy? she sleeps so much better

Please keep putting her down on her back for every sleep until she turns 1. Babies do sleep more deeply on their tummies, and that's partly why tummy sleeping raises the risk of SIDS. Once she can roll both ways on her own, you can leave her in whatever position she rolls into. A snug sleep sack and a consistent routine can help her settle on her back.
pimple in the danger triangle of my face, is it gonna kill me lol

Almost certainly not, as the risk of an infection there spreading to the brain is very rare. Still, that area is the one place where it's best not to squeeze, so treat it with warm compresses and a benzoyl peroxide spot treatment. See a doctor promptly if the area becomes very swollen, hot, intensely painful, or you develop fever, headache or swelling around the eye.
i have a dental phobia and would rather just deal with the pain forever honestly

That fear is really common, and dentists deal with it all the time, so you don't have to just white-knuckle it. Look for an office that advertises anxious-patient or sedation care, tell them upfront, and ask about breaks, numbing gel before injections, nitrous oxide, or oral sedation. Ongoing tooth pain usually means a problem that gets bigger and harder to treat, so a short, gentle visit now is far kinder to you than an emergency later.
whats the fastest way to get my mom to stop being dizzy when she stands up

Have her stand up slowly in stages: sit on the edge of the bed for a minute, pump her ankles, then rise while holding something steady. Drinking a glass of water before getting up helps too. Dizziness on standing is often caused by blood pressure medication or dehydration, so she should tell her doctor, who can check her lying and standing blood pressure and possibly adjust her meds. She shouldn't stop or cut any medication on her own, because that can cause its own problems.
Ok so my migraine meds aren't working anymore, can I just double the dose?

Don't double it on your own. Higher doses of triptans or NSAIDs raise the risk of side effects without reliably working better, and frequent use can lock you into rebound headaches. Meds often seem to fail because they're taken too late in the attack, so try taking them at the very first sign of pain. Talk to your doctor about switching drugs or adding a preventive, since there are many newer options.
my friend says she can give my kid his vaccines at home since she's a vet tech and can get them cheaper. good idea?

No, I'd steer clear of that, even though your friend means well.
