Human vaccines need proper storage and handling, the correct dose and schedule for your child's age, a record that counts officially for school, and someone ready to treat a rare allergic reaction on the spot. If cost is the issue, the Vaccines for Children program provides free vaccines for eligible kids at many clinics and health departments, and most insurance covers childhood vaccines with no copay.
pimple on my upper lip is huge and swollen and my face is puffy now. just pop it?

Don't squeeze it. The area around your nose and upper lip drains toward veins near the brain, so squeezing an infected spot there can rarely spread infection somewhere dangerous. Facial swelling spreading beyond the pimple means it's past the warm-compress stage, so see a doctor today, since you may need antibiotics. If you get fever, vision changes, or swelling around your eye, go to the ER.
Kid swallowed maybe 3 of my blood pressure pills (amlodipine). He seems fine.

Call Poison Control right now at 1-800-222-1222 in the US, or call emergency services. Amlodipine can be dangerous for young children even in small amounts, and symptoms like low blood pressure can be delayed by several hours, so seeming fine doesn't mean he's safe. Keep the pill bottle handy and don't try to make him vomit.
102.5 fever and a really stiff neck, hurts to bend my head forward. probably just slept wrong right

I wouldn't assume that. A fever combined with a stiff neck that hurts when you bend forward is a classic warning sign of meningitis, which needs emergency treatment. Go to the ER now, and call 911 if you also have a bad headache, sensitivity to light, a rash, or confusion. It's far better to get checked and find out it's nothing than to wait on this one.
teen here (16), my heart races when I drink energy drinks, like 2 cans. bad?

Yes, that's your body telling you it's too much caffeine and stimulant, and two cans is well above what's considered safe for a 16-year-old. Racing heart, jitteriness and anxiety are common, and in rare cases energy drinks have triggered dangerous heart rhythms. Cut them out or limit yourself to much less. Tell a parent or doctor if you've ever fainted, had chest pain, or had a racing heart without caffeine, because that should be checked.
Quick q: does caffeine help or hurt headaches

Both, depending on how you use it. A cup of coffee early in a headache can boost painkillers and ease some migraines, but regular heavy intake leads to withdrawal headaches when you miss your usual dose. Keep your intake steady and moderate, roughly under 200 mg a day if you get frequent headaches, and avoid using it as a daily painkiller.
is it bad to look at the sun during an eclipse for just a second

Yes, even a few seconds can burn the retina and leave a permanent blind spot, and it doesn't hurt while it's happening, so you won't notice the damage until later. Regular sunglasses don't protect you either. Use certified eclipse glasses or a pinhole projector instead. If you notice a blurry or dark spot in your vision afterward, see an eye doctor.
Read online that garlic supplements work as well as BP meds. True?

Garlic supplements may lower blood pressure a few points in some people, but the evidence isn't strong enough to call them equal to medication. They can also increase bleeding risk if you take blood thinners. If you want to try garlic, think of it as an add-on rather than a swap, and tell your doctor so they can watch your readings.
Got my wisdom tooth out 4 days ago. Pain was getting better but now it's suddenly way worse and my breath smells awful.

That pattern sounds a lot like dry socket, where the blood clot in the socket is lost and leaves the bone exposed. It's very treatable, so call the dentist or oral surgeon who did the extraction. They can clean the socket and put in a medicated dressing that often relieves pain within hours. Until then, avoid straws, smoking and spitting hard.
just grabbed a hot pan handle, palm is bright red and stings like crazy. ice?

Skip the ice, because it can damage already-injured skin. Run the burn under cool tap water for a solid 20 minutes, which genuinely limits how deep the damage goes even if you start a few minutes late. After that, take off any rings before your hand swells and cover it loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing. If it blisters across a large part of your palm, get it checked, since hand burns can affect movement as they heal.
Came back from Ghana 2 weeks ago, now fever and chills. Probably flu right?

Don't assume it's flu. Fever after travel to a malaria area needs urgent testing for malaria, even if you took preventive pills. Malaria can become severe quickly, especially in the first few weeks after you return. Go to urgent care or the emergency department today and tell them where you traveled.
got hit in the eye with a tennis ball, it's swollen, vision kind of blurry, but I'm fine

Blurry vision after a direct hit means you should get checked today, because blunt trauma can cause bleeding inside the eye, retinal damage, or a fracture around the eye socket. Cold compresses without pressure are fine on the way, but avoid rubbing it and don't take aspirin. Go to the ER right away if you see blood in the colored part of the eye, have double vision, severe pain, or worsening vision.
Is it bad to sleep on my back? Keep waking up on it, 30 weeks

Try to fall asleep on your side from about 28 weeks on, because lying flat on your back can press on major blood vessels and reduce blood flow to the baby. Waking up on your back isn't a cause for alarm, so just roll back over to your side when you notice. A pillow wedged behind your back or a pregnancy pillow makes it much easier to stay put. Either side is fine, although the left is often suggested.
Is it true I should let a bite wound bleed a little before cleaning it?

A little bleeding can help flush out bacteria, so there's no need to stop gentle bleeding immediately. The real priority is washing it thoroughly under running water with soap for several minutes. Don't squeeze or cut the wound to make it bleed more. If it's bleeding heavily, apply firm pressure and get it looked at.
Can I give my 18 month old honey for his cough?

Yes, once a child is over 12 months honey is safe, and it actually works about as well as many over-the-counter cough remedies. Half to one teaspoon before bed is a good amount, either on its own or stirred into warm water. Just never give it to babies under one because of the risk of botulism, and see a doctor if the cough comes with labored breathing, lasts more than a couple of weeks, or he seems really unwell.
what actually helps a tension headache that isn't pills

Heat or massage on your neck and shoulders, a short walk and getting away from screens all help loosen the muscle tension behind these headaches. Drink a big glass of water, check whether you've skipped a meal, and fix your posture if you've been hunched over a laptop. Over the longer term, regular exercise, steady sleep and stress management cut down how often they happen.
my toddler grabbed a curling iron, small red mark on fingers, he stopped crying after 5 min

Run his fingers under cool water for 20 minutes, even though he's calmed down, because it limits how deep the burn goes. Then cover them loosely with a clean dressing. If the mark stays red without blistering, it should heal within a week. Have a doctor look at it if blisters appear, if the burn wraps around a finger, or if it looks white or waxy, since burns on toddlers' hands need careful healing to avoid stiffness.
I got a flu shot 2 weeks ago and now I have the flu. Was it pointless?

Not pointless. The vaccine doesn't block every strain, but people who've had it tend to get milder illness and are much less likely to end up hospitalized. It's possible you caught a strain it doesn't cover well, or something flu-like that isn't flu at all. If you're in a high-risk group or it's within 48 hours of symptoms starting, ask a doctor about antivirals.
My dad (70) suddenly has a headache and his speech is slurred and his face looks droopy on one side

Call 911 right now. Those are stroke signs and every minute counts. Note the time the symptoms started, keep him sitting or lying safely, and don't give him food, drinks or aspirin while you wait for the ambulance.
I have hypothyroidism and take levothyroxine. Started a calcium supplement for my bones. Anything to know?

Yes, timing matters. Calcium can block levothyroxine absorption, so take them at least four hours apart. Most people take levothyroxine first thing in the morning on an empty stomach and calcium later with dinner. Iron and some antacids interfere the same way. If you've been taking them together, mention it at your next thyroid check, since your TSH may have shifted.
My doctor said I have sleep apnea and wants me on CPAP but I hate the mask. Can I just use one of those anti-snoring mouth strips instead?

Mouth tape or snoring strips can reduce snoring noise but don't treat apnea, so your oxygen could keep dropping all night while the problem stays hidden. Since you hate the mask, go back to your doctor or equipment supplier, because there are many styles, including nasal pillows, and finding the right fit makes a huge difference. Depending on how severe your apnea is, a custom oral appliance from a sleep dentist or other treatments might be options too. Don't simply skip treatment, as untreated apnea takes a real toll on your heart.
Can I just give my 85 year old mother my leftover oxycodone for her hip pain? Her doctor is slow to call back.

Please don't. Opioids hit older adults much harder, and a dose that was fine for you can cause dangerous drowsiness, confusion, falls, or slowed breathing in her, especially with her other meds. Call the doctor's office and say the pain is severe and she needs to be seen or have something prescribed today. If she can't put weight on that hip or the pain started after a fall, take her to urgent care or the ER, because it could be a fracture.
pulled my own loose molar with pliers lol, it's bleeding a lot. what now

Fold a clean gauze pad or a damp black tea bag, bite down on the socket with firm, steady pressure for a full 30 to 45 minutes without peeking, and keep your head elevated. Don't rinse, spit, or use a straw for the next day, because that can dislodge the clot. If it's still bleeding heavily after an hour of pressure, or you take blood thinners, get seen urgently. Either way, have a dentist check that no root fragments were left behind.
is it okay to put ice directly on a sprain? I want it to work faster

Don't put ice directly on bare skin, because it can cause frostbite surprisingly quickly. Wrap the ice or a bag of frozen peas in a thin towel and apply it for 15 to 20 minutes, then give your skin at least an hour off before the next round. More cold doesn't speed healing, and those short sessions get you all the benefit.
can i use a steroid inhaler while pregnant

Yes, the commonly used steroid preventers like budesonide are considered safe in pregnancy. Poorly controlled asthma is a much bigger risk to you and the baby than the inhaler is. Keep taking it, and tell your midwife and doctor so they can keep an eye on your asthma as the pregnancy goes on.
Teenage son goes to bed at 2am and is a zombie for school. How do I fix this?

Teens naturally shift toward later sleep times, but 2am is usually being made worse by screens and an irregular weekend schedule. The biggest levers are getting phones out of the bedroom at night, getting bright light soon after waking, and keeping his wake time within an hour or so of school days even on weekends. Shift bedtime earlier gradually, by 15 to 30 minutes every few days, rather than all at once. If he still can't fall asleep earlier despite real effort, his doctor can assess for delayed sleep phase or low mood.
screen headaches every day at work. eyes too. fix?

Try the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Position your monitor about an arm's length away with the top at or slightly below eye level, reduce glare and match screen brightness to the room. If it persists, get an eye exam, since uncorrected vision or a need for computer glasses is a very common culprit.
I'm 68 and my knees ache every morning for about 15 minutes then loosen up. Normal aging or something to worry about?

That pattern of brief morning stiffness that eases with movement is very typical of osteoarthritis, which is extremely common at your age. Staying active with low-impact exercise like walking, cycling, or swimming, plus strengthening the thigh muscles, makes a real difference for most people. Mention it to your doctor at your next visit so they can confirm it and suggest pain options that are safe alongside your other medications. Morning stiffness lasting more than an hour, or warm, swollen joints, would point toward an inflammatory arthritis and is worth a sooner appointment.
Ferret bit my son's ankle. Ferret is ours, vaccinated for rabies. What do we do?

Clean it well with soap and running water, apply antibiotic ointment and a bandage, and watch it for a few days. Since your ferret is vaccinated and healthy, rabies isn't a concern, though if it becomes ill in the next 10 days call your doctor. See a doctor if the bite is deep or shows signs of infection, and make sure your son's tetanus vaccinations are up to date.
I get stomach cramps and diarrhea after milk. Am I lactose intolerant or allergic?

Cramps, gas and diarrhea a few hours after dairy point strongly toward lactose intolerance, which is very common and not dangerous. A true milk allergy usually involves hives, swelling, wheezing or vomiting soon after eating, and that needs a doctor's evaluation. Try lactose-free milk or lactase enzyme pills with dairy and see whether your symptoms disappear. Hard cheeses and yogurt are often tolerated well too.
my 8 year old's bp was flagged high at the pediatrician. how worried should I be?

Kids' blood pressure is judged against charts for their age, sex, and height, and readings in the office often run high because of nerves, so one flag is a reason to follow up rather than panic. The pediatrician will usually recheck it on a couple more visits before calling it high. If it stays elevated, they'll look for an underlying cause, which is more common in children than adults. Keep those follow-ups and you're doing exactly the right thing.
my 4 month old has a fever of 100.6 rectal, is that bad?

At 4 months, 100.6°F rectal counts as a fever, but it's not an emergency on its own. Call your pediatrician today, because babies this age can get sick quickly and the doctor will want to know. Go in right away or head to urgent care if your baby is unusually sleepy, refusing feeds, having fewer wet diapers, breathing fast, or has a rash. If your baby were under 3 months, any temperature of 100.4°F or higher would mean calling the doctor or going to the ER immediately.
I have bad heartburn every night. 28 weeks. What actually helps?

Eating smaller meals, finishing dinner two to three hours before bed, and propping the head of your bed up a few inches can make a real difference. Calcium-based antacids like Tums are generally safe in pregnancy, but check with your midwife or pharmacist before taking anything stronger. If the pain sits under your right ribs rather than behind your breastbone, or comes with headaches or swelling, get it checked because it may not be heartburn.
my 7 year old keeps getting headaches after school. should i worry?

After-school headaches in kids are common and are often caused by dehydration, skipped lunch, tiredness or eye strain, so start by making sure they're drinking water and eating during the day. It's also worth booking an eye test, because uncorrected vision problems are a classic cause. Take them to the pediatrician soon if the headaches wake them at night or come with vomiting in the morning, clumsiness, vision changes or a change in behavior, or if they're becoming more frequent.
Doc wants me on a statin because I have diabetes but my cholesterol is normal. Kinda pointless right?

It's not pointless. Diabetes on its own significantly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke, and statins lower that risk even when cholesterol looks normal, which is why guidelines recommend them for most adults with diabetes over 40. Side effects like muscle aches happen but are usually manageable, often by switching statins or adjusting the dose. Ask your doctor about your overall risk if you want to see the numbers behind the recommendation.
teen son says his heart hurts after vaping. he's 16. overreacting?

It's worth taking seriously, especially if he gets chest pain, palpitations or breathlessness while vaping. Nicotine raises heart rate and blood pressure, and some vapes, especially illicit THC cartridges, have been linked to serious lung injury that can feel like chest pain. Get him seen soon by his doctor, and go to the ER if he has trouble breathing, faints, has a racing heart that won't settle, or has severe pain. It's also a good opening for an honest conversation about quitting, which his doctor can help with too.
16 weeks pregnant, bad cold. what can i take

Saline nasal spray, a humidifier, honey in warm water, rest and plenty of fluids are the safest first steps. Acetaminophen is fine for aches or fever at the label dose. Skip combination cold medicines unless your provider or pharmacist okays them, and avoid oral decongestants like pseudoephedrine unless they specifically clear it. Call your provider if your fever is over 100.4°F, you're short of breath, or you're getting worse after a few days, and ask about the flu shot if you haven't had it.
Is 5 hours of sleep enough if I feel fine?

For almost everyone, no. True short sleepers who thrive on five hours are extremely rare, and research shows chronically sleep-restricted people consistently underestimate how impaired they are. Long-term short sleep is linked to higher risks of weight gain, high blood pressure, weakened immunity, and mood problems. Most adults need seven to nine hours, so try adding even 30 to 60 minutes and see whether your focus and energy improve.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and I think I have the flu, fever 101.5 and aching all over. Should I just ride it out?

Don't ride this one out. Call your OB or doctor today. Flu in late pregnancy carries a higher risk of complications for you and the baby, and antiviral treatment like oseltamivir works best when it's started within the first 48 hours. Acetaminophen is the usual safe choice for the fever in the meantime. If you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or notice decreased fetal movement, go to labor and delivery or the ER right away.
Throat hurts and I'm congested, can I take Sudafed? 10 weeks

I'd hold off on Sudafed (pseudoephedrine) in the first trimester, because it's generally avoided early in pregnancy unless your doctor okays it. Try saline nasal spray, a humidifier, warm salt-water gargles, honey in tea, and sleeping propped up. Acetaminophen is fine for a sore throat or aches. Call your provider if you get a fever over 100.4°F or you're not improving after a few days.
My smartwatch says possible AFib. I feel completely fine. Ignore it?

Don't ignore it, because AFib often causes no symptoms at all, yet it raises your stroke risk and is very treatable once diagnosed. Save the watch readings and book a doctor's appointment soon so they can confirm it with a proper ECG. Go to the ER instead if you develop chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness, or stroke signs like facial droop, arm weakness or slurred speech.
my bp is 210/130 and i have a pounding headache and blurry vision

Call emergency services now. A reading that high with a severe headache and blurry vision can be a hypertensive emergency, and it needs immediate treatment. Don't drive yourself, and don't take extra medication to try to bring it down on your own. Sit or lie down and wait for help.
Is the shingles vaccine actually necessary for my 67 year old mother, she had chickenpox as a kid

Yes. Having had chickenpox is exactly why she needs it, because shingles is that same virus reactivating, and the risk climbs steeply after 50. Shingrix is two doses given two to six months apart and is over 90% effective. It also greatly lowers the risk of long-lasting nerve pain after shingles, which can be miserable in older adults. Most pharmacies give it without an appointment, and it's usually covered by Medicare Part D or insurance.
My 88-year-old father insists on still driving. He's had two small scrapes this year. How do I handle it without destroying our relationship?

Two incidents in a year is a real warning sign, so it's worth acting on, ideally by making his doctor the messenger rather than you. Ask the doctor to assess his vision, reaction time and cognition, or request a formal driving evaluation through an occupational therapist, which feels less personal than a family verdict. When you talk to him, focus on his safety and other people's rather than his age, and come with a concrete plan for how he'll still get to the places he cares about. If he is clearly unsafe and refuses, most states let doctors or family report concerns to the DMV for retesting.
Is it bad that I have a few glasses of wine every night to unwind? Everyone does it.

A few glasses every night adds up to well above what's considered low-risk drinking, and using alcohol as your main way to switch off tends to backfire. It disrupts sleep and makes anxiety worse the next day, which makes you want the wine more the next evening. Try a few alcohol-free nights a week and notice how you feel. If that turns out to be harder than you expected, it's worth taking seriously. Your doctor can help without judgment. Just don't stop suddenly if you've been drinking heavily for a long time, because withdrawal can be dangerous.
My 4 month old has a stuffy nose and is struggling to feed. What can I give her?

At four months, don't give any cold or cough medicine. Saline drops in each nostril followed by gentle suction with a bulb syringe, especially right before feeds, usually helps a lot, and a cool-mist humidifier in her room can help too. Call her pediatrician today if she's taking noticeably less than usual, has fewer wet diapers, or has any fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher. Get urgent care right away if she's breathing fast, her ribs pull in with each breath, or her lips look bluish.
I'm a line cook and burn my forearms constantly on the oven racks. Little stripes. I just ignore them. That fine?

Small, superficial stripes usually heal fine on their own, but even a quick 10 to 20 minutes under cool water right after the burn reduces pain and how deep the damage goes. Keep them clean and covered while you're working around raw food, since an open burn is an easy route for infection. Get any that blister widely, weep or look infected checked. Long gauntlet-style sleeves or oven-rack guards are cheap and save you a lot of these.
My grandma (82) is suddenly confused and agitated, her caregiver says she's fine otherwise. Should I worry?

Yes, sudden confusion in an older person is often the first sign of an infection like a UTI or pneumonia, sometimes even without fever. Get her seen today by her doctor, urgent care or the ER so they can check her urine, blood and lungs. If she's very drowsy, struggling to breathe or can't be roused properly, call emergency services.
I'm on chemo. Can I get the nasal flu vaccine since I hate needles?

Not a good idea. The nasal spray contains a weakened live virus and isn't recommended for people with weakened immune systems, including during chemo. The injected flu shot is the safe choice for you, and timing it with your treatment cycle can help it work better. Check with your oncology team about the best timing, and ask whether your household contacts should get vaccinated too.
bumped my head on a cabinet pretty hard, have a lump. fine to go to sleep tonight?

If you didn't pass out, feel basically normal and only have a goose egg with a mild headache, it's fine to sleep, and the old rule about staying awake doesn't apply. Ice the lump and use acetaminophen for the headache. Get seen urgently if you develop a worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, unusual drowsiness, slurred speech, weakness, a seizure, or one pupil larger than the other. Get checked tonight anyway if you take blood thinners or are over 65, and it's smart to have someone around who knows what happened.
Just found out I'm pregnant (about 5 weeks). Do I really need prenatal vitamins or can I just eat healthy?

Take the prenatal vitamin, because even a great diet usually doesn't deliver enough folic acid, and folic acid matters most right now while the baby's neural tube is forming. A basic over-the-counter prenatal with at least 400 mcg of folic acid is fine to start today. Keep eating well too, and bring the bottle to your first appointment so your provider can check whether you need anything extra like iron or vitamin D.
Can I alternate Tylenol and Motrin for my 4 year old's fever? Someone at daycare said to do it every 2 hours.

Every 2 hours is too often and raises the risk of a dosing mistake. Most pediatricians suggest using one medicine at the right weight-based dose, which is acetaminophen every 4 to 6 hours or ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours. Only alternate if your child's doctor specifically recommends it, and write down every dose. The goal is a comfortable kid, not a normal number on the thermometer.
Quick q, is it ok to go to the gym with a cold?

If your symptoms are all above the neck, like a runny nose or mild sore throat, light to moderate exercise is usually fine. Skip it if you have a fever, body aches, chest congestion or an upset stomach, because working out then can make you feel worse and is hard on your heart. Wipe down equipment and keep your germs to yourself, or just work out at home for a few days. Ease back in rather than going all out.
What's the fastest way to get rid of a bruise

Ice it for 15 to 20 minutes at a time during the first day or two to limit the bleeding under the skin. After that, switch to warm compresses to help clear it. Elevating it helps too, and most bruises fade within one to two weeks no matter what you do. If you bruise easily without a clear reason, or a bruise is very large, painful and swollen, see a doctor.
21F, I get chest pain when I'm anxious. how do I know it's anxiety and not my heart

At 21 with no heart history, anxiety-related chest pain is far more likely, and it usually comes with a racing heart, tingling, fast breathing and a sense of dread, then fades as you calm down. You can't fully tell the difference on your own, though, so get checked once by a doctor, who can do a quick exam and ECG for peace of mind. Pain that comes with exertion, fainting, or a family history of sudden cardiac death deserves prompt attention, and learning slow breathing or getting anxiety treatment can really cut down these episodes.
I'm vegan, do I really need B12 or is that a myth from meat people

It's not a myth. B12 is made by bacteria, and plant foods don't provide a reliable amount, so vegans need a supplement or fortified foods. A deficiency can cause anemia and nerve damage that may become permanent if it goes on long enough. A simple cyanocobalamin supplement of about 50 to 100 mcg daily, or 2,000 mcg weekly, covers it cheaply.
Can I take ibuprofen for a bad headache? 22 weeks

It's best to skip ibuprofen and other NSAIDs during pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks on, because they can affect the baby's kidneys and amniotic fluid levels. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) at the label dose is the usual go-to, along with water, food, rest and a dark quiet room. If the headache is severe, won't go away, or comes with vision changes, swelling in your face or hands, or pain under your ribs, call your provider right away, since those can be signs of preeclampsia.
Doc said I had myocarditis after a virus. It's been 6 weeks and I feel fine. Can I start running?

Don't start running until your cardiologist specifically clears you, even though you feel fine. With myocarditis, the usual advice is to avoid strenuous exercise for around three to six months. Return to activity is normally based on tests like an ECG, an echo, and sometimes a monitor. Exercising too early can trigger dangerous heart rhythms, so getting that follow-up is the key step right now.
Rash on one side of my chest, band shaped, burning pain started a couple days before it. 58 years old.

A painful, band-shaped rash on one side, especially with burning pain beforehand, sounds very much like shingles. See a doctor within the next day or so, because antiviral medication works best when started within about 72 hours of the rash appearing. Early treatment also lowers the risk of lingering nerve pain. Keep the rash covered and stay away from pregnant people, newborns and anyone with a weakened immune system until it crusts over, and ask about the shingles vaccine once you've recovered.
I'm pregnant (9 weeks) and my mom says I should take extra vitamin A for the baby's eyes. Should I?

Please don't take extra vitamin A. High doses of preformed vitamin A (retinol) during pregnancy can cause birth defects, especially in the first trimester. Your prenatal vitamin already contains a safe amount, and many prenatals use beta-carotene for it, which is the safer form. For the same reason, avoid liver and liver-based supplements, and check with your OB before adding anything else.
Back is killing me. Can I take 6 Advil at once to knock it out?

That's 1,200 mg in one shot, and the OTC limit is 400 mg per dose and 1,200 mg per day without a doctor's guidance. Megadoses don't add much pain relief but do raise the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney injury. Stick to 2 tablets every 6 to 8 hours, and consider adding acetaminophen plus heat and gentle movement. If the pain is severe, spreading down a leg, or comes with numbness or bladder problems, see a doctor.
Q-tips deep in the ear every day after shower, any harm?

Yes, that habit usually backfires. Cotton swabs push wax deeper and pack it against the eardrum, and they can scratch the canal or even puncture the drum. Your ears clean themselves, so just wipe the outer ear with a washcloth. If you feel blocked, use softening drops instead of digging.
I've had an earache for 2 days with some yellow stuff draining out. Can I just put some hydrogen peroxide in it?

Hold off on the peroxide, because drainage with ear pain can mean a perforated eardrum, and putting liquids through a hole can irritate the middle ear and worsen things. Leave the ear dry and lightly plug the outer opening with cotton when showering. See a doctor in the next day or so to find out whether it's an outer or middle ear infection, since they're treated with different drops or antibiotics.
is it safe to give my dog the same fish oil i take

Often yes, but the dose has to be scaled to your dog's weight, and human capsules sometimes contain added flavorings or vitamin D that can cause problems. Never use anything with xylitol, which is toxic to dogs. Check with your vet for the right dose, especially if your dog is on other medications or has a surgery coming up, since fish oil can affect bleeding.
I get migraines about twice a month. Is it okay to take ibuprofen every day as prevention so they don't start?

Daily ibuprofen isn't a good prevention strategy. Taking pain relievers on more than about 10 to 15 days a month can cause medication-overuse headaches, and long-term NSAID use carries real risks to your stomach and kidneys. Keep ibuprofen for treating attacks early, and ask your doctor about proper preventive options if two a month is disrupting your life.
sharp pain in my upper right belly after eating fried food, goes away after a few hours. happened 3 times now

That pattern strongly suggests gallstones, which often cause pain after fatty meals. Book a doctor's appointment, because a simple ultrasound can confirm it, and cutting back on fried and fatty foods may help in the meantime. Go to the ER if the pain lasts more than a few hours or if you develop fever, chills or yellowing of your skin or eyes, since those can mean an infection or blockage.
my reading is 88/55 and i feel kind of woozy. i'm 26 and healthy otherwise

Low readings like that can be normal for some healthy young people, but feeling woozy means you should take it seriously. Sit or lie down, drink some water, and eat something if you haven't. If it keeps happening, check in with a doctor to look into dehydration, anemia, or medication effects. Get urgent care if you faint, have chest pain, or feel confused.
lol how fast can I lose the weight I put on being sick in bed for 2 weeks

Some of that gain is probably water and normal fluctuation, and it often settles once you're moving again. Don't try to crash diet or do punishing workouts right after being sick. That combination can slow your recovery and leave you run down. Get back to your normal eating and gradually rebuild your activity over two to three weeks, and most of it should come off on its own.
my friend says a raw egg shake every morning is the best protein source. thoughts?

Raw eggs carry a small but real risk of salmonella, and cooking them actually makes the protein more digestible. If you like the shake idea, use pasteurized eggs, which you can find in cartons, or blend in Greek yogurt, milk or a protein powder instead. Cooked eggs are still a great protein source.
Is it safe to use my steroid inhaler while pregnant? I'm scared it'll hurt the baby

Yes, inhaled steroids like budesonide are considered safe in pregnancy and are widely used. The real danger to the baby is poorly controlled asthma, because that lowers the oxygen getting to them. Don't stop your inhaler. Let your OB and your asthma doctor know you're pregnant so they can coordinate and adjust if needed.
Worried. My back pain has been getting slowly worse for 2 months, it's worse at night and I've lost weight without trying. 58M.

Book a GP appointment this week and tell them exactly those three things. Back pain that steadily worsens, is worse at night, and comes with unexplained weight loss needs blood tests and possibly imaging to rule out serious causes like infection or cancer. Most of the time it turns out to be something else, but this combination shouldn't wait. If you develop fever, leg weakness or bladder problems, go to emergency care.
can i pop a big cystic pimple with a needle if i sterilize it first

I'd skip it, because cystic pimples sit deep under the skin and poking them with a needle usually pushes the inflammation deeper, which raises your odds of infection and a permanent pitted scar. A warm compress for 10 to 15 minutes a few times a day can help it settle, and a hydrocolloid patch keeps you from picking at it. If you get these regularly or one is very painful, a dermatologist can inject it with a tiny dose of steroid and it will often flatten within a day or two. Recurring cysts also respond well to prescription treatment, so they're worth bringing up even if this one clears on its own.
Coughing so hard I threw up a couple times and there's a whoop sound when I breathe in after. Adult, 40s.

That pattern of violent coughing fits, vomiting and a whooping sound when you breathe in is classic for whooping cough (pertussis), and adults can definitely get it. See a doctor soon, since it's diagnosed with a swab and treated with antibiotics, which also stop you from spreading it. Stay away from babies, pregnant people and anyone unvaccinated until you've been evaluated, because pertussis can be deadly for infants. Get emergency care if you have trouble catching your breath after coughing fits or turn bluish.
My dog bit my hand by accident, it's my own dog and vaccinated. Punctures but small. Fine to just bandage?

Clean it very well first. Wash it under running water with soap for several minutes, then bandage it. Even small punctures from dog bites get infected often, especially on the hands, so it's worth calling a doctor today. Many recommend preventive antibiotics for hand bites, and you may need a tetanus booster. Get seen promptly if it turns red, swollen, warm or more painful.
My heart randomly skips a beat or does a little flip-flop maybe a few times a day. I'm 29, otherwise healthy. Should I be freaking out?

No need to freak out. Occasional skipped or extra beats (usually PACs or PVCs) are very common in healthy young people and often get worse with caffeine, alcohol, stress and poor sleep. Mention it to your doctor at your next visit, since a simple ECG is reassuring. Get seen sooner if the flutters come with fainting, chest pain or breathlessness, last for minutes at a time, or if a family member died suddenly at a young age.
Baby hasn't moved much today, 32 weeks. Probably just sleeping, should I check tomorrow?

Don't wait until tomorrow. Lie on your left side, have a cold drink or snack, and count movements; you should feel about 10 in two hours. If you don't, or if your instinct says something is off, call labor and delivery now. Reduced movement is something they genuinely want you to come in for, and checking is quick.
I'm 68 and since my husband died last year I can't get interested in anything. My daughter says I should 'move on.' Is something wrong with me?

I'm sorry about your husband. Grief has no deadline, and a year is not long after a lifetime together. When grief comes with a lasting loss of interest in everything, though, it can turn into depression, which is common and treatable at any age. Tell your doctor how you've been feeling, and ask about bereavement support groups, which many people find comforting. You don't need to 'move on,' but you deserve to feel some light again.
I have a blister about the size of a grape on my forearm from a steam burn. Should I pop it so it heals faster?

Leave it intact, because that blister is a sterile, built-in dressing that protects the raw skin underneath from infection. Cover it loosely with a non-stick dressing so it doesn't get rubbed or burst. If it pops on its own, gently wash it, leave the skin flap in place, and cover it again. See a doctor if it gets increasingly red, hot, swollen or starts oozing pus.
fever 100.8 and I'm 34 weeks pregnant, can I just ride it out

Call your OB or labor and delivery today instead of riding it out. A fever in late pregnancy can point to infections that need treatment, and a high fever isn't good for the baby. Acetaminophen is generally considered safe during pregnancy to bring it down, but avoid ibuprofen in the third trimester.
I'm a line cook and burn my forearms constantly on the oven racks. Small stripes. Just keep working?

Small oven-rack stripes are usually minor, but give each one 20 minutes of cool running water when you can, or at least a few minutes before you go back to the line. Cover fresh ones with a breathable dressing during service, since kitchen grease and heat make them prone to infection. It's worth getting proper oven sleeves or long gauntlets too. See a doctor if any burn blisters widely, oozes or gets angry and red.
My boyfriend said he wants to kill himself if I leave him. I don't know what to do.

That's a frightening and heavy thing to be handed, and you are not responsible for keeping him alive by staying in a relationship. Take the statement seriously. If he seems to be in immediate danger, call emergency services. You can also tell him clearly that you care about his safety and that he needs to call a crisis line, which is 988 in the US. If this is being used to keep you from leaving, that's a form of control, and talking it through with someone you trust or a domestic abuse helpline can help you plan how to leave safely. You deserve support too.
what's a good way to ease back into running after being sick for two weeks?

A good approach is to start with run-walk intervals, like jogging two minutes and walking one, for 20 minutes total at an easy pace. If you feel fine the next day, gradually increase the running parts and total time over a week or two, keeping effort easy enough to talk. Don't try to make up lost mileage, and expect your fitness to come back faster than it took to build. If you feel unusually wiped out afterward, back off for a day or two.
how many mg of caffeine is too much if i'm also taking a decongestant

For most healthy adults the general caffeine limit is about 400 mg a day, roughly four cups of brewed coffee. With a decongestant like pseudoephedrine, aim for half that or less, because both raise heart rate and blood pressure and together can cause palpitations, shakiness and insomnia. Skip the decongestant altogether if you have high blood pressure or heart problems.
I have a tooth abscess and dentist can't see me for 2 weeks. Can I get antibiotics somewhere?

Yes, a primary care doctor or urgent care can often prescribe antibiotics to control the infection until your dental visit. Antibiotics alone won't fix it, though, because the tooth still needs drainage, a root canal or an extraction. Call your dentist and say you have an abscess, since many hold emergency slots. Go to the ER right away if facial swelling spreads, or if you have trouble swallowing or breathing.
Just tell me how much aspirin to take for chest pain so I don't have to go to the ER. I hate hospitals.

Aspirin isn't a substitute for the ER. It only slightly improves the odds during a heart attack while you're getting real treatment, and it does nothing for many other dangerous causes of chest pain. If this pain is new, pressure-like, or comes with sweating, nausea, breathlessness or pain spreading to your arm or jaw, call emergency services now. The standard dose while waiting is one 325 mg tablet, chewed, if you're not allergic and don't have a bleeding problem. Treating a heart attack quickly is what saves heart muscle, so going in is worth it even if you hate hospitals.
My husband uses nitroglycerin for chest pain and wants to try his buddy's Viagra. Is that dangerous?

Yes, this is one of the truly dangerous combinations. Sildenafil plus any nitrate can drop blood pressure severely enough to cause fainting, heart attack or death. He shouldn't take it at all, and certainly not someone else's pills. His cardiologist can talk through erectile dysfunction options that are safe for his heart.
Is it dangerous to ignore a toothache that comes and goes? I'm busy.

Pain that comes and goes is often a cavity or a crack that's getting closer to the nerve, and these problems don't heal on their own. Catching it now usually means a filling, while waiting can mean a root canal, an extraction, or an infection that hits at the worst possible time. Fit in a dental appointment in the next week or two, and go sooner if the pain becomes constant, wakes you up, or comes with swelling.
I fall asleep in meetings and while watching TV no matter how much I sleep. Like 9 hours. Just lazy?

That's very unlikely to be laziness. Falling asleep despite 9 hours in bed points to something like sleep apnea, narcolepsy, a medication side effect, depression, anemia or a thyroid problem. See your doctor and describe exactly how often it happens, and ask about a sleep study. Until you know what's going on, be very cautious about driving, especially when you feel drowsy.
my dentist wants to do xrays and a filling, should i postpone til after baby

No need to postpone, because dental care is safe during pregnancy and untreated cavities or gum infections are worth dealing with. Dental X-rays use a tiny dose, and your belly and thyroid are covered with a lead apron. Local anesthetics like lidocaine are routinely used in pregnant patients. The second trimester is often the most comfortable time for longer procedures, so let your dentist know how far along you are.
tired of driving mom to every appointment, can i just get her prescriptions refilled online without her seeing the doctor

For stable long-term meds, you can absolutely cut the trips. Ask her doctor for 90-day prescriptions with refills, set up mail-order or auto-refill through her pharmacy, and request telehealth visits for routine check-ins. What you shouldn't skip entirely are the visits where they check blood pressure, labs or kidney function, since dosing for many drugs depends on those results. Many areas also offer senior transportation services or Medicare Advantage ride benefits, which can take some of the driving off you.
my 7 yr old keeps getting headaches after school. normal?

Headaches in school-age kids are fairly common and often come from skipped lunch, not drinking enough water, poor sleep, too much screen time or uncorrected vision problems. Start with the easy fixes, like a water bottle at school, a solid lunch and an after-school snack, and get an eye exam if your child hasn't had one recently. See the pediatrician if the headaches are getting more frequent, wake your child at night, come with vomiting in the morning, or come with changes in balance, vision or behavior.
My father is 84 and diabetic. He had a sugar of 52 this morning and was shaky. He's fine now after juice. Do I need to do anything else?

Yes, call his doctor today. A low of 52 means his insulin or diabetes pills, especially sulfonylureas like glipizide, may be too strong for him now. Lows are particularly dangerous in older adults because they can cause falls and confusion. Make sure he eats a meal with some protein soon, and keep checking his sugar more often until his doctor adjusts things. If he ever becomes confused or unresponsive, call 911.
I'm 67 and never had a pneumonia vaccine. Is it too late?

Not at all; the pneumococcal vaccine is recommended for everyone 65 and older, and this age group benefits the most. Most adults now get a single dose of PCV20 or PCV21, or PCV15 followed by PPSV23 about a year later. Your pharmacist or doctor can give it during a routine visit, and many pharmacies offer it without an appointment. Since you're getting caught up anyway, it's a good time to ask whether you're due for shingles, RSV, flu or COVID shots too.
My 2 year old has had a fever of 104 for three days and keeps pulling at her ear. Should I wait it out?

Three days of a high fever in a toddler is your cue to get her seen today rather than keep waiting. Ear-pulling with fever often means an ear infection, and at her age a doctor needs to look in the ear to decide whether she needs antibiotics. Meanwhile, give a weight-appropriate dose of acetaminophen or ibuprofen and keep her drinking. Go to urgent care or the ER right away if she seems unusually drowsy, has a stiff neck, or isn't making wet diapers.
wheezing and short of breath with this chest cold. I have an old inhaler from my son, can I use it?

Don't use someone else's inhaler. It may not be the right medication for you, it could be expired, and it would only cover up a problem that needs a proper diagnosis. Wheezing and shortness of breath with a chest infection can mean bronchospasm or pneumonia, so see a doctor today. If you can't speak full sentences, your lips look bluish, or the breathlessness is getting worse, call emergency services.
my 15 year old is constantly sad and stays in his room, says he's just tired. normal teen stuff?

Some withdrawal is normal for teens, but lasting sadness, pulling away and constant tiredness for more than two weeks can be signs of depression. Pick a calm moment, tell him what you've noticed and ask him directly how he's doing, including whether he's had thoughts of hurting himself. Asking doesn't put the idea in his head. Book a visit with his doctor or a counselor. If he ever talks about suicide, call or text 988 or go to the ER.
whiskey on the tooth to numb it, yes or no

Mostly no. It might numb things briefly, but it irritates the gums and does nothing about the cause, and drinking it on top of painkillers like acetaminophen is a bad combination. A cold compress on the cheek, ibuprofen with acetaminophen, and a dab of clove oil will do a lot more. Then get the tooth looked at.
Deep cut, I can see something yellowish and fatty in there. It stopped bleeding. Can I just butterfly it?

Visible fat means the cut went through the full thickness of the skin, so it needs proper closure rather than butterfly strips. Get to urgent care soon, ideally within a few hours, since wounds closed early heal better and get infected less often. Cover it with a clean damp dressing on the way.
napping good or bad

Napping is good if you keep it short and early. A 10- to 20-minute nap before about 3pm boosts alertness without leaving you groggy or wrecking your night's sleep. Longer or late-afternoon naps can make it harder to fall asleep at bedtime, so skip them if you have insomnia. If you find you badly need naps every day despite sleeping enough at night, mention it to your doctor.
I have a cold, 18 weeks pregnant. What can I take? DayQuil?

Avoid DayQuil, because it contains phenylephrine, a decongestant generally discouraged in pregnancy. Plain acetaminophen for aches, saline nasal spray, a humidifier, honey for a cough and plenty of fluids are all safe choices. Call your provider if you get a fever over 100.4°F, have trouble breathing, or aren't improving after about a week.
is aspirin fine for my 12 year old's fever? it's all we have

Don't give aspirin to anyone under 18 with a fever or viral illness. It's linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare but potentially fatal condition that affects the liver and brain. Use children's or junior-strength acetaminophen or ibuprofen dosed for their weight instead. If you can't get any tonight, fluids and light clothing will keep them comfortable until you can.
My teen has a fever and a rash of tiny purple dots that don't fade when I press a glass on them

Go to the ER right now or call 911. A fever with a rash that doesn't fade under pressure can be a sign of meningococcal infection or sepsis, and these get worse within hours. Don't wait for other symptoms to appear. Getting treatment fast makes a huge difference.
can i stop my bp meds now that my readings are normal? been on them a year

Normal readings usually mean the medication is working, not that you no longer need it. Stopping suddenly can let your pressure rebound, and with some drugs, like beta-blockers or clonidine, it can spike dangerously. If you've also lost weight or changed your lifestyle a lot, it's worth asking your doctor whether a supervised taper makes sense.
My 6 year old is crying about a toothache at bedtime. What can I give her tonight?

Children's ibuprofen or acetaminophen dosed for her weight is the best option tonight, and ibuprofen is especially good for tooth pain. Have her rinse with warm water and gently floss around the sore tooth in case food is stuck there. Skip benzocaine gels for young kids unless your pharmacist or dentist okays them. Call her dentist tomorrow, and seek care sooner if she develops facial swelling or a fever.
Teen here, type 1. My friends are going to a party. How do I not end up in trouble with my sugar?

Go and have fun, just plan ahead: eat a real meal beforehand, carry glucose tabs, and keep your phone charged so you can see your CGM or meter. Tell at least one friend you trust that you're diabetic and what a low looks like, because lows can be mistaken for being drunk. Dancing and alcohol both drop blood sugar, sometimes hours later, so check before bed and have a snack if you're on the low side. If you drink, keep it light and never on an empty stomach.
How many ibuprofen can I take at once for a really bad migraine? 400mg isn't touching it.

For most healthy adults, 400mg is the standard over-the-counter dose, and stacking more pills won't help much while it raises the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain. You'll usually get more relief by taking it early in the attack, with food and a big glass of water, and some people do better with a combination like acetaminophen, aspirin and caffeine. If over-the-counter doses regularly aren't enough, see your doctor about migraine-specific medicines like triptans, which work far better for many people.
feeling chest discomfort after cocaine last night, it's mostly gone now

Cocaine can cause heart attacks, artery spasm and dangerous rhythms even in young healthy people, sometimes hours later, so get checked at an ER today even though it's easing. Be honest with the staff about the cocaine, because it changes which treatments are safe. Go immediately or call emergency services if the pain returns or comes with breathlessness, sweating or a racing heart.
got a fishhook stuck in my thumb, barb is in. gonna just yank it

Don't yank a barbed hook, because the barb will tear tissue on the way out. If it's shallow and not near a joint or tendon, you can push it through, snip off the barb with cutters, and back the rest out, then wash it well. If it's deep, you're unsure, or you can't do it cleanly, have urgent care remove it. Check that your tetanus shot is current either way.
My mother-in-law (88) refuses to use her walker because it 'makes her look old.' How do I get through to her?

Arguing about appearances rarely works. Framing the walker around what she cares about usually lands better, such as staying in her own home, keeping her independence, or not ending up in the hospital with a broken hip. Sometimes a physical therapist can fit her with a sleeker rollator or a cane she likes more, and advice from a professional often carries more weight than family nagging. Ask her doctor to make the point at her next visit too.
what do I do about a boil on my thigh, can I pop it with a needle

Don't pop it yourself. Squeezing or lancing at home can push the infection deeper. Put a warm, damp compress on it for 10 to 15 minutes several times a day, and many boils will drain on their own within a week. Cover it if it opens and wash your hands after touching it. See a doctor if it's larger than about half an inch, very painful, spreading, comes with a fever, or keeps coming back. Those may need proper drainage or antibiotics.
I've had migraines for years but this one has numbness spreading down my arm that's not normal for me

Treat this as an emergency and call for help now. Numbness that's new or different from your usual aura needs urgent assessment to rule out a stroke, even if you have a long history of migraines. Tell the paramedics exactly how this one differs from your typical attacks.
My friend texted me tonight saying she's going to kill herself and saying goodbye. She's not answering now.

Treat this as an emergency and call emergency services now with her address, because a goodbye message and silence is serious. If you can't reach anyone, contact someone who lives with her or near her and get them to check on her. Don't try to handle this alone or wait to see if she replies. Once help is on the way, look after yourself too, because this is frightening.
can i give my 9 month old honey for his cough

No, hold off on honey until he's past his first birthday, because it can carry botulism spores that a baby's gut can't handle yet. For now, saline drops and gentle suction for a stuffy nose will help, along with a cool-mist humidifier and plenty of breast milk or formula. Most infant coughs from colds clear up within a week or two. Call his doctor if he's breathing fast, wheezing, pulling in at the ribs or not feeding well.
Is it ok to use my rescue inhaler like 4 times a day? It works.

It's good that it works, but needing it that often is a sign your asthma isn't well controlled, since most people should need it two days a week or less. Leaning on rescue puffs alone leaves the underlying inflammation untreated and raises your risk of a serious attack. See your doctor soon about a daily controller inhaler, which usually contains a steroid, or a combination option. Get urgent care if the puffs stop lasting or stop helping.
Quick one: does coffee raise blood pressure?

Yes, caffeine can raise blood pressure for a few hours, especially if you don't drink it often. Regular drinkers build up some tolerance, so the effect usually shrinks. For an accurate reading, wait at least 30 minutes after coffee before measuring, and if your blood pressure is already high, cutting back is a reasonable experiment.
can you take sertraline and st john's wort together? trying to boost my mood more naturally

Don't combine them. St John's wort and sertraline both raise serotonin, and together they can cause serotonin syndrome, which brings agitation, a racing heart, sweating and muscle twitching and can be serious. If you feel your sertraline isn't doing enough, bring it up with your prescriber, since a dose change or a different medication might be the answer. Exercise, sunlight and good sleep are safe natural boosts to add alongside it.
whats the fastest way to get rid of a cold, i have a job interview in 2 days

There's no way to actually cure a cold faster, but you can make yourself feel and look a lot better in two days. Prioritize sleep, keep drinking fluids, and use saline spray or a decongestant to clear your nose. Throat lozenges and a dose of ibuprofen or acetaminophen before the interview will help with soreness and that foggy feeling. Some evidence suggests zinc lozenges started early may shave a little time off, but they're not a miracle.
Does weed help with sleep? Thinking of using it nightly

It can make you drowsy at first, but nightly use often backfires. Tolerance builds, it suppresses REM sleep, and stopping can cause rebound insomnia and vivid dreams that make people feel they can't sleep without it. It also isn't well studied as a sleep treatment. For ongoing sleep trouble, CBT for insomnia has much better evidence, and a doctor can help figure out what's keeping you awake.
legs feel creepy crawly at night and i have to move them, cant sleep

That sounds like restless legs syndrome, which is common and treatable. Low iron is a frequent driver, so ask your doctor to check your ferritin level. Supplementing when it's low can make a big difference, but don't start iron on your own without testing. Caffeine, alcohol, nicotine and some antihistamines and antidepressants can make it worse. Walking, stretching, or a warm bath in the evening often eases symptoms.
red patch on white of eye appeared overnight, doesn't hurt, looks scary

That's most likely a subconjunctival hemorrhage, a small burst blood vessel that often happens after coughing, straining, or even for no reason. It looks dramatic but is usually harmless and fades over one to two weeks, like a bruise. See a doctor if it comes with pain, vision changes, or an injury, or if it keeps happening. You should also see one if you take blood thinners or have high blood pressure.
I've stopped my antidepressant cold turkey 3 days ago and feel dizzy with weird brain zaps

That sounds like discontinuation syndrome, which is unpleasant but common when antidepressants are stopped suddenly. Contact your prescriber today, because they'll usually suggest restarting and then tapering slowly over weeks, which prevents most of these symptoms. Avoid driving while you're dizzy. If your mood drops sharply or you have thoughts of harming yourself, seek help urgently.
can i drink baking soda water for heartburn

Half a teaspoon of baking soda dissolved in a glass of water will neutralize acid in a pinch, so it's okay as an occasional fix. It's very high in sodium, though, so skip it if you have high blood pressure, heart or kidney issues, or you're pregnant. Never take it on an overly full stomach, and don't make it a regular habit. If you need it often, a proper antacid or a chat with your doctor is the better route.
I'm diabetic and I've had a gum abscess for 2 days. Can I treat it with salt water rinses?

Salt water rinses are fine for comfort, but with diabetes you shouldn't count on them for an abscess, because infections can spread faster and heal more slowly. Get to a dentist within a day, or go to urgent care if you can't get in, so it can be drained and you can be assessed for antibiotics. Watch your blood sugar too, since infection often pushes it up, and head to the ER if you get a fever or spreading swelling.
my dogs were fighting and one bit me when I broke it up, puncture on my forearm, deep. I'm on chemo.

Being on chemo means your immune system can't fight off a bite infection well, so contact your oncology team or go to urgent care today rather than waiting. Wash the puncture thoroughly with soap and running water and cover it with a clean dressing in the meantime. You'll very likely need preventive antibiotics, and any fever should be treated as an emergency.
My toddler's lips swelled up a bit after trying kiwi. Gone now after an hour. Is that a big deal?

It's worth taking seriously even though it resolved. Lip swelling after a food suggests a true allergy, and the next reaction could be stronger. Keep kiwi out of her diet and see her pediatrician soon for an allergist referral, as they may prescribe an epinephrine auto-injector. If she ever has trouble breathing, repeated vomiting or becomes floppy after eating something, call 911 immediately.
Kid fell on gravel, knees all scraped with little stones stuck in. Bleeding not bad. Do I really need to get every bit out?

Yes, it's worth getting the grit out. Embedded gravel raises the infection risk and can leave permanent dark marks in the skin, known as traumatic tattooing. Rinse the knees under lots of running water, and use clean tweezers or gently wipe with gauze for anything that's left. If pieces are deeply embedded or it's too painful for your child to tolerate, a nurse or urgent care can clean it properly with numbing.
Is it safe to buy antibiotics online from overseas sites without a prescription? Way cheaper.

It's risky and I'd avoid it. Pills from unregulated sites are often counterfeit, wrong-dose or contaminated, and self-choosing an antibiotic means you may take the wrong drug for your infection. If cost is the issue, many common antibiotics cost just a few dollars as generics, and discount programs like GoodRx or a community health clinic can get you a legitimate prescription and cheap pills.
I'm 45, smoker, my chest gets tight walking uphill and goes away when I stop. Been a month. Can I wait till my annual physical in 3 months?

Three months is too long to wait. Chest tightness that comes with exertion and goes with rest is the textbook picture of angina, a sign your heart isn't getting enough blood, and smoking raises that risk substantially. Book an appointment within the next few days and say exactly what you told me. Call emergency services if the tightness starts at rest, lasts more than a few minutes, or gets noticeably worse.
got hit in the chest with a baseball at practice, my son is 12, he seems okay but his chest hurts

Most chest bruises from a ball heal fine with rest and ice, but keep him out of practice for today and watch him closely. Get him to the ER right away if he has trouble breathing, faints, has a racing or irregular heartbeat, gets dizzy or pale, or the pain gets worse instead of better. If he collapsed even briefly when hit, that needs emergency evaluation now, because a hard blow to the chest can occasionally disrupt the heart's rhythm.
Is it safe to use apple cider vinegar straight on a mole to remove it? Saw it on TikTok

That's a bad idea, because undiluted vinegar can cause chemical burns and scarring, and destroying a mole at home means nobody can check whether it was harmless. A dermatologist can remove a mole quickly and send it for testing if needed, usually with a much better cosmetic result. If the mole is changing, bleeding, or itchy, that's even more reason to have it looked at first.
I've been waking up with headaches and my wife says I snore really loudly and stop breathing sometimes

That sounds a lot like sleep apnea, a common cause of morning headaches, and it raises your risk of high blood pressure and heart problems if it isn't treated. Ask your doctor about a sleep study, which can often be done at home now. Treatment like CPAP usually clears up the headaches and leaves you far less tired.
is neosporin necessary or just vaseline fine for scrapes

Plain petroleum jelly is fine for most everyday scrapes and cuts, because what matters most is keeping the wound clean and moist. Antibiotic ointments don't add much for clean minor wounds. Some people also develop skin allergies to neomycin, one of the ingredients in Neosporin. Wash the scrape first, apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly, and cover it until it heals. Save a doctor visit for wounds that look infected or were especially dirty.
My father in law (90) refuses to use his walker. Keeps furniture-walking around the house. Should I just take it as his choice?

Respect his say, but don't drop it. Furniture-walking is a classic setup for a serious fall, and at 90 a broken hip can change everything. Ask his doctor for a physical therapy referral. A therapist can fit the walker properly, show him how to use it, and may suggest a lighter or different model he actually likes. Meanwhile, clear walkways, secure rugs, and add lighting so the house is safer either way.
I'm 7 months pregnant and have a horrible toothache. Is it even safe to see a dentist right now?

Yes, dental care is safe during pregnancy, and leaving a tooth infection untreated is riskier for you and the baby than getting it treated. Tell the dentist how far along you are so they can position you comfortably and pick suitable medications. Local anesthetic and shielded X-rays are considered fine. For pain in the meantime, acetaminophen is generally the go-to, but avoid ibuprofen in the third trimester unless your doctor says otherwise.
Is there a natural supplement for preventing migraines that's legit?

A few have real evidence. Magnesium (often 400 to 600 mg a day), riboflavin (vitamin B2, 400 mg a day) and coenzyme Q10 can reduce migraine frequency for some people, though they usually take two to three months to show an effect. Magnesium can cause loose stools and isn't for people with kidney disease, so check with your doctor first, especially if you're pregnant or take other medications. Avoid butterbur products unless they're certified free of PA compounds, which can damage the liver.
Can I get the flu shot and Tdap while pregnant or should I wait till after?

Get them during pregnancy; both are recommended and safe. The flu shot can be given in any trimester, and Tdap is given between 27 and 36 weeks. The antibodies you make pass to your baby and help protect them from flu and whooping cough during the first months of life, before they can be vaccinated themselves. Ask about the RSV vaccine too, which is offered late in pregnancy during RSV season.
how long after strep throat can i swim

You're generally not contagious after about 24 hours on antibiotics. Once your fever is gone and you feel reasonably normal, easy swimming is fine. Start with a lighter session than usual, because your stamina may lag for a few days. Make sure to finish the full course of antibiotics, even if you're back in the pool.
Headache, fever, stiff neck and the light hurts my eyes. Been about 6 hours.

That combination can be meningitis, which needs emergency care right away. Go to the ER now or call 911, especially if you also have a rash, confusion or vomiting. Don't wait to see whether it improves.
Had a bad reaction to my first Shingrix shot, felt awful for 2 days. Do I really need the second?

Yes, get the second dose, because one dose gives noticeably weaker and shorter protection than the full series. Feeling flattened for a day or two is common with Shingrix and isn't a reason to skip it unless you had a true allergic reaction like hives, facial swelling, or trouble breathing. Plan the second shot before a quiet day off, and stay hydrated. Shingles and the nerve pain that can follow it are far worse than two bad days.
should I take my iron pill with my thyroid med to save time?

Better to separate them. Iron binds to levothyroxine and can block a big chunk of it from being absorbed, so your thyroid levels may drift off target. Take the levothyroxine on an empty stomach first thing in the morning, and leave about four hours before the iron. Calcium and antacids need the same spacing.
35yo, just did a bunch of coke and my chest really hurts and heart is going fast. dont want cops involved

Chest pain after cocaine can be a real heart attack even at 35, so call emergency services now. Paramedics are there to treat you, not to arrest you, and in many places the law protects people who call for an overdose. Tell them about the cocaine, because it changes which drugs are safe to give you, including avoiding certain beta blockers. Don't take anything else, and stay with someone until help arrives.
is it ok to drink a couple beers while on amoxicillin

A couple of beers won't interact dangerously with amoxicillin, which is not one of the antibiotics that reacts badly with alcohol. Your body is still fighting an infection, so keep it moderate and stay hydrated. Just make sure you don't skip or delay doses because you've been drinking. If you're ever put on metronidazole or tinidazole instead, avoid alcohol completely, because that combination can make you violently ill.
i self harm sometimes but its under control. dont tell me to see a doctor

Thanks for trusting me with that, and I'm not going to lecture you. Self-harm usually means you're carrying something heavy, and you deserve support that doesn't involve hurting yourself, even if it feels manageable right now. When the urge hits, some people find holding ice, snapping a hair tie or doing intense exercise takes the edge off. Keep proper wound care in mind, and get urgent help if a wound is deep or won't stop bleeding. If things ever feel less in control, texting a crisis line like 988 in the US is an option that doesn't involve a doctor's office.
What's the actual difference between a cold and allergies? I've had a runny nose for 3 weeks.

Three weeks points toward allergies, since colds usually clear up in 7 to 10 days. Allergies typically cause itchy eyes and nose, clear watery mucus, sneezing fits and no fever, and they often flare with seasons or certain places. Colds bring body aches, a sore throat and sometimes a low fever. Try a non-drowsy antihistamine or a steroid nasal spray for a week. If it doesn't improve, or you get facial pain and thick discolored mucus, see a doctor to check for a sinus infection.
Is coughing hard during a heart attack a real thing? Saw it on facebook.

No, "cough CPR" is a myth that's been circulating for years, and heart organizations specifically advise against it for people having a heart attack. It wastes precious time and has no proven benefit. The right move is to call emergency services immediately and chew an aspirin if you're not allergic and it's safe for you. Then rest while you wait for help.
Can I use retinol serum while pregnant? It's just skincare.

Stop the retinol, because vitamin A derivatives are advised against in pregnancy, as oral versions are known to cause birth defects. Absorption through the skin is low, so don't worry about what you've already used. Azelaic acid, vitamin C and niacinamide are generally considered good pregnancy-safe swaps.
my bp med makes me cough nonstop, can i just quit it

That dry cough is a well-known side effect of ACE inhibitors like lisinopril or enalapril, so you're not imagining it. Don't just quit, though. Call your doctor and ask about switching, because an ARB like losartan works similarly and rarely causes cough. The cough can take a few weeks to fade after the switch.
Asthma flare plus a chest infection, finished steroids yesterday. Back to CrossFit Monday?

That's probably too soon for full CrossFit, since your airways are still settling after a flare and a chest infection. Start with lighter, steady sessions and scale down the high-intensity parts for the first week or two, keeping your reliever inhaler with you every time. If you need your reliever more than usual or your breathing feels tight, stop and check in with your doctor. If you're not sure your asthma is back under control, a quick review before you return is a good idea.
Is it okay to use adult Tylenol and just cut the pill for my 6 year old? We ran out of the kids one.

It's better not to, because cutting adult tablets makes it easy to get the dose wrong, and acetaminophen overdose can seriously damage the liver. A 6-year-old's dose depends on their weight, and a regular 325 mg adult tablet is often more than a younger or smaller child should take at once. Ask a pharmacist, who can tell you exactly what's safe from what you have, or pick up children's chewables or liquid instead.
how long does a 3 yr old need to be fever free before going back to daycare

The standard rule is 24 hours without a fever and without any fever-reducing medicine. Giving Tylenol in the morning to get the fever down doesn't count. Most daycares also want your child eating and acting close to normal. Check your center's policy too, since some have stricter rules for things like vomiting or pink eye.
My dad (80) has had a cold for a week and today he's confused and breathing fast. Is this just because he's tired?

Don't assume that. New confusion plus fast breathing in an 80-year-old after a respiratory infection can mean pneumonia or sepsis, and he needs to be seen today, ideally at an ER. Older adults often don't run a high fever even when they're seriously ill, so confusion is a key warning sign. If he's struggling to breathe or very drowsy, call 911.
I have tinnitus after a concert last night. Ringing still going. Will it go away?

Ringing after a loud concert is very common and usually fades within a day or two as the stressed hair cells in your inner ear recover. Give your ears a quiet rest in the meantime, and avoid headphones and noisy places. If it's still there after a few days or comes with muffled hearing, get a hearing test, since prompt evaluation matters for noise-related loss. It's also a sign the volume was damaging, so foam earplugs at future shows are worth it.
Is it safe to take melatonin every night long term? I'm 29.

For most healthy adults, nightly melatonin at low doses looks reasonably safe, though long-term research is limited. Lower doses, around 0.5 to 3 mg taken an hour or two before bed, often work as well as larger ones and cause less grogginess. If you've needed it for months, it's worth looking at sleep habits or seeing a doctor about the cause. CBT for insomnia works better long term than any pill.
rabies shots after a bat was in my bedroom while I slept but i dont see a bite. overreacting?

You're not overreacting, and you should contact your doctor or local health department today. Bat bites can be so small that you don't notice them, so if a bat was in the room while you were asleep, that's generally treated as a possible exposure. Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms start, but post-exposure shots work extremely well when given promptly. If the bat can be safely contained without touching it with your bare hands, do that, because testing it could mean you don't need the shots.
I had Guillain-Barré 3 years ago. Should I still get my flu shot? my doctor's office is closed till monday

This is a decision you really should make with your doctor, so it's worth waiting until Monday to call. Having a history of Guillain-Barré that developed within six weeks of a previous flu shot is a precaution, and depending on what triggered your case, your doctor may weigh the risks of the vaccine against the risk of flu, which can also trigger GBS. Waiting a few days won't affect your protection for the season, so don't let a pharmacy give you a shot before you've spoken with your doctor.
Can I take Pepto with my aspirin?

It's best not to combine them without checking first. Pepto-Bismol contains bismuth subsalicylate, which is chemically related to aspirin, so together they raise your risk of bleeding and salicylate side effects. If you take daily aspirin, particularly for your heart, ask your pharmacist for an alternative like loperamide for diarrhea or a simple antacid for an upset stomach.
my eyes are dry all day at work, is it ok to use Visine every day

Redness-relief drops like classic Visine shrink blood vessels, and daily use can cause rebound redness while doing little for dryness. Preservative-free artificial tears are the better pick and are safe to use several times a day. Blink deliberately, take screen breaks, and if dryness continues despite that, see an eye doctor to check for dry eye disease or eyelid gland problems.
Got splashed with drain cleaner on my hand, it's tingling. Already wiped it off.

Wiping isn't enough. Get your hand under running lukewarm water right now and keep rinsing for at least 20 minutes, taking off any rings or contaminated clothing. Chemical burns can keep working on the skin after the liquid looks gone. Call poison control or go to urgent care afterward, and bring the bottle with you, especially if the skin is red, painful, blistering, or any got near your eyes.
Honestly does vitamin C actually do anything for colds or is it a scam

It's somewhere in between. Taking vitamin C regularly before you get sick may slightly shorten colds, by roughly a day at most, but starting megadoses once you're already sick doesn't reliably help. It won't prevent colds for most people either. It's cheap and safe at normal doses, but very high doses can cause stomach upset and diarrhea, so don't bother going overboard.
My mother seems depressed since my father died last year. She's 76. Is this just grief?

Grief can last a long time, but if a year on she's withdrawn, losing interest in things, sleeping or eating poorly, or seems hopeless, it may have become depression, which is very treatable at any age. Encourage her to see her doctor, and mention grief counseling or support groups for widows and widowers. If she ever talks about not wanting to live, contact her doctor or a crisis line right away.
I'm 19 and I think I might have ADHD. Can I just buy something online to try?

Please don't buy stimulants online. They're often counterfeit, and pills sold as Adderall are sometimes pressed with meth or fentanyl, which can kill on the first dose. Get properly assessed instead, through your doctor or your college health service, who can refer you for an ADHD evaluation. Lots of things mimic ADHD, like anxiety, depression and poor sleep, so a real assessment also makes sure you end up treating the right thing. While you wait, structure, body doubling and breaking tasks into small steps can help a surprising amount.
headache every morning when i wake up, goes away by lunch

Morning headaches that fade as the day goes on often come from poor sleep, sleep apnea, teeth grinding, caffeine withdrawal overnight or drinking alcohol the night before. If you snore or wake up unrefreshed, sleep apnea is worth asking your doctor about specifically. Get checked promptly if they're new, getting worse, or come with vomiting, vision changes or weakness, because headaches that are worst on waking can occasionally signal raised pressure in the head.
I think I'm allergic to my new laundry detergent, itchy red rash wherever my clothes touch. What do I do

That pattern strongly suggests contact dermatitis from the detergent or a fabric softener. Rewash your clothes and bedding with a fragrance-free, dye-free detergent, and run an extra rinse cycle.
