In the meantime, an over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream and an oral antihistamine can calm the itch. See a doctor if the rash spreads widely, blisters, gets infected, or doesn't improve within a week or two of switching.
I got hit in the eye with a squash ball. Hurts but I can see. There's a bit of blood pooled at the bottom of the colored part.

Blood pooling in front of the iris is a hyphema, and it needs to be seen today at an ER or eye clinic, even if your vision seems okay. It can raise the pressure in your eye or rebleed. Keep your head elevated and rest. Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen, since they can increase bleeding, and wear protective goggles for squash from now on.
how long can a human go without sleep

The documented record is around 11 days, but that's an extreme case, and serious problems start far earlier. After about 24 hours without sleep your reaction time and judgment are similar to legal drunkenness. By 48 to 72 hours, microsleeps, hallucinations and paranoia are common. It isn't something to test on yourself, and if someone can't sleep for days at a time, especially with racing thoughts or high energy, they need medical attention promptly.
is it ok to give my 4 year old melatonin gummies so she goes to bed easier?

I'd check with her pediatrician before starting, because melatonin isn't regulated as a medicine, and gummies often contain much more or less than the label says. For most young children, bedtime struggles respond well to a consistent routine, an earlier and predictable bedtime, a dark quiet room, and no screens for an hour before bed. If her doctor does suggest melatonin, it's usually a very low dose for a short time. Keep gummies stored out of reach, since kids treat them like candy.
teething causing my baby's 103 fever right?

Teething doesn't cause a fever that high. At most it causes a slight temperature rise. A 103°F fever means something else is going on, like an ear infection or another illness. Call your pediatrician to get your baby checked, and go to the ER if your baby is very drowsy, hard to wake, or not drinking. If your baby is under 3 months, any fever of 100.4°F or higher needs immediate care.
Is melatonin a vitamin? Taking 10mg nightly for like a year now.

It's actually a hormone, not a vitamin, and 10 mg is a lot higher than most people need. Doses of 0.5 to 3 mg often work as well with less grogginess. Daily use for a year also suggests there may be an underlying sleep problem worth looking into, and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia works well long term. Mention it to your doctor and consider tapering down to a lower dose rather than stopping abruptly.
dog allergy but my kid really wants one. are hypoallergenic breeds legit

No dog breed is truly allergen-free. The allergens come from saliva and skin, not just hair, and individual dogs vary more than breeds do. Low-shedding breeds like poodles may spread less dander around the house, which helps some people. The smartest move is spending real time around the specific dog before committing, ideally over several visits. If anyone in the house has asthma, see an allergist first, because rehoming a pet later is hard on everyone.
I got bitten by a raccoon I was trying to feed. Tiny bite. Overreacting if I go to the doctor?

Not at all, so please go today, because raccoons are a major rabies carrier and any bite from one is treated as a possible exposure. Wash the bite thoroughly with soap and water for 15 minutes and call your doctor, urgent care or local health department right away. Post-exposure vaccination is very effective if started promptly, but rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear.
Pet rat bit me and now 4 days later I've got a fever, joint aches and a weird rash on my hands. Probably just a cold?

That combination after a rat bite sounds like rat bite fever, a bacterial infection that can become serious if untreated. See a doctor today and tell them about the rat bite specifically, because it's easy to miss otherwise. It usually responds well to antibiotics when caught early. Go to the ER if you feel very unwell, have chest pain or the fever is high.
wisdom tooth pain. gum flap over it is puffy and gross tasting

That sounds like pericoronitis, which is an infection of the gum flap over a partially erupted wisdom tooth. Rinse with warm salt water several times a day and gently clean under the flap with a soft brush or irrigator, and ibuprofen can help with the ache. See a dentist within a few days, since this often needs a professional cleaning, sometimes antibiotics, and it tends to recur until the tooth is dealt with. Get seen sooner if you can't open your mouth fully, it hurts to swallow, or your face swells.
Type 2 diabetic here. My sugar was 310 after dinner. Should I take extra metformin to bring it down?

No, extra metformin won't drop your sugar quickly. It works gradually, and doubling up mainly raises your risk of stomach upset and, rarely, lactic acidosis. Drink water, take a gentle walk if you feel okay, and recheck in a couple of hours. One high reading after a big meal isn't an emergency, but if you're regularly above 250 or feel very thirsty, confused or nauseated, call your doctor, because your treatment plan may need adjusting.
is it normal for a 2 year old to not be talking yet? only says like 5 words

Most 2-year-olds say at least 50 words and are starting to put two words together, so 5 words is behind where most kids are. Bring it up with your pediatrician soon, and ask about a hearing test and an early intervention evaluation, which is free in the US. Many late talkers catch up, but starting help early is low-cost and makes a real difference if there's an underlying issue. Keep reading together and narrating your day to them in the meantime.
pregnant, 28 weeks, lower back and butt pain shooting down one leg. what can i take?

Acetaminophen at standard doses is generally the go-to pain reliever in pregnancy. Avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs, especially in the third trimester, since they can affect the baby's heart and kidneys. Heat on the low back, prenatal stretches, a pregnancy support belt, and sleeping on your side with a pillow between your knees often help this kind of sciatic pain. Mention it to your midwife or OB, who can refer you to a pelvic or prenatal physiotherapist, and call them sooner if you get numbness, weakness, or anything that feels like rhythmic tightening.
tonsillitis done, any reason not to hit a spin class?

If your fever's gone and you're swallowing and eating normally, a spin class is fine, though I'd keep the resistance moderate and skip the all-out sprints for the first session or two. Drink plenty, since a sore throat probably meant you weren't drinking much. If you finished antibiotics recently and feel fatigued, give yourself another day or two.
I'm on chemo, can I get the nasal flu vaccine since I hate needles

No. The nasal flu vaccine contains a live, weakened virus, so it's not recommended for anyone whose immune system is suppressed by chemotherapy. The injected flu shot is the safe choice, and it's especially important for you. Ask your oncology team about the best timing relative to your treatment cycles. Also make sure the people you live with get vaccinated.
One pupil looks way bigger than the other suddenly and I have a bad headache

A suddenly enlarged pupil with a bad headache needs emergency care right now, so call emergency services or go straight to the ER. It can signal acute glaucoma, a nerve problem, or bleeding in the brain, all of which need rapid treatment. Don't drive yourself, and mention any recent eye drops or patches like scopolamine, since those can also cause it.
grandpa coughing for 3 weeks now

Three weeks is long enough that he should see a doctor rather than wait it out. In older adults a lingering cough can mean pneumonia, a heart issue, medication side effects (some blood pressure pills cause it), or something that needs a chest X-ray. If he has a fever, shortness of breath, chest pain or is coughing up blood, get him seen today.
Pretty bad sunburn on my shoulders, blistering a bit. Can I just put aloe on and go back out tomorrow?

Aloe and cool compresses are fine, but stay out of the sun until it heals, because blistering means it's a second-degree burn. Leave the blisters intact, take ibuprofen for pain and swelling, and drink extra water. Get medical care if the burn covers a large area or you develop fever, chills, nausea or dizziness, since that suggests sun poisoning or dehydration.
bronchitis cough still hanging on after 3 weeks but i feel ok otherwise. swimming ok?

A lingering cough after bronchitis is common and can last several weeks, so easy swimming is generally fine if you otherwise feel well and have no fever. Keep it relaxed at first, since chlorinated pool air can irritate your airways and set off coughing. If the cough is getting worse, you're wheezing, or you're coughing up discolored mucus or blood, see a doctor. Any cough past about eight weeks should be checked too.
What number is considered a hypertensive crisis?

Readings above 180 systolic or 120 diastolic count as a hypertensive crisis. If you have symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, confusion or vision changes, call emergency services. If you have no symptoms, rest and recheck within a few minutes, and contact your doctor the same day if it's still that high.
sunburn. bad. blisters on my shoulders. what now

Cool the skin with cool showers or damp cloths, drink plenty of water, and take ibuprofen if you can safely use it, since it eases both pain and inflammation. Leave the blisters intact because they protect the raw skin underneath, and use a gentle aloe or fragrance-free moisturiser around them. Keep the area completely out of the sun until it heals. Get seen urgently if the blistering covers a large area, or if you develop fever, chills, confusion or feel faint, because that's sun poisoning territory.
fish oil — does it do anything

For most healthy people, fish oil capsules don't do much for heart attack prevention, but prescription-strength omega-3 can lower very high triglycerides. Eating fatty fish like salmon or sardines twice a week is the better-supported approach. If you take blood thinners or have a heart rhythm condition, check with your doctor before taking high doses, since large amounts have been linked to atrial fibrillation.
is it true you can reverse type 2 diabetes with keto

Many people can get type 2 diabetes into remission, meaning normal blood sugars without medication, mostly through significant weight loss, and low-carb diets like keto are one way some people get there. It doesn't work for everyone, and it's harder the longer you've had diabetes. If you're on insulin or sulfonylureas like glipizide, cutting carbs sharply can cause dangerous lows. Talk to your doctor before starting so they can adjust your meds as your sugars drop.
how much water should an 80 year old drink, my mom barely drinks anything

A rough target for most older adults is around 6 to 8 cups of fluid a day, though heart failure or kidney disease can change that, so check with her doctor if she has either. Older people often lose their sense of thirst, so waiting until she's thirsty doesn't work. Offer drinks on a schedule, like a glass with every meal and medication, and count soup, tea, milk and watery fruit too. Watch for dark urine, dizziness, constipation or new confusion, all of which can signal she's running low.
I'm allergic to penicillin (rash as a kid). Doctor wants to give me amoxicillin. Should I refuse?

Don't just refuse. Do tell the doctor about that childhood rash, because amoxicillin is a penicillin and they need to know before prescribing it. That said, most people with a vague childhood penicillin rash turn out not to be truly allergic, and an allergist can test you and often remove the label for good. Until that's sorted, let your doctor choose between a different antibiotic and a supervised test dose. Being cleared opens up better and cheaper treatment options for the rest of your life.
pregnant 10 weeks and cant keep anything down, even water, for like a day now

Some morning sickness is normal, but not keeping even water down for a full day is a reason to call your OB or midwife today. This can be hyperemesis gravidarum, which causes dehydration quickly, and IV fluids plus safe anti-nausea medication can make a huge difference. Go to the ER if you're dizzy, barely peeing, or your urine is dark.
My 6 year old swallowed a penny about an hour ago. He's eating and acting fine.

That's reassuring, since most swallowed coins pass on their own within a few days. Call his pediatrician today, though, because they sometimes want an X-ray to make sure it isn't stuck in the esophagus. Go to the ER right away if he drools, has trouble swallowing, has chest or belly pain, vomits or won't eat. Be sure it was actually a coin, because a button battery or magnet is an emergency.
My 15 yo son nearly passed out during basketball and said his heart was racing. He feels fine now. Coach says it's dehydration.

Nearly fainting during exercise with a racing heart is a red flag in a teenager and shouldn't be written off as dehydration. Keep him out of sports until his doctor has seen him. Ask about an ECG and possibly an echocardiogram to rule out inherited heart conditions. If he actually faints, has chest pain, or it happens again, take him to the emergency department.
My 8 year old gets stomach aches every school morning. Pediatrician says nothing physical. Anxiety?

Quite possibly. Morning stomach aches on school days are one of the most common ways anxiety shows up in kids, since they often feel worry in their bodies before they can name it. Gently ask about specific parts of the day, like the bus, lunch, a particular kid or a teacher, because the trigger is often concrete. Keep sending them to school with lots of empathy, since avoidance tends to make anxiety grow. If it persists, ask your pediatrician for a referral to a child therapist, because CBT for kids works really well.
Should I get an MRI for my back pain? It's been 2 weeks.

For most back pain without warning signs, an MRI at two weeks won't change treatment. It often picks up harmless age-related changes that can cause unnecessary worry. Most episodes improve within six weeks with staying active, pain relief and exercise. A scan becomes worthwhile if you have red flags like leg weakness, bladder or bowel changes, fever, a cancer history or major trauma, or if severe pain isn't improving after several weeks of proper treatment.
I'm 60 and my knees ache every morning for about 15 minutes then loosen up. Arthritis? Should I stop walking so I don't wear them out?

Brief morning stiffness that eases within half an hour is typical of osteoarthritis. Keep walking, because movement nourishes the cartilage and strengthens the muscles that protect the joint. Stopping tends to make knees stiffer and weaker. Leg strengthening exercises, keeping a healthy weight, and low-impact options like cycling or swimming all help. See your doctor if the knees get hot or swollen, or if morning stiffness starts lasting over an hour, which can point to an inflammatory arthritis instead.
My elderly mom (82) has suddenly gotten really confused and agitated over two days. No fever. Family says it's just age.

Sudden confusion over a day or two isn't normal aging, so get her seen by a doctor today. In older adults, infections like UTIs or pneumonia often show up as confusion without fever, and so can medication problems, dehydration or a stroke. If she has slurred speech, weakness on one side, trouble breathing, or you can't keep her safe, call emergency services. Bring a list of all her medications.
My mom's hearing is getting bad but she won't get hearing aids. Is it worth pushing?

Yes, it's worth a gentle push, because untreated hearing loss is linked to social isolation, depression and a higher risk of cognitive decline. Start with a hearing test from an audiologist, which is low-pressure and gives her real information. Modern hearing aids are small and discreet, and over-the-counter options now exist for mild to moderate loss. Also ask her doctor to check for earwax buildup, which is common and easily fixed.
Sharp zing of pain when I drink cold water, goes away in a second. Front teeth. 34F

A quick zing that fades right away usually points to sensitivity from exposed root surfaces or worn enamel, which is often caused by brushing too hard or gum recession. Switch to a soft brush and a sensitivity toothpaste with potassium nitrate or stannous fluoride, and give it two to four weeks to work. If the pain lingers after the cold is gone, or one tooth hurts much more than the others, have a dentist check it for a cavity or crack.
Quick q - can I drive myself home after a root canal?

Usually yes, because a standard root canal uses only local numbing, which doesn't affect your ability to drive. The exception is if you're given sedation such as nitrous oxide that hasn't fully worn off, oral sedative pills, or IV sedation, and in that case you need someone else to drive you. Ask the office ahead of time what they're planning so you can arrange a ride if you need one.
what's a normal a1c

For people without diabetes, it's below 5.7% (39 mmol/mol). A reading of 5.7 to 6.4% is prediabetes, and 6.5% or higher suggests diabetes. If you already have diabetes, most people aim for around 7% (53 mmol/mol) or lower. Your doctor may set a different target based on your age and your risk of lows.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and I think I have the flu, fever 101 and body aches. Should I just ride it out?

Call your OB or doctor today rather than riding it out. Pregnant women are at higher risk of serious flu complications, and antiviral treatment like oseltamivir works best when started within 48 hours of symptoms, and it's considered safe in pregnancy. Acetaminophen is the usual choice for bringing the fever down in the meantime. Go to the ER if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or notice decreased baby movement.
Can I take my wife's nitroglycerin for my chest pain? Same symptoms she gets.

Don't take her nitroglycerin. If you've taken Viagra, Cialis or a similar drug in the last day or two, it can drop your blood pressure dangerously, and it can also hide what's actually happening. If you have chest pain right now, call emergency services so you get assessed properly. If this is a recurring pattern, see your own doctor soon so you can get the right diagnosis and your own prescription if you need one.
quick q, can hay fever make you feel exhausted?

Yes, hay fever commonly causes fatigue, both from the inflammation itself and from poor sleep caused by congestion. Treating the congestion with a steroid nasal spray can noticeably improve your energy, and a non-drowsy antihistamine works better than older sedating ones like diphenhydramine. If you have a fever, body aches or it drags on for weeks, see a doctor, since that points to something other than allergies.
is turmeric safe to take with my blood thinner (warfarin)?

Check with your doctor or anticoagulation clinic before starting it. Turmeric and curcumin supplements can increase warfarin's effect and raise your bleeding risk. The amount you'd use in cooking is generally fine. Concentrated capsules are the concern, and if you do start one, your INR should be monitored more closely.
99.5 fever, should i be worried

That's barely above normal and generally isn't considered a true fever. Most doctors use 100.4°F as the cutoff. Body temperature also shifts throughout the day and after exercise or a hot drink. Rest, drink fluids, and recheck later. The exception is a baby under 3 months, so call a doctor if that's who has the temperature.
can i space out my toddler's vaccines so he doesn't get so many at once? like one per month

I'd stick with the standard schedule, because spreading shots out leaves your toddler unprotected for longer during the age when these diseases are most dangerous. It also means more appointments and more needle sticks overall. Getting several vaccines at once is safe, since his immune system handles far more than that from everyday germs. If shot visits are stressful, ask the pediatrician about combination vaccines and comfort tricks like holding him or numbing cream.
Mom is 79 and her blood pressure at home read 185/100 this morning. No symptoms. Should I take her to the ER?

Recheck it after she's rested quietly for five minutes, then call her doctor today if it's still that high. A reading like that needs prompt attention, but without symptoms it usually isn't an ER emergency. Go to the ER or call 911 if she has chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, vision changes, confusion, or weakness on one side. Don't double up on her blood pressure pills on your own.
pregnant and my glucose test came back high, gestational diabetes. will the baby be ok??

Most babies are completely fine, especially when gestational diabetes is caught and managed, and you've caught it. Treatment usually starts with diet changes, gentle activity and checking your sugar at home, and some people also need insulin or metformin, both of which are safe in pregnancy. Keep up your appointments and growth scans, and ask for a referral to a dietitian. It usually goes away after delivery, though you'll need a follow-up test later.
My grandma says put butter on a burn. Is she right?

No. Butter traps heat in the skin and can raise the risk of infection, so it's an old remedy worth retiring. The right move is cool running water for about 20 minutes, then a clean, non-stick covering if needed. Your grandma's heart is in the right place, but the water does the actual work.
Can I take ibuprofen and Tylenol together for a bad migraine?

Yes, ibuprofen and acetaminophen work differently and are safe to combine or alternate for most healthy adults, which often works better than either alone. Stick to the label limits for each, take the ibuprofen with food, and skip it if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers or are on blood thinners. If you're needing this combo more than a couple of days a week, see your doctor about a proper migraine plan.
is it ok to take my vitamin d gummies like 4 at a time if I forgot for a few days

Skip the catch-up dose and just take your normal amount today. Missing a few days of vitamin D doesn't matter much because your body stores it. Doubling up occasionally isn't dangerous, but it's a bad habit to build, since vitamin D toxicity does happen with sustained high doses. Gummies are also easy to overdo, so keep them out of reach of kids, who sometimes treat them like candy.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant with a migraine. Is ibuprofen fine?

Avoid ibuprofen now. After about 20 weeks, and especially in the third trimester, NSAIDs can affect the baby's kidneys and heart circulation. Acetaminophen is the standard choice in pregnancy, along with rest, a dark room and fluids. A severe or unusual headache this late in pregnancy, especially with vision changes or swelling, can signal preeclampsia, so call your midwife or OB today.
Recovered from a viral infection, but now my heart races during workouts more than before. I'm 34. Worth worrying about?

It's worth getting checked. Viral infections can occasionally cause myocarditis, which is inflammation of the heart muscle, and exercising hard with it can be dangerous. Hold off on intense workouts and see your doctor soon so they can listen to your heart and possibly run an ECG. If you have chest pain, fainting, or severe shortness of breath, go to urgent care right away.
my boss keeps emailing me at 11pm and i feel like i have to reply. burnout is real. how do i stop

Turn off work notifications after a set time, and move email off your home screen so you're not checking it by reflex. Most late-night emails aren't actually urgent, and replying at 8am the next morning quietly resets expectations. If it keeps going, have a calm conversation with your boss about response times, and frame it around doing better work. If you're already exhausted, cynical and dreading every day, that's burnout, and it's worth raising with your doctor.
Got stung by a bee on my arm, it's red and puffy. What do I do

Scrape the stinger out sideways with a fingernail or card as soon as you can, then wash the spot and hold a cold pack on it to ease the swelling. An oral antihistamine and some hydrocortisone cream help with itching, and a puffy red area around the sting is a normal local reaction. Call emergency services immediately if you get any trouble breathing, throat or tongue swelling, hives spreading elsewhere, dizziness or vomiting, since those are signs of anaphylaxis.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and my home cuff says 145/95, plus I have a headache that won't go away. Probably just stress right?

Please don't assume it's stress. At 34 weeks, a reading like that together with a persistent headache can be a sign of preeclampsia. Call your maternity unit or obstetric provider now, or go to labor and delivery to be assessed today. Go immediately if you notice vision changes, upper belly pain or sudden swelling.
whats the fastest way to stop a nosebleed... no wait, a paper cut that won't stop bleeding lmao

Squeeze it closed with a clean tissue for two or three minutes without peeking, and it'll almost always stop. Then wash it and put on a small plaster. That keeps it clean, and it also helps with the sting, since covered paper cuts hurt much less.
I'm pregnant and have asthma. Should I stop my inhalers to protect the baby?

No, keep taking them. Uncontrolled asthma is a much bigger risk to your baby than the inhalers, because poorly controlled asthma reduces the oxygen your baby gets. Most standard asthma inhalers, including albuterol and inhaled steroids like budesonide, are considered safe in pregnancy. Let your OB and your asthma doctor know, so they can watch your control closely, since asthma can change during pregnancy.
just tell me which antibiotics to take for a dog bite, i have some leftover amoxicillin

Please don't self-treat with leftover amoxicillin, because plain amoxicillin doesn't cover all the bacteria common in dog bites and a partial old course can mask a worsening infection. Bite infections are usually treated with a specific combination prescribed for the right length of time, and the wound may need proper cleaning too. Wash the bite well and get it seen at urgent care, which is quick for this.
Stray dog grazed my ankle with its teeth while I was jogging, didn't break the skin. Need rabies shots?

If the skin truly isn't broken and there's no saliva on an open cut, rabies risk is very low, and shots usually aren't needed. Wash the area well anyway, and look closely for any scratch or puncture. Since it's a stray, call your local health department to report it and confirm the risk where you live, because rabies rates vary a lot by region.
keto for 2 months, cholesterol jumped a lot at my checkup. ignore it?

Don't ignore it. A large jump in LDL on keto is fairly common, and some people are big responders whose LDL rises well into risky territory. Go over the numbers with your doctor, and try swapping butter, red meat and coconut oil for olive oil, nuts, avocado and fish, which often brings LDL down while staying low-carb. Recheck in a couple of months to see where you land.
I've gone vegan 2 months ago. What supplements do I actually need, I don't want to buy a whole pharmacy

B12 is the one you can't skip. Take either 50 micrograms daily or about 2,000 micrograms once a week, because plants don't provide it reliably. Vitamin D is worth taking in winter, and an algae-based omega-3 is a sensible optional extra. Use iodized salt or check your plant milk for iodine. Most other nutrients, iron included, you can get from food if you eat legumes, whole grains and leafy greens regularly.
is it ok to take ibuprofen every day for my back if i have high blood pressure

Daily ibuprofen isn't a great idea with high blood pressure. NSAIDs can raise your pressure, blunt some blood pressure medications and strain your kidneys over time. Acetaminophen is usually the safer choice for regular use, as long as you stay within the daily limit. Talk to your doctor about long-term options for your back.
Had chlamydia treated last month. Partner never got tested. Am I good to have sex again?

Not until your partner has been tested and treated too, or you'll likely get reinfected. That's very common and why repeat infections happen. After you both finish treatment, wait seven days before having sex again. It's also recommended that you get retested about three months after treatment, since reinfection often has no symptoms.
My son hit his head on the coffee table, he's 2. He cried right away and now seems normal. Should I worry?

Crying right away and then acting like himself is reassuring, and most bumps like this are minor. Watch him closely for the next 24 hours. Go to the ER if he vomits more than once, gets unusually sleepy or hard to wake, acts confused or off-balance, has a seizure, or develops a soft, squishy swelling on the side of his head. It's fine to let him nap, but check that he wakes normally.
is it normal to need my rescue inhaler like 4 times a week?

That's more than it should be. Needing a rescue inhaler more than twice a week usually means your asthma isn't well controlled. It's worth seeing your doctor about starting or adjusting a daily controller, or switching to a combination inhaler regimen. Also think about triggers like allergies, smoke or reflux that might be driving it. Well-managed asthma should barely interrupt your week.
whats the fastest way to get water out of my ear after swimming

Tilt your head with the plugged ear down, then gently tug the earlobe in different directions while hopping or jaw-wiggling, and gravity usually does the rest. A hairdryer on low and cool, held about a foot away, can help dry it out. Avoid sticking fingers or swabs in there, since scratching the wet canal is how swimmer's ear starts. If the ear becomes painful, itchy or swollen over the next day or two, see a doctor for drops.
Heartburn every night after dinner. What actually helps?

The biggest wins are finishing dinner at least three hours before bed, eating smaller evening portions, and raising the head of your bed by about six inches with blocks or a wedge, since extra pillows alone don't do much. Common triggers are alcohol, coffee, chocolate, mint, fatty or fried food, tomato sauces and late snacking, so cut back on whichever ones apply to you. An antacid or an over-the-counter H2 blocker like famotidine can help in the short term. If you need medication most nights for more than two weeks, see a doctor, because ongoing reflux deserves a proper look.
Can I just take a double dose of Zyrtec? Pollen is killing me today.

Don't double up on your own. Doubling cetirizine mostly adds drowsiness without much extra relief. A better move is to pair your normal dose with a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, and maybe antihistamine eye drops if your eyes are itchy. Showering and changing clothes after being outside also helps a lot. If one standard dose regularly isn't enough, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether a higher dose is right for you.
do migraine glasses (the rose tinted ones) actually work?

FL-41 tinted glasses have some modest evidence behind them and can help people who are very light-sensitive, especially under fluorescent lights or screens. They're low-risk and worth trying if light is a big trigger for you. Treat them as an add-on, though, not a substitute for proper migraine treatment.
What's the fastest way to fall asleep? Like actually fastest.

For most people the fastest reliable approach is to get your body into rest mode: dim the lights an hour before bed, keep the room cool (around 65 to 68°F), and put your phone out of reach. Once in bed, slow your breathing, for example inhaling for four counts and exhaling for six or eight, while relaxing each muscle group from your feet up. If you're still awake after about 20 minutes, get up and do something boring in dim light until you feel sleepy, rather than lying there frustrated. Skipping caffeine after early afternoon makes all of this work much better.
grease fire splashed on my face cooking, cheeks red, eyebrows singed. eyes seem ok but stinging a bit

Cool the burned areas gently with cool running water or wet cloths for 20 minutes. Rinse your eyes with clean water too, since they're stinging. Then go to urgent care or the ER, because facial burns should be assessed, and stinging eyes after a grease splash need checking. Get emergency help right away if your voice goes hoarse, you're coughing, or breathing feels off, as these can signal airway irritation.
how long after a dog bite can I wait before getting it checked? it happened this morning, now it's evening

Go tonight rather than waiting until tomorrow, especially if it's deep, on the hand, face or a joint, or the dog's vaccination status is unknown. Doctors prefer to see bites within about 8 hours to decide on cleaning, closure and antibiotics, though they can still help later. Until then, keep washing it with soap and water and keep it covered. If it's just a minor scrape from a vaccinated dog, home care is reasonable.
Is the neck check thing real? Exercise if symptoms are above the neck, not below?

It's a reasonable rule of thumb. With a stuffy nose or mild sore throat, light to moderate exercise is usually fine if you feel up to it. With chest congestion, a deep cough, body aches, an upset stomach or any fever, you should rest. Fever is the big one: never work out with a fever, because it raises the strain on your heart and the risk of complications.
teen son wants to start creatine for football. hes 16. fine?

Creatine is one of the better-studied supplements, but pediatric groups generally advise against it for teens under 18. The long-term effects at this age aren't well established, and supplements aren't tightly regulated for purity. At 16, he'll get bigger gains from consistent strength training, enough protein and calories, and solid sleep. If he's set on it, have him talk it through with his doctor first.
i want to do a 7 day water fast to detox. tips?

Your liver and kidneys already handle detoxing, and a week with no food carries real risks, including dangerous electrolyte shifts, fainting and heart rhythm problems. It's especially risky if you take any medications or have health conditions. If what you're after is a reset, try time-restricted eating, like a 14 to 16 hour overnight fast, which is far safer. If you're set on a longer fast, do it only with medical supervision.
what's the best sleeping position for back pain

Sleeping on your side with a pillow between your knees, or on your back with a pillow under your knees, is usually easiest on the lower back. Stomach sleeping tends to arch your spine and strain your neck, so it's best avoided if your back hurts. A medium-firm mattress works well for most people. If the pain is new and severe, shoots down your leg, or comes with numbness or bladder changes, get it checked by a doctor.
Can I get my flu and RSV shots on the same day? I'm 72 and don't want to make two trips.

Yes, you can get them at the same visit, and many pharmacies routinely offer them together, usually one in each arm. You might have a little more soreness or tiredness for a day than with one shot alone, but it's generally mild. At 72, RSV is recommended as a single dose rather than every year, so once you've had it you won't need it every fall like the flu shot.
Just quick, how long after the flu shot does it start working

It takes about two weeks to build full protection. That's why getting it in September or October, before flu season ramps up, is ideal. Getting it later in the season is still worthwhile, though, since flu often circulates into spring.
My 12yo daughter has had a headache 3 days now and today she threw up and says light hurts her eyes. Probably a migraine right?

It could be a migraine, but a headache with vomiting and light sensitivity needs to be checked today, not waited out. Call her doctor now, or go to the ER if she has a fever, a stiff neck, unusual sleepiness, confusion or a rash. Those can point to something more serious, like meningitis. Even if it does turn out to be a migraine, a doctor can give her proper treatment and rule out other causes.
My grandma's eye suddenly got blurry and she sees like a curtain over part of it. She wants to wait and see.

Please don't wait. A curtain or shadow over part of her vision can mean a retinal detachment or a blocked blood vessel in the eye, and both can cause permanent vision loss within hours to days. Get her to an eye doctor or emergency department today. If it comes with facial drooping, weakness or speech trouble, call emergency services because it could be a stroke.
My 70yo dad refuses the RSV vaccine bc he 'never gets sick'. worth pushing?

It's worth a gentle push. RSV puts tens of thousands of older adults in the hospital every year, often people who were otherwise healthy, and the risk rises after 75 or with heart or lung conditions. It's a single dose, not an annual one. Framing it as protecting himself from a hospital stay, or protecting grandkids, sometimes works better than arguing statistics, and a nudge from his own doctor often carries more weight than family.
Cold for 3 days. Do I need antibiotics?

No, colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics do nothing against them. They can also cause side effects and contribute to resistance. Rest, fluids, and over-the-counter remedies for symptom relief are the way to go. See a doctor if you're getting worse after a week, if a fever spikes again after improving, or if you get sinus pain or ear pain that won't quit.
Is it okay to take ibuprofen BEFORE my vaccine so I don't feel crappy after?

It's better not to take it beforehand. There's some evidence that pre-dosing could slightly blunt the immune response, and it's unnecessary anyway. If you feel achy or feverish afterward, taking ibuprofen or acetaminophen then is fine and won't undermine the vaccine.
Kids keep getting lice at school, can I just use the dog's flea shampoo on them? It's basically the same thing

Please don't. Pet flea products aren't made or dosed for children's skin and can contain ingredients that are toxic to kids. Use an over-the-counter lice treatment with permethrin or pyrethrins and follow the directions exactly. Comb out nits carefully with a fine-tooth nit comb over the next couple of weeks. If over-the-counter treatments keep failing, a pediatrician or pharmacist can recommend prescription options that work on resistant lice.
Do I really need the eye doctor every year? My vision is perfect.

Yes. Diabetic retinopathy usually causes no symptoms until it's fairly advanced, so perfect vision doesn't rule it out. A dilated eye exam can catch it early, when treatment works well and can prevent vision loss. If your previous exams have been clear and your sugars are well controlled, your eye doctor may say every two years is fine, but let them make that call.
traveling to Kenya in 3 weeks, what shots do i need, can i just get them at the airport lol

You can't get them at the airport, and three weeks is already tight, so book a travel clinic or your doctor this week. For Kenya you'll typically need yellow fever, plus typhoid and hepatitis A, malaria pills, and a check that your routine vaccines are current. Some vaccines need time to take effect, and yellow fever has to be given at least 10 days before arrival for your certificate to be valid.
pet rat nipped me, tiny cut. anything special about rat bites?

Yes, rats can carry bacteria that cause rat-bite fever, even healthy pet rats. Wash the cut well with soap and water and keep it clean. Most small nips heal fine, but if you develop fever, chills, a rash, vomiting or joint pain over the next few weeks, see a doctor and mention the rat bite. It's very treatable with antibiotics when caught.
I drink about 4-5 glasses of wine a night. Is tylenol actually dangerous for me?

At that level of drinking, yes, your liver is more vulnerable to acetaminophen. Keep it to no more than 2000 mg a day and avoid taking it on nights you drink heavily. Ibuprofen isn't automatically safer either, since alcohol plus NSAIDs raises the risk of stomach bleeding. Four to five glasses a night is also worth discussing with a doctor, who can check your liver and help if you want to cut back.
is it safe to do a 5 day water fast to 'reset' my anxiety? saw it on tiktok

I'd skip it, because there's no good evidence that fasting resets anxiety, and five days without food can cause low blood sugar, electrolyte problems, and dizziness that often makes anxiety feel worse. It's also risky if you have diabetes, take medication, or have any history of disordered eating. Regular meals, sleep, cutting back on caffeine, and exercise will do far more for your anxiety, and a therapist can help with the rest.
whats the best sleeping position for back pain

Lying on your side with a pillow between your knees is usually the most comfortable, because it keeps your hips and spine aligned. If you sleep on your back, a pillow under your knees takes strain off your lower back. Stomach sleeping tends to make back pain worse, but if you can't give it up, a flat pillow under your pelvis helps. See a doctor if the pain wakes you at night regularly or comes with fever, numbness or weight loss.
keto diet ok for type 1 diabetic? want to drop 20 lbs fast

Don't start keto on your own with type 1 diabetes. Very low-carb eating changes your insulin needs a lot, which raises the risk of hypoglycemia, and it can make diabetic ketoacidosis harder to spot. Some people with type 1 do eat lower-carb safely, but only with their endocrinologist or diabetes educator adjusting insulin doses as they go. Ask for that appointment first, and aim for steady loss rather than fast.
dizzy and room spinning when I roll over in bed, ear thing?

Brief spinning when you roll over or tilt your head is often BPPV, an inner ear problem where tiny crystals shift, and it's very treatable. A doctor or physical therapist can confirm it and do a simple repositioning maneuver that often fixes it in one visit. Get urgent care right away if the dizziness comes with a severe headache, trouble speaking, weakness, numbness, double vision, or difficulty walking, since those can point to a stroke.
is collagen powder legit or a scam

It's not a total scam, but it's oversold. A few studies show modest improvements in skin elasticity and joint pain, often funded by manufacturers. Your body breaks collagen down into amino acids like any other protein, so eating enough protein overall matters most. If you enjoy it and the cost doesn't bother you, it's harmless for most people, but don't expect dramatic results.
sunburn is blistering pretty bad on my shoulders, should i pop the blisters

Leave the blisters intact, because they protect the raw skin underneath from infection. Cool the area with damp cloths or cool showers, use aloe or a plain moisturizer, drink extra water, and take ibuprofen for the pain and inflammation if it's safe for you. If a blister breaks by itself, wash it gently and cover it with a non-stick dressing. If the blistering covers a large area or you have fever, chills, confusion, or feel faint, get seen today.
Can I use lemon juice to lighten my dark spots?

Lemon juice is too acidic and unpredictable for skin. Combined with sunlight, it can actually cause burns and blistering (phytophotodermatitis) that leave darker marks. Better options are vitamin C serums, azelaic acid, niacinamide or a retinoid, and daily SPF 30+ matters most of all, because sun keeps re-darkening spots. If a spot is changing, irregular or new in adulthood, have a dermatologist check it before trying to fade it.
Mom's 77 and her doctor put her on a blood thinner. Can she still take ibuprofen for her arthritis?

She should avoid ibuprofen unless her doctor specifically okays it, because combining it with a blood thinner significantly raises the risk of stomach and other bleeding. Acetaminophen is usually the safer choice for arthritis pain, kept within the daily limit her doctor or pharmacist recommends. Topical options like diclofenac gel may also be worth asking about, since less of the drug reaches the bloodstream. Have her pharmacist review all her medications, including supplements, for other interactions.
My jaw aches and my teeth hurt in the morning. What gives?

Waking up with a sore jaw and achy teeth is a classic sign of grinding or clenching at night, which is often linked to stress. A dentist can fit a night guard, which protects your teeth and usually eases the jaw pain a lot. In the meantime, try warm compresses, soft foods and consciously relaxing your jaw during the day. If the pain comes with a clicking or locking jaw, or doesn't improve, a dental exam is worth it.
i'm 34 weeks pregnant with awful allergies, what can I safely take

Loratadine and cetirizine are generally considered reasonable antihistamine choices in pregnancy. Saline rinses and nasal sprays are a great first step since they carry essentially no risk. Steroid nasal sprays like budesonide are also commonly used. Skip oral decongestants like pseudoephedrine unless your doctor okays them, since they can raise blood pressure. Run whatever you choose by your OB or pharmacist, especially this late in pregnancy.
ugh burned my tongue on coffee. how long does this last

A scalded tongue usually feels better within a few days and fully heals within about a week, since the mouth repairs itself quickly. Sip cool water or suck on an ice chip, and avoid hot, spicy, salty or acidic foods while it heals. If it blisters badly or still hurts after a week, have it checked.
There's a little pimple on my gum above a tooth that oozes salty stuff sometimes. Doesn't hurt.

That's most likely a fistula, a drainage channel from an abscess at the tip of the tooth's root. It doesn't hurt because the pus has an exit, but the infection is still there. It won't go away on its own, so book a dentist soon. You'll likely need a root canal or extraction to clear it before it flares up.
ear is super itchy and kinda painful when i pull on it, been swimming a lot this week

That sounds a lot like swimmer's ear (otitis externa), a skin infection of the ear canal that hurts when you tug the ear. It usually needs prescription antibiotic drops, so it's worth a quick visit to a doctor or urgent care. Until then, keep the ear dry, skip swimming, and don't put anything in the canal. If your face swells, you get a fever, or you're diabetic, get seen promptly.
got a hard lump where i had the vaccine 2 days ago. normal?

A small, firm lump at the injection site is common and usually fades over a few days to a couple of weeks. A cool compress can help with tenderness. Have it looked at if it keeps growing, becomes hot and increasingly red, starts to drain, or comes with a fever.
What's the difference between angina and a heart attack? My doctor said I have stable angina.

Angina is chest discomfort caused by temporarily reduced blood flow to the heart, and in stable angina it's predictable: it comes on with exertion or stress and settles within a few minutes of rest or nitroglycerin. A heart attack is when blood flow is blocked long enough to damage heart muscle, and the pain usually lasts longer, is more severe, or comes on at rest. A good working rule is that if your usual angina doesn't ease after rest and nitro as your doctor directed, or it's clearly worse or different from normal, call emergency services rather than waiting it out.
how long should i meditate a day to actually see results

Ten minutes a day is plenty to start, and consistency matters far more than length. Studies showing reduced stress and anxiety often use 10 to 20 minutes daily over about eight weeks. Apps like Insight Timer or Headspace make it easier to stick with. If meditation ever stirs up distressing memories or panic, which can happen with trauma, scale back and consider working with a therapist.
I'm 34, female, healthy, and I get a sharp stabbing pain under my left breast for a few seconds when I breathe in. Heart?

A brief, sharp, stabbing pain that changes with breathing and lasts only seconds is much more typical of chest wall or nerve irritation, sometimes called precordial catch, than of a heart problem, especially at your age. Heart pain is usually more of a pressure, squeezing or heaviness that builds over minutes. Still, pain that worsens with breathing can also come from pericarditis or a blood clot in the lung, so get seen promptly if it becomes persistent, if you're short of breath, have a fast heart rate, leg swelling, recently traveled or take estrogen-containing birth control. If it's just these quick catches and you otherwise feel fine, mention it at your next checkup.
is it ok to pop a blister from new shoes

Leave it intact if you can, since the skin over it is the best sterile bandage there is. Cover it with a padded blister plaster and switch shoes for a few days. If it's big, tense and painful enough that it'll burst anyway, wash your hands, sterilize a needle with alcohol, prick it at the edge, let the fluid drain, and leave the roof of skin in place, then cover it. If you have diabetes, poor circulation or signs of infection like spreading redness or pus, have it looked at.
I got a flu shot and my aunt freaked out saying it's dangerous while pregnant. Did I mess up?

You didn't mess up, because the inactivated flu shot is recommended during pregnancy at any stage. It protects you from serious flu complications, and the antibodies you make pass to your baby, which helps protect them for their first few months. The only flu vaccine to avoid is the live nasal spray, and the shot is not that vaccine.
I fainted while standing in a hot crowded concert, came round in seconds, feel totally fine now. 27. Need to see someone or nah?

Fainting while standing for a long time in heat and crowds is very often a simple vasovagal faint, and recovering quickly and fully is reassuring. It's still worth a routine GP visit and a basic ECG, because a first faint is a reason to rule out rarer rhythm issues. That matters especially if anyone in your family has had sudden unexplained deaths or you've had palpitations. Seek prompt care if you ever faint during exercise, while lying down, or without warning.
How long after taking zyrtec can I take benadryl? Hives are bad.

Combining two antihistamines mostly adds drowsiness without much extra relief, so don't stack them casually. For bad hives, many doctors instead increase the non-drowsy antihistamine itself, for example cetirizine up to twice daily, but get their okay before doing that. If the hives come with lip or tongue swelling, wheezing or trouble breathing, use epinephrine if you have it and call emergency services.
is it safe to sleep with a fan on all night

For most people it's perfectly fine, and the white noise and cooler air can actually help sleep. Some people wake up with a dry throat, stuffy nose or stiff neck, so point it away from your face if that happens. Keep the fan clean, since dust buildup can bother allergies. Don't place it where it could tip onto bedding or a child.
what's a natural supplement that lowers bp so i dont need meds

Some supplements have modest evidence behind them, such as potassium (if your kidneys are healthy), magnesium, beetroot, and garlic extract, but they usually lower pressure by only a few points. The changes that make a bigger difference are cutting sodium, losing weight, exercising regularly and drinking less alcohol. Lifestyle changes can sometimes replace medication for mild hypertension, but supplements generally can't. Check with your doctor before adding potassium in particular, because it can interact with common BP drugs.
I found a tick on my leg this morning and pulled it off. Now there's a small red bump. Should I worry?

A small red bump right where the tick was is normal and usually fades within a few days. Clean it with soap and water and keep an eye on it for the next month. See a doctor if you notice a red rash expanding outward, especially a bullseye pattern, or if you get fever, fatigue, aches or headache, because those can be signs of Lyme disease or another tick-borne illness. If you live in a high-risk area, tell your doctor about the bite now, since sometimes a single preventive antibiotic dose is offered.
pregnant 30 weeks, can't sleep, can I take unisom?

Doxylamine, the active ingredient in Unisom SleepTabs, is commonly used in pregnancy and generally considered low risk. Still, check with your OB or midwife before using it for sleep, since they know your situation. Many Unisom products use diphenhydramine instead, so look at the label to see which one you have. Side sleeping with a pregnancy pillow, cutting fluids in the late evening, and treating heartburn can also help a lot in the third trimester.
cat bit me 3 days ago, now there's a red line going up my arm

A red line spreading up your arm from a bite can mean the infection is moving into your lymphatic system, so go to urgent care or the ER today, not tomorrow. This usually responds well to antibiotics when treated promptly, but it can become serious if it's left alone. Go to the ER straight away if you have a fever, chills, or the line is advancing quickly.
I'm a teacher and have a sore throat and cough, no fever. Do I have to call in sick?

Without a fever and if you feel well enough, going in is usually reasonable. Wash your hands often, cover your coughs, and consider wearing a mask to protect your students. A quick COVID test is worth doing given how you're spending your day. If you get a fever, feel wiped out, or your throat is severe without much cough, stay home and consider getting checked for strep.
Is it okay to sweat out a fever at the gym?

No. Exercising with a fever raises your body temperature further, puts strain on your heart, and dehydrates you without speeding recovery. In rare cases, exercising during a viral illness can even inflame the heart muscle. Rest until you've been fever-free for at least a day without medicine, and you'll also avoid spreading it to everyone at the gym.
I have leftover amoxicillin from last year, can I take it for this fever? Pretty sure it's the same infection.

Don't. Most fevers are viral, and antibiotics do nothing against viruses. Old leftovers may also be the wrong drug, the wrong dose, or not enough for a full course, which helps breed resistant bacteria. If you think it's bacterial, like a strep throat or a urinary infection, see a doctor so they can test you and prescribe the right thing.
I'm 68 and I've got a sore on my nose that bleeds a little, scabs, heals, then comes back. It's been like 3 months.

A sore that keeps bleeding and healing over and over for months is a classic sign of basal cell carcinoma, a common skin cancer that's very curable but should not be left alone. Please book a dermatologist appointment soon and mention exactly what you've told me, since they'll likely do a quick biopsy. The good news is that caught at this stage, treatment is usually simple and effective.
pulled an all-nighter, have a 3 hour drive home now. i'll be fine with a red bull right?

I'd really push back on that one, because driving after a night without sleep impairs you about as much as being legally drunk, and caffeine doesn't fully fix it. Energy drinks can also wear off suddenly, and microsleeps can hit without warning. The safest move is a 20 to 30 minute nap before you leave, ideally right after a coffee so the caffeine kicks in as you wake. Better still, get a ride, take a train, or delay the trip until you've slept.
My kid's friend has chickenpox and they played together yesterday. My daughter is 5 and fully vaccinated. Do I need to do anything?

Since she's had her varicella shots, she's very well protected, and if she does catch it, it's usually a mild case with fewer spots. Watch for fever or an itchy, blister-like rash over the next 10 to 21 days. If one appears, call her doctor before you go in so they can keep other patients from being exposed. Avoid giving her aspirin if she gets sick, because it's linked to Reye's syndrome in kids with chickenpox.
quick q - forgot my antibiotic dose this morning, it's 6pm now. double up?

Don't double up. Take the missed dose now, then space the rest out evenly from here, unless your next dose is due within a few hours, in which case skip the missed one and carry on as normal. The exact rule varies a bit by drug, so a quick check with your pharmacist or the leaflet will confirm the timing for yours.
my son (7) has a nut allergy and his school says he can't carry his own epipen. is that ok?

Many schools keep epinephrine in the office for younger kids. What matters is that it's always quickly reachable wherever he is, including on the playground, in the cafeteria and on field trips. Ask the school for a written allergy action plan, confirm which staff are trained to use it, and ask how it travels with him off-site. Your pediatrician or allergist can provide a form and back you up if you feel the arrangement leaves gaps.
can i give my 18 month old adult tylenol if i just cut the pill in half?

Please don't do that. Half an adult tablet is still far too much for a toddler, and acetaminophen overdose can seriously damage the liver. Use children's liquid acetaminophen with the syringe that comes in the box, and dose by your child's weight. If you're unsure of the right amount, a pharmacist can tell you in under a minute.
Can I keep doing my CrossFit workouts? I'm 14 weeks and have done it for years.

If you're experienced and your pregnancy is uncomplicated, you can usually continue with modifications, so run your routine past your OB first. As you progress, avoid lying flat on your back for long periods, contact or fall risks, and lifting to the point where you strain or hold your breath. Scale the intensity so you can still talk during workouts. Stop and call your provider if you have bleeding, leaking fluid, dizziness or chest pain.
Sudden severe back pain, feels like tearing, I'm 67 with high blood pressure. Just took a painkiller.

Call emergency services now. Sudden, severe tearing back pain at your age with high blood pressure can be an aortic dissection or a ruptured aortic aneurysm, both life-threatening emergencies. Don't drive yourself, and don't wait to see if the painkiller works.
Is it safe to give ibuprofen to my 4 month old for teething pain?

Ibuprofen generally isn't recommended under 6 months unless your pediatrician specifically says so. Check with them before giving any pain reliever at this age. For teething, a chilled (not frozen) teether, a clean finger rubbed on the gums or a cold washcloth to chew on work well. Avoid numbing gels with benzocaine and teething necklaces, because both carry real risks for babies.
my cat bit my hand pretty deep, two little puncture holes, it's kinda swollen already. do i just put a bandaid on it?

Wash it well with soap and running water for a few minutes, but don't stop at a bandaid, because cat bites are deep, narrow punctures that trap bacteria and get infected fast, especially on the hand. Swelling already starting is a sign you should see a doctor today, since you'll likely need antibiotics. If you notice red streaks, increasing pain, or trouble moving your fingers, go to urgent care or the ER right away.
I ate something with sesame at a restaurant and used my epipen, symptoms are gone now. do I still need to go to the ER?

Yes, go now even though you feel fine. Epinephrine wears off in roughly 15 to 20 minutes, and symptoms can return or a second wave can hit hours later. Call emergency services or have someone drive you; don't drive yourself. Bring the used pen, and replace it as soon as possible.
I have a penicillin allergy listed from when I was a baby. Do I really have it?

Quite possibly not, because most people labeled penicillin-allergic in childhood turn out not to be allergic when they're tested, especially since the reaction often fades over the years. It's worth asking your doctor about a penicillin allergy evaluation, which usually involves skin testing and a supervised test dose. Don't test it yourself by taking an antibiotic, but getting the label cleared can give you access to safer, more effective antibiotics later.
quick q, can my 80 yr old dad get the shingles vaccine? he had chickenpox as a kid

Yes, and having had chickenpox is exactly why he's at risk, since shingles is a reactivation of that same virus. The recombinant vaccine is recommended for adults 50 and older as two doses a few months apart, and it works well even at his age. He can get it at most pharmacies or his doctor's office. Ask whether he's also due for pneumonia, flu, COVID and RSV vaccines while he's there.
is it better to use a humidifier or a vaporizer when you have a cough

A cool-mist humidifier is usually the better pick, especially in homes with kids, because warm-mist vaporizers can cause burns if they're knocked over. Both add moisture that soothes irritated airways, so the benefit is similar. Whichever you use, clean it every day or two and empty the standing water, since a dirty unit can spray mold and bacteria into the air.
dog bit me, it was a stray and ran off. it's just a small bite on my calf. probably fine to skip shots?

Please don't skip the evaluation, since an unknown stray that ran off can't be observed or tested for rabies. Wash the bite thoroughly with soap and water for several minutes, then contact your doctor or local health department today. They'll decide whether you need rabies shots based on local risk, and you may also need a tetanus booster. Rabies treatment works very well when started promptly.
I'm a hiker and I want to know, should I suck the venom out if I get bitten by a rattlesnake?

No, sucking, cutting, ice and tourniquets all do more harm than good and waste time. Move away from the snake, keep calm and still, take off rings or tight items near the bite before swelling starts, and keep the limb at roughly heart level. Then call 911 or get to a hospital as fast as safely possible, since antivenom is the only real treatment. If you're far out, walk out steadily rather than waiting, and mark the edge of the swelling with the time if you have a pen.
Friend cut his hand on a broken glass at the party and it's spurting. what do we do

Call 911 now, because spurting blood can mean an artery is cut. Press down hard on the wound with a clean cloth or whatever fabric you have, keep his hand raised above his heart, and don't let up. If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top rather than removing the first layer. Have him sit or lie down in case he gets faint.
My teenager sleepwalks sometimes. Last night he went outside. How worried should I be?

Going outside makes this a safety issue, so take some precautions now. Lock outside doors with locks he can't easily open half-asleep, consider a door alarm, and keep stairs, windows, car keys and sharp objects secure. Sleep deprivation, stress and an irregular schedule are common triggers, so protecting his sleep often reduces episodes. Since he left the house, it's worth seeing his doctor to rule out other causes and talk through options.
Arm swollen hot and red about 3 inches around the spot 2 days after my tetanus shot. Infection?

Redness, warmth and swelling at the injection site a day or two after a tetanus shot is a fairly common local reaction and is usually not an infection. A cool compress and an over-the-counter pain reliever usually help, and it should start easing within a few days. Because the area is a few inches wide, it's worth calling your doctor to have it looked at, and get seen promptly if the redness keeps spreading, you see red streaks, the area drains pus, or you develop a fever, since those point toward infection.
My 10 year old gets stomach aches basically every school morning. Doctor found nothing. Am I overreacting?

You're not overreacting, and a recurring morning stomach ache with a normal exam often points to stress or anxiety, which can cause very real pain. Try talking with him calmly about how school is going, including friends, teachers, and any bullying, and check in with his teacher too. If it continues, ask the pediatrician about a referral to a child therapist, because addressing anxiety early tends to help a lot.
chemical burn from oven cleaner on my hand. it stings like crazy

Rinse it under lots of running water right away and keep going for at least 20 minutes, removing any rings or contaminated clothing as you go. Don't try to neutralize it with vinegar or anything else, because plain water is the safest option. Check the can for first aid instructions, and call poison control if you're unsure. If the skin looks white, broken or blistered, or the pain persists after rinsing, get it seen today, since oven cleaner is strongly alkaline and can keep burning deeper.
teenager is up til 2am every night and impossible in the morning. lazy or something else?

It's mostly biology. Puberty shifts the body clock later, so teens genuinely don't feel sleepy until late, and phones in bed push it later still. They also still need about 8 to 10 hours. Phones out of the bedroom an hour before bed, bright light in the morning and a consistent wake time, including weekends, make a real difference. If they still can't function, or seem low or anxious, a chat with their doctor is worthwhile.
Red eye, severe pain, headache, nausea, and halos around lights. Started tonight. Should I sleep on it?

Don't sleep on it, go to the ER now. A painful red eye with headache, nausea and halos around lights is a textbook picture of acute angle-closure glaucoma. That's a sudden pressure spike that can permanently damage vision within hours, and it's very treatable if handled fast.
Anxiety attack or heart attack?? I have panic disorder and my chest is tight and I can't tell anymore

Panic attacks usually peak within about 10 minutes and come with tingling, a racing heart and a sense of dread, while heart pain tends to be heavy pressure that may spread to the arm, jaw or back. Even so, they genuinely can look alike. If this feels different from your usual attacks, is getting worse, or you have heart risk factors, call emergency services, and nobody there will think you've wasted their time. Longer term, it's worth getting a baseline heart check with your doctor so you have more confidence next time.
teeth hurt when i drink cold stuff. like a quick zing. normal?

A brief zing with cold that fades within a few seconds is usually sensitivity from worn enamel or receding gums, and it's very common. Switch to a sensitivity toothpaste with potassium nitrate or stannous fluoride, and use it twice daily for a couple of weeks to see the full effect. Also brush gently with a soft brush. If the pain lingers long after the cold is gone, or it's centered on one tooth, have a dentist look for a cavity or crack.
how often should a diabetic actually check their feet

Every day, ideally at the same time, such as after a shower. Look for cuts, blisters, redness, swelling, cracks between the toes or nail problems, and use a mirror or ask someone for help if you can't see the bottoms well. You should also have a professional foot exam at least once a year. See your doctor promptly about anything that isn't healing within a few days, because small problems can escalate quickly with diabetes.
My doctor won't give me antibiotics for my cold. I always get them and I always get better. Isn't she being stubborn?

She's actually doing it right, because colds are caused by viruses and antibiotics have no effect on them. You got better those other times because colds clear on their own in about 7 to 10 days, not because of the pills. Unnecessary antibiotics carry real costs like diarrhea, allergic reactions and resistance. Go back if you're still getting worse after 10 days or you develop a high fever or facial pain after seeming to improve.
Grandma's bp monitor says 210/120 and she's slurring words, should I give her an extra pill?

Call emergency services right now, because slurred speech with that pressure could be a stroke. Don't give her extra medication, since lowering pressure the wrong way during a stroke can cause harm. Note the time her symptoms started and keep her safe until help arrives.
toddler drank some of grandma's pills?? not sure how many

Call Poison Control right now at 1-800-222-1222 in the US, or 911 if your child is drowsy, having trouble breathing, or having a seizure. Have the pill bottle in hand so you can tell them the name, strength, and how many might be missing. Don't try to make your child vomit. Some adult medications, like heart and diabetes pills, can be dangerous even in a single dose for a toddler.
I've had type 1 for 20 years and want to try running a marathon. My endo is slow to respond. Just tell me how to dose.

Plenty of people with type 1 run marathons, but I can't give you specific doses, because the right numbers depend on your regimen, your pump or injection setup, and how your body responds. The usual approach is to lower your basal or pre-run bolus, carry fast carbs and fuel every 30 to 45 minutes, and wear a CGM if you can. People also commonly see delayed lows overnight after long runs. Use your training runs to log patterns, and push for an appointment with your endo or a diabetes educator who works with athletes, because that is exactly what they're good at.
My 7yo has been peeing a lot and drinking tons of water lately, also seems tired and lost a bit of weight.

Get this checked by her doctor today or tomorrow, not at a routine visit weeks out. Heavy thirst, frequent peeing, tiredness, and weight loss together are classic signs of type 1 diabetes, which can be diagnosed with a simple urine or finger-prick test. Go to the ER instead if she starts vomiting, breathing fast or deeply, has stomach pain, or seems confused, since those can signal diabetic ketoacidosis.
how long does cat scratch fever take to show up

Cat scratch disease usually starts with a small bump or blister at the scratch site within 3 to 10 days, followed by swollen, tender lymph nodes nearby, often in the armpit or neck, one to three weeks after the scratch. Fever, tiredness and headache can come along with it. If you notice swollen nodes after a cat scratch, see a doctor, especially if you have a weakened immune system.
pregnant and craving deli turkey sandwiches lol is that bad

Cold deli meats carry a small risk of listeria, which is rare but can be serious in pregnancy. The easy fix is to heat the turkey until it's steaming hot, like in a toasted panini or microwaved, which kills any bacteria. Then you can enjoy the craving safely.
My husband burned his face lighting the grill, eyebrows singed, cheek red and hoarse voice. He says he's fine.

The hoarse voice is the worrying part, because it can mean he inhaled hot air or smoke and his airway may swell over the next few hours. Please take him to the ER now rather than waiting to see how it goes. Call emergency services if he has any trouble breathing, wheezing or difficulty swallowing. While you get ready, cool the cheek gently with a cool, damp cloth, but don't let that delay getting him seen.
My 6 month old has red dry patches on her cheeks and behind her knees, she keeps rubbing them. What can I do?

That pattern sounds a lot like infant eczema, which is very common at this age. Use a thick fragrance-free moisturiser such as plain emollient ointment several times a day, especially straight after a short lukewarm bath, and dress her in soft cotton. Use fragrance-free soap substitutes and laundry products. Have her GP or health visitor confirm it, because they can prescribe a mild steroid cream if moisturising isn't enough. See them sooner if the patches weep, crust or turn yellow, since that can mean infection.
My teenager is going to college and living in a dorm. Any vaccines she needs?

Yes, make sure she's had the MenACWY meningococcal booster at 16 or later, because meningitis spreads more easily in dorms and can be deadly within hours. Ask her doctor about the MenB vaccine too, plus checking that her HPV series is complete and getting this year's flu and COVID shots. Many colleges require proof of meningococcal vaccination, so check the school's requirements.
ok so my big toe joint suddenly went red, hot, swollen overnight and I can't even stand the bedsheet touching it

That is a textbook description of gout, which happens when uric acid crystals inflame the joint. An NSAID like naproxen can help if it's safe for you, along with ice, elevation, plenty of water and avoiding alcohol. See a doctor in the next day or two to confirm the diagnosis and get proper treatment. If you have a fever or feel unwell, get seen the same day, because an infected joint can look similar and needs urgent care.
Is it normal for my grandpa's ankles to swell up by the end of the day? He's 84.

Mild swelling that goes down overnight is common at his age, often from sitting a lot or weak leg veins. It can also be a sign of heart, kidney or liver problems, or a side effect of drugs like amlodipine, so mention it to his doctor. Get urgent care if one leg is suddenly swollen, red or painful, which can mean a blood clot, or if the swelling comes with shortness of breath.
Can I just take my friend's EpiPen if I start reacting? I don't have one yet.

In a true emergency, like trouble breathing, throat swelling or fainting after an exposure, using someone else's epinephrine auto-injector is far safer than waiting, and you should still call emergency services immediately afterward. It shouldn't be your plan, though. Expired or borrowed pens may not be there when you need them, so ask your doctor for your own prescription and carry two at all times.
Teen son has athlete's foot. Will it go away on its own if he just ignores it?

It rarely clears on its own and tends to spread to the toenails or groin, so treating it is worth it. An over-the-counter terbinafine or clotrimazole cream twice daily usually works. He should keep using it a week or two after it looks gone. Dry feet well, change socks daily, and wear shower sandals in locker rooms. See a doctor if it cracks open, gets red and swollen, or doesn't improve after two to four weeks.
Woke up with my lips and eyelids swelling and hives all over after eating at a new restaurant. Kind of hard to swallow?

Trouble swallowing with lip and eyelid swelling can be a severe allergic reaction, so call emergency services now. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector, use it immediately. Don't drive yourself, and don't wait to see if it improves, because these reactions can worsen quickly.
I've been thinking that everyone would be better off without me. I'm not going to do anything, I just think it a lot.

I'm really glad you said this out loud, because thinking that often is a sign you're carrying a lot more pain than anyone should carry alone, even if you have no plans to act on it. Please tell someone today, whether that's your doctor, a therapist, or a trusted person. In the US you can call or text 988 anytime just to talk it through, and if you're elsewhere, your local crisis line is there for exactly this. These thoughts usually ease with the right support, and the belief that people would be better off without you is the depression talking, not the truth.
chemical burn from oven cleaner on my hand, it's tingling

Rinse it right away under cool running water for at least 20 minutes, and take off any rings or contaminated clothing. Don't try to neutralize it with vinegar or anything else, because plain water is safest. Oven cleaners are often strong alkalis that keep damaging skin, so call poison control or get seen if pain, redness, or blistering continues after rinsing.
My kid has a rash all over his trunk, little red dots, he had a fever for 3 days that just broke. He's 14 months.

That pattern, a few days of high fever followed by a rash on the trunk once the fever breaks, sounds a lot like roseola, a common and usually harmless virus at this age. The rash typically fades in a few days and doesn't itch. It's still worth a quick call to his pediatrician to confirm, and get seen right away if the spots look like tiny bruises or don't blanch when you press a glass against them, or if he seems lethargic.
My 14 year old son complains his knees hurt below the kneecap, plays soccer 5 days a week. Normal growing pains?

Pain just below the kneecap in an active teen is very often Osgood-Schlatter disease, which is irritation where the patellar tendon attaches to the growing shinbone. It's common and not dangerous. It usually improves by cutting back activity when it flares, icing after training, and stretching the quads and hamstrings, and it settles once he's done growing. Have his doctor take a look to confirm it, especially if there's significant swelling, limping, pain at night, or pain in only one knee that's getting worse.
Been on a long flight, my ear is still blocked a day later. Annoying but whatever.

Try swallowing, yawning, or gently pinching your nose and blowing until you feel a pop, and a decongestant spray for a few days can help open the tube. Usually it clears within a few days. If it lasts more than a week, becomes painful, or comes with hearing loss, dizziness, or fluid, get it checked.
found ibuprofen that expired in 2021, still good?

It's almost certainly safe and probably still works, though it may have lost a bit of potency, so taking it for an ordinary headache is reasonable. Throw it out if it's crumbling, discolored or smells off. Be stricter with liquid antibiotics, insulin, nitroglycerin and EpiPens, which genuinely shouldn't be used past their date.
My 4 year old has had diarrhea since yesterday but she's still playing. Should I worry?

If she's playful and still drinking, this is most likely a stomach bug that will run its course in a few days. Your main job is keeping her hydrated with small, frequent sips of water or an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte, and she can keep eating her normal foods. Call her pediatrician if she stops peeing regularly, has a dry mouth or no tears, gets very sleepy, has blood in her stool, or runs a high fever. Also call if the diarrhea lasts more than a few days.
My teenager got hit in the mouth playing soccer and a front tooth came completely out. What do I do??

Act fast, because reimplanting the tooth within about 30 to 60 minutes gives it the best chance to survive. Pick it up by the crown rather than the root, rinse it briefly with milk or water if it's dirty without scrubbing, and gently push it back into the socket if you can, having your teen bite on a cloth to hold it. If that isn't possible, keep the tooth in milk or tucked inside their cheek, and get to an emergency dentist or ER right now.
cough wont go away, its been 5 weeks since my cold

A cough can linger a few weeks after a cold, but five weeks is long enough to get checked. Common causes include postnasal drip, reflux, asthma-like airway irritation, or occasionally whooping cough or pneumonia. Your doctor can sort out which it is, and the treatment is often simple. Go sooner if you're coughing up blood, losing weight, having night sweats, or getting short of breath.
