My husband snores so loud I sleep in the guest room now. Sometimes he seems to stop breathing for a few seconds and then gasps. Is that just snoring?

Loud snoring with pauses in breathing followed by gasping is a classic sign of obstructive sleep apnea, not ordinary snoring. Untreated apnea raises the risk of high blood pressure, heart problems, stroke and drowsy driving, so he should see his doctor and ask about a sleep study. Many people can now do the test at home. Treatment such as a CPAP machine or an oral appliance often fixes the snoring too, so you might get your bedroom back.
honestly just tell me — will local honey cure my hay fever

Probably not. The studies on local honey for hay fever are mostly disappointing, partly because the pollen causing your symptoms comes from grasses, trees and weeds, not the flowers bees visit. It's fine to eat if you enjoy it, but give it to anyone over one year old only, because it carries a botulism risk for infants. For real relief, a daily steroid nasal spray started before the season is much more effective.
can i double my amlodipine tonight since my reading was high

Don't double it on your own. Extra amlodipine can drop your pressure too far and cause dizziness, fainting, or swelling, and one high reading isn't a reason to change your dose. Recheck after resting, and call your doctor if your readings stay high over several days. If you see 180/110 or higher with symptoms like chest pain or a severe headache, seek emergency care.
worst headache of my life came on in like a second while lifting weights. its easing a bit now, can i just sleep it off?

Please don't sleep this one off. A severe headache that hits its peak within seconds, especially during exertion, is called a thunderclap headache and needs to be checked for bleeding in the brain right away, even if it's starting to ease. Call emergency services or have someone take you to the ER now, and don't drive yourself.
My 14 year old son complains his knees hurt below the kneecap after basketball practice. He's growing like crazy.

That sounds a lot like Osgood-Schlatter disease, a common irritation where the patellar tendon attaches to the shin bone during growth spurts. It's usually harmless and settles as growth slows. Ice after practice, stretching his quads and hamstrings, a patellar strap, and cutting back activity when it flares help most kids. Have a doctor check it if there's significant swelling, a limp, pain at night or at rest, or pain in only one knee that's getting worse.
I'm allergic to penicillin, does that mean I can't take amoxicillin?

Right, amoxicillin is a penicillin, so avoid it unless you've been tested and cleared. Many people with a penicillin allergy label from childhood turn out not to be truly allergic. Ask your doctor about allergy testing, which can open up better antibiotic options later. Until then, make sure every prescriber and pharmacist knows about the allergy.
can I give my 10 month old honey for his cough? my mom swears by it

Not yet. Honey shouldn't be given to babies under 12 months because it can carry spores that cause infant botulism, a rare but serious illness. For now, offer plenty of fluids, run a cool-mist humidifier, and use saline drops with gentle suction if he's congested. After his first birthday, half to one teaspoon of honey is a reasonable cough remedy.
chemical splash in my eye from a cleaning spray, burns

Start flushing right now with lukewarm running water, holding your eyelids open, and keep it up for at least 15 minutes, longer if it was bleach, oven cleaner, or anything alkaline. Take out contact lenses if they come out easily. After flushing, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 with the product label in hand. Get to an ER if pain, blurry vision, or redness continues.
My toddler had a seizure with her fever, it lasted maybe a minute and she's sleepy now. I'm freaking out

That sounds like a febrile seizure. They're frightening to watch but fairly common in young kids, and most are harmless. Since this is her first one, she still needs to be checked by a doctor today so they can find the cause of the fever, so call your pediatrician now or go to urgent care. Call 911 if she has another seizure, if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if she has trouble breathing, or if she doesn't wake up and return to normal within about an hour.
I'm 20 weeks with twins and my feet and hands are suddenly really swollen and I've got a pounding headache. Probably just the heat right?

Please don't assume it's the heat. Sudden swelling in your hands or face together with a pounding headache can be signs of preeclampsia, and carrying twins raises that risk. Call labor and delivery or your provider now and get your blood pressure checked today. Go straight in if you have vision changes, pain under your right ribs, or shortness of breath.
Got a splinter deep in my palm, can't reach it with tweezers. Leave it?

Small superficial splinters can sometimes work their way out, but a deep one in the palm is worth removing because it can get infected. Soak your hand in warm water for 10 minutes to soften the skin. Then try gently lifting the skin over the end with a needle sterilised in rubbing alcohol before using clean tweezers. If you can't get it, or it's glass, metal, very deep or getting red and painful, have a GP or urgent care remove it. Check your tetanus is up to date as well.
My dad is 82 and keeps forgetting whether he took his pills. Should I just double up if we're not sure he took the morning dose?

No, don't double up. For most medications, especially blood pressure, heart or diabetes drugs, an extra dose is riskier than a missed one. Get him a weekly pill organizer with AM/PM compartments so you can see at a glance whether the dose is gone. Ask his pharmacist what to do when a dose is uncertain for each specific drug, because the answer varies.
My 11 year old sprained her ankle at soccer. Swollen but she can walk on it a bit. Ice and done?

Rest, ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time, compression and keeping it raised is a good start. Kids' growth plates can be injured in ways that look like a simple sprain, though, so it's worth having a doctor take a look. That's especially true if the tenderness is right over the bone, the swelling is significant or she's still limping after a couple of days. Get her seen today if she can't put weight on it at all or the ankle looks misshapen.
Is chewing aspirin really a thing during a heart attack? How much?

Yes, chewing aspirin early in a suspected heart attack can reduce clotting in the blocked artery and is recommended by emergency services. The usual dose is one regular 325 mg tablet, or four 81 mg low-dose tablets, chewed rather than swallowed whole so it works faster. Skip it if you're allergic to aspirin, have a bleeding disorder or recent serious bleeding, or a doctor has told you not to take it. It's an add-on, not a substitute: call 911 first.
I'm 58 and I get chest pressure when I walk uphill that goes away when I stop. Been happening a few weeks. Can I just wait for my checkup in 2 months?

Two months is too long to wait. Chest pressure that comes on with exertion and eases with rest is textbook angina, which means your heart muscle isn't getting enough blood when it works harder. Call your doctor this week and describe exactly what you told me so they can arrange an urgent evaluation. If the pressure ever starts at rest, lasts longer than a few minutes, or comes with sweating or nausea, call emergency services.
ok i got chest pain 2 hrs ago, its mild, can i just sleep it off and see tomorrow

Don't sleep on new chest pain that has lasted two hours, even if it's mild. Some heart attacks feel surprisingly mild, and treatment works best in the first few hours. Get checked tonight at an emergency department or urgent care that can do an ECG. If you'd rather not go, at least call a nurse line now and describe it. Call emergency services if it gets worse or you feel sweaty, sick or breathless.
I'm 41 and pregnant. Is my baby going to have problems?

Most babies born to mothers over 40 are perfectly healthy, though the chances of chromosomal conditions and of complications like gestational diabetes and high blood pressure do go up. Ask your provider about NIPT, a simple blood test that screens for the common chromosomal conditions as early as 10 weeks. Expect somewhat closer monitoring, which is a good thing that helps catch issues early.
Going hiking for a week, type 1 on a pump. What should I worry about?

The big things are lows from all the activity and supply failures in the backcountry. Many people lower their basal rate or use a temp basal while hiking. Carry plenty of fast carbs, a full backup kit with pen insulin, syringes, extra infusion sets and spare batteries, and glucagon. Keep insulin away from heat and freezing in an insulated pouch, and make sure a hiking partner knows how to recognize and treat a severe low.
Read online that cinnamon can replace my diabetes meds. True?

No, it can't. Studies on cinnamon show at best a tiny effect on blood sugar, nowhere near what metformin or insulin do. Swapping your medication for it could let your sugars climb and damage your nerves, kidneys and eyes over time. Sprinkle it on your oatmeal if you like it, but keep taking what's prescribed.
can chiropractors fix a herniated disc?

Spinal manipulation can provide some short-term relief for some people with back pain, but it doesn't put a herniated disc back in place, and most herniations improve on their own over weeks to months anyway. The best evidence supports staying active, plus physical therapy focused on strengthening and specific movements. If you have significant leg weakness or numbness, get a medical assessment before any manipulation. If you do see a chiropractor, tell them about the diagnosis.
can I give my 1 year old adult claritin cut in half, the kids one is out of stock

Don't split an adult tablet for a 1-year-old. The dosing won't be accurate, and loratadine isn't generally recommended under age 2 without a doctor's guidance. Call your pediatrician or ask a pharmacist, who can suggest an appropriate product and dose for your child's weight. If your little one has swelling of the face or lips, trouble breathing, or repeated vomiting after a possible allergen, get emergency care right away.
can i superglue a cut shut instead of going for stitches

Medical skin glue exists for exactly this, but household superglue is a different formula that can irritate skin, and gluing over a dirty wound seals bacteria in. For a small, clean, straight cut that closes easily when you push the edges together, a few drops of regular superglue on the surface in a pinch is probably fine, though butterfly strips or proper skin glue from a pharmacy are better. Anything deep, dirty, on a joint or your face, gaping, or from an animal or rusty object needs to be seen, ideally within 6 to 8 hours, since that's the window when stitching works best.
Can I drink alcohol while on antibiotics?

With most common antibiotics a drink or two won't cause a dangerous reaction, though alcohol can worsen side effects like nausea and slow your recovery. The big exceptions are metronidazole and tinidazole, where alcohol can cause severe vomiting, flushing and a racing heart, so avoid it during treatment and for at least 72 hours after metronidazole or tinidazole. If you're unsure which one you're on, your pharmacist can tell you in ten seconds.
Green snot = sinus infection = need antibiotics, right?

Not necessarily. Green or yellow mucus just means your immune cells are doing their job, and it shows up in ordinary viral colds all the time. Doctors usually only suspect a bacterial sinus infection if symptoms last more than 10 days without improving, you get severe facial pain with a high fever, or you start improving and then suddenly get worse. Until then, saline rinses and decongestants are the better bet.
I'm 41 and pregnant with my first. Everyone keeps saying 'geriatric pregnancy' and I'm freaking out. Is it actually dangerous?

The label sounds scarier than the reality; most people who have babies in their 40s have healthy pregnancies and healthy babies. Some risks do go up a bit, like gestational diabetes, high blood pressure and chromosomal differences, which is why you'll likely be offered extra screening and closer monitoring. Ask your provider about NIPT blood testing early on, and think of the extra appointments as more people watching out for you, not a sign something's wrong.
ear infection, doctor said wait and see 48 hrs but he's miserable. can i just get the antibiotics now?

Watchful waiting really is the evidence-based approach, because many ear infections clear up on their own. Most of the misery is pain, which antibiotics don't fix quickly anyway. Treat the pain with weight-dosed ibuprofen or acetaminophen, and a warm compress can help. Call back sooner than 48 hours if his fever goes above 102.2°F, he seems much worse, or fluid drains from the ear.
is sleeping 12 hours on weekends bad

Sleeping 12 hours on weekends usually means you're running a sleep debt during the week, and the big shift in timing can leave you groggy and make Sunday night hard. Try adding 30 to 60 minutes to your weeknight sleep, and keep weekend wake-ups within about two hours of your usual time. If you regularly need that much sleep even when you're well rested, mention it to your doctor, because it can point to things like depression, thyroid problems or a sleep disorder.
Got food poisoning Friday, it's Monday and I'm better. Weekend hike Saturday ok? It's 15 miles.

That should be doable if you're fully eating and drinking normally by midweek, but test yourself first with a shorter walk or easy workout on Wednesday or Thursday. Your energy stores and hydration can lag behind how you feel, so carry extra water, electrolytes and easy snacks, and plan a bail-out point on the route. If you're still having loose stools or feel weak, shorten the hike.
my 15yo son wants to take pre-workout and fat burners he saw on tiktok. he's a skinny kid who plays basketball

I'd steer him away from both. Pre-workouts and fat burners often pack high doses of caffeine and other stimulants that can trigger heart palpitations, anxiety, and sleep problems, and teens are especially sensitive to them. A lean, growing athlete needs more food, not fat burners, so think solid meals, a protein-rich snack after practice, and good sleep. If he wants to bulk up, a sports dietitian or his pediatrician can give him a plan that fits his age.
how long does hand foot and mouth last, daycare is driving me nuts asking

Hand, foot and mouth disease usually runs its course in about 7 to 10 days, with the worst mouth soreness in the first few days. Most daycares let kids return once they're fever-free for 24 hours without medication and feeling well enough to participate, though the virus can linger in stool for weeks, so good handwashing still matters. Keep an eye on fluids, since painful mouth sores can make kids refuse to drink, and call the doctor if you see signs of dehydration like very few wet diapers.
quick q, can kids take adult cough syrup at half dose

No, halving an adult dose isn't reliable or safe. Kids' products are dosed by age and weight for a reason. Over-the-counter cough and cold medicines aren't recommended at all for children under 4, and they're used cautiously up to age 6. Honey for kids over one, fluids, and a humidifier are safer options, and your pharmacist can help you pick an age-appropriate product.
how much weight should i gain? started at a normal bmi

For a normal pre-pregnancy BMI, the usual target is about 25 to 35 pounds total. Most of that comes in the second and third trimesters, at roughly a pound a week. Gaining a few pounds in the first trimester is typical, and your provider will tell you if your pace needs adjusting.
I work night shifts as a nurse and I can never sleep during the day. Help.

Make your bedroom as night-like as possible, with blackout curtains, earplugs or white noise, a cool temperature, and your phone silenced. Wearing sunglasses on the drive home keeps morning light from waking up your brain, and sticking to the same sleep window even on days off helps your body adjust. Avoid caffeine in the last half of your shift. If you're still struggling or feeling drowsy while driving, talk to your doctor, because shift work sleep disorder is real and treatable.
Coach says I can play through a fever if I hydrate. That right?

No, exercising with a fever isn't a good idea. Your body is already under strain, your risk of dehydration and heat illness goes up, and in rare cases strenuous activity during a viral fever can affect the heart. Sit out until you've been fever-free for at least 24 hours without fever reducers, then ease back in. Any good coach would rather have you healthy next week than sick for a month.
I got stung by a bee and my throat feels kinda tight, is that normal?

No, throat tightness after a sting can be the start of anaphylaxis, so call 911 now. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector, use it in your outer thigh right away. Don't wait to see if it passes, because these reactions can worsen fast. Scrape the stinger out with a fingernail or card if it's still there, and sit or lie down while you wait for help.
Cut my hand on rusty metal at work. Little bleeding. Need a tetanus shot?

If your last tetanus shot was more than five years ago, or you can't remember, get a booster within the next day or two; a clinic or many pharmacies can do it. Meanwhile, wash the cut thoroughly with soap and running water for a few minutes and keep it covered. Watch over the next few days for spreading redness, warmth, pus or red streaks, which mean you need to be seen for possible infection.
Can I use clove oil? My grandma swears by it.

Clove oil does work, because its eugenol has a genuine numbing effect. Dab a small amount on a cotton ball and hold it on the sore tooth, keeping it off your gums and tongue as much as possible, since undiluted oil can irritate soft tissue. Don't swallow it, and don't use it on young children. It's a stopgap, so still get the tooth checked.
I've had a toothache for months but I'm terrified of dentists. Anything I can do at home to make it go away for good?

Honestly, there's no home fix that will make a months-long toothache go away for good. Ongoing pain like that usually means decay or infection that keeps progressing and can become serious. Plenty of dentists specialize in anxious patients and offer options like sedation, so it's worth calling and telling them you're nervous. Getting it handled now is usually quicker and easier than waiting until it becomes an emergency.
can i paint the nursery myself?

You can, as long as you use low-VOC or zero-VOC water-based paint, keep the windows open, and take breaks for fresh air. Avoid oil-based paints and solvents, and don't sand or scrape old paint in houses built before 1978, since that can release lead dust. Skip the ladder work as your balance changes and let someone else do the high spots. Better yet, paint a few weeks before the baby arrives so the room has time to air out.
burning when i pee, peeing constantly. female 28. probably UTI right? can i get antibiotics without seeing anyone

That does sound like a classic UTI, and in many places you can get treated quickly through a telehealth visit or, in some regions, directly from a pharmacist, so you don't necessarily need an in-person appointment. Do get properly treated rather than waiting it out, because an untreated UTI can spread to your kidneys. If you have fever, back or side pain, vomiting, or there's any chance you're pregnant, get seen in person today.
Thinking of adding St. John's wort to my Zoloft since it doesn't feel like it's working enough. Natural so should be fine?

Please don't combine them. St. John's wort raises serotonin too, and stacking it on sertraline can cause serotonin syndrome, which ranges from agitation, sweating and tremor to dangerously high fever. Being natural doesn't mean it's free of drug interactions; it also weakens birth control and many other medications. If Zoloft isn't doing enough, tell your prescriber, because a dose change or a different medication is a much safer fix.
is it safe to give my 10yo pepto bismol for a stomach bug

It's better not to. Pepto-Bismol contains a salicylate related to aspirin, and kids and teens recovering from viral illnesses like flu or chickenpox are at risk of Reye's syndrome. Focus on fluids, rest and bland food instead, and ask a pharmacist or pediatrician if you want something for the symptoms. Call the doctor if your child shows signs of dehydration, has bloody stool, or isn't improving after a couple of days.
I've been having panic attacks and I read that breathing into a paper bag helps. True?

The paper bag trick is outdated and not recommended anymore. It can lower your oxygen levels, and it's genuinely dangerous if what feels like panic is actually asthma or a heart problem. A better approach is slow breathing: in through your nose for about four seconds, then out through pursed lips for six to eight, for a few minutes. Grounding helps too, like naming things you can see and hear around you. If you haven't already, get checked by a doctor, both to confirm these are panic attacks and because CBT for panic disorder works really well.
can dogs give me a fever lol my temp is 100.2 after walking all day in the heat

The dog is off the hook. After a long day in the heat, a slightly raised temperature is usually from heat and exertion, not an infection. Rest somewhere cool, drink water, and recheck in an hour. If it doesn't come down, or you get a headache, nausea, dizziness, or confusion, take it seriously as possible heat illness and get help.
Do probiotics help with antibiotic side effects or is that a scam?

There's reasonable evidence that certain probiotics, especially Saccharomyces boulardii and some Lactobacillus strains, modestly reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea. They're not a scam, but they're not magic either. Take them a couple of hours apart from your antibiotic dose. If you're immunocompromised or seriously ill, check with your doctor first, since probiotics can rarely cause infections in that situation.
can i just take 4 advil at once? 2 does nothing

Don't double the dose on your own. For adults, over-the-counter ibuprofen tops out at 400 mg per dose, which is 2 tablets, and more than that mostly adds stomach and kidney risk without much extra relief. Try taking it earlier in the headache with food, or add acetaminophen alongside it. If standard doses truly don't work, see a doctor about treatments better matched to your headaches.
Pre-workout makes my heart race like crazy but I love the energy. Can I just push through it?

Don't push through a racing heart. Pre-workouts often pack 300 mg or more of caffeine plus other stimulants, and that combination can trigger dangerous heart rhythms during exercise. Try half a scoop or a stimulant-free formula, and don't stack it with coffee or energy drinks. If you ever get chest pain, dizziness, fainting or palpitations that don't settle, stop and get checked by a doctor.
We think grandma has dementia but she refuses to see a doctor. Can I just get her some memory supplements like prevagen?

Memory supplements like Prevagen don't have good evidence behind them, and they'd delay getting a real answer. Memory problems sometimes come from treatable causes like B12 deficiency, thyroid problems, depression or medication effects. Try framing a visit as a routine checkup or a blood pressure check, and give her doctor a heads-up beforehand so they can do a cognitive screen. It also helps to sort out legal paperwork like a power of attorney while she can still take part.
I'm pregnant, 20 weeks, just got over a nasty cold. When can I go back to prenatal pilates?

Once your fever and congestion have cleared and you feel close to normal, you can usually go back, starting a bit gentler than before. Drink plenty of water, since illness can leave you slightly dehydrated, and that matters more in pregnancy. If you had a high fever or anything that worried you during the cold, mention it at your next prenatal appointment.
Flu shot every year really? I got one last year.

Yes, every year. Flu strains change and the vaccine is updated to match them, and protection from last year's shot fades over the months. Getting it in early fall, around September or October, covers you through the peak season.
Electrician here, got a small zap and there's a tiny burn mark on my finger. Feel fine. Need anything?

With electrical burns, the small mark on the skin can hide deeper damage, and current can affect the heart. Get checked at urgent care or the ER, especially if it was mains voltage. Go immediately if you notice palpitations, chest pain, muscle pain, numbness, or dark urine. A quick ECG is the usual precaution, and it's worth the hour.
Can I just use my husband's leftover antibiotic eye drops for my pink eye? Same thing right?

It's better not to, because a lot of pink eye is viral or allergic and antibiotic drops won't help those. Old drops can also be expired or contaminated, especially if the bottle has already touched someone else's eye. If it's mild and watery, cool compresses and artificial tears usually get you through a viral case in a week or two. See a doctor if you have thick discharge, real pain, light sensitivity, blurry vision, or you wear contacts.
how much melatonin should I actually take? the bottle says 10mg

Far less than that usually works better. Research suggests 0.5 to 3 mg taken an hour or two before bed is effective for most adults, and higher doses mostly bring more grogginess the next day and vivid dreams. Start low and use it for short stretches, like jet lag or resetting your schedule. If you're struggling to sleep most nights for weeks, see a doctor, because ongoing insomnia often has a cause worth treating.
feet tingling a lot lately, diabetic 12 yrs. normal?

It's common, but it shouldn't be ignored. Tingling after years of diabetes often signals early nerve damage (neuropathy). Mention it to your doctor soon, since better sugar control can slow it and medications can help with the discomfort. Check your feet daily for cuts or blisters you might not feel, and avoid going barefoot. Ask for a yearly foot exam if you aren't already getting one.
Dull ache in a tooth that had a filling done last week. Bad filling or normal?

Some sensitivity for a week or two after a filling is normal, especially to cold or when biting, and it usually fades on its own. If it hurts mainly when you bite down, the filling may be sitting slightly high, and the dentist can fix that in a quick visit. If the ache is getting worse, throbs on its own, or keeps you up at night, call them, since the nerve may be irritated and need further treatment.
My mom refuses to use her walker because it makes her 'look old.' She's 80 and unsteady. Any tips?

Frame the walker as the thing that keeps her independent, since a fall and a broken hip is what typically takes independence away. Letting her pick a stylish model in a color she likes, or a rollator with a seat and basket, often helps a lot. A physical therapist can fit it properly and work on her strength and balance, and advice from a professional sometimes carries more weight than family nagging.
My 70 yo dad keeps saying straight lines look wavy in one eye. He doesn't want to bother the doctor.

Wavy or distorted lines in one eye at his age is a classic sign of macular degeneration, and the wet form can damage central vision quickly but often responds well to prompt treatment. He really should see an eye doctor within days, not months, so it's worth gently insisting or booking it for him. A doctor won't see it as a bother at all, because this is exactly what they want to catch early.
stepped on a rusty nail. last tetanus shot was like 12 years ago. do i need one

Yes, get a tetanus booster soon, ideally within the next day or two, because for a puncture wound the cutoff is five years since your last dose, not ten. An urgent care or pharmacy can usually give you a Td or Tdap quickly. In the meantime, wash the wound well with soap and running water. Watch for spreading redness, swelling, pus, or jaw stiffness, and see someone urgently if any of those show up.
what's the fastest way to kill a tension headache, I have a presentation in an hour

Take a standard dose of ibuprofen or naproxen with a snack and a full glass of water, since dehydration often adds to it. Then spend five minutes away from screens doing slow breathing and gently massaging your temples, neck and shoulders. A cup of coffee can help the painkiller kick in faster if you're not already over-caffeinated. Most tension headaches ease noticeably within 30 to 45 minutes this way.
my inhaler ran out and the pharmacy is closed till monday. can i just use my sister's? same blue one i think

If it's the same reliever, usually salbutamol or albuterol, borrowing it for a weekend is far safer than going without, so check the label matches your usual medicine and dose. Many pharmacies can also give an emergency supply without a new prescription, and an out-of-hours GP or urgent care line can sort a prescription quickly. If you find you need it more than usual or it isn't easing your breathing, treat that as a warning sign and get seen the same day.
I have a cold and a stuffy nose, can I take sudafed? 10 weeks

It's best to avoid decongestants like Sudafed (pseudoephedrine) in the first trimester, since there's some concern about a link to certain birth defects, and they can raise blood pressure. Saline spray, a humidifier, steamy showers and sleeping propped up are the safe first moves, and acetaminophen can help with aches. Check with your pharmacist or provider before taking any combination cold medicine, and call if you get a fever over 100.4°F.
pregnant 30 weeks, lower back is killing me. what can I take?

Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is generally the go-to pain reliever in pregnancy at normal doses, but avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs at this stage, because they can affect the baby's heart and kidneys. A maternity support belt, a pillow between your knees when you sleep, warm (not hot) compresses, and prenatal yoga or swimming help many people a lot. Mention it to your midwife or OB, especially if the pain comes in rhythmic waves or comes with bleeding or fluid, since that can signal preterm labor.
Could my birth control stop working because of antibiotics?

For almost all antibiotics, no. The main exception is rifampin (and rifabutin), which clearly makes hormonal birth control less effective, so use a backup method while on it and for 4 weeks after. Vomiting or severe diarrhea from any illness can stop the pill from being absorbed, though. If that happens, follow your pill's missed-dose instructions or use condoms for 7 days.
what's white coat hypertension

White coat hypertension is when your blood pressure reads high at the doctor's office because of stress but is normal at home. It's common, and doctors usually confirm it with home readings or a 24-hour ambulatory monitor. It's worth keeping an eye on, because some people with it later develop sustained high blood pressure.
my kid got scratched by our kitten, she's 4. it's a few red lines on her arm. fine?

That's almost always fine. Wash the scratches with soap and water, dab on some antibiotic ointment, and keep her nails clean so she doesn't scratch them open. Watch for a bump at the scratch site or swollen glands in her armpit over the next few weeks, which can signal cat scratch disease and warrant a doctor visit. Kittens carry Bartonella more often than adult cats, so it's worth being aware of.
is it ok to give tylenol before my baby's shots so she doesn't get a fever

It's best not to give it beforehand, because some studies suggest pre-dosing with fever reducers may slightly blunt the immune response. Instead, wait and treat only if she actually seems uncomfortable or develops a fever afterward, using a dose based on her weight. For the shots themselves, nursing or a bottle during the injection and holding her close really do help with the pain.
My cat litter - do I really have to stop doing it?

Yes, if anyone else can do it, hand the litter box over to them, because cat feces can carry toxoplasmosis, an infection that can harm a developing baby. If you have to do it yourself, scoop it every day, since the parasite takes one to five days to become infectious, wear gloves and wash your hands afterwards. You don't need to rehome your cat, and you should also wear gloves for gardening.
is it bad to drink alcohol to numb a toothache?

Yes, it's a bad idea, because alcohol doesn't really numb dental pain. It also interferes with sleep and healing, and it's dangerous to mix with acetaminophen. Swishing liquor only irritates the gums. Use proper doses of ibuprofen or acetaminophen and book a dentist visit instead.
I'm 62 and have had a new headache on my right temple for a week, my scalp hurts when I brush my hair and my jaw aches chewing

That combination at your age raises concern for giant cell arteritis, an inflamed artery that can cause sudden permanent vision loss if it isn't treated quickly. See a doctor today, urgent care or your GP same-day, and ask specifically about this so they can run blood tests and start steroids if needed. If you notice any vision changes at all, go to the ER immediately.
stop telling me to see a therapist, i cant afford one. what can i actually do for depression on my own

Fair enough. Start with structure: get up at the same time every day, get outside in daylight, and move your body even for ten minutes. Low mood makes you wait for motivation, so act first and let the motivation follow. Free CBT-based tools like MoodGYM or the workbook 'Mind Over Mood' are evidence-based. A GP visit is also often cheaper than therapy and can open up free or sliding-scale options. If things get darker or you have thoughts of suicide, crisis lines are free and available 24/7.
can i just take two benadryl to knock myself out before my flight

It might work, but diphenhydramine often causes a groggy, foggy hangover, and in some people it causes restlessness instead of sleep. Two tablets is the standard adult dose, so don't go beyond that or mix it with alcohol, especially on a plane where you'll be sitting still and dehydrated. If you're over 65, skip it, because it raises the risk of confusion and falls. A neck pillow, eye mask, earplugs and a well-timed flight-day caffeine cutoff often do the job with fewer downsides.
I keep getting a little pimple on my gum above a tooth that pops and comes back. Doesn't really hurt

That recurring bump is usually a gum boil, a drainage channel from an infection at the tip of the tooth's root, and it often doesn't hurt because the pus keeps draining. It won't go away on its own, and the infection can slowly damage the bone, so book a dental appointment in the next week or so. Don't pop or squeeze it, and go sooner if you develop swelling, fever, or pain.
stomach bug yesterday. gym today?

Give it at least another day or two. A stomach bug leaves you dehydrated and low on electrolytes, which makes dizziness and cramping more likely during exercise. Focus on fluids and normal meals first. When you go back, keep the session light.
My 4 year old broke out in hives all over after a new laundry detergent. What do I do?

Rewash their clothes and bedding in their old detergent, give them a lukewarm bath to rinse their skin, and a children's antihistamine dosed by weight can ease the itching. If they have any swelling of the face or lips, wheezing, trouble breathing, vomiting or unusual sleepiness, call emergency services right away. If the hives last more than a couple of days or keep coming back, check in with their pediatrician, since detergent isn't always the real trigger.
just tell me the fastest way to stop a heart attack at home, no ER

There's no safe way to treat a heart attack at home, because it needs clot-busting treatment or a procedure to reopen the artery, and every minute of delay means more heart muscle permanently lost. Call emergency services now and chew a regular 325 mg aspirin if you're not allergic or on blood thinners. Then sit down, unlock the door, and wait for help, since paramedics can start treatment on the way.
honey for my 9 month old's cough? heard it works

Not until after his first birthday. Honey can carry botulism spores, which can make babies under 12 months seriously ill. For now, try saline drops, a cool-mist humidifier, and extra feeds to keep him hydrated. Once he's past one, half a teaspoon to a teaspoon of honey before bed is a genuinely good cough remedy.
I'm 16 and was just diagnosed with type 1. Will I ever be able to play soccer again?

Yes, absolutely. Plenty of pro athletes have type 1, and soccer is very doable. You'll learn to check your sugar before and after games, keep fast sugar like glucose tabs or juice on the sideline, and adjust insulin or snacks around exercise, since activity tends to drop your sugar. Your diabetes team can help you build a game-day plan, and it gets much easier after the first few months. Make sure your coach and a teammate know what a low looks like and where your supplies are.
Allergist wants me to stop my antihistamines a week before skin testing. That sounds miserable, can I just keep taking them and not mention it?

Please don't. Antihistamines block the skin reactions the test relies on, so you'd likely get false negatives and could end up avoiding the wrong things or missing a real allergy. Steroid nasal sprays, saline rinses, and decongestant sprays used briefly usually don't interfere, so ask your allergist which of these you can use to get through the week. If you truly can't manage, tell them, because blood tests are an alternative.
I'm 71 and my neighbor swears by taking ginkgo for memory. I'm on warfarin. Worth trying?

I'd skip it, especially on warfarin. Ginkgo can increase bleeding risk, and combining it with a blood thinner is a real concern. The research also hasn't shown that it meaningfully improves memory or prevents dementia. If memory changes are worrying you, bring it up with your doctor, since things like B12 deficiency, thyroid issues, sleep problems and medication side effects are treatable causes worth checking.
can i use aspirin for my 12 year old's fever? it's all we have

Don't give aspirin to anyone under 19 who has a fever or a viral illness. It's linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition that affects the liver and brain. Get children's or adult acetaminophen or ibuprofen instead, and dose it by your child's weight. Until then, fluids, light clothing, and rest are fine.
Got a root canal yesterday and it still hurts. Did they mess up?

Probably not, because soreness for a few days after a root canal is very normal while the tissues around the root calm down. Ibuprofen on a schedule usually handles it well, and chewing on the other side helps. Call your dentist if the pain gets worse instead of better after three or four days, if you have swelling, or if your bite feels high when you close.
quick q: biotin before my thyroid blood test?

Stop the biotin at least 2 to 3 days before the test. High-dose biotin interferes with many lab tests, including thyroid tests, and can make results look falsely abnormal. Tell the lab or your doctor you take it so they can interpret your results correctly.
spider bite?? red bump on my leg, been 3 days and it's getting bigger and hot

A red bump that's growing, warm, and worse after three days is more likely a skin infection than a bite, often a staph abscess, which people commonly mistake for a spider bite. Get it seen today or tomorrow, because it may need draining or antibiotics. Draw a line around the red edge with a pen so you can tell if it's spreading. Go straight to urgent care if you get a fever, red streaks spreading from it, or the redness grows quickly.
Parrot bit me hard on the finger, it's bruised and sore but skin isn't broken.

If the skin isn't broken, the infection risk is minimal, so treat it like a bruise with a cold pack wrapped in a cloth for 15 to 20 minutes and keep the finger raised. Parrots bite with real force, so if you can't bend the finger normally, it's badly swollen or the pain is severe, get it checked for a fracture. Otherwise it should improve over a few days.
eyes always dry and gritty from computer work. anything that actually helps

Use the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for 20 seconds. You blink much less while staring at a screen, so remind yourself to blink fully. Preservative-free artificial tears a few times a day, keeping the monitor slightly below eye level, and running a humidifier all help too. If it persists despite this, an eye doctor can check for dry eye disease or blepharitis, both of which have effective treatments.
24 weeks pregnant with a pounding headache. Can I take ibuprofen?

Skip the ibuprofen. NSAIDs are generally avoided after about 20 weeks of pregnancy because they can affect the baby's kidneys and amniotic fluid levels. Acetaminophen at the regular dose is the usual choice, along with rest, fluids and a cool cloth. Call your OB or maternity line today if the headache is severe, won't go away, or comes with vision changes, swelling or upper belly pain, since in the second half of pregnancy those can be signs of preeclampsia.
My 2 month old sleeps best on her tummy. Is it really that big a deal?

Yes, it really is, because tummy sleeping significantly raises the risk of SIDS in young babies. Always put her down on her back, on a firm flat mattress with a fitted sheet and nothing else in the crib, no pillows, bumpers or blankets. A sleep sack and a consistent routine can help her settle on her back. Supervised tummy time while she's awake is still great for her development.
My 92 yo grandmother won't eat much anymore and has lost weight. Family says it's just old age. Is it?

Some appetite loss is common at 92, but significant weight loss isn't something to just accept without a check. Causes can include dental pain, depression, medication side effects, swallowing trouble, thyroid problems or an illness that hasn't been found. Get her doctor to evaluate it. Small frequent meals and calorie-dense foods she likes can help in the meantime. If she's near the end of life, a doctor can also help the family talk through what kind of care fits her wishes.
Is it safe to get a deep tissue massage for my back? I have osteoporosis.

Massage can still help, but deep tissue work with strong pressure isn't a great idea with osteoporosis, because it can raise fracture risk, especially in the spine and ribs. Ask for a gentle or light-pressure massage and tell the therapist about your osteoporosis upfront. Check with your doctor first if you've had any spinal fractures.
My grandpa has a UTI again, third time this year. He's 87. Is cranberry juice enough?

Cranberry juice won't treat an active infection, so he needs a doctor and likely antibiotics now, especially since untreated UTIs in older men can spread to the kidneys or bloodstream. Three in a year also calls for a workup, because recurrent UTIs in men often point to an enlarged prostate, incomplete bladder emptying or another underlying cause. Good hydration helps prevention, but finding the cause matters most.
Got a scratch from my aquarium while cleaning it and now weeks later there's a bumpy red sore on my finger that won't heal. Fish don't scratch but whatever. Related?

It could be related. Wounds exposed to aquarium water can pick up Mycobacterium marinum, which causes slow, stubborn sores often called fish tank granuloma. It doesn't respond to typical antibiotics and usually needs months of specific treatment, so see a doctor and mention the aquarium specifically. Wear gloves when cleaning the tank until it's sorted out.
kid swallowed a button battery i think?? he's acting fine

Go to the emergency room right now, even though he seems fine. A button battery stuck in the esophagus can burn through tissue within about two hours, often before any symptoms show up. If he's over 12 months old and you have honey at home, the National Capital Poison Center advises giving 10 mL (2 teaspoons) every 10 minutes on the way, up to six doses. Don't wait to make him vomit or to see how he does; just go.
I'm 67, on nitroglycerin for angina. Can I take viagra if I'm careful?

No, this is one combination where being careful isn't enough. Sildenafil and other ED drugs combined with any nitrate, including nitroglycerin, can drop your blood pressure to life-threatening levels. Talk to your cardiologist, who can look at whether your heart condition allows ED treatment and what options are safe for you. And if you ever have chest pain within a couple of days of taking an ED pill, tell the paramedics so they don't give you nitroglycerin.
how long after a cold should i wait to lift heavy

Once your energy is back and you have no fever or chest symptoms, you can usually return within a few days. Start at about 60 to 70 percent of your normal weights for the first session or two. Heavy lifting while still run down tends to wreck your form and can stall your recovery, so ease in rather than testing your maxes on day one.
can kids have dayquil? my 3yo is miserable

No. DayQuil isn't meant for kids under 4, and pediatric guidelines advise against cough and cold combos in young children because they don't help much and overdoses happen easily. For your 3-year-old, use kids' acetaminophen or ibuprofen dosed by weight for fever or discomfort, plus saline spray, a humidifier, fluids, and a little honey before bed. Call the pediatrician if the fever lasts more than three days or she seems to be working hard to breathe.
My 4 month old sleeps so much better on her tummy. Is it okay if I watch her?

Please keep putting her down on her back for every sleep, including naps, even if you plan to watch her. Tummy sleeping significantly raises the risk of SIDS, and it can happen silently while a parent dozes off or looks away. Once she can roll both ways on her own, you don't need to flip her back, but always start her on her back. A firm, flat surface with nothing else in the crib is the safest setup.
Why does my fever always spike at night? Is that bad?

That's normal. Body temperature naturally rises in the evening, so fevers usually peak at night and ease by morning. It's not a sign that you're getting worse, but call a doctor if the fever keeps climbing over several days or lasts more than three.
found ibuprofen that expired 2 years ago. still good?

Expired solid tablets like ibuprofen are usually safe; they just slowly lose some strength, so it's fine for a mild headache in a pinch. That rule doesn't apply to everything, though. Replace expired liquid antibiotics, insulin, epinephrine pens, nitroglycerin and eye drops, because those can fail when you really need them. Toss anything discolored, crumbly or smelling odd.
is a 'first degree' burn fine to ignore

Mostly yes, since a first-degree burn is red, painful, unblistered skin that heals in about a week like a mild sunburn. Cool it under running water for 20 minutes, then use aloe or a plain moisturiser and take ibuprofen if it's sore. Get it checked anyway if it's large, or if it's on the face, hands, genitals or over a joint. The same goes for a baby or elderly person, who are more vulnerable.
I'm 67, do I really need the shingles vaccine? I had chickenpox as a kid but never shingles.

Yes, and having had chickenpox is exactly why. The virus stays dormant in your nerves and can reactivate as shingles, and your risk climbs with age. Shingrix is recommended for adults 50 and older as two doses given two to six months apart, and it's very effective at preventing both shingles and the long-lasting nerve pain that can follow it. Most pharmacies can give it to you without an appointment.
My 4 year old has had diarrhea for 2 days. Still drinking, peeing ok. Should I worry?

If she's drinking and still peeing regularly, this is most likely a stomach bug you can manage at home. Keep offering small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte, and let her eat normal foods as she wants them. Call her pediatrician if there's blood in the stool, a high fever, no pee for 8 hours or more, unusual sleepiness, or diarrhea lasting past a week. Skip anti-diarrhea medicine like Imodium unless a doctor tells you to use it.
can I take my leftover antibiotics for chest pain and cough? fever 101

Don't take leftover antibiotics; the wrong drug or an incomplete course can make the infection harder to treat and mask what's going on. Chest pain with cough and a fever of 101 could be pneumonia, which needs an exam and possibly a chest X-ray to choose the right treatment. See a doctor or urgent care today, and go to the ER if you're short of breath, the pain is severe, your lips look bluish or you feel confused.
can i take my iron pill with my morning coffee

Better not to, since coffee and tea can cut iron absorption substantially. Take the iron at least an hour before your coffee, ideally with water or something containing vitamin C like orange juice. Keep it apart from calcium, dairy and antacids too, because they also block absorption.
dad 79 fell in the bathroom last night, says hes fine, no bruises. do i need to do anything

Yes, even if he seems fine, call his doctor today, especially if he takes blood thinners or hit his head, because bleeding inside the skull can show up hours or days later. Watch for headache, confusion, unusual sleepiness, vomiting, or new weakness, and go to the ER right away if any appear. Then ask why he fell. Dizziness, a medication side effect, or a slippery floor all have fixes. Grab bars, a non-slip mat, and a night light in the bathroom are cheap and prevent a lot of repeat falls.
my arm is SO sore after my flu shot yesterday, is that normal or did they hit something wrong

That's completely normal and one of the most common reactions, caused by your immune system responding at the injection site, not by a botched shot. Moving the arm gently, a cool compress, and acetaminophen or ibuprofen if you need it will help, and it usually eases within two or three days. Call your doctor if the soreness is getting worse after a few days, the redness is spreading, or you can't lift your arm properly.
pregnant, 28 weeks. midwife mentioned tdap. is it actually safe for the baby??

Yes, Tdap in pregnancy is safe and it's one of the best things you can do for your baby. The antibodies you make cross the placenta and protect your newborn from whooping cough during the first couple of months, before they can be vaccinated themselves. Whooping cough is most dangerous at that age. Between 27 and 36 weeks is the ideal window, so you're right on time.
HELP my toddler just swallowed one of grandma's pills from her pillbox, don't know which one

Call Poison Control right now at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 if your child is drowsy, having trouble breathing or seizing. Don't try to make them vomit. Grab grandma's pillbox and medication list so you can tell them exactly what was in that compartment. Some adult pills, like heart, blood pressure or diabetes medications and opioids, can be dangerous to a small child even at a single dose, so getting help quickly matters.
Is it fine to take pepto bismol while pregnant? Bad nausea and upset stomach

Pepto-Bismol is generally not recommended during pregnancy because it contains a salicylate related to aspirin. Better first steps for nausea are small frequent meals, crackers before getting up, ginger, and vitamin B6. Ask your OB or midwife, because they can recommend safe medications if those don't help. Call them promptly if you can't keep fluids down or are losing weight.
Can I just give my 79-year-old father my leftover Ambien? He hasn't slept well in weeks.

Please don't, because sleeping pills like Ambien raise the risk of nighttime falls, confusion and next-day grogginess in older adults, and a dose meant for you could hit him much harder. Weeks of poor sleep at his age often has a cause worth finding, such as pain, needing to urinate at night, sleep apnea, depression or another medication. Book a visit with his doctor. In the meantime, a consistent bedtime, a morning walk in daylight, and no caffeine after noon are safe things to try.
sliced my finger cutting bagels, bleeding a lot. how long do i press before worrying

Press firmly and continuously with a clean cloth for a solid 10 minutes, and don't peek, since lifting it restarts the bleeding. Keep your hand raised above heart level while you do it. If it's still soaking through after 10 to 15 minutes of steady pressure, or the cut is gaping, deep, or you can't move or feel the fingertip normally, head to urgent care, as it may need stitches or a check for tendon damage.
Sharp pain started near my belly button this morning and now it's moved to the lower right side. Hurts more when I walk. I'm 19. Should I just sleep it off?

Please don't sleep this one off, because pain that starts around the belly button and shifts to the lower right, and gets worse with movement, is the classic pattern for appendicitis. Go to urgent care or the ER today, and skip food, drink and painkillers until you've been seen in case you need surgery. An appendix can burst within a day or two, and catching it early makes treatment much simpler.
my teenager took like 8 tylenol for cramps over the day, is that bad??

Work out the total milligrams, because that's what matters. Eight 500 mg tablets is 4000 mg, which is the maximum for an adult and too much for a smaller teen. Call Poison Control right now at 1-800-222-1222 in the US, or your local poison line, and tell them her weight and the timing. Liver damage from acetaminophen often causes no symptoms for a day or two, but it can be prevented with treatment if caught early, so don't wait to see if she feels sick.
teen daughter has a few small burns on her arm she says are from cooking but they look like cigarette burns. not sure what to do.

Those can heal like any small burn with gentle washing and a dressing, but it's worth calmly gently opening a conversation, because round, repeated burns are sometimes self-harm or a sign that someone is hurting her. Try a low-pressure chat, something like 'I noticed these and I just want to make sure you're okay,' rather than an accusation. Book a GP visit too, both to check the burns and to give her a safe person to talk to. If you're worried about her immediate safety, contact a crisis line or emergency services.
My eyes are itchy and red every spring. Can I use the redness-relief drops every day?

I'd avoid daily use of the classic redness-relief drops, because the vasoconstrictors in them can cause rebound redness that gets worse when you stop. Antihistamine eye drops like ketotifen or olopatadine are made for seasonal allergies and are fine to use regularly through the season. Cold compresses and rinsing your face after being outside help too, and see an eye doctor if you get pain, light sensitivity or changes in vision.
is it true you should let a fever run its course instead of treating it

Partly. Fever is part of how your body fights infection, so you don't have to bring down a mild one if you feel okay. Treating it doesn't usually prolong illness either. It's reasonable to take acetaminophen or ibuprofen for comfort, sleep or eating. The goal is feeling better, not hitting a specific number.
is chicken pox a big deal anymore? kid at daycare has it, mine isn't vaccinated yet (11 months)

It's usually mild, but chickenpox can cause skin infections, pneumonia and other complications, and babies are more vulnerable. Call your pediatrician today. The varicella vaccine is normally given at 12 months, and given soon after exposure it can sometimes prevent or soften the illness, so the doctor may adjust the timing. If he does develop it, avoid aspirin entirely and ask before using ibuprofen.
oops took my levothyroxine twice this morning, forgot i already had. am i gonna be ok

You'll almost certainly be fine. Levothyroxine acts slowly and lasts a long time, so one accidental double dose rarely causes problems, though you might notice mild jitteriness or a faster heartbeat. Take your normal dose tomorrow and don't skip it to compensate. If you get chest pain or a racing, irregular heartbeat, get checked. A weekly pill organizer helps prevent this.
My teenager says her stomach hurts every morning before school but she's fine on weekends.

That pattern often points to anxiety, because stress really does cause stomach pain and nausea in kids, and the pain is real rather than faked. Have a calm, non-judgmental chat about what's happening at school, including friends, bullying and pressure. It's still worth a pediatrician visit to rule out physical causes and get support. Go sooner if there's weight loss, vomiting, or pain that wakes her at night.
is it fine to take 2 extra strength tylenol every 4 hours for my back? it's the only thing that works

Two extra-strength tablets every 4 hours works out to about 6,000 mg a day, well over the usual 3,000 to 4,000 mg maximum, and that's enough to cause serious liver damage. Stick to the dose on the label, keep the total under the max including any combination cold or sleep products, and be extra careful if you drink alcohol. If you need that much to cope, please see a doctor about better options for your back.
feeling better after 4 days of my 10 day antibiotic course. can i stop?

Keep going and finish the course unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Feeling better means the infection is retreating, not necessarily gone, and stopping early can let it bounce back. Some infections are now treated with shorter courses, so if you'd like to stop sooner, call the prescriber and ask whether a shorter course is fine for your specific infection rather than deciding on your own.
Dad's legs are swollen at the ankles, worse by evening. He's 81. Compression socks from the pharmacy okay?

Hold off on the socks until his doctor has looked at him, because ankle swelling at his age can come from heart failure, kidney issues, medications, or a clot, and compression is the wrong move for some of those. Get an appointment this week. Go to the ER now if one leg is suddenly more swollen, red, or painful than the other, or if he's short of breath. Once the cause is clear, the doctor can tell you whether compression is safe and what strength to use.
migraine for 4 days straight now nothing works

A migraine that lasts more than 72 hours is called status migrainosus and is worth getting treated rather than riding out. Urgent care or the ER can give medications like IV fluids, anti-nausea drugs and stronger migraine treatments that often break it. Go straight away if it feels different from your usual migraines or comes with weakness, confusion, fever or a stiff neck.
Woke up with severe upper belly pain going through to my back after drinking heavily last night

Severe upper abdominal pain that bores through to the back after heavy drinking is a red flag for pancreatitis. Get to an emergency department now rather than waiting it out, especially if you're vomiting or have a fever. Don't drink any more alcohol and avoid eating until you're assessed.
just a quick one — dandruff shampoo for flaky eyebrows?

Yes, that works well. Flaky eyebrows are usually seborrheic dermatitis, the same condition as dandruff, so lather a ketoconazole or zinc pyrithione shampoo into your brows, leave it a minute or two, and rinse, a few times a week. Keep it out of your eyes. If it doesn't improve in a few weeks, a doctor can prescribe a stronger cream.
Can I use toothpaste on a pimple overnight? Big event tomorrow

Toothpaste tends to irritate and dry out the skin, which can leave you with a red, flaky spot that's harder to cover. A hydrocolloid pimple patch overnight or a dab of 2.5% benzoyl peroxide works much better, and a cold compress can reduce swelling in the morning. Avoid squeezing it tonight, because that usually makes it bigger and redder for your event.
I've been waking up at 4am every night with my heart racing and can't get back to sleep. It's been like three weeks. Is this anxiety or something worse?

Early waking with a racing heart is a really common pattern with anxiety and stress, because cortisol naturally rises in the early morning and an already-wound-up system overreacts to it. That said, three weeks is long enough to see a doctor, partly to rule out things like an overactive thyroid, heart rhythm issues or sleep apnea, which can feel identical. In the meantime, cut caffeine after noon, skip alcohol in the evening (it causes rebound wake-ups), and if you're awake for more than 20 minutes, get up and do something dull in dim light rather than lying there checking the clock. If you ever get chest pain, fainting or breathlessness with it, get seen urgently.
Kitten scratched my eye. It's watering and stings.

Get this checked today by an eye doctor, urgent care or the ER, because scratches to the eye can cause corneal abrasions or infections that need prompt treatment. Rinse gently with clean water or saline, and don't rub it or put any drops in it besides that. Wearing sunglasses can ease light sensitivity on the way, and if your vision is blurry, go urgently.
Headache, fever, stiff neck, and light hurts my eyes. Probably just flu?

That combination needs emergency care now, not a flu wait-and-see. Fever, headache, a stiff neck and light sensitivity together can be meningitis, which can worsen within hours. Go to the ER right away, and mention any rash you notice.
can i pop a cyst with a sterilized needle

Please don't, because cysts have a sac under the skin that a needle won't remove, and squeezing can push the contents deeper, cause infection, or leave a bigger scar. A warm compress for 10 to 15 minutes a few times a day can help it settle or drain on its own. If it's painful, red, growing, or keeps coming back, a doctor can drain it properly or remove the whole sac so it doesn't return.
fever and the worst headache of my life and my neck hurts to bend

Please go to the emergency department now or call emergency services. Fever combined with a severe headache and a stiff neck can be a sign of meningitis, which needs urgent treatment. Don't wait to see whether it improves, and don't drive yourself if you feel confused or very unwell. Getting seen quickly makes a real difference here.
Good sleeping position for lower back pain?

Side sleeping with a pillow between your knees is usually the best option, since it keeps your hips and spine aligned. If you prefer your back, put a pillow under your knees to take pressure off your lower spine. Stomach sleeping tends to aggravate back pain, so try to avoid it. If your pain is severe, getting worse, or comes with numbness, leg weakness, or bladder changes, see a doctor promptly.
I've been feeling really high energy, barely sleeping and still not tired, spending a lot, starting a ton of projects. Feels great honestly. Anything to worry about?

I'm glad you feel good, but needing very little sleep without feeling tired, combined with heavy spending and lots of new projects, can be a sign of hypomania or mania, which is part of bipolar disorder. It's worth seeing a doctor soon, ideally this week, even though nothing feels wrong. These episodes can escalate, and they're often followed by a hard crash into depression. Try to hold off on big financial decisions until you've been checked out. Ask someone close to you whether they've noticed a change in you too.
I'm 16 and I feel sad basically all the time but I don't want my parents to know. What do I do?

Feeling sad most of the time is something you deserve help with, and you don't have to sort it out alone. If your parents feel like too much right now, start with another adult you trust, like a school counselor, teacher, coach or your doctor, who can help you figure out next steps and even help you talk to your parents later. If you ever have thoughts of hurting yourself, you can call or text 988 in the US anytime to reach someone, or contact your local crisis line elsewhere. Reaching out is a strong move, not a weak one.
Dad's 90 and has been sleeping like 14 hours a day lately, way more than before

A sudden big jump in sleep is worth a doctor's visit soon, because in someone his age it can point to an infection, depression, heart or thyroid problems, anemia or a medication side effect. Make a list of all his medications, including any new ones or dose changes, since sedating drugs are a very common culprit. If he's hard to wake, confused when awake, or has a fever or breathing problems, get him seen urgently.
my throat feels kinda tight after eating thai food but i can breathe fine. probably nothing right?

Throat tightness after eating is worth taking seriously even if you can breathe now, since peanuts, shellfish, and fish sauce in Thai dishes are common allergens. If it gets worse, or you develop hives, voice changes, trouble swallowing, wheezing, or dizziness, call emergency services immediately. Use epinephrine if you have it. Even if it fades, don't stay alone for the next few hours. Follow up with a doctor to figure out the trigger, because a future reaction could be stronger.
Contractions every 10 min for an hour at 31 weeks, kinda mild. Braxton Hicks I assume?

Don't assume that this early. Regular contractions at 31 weeks could be preterm labor, so call labor and delivery now. Meanwhile, drink a big glass of water, empty your bladder and lie on your left side. If they ease off, great, but you should still get checked, because there are treatments that can delay preterm labor if it's caught early.
Sharp zing in my front teeth whenever I drink something cold. Goes away in a second. Big deal?

A brief zing that fades fast is usually sensitivity from exposed dentin, often from gum recession, enamel wear or brushing too hard. Switch to a sensitivity toothpaste with potassium nitrate or stannous fluoride and a soft brush, and give it two to four weeks. Mention it at your next checkup, and go sooner if the pain lingers after the cold is gone or starts happening without any trigger.
I'm 72 and just tested positive for flu this morning. Do I need to do anything or just ride it out?

Call your doctor today rather than riding it out, because at 72 you're in a higher-risk group, and antivirals like Tamiflu work best when started within 48 hours of symptoms. Rest, drink plenty, and use acetaminophen for fever and aches if that's safe for you. Seek care urgently if you get short of breath, chest pain, confusion, or a fever that returns after improving, since those can signal pneumonia.
Can I sweat out a cold by going for a hard run?

No, that's a myth. Sweating doesn't clear the virus, and a hard effort while you're sick can leave you feeling worse and make the illness last longer. If it's a mild head cold, an easy jog or a walk is fine. Otherwise rest, drink plenty of fluids, and save the hard run for when you're better.
Dad suddenly can't find words and his face looks droopy on one side

Call 911 right now, because those are classic stroke signs and every minute counts. Don't drive him yourself, since paramedics can start treatment and alert the stroke team on the way. Note the exact time you first noticed the symptoms or when he was last seen normal, because that decides which treatments he can get. Don't give him food, drink or aspirin while you wait.
Is melatonin safe to take every night long term? I'm 45

Melatonin appears fairly safe for a lot of people, but long-term nightly use isn't well studied, and supplement doses often far exceed what you need. Try 0.5 to 3 mg about an hour before bed. If you need it every night to sleep, it's worth looking into the cause with a doctor, since CBT for insomnia works better long-term and conditions like sleep apnea are common at your age.
I'm 30 weeks pregnant and think I have the flu. Fever 101, aches everywhere.

Call your OB or midwife today. Pregnancy raises the risk of serious flu complications, and antiviral treatment like oseltamivir is recommended for pregnant people and works best when started early. Acetaminophen is generally the preferred fever reducer in pregnancy, so ask about using it, and drink plenty of fluids. If you have trouble breathing, chest pain, reduced baby movement or a fever that won't come down, go to the hospital right away.
can i superglue a cut shut instead of going to get stitches? its on my knee and kinda deep

Superglue is only okay for small, shallow, clean cuts, and a deep cut on a knee isn't a good candidate. The joint flexes constantly and will pull the wound open, and sealing a deep wound can trap bacteria inside. Get it seen within the next few hours, since stitches work best when done early. Until then, apply pressure and keep it covered.
I'm pregnant (24 weeks) and just got told I have gestational diabetes. Did I cause this by eating badly? Is the baby ok?

You didn't cause this. Gestational diabetes mostly comes from pregnancy hormones making your body more insulin resistant, and it happens to lots of people who eat well. The good news is that when it's managed with diet, glucose monitoring, and sometimes insulin, most babies are born perfectly healthy. Follow up with your care team and any diabetes educator they refer you to, because steady control is what protects the baby. It usually goes away after delivery, but get tested again afterward.
hi, 68 yo, on warfarin, just got prescribed cipro for a bladder infection. anything I should worry about?

Yes, that combination needs attention. Ciprofloxacin can boost warfarin's effect and raise your bleeding risk, so let your doctor or anticoagulation clinic know and ask whether you need an extra INR check this week. Watch for unusual bruising, bleeding gums or dark stools. At your age, cipro also carries a higher risk of tendon problems, so stop it and call your doctor if you feel sudden heel or calf pain.
Type 2 diabetic here. Can I stop metformin if I've been eating low carb and my sugars look great?

That's genuinely good news, but don't stop it on your own. Your readings may look great partly because the metformin is still working. Book a review with your doctor and bring your recent numbers. They may well reduce or stop it and then recheck your HbA1c in about three months to make sure your sugars stay in range.
I'm 34 and suddenly allergic to shrimp?? ate it my whole life. last time my mouth itched and I got hives. can I just eat a little to see if it was a fluke

Please don't test it at home. Adult-onset shellfish allergy is real and common, and a reaction can be worse the next time even if the last one was mild. Avoid shellfish completely for now and book an allergist, who can do skin or blood testing and, if appropriate, a supervised food challenge. Ask your doctor whether you should carry an epinephrine auto-injector in the meantime.
is it normal my 13 yo daughter has really heavy periods that soak through a pad every hour

That's heavier than normal, and it's worth having her seen by a doctor soon. Soaking a pad every hour can lead to anemia, and sometimes it points to a bleeding disorder like von Willebrand disease. If she feels dizzy, faint or short of breath, or the heavy bleeding goes on for more than a few hours, take her in that same day.
My 2 year old ate maybe 4 or 5 of my iron pills, they look like candy. What do I do??

Call Poison Control right now at 1-800-222-1222 in the US, or your local emergency number, and do not wait for symptoms. Iron overdose is one of the most dangerous poisonings in small children, and a child can look fine early on even when the situation is serious. Have the bottle in hand so you can tell them the exact product and strength, and don't try to make your child vomit unless they tell you to.
I'm so behind on marathon training after being sick with bronchitis for 10 days. Can I just double my mileage this week to catch up?

Doubling your mileage right after bronchitis is a fast route to a setback or an injury. Your lungs and fitness need time to recover, so expect your first runs to feel harder than usual. Ease back in at roughly half your previous volume and build up over one to two weeks. If it means changing your race goal, that's still better than missing the race entirely.
Can I crush my mom's pills and put them in applesauce? She has trouble swallowing.

Sometimes yes, but check with her pharmacist before crushing anything. Extended-release, enteric-coated and some other pills can release a dangerous dose all at once or stop working if crushed. The pharmacist can tell you which ones are safe to crush and may offer liquid versions or alternatives. Mention the swallowing trouble to her doctor too, since a swallowing evaluation can reduce her risk of choking or aspiration pneumonia.
Touched my hand to a bleach solution and the skin looks red and stings. Is that a burn?

Yes, that's a mild chemical burn, and the fix is to rinse it under lots of running water for at least 20 minutes to wash all the chemical off. Remove any rings or contaminated clothing. After that it should calm down over a day or two with a plain moisturizer. See a doctor if it blisters, the pain gets worse, or any splashed in your eyes, which needs immediate flushing and urgent care.
Is it fine to crack my own neck when it feels stiff? I do it like 20 times a day lol

Occasional gentle cracking isn't harmful for most people, but forcefully twisting your neck twenty times a day is a habit worth breaking. Forceful neck manipulation has rarely been linked to tears in the arteries that supply the brain. Swap the cracking for slow chin tucks, side tilts and shoulder rolls, and look at how you sit and where your screen is. If the stiffness keeps coming back or comes with headaches or arm tingling, a physiotherapist can find out what's driving it.
dad has hearing loss but refuses hearing aids. does it actually matter

It matters more than people think. Untreated hearing loss is linked to social isolation, depression, falls and faster cognitive decline, and research suggests hearing aids may slow decline in some people. Many people resist because of stigma or bad experiences with old devices. A proper audiology fitting, or even trying modern over-the-counter aids, can change their mind. Start with a hearing test so he has real numbers to look at.
how do i pop a cyst on my neck at home, its huge and annoying

Don't squeeze or lance it yourself. Cysts have a sac under the skin, so popping one rarely clears it, and it often drives infection deeper and leaves a worse scar. A warm compress for 10 to 15 minutes a few times a day can help it settle or drain on its own. If it's large, painful, red or keeps coming back, a GP or dermatologist can drain it cleanly or remove the whole sac so it doesn't return.
My 4 year old has a fever of 102 and I only have adult Tylenol tablets. Can I just cut one in half?

Please don't. Half of a 500 mg adult tablet is 250 mg, which may be too much for a small child, and cutting tablets makes the dose unpredictable. Children's acetaminophen is dosed by weight, roughly 15 mg per kg, so a 16 kg (35 lb) four-year-old would get about 240 mg, or 7.5 mL of the 160 mg/5 mL children's liquid. Pick up the children's version, or call a pharmacist, who can tell you the exact dose for your child's weight.
mom fell yesterday, says shes fine, no bruises. do i need to do anything

Keep an eye on her for the next couple of days, because older adults can have hip fractures or slow head bleeds that don't show up right away. Get her seen promptly if she hit her head, takes a blood thinner, or develops pain when walking, confusion, unusual sleepiness, headache or vomiting. Even if she stays fine, a first fall is worth telling her doctor about, since it often points to a fixable cause like medication side effects, low blood pressure or vision problems.
I got bitten by a stray cat I was trying to feed. It ran off. I feel fine. Is it really a big deal?

Yes, this one is a big deal, because a stray can't be checked for rabies, and rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear. Wash the bite with soap and water for 15 minutes and see a doctor or go to urgent care today to discuss rabies post-exposure shots, which work very well when started promptly. Feeling fine doesn't tell you anything yet, so don't wait for symptoms.
My 2 year old pulled a mug of tea onto his chest. The skin is red and some bits are blistering. He's screaming.

Get his wet clothing off right away and run cool water over the area for 20 minutes, keeping the rest of him warm so he doesn't get chilled. Then cover the burn loosely with plastic cling film or a clean nonstick cloth and take him to urgent care or the ER now. Blistering scald burns on a toddler's chest need professional assessment, because small children lose fluid fast and these burns are often deeper than they look. Don't put any creams, ice or butter on it.
my epipen expired 3 months ago, is it still ok to carry or totally useless now

Keep carrying it until the replacement arrives, because an expired auto-injector still delivers some epinephrine and is far better than nothing in a real reaction. The drug slowly loses potency after the expiry date, though, so get a new prescription filled this week rather than relying on the old one. If the liquid in the window looks brown, cloudy or has particles, it has degraded more, which makes replacing it even more urgent.
got a pimple on my nose that's really swollen and red, can i just pop it with a needle?

Skip the needle, especially on your nose, which sits in the area where skin infections can occasionally spread to deeper tissues, and poking a deep, swollen pimple usually pushes bacteria further in and leaves a scar. Hold a warm compress on it for 10 minutes a few times a day to help it come to a head on its own, and dab on a little benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid. If it keeps getting bigger and more painful, or you get a fever or swelling spreading around your eye, see a doctor that day.
Read that cinnamon lowers blood sugar. Can I replace my meds with it?

No. Studies on cinnamon show at most a small, inconsistent effect on blood sugar, nowhere near what metformin or other diabetes drugs do. It's fine to sprinkle it on your food, but large supplement doses of cassia cinnamon can actually stress the liver. Keep your meds and talk to your doctor if you want to reduce them through diet and exercise.
My grandpa (80) is clutching his chest and sweating and refuses to go to the hospital. What do I do?

Call emergency services now, even if he objects. Chest pain with sweating in an 80-year-old is a likely heart attack, and paramedics can assess him and talk him round. If he isn't allergic and doesn't have a bleeding problem, have him chew one regular 325 mg aspirin while you wait. Keep him sitting and calm. If he becomes unresponsive and isn't breathing normally, start CPR and follow the dispatcher's instructions.
Can I just skip my metformin on weekends? I feel fine and it upsets my stomach.

Skipping weekends isn't a good idea, because metformin works through steady daily use, and stopping and restarting can actually make the stomach upset worse each Monday.
