Feeling fine is common with type 2 diabetes even when sugars are running high, so it's not a reliable sign you can take breaks. The stomach issues are very fixable: taking it with food, raising the dose more slowly, or switching to the extended-release version helps most people. Ask your doctor about the extended-release option before changing anything on your own.
is it safe to let my dog lick my cut finger? people say dog spit heals

That's a myth worth skipping. Dog saliva carries plenty of bacteria, including some, like Capnocytophaga, that can occasionally cause serious infections, especially in people with weakened immune systems. Keep the cut washed and covered, and let it heal on its own.
Need to stay awake for a 10 hour drive tonight after work. Best energy drinks?

Please don't plan a 10-hour overnight drive after a full workday, because drowsy driving causes thousands of crashes a year and energy drinks only mask fatigue rather than fixing it. The safest option is to sleep first and leave early in the morning, or split the trip with an overnight stop. If you must go, take a 20-minute nap before leaving, share the driving, and stop every two hours. If you notice drifting lanes, heavy eyelids, or missing exits, pull over somewhere safe and sleep.
My dad (78) fell yesterday and now has sudden mid-back pain, he says it's just a bruise. He has osteoporosis.

With osteoporosis, a fall followed by sudden back pain could easily be a vertebral compression fracture, so he should see a doctor and probably get an X-ray rather than write it off as a bruise. These fractures are treatable, and diagnosing one also matters because it may change his bone medication and fall prevention plan. If he has numbness or weakness in his legs, or the pain is severe and getting worse, take him to the emergency department.
seasonal allergies are wrecking me. how many zyrtec can i take a day, like 3?

Stick to one 10 mg cetirizine tablet in 24 hours, because taking three won't relieve your symptoms much better and will mostly add drowsiness and other side effects. If one isn't enough, a daily steroid nasal spray like fluticasone usually makes a bigger difference for congestion and sneezing, especially if you use it consistently for a week or two. If you're still miserable, a doctor or allergist can look at prescription options or allergy shots.
Back to lifting after food poisoning, anything I should know?

Make sure you're fully rehydrated and eating normally first, because vomiting and diarrhea can leave you low on fluids and electrolytes for a couple of days. For your first session, drop the weights to around 60 to 70 percent of your usual load and keep the volume lower. Drink well before and during the workout. If you feel lightheaded or crampy, stop and give it another day.
My mom suddenly can't lift her right arm and her words sound slurred. She wants to lie down and see if it passes.

Call 911 right now. Those are classic stroke signs, and stroke treatments only work within a few hours. Don't let her lie down to wait it out, and don't drive her yourself if an ambulance can come. Note the time her symptoms started, because doctors will ask.
how long am i contagious with the flu

Most adults are contagious from about a day before symptoms start until roughly 5 to 7 days after, and you're most infectious in the first 3 to 4 days. Children and people with weakened immune systems can spread it for longer. A good rule is to stay home until you've been fever-free for at least 24 hours without fever reducers and you're feeling generally better.
honestly can i just mix benadryl and zyrtec to knock out these hives faster

Doubling up on antihistamines adds sedation and side effects without much extra benefit. Benadryl especially can make you groggy and impair driving, so I wouldn't combine them on your own. A better move is to take a non-drowsy one like cetirizine, which doctors sometimes raise to higher doses under supervision for stubborn hives. If you get lip or tongue swelling or trouble breathing, that's an emergency. If the hives keep coming back for weeks, see a doctor about it.
back pain

Most back pain is muscular and gets better within a few weeks with gentle movement, heat, and over-the-counter pain relief if needed. Stay active rather than resting in bed, and avoid heavy lifting while it's sore. See a doctor if it follows a fall or injury, comes with fever, unexplained weight loss, leg weakness, or numbness, or if it's not improving after a few weeks. If you share more about how it started and where it hurts, I can be more specific.
is it normal to feel nothing? not sad, just numb. 41M

Emotional numbness is actually a common form of depression, especially in men, who often don't feel classic sadness. It can also follow long-term stress or burnout, and some antidepressants cause it as a side effect. If it's lasted more than a couple of weeks, see your doctor and describe it just like you did here. It's treatable, and feeling flat isn't something you have to live with.
I got a really small electric shock from an outlet and there's a little burn mark on my finger. Feel fine.

Electrical burns can be deeper than they look on the surface, and any shock from mains power is worth a call to your doctor or a nurse line to see whether you should be checked. Cool the mark under running water and cover it. Get urgent care immediately if you notice chest pain, palpitations, numbness, muscle pain, or if you felt the current travel through your body.
can I use my rescue inhaler every day? it helps

Needing it every day means your asthma isn't controlled, and relying on rescue inhalers alone is linked to a higher risk of serious attacks. What usually helps is a daily controller inhaler with a steroid, which treats the underlying inflammation. See your doctor soon to get on the right maintenance plan. Until then, keep using the rescue inhaler as needed, and get urgent care if it stops working.
can dehydration really cause a headache or is that a myth

It's real. Even mild dehydration can trigger a headache, especially in heat, after exercise or after drinking alcohol. Drink a couple of glasses of water and you'll often notice relief within an hour. If you're well hydrated and still getting regular headaches, look for other causes like sleep, screen time or stress.
Got back from Ghana 10 days ago, now fever and chills. Probably just a cold right?

Don't assume that. A fever within weeks of returning from West Africa needs prompt testing for malaria, which can turn serious quickly even if you took prophylaxis. See a doctor or urgent care today and tell them where you traveled.
I'm 45, BP is 150/100 every time, doc wants to start meds but I'd rather try diet for 6 months first. Reasonable?

At 150/100 that's stage 2 hypertension, and most guidelines recommend starting medication along with lifestyle changes rather than waiting six months. Pressure that high quietly stresses your heart, kidneys and blood vessels the whole time. Starting meds now doesn't have to be forever, though. If diet and exercise work, your doctor can often lower or stop the dose later, so the two approaches aren't either-or.
no insurance, tooth hurts bad, can't afford a dentist. options?

Look up dental schools and community health centers near you, since they often offer treatment at sharply reduced cost or on a sliding scale. Some areas also run free dental clinic days. Meanwhile, alternate ibuprofen and acetaminophen at safe doses and rinse with warm salt water. If you develop facial swelling, fever or trouble swallowing, go to the ER regardless of cost, because a spreading dental infection can become dangerous.
elderly dad (82) won't eat, says his dentures hurt. he says it's nothing

Painful dentures are worth sorting out quickly, because not eating can wear an 82-year-old down fast. Check his gums for sore spots, ulcers, or white patches, and have him leave the dentures out for a while to let the tissue rest, offering soft foods meanwhile. Book a dentist to adjust or reline them, and if any sore lasts more than two weeks, make sure it gets examined, since it needs to be ruled out as something more serious.
can i stop my metformin if i've been eating keto and my sugars look good?

Possibly, but make that decision with your doctor rather than on your own, because good numbers may partly be the metformin doing its job. Your doctor can check your A1c and either taper you off or lower the dose while you keep monitoring. Keto on its own is a reasonable tool for many people with type 2 diabetes, and metformin carries little risk of lows, so this is a fair question to raise at your next visit. Just don't quit cold and assume the readings will stay put.
Is it better to sleep on a hard or soft mattress for back pain?

A medium-firm mattress tends to work best for most people with back pain. Very hard mattresses don't support the spine any better and can create pressure points, while very soft ones let your hips sink out of alignment. If you sleep on your side, a pillow between your knees helps, and back sleepers often do well with one under the knees.
Stuffed up with a cold. I have high blood pressure. Is Sudafed ok?

Pseudoephedrine can raise blood pressure and heart rate, so it's best avoided if your pressure isn't well controlled, and worth checking with your doctor even if it is. Saline rinses, a humidifier and steroid nasal sprays like fluticasone are good alternatives that don't affect blood pressure. If you want a combination product, look for ones made for high blood pressure, and run it past your pharmacist first.
is apple cider vinegar good for acid reflux

The evidence for it is weak, and for many people it actually makes reflux worse because it's acidic and irritates an already inflamed esophagus. You're better off with proven moves: smaller meals, no eating close to bedtime, raising the head of the bed, and an antacid or famotidine as needed. If reflux is a regular thing, a doctor can help you sort out the right treatment.
is it ok to take my vitamin D with my morning coffee or does that mess with absorption

Coffee isn't a real problem for vitamin D, so you're fine there. What matters more is taking it with a meal that has some fat in it, because vitamin D is fat-soluble and absorbs noticeably better that way. If your morning coffee comes with breakfast, eggs, yogurt or toast with butter, you're set.
i'm a nurse, mild cold symptoms, short staffed. fine to work in a mask?

Follow your facility's illness policy and talk to your manager or employee health, rather than deciding on your own. Many hospitals let staff with mild symptoms and no fever work masked, but some require testing for COVID or flu first, especially if you care for immunocompromised patients, newborns or the elderly. Get tested if you can, and stay home if you have a fever or are coughing a lot. Being short staffed is real, but bringing flu onto a unit can make things much worse.
Our new rescue dog bit my toddler's cheek. Small puncture. It's evening, can we wait till morning?

Wash it gently with soap and running water now, but I'd take her to urgent care or the ER tonight rather than waiting, because facial bites on small children need careful assessment for infection and scarring, and antibiotics work best when started early. A rescue dog's vaccination history may also be uncertain, which the doctor will want to consider. Keep your toddler and the dog apart until you've worked out what triggered the bite.
I'm 55 and I've noticed my bowel habits changed over the last couple months, thinner stools and some blood. Probably hemorrhoids yeah?

It could be hemorrhoids, but at 55 a change in bowel habits plus blood needs to be checked by a doctor rather than assumed. Thinner stools and bleeding together are also symptoms of colorectal cancer, which is very treatable when it's caught early. Make an appointment in the next week or two, and ask about a colonoscopy, especially if you haven't had one. Get seen sooner if you're losing weight, feel tired or short of breath, or have a lot of bleeding.
high dose vitamin C to cure my cold? like 5000mg

That won't cure it. Studies show vitamin C at most slightly shortens colds when taken regularly beforehand, and big doses after you're sick don't do much. At 5,000 mg you're also likely to get diarrhea and cramps, and in some people it raises the risk of kidney stones. Rest, fluids and time are what work.
type 1 here, going to a party tonight and planning to drink. any tips or should i just not

You can drink with type 1, but alcohol blocks your liver from releasing glucose, so the real danger is a low several hours later, often while you're asleep. Eat carbs while you drink, stick to a moderate amount, and check your sugar before bed. Have a snack if you're under about 130 to 150, and consider lowering your basal or setting an alarm to check overnight. Wear medical ID and make sure a friend knows you're diabetic, because a low can look a lot like being drunk.
toothache so bad, anything I can do RIGHT NOW at 2am

Right now, take an over-the-counter pain reliever as labeled, such as ibuprofen if it's safe for you, and use a cold pack on your cheek for 15 to 20 minutes at a time. Rinsing gently with warm salt water, using a benzocaine gel or a dab of clove oil on the tooth, and sleeping with your head propped up can all help too. Call your dentist first thing in the morning, and go to the ER tonight if you develop facial swelling, fever, or trouble swallowing or breathing.
Does exercise really help depression or is that just something people say

It really helps. Studies show regular exercise, especially moderate aerobic activity a few times a week, can reduce mild to moderate depression about as much as therapy or medication for some people. The catch is that depression saps the motivation to do it, so start embarrassingly small, like a ten-minute walk outside, and build up from there. For moderate or severe depression, exercise works best alongside proper treatment rather than instead of it, so keep your doctor in the loop.
Teen daughter (15) wants to do a juice cleanse with her friends for a week. Harmless?

A week of only juice isn't a great idea for a growing teen, since it's low in protein and calories and can leave her dizzy, irritable, and tired, plus it doesn't actually detox anything. It's also worth a gentle conversation about why the group wants to do it, because restrictive dieting at her age can sometimes slide into disordered eating. If they want a health challenge, something like adding more fruits and veggies or cutting soda together is a much better project.
My friend says I should get my back cracked by a chiropractor for my sciatica, and my GP wants physio. Who's right?

Your GP's suggestion has the stronger track record for sciatica. A physiotherapist can give you targeted exercises, nerve mobility work and posture advice that tend to help over time. Some people do find spinal manipulation gives short-term relief, but it's not clearly better than physio. Start with the physio, and get reassessed if you develop leg weakness or numbness, or if the pain is getting worse.
my dog bit me but its our own dog and vaccinated. do i need a rabies shot

If your dog is up to date on rabies vaccination and is healthy, you very likely don't need rabies shots, but watch the dog for 10 days, and if it gets sick or behaves strangely, call a doctor right away. Wash the bite thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes. Get it looked at if it's deep or on your hand or face, since dog bites get infected easily and you may need antibiotics or a tetanus booster.
Splinter deep in my palm, can't get it out with tweezers

Soak your hand in warm water for 10 to 15 minutes to soften the skin. Then use a needle sterilized with alcohol to gently open the skin over the end of the splinter and lift it out, pulling in the direction it went in. If it's very deep, glass or metal, or you can't get it after a couple of careful tries, have urgent care remove it rather than digging. Watch for redness or swelling over the next few days.
on metronidazole for 7 days, my friend's wedding is saturday. one or two drinks fine right?

Not on metronidazole. Combining it with alcohol can cause pounding headache, flushing, nausea, vomiting and a racing heart, and even a small amount can set it off. Avoid alcohol for the whole course and for at least 72 hours after your last pill. If the timing really clashes with the wedding, ask your doctor whether a different antibiotic would work, but don't stop this one early on your own.
migraine for 3 days straight now, nothing touches it, throwing up. can't keep pills down. what do i do

A migraine lasting over 72 hours with vomiting is called status migrainosus, and it needs medical treatment, not more waiting. Go to urgent care or the ER, where they can give fluids and anti-nausea and migraine medications by IV or injection. Go to emergency right away if you have any weakness, confusion, vision loss or fever, or if this feels different from your usual migraines.
how often should I check my blood pressure at home

If you're starting or changing treatment, take two readings a minute apart each morning and evening for a week, and share the log with your doctor. Once things are stable, checking a few days a month is usually enough. Measure at consistent times, before coffee or exercise, after five minutes of sitting quietly.
suddenly my face is drooping on one side and I have a headache, my arm feels weird

Call 911 right now. Face drooping, arm weakness or numbness, and a headache can be signs of a stroke, and every minute counts for treatment. Don't drive yourself, and note the time your symptoms started to tell the paramedics.
Is it ok to use Q-tips to clean earwax? I do it every day after showering.

Daily Q-tip use actually tends to push wax deeper, irritate the canal skin, and can cause impaction or even a perforated eardrum. Your ears clean themselves, so wiping the outer ear with a washcloth is usually all you need. If you feel blocked, a few days of over-the-counter softening drops or a doctor's cleaning is the safer route.
pregnant and my doctor wants me to get the flu shot and tdap. are vaccines safe for the baby??

Yes, both are recommended specifically because they protect you and the baby. The flu shot lowers your risk of serious illness, which is more dangerous during pregnancy. Tdap, given around 27 to 36 weeks, passes antibodies to the baby that protect against whooping cough in the first months before they can be vaccinated. These vaccines have been studied extensively in pregnant people with a strong safety record. Just avoid live vaccines like MMR during pregnancy.
can i drink alcohol on insulin

Yes, in moderation, but alcohol can cause delayed lows, sometimes many hours later while you're asleep. Eat carbs with your drinks, check your sugar before bed, and consider a snack or a slightly lower dose afterward if your team has advised it. Tell your friends you're diabetic, because a hypo can look a lot like being drunk.
omeprazole every day for 3 years, fine right?

Many people take omeprazole long term without trouble, but it's worth a check-in with your doctor. Years of use are linked to lower B12 and magnesium and a slightly higher fracture and infection risk. Your doctor can confirm you still need it, check those levels, and possibly step you down to a lower dose or as-needed use. Don't stop abruptly, because acid often rebounds for a week or two before settling.
Got a red streak running up my arm from a cut on my hand. Is that bad?

Yes, take that seriously and get seen today. A red streak spreading from a wound can mean the infection is moving through the lymphatic system, which is called lymphangitis, and it usually needs prompt antibiotics. Go to the ER if you have a fever or chills, or if the streak is spreading quickly. Marking the edge of the redness with a pen helps you and the doctor track whether it's growing.
Im pregnant (20 wks) and my hay fever is brutal. what can I take

Several options are generally considered reasonable in pregnancy, but confirm with your OB or pharmacist first since they know your history. Saline rinses and saline sprays are completely safe and surprisingly effective. Loratadine and cetirizine are the antihistamines most often recommended in pregnancy, and budesonide nasal spray has good safety data. Avoid oral decongestants like pseudoephedrine unless your doctor specifically okays them.
My back pain is worst in the morning, lasts over an hour, and gets better with exercise. I'm 26. Weird?

That pattern is worth getting checked. Back pain that's worst in the morning, comes with more than 30 minutes of stiffness and improves with movement can point to inflammatory back pain such as ankylosing spondylitis. This is especially worth considering when it starts before 45 and has lasted months. Ordinary mechanical back pain usually behaves the opposite way. Ask your doctor about it, since it's diagnosed with blood tests and imaging and often treated by a rheumatologist, and early treatment really helps.
pain in upper teeth on both sides + stuffy nose for a week

That combination often points to sinusitis, because your upper back tooth roots sit right below the sinuses and get pressure pain when they're inflamed. Saline rinses, steam and a decongestant or ibuprofen often help. If the tooth pain persists after the congestion clears, or it's focused on one tooth, see a dentist. See a doctor if you have a high fever or symptoms beyond 10 days.
I got burned by a fire pit spark and there's a white patch that doesn't hurt much. Good sign right?

A white or leathery patch with little pain is actually a warning sign rather than a good one. It can mean the burn went deep enough to damage the nerve endings. Cool it under running water anyway, then cover it with cling film or a clean dressing. Have a doctor look at it in the next day, since deep burns, even small ones, may need specialist care to heal properly.
Day 4 after wisdom teeth removal and suddenly the pain is way worse and radiating to my ear. bad breath too

That sounds a lot like dry socket, which typically shows up 2 to 4 days after an extraction when the blood clot breaks down and leaves bone exposed. Call your oral surgeon today, because they can rinse the socket and pack it with a medicated dressing that often relieves the pain within hours. Fever, increasing swelling, or pus would point more toward infection, which also needs prompt attention.
glucose test is gross, can I just skip it? I don't have diabetes

It's worth doing, because gestational diabetes often has no symptoms and develops in people who've never had blood sugar issues. Left untreated, it can lead to a very large baby, a tougher delivery and blood sugar problems for the newborn. If the drink is the dealbreaker, ask your provider about alternatives, since some practices offer options like fasting blood tests or monitoring with a glucose meter.
Severe itching on my palms and feet at 33 weeks, worse at night. Just dry skin?

Intense itching on the palms and soles in late pregnancy can be a sign of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, a liver condition that needs monitoring because it raises risks for the baby. Call your provider and ask for bile acid and liver function blood tests soon. Don't just treat it as dry skin.
quick q, does exercise actually help anxiety or is that a myth

It genuinely helps, and the research on it is solid. Regular aerobic exercise like brisk walking, cycling or swimming lowers baseline anxiety and makes your body less reactive to stress. Aim for about 30 minutes most days, and you'll usually notice a difference within a few weeks. It works well alongside therapy or medication, but it's not always enough on its own for severe anxiety.
I've had asthma for 20 years and I use my rescue inhaler like 4-5 times a week now. Is that a problem?

Yes, that's a sign your asthma isn't well controlled. The usual benchmark is needing your rescue inhaler two days a week or less. Using it that often means there's ongoing inflammation in your airways that the rescue inhaler doesn't treat, and that raises your risk of a serious attack. Book an appointment with your doctor soon. They'll likely add or adjust a daily controller inhaler and look at what's triggering it.
Why won't my doctor give me antibiotics for my cold?? I literally can't afford to be sick at work.

Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics only kill bacteria, so they truly won't shorten a cold. They'd just expose you to side effects like diarrhea for no benefit. Your doctor isn't being stingy. Rest, fluids, decongestants and pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen will help you function in the meantime. If you're not improving after 10 days, or you get better and then suddenly worse with a high fever, go back, because that can signal a secondary bacterial infection.
Hives all over after eating shrimp, lips feel a bit tingly. Should I just take a Benadryl and sleep?

Don't just sleep it off. Hives with tingling lips after a food can be the start of anaphylaxis. Call emergency services right away if you have any swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, trouble breathing or swallowing, wheeze, dizziness or vomiting, and use an epinephrine auto-injector if you have one. If symptoms are only mild, an antihistamine is reasonable, but stay awake with someone around who can watch you. Get checked the same day, and ask about allergy testing and an auto-injector for the future.
My hamster nipped my 6 year old's finger. She's crying more than bleeding lol. Rabies?

You can relax about rabies, because pet hamsters and other small rodents are essentially never a rabies risk and don't require shots. Wash the finger with soap and water, put on a bandage, and give her some extra comfort. Keep an eye on it for a few days, and call her doctor if it becomes red, swollen or pus-filled, or if she gets a fever or rash.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and my lower back and pelvis ache constantly. Can I take ibuprofen?

Avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs at this stage, because after about 20 weeks they can affect the baby's kidneys and heart circulation. Acetaminophen is generally the go-to option in pregnancy, at the lowest dose that helps. A pregnancy support belt, a pillow between your knees at night, warm (not hot) compresses and prenatal physical therapy can all ease pelvic and back pain. Mention it to your OB or midwife, and call them promptly if the pain comes in regular waves or tightenings, since that can be labor.
I saw a little bright red blood on the toilet paper after a hard poop. Do I need to freak out?

No need to freak out, because a small amount of bright red blood after straining is most often from a hemorrhoid or a small tear called a fissure. More fiber, plenty of water and not straining usually let it heal within a week or two. If it keeps happening, the amount increases, or your stool looks dark or tarry, see a doctor. The same goes if you're over 45, or if it comes with weight loss, fatigue or a change in your bowel habits, because those need a proper exam to rule out anything more serious.
Gallbladder attack I think. Pain under right ribs after a fatty dinner, lasted 2 hours then stopped. Doctor needed or wait for the next one?

That does sound like a typical gallbladder attack, and it's worth booking a regular doctor's visit rather than waiting for the next one, because an ultrasound can confirm gallstones easily. Until then, keep meals low in fat to reduce the chance of another attack. Go to the ER if the pain lasts more than a few hours or comes with fever, vomiting, or yellowing of your skin or eyes, since those suggest infection or a blocked duct.
I tripped and landed on my belly at 28 weeks. Feel fine. Need to do anything?

Yes, call your provider or labor and delivery today even though you feel fine. A direct hit to the belly in the second half of pregnancy can occasionally cause placental abruption, which may not show symptoms right away. They will usually want to monitor you and the baby for a few hours. Go in immediately if you have bleeding, leaking fluid, belly pain or tightening, or less movement.
A stray dog bit my son's leg at the park, broke the skin. We can't find the dog. What do we do??

Wash the wound well with soap and running water for at least five minutes, then take him to a doctor or urgent care today. A bite from an unknown animal that breaks the skin needs a medical assessment for rabies risk and possible post-exposure vaccination, which is very effective when started promptly. Report the bite to your local animal control or health department too, since finding the dog could spare him the shots.
eye doctor said I have cataracts. can eye drops dissolve them? saw an ad

No drops have been proven to dissolve cataracts, and the ones sold online are a waste of money that can also delay real treatment. Cataract surgery is the fix. It's quick and routine, and it usually restores clear vision very well. You don't need surgery until the cataracts start affecting daily life, like driving at night or reading. In the meantime, a stronger glasses prescription and brighter lighting can help.
35F, wake up with stiff swollen fingers and wrists for like an hour every morning, been about 2 months. just sleeping wrong?

Probably not. Morning stiffness lasting over an hour, along with swelling in the small joints of both hands and wrists for weeks, is a pattern doctors take seriously because it can point to inflammatory arthritis like rheumatoid arthritis. Book a doctor's appointment soon and ask about blood tests and a possible rheumatology referral. Starting treatment early can prevent permanent joint damage.
is it ok to crack my own back? i do it like 10 times a day

The popping itself is just gas releasing from the joint and isn't harmful, so occasional cracking is fine. Ten times a day suggests your back feels stiff a lot, though, and forcing twists repeatedly can irritate the ligaments over time without fixing the stiffness. You'll get more lasting relief from regular stretching, core and hip strengthening, and breaking up long periods of sitting. If you feel the urge because of real pain, have it looked at.
I'm 22 and my migraines make me throw up so much I can't keep pills down. anything else?

Yes, there are good options that skip the stomach. Sumatriptan comes as a nasal spray and an injection, zolmitriptan comes as a nasal spray, and anti-nausea meds come as dissolving tablets or suppositories. Ask your doctor about a rescue plan with these. Go to urgent care if you've been vomiting for hours and can't keep fluids down, because dehydration will make the attack worse.
best protein intake for building muscle? I'm 25, lifting 4x a week

Around 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day captures most of the muscle-building benefit, so roughly 0.7 grams per pound. Spread it over three or four meals with about 25 to 40 grams each. Whole foods work great, and a protein shake is just a convenient way to fill gaps. For a healthy person, intakes up to around 2.2 g/kg are fine.
My 6 month old has red, dry, rough patches on her cheeks and the creases of her elbows. She keeps rubbing her face on me. What is this?

That pattern sounds a lot like infant eczema, which is very common at this age and usually shows up on the cheeks and in skin folds. Short lukewarm baths, patting her dry, and slathering on a thick fragrance-free ointment or cream several times a day often makes a big difference, and soft cotton clothing helps too. It's worth having her pediatrician confirm it and suggest a gentle treatment for flares, and go sooner if the patches ooze, crust yellow, or she seems unwell, since eczema skin can get infected.
Sunburn. Bad. Blisters on my shoulders. Should I pop them?

Don't pop them, because the blister roof protects the raw skin underneath from infection. Cool the area with damp cloths or a cool shower, keep using a gentle moisturizer or aloe, drink plenty of water and take ibuprofen if it's sore. Blistering means this is a second-degree burn, so get seen promptly if it covers a large area or you develop fever, chills, nausea, confusion or signs of infection like spreading redness or pus. Keep the area completely out of the sun while it heals.
Can I take my husband's sumatriptan? We both get migraines and mine is awful today

I'd hold off. Sumatriptan isn't safe for everyone: it can be risky with heart disease, uncontrolled blood pressure, certain migraine types, or alongside some antidepressants. For today, try an over-the-counter option like ibuprofen or naproxen with a dark, quiet room. Then ask your own doctor about a triptan prescription, because if it suits you, it's a great tool to have.
slow heart rate, like 48 bpm resting. I don't exercise much. 60yo. should I care

A resting rate of 48 can be normal in fit athletes, but in a 60-year-old who doesn't exercise much it deserves a check. It can point to a conduction problem or a side effect of medications like beta blockers. See your doctor in the next week or two for an ECG. Go sooner, or to the ER, if you feel dizzy, faint, unusually tired, breathless, or confused.
I'm allergic to penicillin (rash as a kid). Does that mean I can never take any antibiotic in that family?

Not necessarily, because most people who were labeled penicillin-allergic as children turn out not to be allergic when tested, and a childhood rash is often from the illness itself. Ask your doctor about penicillin allergy testing, which is quick and can open up better, cheaper treatment options. Until you've been formally cleared, keep listing the allergy and don't try penicillins on your own.
Is it ok to take a mental health day from school? I'm 16 and just overwhelmed.

An occasional day to reset can genuinely help when you're overwhelmed, and it's worth asking a parent to call it in so it's above board. Use the day to rest and figure out what's piling up, whether that's a specific class, friend stuff, or not sleeping, rather than just dreading going back. If you're feeling this way a lot, talk to your school counselor, because they can often ease the workload or connect you with more support.
Hep B vaccine as an adult — worth it? I'm 30, diabetic.

Yes. Hepatitis B vaccination is now recommended for all adults up to 59, and people with diabetes are a group it's especially pushed for, partly because of shared glucose monitoring equipment in some settings. Depending on the brand, it's two or three doses, and your doctor or a pharmacy can give it. It's long-lasting protection against a virus that can cause chronic liver disease.
can i take ibuprofen for a headache, 20 weeks

It's best to avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs during pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks onward, because they can affect the baby's kidneys and amniotic fluid levels. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) at the normal dose is the usual go-to, along with water, food, rest and a dark room. If the headache is severe, won't go away, or comes with vision changes or swelling, call your provider promptly, since that can be a sign of preeclampsia.
how often should a 50 year old get bp checked

At 50, get your blood pressure checked at least once a year, and more often if you've had elevated readings, have diabetes or kidney disease, or have a family history of hypertension. A home monitor makes regular checks easy and gives your doctor more useful data than an occasional office reading.
Cough for 4 weeks now after a cold. Everything else is fine. Normal?

A lingering post-viral cough can hang around for three to eight weeks, so it's often not alarming. At four weeks, though, it's reasonable to get checked, especially to rule out things like asthma, reflux, postnasal drip, or whooping cough. Go sooner if you're coughing up blood, losing weight, having night sweats, or getting short of breath. Honey and staying hydrated can take the edge off in the meantime.
stomach bug for 2 days, finally keeping food down. soccer game tonight, coach says play through it

I'd sit this one out or play only limited minutes, because after two days of vomiting or diarrhea you're probably still dehydrated and low on electrolytes. That raises your risk of cramping, dizziness and heat illness. Spend today drinking fluids with some salt and sugar, like an oral rehydration drink, and eating easy carbs. If you're peeing normally and feel steady by tomorrow, you can ease back into practice.
woke up and one ear is just... muffled. no pain, no cold. hearing is way down on that side

Sudden hearing loss in one ear without a cold or blockage is treated as an emergency. It can be sudden sensorineural hearing loss, and steroid treatment works best within the first few days. Get seen today by urgent care, an ENT, or the ER, and ask specifically for a hearing check rather than assuming it's wax.
is 40 degrees going to cause brain damage in my 5 year old???

No, fevers caused by infections don't damage the brain. The body keeps them from rising high enough to do that, and harm only happens around 42°C from heatstroke-type causes. A fever of 40°C still deserves a call to her doctor today, mainly to find what's causing it. Go in urgently if she's hard to wake, breathing fast or has a rash that doesn't fade.
how much water should i drink a day honestly

There's no magic number. Most adults do well with roughly 2 to 3 liters of total fluid a day, and food and other drinks count toward that. If your urine is pale yellow and you're rarely thirsty, you're likely fine. Drink more in heat, during exercise or when you're sick, but don't force down huge amounts, since overdoing it can dangerously dilute your sodium.
My grandma always put butter on burns. Is that actually ok for my son's finger? He touched the oven door.

Butter is a myth worth retiring, since it traps heat in the skin and raises the risk of infection. Hold his finger under cool running water for 20 minutes, which is the single most effective thing you can do. Then cover it loosely with cling film or a clean dressing and give a child's dose of paracetamol or ibuprofen if he's sore. If it blisters badly, looks white or leathery, or he's under five and the burn is bigger than a small patch, have a doctor look at it.
I have asthma and I think I'm getting the flu. Body aches, fever 101, started yesterday. Should I worry?

Call your doctor today, because asthma puts you at higher risk of flu complications and you're still inside the 48-hour window where antivirals like Tamiflu help most. Keep your rescue inhaler close and follow your asthma action plan if your breathing tightens. Go to urgent care or the ER if your inhaler isn't giving relief, you're struggling to speak in full sentences, or your lips look gray or blue.
I'm 45 with a cough for 3 weeks, some weight loss and night sweats. Probably just a lingering bug?

That combination deserves a doctor's visit soon rather than waiting it out. A three-week cough with weight loss and night sweats can point to things like tuberculosis, pneumonia or other conditions that need testing, usually a chest X-ray and bloodwork. Make an appointment this week. If you cough up blood or get short of breath, get seen urgently. Until you know what it is, cover your coughs and avoid close contact with vulnerable people.
Is it safe to fast for Ramadan with type 2 diabetes on gliclazide?

Many people with type 2 diabetes fast safely, but gliclazide can cause lows during long fasts, so see your doctor before Ramadan starts. They'll often move the dose to iftar or reduce it. Check your sugar during the day, and break your fast if you drop below 3.9 or go above 16.7 mmol/L. Religious guidance permits this when your health is at risk.
my toddler just swallowed a coin. she seems totally fine. do i need to do anything

Call your pediatrician or go to urgent care now even if she seems fine, because a coin can lodge in the esophagus without obvious symptoms and an X-ray is the only way to know where it is. Go to the ER immediately if she drools, refuses to swallow, vomits, coughs persistently or has any breathing trouble. And be sure it was really a coin, because if there's any chance it was a button battery, that's an emergency and she needs to be seen right away.
My grandpa is 89 and keeps getting UTIs. Can we just keep some antibiotics at home for when it happens?

Ask his doctor rather than stockpiling. Using the wrong antibiotic or treating every symptom on guesswork breeds resistant bacteria, and in older adults symptoms like confusion get blamed on UTIs that often aren't there. With frequent infections he deserves a look for an underlying cause, such as an enlarged prostate or incomplete bladder emptying. His doctor may also suggest prevention strategies. Fever, back pain, or sudden confusion means he needs to be seen promptly.
can i get the covid and flu shot same day or is that too much for my body

Yes, you can get both the same day, and it's safe. Studies show your immune system handles both well and the protection is just as good. You might feel a bit more tired or achy for a day, so many people get one in each arm and plan a quiet evening. It saves you a second trip.
Woke up with painful blisters in a band on one side of my ribs. 58 years old.

A painful band of blisters on one side of the body is classic shingles. See a doctor today if you can, because antivirals like valacyclovir work best when started within about 72 hours of the rash appearing. Early treatment can also lower the chance of lingering nerve pain. Keep the blisters covered and stay away from pregnant women, newborns and anyone with a weakened immune system until they crust over. Once you've recovered, ask about the shingles vaccine.
how long can a person actually go without sleep before it gets dangerous? i have finals and want to pull two all-nighters back to back

After about 24 hours awake, your reaction time and judgment are roughly as impaired as being legally drunk, and by 48 hours you'll start having microsleeps you don't even notice. Two back-to-back all-nighters will almost certainly hurt your exam scores more than the extra study time helps, because sleep is when your brain locks in what you learned. A better plan is to study hard in the evening, sleep at least five or six hours, and review key points in the morning. Whatever you do, don't drive anywhere after a night without sleep.
how many ibuprofen can I take at once for a really bad toothache, the regular dose isn't cutting it

Don't go above the label dose, because higher doses raise your risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems without much extra pain relief. Pairing ibuprofen with acetaminophen, each at its own label dose, works better than either alone and is often as effective as stronger prescription options. Check with a pharmacist first if you have stomach, kidney or heart issues. Pain that strong means you need a dentist soon, ideally an emergency appointment.
can i just give my 8 year old adult tylenol cut in half? out of kids stuff

It's better not to guess with pill-splitting, because the right acetaminophen dose for a child depends on their weight. A half tablet can easily be too much or too little. Call a pharmacist, who can work out a safe dose from your child's weight in a minute, or run out for children's chewables or liquid. Whatever you give, track the timing and don't combine it with other products that also contain acetaminophen.
my newborn's eye is goopy and watery all the time

Mention it to your pediatrician, but a watery, crusty eye in a baby is most often a blocked tear duct. That's common and usually opens on its own within the first year. Wipe the eye from the inner corner outward with a clean, warm damp cloth. Call sooner if the white of the eye turns red, the eyelid swells, the discharge is heavy, or the baby is under 4 weeks old, since infections in newborns need prompt care.
My 4 year old has had diarrhea for 2 days, still playing but not eating much. Should I give her Imodium?

Skip the Imodium. It isn't recommended for young children and can cause serious side effects, and most toddler diarrhea clears up on its own. Fluids are what matter, so offer small frequent sips of water or an oral rehydration solution, and food can wait until her appetite returns. Call her doctor if she has fewer wet diapers or trips to the toilet, seems unusually sleepy, has blood in her stool, a high fever, or isn't improving after another day or so.
My grandmother suddenly seems really confused since yesterday, talking nonsense. She's 88. Is this just dementia getting worse?

Sudden confusion over a day or two is not typical dementia progression and needs same-day medical attention. In older adults, a common cause is delirium, often triggered by a urinary tract infection, dehydration, a new medication or another illness, and it's usually treatable. If she also has facial drooping, weakness on one side or slurred speech, call emergency services immediately, because that could be a stroke.
do those magnetic copper bracelets help arthritis? my aunt swears by hers

Controlled studies haven't found copper or magnetic bracelets to do anything beyond placebo for arthritis pain. They're harmless, so there's no need to argue with your aunt if she enjoys hers. The things with real evidence behind them are regular exercise, strength work, weight management, and appropriate pain relief.
Can I just skip my toddler's 18 month shots and catch up when she starts preschool? We're busy.

I'd strongly advise against waiting that long. The schedule is timed to protect kids during the years when diseases like whooping cough, measles and Hib are most dangerous to them, and a gap of a year or more leaves her exposed at daycare, playgrounds and family gatherings. Most clinics can fit a quick shot visit in under 20 minutes, and some pharmacies vaccinate toddlers too. Call your pediatrician and ask for the earliest short slot.
Dog bit my hand, broke the skin, it's my neighbor's dog and they say it's vaccinated. Am I fine?

Wash the bite thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes, then get it seen today. Dog bites to the hand get infected easily and often need antibiotics, and you may need a tetanus booster. If the dog's rabies vaccination is documented and the dog stays healthy during a 10-day observation, you probably won't need rabies shots, but a doctor or local health department should make that call. Ask your neighbor for the vaccine certificate.
My dad (65) refuses to see a doctor, he's had a fever and bad cough for a week and gets winded walking to the kitchen

Push hard on this one, because getting winded at rest with a week of fever and cough at 65 is a real warning sign for pneumonia. If he won't go to an office, offer a telehealth visit or urgent care, and a cheap fingertip pulse oximeter can help. A reading below about 92 percent means he needs care today. If his lips look bluish, he's confused, or he can't catch his breath, call emergency services whether he likes it or not.
My toenail is thick, yellow and crumbly. Can I just soak it in bleach?

Don't soak your foot in bleach, because it can burn and crack your skin and won't actually reach the fungus living under the nail. Nail fungus is stubborn, and over-the-counter treatments only clear a small share of cases, so prescription topical or oral medication from a doctor is usually the most effective route. Keeping nails trimmed, feet dry, and wearing breathable socks and shoes helps either way, and if you have diabetes, get any nail or foot changes looked at promptly.
can you take too much vitamin D? i take 10,000 IU a day

Yes, you can, and 10,000 IU a day is above the generally recommended upper limit of 4,000 IU for adults. Some people take that much safely under medical supervision, but over time it can push calcium too high and cause nausea, kidney stones or kidney damage. Unless a doctor prescribed that dose based on your levels, drop to 1,000 to 2,000 IU and ask for a blood test to see where you stand.
Read online that beet juice lowers bp fast. Can I use that instead of my meds tonight?

Keep taking your meds tonight. Beet juice can lower blood pressure a few points for a few hours, but it isn't strong or consistent enough to replace prescribed medication. Enjoy it alongside your meds if you like it, and talk to your doctor before making any change to your treatment.
I had COVID a month ago and now I get dizzy and my heart races when I try to jog. Should I just push through it?

Don't push through those symptoms. A racing heart and dizziness with exertion after COVID can point to things like heart inflammation or post-viral problems with heart rate regulation, and both need to be checked out. See your doctor before running again, and mention exactly what happens when you exercise. If you get chest pain, fainting, or severe shortness of breath, seek urgent care right away.
on lisinopril, doc says cut salt so I bought salt substitute. good swap?

Check with your doctor first. Most salt substitutes replace sodium with potassium chloride, and lisinopril already makes your body hold on to potassium. The combination can push potassium to dangerously high levels, especially if your kidneys aren't working at full strength, and that can disturb your heart rhythm. Herbs, lemon, garlic and salt-free spice blends without potassium are safer ways to add flavor.
My 4 year old shoved a bead in her ear. I have tweezers, should I try?

Put the tweezers down. Round, smooth objects like beads tend to get pushed deeper when you grab at them, and a squirming kid makes it easy to scratch the canal or damage the eardrum. If you can't see the bead, or it doesn't fall out when she tilts her head to that side, have a pediatrician or urgent care remove it with the proper tools. It's rarely an emergency unless she's in a lot of pain or something is draining from the ear.
My readings at the doctor are always high but normal at home. Do I even need treatment?

You might have white coat hypertension, where nerves push your numbers up only in the clinic. That's common, and your home readings matter a lot. Bring your home cuff to an appointment to check it against the office machine, and ask about 24-hour ambulatory monitoring, the gold standard for sorting this out. Even if it is white coat hypertension, it's worth keeping an eye on, because it can raise your long-term risk a bit.
Low blood pressure, 92/60, feel totally fine. Problem?

If you feel fine, 92/60 is usually not a problem. Plenty of healthy people, especially younger, active people, naturally run that low. It's only a concern if it comes with dizziness, fainting, fatigue or a sudden drop from your usual numbers, and in that case get it checked.
Is it okay to drink energy drinks if I have a heart murmur? My doctor said it's an innocent one.

If your doctor has confirmed it's an innocent murmur, your heart structure is normal and the murmur itself isn't a reason to avoid caffeine. Energy drinks still pack a lot of caffeine and stimulants, so keep it to about one a day at most, and don't mix them with alcohol or drink them before intense exercise. Cut back if you notice palpitations, chest discomfort or dizziness, and see your doctor if those symptoms show up.
can i use a heating pad on my stomach for cramps or does that make it worse

A heating pad on low to medium for 15 to 20 minutes at a time is a great, safe way to ease ordinary cramps from gas, periods or IBS. Put a layer of fabric between it and your skin, and don't fall asleep with it on, to avoid burns. Skip it if the pain could be appendicitis or something serious, because severe or worsening pain needs a doctor, not a home remedy.
my stomach has been hurting on the lower right side since last night and now it's worse when i walk. probably just gas right?

Pain that settles in the lower right side and gets worse when you walk or move is a classic warning sign of appendicitis, so please don't write it off as gas. Get seen at urgent care or the ER today, especially if you have fever, nausea or loss of appetite. Avoid painkillers, laxatives or heating pads until you've been checked, because they can mask symptoms or make things worse. If it's gas you'll have lost a few hours, but if it's your appendix, catching it early matters a lot.
can I keep running on a sore knee if I strap it up

Strapping can make running feel better, but it hides the problem rather than fixing it, so it depends on the pain. Mild aching that eases as you warm up and doesn't worsen afterwards is usually fine if you cut your distance. Sharp pain, swelling, locking, giving way, or pain that builds as you run means stop and get it assessed by a physio, since pushing through can turn a minor overuse issue into months off.
my arm is super sore after my flu shot yesterday, is that normal??

Yes, a sore arm for a day or two is the most common reaction to a flu shot and just means your immune system is responding. Moving the arm around, a cool compress, and an over-the-counter pain reliever like ibuprofen or acetaminophen can all help. If the redness keeps spreading after a few days, the arm gets hot and swollen, or you develop a high fever, get it checked by a doctor.
my 2 month old feels hot, thermometer says 38.2 rectal. is it ok to wait til morning?

No, don't wait. A rectal temperature of 38.0°C (100.4°F) or higher in a baby under 3 months needs medical evaluation right away, even if she seems fine otherwise. Call your pediatrician's after-hours line now or go to the emergency department. Young infants can have serious infections that show few other signs.
my grandma has dementia and keeps saying her belly hurts but cant say where

Take this seriously, because people with dementia often can't describe their pain well and may underreport how bad it is. Watch for clues like guarding her belly, not eating, vomiting, fever, changes in bowel movements, or new confusion or agitation. Constipation and urinary tract infections are common culprits in older adults, but more serious problems need to be ruled out. Have her doctor see her soon, and go to the ER if she's vomiting, has a hard swollen belly, or seems much more unwell than usual.
Is walking or running better for someone with mild arthritis in the hips? 55F.

Walking is the safer bet to build on. It's low-impact, strengthens the muscles around the hip, and helps arthritic joints stay mobile. Running isn't automatically off the table with mild arthritis, but listen to your body: if the hip feels worse for more than a day afterward, scale back. Cycling and swimming are excellent ways to add more exercise without extra stress on the joint.
Why do I keep getting yeast infections after antibiotics??

Antibiotics kill off the protective bacteria in the vagina, which lets yeast overgrow, so this is a really common pattern. If you know antibiotics trigger it for you, ask your prescriber about a single fluconazole pill to take afterward. If you're getting four or more infections a year, or symptoms don't clear with treatment, get checked, since it may be something else or a resistant yeast.
Knee swelled up big after hiking and it's hot and red, plus I feel feverish. Gonna wrap it and rest.

Don't just wrap it. A hot, red, swollen knee with fever can be a joint infection, which can damage the joint quickly and needs antibiotics, sometimes drainage. Go to urgent care or the ER today so they can examine it and likely test fluid from the joint.
Is it ok to go to the gym with a cold? just a runny nose

If it's only above-the-neck symptoms like a runny nose or a mild sore throat, light to moderate exercise is generally fine. Dial back the intensity and wipe down equipment so you don't spread it. If you have a fever, body aches, chest congestion, or a deep cough, rest instead until those have passed.
quick q - are blue light glasses worth it for eye strain

The evidence that blue light glasses reduce eye strain is weak, so they're mostly not worth paying extra for. Screen strain mainly comes from staring and blinking less. Try the 20-20-20 rule (every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds), use artificial tears, and set up good lighting. If strain persists, an eye exam may turn up a small prescription that helps far more.
I've read that magnesium helps migraines. how much should I take?

Magnesium does have decent evidence for migraine prevention, and studies commonly use around 400 to 600 mg a day, often as magnesium citrate or glycinate. Start lower to avoid diarrhea, which is the main side effect, and give it two to three months to judge. Check with your doctor first if you have kidney problems or take other medications, since magnesium can interfere with absorption of some antibiotics.
Got a tooth pulled yesterday and I'm dying for a cigarette. How long do I really have to wait?

Wait at least 72 hours if you can, because smoking dramatically raises your risk of dry socket, a very painful condition where the protective blood clot comes out of the socket. Both the sucking motion and the chemicals interfere with healing, so a nicotine patch is a much safer way to get through the craving. If you absolutely can't hold off, put gauze over the site, but every extra day you manage helps.
Upper stomach pain after fatty meals, kind of under my right ribs, lasts an hour or two. 45F

Pain under the right ribs after fatty meals is a typical pattern for gallstones, so it's worth seeing your doctor, who will likely order an ultrasound. Smaller, lower-fat meals can reduce attacks while you wait. Go to the ER if the pain lasts more than several hours or comes with fever. The same applies if you notice yellow skin or eyes, dark urine or pale stools, since those suggest a blocked or infected gallbladder.
can i eat sushi pregnant? craving it SO bad

Raw fish is usually off the menu during pregnancy because of the risk of listeria and parasites, but you can still scratch the itch. Cooked rolls like shrimp tempura, eel, California rolls with cooked imitation crab, and veggie rolls are all fine. Just steer clear of high-mercury fish like king mackerel and swordfish, even when cooked.
I'm 68 and on blood thinners. Cut my forearm on a cabinet edge, it keeps oozing even after 20 minutes of pressure.

Twenty minutes of steady oozing on a blood thinner is reason to get seen, so please go to urgent care or call your doctor now. Meanwhile, keep firm, unbroken pressure on it with a clean pad, and hold your arm raised. Don't stop taking your medication on your own, but do tell the staff which blood thinner you take. Older skin also tears easily, and a skin flap may need special closure strips rather than stitches.
My daughter (8) keeps getting headaches after school, like 3-4 times a week now. Is this just dehydration or should I worry

Dehydration, skipped meals, poor sleep and screen time are common culprits, so it's worth tightening those up. Still, headaches 3 to 4 times a week deserve a visit to her pediatrician, partly because vision problems are a frequent and easily fixed cause at this age. Keep a quick log of when the headaches start, how long they last and what she was doing. Get her seen promptly if a headache wakes her from sleep, comes with vomiting in the morning, or involves weakness, confusion or changes in her vision.
My doctor wants to start me on medication but I'd rather try diet and exercise first. Is that unreasonable?

It's a reasonable conversation to have, and for mildly raised pressure with low overall risk, a few months of lifestyle changes is often acceptable. If your numbers are high, or you have diabetes, kidney disease or a heart condition, medication now is usually the safer choice. Ask your doctor for a specific target and a recheck date so the trial has a clear deadline.
My doctor told me to rest for 2 weeks after bronchitis but that's ridiculous, I always bounce back fast. Can I ignore it?

I'd follow your doctor's advice. They know the specifics of your case, and bronchitis can linger or turn into pneumonia if you push too hard too soon. Bouncing back fast before doesn't guarantee it this time. If two weeks feels excessive, call and ask whether gentle walking is okay in the meantime.
honestly just tired of everything lately

That sounds heavy, and I'm glad you said it. Has this been going on for a couple of weeks or more? Is it affecting your sleep, appetite or interest in things? If so, it's worth talking to a doctor, because depression often shows up as exactly this kind of tiredness. And if 'tired of everything' ever turns into thoughts of not wanting to be alive, please reach out to a crisis line like 988 in the US or someone you trust right away.
lol is it true orgasms can cause headaches?? happened twice now

Yes, it's a real thing called primary headache associated with sexual activity, and it's usually harmless. Still, a sudden explosive headache during sex the first time it happens should be checked, because it can occasionally signal bleeding or a vessel problem. Since it's happened twice, see a doctor for an evaluation. Head to the ER if one is severe and abrupt or comes with neck stiffness or vomiting.
threw up 3 times this morning, think its food poisoning from sushi. what now

Let your stomach rest for an hour or two, then start taking small sips of water or an electrolyte drink every few minutes rather than gulping. Once you've kept fluids down for a few hours, try bland foods like crackers, rice or toast. Most food poisoning passes within a day or two. See a doctor if you can't keep any fluids down for 12 hours, notice blood in your vomit or stool, have a high fever, feel dizzy when standing, or aren't improving after 2 days.
Rolled my ankle playing basketball 2 hours ago. Swollen, can walk on it but it hurts. Ice or heat?

Use ice for the first couple of days, about 15 to 20 minutes at a time with a cloth between the ice and your skin. Keep the ankle elevated and use a compression wrap. Heat early on can increase swelling, so save it for later if the ankle feels stiff. Since you can walk on it, it's likely a sprain, but get an X-ray if you have tenderness right on the bony knobs of the ankle or can't manage four steps. Start gentle range-of-motion movements after a couple of days, because that speeds recovery.
I'm 34 and pregnant (28 weeks) and my pelvis/lower back aches constantly. Is this normal and what can I do?

Pelvic girdle and lower back pain are very common in the third trimester as ligaments loosen and your posture shifts, and they usually ease after birth. A pregnancy support belt, a pillow between your knees when you sleep, keeping your knees together when you get out of bed or a car, and taking smaller steps can all help a lot. Ask your midwife about a referral to a women's health physiotherapist. Call your maternity unit promptly if the pain comes in rhythmic waves, or if you have bleeding, fluid leaking or a fever, since that can signal early labour or an infection.
What vaccines should my 70 year old parents actually be getting? They're confused by all the news.

The core vaccines for people over 65 are a yearly flu shot (a high-dose or enhanced version is preferred), a pneumonia vaccine, the two-dose Shingrix series for shingles, and an updated COVID vaccine. RSV vaccine is recommended for adults 75 and older, and for those 60 to 74 with certain health conditions. They should also have a tetanus booster every ten years. Their doctor or pharmacist can pull up their records and tell them exactly which ones they're missing.
ok so i used bleach mixed with water on a fungal spot on my foot, it burns like crazy. did i mess up

Yes, rinse it now with plenty of cool running water for at least 10 to 15 minutes, because bleach can cause chemical burns. Don't put more home remedies on it. Afterwards, keep it clean and covered loosely. If you see blistering, open raw skin, worsening pain or signs of infection, get it seen promptly. Once it's healed, treat the fungus with an over-the-counter terbinafine or clotrimazole cream, which works without damaging your skin.
how much water should a 75 yo drink? my mom barely drinks anything

A reasonable target for most older adults is about 6 to 8 cups of fluid a day, though her doctor may set a different amount if she has heart or kidney problems. Thirst signals weaken with age, so she may genuinely not feel thirsty. Offer drinks at set times, like with every meal and medication, and count soups, fruit and herbal tea. Watch for dark urine, dizziness or new confusion, which suggest she's dehydrated and should see her doctor.
My 6 year old has a nosebleed and my husband is telling her to tip her head back. Is that right??

Actually, have her lean slightly forward instead, because tipping back sends blood down her throat, which can make her gag or vomit. Pinch the soft part of her nose just below the bony bridge firmly and continuously for 10 to 15 minutes without peeking, and have her breathe through her mouth. If it's still going strong after 20 minutes of steady pressure, or it followed a hard knock to the head, take her to be seen.
I keep checking that my door is locked like 10+ times before I leave. Weird?

It's not weird, but checking ten or more times and feeling unable to stop can be a sign of OCD, which is common and very treatable. A useful test is whether it eats up time, causes real distress, or makes you late. If it does, see a doctor or a therapist who does exposure and response prevention (ERP), the most effective treatment for this. Taking a photo of the locked door to check later is a quick fix that can sometimes feed the habit, so it's better addressed properly.
Elbow hurts on the outside when I grip stuff, I play tennis like 4x a week

That's very likely tennis elbow, an overload of the tendons that extend your wrist where they attach on the outside of the elbow. Ease up on playing for a few weeks, use a counterforce strap just below the elbow, and start slow eccentric wrist exercises, which have good evidence behind them. Having a pro check your grip size and backhand technique can help prevent it coming back. It can take a few months to settle fully, so see a physical therapist if it's not improving after six weeks.
Splashed bleach in my eye cleaning the bathroom!!

Rinse it right now under lukewarm running water for at least 15 to 20 minutes, holding the eyelids open, and take out contact lenses if you're wearing them. Don't rub it or put anything else in it. After flushing, get seen urgently at an ER or eye clinic, or call poison control on the way, because chemical eye injuries can cause damage that isn't obvious at first.
heart randomly pounding like crazy while i'm just sitting on the couch. like 150. it stopped after 10 min. what was that

A sudden jump to 150 at rest that switches off abruptly is often a rhythm problem such as SVT. It's usually not dangerous in a healthy person, but it does need proper diagnosis. Book an appointment with your doctor and mention that it started and stopped suddenly. If it happens again, try to get it recorded on an ECG or a smartwatch. If an episode comes with fainting, chest pain or real shortness of breath, or won't stop, go to the emergency department.
Had a concussion in a soccer game 4 days ago. Headache is mostly gone. Can I train hard this weekend to prove I'm fine?

Please don't train hard this weekend, because getting hit or overexerting your brain before a concussion fully heals can make it much worse and can even be dangerous. The standard approach is a step-by-step return to sport, starting with light exercise and moving up only if symptoms don't come back, ideally with a doctor or trainer guiding it. You'll need to be fully symptom-free, including headaches, before any contact or intense training. Proving you're fine isn't worth risking a longer recovery.
Doc gave me metronidazole. Friend's wedding is Saturday. How bad is it really if I drink?

With metronidazole it really can be bad: alcohol can cause flushing, pounding headache, vomiting and a racing heart, and it can wreck your night. You need to avoid alcohol for the whole course and for at least 48 hours after your last dose. If the timing doesn't work, toast with something nonalcoholic. Don't skip doses so you can drink, because that risks the infection coming back.
I keep getting UTIs, like 4 this year. Can I just get a stash of antibiotics to keep at home?

Some doctors do exactly that for people with recurrent UTIs. It's called patient-initiated therapy, so it's a fair thing to ask about. With four in a year, it's also worth a proper workup, including a urine culture to confirm the bacteria and their sensitivities, and possibly checking for underlying causes. Options like low-dose preventive antibiotics, vaginal estrogen after menopause, or post-sex dosing can cut recurrences a lot. Bring up all of it with your doctor or a urologist.
on chemo, my grandson is getting his MMR next week, is that a risk for me?

The MMR vaccine almost never spreads from the vaccinated person to others, so your grandson getting it doesn't put you at risk and actually helps protect you from measles. Experts recommend that household contacts of people on chemo stay fully up to date on vaccines. Mention it to your oncology team anyway, especially if he's getting other vaccines at the same visit, such as the rotavirus vaccine for babies, which calls for careful handwashing after diaper changes, or the nasal flu spray, which isn't recommended for people around severely immunocompromised patients.
Quick q: is 10,000 IU vitamin D daily too much? Doc never told me my levels

That's above the 4,000 IU daily upper limit for adults, and taking it long-term without knowing your levels risks high calcium, kidney stones and other problems. Some people do need that dose short-term to correct a deficiency, but only with blood monitoring. Drop to 1,000 to 2,000 IU for now and ask your doctor for a 25-hydroxy vitamin D test so you can dose based on actual numbers.
my legs feel crawly and I have to move them at night, it's driving me crazy

That sounds a lot like restless legs syndrome, which is common and treatable. Low iron is a frequent and fixable cause, so ask your doctor to check your ferritin. Caffeine, alcohol, nicotine and some antihistamines and antidepressants can make it worse. Stretching, a warm bath or leg massage before bed often help in the meantime.
My dog's flea meds are cheap. Could I put a drop on my itchy bug bites?

Don't use pet flea medication on yourself. Those products are pesticides dosed for animals, and they can be toxic or irritating to human skin. For itchy bites, use a cold compress, 1% hydrocortisone cream or calamine, and an oral antihistamine at night if the itch is keeping you up. If you suspect fleas are biting you, treat the pets and your home, and the bites will stop.
I had a mild heart attack 3 weeks ago. I want to start jogging again.

Please don't start jogging on your own yet. Ask your doctor about a cardiac rehab program, which is the safest way back to exercise after a heart attack. In rehab, your exercise is monitored and your intensity is set based on testing. In the meantime, gentle walking within whatever limits your doctor gave you is the right level. Stop and get help right away if you have chest pain, unusual breathlessness, or dizziness.
can i take tylenol and advil at the same time or is that bad

Yes, you can, and it often works better than either one alone because they relieve pain in different ways. Take each at its normal label dose, either together or staggered a few hours apart. Keep healthy adults under about 3,000 to 4,000 mg of acetaminophen a day, which means checking cold and flu products that sneak it in, and under 1,200 mg of ibuprofen a day unless a doctor tells you otherwise. If you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers or take blood thinners, ask a pharmacist before adding the ibuprofen.
My mom is 82 and keeps forgetting whether she took her morning pills, so sometimes she takes them twice. Any tricks?

A weekly pill organizer with separate morning and evening compartments is the simplest fix, because an empty slot answers the question instantly. If she's still confused with that, an automatic dispenser that unlocks one dose at a time and beeps is worth the cost. Also ask her pharmacist which of her meds would be risky if doubled, since things like blood thinners or diabetes pills make this more urgent. Mention the memory slips to her doctor too, because new forgetfulness deserves a look.
Had a fever for 2 days, now I'm shivering, heart racing, feel really out of it, and peeing hardly anything. Just flu?

Those signs together—shaking chills, a racing heart, confusion and very little urine—can point to sepsis, so don't wait it out at home. Go to the ER now or call emergency services if you're too unwell to get there safely. Sepsis is very treatable when it's caught early, but it can deteriorate quickly, so getting seen promptly really matters.
what vitamins should my 75 year old parents be taking

Most older adults don't need a pile of supplements. The common gaps are vitamin D, B12 and calcium, so ask their doctor to check D and B12 levels with a blood test rather than guessing. B12 absorption drops with age and with medications like metformin and acid reducers, and low levels can cause fatigue, numbness and memory problems. Run any supplement past their pharmacist first, because things like vitamin K, fish oil and St. John's wort interact with common heart and blood-thinning drugs.
i've had a cough for 5 weeks now after a cold. everything else is gone. normal?

A post-viral cough can hang on for three to eight weeks, so this can be normal, but five weeks is long enough that it's worth getting checked. A doctor can look for things that keep a cough going, like postnasal drip, reflux, asthma triggered by the infection, or whooping cough. Go sooner if you're coughing up blood, losing weight, short of breath, or have night sweats or a fever.
MY MOM IS 84 AND HAS CHEST PAIN BUT SAYS ITS JUST INDIGESTION. SHE DOESNT WANT ME TO CALL ANYONE

Call emergency services now, even if she objects. In older women, heart attacks often feel like indigestion, nausea, jaw or back pain, or unusual fatigue rather than classic crushing chest pain. While you wait, keep her seated and calm, and if she isn't allergic and hasn't been told to avoid it, the dispatcher may advise chewing an aspirin. It's far better to be wrong about indigestion than to wait on a heart attack.
38 weeks and water might've broken?? just a trickle, not a gush. can i wait till morning

Call labor and delivery now rather than waiting, even if it's just a trickle and you're not having contractions. Once your water breaks, the risk of infection starts climbing, and they'll want to check you and the baby. Note the time it started and whether the fluid is clear, green or brown, because green or brown fluid means you should head in right away.
my 14yo son had mono and wants to play football next week. doctor said wait but he's feeling fine now. is the doctor being overcautious?

The doctor isn't being overcautious, because mono can enlarge the spleen even when your son feels completely fine, and a hit in football can rupture it, which is a genuine emergency. The usual guidance is no contact sports for at least three to four weeks from when symptoms started, sometimes longer, and the doctor should be the one to clear him. Light activity like walking or gentle shooting drills without contact may be okay in the meantime if the doctor agrees. I know it's frustrating for him, but this is one rule worth sticking to.
do blue light glasses actually do anything

Not much, according to the evidence. Studies haven't found that blue light from screens damages the eyes, and blue-light glasses don't noticeably reduce eye strain. Most screen fatigue comes from blinking less and focusing for too long, so regular breaks, artificial tears and an up-to-date prescription help far more. Cutting screen time before bed may help you sleep, though.
My teenage son wants to use his friend's leftover antibiotics for acne. Harmless right?

Not a great idea. Acne antibiotics like doxycycline or minocycline work only with steady use over months and are usually paired with topical treatments, so a few borrowed pills won't help and can cause side effects. A doctor or dermatologist can build a proper plan, often starting with benzoyl peroxide and a retinoid. That approach works better and avoids needless antibiotic use.
I don't have a spleen (removed after an accident). My dog licked a small cut on my hand and then nipped me lightly. Overreacting?

You're not overreacting, because people without a spleen are at risk of a rare but rapidly dangerous infection from bacteria found in dog mouths, called Capnocytophaga. Wash the area thoroughly now and call your doctor today about preventive antibiotics, which are commonly recommended for this situation. If you develop a fever, chills or feel unwell in the coming days, go to the ER and tell them about the bite and that you have no spleen.
I'm a nurse and my hands are cracked and bleeding from washing them constantly. Any fix?

Hand dermatitis is really common in healthcare work, and the biggest fix is applying a thick fragrance-free cream or ointment after every wash and a heavy layer at bedtime under cotton gloves. Use alcohol-based sanitizer when appropriate, since it's often gentler than repeated soap and water, and pat your hands dry thoroughly. If the cracks don't heal in a couple of weeks or look infected, see occupational health or a dermatologist, since a prescription cream or patch testing for a glove or soap allergy may help.
can i just take like 4 ibuprofen at once for my knee, 2 isn't doing anything

Don't double up on your own. Four standard 200 mg tablets is 800 mg, which is a prescription-level dose that raises the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain, especially if you take it regularly or drink alcohol. Stick to the label dose. You can alternate or combine it with acetaminophen, which works differently, and add ice and rest for the knee. If the pain needs more than that, have a doctor look at the knee and decide on stronger treatment safely.
been staring at screens 12 hrs a day and my eyes burn by evening. normal?

Very common. When you focus on a screen you blink much less, so your eyes dry out and get tired. Try the 20-20-20 habit: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Preservative-free artificial tears and keeping the screen slightly below eye level can help too. If the burning continues after a couple of weeks of changes, or your vision gets blurry, get a regular eye exam, because an outdated prescription is often part of the problem.
My doctor wants me on meds but I'd rather try diet and exercise first for 6 months. Is that dumb?

It's not dumb, but whether it's safe depends on how high your numbers are and what other risks you have. For mild hypertension, a few months of lifestyle changes is often a reasonable trial. At higher levels or with diabetes or kidney disease, waiting carries real risk. Ask your doctor if you can do a monitored trial with home readings and a set check-in date.
do i really need to go to the ER for chest pain that went away after 10 min? feel fine now

Yes, you should still get checked today, because chest pain that comes and goes can be unstable angina, which often comes right before a heart attack.
