Doctors can run an ECG and blood tests to look for heart strain even after the pain has stopped, but the results are most useful soon after the episode. Go to the ER now, especially if you're over 40 or have risk factors like smoking, diabetes, high blood pressure or high cholesterol. Call 911 if the pain comes back.
quick one - can I drink alcohol on insulin

Yes, in moderation, but alcohol can cause delayed lows for many hours, even overnight. Always drink with food, don't skip your carbs, and check your sugar before bed, possibly with a small snack. Wear a medical ID, because a severe low can look like drunkenness to other people.
my bunny nipped me. rabies?

Pet rabbits kept indoors are extremely unlikely to have rabies, and rabbit bites almost never require rabies shots. Just wash the nip with soap and water and keep it clean. If your rabbit spends time outdoors and was attacked by a wild animal recently, mention that to a doctor to be safe.
Sudden curtain over part of my vision in my right eye this morning, plus a bunch of new floaters and flashes. Probably just tired?

That's not tiredness. New flashes, a shower of floaters, and a curtain or shadow over your vision are classic signs of a retinal detachment. Go to an eye emergency service or ER today, not next week, because the sooner it's repaired the better your chance of keeping your vision.
I'm 68 and just getting over pneumonia. How soon can I get back to my walking group?

Pneumonia takes real time to recover from, especially in your late 60s, so expect weeks rather than days. Start with short, slow walks around home, maybe 5 to 10 minutes, and add a few minutes every couple of days as long as your breathing stays comfortable. Rejoin the group once you can manage a similar distance on your own without getting badly winded. It's a good idea to ask your doctor at your follow-up visit whether there's anything specific you should watch for.
can i eat sushi pregnant yes or no

Cooked or vegetarian rolls like shrimp tempura, eel or California rolls are a yes. Raw fish is generally a no, because of the risk of listeria and parasites. High-mercury fish like swordfish, king mackerel and bigeye tuna are worth avoiding even when cooked.
I'm 58 and I've had a heavy, squeezing feeling in my chest for about 20 minutes, kind of spreading to my left arm. Probably just indigestion right?

Don't assume it's indigestion. Twenty minutes of squeezing chest pressure spreading to your arm is a classic heart attack pattern, so call emergency services right now rather than driving yourself. If you aren't allergic and haven't been told to avoid it, chewing a regular 325 mg aspirin while you wait can help, but the call comes first.
I accidentally took my lisinopril twice this morning, I forgot I already had it. Am I going to be ok??

One accidental double dose of lisinopril is usually not dangerous for most people, so take a breath. The main thing to watch for over the next several hours is low blood pressure: dizziness, lightheadedness when standing, or feeling faint. Stand up slowly, drink some water, and skip nothing else unless your doctor says so. Call your pharmacist or Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 for personalized advice, and seek emergency care if you faint, feel very weak or notice swelling of your lips or tongue.
I'm on an SSRI. Can I add St John's Wort to give it a boost?

Please don't combine them. St. John's Wort with an SSRI can cause serotonin syndrome, which can be dangerous, with agitation, fever, rapid heart rate and muscle twitching. It also interferes with many other medications, including birth control. If your antidepressant doesn't feel like it's doing enough, tell your prescriber, because a dose change or a different medication is the safer route.
pregnant 33 weeks, bp was 145/95 today and i have a headache that won't go away and see spots

Go to labor and delivery or the ER now, or call your maternity unit right away. High blood pressure with a persistent headache and vision changes at 33 weeks can be preeclampsia, which needs same-day assessment. Don't wait to see if it settles.
Does the HPV vaccine still make sense at 35? Married, monogamous.

It's approved up to age 45, but after 26 it's a shared decision rather than a routine recommendation, because the benefit drops if you've likely already been exposed. Being in a monogamous relationship lowers your future risk further, so the benefit may be modest. It's worth discussing with your doctor if you think your situation could change or you have specific concerns, but skipping it at 35 is a reasonable choice for many people.
Ugh my BP is like 128/82 every time. Do I really need to do anything or is that fine

It's not an emergency, but it's worth acting on now while it's easy to bring down. That range is elevated to stage 1, and lifestyle changes alone often fix it. Cutting salt, walking most days, drinking less alcohol, and losing a few pounds if you're overweight can each lower it several points. Recheck in a few months and keep your doctor in the loop.
My 15 year old's bp was 135/85 at the sports physical. Should I be worried?

That reading is high for a 15-year-old, so it's worth following up on, though there's no need to panic. Teens often read high at a single check because of nerves, caffeine or a cuff that's the wrong size. Ask the pediatrician to recheck it on a couple of separate visits, because if it stays high they'll want to rule out underlying causes.
My kid's EpiPen expired last month. She also has asthma. Is it still safe to keep around as a backup or toss?

Keep it as a backup until the new one arrives, but replace it right away. Recently expired epinephrine still works in an emergency, just a bit less strongly, and that matters more for a kid with asthma, who's at higher risk of a severe reaction. If the liquid in the window looks discolored or has particles, it's no good. Call her doctor or pharmacy today for a refill, and set a reminder for the next expiration date.
I get anxious calling people on the phone, like I'll put off booking a doctor's appointment for weeks. Is that weird?

It's not weird. Phone anxiety is really common, especially among people who grew up texting. For the short term, use workarounds without guilt: online booking, email, or asking a friend to sit with you while you call. Writing a quick script of what you'll say helps too. If the avoidance is starting to cost you things like healthcare, jobs or money, that leans more toward social anxiety, and CBT is very effective for it. Please do book that doctor's appointment, though, even if it has to be online.
can i do pilates

Usually yes, and Pilates can be great for core and pelvic floor strength during pregnancy, ideally in a prenatal class or with an instructor who knows you're pregnant. Skip moves that have you lying flat on your back for long after the first trimester, deep twisting, and anything that makes your belly cone or bulge down the middle. Check with your provider first if you have complications like placenta previa or a short cervix.
can i crush my moms pills so she can swallow them easier

Not without checking first. Some pills, like extended-release, enteric-coated, or some capsules, become dangerous or useless when crushed because the whole dose hits at once. Call her pharmacist with the list. They can tell you which are safe to crush and often offer liquid or smaller versions of the rest. If she's having real trouble swallowing, mention it to her doctor, since that can signal a swallowing problem worth evaluating.
We had sex and now I'm cramping a bit and there's a tiny bit of spotting. 22 weeks. Did we hurt the baby?

Very unlikely, because the baby is well protected, and the cervix is more sensitive and bleeds easily in pregnancy, so a bit of spotting after sex is fairly common. Mild cramping that settles with rest is usually from orgasm or the uterus tightening. Call your provider if the bleeding becomes more than spotting, the cramps turn rhythmic or painful, or you notice fluid leaking.
My 4 year old shoved a bead in his ear. I have tweezers. Should I just grab it out?

Skip the tweezers, because round beads tend to slip further in when you try to grip them, and a wriggling kid makes it easy to scratch the canal or hit the eardrum. If the bead is clearly visible right at the opening, you can try tilting his head so that ear faces down and gently shaking. Otherwise a doctor or urgent care can remove it quickly with the right tools. If he has pain, bleeding, or discharge, get him seen promptly.
my dog ate something and I'm throwing up too lol jk. but real q: how long does stomach flu last

Stomach flu (viral gastroenteritis) usually lasts one to three days, though some people feel tired or off for up to a week. It spreads easily, so wash your hands with soap, since sanitizer doesn't kill norovirus well, and clean surfaces with bleach. You're typically contagious for at least a couple of days after symptoms stop. See a doctor if you get dehydrated, have bloody diarrhea, or aren't improving after three days.
My doctor wants me to start insulin for type 2. Does that mean I failed?

No. Type 2 diabetes tends to progress over time as the pancreas makes less insulin, so many people eventually need insulin no matter how well they've managed. Starting insulin is a tool to protect your eyes, kidneys, and nerves from high sugar, not a judgment of your efforts. Many people feel better once their numbers come down, and the needles are much smaller and easier than most people expect.
Stepped on a rusty nail in the garden. Tiny hole, barely bled. Last tetanus shot was... maybe 2012?

Puncture wounds look minor, but they're the classic tetanus risk, and you're likely due for a booster. Get one within the next day or two at a pharmacy, GP or urgent care. Wash the wound well with soap and running water, then keep it clean and covered. Watch it over the next few days, and get seen if redness spreads or it swells, throbs or drains pus, since foot punctures can get infected deep under the skin.
I'm on chemo and my temp is 100.5. Do I really need to call? It's 2am.

Yes, call now. Your oncology team wants that call at 2am. A fever during chemo can mean a serious infection while your immune system is low, and it often needs urgent antibiotics. If you can't reach them, go to the ER and tell them you're on chemotherapy.
found a stray kitten and it scratched me pretty deep. do I need a rabies shot or is that overkill

Not overkill. Contact your doctor or local health department today, because a deep scratch from an unknown stray is the kind of exposure they want to assess. Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms start, but post-exposure shots work extremely well if given promptly. Wash the scratch thoroughly with soap and running water for 15 minutes now, and if the kitten can be safely confined, it can be observed, which may spare you the shots.
my fingers went white and numb after shoveling snow, now they're red and burning. rub them hard to warm up?

Don't rub them, because friction can damage cold-injured tissue. Warm them in lukewarm water, around body temperature, for 15 to 30 minutes, or tuck them into your armpits, and avoid heaters or hot water since numb skin burns easily. Burning and redness as they rewarm is typical of frostnip, but blisters, skin that stays grey or hard, or numbness that doesn't return means you should get seen promptly.
I'm 30 and one tooth hurts only when I bite down on something hard, sharp pain then gone. Weird?

Sharp pain that comes only when you bite down and then quickly disappears is a classic sign of a cracked tooth, especially if there's a filling in it or you grind your teeth. Cracks tend to spread over time and can eventually reach the nerve or split the tooth, so see a dentist within the next couple of weeks. Until then, chew on the other side and avoid hard foods like ice, nuts, and hard candy.
Quick q - is it fine to take my wife's nitroglycerin spray for my chest pain? Same symptoms she gets.

Don't use her nitroglycerin. It can drop your blood pressure dangerously, especially if you've taken erectile dysfunction medication or have certain heart conditions you may not know about. It would also mask what's actually going on. If your chest pain is happening right now, call emergency services. If it comes and goes, see a doctor soon so they can work out the cause and prescribe the right treatment for you.
Does peppermint tea actually help an upset stomach or is that a myth

It genuinely helps for some things, because peppermint relaxes the muscles of the gut, which can ease cramping, gas and IBS-type discomfort. The catch is that it also relaxes the valve at the top of your stomach, so it can make heartburn and reflux worse. Reach for it for crampy, gassy discomfort and skip it if your problem is burning in your chest or throat, where ginger tea is a better bet for nausea.
can lack of sleep actually kill you?

Directly it's extremely rare, but indirectly it absolutely can. Drowsy driving causes a large number of fatal crashes each year. Long-term short sleep is linked to heart disease, stroke, diabetes and a weaker immune system. Untreated sleep apnea in particular raises cardiovascular risk significantly. Sleep is a basic health need, not a luxury.
just found out im pregnant and ive been using tretinoin cream for acne. how bad is this

Stop the tretinoin now, but try not to panic, because the amount absorbed through the skin from topical use is very small and the risk is considered low. It's still on the avoid list because oral retinoids are known to cause birth defects, so tell your provider at your first appointment so they have the full picture. Azelaic acid is a commonly recommended pregnancy-safe alternative for acne. If you were ever taking oral isotretinoin (Accutane), call your doctor right away.
60 yo man. tearing pain in chest going straight through to my back, came on super sudden. what is it

Call emergency services immediately. Sudden, severe, tearing pain that goes through to the back is a warning sign of aortic dissection, a tear in the body's main artery that needs urgent treatment. Don't take aspirin and don't drive yourself. Stay still and wait for the ambulance.
Can I just take a bunch of Tums? Like 10? Heartburn is killing me.

Don't take 10 at once; stick to the dose on the label, which is usually 2 to 4 tablets, and don't go over the daily maximum. Too much calcium carbonate can cause constipation and, in larger amounts, raise your blood calcium enough to cause real problems. If the label dose isn't touching it, an H2 blocker like famotidine is a reasonable next step. If you have heartburn more than twice a week, or it feels like pressure in your chest or spreads to your arm or jaw, see a doctor promptly, since heart problems can masquerade as heartburn.
How do I make my parents' house safer from falls? They're both in their 80s.

The biggest wins are grab bars by the toilet and in the shower, a non-slip bath mat, and getting rid of loose rugs and cords. Add bright lighting, nightlights from bedroom to bathroom, and sturdy railings on both sides of the stairs. Keep everyday items at waist-to-shoulder height so nobody climbs on stools. Ask their doctor about a fall-risk review of their medications and about physical therapy or tai chi for balance.
Woke up and suddenly can't hear out of my left ear at all. No pain, no cold. Probably wax right? I'll just wait it out.

Don't wait this one out, because sudden hearing loss in one ear with no obvious cause can be sudden sensorineural hearing loss, which is a nerve problem rather than wax. It's treated most effectively with steroids started within the first few days, and the chances of recovery drop the longer it goes untreated. Get seen today at urgent care, an ENT or an emergency department, and say the words 'sudden hearing loss' so they take it seriously. If it turns out to be wax, great, but that's something to confirm, not assume.
Is the flu shot worth it if I'm healthy and 25?

Yes, it's worth it. Healthy young adults still get hit hard by flu, lose a week to it, and can pass it to more vulnerable people around them. Even in years when the match isn't perfect, the shot lowers your risk of getting sick and makes illness milder if you do catch it. It's quick, cheap or free at most pharmacies, and serious side effects are rare.
Is it okay to take ibuprofen for stomach cramps?

Ibuprofen is a poor choice for stomach pain, because it can irritate the stomach lining and make things worse, especially if an ulcer or gastritis is behind the cramps. For period cramps it works well when taken with food, but for gut cramps acetaminophen is gentler on the stomach. A heating pad and peppermint tea can also help with gassy or spasmy pain. If the cramps are severe, keep coming back, or come with fever or blood in your stool, have a doctor take a look.
omg my son just got stung by a bee and he's never been stung before, how do I know if he's allergic??

Most kids just get a red, swollen, painful spot at the sting site, which is a normal reaction even if the swelling gets fairly big over the next day. Scrape the stinger out with a fingernail or card, wash the area, and use a cold pack and an age-appropriate antihistamine if it's itchy. Call 911 right away if he develops hives away from the sting, swelling of the face, lips or tongue, wheezing, trouble breathing, vomiting, or if he becomes faint or floppy, which usually shows up within 30 minutes. Keep a close eye on him for the next hour or so and you'll know.
Is local honey actually good for allergies or is that a myth

It's mostly a myth. The pollen that triggers hay fever comes largely from wind-pollinated trees and grasses, not the flowers bees visit, and studies haven't shown honey reliably reduces symptoms. It's harmless for most adults, so there's no need to quit if you enjoy it. Never give honey to babies under 1, though, because of the botulism risk, and don't count on it in place of meds that actually work.
does dehydration really cause headaches or is everyone just obsessed with water

Dehydration genuinely can cause headaches, and it's a common trigger for migraines too. You don't need to chug gallons, though. Drink enough that your urine is pale yellow, and drink more in heat, after exercise, or after alcohol. If a big glass of water and a snack fixes your headache, that was probably part of it.
can i give my 10 year old aspirin for fever, out of everything else

Don't give aspirin to anyone under about 19 with a fever or a viral illness. It's linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition affecting the liver and brain. Run to a pharmacy or ask a neighbor for children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen instead. In the meantime, fluids, rest, and light clothing will keep her comfortable.
tetanus shot... last one was maybe 12 yrs ago. dog bite, small. need one?

Yes, after 12 years you're due. For any bite that broke the skin, a booster is recommended if it's been more than 5 years. Wash the bite well and get the shot at urgent care, a pharmacy that offers it or your doctor's office within the next day or two. While you're there, have them look at the bite.
My 2 year old has had a fever of 104 for three days and is really sleepy. Should I wait it out?

Don't wait. Have her seen today, at urgent care or the ER if your pediatrician can't fit her in. Three days of high fever in a toddler needs an exam to rule out things like an ear infection, a urinary infection or pneumonia. Unusual sleepiness is a red flag on its own. If she's hard to wake, floppy, breathing fast or not making wet diapers, go to the ER now.
bleeding a little bit, like pink when I wipe, 7 weeks. normal or not

Light pink spotting in early pregnancy is common and often harmless, but it's always worth a call to your provider so they can decide whether you need a check. Go in urgently or to the ER if the bleeding gets heavier like a period, you pass clots, or you have strong cramping or one-sided pain, especially with dizziness or shoulder pain. Those can signal a miscarriage or an ectopic pregnancy, which needs fast care.
Woke up with a pimple-like bump on my gum near a sore tooth. Should I pop it?

Don't pop it, because that bump is likely a gum boil draining an infected tooth. Squeezing can push bacteria deeper or into surrounding tissue. Rinse with warm salt water and see a dentist within a day or two, as the source usually needs a root canal or extraction even if the bump drains on its own. Go urgently if your face swells or you get a fever.
my stomach hurts after eating pizza every time, is that normal or am i dying lol

You're almost certainly not dying, but pain after the same food every time is worth paying attention to. Pizza combines fat, acidic tomato and often a lot of cheese, so common culprits are reflux, a sluggish response to fatty meals, or lactose intolerance. Try a week of smaller portions and maybe a lactose-free cheese option to see what changes. If the pain is sharp, sits under your right ribs, or comes with nausea or vomiting, get it checked, because that pattern can point to gallbladder trouble.
Is the 'neck rule' legit? Like if symptoms are above the neck it's ok to work out?

It's a reasonable rough guide. With a mild head cold, meaning a runny nose, sneezing, or a slight sore throat, light to moderate exercise is usually fine. If you have a fever, body aches, chest congestion, or stomach symptoms, rest until they clear. Even with above-the-neck symptoms, turn the intensity down and stop if you start feeling worse.
can i just take a bunch of tums, like 10 at once, my stomach is on fire

Don't take ten at once, because most regular-strength Tums cap out at around 7 to 10 tablets in a full 24 hours and too much calcium can cause its own problems. Take the dose on the label, give it 15 to 30 minutes, and sip some water while staying upright. If the burning is severe, spreads to your chest, arm, jaw or back, or comes with sweating or shortness of breath, call emergency services, because heart trouble can feel like heartburn. If the pain is still intense after the normal dose, that's a reason to get checked rather than to take more.
Is hydrogen peroxide good for cleaning a cat bite?

Skip the hydrogen peroxide, since it can damage healthy tissue and slow healing without cleaning much better than plain water. Rinse the bite under running water with mild soap for several minutes, which is what actually flushes out bacteria. Because cat bites are deep punctures with a high infection rate, it's worth having a doctor look at it, especially if it's on your hand.
Had food poisoning 4 days ago, feeling mostly normal. Running a 10k this weekend, should I go for it?

If you're eating normally, staying hydrated, and an easy run this week feels okay, you can probably do the 10k. Run it at a relaxed pace rather than chasing a time, and drink well beforehand. If that test run leaves you weak or brings your stomach symptoms back, skip the race this time.
Can I give my 8 month old honey for his cough? Natural remedy and all

No, honey isn't safe for babies under 12 months because it can contain spores that cause infant botulism, a serious illness. For his age, stick with saline drops and a nasal aspirator, a cool-mist humidifier, and plenty of breast milk or formula. Call his pediatrician if he has a fever over 100.4°F, is breathing fast, has trouble feeding, or seems unusually fussy or sleepy. Once he's past his first birthday, a little honey is a great cough remedy.
stinging eyes all the time, dry, worse at work. eye drops ok to use daily?

Preservative-free artificial tears are safe to use daily, even several times a day, and they're the go-to first step for dry eye. Avoid 'get the red out' redness-relief drops, because daily use causes rebound redness. Run a humidifier at your desk if you can and take regular screen breaks. If you still need drops constantly after a few weeks, an eye doctor can check for problems like blepharitis and offer stronger treatments.
fever 38.9 and burning when i pee, lower back hurts on one side. can i just drink cranberry juice

Cranberry juice won't be enough here. Fever, painful urination and one-sided back pain suggest the infection may have reached your kidney, which needs antibiotics. Get seen today at a doctor's office or urgent care. If you're vomiting and can't keep fluids down, go to the emergency department.
whats the fastest way to break a fever? ice bath?

Skip the ice bath. It causes shivering, which can actually push your core temperature up, and it's miserable. The quickest safe approach is a standard dose of acetaminophen or ibuprofen, light clothing, a cool room, and lots of fluids. A lukewarm sponge bath can help with comfort if you like, but the medicine does most of the work.
Gums bleed when I brush and one area aches. Should I stop brushing there so it heals?

Keep brushing there, gently, because bleeding gums usually come from plaque buildup, and skipping that spot makes it worse. Use a soft brush, floss once a day, and the bleeding often improves within a week or two. If the aching spot doesn't settle or you notice swelling, pus or a loose tooth, see a dentist, since that could be gum disease or a gum abscess.
Do I really need a hep B vaccine if I'm not doing drugs or sleeping around? Job wants it.

It's worth getting, especially if your employer wants it, which usually means you might come into contact with blood or body fluids at work, and that's a real way hepatitis B spreads. Hep B can also be spread through things like shared razors or a household member who doesn't know they're infected, and many people with chronic hep B have no symptoms. Vaccination is now recommended for all adults up to 59, the vaccine is very safe, and it protects for decades, and if your job requires it, your employer typically has to cover the cost.
ugh my 10 month old has diarrhea since yesterday, like 6 times today. still drinking ok. what do i do

Keep offering breast milk or formula as usual, and ask his pediatrician about adding an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte between feeds. Avoid juice, which can make diarrhea worse. Track his wet diapers closely. Fewer than 4 a day, a dry mouth, no tears or unusual sleepiness are signs of dehydration and mean he needs to be seen promptly. Also call his doctor if there's blood in the stool, he has a fever, he keeps vomiting, or it goes beyond a couple of days.
Pregnant, 30 weeks, can't get comfortable at night at all. Help.

Side sleeping, especially on your left, is generally recommended in the third trimester because it supports good blood flow to the baby. A pregnancy pillow or regular pillows between your knees, under your bump and behind your back can make a big difference. Small evening meals and staying upright after eating help with heartburn, and cutting back on fluids late in the evening can reduce bathroom trips. Ask your midwife or doctor before taking any sleep aid, and mention it if you snore heavily or have severe swelling or headaches.
I've had seasonal allergies for 20 years. Are allergy shots actually worth it or just a money grab?

For long-term seasonal allergies, allergy shots are one of the few treatments that actually change how your immune system responds rather than just masking symptoms. Many people see big improvements that last years after they finish. The catch is commitment: weekly visits at first, then monthly for about three to five years. After 20 years of symptoms, it's worth asking an allergist whether you're a good candidate, and whether under-the-tongue tablets might work for your specific pollens.
can i watch the eclipse with sunglasses if i only look for a few seconds

No. Even dark sunglasses let through enough light to burn the retina, and the damage is painless and can be permanent, so you won't feel it happening. Use certified eclipse glasses or a pinhole projector, and check that the glasses aren't scratched. The only time it's safe to look with bare eyes is during the brief moment of totality, if you're in the path of totality.
flu shot or nasal spray for my 6 year old, which is better

Both work well for most healthy kids, and the CDC doesn't prefer one over the other for a healthy 6-year-old, so the best one is whichever your child will actually get. The nasal spray is a live, weakened vaccine, so it's not suitable if your child has asthma with recent wheezing, a weakened immune system, or close contact with someone who is severely immunocompromised. If any of those apply, or you're not sure, go with the shot and let the pediatrician or pharmacist confirm.
how long am i contagious with a cold

You're most contagious in the first two to three days of symptoms, and you can spread it starting a day or so before you feel sick. Most people can still pass it on for up to about a week. Washing your hands often, coughing into your elbow and not sharing cups make a real difference. Once your fever is gone and you're mostly just sniffly, the risk drops a lot.
is it normal to feel a skipped heartbeat sometimes? like a flutter then a thump

Yes, that flutter-then-thump feeling is usually an extra beat, like a PVC or PAC, and most people get them at some point. Caffeine, alcohol, poor sleep, stress and dehydration all make them more frequent. Mention it at your next checkup, and see a doctor sooner if they're becoming very frequent or come in runs. Get seen urgently if they come with fainting, chest pain or breathlessness.
I think I have a UTI again. Can I buy antibiotics online without seeing anyone? I know what it feels like.

You likely do recognize it, but skip the sketchy online pills, since you can't be sure what's in them or whether they suit your infection. Plenty of legitimate telehealth services and pharmacies can treat a straightforward UTI quickly, often the same day. If UTIs keep coming back, it's worth getting a urine culture so you're treated with an antibiotic that actually works on your bacteria. Get seen in person promptly if you develop fever, back or side pain, or vomiting, because those suggest a kidney infection.
teen daughter wants HPV vaccine but I feel like it encourages sex? talk me thru it

Many parents worry about this, but large studies have consistently found that getting the HPV vaccine doesn't make teens start having sex earlier or take more sexual risks. The vaccine works best when given well before any exposure, which is why it's recommended at ages 11 to 12, and it prevents most cases of several cancers later in life, including cervical, throat and anal cancer. If she's asking for it herself, that's a great opening to talk about her health, and her pediatrician can answer questions with both of you there. If she's starting the series at 15 or older, she'll need three doses instead of two.
My dad's 78 and has a low fever and seems kind of confused today. He's usually sharp.

New confusion in an older adult with even a mild fever is a warning sign, often of an infection like a UTI, pneumonia, or sepsis, so he should be evaluated today. Take him to urgent care or the ER. Call 911 if he's very drowsy, breathing fast, or his skin looks mottled. Older people often don't run high fevers even when they're seriously ill.
Pregnant (24 weeks) and have a horrible cold. What's actually safe to take?

Acetaminophen at the regular dose is the go-to for aches and fever in pregnancy, and saline spray, a humidifier, honey, and warm fluids are all safe for congestion and cough. Avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs, and check with your OB or pharmacist before using any decongestants or combination cold products. Call your OB if you get a fever of 100.4°F or higher, since flu in pregnancy is treated promptly with antivirals.
got a bit of poison ivy on my arms after hiking. how bad is this gonna get

Poison ivy usually peaks over the first few days with red, itchy, sometimes blistering streaks, then clears in one to three weeks. Wash your skin, clothes, and gear with soap and water now to remove any oil left behind. Calamine, cool compresses, oatmeal baths, and 1% hydrocortisone help with the itch. See a doctor if it covers a large area or reaches your face, eyes, or genitals, because oral steroids work well then.
I've had a sore on my lower lip for like 2 months that scabs over and comes back. I'm a farmer, outside all day.

A lip sore that keeps healing and reopening for two months needs to be checked by a doctor or dermatologist. With years of sun exposure, it could be a precancer (actinic cheilitis) or an early skin cancer. These are very treatable when caught early. Use an SPF lip balm every day outdoors in the meantime, and try to get an appointment within the next couple of weeks.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and getting chest pain and shortness of breath, worse lying down. OB appt is Friday.

Don't wait until Friday. Call your OB's after-hours line or labor and delivery today. Some breathlessness is normal late in pregnancy, but chest pain on top of it needs prompt checking for things like a blood clot, preeclampsia or a pregnancy-related heart problem. Go to the emergency department right away if it's sudden or severe, you're coughing blood, your heart is racing, or you have a headache or swelling.
how much protein do i actually need. im 34, lift 4x a week

For someone lifting four times a week, about 1.6 grams of protein per kilo of bodyweight a day is a solid target. Going up to around 2.2 g/kg is fine but adds little for most people. For an 80 kg person that works out to roughly 130 to 175 grams. Spreading it over three or four meals of 25 to 40 grams each works better than cramming it into one sitting.
Cut my hand on a box cutter at work, a week ago. Healed mostly but my fingertip is still numb. Big deal?

Numbness that persists a week after a hand cut suggests a nerve may have been nicked, which is worth having checked. Book a GP or hand clinic appointment soon rather than waiting it out. Some nerve injuries recover better with early repair. In the meantime, be careful with heat and sharp objects on that fingertip, since you might not feel an injury.
how often should a type 2 diabetic get an A1C

Usually every three months if your treatment has recently changed or you're not at your target. Once you're stable and in range, every six months is typical. You should also be getting a yearly eye exam, kidney checks, and a foot exam, because those catch problems early.
flu shot gave me the flu last year so not getting it again

The flu shot can't give you the flu, because the injectable versions contain no live virus. Some people get a sore arm, mild aches or a low fever for a day or two as their immune system responds, which can feel flu-ish. You also could've caught a different virus around the same time, since shots are given during cold season. It's worth getting this year, since it lowers your odds of getting sick and makes a serious case much less likely.
is it ok to look at the eclipse for like a few seconds without glasses

No, even a few seconds of looking at the partially covered sun can burn the retina, and it doesn't hurt while it's happening, so you won't get a warning. Use proper ISO 12312-2 eclipse glasses or a simple pinhole projector instead. Regular sunglasses aren't nearly enough protection.
Wrist hurts and tingles at night, fingers numb, I type all day. Carpal tunnel?

That combination, especially numbness in your thumb, index and middle fingers that's worse at night, fits carpal tunnel syndrome well. A wrist splint that keeps your wrist straight while you sleep often helps a lot. During the day, take regular typing breaks and keep your wrists neutral rather than bent. See a doctor if it continues for more than a few weeks, if your hand feels weak or clumsy, or if you notice wasting at the base of your thumb, since ongoing nerve compression can cause lasting damage.
fever's gone, but still feeling foggy and tired after covid. Should I try HIIT to snap myself out of it?

HIIT isn't a good fix for post-viral fog and fatigue, because hard intervals can deepen the exhaustion and set back your recovery. Go for short, easy walks or light cycling where you can talk comfortably, and see how you feel the next day before adding more. Sleep, hydration and regular meals will do more for the fog right now. If it's still there after a few weeks, or exertion makes you crash, see your doctor.
Can allergies cause a sore throat or is that definitely a cold?

Allergies can cause a sore, scratchy throat, mainly from postnasal drip running down the back of your throat. That kind usually comes with itchy eyes, sneezing, and clear mucus, with no fever or body aches. Fever, aches, or a really painful throat with swollen glands point toward an infection instead. If it's severe, or you can't swallow well, get checked for strep.
is it bad to take expired cough medicine? like 2 years past

It's unlikely to be dangerous, but it may have lost some of its strength. Liquids are more prone to changes than tablets. If it looks cloudy, smells off, or has crystals in it, toss it. Given how cheap it is to replace, buying a fresh bottle is the better call, especially for kids' medicine, where accurate dosing matters.
sunburn is really bad, blistering on my shoulders, kinda chills too

Blistering plus chills points to a severe sunburn and possibly sun poisoning. Take cool showers, drink plenty of fluids, take ibuprofen for the pain and inflammation, and don't pop the blisters. See a doctor if the burn covers a large area, or you develop a fever, dizziness, confusion, vomiting, or signs of infection like pus or spreading redness. Stay out of the sun completely until it heals.
Diarrhea since starting clindamycin, like 8 times a day now. Normal?

Mild loose stools can happen on antibiotics, but eight times a day is too much, especially on clindamycin, which is strongly linked to C. diff, a serious gut infection. Call your prescriber today, and don't take anti-diarrhea medicine like loperamide until you've talked to them. Go to the ER if you see blood, have severe cramping or fever, or feel dizzy and dehydrated. Keep sipping fluids in the meantime.
lips tingle when i eat raw apples but cooked apple pie is fine. weird?

That's a classic pattern called oral allergy syndrome, usually linked to birch pollen allergy, where proteins in raw fruit resemble the pollen and cooking breaks them down. It's typically mild and confined to the mouth, so avoiding raw apples or peeling them often helps. Mention it to your doctor, and seek urgent care if you ever get throat tightness, swelling beyond the lips or trouble breathing.
what's the right way to take bp at home, my readings are all over the place

Sit with your back supported and your feet flat for five minutes first, with your arm resting at heart level and the cuff on bare skin. Don't talk, and skip caffeine, exercise and smoking for 30 minutes beforehand. Take two readings a minute apart, morning and evening, for a week, and average them. Also check the cuff fits your arm, because a cuff that's too small reads falsely high.
Is it bad that my blood pressure is 95/60? Everyone says low is good.

If you feel fine, 95/60 is often perfectly healthy, especially for younger, slim or very active people. It becomes a concern if you get dizziness, fainting, blurred vision, unusual fatigue or confusion, or if it's a sudden drop from your usual numbers. If you have those symptoms or recently started a new medication, it's worth checking in with your doctor.
We're planning to get pregnant in a couple months. Anything vaccine-wise I should do first?

Good timing to ask. Get a quick check of your immunity to rubella and chickenpox, because those live vaccines need to be given at least a month before you conceive and can't be given during pregnancy. Make sure your flu and COVID shots are current, since both are also safe during pregnancy. A preconception visit with your doctor is a great place to sort it all out, along with starting folic acid.
my jaw and teeth hurt every morning when i wake up

Morning jaw and tooth soreness is a classic sign of clenching or grinding your teeth at night, often linked to stress. A dentist can check for wear and fit you with a night guard, which protects your teeth and usually eases the soreness, and it's worth mentioning snoring if you have it because grinding can go along with sleep apnea. In the meantime, warm compresses, avoiding gum, and cutting back on caffeine and alcohol late in the day can help.
what's the fastest way to calm down from a panic attack

Slow your breathing with a long exhale, such as breathing in for 4 counts and out for 6 to 8, because this directly calms your nervous system. Ground yourself by naming a few things you can see, hear, and touch, and remind yourself that panic peaks within about 10 minutes and passes on its own. If these attacks happen regularly, CBT is very effective, and if you ever have chest pain or symptoms that feel different from your usual panic, get checked medically.
big toe joint suddenly red hot swollen overnight, can't stand the sheet on it

That's the textbook picture of gout, a flare caused by uric acid crystals forming in the joint. Get seen within a day or so to confirm it and start treatment, because the right anti-inflammatory or other medication can cut the attack short. If you also have a fever or feel unwell, go sooner, since an infected joint can look similar and is urgent. Meanwhile, rest and elevate the foot, use a cool pack, drink plenty of water, and avoid alcohol.
I'm 7 months pregnant and our cat scratched me pretty deep. Toxoplasmosis??

Toxoplasmosis mostly spreads through cat feces, such as litter boxes and contaminated soil, not through scratches, so this is unlikely to be the issue. A deep scratch can still get infected or cause cat scratch disease, so wash it thoroughly with soap and water and keep it clean and covered. Mention it to your OB, and call promptly if you notice spreading redness, swollen lymph nodes or fever. In the meantime, have someone else handle litter box duty.
I get a headache every single time I bend over or cough, started a month ago

A new headache triggered by coughing, straining or bending is worth getting checked, because it occasionally comes from a structural problem at the base of the skull or from changes in brain pressure. Book an appointment with your doctor in the next week or so, and they'll likely order imaging. Go sooner, or to the ER, if you develop vision changes, weakness, numbness or trouble walking.
Got my wisdom teeth out yesterday, I'm bored, can I hit the gym?

Give it at least three to four days before working out. Exercise raises your blood pressure, which can restart bleeding or dislodge the clot. If that clot comes out, you can get a dry socket, which is very painful. Light walking is fine in the meantime. When you go back, avoid heavy lifting or straining for the first week.
My Apple Watch keeps saying possible AFib. I feel fine though. Ignore?

Don't ignore it. AFib often causes no symptoms at all, yet it significantly raises stroke risk, and the watch's alert is reasonably accurate. Book an appointment with your doctor and bring the watch readings so they can confirm with a proper ECG. If you get stroke symptoms like face drooping, arm weakness or slurred speech, call emergency services immediately.
vertigo when i roll over in bed, room spins for like 30 sec. inner ear thing?

That pattern of brief spinning set off by turning over is classic BPPV, where tiny crystals in the inner ear have moved out of place. It's harmless and very treatable. A doctor or physical therapist can do the Epley maneuver, which often fixes it in one or two sessions, and you can learn to do it yourself at home once BPPV is confirmed. Get checked promptly instead if the vertigo comes with a severe headache, weakness, double vision, or trouble speaking or walking.
Kid (6) sleepwalks sometimes. Should I wake him up?

Don't try to fully wake him. It usually just confuses or upsets him. Gently guide him back to bed instead. Sleepwalking is common at that age and usually outgrown, and it's more likely when he's overtired, so a consistent, early enough bedtime helps. Make the house safe by locking outside doors and windows and gating stairs, and see his pediatrician if it's frequent, he gets hurt, or he snores heavily.
pain in my chest after the gym. pushes on one rib and it hurts more. did heavy bench today.

Pain that gets sharper when you press one specific rib, right after heavy bench, points strongly to a strained muscle or irritated rib cartilage rather than your heart. Rest from pressing movements for several days, use ice or heat, and an over-the-counter pain reliever is fine if it's safe for you. Get checked if it isn't improving within a week or two. Get urgent help if you develop pressure that spreads, breathlessness, sweating or nausea, because that would not fit a simple strain.
I have leftover Tamiflu from last year, can I just start it since I feel the flu coming on?

It's better to call your doctor or use a telehealth visit first. They can confirm it's likely flu and check that the leftover pills are a full course that hasn't expired. Partial courses are common with leftovers and won't treat it properly. Many clinics will prescribe quickly if you're within the first 48 hours, so reach out today rather than self-starting.
Newborn (10 days) seems a little yellow, especially his eyes. Breastfeeding going ok I think.

Some yellowing is common in the first couple of weeks, but you should call his doctor today rather than waiting for the next checkup. They'll likely want a quick bilirubin check, because high levels need treatment and jaundice that's still present or spreading at 10 days deserves a look. Call urgently if he's very sleepy, hard to wake for feeds, has pale stools or dark urine, or the yellow is spreading down to his belly and legs.
is it ok to put rice cereal in my 6 week olds bottle so he sleeps longer

Please don't. Cereal in the bottle raises the risk of choking and overfeeding. It also doesn't reliably help babies sleep longer, and at 6 weeks his gut isn't ready for solids anyway. Frequent waking is completely normal at this age because his stomach is tiny. If you're running on empty or worried about his feeding or weight gain, talk to his pediatrician, who can check that everything's on track and suggest safer ways to get you more rest.
can i just superglue a cut shut instead of going in for stitches

For a small, clean, shallow cut whose edges come together easily, medical-grade skin glue works well, and people do use household superglue in a pinch. Don't glue anything deep, gaping, dirty, or bleeding heavily, anything from a bite, or anything on a joint or your face. Those need proper cleaning and closure by a professional within a few hours. If you're asking because it looks like it needs stitches, it probably does.
Quick one - what's the best way to get rid of a wart on my finger?

Over-the-counter salicylic acid is the first choice. Soak the wart, file the top gently with an emery board you don't use for anything else, then apply the acid daily and cover it, and keep going for several weeks. Home freezing kits are another option, though they're less effective than the cryotherapy a doctor can do. Don't cut it off, and if it hasn't budged after about 12 weeks, or it's spreading or painful, see your GP.
I had chickenpox as an adult, spots are scabbing. Gym tomorrow?

Wait until every spot has crusted over before going to a shared gym, because you're contagious until then. That's especially important for anyone there who is pregnant or has a weak immune system. Adult chickenpox can also leave you quite drained, so when you do go back, keep the first few sessions light. Keep sweaty clothing off healing skin to lower the risk of infection.
can I take ibuprofen and go play basketball if I've got body aches from a virus?

I'd skip that plan. Body aches mean your body is still fighting the virus, and masking them with ibuprofen doesn't make it safe to exercise hard. It can also hide a fever and lead you to overexert yourself. Rest until the aches and any fever are gone, then come back with a lighter game.
dog bite on my hand from my own dog while breaking up a fight. small punctures, he's vaccinated. just a bandaid?

Hand bites get infected more often than people expect, even from a healthy, vaccinated dog, because the punctures are deep and narrow. Wash them thoroughly under running water with soap for several minutes. Then see a doctor today, since antibiotics are usually recommended for hand bites and they'll also check your tetanus status. Watch for swelling, throbbing, or trouble moving your fingers, which need prompt attention.
Got my COVID booster 2 hours ago and now my heart is racing and I feel lightheaded. probably just anxiety right?

It might be anxiety, but don't assume that. Sit or lie down now and have someone stay with you. If you have chest pain, trouble breathing, swelling of your face or throat, hives, or you feel like you might faint, call emergency services right away. Even if it settles, call your doctor or a nurse line today, because a racing heart after a vaccine is worth getting checked.
Explain allergy shots quickly. worth it?

Allergy shots expose you to gradually increasing doses of your allergens so your immune system becomes less reactive. The full course usually runs 3 to 5 years, with weekly shots at first and then monthly ones. They work well for pollen, dust mites, pet dander and insect venom, and the benefit often lasts years after you stop. They're worth considering if medications aren't cutting it, but they take commitment, and you'll wait in the office about 30 minutes after each shot in case of a reaction.
I've been throwing up 8-10 times a day, can't keep water down, 10 weeks. Everyone says morning sickness is normal so just push through?

That goes beyond ordinary morning sickness and could be hyperemesis gravidarum, which can cause dangerous dehydration if it isn't treated. Call your provider today, and go to urgent care or the ER if you can't keep fluids down for 12 hours or more, are urinating very little, or feel faint. There are safe, effective treatments like IV fluids and anti-nausea medications, so you shouldn't just tough it out.
ok so I got stung by a bee on my hand an hour ago and now my whole forearm is swollen and itchy but I can breathe fine. normal??

That sounds like a large local reaction, which is common and usually not dangerous on its own. Ice it, keep the arm elevated, and take an oral antihistamine like cetirizine to help with the itch and swelling, which can keep spreading for a day or two. Get emergency help right away if you develop hives elsewhere, throat tightness, wheezing, dizziness or vomiting. Mention this reaction to your doctor, since some people with big reactions benefit from an allergist review.
I'm 22 and my parents are divorcing and I feel like I'm falling apart even though I'm an adult. Is that weird?

Not weird at all. Your parents splitting up can shake your sense of home and family at any age, and adult children often get pulled into the middle in ways younger kids don't. Set some boundaries about not being either parent's confidant, and lean on friends. If it's affecting your sleep, studies, or work, a counselor can help a lot, and many colleges offer free sessions.
my toddler is allergic to eggs. can she get the flu shot?

Yes, she can get the flu shot, because current guidelines say kids with egg allergy can receive it safely, even if the allergy is severe. The amount of egg protein in flu vaccines is tiny, and serious reactions are extremely rare. Just mention the allergy to her doctor or nurse, and they'll have her wait the usual few minutes afterward.
Baby rolled off the bed, maybe 2 feet onto carpet. Cried right away then stopped. Shes 6 months

Crying right away and then settling is reassuring, and most short falls like this onto carpet turn out fine. Still, call your pediatrician to let them know, and watch her closely for the next 24 hours. Go to the ER if she vomits more than once, is unusually sleepy or hard to wake, won't feed, has a bulging soft spot or swelling on the head, or just isn't acting like herself. It's fine to let her nap, but check that she wakes normally.
I'm 31 weeks pregnant and my reading was 146/94 with some swelling in my face. Can it wait til my appointment next week?

Please don't wait a week. A reading that high with facial swelling at 31 weeks could be preeclampsia, which can get worse quickly. Call your maternity unit or OB today, and go straight in if you also have a headache, vision changes or pain under your right ribs.
what's the fastest way to fix jet lag, flying to tokyo next week

Light is your strongest tool. Once you land, get outdoor daylight in the morning Tokyo time and avoid bright light in the late evening, and switch to local mealtimes and bedtime right away. A low dose of melatonin, around 0.5 to 3 mg taken at local bedtime for a few nights, can help when traveling east. Keep naps under 30 minutes on day one, and go easy on alcohol on the flight.
my son (8) fell off his bike and has gravel stuck in his knee. how do i get it out

Rinse the knee under running water for a few minutes, which flushes out a lot of the grit, then gently pick out remaining pieces with tweezers cleaned with alcohol. Wash around it with mild soap, pat dry, and cover with a non-stick dressing. If there's gravel embedded deeply that won't come out, or a large dirty area, have a doctor clean it, because leftover grit can cause infection and permanent dark 'tattoo' marks. Check that his tetanus vaccines are up to date.
Cut my hand on a rusty nail in the garage. Do I really need a tetanus shot or is that a myth?

Tetanus is real and serious, but rust itself isn't the issue; the risk comes from soil and dirt bacteria that tend to be on old nails. If your last tetanus shot was more than five years ago, or you don't remember, see a doctor or pharmacist for a booster within a day or two. Meanwhile scrub the wound well under running water with soap and keep it clean and covered.
Is it okay to give my 10yo ibuprofen for a headache?

Yes, ibuprofen is fine for most 10-year-olds. Dose it by weight using the children's formulation or label directions, and give it with some food. Avoid aspirin in kids, because it's linked to a rare but serious condition called Reye's syndrome. If headaches are happening often or waking them from sleep, mention it to their pediatrician.
fever with a rash of tiny purple dots that don't fade when i press a glass on them, on my son

Go to the emergency department now or call emergency services. A fever with a rash that doesn't fade under a glass can be a sign of meningococcal infection or sepsis, which can get worse very fast. Don't wait for other symptoms to appear. This needs urgent care right away.
I'm on warfarin. Sprained my ankle. Ibuprofen ok for a couple days?

Best to avoid it. Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs like naproxen raise your bleeding risk on warfarin, including stomach bleeds, and can push your INR around. Acetaminophen is the usual pick for pain, along with ice, rest and elevating the ankle. Since you're on a blood thinner, let your doctor know about the sprain if it's badly swollen or bruising a lot.
dad's 70 and on blood thinners, fell and bumped his head, says he's fine. do we need to go in?

Yes, take him in today even if he seems fine. People on blood thinners have a higher risk of slow bleeding inside the skull after even minor head bumps, and symptoms can show up hours later. Doctors often recommend a CT scan in this situation. On the way, watch for worsening headache, confusion, drowsiness or vomiting, and call 911 if any of those appear.
is it bad to have a couple glasses of wine every night to unwind? work is insane rn

A couple of glasses every night adds up to around 14 or more drinks a week, which is above recommended limits. It also tends to make sleep and anxiety worse over time, even though it feels relaxing in the moment. The bigger risk is that your brain learns wine is the only way to switch off. Try alcohol-free nights during the week and swap in something else that marks the end of the workday, like a walk or a shower. If cutting back feels hard, mention it to your doctor.
can i take turmeric supplements while on blood thinners? it's natural so should be fine right

Being natural doesn't make it safe here. Concentrated turmeric and curcumin supplements may increase bleeding risk when combined with blood thinners like warfarin or apixaban. Turmeric used as a spice in cooking is fine, but check with your doctor or pharmacist before starting a supplement. If you're on warfarin, your INR may need monitoring.
Dizzy every time I stand up since starting my new BP pill. Is that normal?

Lightheadedness when you stand is a fairly common side effect when you start a blood pressure medication, especially if your pressure is now dropping lower than before. Stand up slowly, stay hydrated, and sit down right away if the room starts to spin. Let your doctor know soon, because the dose may need adjusting. If you actually faint or fall, get checked promptly.
Heartburn every night after dinner. Can I just keep taking Tums forever?

Tums are fine for occasional heartburn, but needing them every night means something should change rather than just being covered up. Try eating dinner at least three hours before bed, cutting back on big, fatty or spicy meals and alcohol, and raising the head of your bed a few inches. If it's still happening most nights after a couple of weeks, see your doctor, because ongoing reflux can irritate the esophagus and there are better long-term treatments. Go sooner if you have trouble swallowing, weight loss or black stools.
My 2 year old has had a fever of 104 for three days and is really sleepy. Should I wait until Monday to see the pediatrician?

Don't wait, get her seen today at urgent care or the ER. Three days of high fever plus unusual sleepiness in a toddler needs a prompt exam to rule out something like a serious bacterial infection. If she's hard to wake, has a stiff neck, a rash that doesn't fade when pressed, or trouble breathing, call emergency services right away.
Tooth pain only when I bite down on one spot, otherwise fine.

Pain that shows up only when you bite on a specific spot often points to a cracked tooth, a high filling, or inflammation around the root. Avoid chewing on that side and skip hard foods like ice, nuts, and hard candy, because a crack can spread and split the tooth. See a dentist in the next week or two, since a crack caught early can often be saved with a crown.
Is it safe to give my dog Benadryl for his itchy skin? I have some at home.

Plain diphenhydramine is often used in dogs, but call your vet for the right dose before you give any. The dose depends on his weight and health, and it can interact with other medications. Check the label carefully too: anything with a decongestant like pseudoephedrine, or liquid versions containing xylitol, can be dangerous for dogs. Ongoing itchy skin in dogs is often due to allergies, fleas or infection, so a vet visit is worth it anyway.
I'm 7 months pregnant and my cat scratched me. Toxoplasmosis risk?

Toxoplasmosis is spread mainly through cat feces, not scratches, so a scratch carries very little risk for that. Wash the scratch with soap and water and keep it clean, and watch for redness or swollen glands, which could suggest cat scratch disease. Mention it to your midwife or OB at your next visit, and keep letting someone else handle the litter box.
my wife sliced her palm on a broken glass, there may still be glass in it

Don't dig around in it. Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth around the cut, but avoid pressing directly on any glass you can see, and keep her hand raised. Palm cuts with possible glass inside should be seen today, since small fragments can be hard to spot and the hand has tendons and nerves close to the surface. Go right away if she has numbness or can't move her fingers normally.
Can I take DayQuil and Tylenol together? My head is killing me

Not a good idea, because DayQuil already contains acetaminophen, which is the same active ingredient as Tylenol. Doubling up makes it easy to go over the daily limit, which can seriously damage your liver. If you need extra headache relief, ibuprofen is a different drug and is generally fine alongside DayQuil for most people, as long as you don't have stomach ulcers or kidney issues. Always check labels for acetaminophen when combining cold products.
Can ibuprofen affect my blood pressure? I take it most days for my back.

Yes, it can. Regular ibuprofen and other NSAIDs can raise blood pressure, make BP medications less effective, and strain your kidneys over time. Taking it most days is worth bringing up with your doctor. Acetaminophen is often a safer option for frequent pain relief, and your doctor can also help you look into other treatments for your back.
Is it safe to pull my own loose tooth? I'm 35 and it's been wobbly for weeks and hurts.

Don't pull it yourself. A loose adult tooth usually means advanced gum disease, infection or injury, and a DIY extraction risks breaking the root, heavy bleeding and spreading infection. A dentist may even be able to save it, or at least remove it cleanly and plan a replacement. Book an appointment soon.
teen son wants to skip meningitis booster before college, says he's healthy. thoughts?

I'd push for the booster, because being healthy doesn't protect against meningococcal disease, and college students living in dorms are at higher risk. It can progress from flu-like symptoms to life-threatening within hours and can cause amputations or brain damage in survivors. Many colleges require the MenACWY booster anyway, and it's worth asking his doctor about the MenB vaccine too.
15 weeks pregnant and got rear-ended at a stoplight, I feel totally fine. Do I need to go in?

Yes, get checked even though you feel fine. Even a low-speed crash can occasionally cause a placental abruption that doesn't show symptoms right away. Call your OB or go to labor and delivery or the ER today so they can examine you and check the baby. Go in urgently if you notice bleeding, cramping, abdominal pain, or fluid leaking.
Can I put a crushed aspirin directly on my sore gum to numb the tooth?

Skip that trick, because aspirin held against the gum causes a chemical burn and leaves a painful white ulcer on top of the toothache. Aspirin only works when you swallow it, so take it or ibuprofen by mouth as directed on the package if it's safe for you. A cold compress on the outside of your cheek and a dab of clove oil or an over-the-counter benzocaine gel can help in the meantime, and the tooth still needs a dentist to fix whatever's causing the pain.
On doxycycline and my stomach's upset, can I take Tums with it

Not at the same time. The calcium in Tums binds to doxycycline and can stop much of it from being absorbed. Space them at least two to three hours apart. To ease the nausea, take the doxycycline with a meal (not dairy) and a full glass of water, and stay upright for half an hour afterward to avoid throat irritation.
can i use q tips to clean my ears every day? feels gross not to

Wiping the outer ear with a washcloth is fine, but daily Q-tips inside the canal usually do more harm than good. They push wax deeper, irritate the skin, and are a common cause of blockages and even eardrum perforations. Ears clean themselves by moving wax outward on their own. If you get a lot of buildup, a few drops of mineral oil or an over-the-counter softening drop now and then is a gentler option.
Ran out of my rescue inhaler. Can I just use my daughter's? Same stuff, albuterol.

In a genuine breathing emergency, using an albuterol inhaler that isn't yours is far better than struggling without one, and it's the same medication if hers is albuterol too. Don't make it a habit, though, and call your pharmacy or doctor today for a refill, since many pharmacies can give an emergency supply. If you're needing albuterol more than a couple of times a week, your asthma isn't well controlled and it's worth a visit to adjust your plan. If the inhaler isn't helping and you're struggling to breathe or speak, call emergency services.
can i drink to take the edge off when im stressed or is that bad

An occasional drink isn't a disaster, but using alcohol specifically to manage stress is a slippery habit, because it worsens sleep and causes rebound anxiety the next day, so you end up needing more. If you're reaching for it most stressful evenings, swap in something that actually lowers stress, like a walk, a workout, a call with a friend, or a hot shower. If cutting back feels hard, mention it to your doctor.
can i just double my sertraline dose this week? exams are killing me and i feel like it's not working

Don't double it on your own, because jumping the dose can cause side effects like agitation, nausea and sleep problems, and in rare cases serotonin syndrome. Sertraline also takes four to six weeks to work fully, so if you're early in, it may simply need more time. Call your prescriber this week, since dose changes are routine and they can often adjust it quickly by phone.
Sudden ripping pain in my chest going into my back. Worst pain I've ever had.

Call 911 immediately; sudden, tearing pain from the chest into the back can mean an aortic dissection, which is a life-threatening emergency. Don't take aspirin for this, because if it is a dissection, aspirin can worsen bleeding, so leave medication decisions to the paramedics. Stay as still and calm as you can and unlock the door for the responders.
I'm 32 and have no idea if I ever got the MMR. My mom doesn't remember. What do I do?

There are two easy routes. You can simply get the MMR now, since an extra dose is safe even if you were vaccinated as a kid. Or your doctor can order a titer blood test to check your immunity. Getting the shot is often quicker and cheaper than testing, especially if you're planning a pregnancy or traveling. If you might want to get pregnant, wait at least one month after MMR before trying.
I'm 55 and suddenly getting headaches for the first time ever, plus some weight loss.

Book a doctor's appointment soon rather than waiting it out. New headaches starting after 50, especially with unexplained weight loss, need a proper evaluation, which might include blood tests and possibly imaging. Most causes turn out to be treatable, but this combination shouldn't be self-managed.
lactose intolerant? i get gassy and crampy after milk

That's a common sign of lactose intolerance. You can test it yourself by cutting out dairy for a week or two and seeing if the symptoms go away. Many people do fine with hard cheeses, yogurt or lactose-free milk, and lactase pills taken with dairy can help too. If symptoms continue without dairy, or you have weight loss, blood in your stool or diarrhea that wakes you at night, see a doctor to check for other causes like celiac disease.
can i drink activated charcoal for gas

There's some weak evidence it helps with gas, and occasional use is generally fine for healthy adults. The big catch is that it binds medications, including birth control, and makes them less effective, so take it at least a couple of hours away from any pills. Simethicone, eating more slowly and cutting back on fizzy drinks or beans are usually more reliable first steps.
can I just skip the second shingles shot? the first one made me feel awful

Feeling rough for a day or two after Shingrix is really common, and it's a sign your immune system is responding, but skipping the second dose leaves you with noticeably weaker and shorter-lasting protection. The second shot is due 2 to 6 months after the first, and if you've passed that window you don't need to restart, just get it as soon as you can. Plan it for a day when you can rest afterward, and ask your doctor or pharmacist about taking acetaminophen or ibuprofen for the side effects. The reaction to the second dose is often similar to the first, but it passes, and shingles itself can cause weeks of pain or long-term nerve pain.
Teenager wants to take extra Robitussin DM because 'it helps more.' how much is too much?

Anything over the label dose is too much. Dextromethorphan in large amounts causes hallucinations, rapid heart rate, and dangerous reactions, and it's sometimes misused by teens for exactly that effect. Keep the bottle with you and hand out the doses yourself. It's worth having a calm, direct conversation with him about why he wants more. If he's taken a large amount, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 or emergency services right away.
is it bad to let my 2 year old drink juice all day? its 100% juice

Even 100% juice is a lot of sugar sipped all day, which is rough on teeth and can fill toddlers up so they eat less real food. The guidance for ages 1 to 3 is no more than about 4 ounces a day, ideally served in a cup with a meal rather than carried around in a sippy cup. Water and milk should be the main drinks, and whole fruit beats juice whenever you can manage it.
I need to know right now if this dog bite needs stitches, it's on my palm and I can see something white inside

Go to an ER now. Something white in a palm wound can be tendon or other deep tissue, and hand injuries like this need prompt professional repair and cleaning to protect your grip and prevent serious infection. Cover it with a clean cloth, apply gentle pressure if it's bleeding, and keep the hand raised. Check whether you can bend each finger, and tell the staff if any feel numb or won't move.
Slept in my contacts for 3 nights, now my eye is red and painful and light hurts. Just dry?

Pain, redness, and light sensitivity after sleeping in contacts can be a corneal ulcer, which is serious and can scar quickly, so this is not one to wait out. Take the lenses out, don't put any in, and see an eye doctor today or go to urgent care. Bring the lenses and case with you, since they may help identify the infection.
I think im allergic to penicillin from when I was a kid but not sure. does it matter?

It matters quite a bit. Most people labeled penicillin-allergic in childhood turn out not to be allergic when tested, and carrying the label means getting broader, often less effective antibiotics. Ask your doctor about a referral for penicillin allergy testing, which is quick and safe in an allergist's office. Until you've been tested, keep the allergy listed in your records rather than trying penicillin on your own.
Parrot bit my lip, kind of deep. Birds don't carry anything bad do they?

Birds can carry bacteria, and a deep bite on the lip deserves attention, both for infection risk and because the lip can scar or heal unevenly. Rinse it well with clean water, apply gentle pressure to stop any bleeding, and have a doctor or urgent care look at it today. They can check whether it needs closing, antibiotics or a tetanus booster. Bird droppings and dust can separately transmit psittacosis, so mention any flu-like symptoms in the coming weeks.
rolled my ankle playing basketball 20 min ago, swelling fast, can kinda walk. walk it off?

Don't play on it. Get it elevated, put ice on it for about 15 to 20 minutes at a time, and use a compression wrap for the next day or two. Since you can still put some weight on it, it's probably a sprain. Get an X-ray if you can't take four steps, if there's tenderness right on the bony knobs of the ankle or along the outer edge of the foot, or if it isn't clearly better in a few days. Once the worst swelling eases, gentle movement helps it heal better than total immobilization.
Spilled boiling water on my thigh about an hour ago, it's blistered over an area bigger than my hand. I'd rather not go to the doctor if I can avoid it.

That one needs medical care. A blistering burn larger than your palm is big enough that you need a proper assessment, dressing, and infection prevention, ideally today. If you haven't already, cool it under running water for 20 minutes, then cover it loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy cloth on the way in. Skipping care on a burn that size risks infection and worse scarring.
how much water should my 80 year old dad drink he never seems thirsty

Older adults lose much of their thirst signal, so not feeling thirsty doesn't mean he's hydrated. For most people a rough target is 6 to 8 cups of fluid a day, including soups, milk and water-rich foods. If he has heart failure or kidney disease, though, his doctor may want him on a fluid limit, so check first. Keeping a glass within reach and offering drinks at set times works better than waiting for him to ask.
dad's sugar keeps hitting 400s, he says he feels fine so no big deal

Readings in the 400s are a big deal even if he feels fine, because sugar that high damages the body and can tip into dangerous conditions like HHS or DKA. He should contact his doctor today about adjusting his treatment. If he becomes very thirsty or confused, starts vomiting, or turns drowsy, take him to the ER right away. Feeling fine with sugars like these often means his body has gotten used to running high, not that it's safe.
can i get the MMR if im trying to get pregnant next month

You can, but you should wait at least one month after the MMR before trying to conceive, since it's a live vaccine and isn't given during pregnancy. If you need it, get it now and push your plans back by a few weeks, or have your doctor check a blood test first because you may already be immune. It's absolutely worth sorting out, since rubella during pregnancy can cause serious birth defects.
small cut, should i use hydrogen peroxide on it

Plain running water and a bit of mild soap around the edges are better. Peroxide damages healthy tissue and can slow healing. Once it's clean, a thin layer of petroleum jelly and a bandage keep it moist and heal it faster with less scarring. Change the bandage daily, and watch for spreading redness or pus.
Woke up with my lower back totally seized, can barely stand up straight. 34, no idea what I did. Should I just stay in bed till it passes?

Staying in bed is actually one of the slower ways to recover, because gentle movement like short walks around the house helps acute low back pain settle faster than rest. Use heat or an over-the-counter anti-inflammatory like ibuprofen if it's safe for you, and change positions often rather than holding one. Most cases like this improve a lot within one to two weeks. Get seen urgently if you develop numbness around your groin or buttocks, trouble controlling your bladder or bowels, or weakness in your legs, because those can signal nerve compression that needs prompt treatment.
dad 86 coughing for 3 weeks, no fever. probably just a cold right

A cough lasting three weeks at his age deserves a doctor's visit rather than more waiting. Possible causes include a lingering infection, pneumonia (which often has no fever in older adults), heart failure, acid reflux or a medication side effect, especially ACE inhibitors for blood pressure. Get him seen sooner if he's short of breath, coughing up blood, losing weight or more tired than usual.
I had long-ish covid symptoms, mostly fatigue, and every time I try to work out I crash for days after. Should I just push through to rebuild stamina?

Don't push through. Crashing for days after exertion sounds like post-exertional malaise, and with that pattern, a graded "push harder" approach can set you back significantly. Pacing works better: keep activity below the level that triggers a crash, even if that's quite low for now, and increase only very slowly once you're stable. It's worth seeing your doctor or a long COVID clinic so they can guide this properly and rule out other causes.
I'm a nurse working nights and I'm completely fried. Any actual tips that aren't just 'self care'?

Treat your sleep as non-negotiable. Use blackout curtains or a sleep mask, earplugs or white noise, and keep the same sleep block on work days as much as you can. Wear sunglasses on the drive home so the morning light doesn't wake your brain up, and have your last coffee no later than the middle of your shift. Eat a light meal before work and something small partway through, rather than a heavy meal at 3am. If you're dozing at the wheel or feeling constantly hopeless, raise it with occupational health or your doctor, because shift work can genuinely tip people into depression.
got hit in the eye with a tennis ball. vision seems a bit blurry. it'll clear up right?

Blurry vision after a direct hit to the eye is not something to wait out, because it can signal bleeding inside the eye, a detached retina, or a fracture around the eye socket. Get seen today by an eye doctor or an ER, and go immediately if you see blood in the colored part of the eye, flashes, floaters, a curtain over your vision, double vision, or severe pain. Until then, cover it gently with a shield or cup without pressing on the eye, and avoid aspirin or ibuprofen, which can worsen bleeding.
pregnant 30 weeks, bad upper stomach pain under my ribs on the right and a headache. just gas right?

Don't assume it's gas. Upper right abdominal pain with a headache in the third trimester can be a sign of preeclampsia or HELLP syndrome, and both need urgent attention. Call your maternity unit or labor and delivery now, or go in, so they can check your blood pressure and urine. It's quick to rule out, and they'd much rather see you.
My dentist prescribed me oxycodone after a root canal but honestly the pain is mild. Should I take it anyway so it doesn't get worse?

There's no need to take an opioid preemptively if your pain is mild. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen at label doses usually handle post-root-canal soreness well, with far less risk. Keep the oxycodone in reserve for severe pain only. Safely dispose of any you don't use, and call your dentist if the pain gets significantly worse instead of better.
My OB is booked for 3 weeks. I've had a bad headache for two days at 34 weeks and my feet are super swollen. Can I just take Tylenol and wait?

Please don't wait on this. A persistent headache with swelling late in pregnancy can be a sign of preeclampsia, which needs a blood pressure check today. Call your OB's after-hours line or go to labor and delivery triage now, and go immediately if you also notice vision changes, upper belly pain or shortness of breath. Tylenol is generally safe in pregnancy, but it shouldn't replace getting checked.
I'm a line cook and I burn my forearms constantly. Anything better than just ignoring them?

A quick blast of cool water during a break makes a real difference, even if you can't manage the full 20 minutes mid-service. After your shift, keep the burns clean and lightly moisturized with petroleum jelly, and cover any open or blistered ones so grease and bacteria from the kitchen can't get in. Long-sleeve cook's sleeves or oven gauntlets for the oven and fryer are worth it for prevention. Any burn that becomes red, hot, swollen or pus-filled should be seen by a doctor, since kitchen burns do get infected.
can i mix my ambien with a glass of wine to make it work better

Please don't, because alcohol and Ambien together can dangerously slow your breathing and greatly increase the risk of sleepwalking, sleep-driving, falls, and memory blackouts. Even one glass meaningfully strengthens the drug's effects in unpredictable ways.
