If your Ambien isn't working well anymore, tell your prescriber so they can adjust your plan rather than boosting it yourself.
cut my finger slicing onions, it's bleeding a lot but not huge. what do i do

Press a clean cloth or paper towel firmly on the cut and hold steady pressure for a full 10 minutes without peeking, keeping your hand raised above your heart. Once it stops, rinse it under running water, put on a thin layer of petroleum jelly and cover it with a bandage. If it's still bleeding after 10 to 15 minutes of solid pressure, gapes open, or you can't move or feel the fingertip normally, get it looked at today because it may need stitches.
can stress cause chest pain?

Yes. Stress and anxiety can cause chest tightness and pain, often with a racing heart or shortness of breath. But you shouldn't assume chest pain is stress without getting it checked, especially if you're over 40 or have risk factors. Call emergency services if the pain is crushing, spreads to your arm, jaw or back, or comes with sweating, nausea or breathlessness. If it keeps coming back, see your doctor to rule out heart causes.
my 4 year old keeps crying and pointing at her mouth, I can see a dark spot on one of her back teeth

That dark spot is quite possibly a cavity, and baby-tooth cavities can hurt and get infected just like adult ones, so book her in with a dentist this week. For tonight, children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen dosed by her weight can ease the pain. Avoid numbing gels with benzocaine. If her face swells or she gets a fever, get her seen the same day.
my daughter (7) has a peanut allergy and her school wants to keep her epipen in the nurse's office across the building. is that fine?

That's worth pushing back on, because epinephrine works best when it's given within minutes, and a long walk to the nurse's office can cost precious time. Many schools let kids keep an auto-injector in the classroom or with a trusted adult, or keep a second one there. Ask your allergist for a written anaphylaxis action plan and a note supporting that arrangement. Then work with the school on a formal plan, such as a 504 plan in the US, so the setup is guaranteed.
I keep getting these stabbing pains behind one eye, same time every night, eye waters and nose runs on that side. Lasts maybe 45 min. Been going on for 2 weeks.

That pattern sounds a lot like cluster headaches, which come in nightly bouts with one-sided eye pain, tearing and a runny nostril. See a doctor soon, because regular painkillers usually don't help them, but high-flow oxygen and specific prescription treatments can stop attacks fast. Avoid alcohol during a cluster period, since it's a common trigger.
My 3 year old has a rash of little red dots that don't fade when I press a glass on them. She also has a fever.

Take her to the ER now. A fever with a rash that doesn't fade under a glass can be a sign of a serious infection like meningococcal disease, which needs treatment fast. Don't wait to see if she gets worse, even if she seems only mildly unwell. Call 911 if she's very drowsy, floppy or hard to wake.
Nursing student here, need hep B series for clinicals but I'm behind on the second dose by like 3 months. Do I restart?

No, you don't need to restart. Hepatitis B series don't reset because of delays, so just get the next dose as soon as you can and continue from there. Your school may also want a titer test after the series to confirm immunity, so check their requirements. Let the clinic know which brand you started with, because the schedules differ.
lots of floaters suddenly plus little flashes of light at the edge. I'm nearsighted

Get a dilated eye exam today. A sudden shower of new floaters with flashes can mean the gel inside your eye is tugging on the retina, and nearsighted people are more prone to tears. A tear caught early can usually be sealed with a quick laser treatment, before it turns into a detachment. Don't wait to see if it settles.
Pregnant, 20 weeks, bad headache since this morning and my vision is kind of sparkly. My ankles are swollen too but that's normal right?

Please call your maternity unit or OB right now, or go to labor and delivery. A severe headache with visual changes and swelling in the second half of pregnancy can be signs of preeclampsia, which needs a blood pressure check and urine test urgently. Don't wait to see if it settles.
Baby got her rotavirus vaccine 3 days ago and now she's pulling her legs up and screaming in waves and had a weird jelly poop. probably just gas right?

Please don't wait on this; take her to the emergency room now or call 911 if she seems very unwell. Waves of intense crying with her legs pulled up, especially combined with stool that looks like jelly or has blood, can be signs of intussusception, a bowel blockage that is a rare complication within the first week after the rotavirus vaccine. It's very treatable when caught early, but it needs urgent evaluation. Tell the ER staff she recently got the rotavirus vaccine.
had a fever and chills the night after my shot. am i allergic and should i stop getting it

Fever and chills the next day are a normal immune response, not an allergy, and they usually clear within 24 to 48 hours. A true allergic reaction happens within minutes to hours and looks like hives, swelling of the face or lips, or trouble breathing. That means you can safely keep getting the vaccine, but mention it to your provider so they can give tips for next time.
My son is 3 and still not really talking, maybe 10 words. Everyone says boys are just late. Should I wait?

I wouldn't wait, because by age 3 most kids use hundreds of words and short sentences, and ten words is a meaningful delay regardless of gender. Ask his pediatrician for a hearing test and a referral for a speech-language evaluation, and in the US you can also contact your school district directly for free early evaluation. Getting help early makes a real difference, and if it turns out to be nothing, you've lost nothing by checking.
headache + stiff neck + fever 102. college dorm. ugh

That combination needs to be checked today, not slept off, because fever, headache and a stiff neck together can mean meningitis, which spreads in dorms and can get serious fast. Go to urgent care or the ER now, and go straight to the ER if you notice a rash, confusion or sensitivity to light. Tell a roommate or RA what's going on so someone knows.
friend gave me some of her ambien. one pill is fine right?

I'd skip it. Zolpidem can cause complex sleep behaviors like sleepwalking, sleep-driving or eating without remembering it, and the right dose depends on things like your sex, other medications and whether you drink. Women are usually prescribed a lower dose because it clears more slowly. Mixing it with alcohol or other sedatives is genuinely dangerous. If sleep is bad enough that you're tempted, see a doctor who can prescribe properly or point you to better options.
Is it ok to take ibuprofen for stomach cramps?

It's usually not the best choice for stomach pain, because ibuprofen can irritate the stomach lining and worsen things like gastritis or ulcers. For period cramps it works well, ideally taken with food. For general belly cramps, acetaminophen is gentler, and a heating pad can help a lot. If the cramps are severe, keep coming back, or come with fever or blood in the stool, get checked rather than just treating the pain.
my 78 yo dad has chest pressure but says its just indigestion and refuses to go anywhere

Chest pressure in a 78-year-old should be treated as a possible heart attack until proven otherwise, so call 911 even if he's resisting. Paramedics can do an ECG on the spot, and if it really is indigestion, he loses an hour, while waiting on a heart attack can cost him his heart muscle or his life. If he isn't allergic and hasn't been told to avoid it, the dispatcher may tell him to chew a regular aspirin. Don't let him drive himself anywhere.
Flu test came back positive this morning. I'm 34 and healthy. Do I need Tamiflu or is it pointless?

It's not pointless, especially since you're within the first 48 hours. Started early, oseltamivir can shorten flu by about a day and reduce the chance of complications. For a healthy 34-year-old it's optional rather than essential, so it's a reasonable call either way, but it's more worth taking if you live with someone vulnerable like a baby, a pregnant person or an older relative. Call your doctor or a telehealth service today, because the benefit drops off the longer you wait.
ok so day 3 of antibiotics for UTI and i feel totally fine. can i stop?

Finish the course unless your prescriber specifically told you a shorter one is fine. Feeling better on day 3 is normal, but stopping early can leave bacteria behind and let the infection come back. Many UTI courses are only 3 to 5 days anyway, so check the label. You may be almost done.
My Apple Watch keeps saying possible AFib. I feel totally fine. Ignore it?

Don't ignore it; repeated AFib alerts are worth a doctor's visit even if you feel fine. Atrial fibrillation is often silent but significantly raises stroke risk, and whether you need blood thinners depends on your age and other health factors. Book an appointment in the next week or so and bring the watch ECG recordings, and expect a proper ECG or a wearable monitor to confirm it. Go to the ER if you develop chest pain, fainting or breathlessness, or any stroke signs like face drooping, arm weakness or slurred speech.
Could my toothache actually be a heart attack? My upper left molars hurt and I feel kind of sweaty and short of breath.

Call emergency services now. Jaw or tooth pain together with sweating and shortness of breath can be a sign of a heart attack, especially in women and older adults. Don't drive yourself to the hospital. It's far better to get checked and have it turn out to be your tooth than to wait.
Got some bleach-based cleaner splashed in my eye a minute ago, it burns like crazy. What do I do??

Start flushing that eye right now with lukewarm running water from a tap or shower, holding the lid open, and keep going for a full 15 to 20 minutes even if it starts feeling better. Take out any contact lens if it comes out easily, but don't let that delay rinsing. Once you've flushed, get seen urgently at an ER or eye clinic, because chemical splashes can damage the cornea in ways you can't judge by how it feels.
Can I use a tanning bed to clear up my acne? A friend said it worked for her.

I'd steer clear. Tanning beds may make acne look slightly better for a little while, but the UV significantly raises your risk of melanoma and causes premature skin ageing. Acne also often flares back once the tan fades. Proven treatments like benzoyl peroxide, adapalene, or prescription options from a doctor will do far more good without that risk. If your acne is stubborn, a dermatologist can also talk to you about medically supervised light therapy, which is a different and safer thing.
is journaling actually useful or just a trend

It's genuinely useful. Research on expressive writing shows that 15 to 20 minutes of writing about stressful things can reduce stress and improve mood for many people. It works best when you go beyond venting and try to make sense of what happened or plan a next step. If rehashing upsetting events leaves you feeling worse, switch to gratitude or planning-style entries, or bring that material to a therapist instead.
can you get a headache from too much sleep? slept 12 hrs and feel awful

Yes, oversleeping is a well-known headache trigger, likely from disrupted sleep rhythms, low blood sugar, dehydration and missing your usual morning caffeine. Drink water, eat something, get some daylight and have your usual coffee if you drink it. Keeping a steady wake time, even on weekends, helps prevent it.
Burned my hand on a pan. Mom says put butter on it.

Skip the butter, since it traps heat and can raise infection risk. Run the burn under cool (not icy) running water for a good 20 minutes. Then cover it loosely with a clean non-stick dressing and take ibuprofen or acetaminophen for pain. See a doctor if the burn is larger than your palm, is on the fingers or a joint, has big blisters, or looks white or leathery.
Ear has been draining yellowish fluid since a really bad earache stopped hurting suddenly

When a bad earache suddenly eases and fluid starts draining, the eardrum has often perforated from the pressure. Most heal on their own, but you should see a doctor in the next day or so to confirm it and treat the infection. Keep water out of that ear and don't put drops in unless a doctor prescribes them. Get seen sooner if you have fever, worsening pain, dizziness, or swelling behind the ear.
Is it normal to feel nauseous after taking vitamins in the morning?

Yes, that's really common, especially with iron and zinc on an empty stomach. Take them with breakfast, or switch to taking them with dinner, and the nausea usually goes away. If it continues, a gentler form like iron bisglycinate or a smaller dose may help. Ask your doctor before stopping something you were prescribed, such as prenatal vitamins or iron for anemia.
quick panic attack fix?? having one rn

You're safe, and this will pass, usually within 10 to 20 minutes. Breathe in slowly through your nose for 4 counts and out through your mouth for 6 to 8, and keep the exhale longer than the inhale. Plant your feet and name five things you can see and four you can touch to anchor yourself. If you have chest pain, trouble breathing that doesn't ease, or this feels different from usual, call emergency services to rule out something physical.
is it ok to send my kid to school, fever was 101 last night but he's fine this morning after motrin

Keep him home today. Motrin may be hiding the fever, and the standard rule is 24 hours fever-free without any fever-reducing medicine before going back to school. That protects his classmates and gives him time to actually recover.
grinding my teeth at night, jaw and teeth sore every morning. any quick fix?

The real fix is a custom night guard from your dentist, which protects your teeth and takes pressure off your jaw. Store-bought boil-and-bite guards can work as a stopgap, and a warm compress, soft foods and cutting back on evening caffeine and alcohol can help. Get it checked, because years of grinding can crack teeth and wear down enamel.
I haven't slept more than 4 hours a night for two weeks because of work stress. Can I just take a couple of my mom's Ambien?

Don't take your mom's Ambien, because the dose was chosen for her, it can cause sleepwalking or sleep-driving, and it's dangerous combined with alcohol or other sedatives. Two weeks of four-hour nights is worth a doctor's visit, and they can prescribe something short-term if it's really needed. Meanwhile, keep a fixed wake time, stop screens and work email an hour before bed, and get out of bed if you're lying awake for more than 20 minutes.
I'm traveling abroad for another 10 days and a filling just fell out. it's sensitive but not super painful. can it wait?

If it's only mildly sensitive, it can usually wait a short while. Pick up a temporary filling kit from a pharmacy to cover the hole and protect the tooth. Chew on the other side, avoid very sweet or sticky foods, and keep the area clean. If you get throbbing pain, swelling or fever, see a local dentist rather than waiting until you're home.
Going to start intermittent fasting 16:8. Anything I should watch out for? Type 1 diabetic btw

With type 1 diabetes, talk to your endocrinologist before starting, because fasting windows can cause serious lows and your basal and bolus doses will likely need adjusting. Plan to check your glucose more often or lean on your CGM, keep fast-acting sugar on hand, and break the fast if you go low. Done with medical guidance it can work for some people, but it isn't something to wing.
Is it safe to pull my own loose tooth? It's an adult tooth and it's wiggly and hurts.

Don't pull a loose adult tooth yourself. Looseness usually means gum disease, infection or trauma underneath, and yanking it out can break the root, cause heavy bleeding or spread infection. A dentist may even be able to save it. Avoid chewing on that side and book an appointment soon.
My wrist has hurt for 2 months since I fell on it skating. Figured it was a sprain. Still sore at the base of the thumb.

Two months of pain at the base of the thumb after falling on an outstretched hand needs an X-ray, because that's the classic spot for a scaphoid fracture. That bone is often mistaken for a sprain and can heal poorly if it's missed. Get it seen by a doctor soon, and mention exactly where it hurts so they image it specifically.
Can I drive home after getting my eyes dilated?

Many people can, but dilation makes your vision blurry and very sensitive to light for several hours, which can make driving unsafe, especially in bright sun or at night. If you can, have someone drive you or use a ride service. If you have to drive, wear dark sunglasses and wait until close-up and distance vision both feel clear. Many offices will tell you how you look once the drops have taken effect.
My 6 year old has a bad cough and I have some adult Robitussin. Can I just give him half a dose?

Please don't halve an adult cough medicine for a child, because the ingredients and dosing don't scale down reliably and kids can react badly to them. Over-the-counter cough and cold medicines aren't really recommended for young children anyway, since they don't work well and carry real risks. Honey, fluids, a humidifier, and rest are better bets, and call the pediatrician if the cough lasts more than a couple of weeks or comes with fever, wheezing, or fast breathing.
grandpa hasn't pooped in 5 days, should we just give him a bunch of laxatives

Don't load him up, because a strong dose in an older person can cause dehydration and electrolyte problems, and if there's a blockage it can make things worse. If he has belly swelling, severe pain, vomiting, or can't pass gas, get him seen today, since that could be an obstruction. If he otherwise feels okay, a standard dose of something gentle like polyethylene glycol (MiraLAX), plus extra fluids and some movement, is a reasonable start. Call his doctor if nothing happens in a day or two, and ask whether any of his medications, like opioids or iron, are the cause.
allergy shots seem like a lot of work, are they actually worth it

For the right person they're very worth it. Allergy shots are the only treatment that changes the immune response itself, and benefits often last years after you finish. The catch is the commitment: weekly shots for several months, then monthly for three to five years. You also wait in the office about 30 minutes afterward in case of a reaction. If meds aren't controlling your symptoms, or you have allergic asthma, ask an allergist whether you're a good candidate or whether under-the-tongue tablets could fit your schedule better.
tldr: steam burn on forearm from kettle 2 days ago, now it's redder around it, warm and kinda pussy. normal?

Spreading redness, warmth, and pus after two days sounds like infection, which isn't normal healing. See a GP or urgent care today, because you may need antibiotics. Go sooner, or straight to the ER, if red streaks are spreading from it or you develop a fever. Until then, keep it clean and covered, and don't put home remedies on it.
is 99.5 a fever

Not really. Most doctors don't count a fever until 100.4°F (38°C), and normal body temperature varies through the day and after exercise or a hot drink. If you feel sick, keep an eye on your symptoms, but 99.5 on its own isn't anything to worry about.
spilled boiling water on my thigh, big patch maybe the size of 3 hands, some white areas. honestly it doesn't even hurt that much

This needs emergency care now, so call an ambulance or get to the ER. A burn that large is serious on its own, and white areas that don't hurt much can mean the burn is deep enough to have damaged the nerves. While you wait, cool it with running water for up to 20 minutes, remove clothing that isn't stuck to the skin, and cover it loosely with cling film. Keep the rest of your body warm.
I'm pregnant (24 wks) and just recovered from a bad cold. Ok to go back to my prenatal workout classes?

Yes, if you're fever-free, eating and drinking well and feeling mostly back to normal, you can usually return to your prenatal class, just take it easier for the first session or two. Stay well hydrated and stop if you feel dizzy, short of breath or have any contractions. If you had a high fever while sick, or have any new symptoms like reduced baby movements, check in with your midwife or OB first.
is it safe to take expired antibiotics from last year for my sore throat

Don't. Most sore throats are viral, so antibiotics won't help, and leftover pills are probably the wrong drug, dose or amount for whatever you have. Expired medicine can also lose potency. Gargling salt water, lozenges and ibuprofen or acetaminophen are the right moves for now. See a doctor if you have a high fever, white patches, swollen glands without a cough, or trouble swallowing, since strep needs a proper test and prescription.
lifted something at the gym and felt a pop in my shoulder, now can't lift my arm above my head. ice it and wait?

Ice and rest are fine for the next day or two, but a pop followed by not being able to raise your arm raises the possibility of a rotator cuff tear. That's worth getting examined within a week or so, because some tears do better if repaired early. If you have major weakness, a deformed-looking shoulder, or numbness down the arm, go in sooner.
low grade fever every evening for 3 weeks, night sweats, lost some weight without trying. 45M

Book an appointment with your doctor this week rather than waiting it out. Weeks of evening fevers, night sweats and unexplained weight loss need proper investigation. Possible causes include tuberculosis, other chronic infections, thyroid problems and some cancers like lymphoma. Bring a log of your temperatures and weight to the appointment.
can diabetics drink alcohol

Usually yes, in moderation, but alcohol can cause delayed low blood sugar, especially if you take insulin or sulfonylureas. Drink with food, avoid sugary mixers, and check your sugar before bed. Wear something that identifies you as diabetic, because a low can look a lot like being drunk.
itchy scalp, my kid's school sent a lice letter home. ugh. what actually works

Check carefully with a fine-toothed nit comb on wet, conditioned hair, since only people with live lice need treating. Use an over-the-counter treatment such as dimeticone, which suffocates lice and avoids resistance problems, following the packet exactly. Repeat it about a week later to catch newly hatched lice. Comb every few days for two weeks, wash pillowcases and hats in hot water, and skip any kerosene or other harsh home remedies.
how long after starting antibiotics is strep no longer contagious

Generally after about 12 to 24 hours on an effective antibiotic, provided the fever has gone. That's why most schools and workplaces let people return after a full day of treatment. Keep taking the whole course even once you feel fine, because stopping early raises the risk of relapse and rare complications like rheumatic fever.
Jammed my finger catching a ball. It's swollen and I can't fully straighten the tip. Just buddy tape it?

A fingertip you can't straighten is often mallet finger, where the tendon tears or pulls a bit of bone loose. Buddy taping won't fix that. It usually needs a dedicated splint worn continuously for several weeks, so see a doctor or urgent care within the next few days and get an X-ray. Until then, ice it and keep it straight.
Heart racing at 180 bpm out of nowhere while sitting on the couch, been about 15 minutes, feel a bit dizzy. 34F.

A sudden resting heart rate of 180 that has lasted 15 minutes with dizziness needs emergency care now, so call an ambulance or have someone drive you. It's often a fixable rhythm problem like SVT, but it has to be confirmed on an ECG and treated properly. While you wait, you can try bearing down hard as if straining on the toilet for 15 seconds, which sometimes resets the rhythm. Don't drive yourself.
toddler drank some of the dishwasher pod liquid, maybe a little. throat looks ok

Call Poison Control right now (1-800-222-1222 in the US) or your local poison center. Detergent pods are concentrated and can cause burns, breathing trouble or vomiting even from a small amount. Rinse his mouth gently, don't make him vomit, and watch his breathing closely. If he coughs, wheezes, drools, vomits or seems very sleepy, call emergency services immediately.
Quick q: sharp stabbing pain on the left side of my chest when I take a deep breath. 24, healthy. Worth worrying?

Pain that stabs when you breathe in is often from the chest wall or the lining around the lungs rather than the heart. Some causes still matter, though, like pericarditis, pneumonia, a partially collapsed lung or a blood clot. Get seen today if you're short of breath, have a fever, recently flew long distance, take hormonal birth control, or the pain is getting worse. If it's mild and you can reproduce it by pressing on one spot, it's more likely muscular, but book a doctor's visit if it lasts more than a few days.
Are collagen powders worth it or just expensive protein

Mostly expensive protein, and incomplete protein at that, since collagen is missing an essential amino acid. A few studies suggest small benefits for skin elasticity and joint pain, but many of them are industry-funded and the effects are modest. If you enjoy it, it's harmless. If you're on a budget, sunscreen and enough total protein will do more for your skin.
Can I just keep running on my shin and knee pain? Marathon is in 3 weeks and I don't want to lose fitness

Running through pain that's getting worse is how a niggle becomes a stress fracture that ends your season, so cut back now. Swap some runs for cycling, pool running, or the elliptical to hold your fitness, and only keep running sessions that stay pain-free. Pain in one specific spot on the shin bone, or pain at rest or at night, needs a sports doctor before you run again. Three weeks out, a slightly undertrained start is far better than a DNS.
I'm a nurse on night shift and I constantly have indigestion. Any tips that actually work?

Shift work disrupts digestion, so timing is where you'll get the most mileage. Eat your main meal before your shift, stick to lighter snacks overnight, and avoid a big meal within two or three hours of sleeping. Cutting back on coffee late in the shift and sleeping with your head slightly raised also helps a lot of people. If you're still reaching for antacids most days after those changes, see your doctor about a short course of acid-reducing medication.
My son (6) had a seizure with his fever, lasted maybe a minute, he's sleepy now but ok. Do we need to go in?

Yes, he should be checked by a doctor today, especially if this is his first seizure. Febrile seizures are usually harmless, but a clinician needs to confirm that and look for the cause of the fever. Six is also at the older end of the typical age range for them. Call emergency services if he has another seizure, one lasts over five minutes, or he doesn't return to his normal self within an hour.
My 2 year old drank a bit of the dishwasher detergent pod, she coughed a bit, now seems ok

Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 right now. Detergent pods are more dangerous than regular soap, and coughing after swallowing one can mean some got into her airway. Don't make her vomit, but do wipe out her mouth and give her a few sips of water. Call 911 if she has any trouble breathing, keeps coughing, drools, vomits repeatedly or becomes drowsy.
neck stiff after sleeping weird. fix?

Gentle movement is your friend here. Slowly turn and tilt your head within a comfortable range several times a day, apply heat for 15 minutes, and take an over-the-counter pain reliever if it's safe for you. A sleeping-wrong neck usually loosens up within a few days. If you also have a fever, a severe headache, or numbness or weakness in your arm, that's not a sleeping issue and you should get seen promptly.
31 weeks, getting tightenings like every 10 min for the last hour. braxton hicks right?

Maybe, but tightenings that keep coming regularly every 10 minutes at 31 weeks need a call to labor and delivery now, since that can be preterm labor. While you call, empty your bladder, drink a big glass of water and lie on your left side. Braxton Hicks usually ease off with rest and fluids. Don't wait it out, and go in right away if you have pelvic pressure, low back ache, bleeding or leaking fluid.
Found a tick on my leg after hiking. Best way to get it off?

Grab it with fine-tipped tweezers as close to the skin as possible and pull straight up with steady pressure, without twisting or squeezing the body. Skip matches, nail polish or petroleum jelly, which can make it release more saliva into you. Clean the spot, note the date, and see a doctor if you develop an expanding rash, fever, aches or fatigue over the next few weeks.
do ibuprofen and bp meds mix

Not well with regular use. NSAIDs like ibuprofen and naproxen can raise blood pressure, blunt the effect of many bp meds and strain the kidneys. An occasional dose is usually fine, but acetaminophen is generally the safer go-to for regular pain relief. Check with your doctor if you need something ongoing.
My 18 month old isn't saying any words yet. My husband says boys talk late and not to worry. Who's right?

It's worth bringing up with your pediatrician now rather than waiting. Most kids have several words by 18 months, and early speech therapy, if it's needed, works best when it starts sooner. Plenty of late talkers do catch up, but a hearing check and developmental screen can rule out issues like hearing loss. In the meantime, keep narrating your day, reading together and naming things he points at.
spilled boiling water on my 2 year old's arm, big red patch, some blisters forming. treating at home ok?

Cool it under lukewarm running water for 20 minutes right now, and remove any clothing or jewelry from the area unless it's stuck. A burn with blisters on a toddler that's more than a small coin-sized spot needs to be seen today, because young children's skin burns deeper than it looks and they can lose fluids. Cover it loosely with cling film or a clean nonstick cloth and avoid ice, creams or butter. Keep them warm otherwise, and call 911 if the burn is large, on the face, hands or genitals, or they seem unwell.
Chest tightness and BP 170/105 right now, I'm 58. Probably just stress from work?

Treat this as an emergency and call emergency services now. Chest tightness with high blood pressure at 58 could be a heart attack or another serious problem, and stress can't be assumed. Unless you're allergic or have been told not to take it, chewing a regular aspirin while you wait is often advised, and dispatchers can guide you. Don't drive yourself.
my throat feels kind of tight after eating shrimp for the first time, is that normal or am i overthinking

Throat tightness after eating shrimp is a classic warning sign of a shellfish allergy, so you're not overthinking it. If it's getting worse, or you have trouble breathing or swallowing, swelling of your lips or tongue, hives, dizziness or vomiting, call emergency services right now, and use an epinephrine auto-injector if one is available. Even if it fades, see a doctor soon about allergy testing and avoid shellfish until then, because reactions can be stronger the next time.
Dad has a bad bruise on his arm and he's on warfarin. Do we need to worry

One bruise from a known bump is common on warfarin and usually fine, but call his doctor or anticoagulation clinic to check whether his INR needs testing, especially if the bruises are large, new ones appear without a reason, or he recently started a new medication or antibiotic. Go to the ER for blood in his urine or stool, black tarry stools, vomiting blood, a severe headache, or any head injury, even a minor-looking one. Make sure he's not taking ibuprofen, naproxen or aspirin unless prescribed, since they raise bleeding risk with warfarin.
ugh fever of 103 in my 20 year old son, he's had it for 4 days and now has a rash and stiff neck

He needs to go to the emergency room now, don't wait. Fever with a stiff neck and a rash can signal meningitis, which needs urgent treatment and can get worse quickly. Check whether the rash fades when you press a glass against it, but go regardless of the result. Call emergency services if he's very drowsy or hard to wake.
I'm allergic to bees and going hiking alone next weekend. I don't really want to pay for an epipen refill, it's $300. I'll be careful.

With a known bee allergy, hiking alone without epinephrine is a genuinely dangerous gamble, because a sting can come out of nowhere and help may be hours away. There are cheaper routes: generic epinephrine auto-injectors and manufacturer coupons can bring the cost way down, and pharmacy discount apps often help too, so ask your pharmacist. Also bring a hiking buddy or at least share your route, and carry a phone or satellite messenger.
Back pain plus I suddenly can't feel the inside of my thighs and peeing feels weird. Probably just a pinched nerve right?

Please go to an emergency department now rather than waiting to see if it settles. Numbness in the groin or inner thighs together with changes in urination can be signs of cauda equina syndrome, where the nerves at the base of the spine are being compressed. It needs urgent imaging and sometimes surgery within hours to prevent permanent damage. This is not one to sleep on.
is turmeric safe to take with blood thinners

Be cautious there. Concentrated curcumin supplements may add to the bleeding risk of blood thinners like warfarin, apixaban or clopidogrel. Turmeric used as a spice in food is generally fine. Talk to your prescriber or pharmacist before starting a supplement, especially if you have a procedure coming up.
how do i know if my baby is getting enough breast milk

The best signs are diapers and weight. After the first week, look for about 6 or more wet diapers a day, regular yellow stools, and steady weight gain at checkups, with birth weight regained by around 2 weeks. A satisfied baby who seems relaxed after most feeds is a good sign too. If diapers drop off, she's very sleepy and hard to wake for feeds, or you're worried about her weight, see your pediatrician or a lactation consultant soon.
hit my head on a cabinet door pretty hard, got a goose egg. i'm fine but kinda want to sleep. is that ok?

Ice the bump for 15 minutes at a time. Sleep is generally fine if you're alert, thinking clearly, and have no other symptoms, but it's best to have someone check on you tonight. Get to the ER right away if you develop vomiting, a worsening headache, confusion, slurred speech, unequal pupils, weakness, or trouble waking up. Tiredness right after a hard hit is worth a call to a doctor or nurse line if you're unsure.
Pretty sure I have a sinus infection. Can I still do my morning spin class?

If it's just congestion and pressure without fever, a lighter ride could be okay. You'll probably find intense cycling uncomfortable with your sinuses blocked, though. If you have a fever, feel achy, or are really drained, skip it and rest. If symptoms last more than about ten days or get worse after improving, see a doctor.
kid has fever and won't drink anything, hasn't peed since morning (it's 7pm). she's 2

She needs to be seen tonight. Going 10 or more hours without peeing at her age suggests she's getting dehydrated. Try small sips of an oral rehydration solution every few minutes on the way. Head to urgent care or the emergency department, especially if she's very sleepy, has a dry mouth or cries without tears.
how many days of jet lag is normal after flying from LA to London

A common rule of thumb is about a day to adjust for each time zone crossed, so with an eight-hour jump eastward, expect several days to a week to feel fully normal. Get outdoor light in the morning in London, avoid long naps, and keep any nap under 30 minutes. Low-dose melatonin in the early evening local time for a few days can help speed things up. Eastward travel is usually harder than flying west.
zyrtec not working anymore, can i take 2 a day

Don't double up on your own. Cetirizine above the labeled dose mostly adds drowsiness without much extra relief, so a pharmacist or doctor should sign off before you take more. A better first move is adding a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, which often works better than any antihistamine for nasal symptoms. Some people also do better switching to a different antihistamine such as fexofenadine. If nothing is controlling it, an allergist can test you and talk about allergy shots.
toddler had a fever and then just started shaking and went stiff for like a minute, now sleepy. WHAT DO I DO

That sounds like a febrile seizure, and since it's the first one, your child needs to be seen by a doctor now. Call emergency services if the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if your child has trouble breathing, if another seizure starts, or if they don't start waking up and acting more like themselves. Otherwise, head to the ER or call your pediatrician right away. Lay your child on their side and don't put anything in their mouth. Febrile seizures are usually harmless, but a doctor should check for the cause of the fever.
got stung by a bee, my lip is swelling and my throat feels kind of tight

Throat tightness after a sting can be anaphylaxis. Call 911 right now. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector, use it in your outer thigh immediately. Don't drive yourself, and sit upright or lie down while you wait for help. Treat this as an emergency even if you start to feel a little better.
brushed too hard and now my gum line is sore. big deal?

Usually not a big deal, because gums irritated by harsh brushing tend to settle within a few days. Switch to a soft-bristled brush, use gentle circles instead of scrubbing, and rinse with warm salt water. Over the long term, hard brushing can cause gum recession. If the soreness lasts beyond a week or you notice bleeding or swelling, have a dentist check for gum disease.
My 4 year old has red cheeks and a lacy rash on her arms after a cold last week. She's playing normally. Should I worry?

That sounds a lot like fifth disease (slapped cheek), a common viral rash in young kids. It usually shows up after the cold symptoms, by which point she's no longer contagious. If she's eating, drinking and playing normally, it typically fades within one to three weeks and may flare with heat or sun. Call your pediatrician if she seems unwell, has joint pain, or has a blood condition like sickle cell. Also tell anyone pregnant who's been around her, because the virus can occasionally affect a pregnancy.
kid has pinkeye, can i use my leftover antibiotic eye drops from last year

Better not. Leftover drops may be expired or contaminated, and they might not be the right medicine. A lot of pinkeye in kids is viral, which antibiotics won't help. Clean his eyes with warm, damp cloths and keep up the handwashing. See his doctor if there's thick yellow-green discharge, eye pain, sensitivity to light, or vision changes, or if he's a newborn.
my dad wont take his blood pressure meds because they make him pee all the time. can he just skip them on days he goes out

Skipping now and then isn't ideal, and with some drugs, especially beta blockers or clonidine, stopping suddenly can spike his blood pressure. If the culprit is a water pill like furosemide or hydrochlorothiazide, his doctor may let him shift the dose timing on outing days, or switch him to a different blood pressure medicine that doesn't cause this. The fix is a quick call to his doctor rather than his own schedule. Tell them the side effect is why he's skipping, because that's a very common and very solvable problem.
can i skip insulin for a day if i'm sick and not eating

No, especially if you're on long-acting or basal insulin, because your body still needs it when you're sick and illness often pushes sugar up. Keep taking your basal dose, check your sugar every 3 to 4 hours, drink fluids, and test for ketones if you have type 1. Call your diabetes team for sick-day dosing advice. Go to the ER if you're vomiting and can't keep fluids down or your ketones are moderate or high.
I have some leftover amoxicillin from last year. Can I just take that for my tooth infection?

Don't take leftover antibiotics. An old partial supply won't be a full course, it may not be the right drug or dose for this infection, and taking it on and off encourages resistance. Antibiotics also don't fix the source, which usually needs drainage, a root canal or an extraction. See a dentist or urgent care so they can treat it properly.
quick q - coffee before a bp reading, does it matter

Yes, caffeine can push your reading up by several points for an hour or so. For an accurate number, skip coffee, exercise and smoking for at least 30 minutes beforehand. Sit quietly for five minutes with your back supported, feet flat and arm resting at heart level.
My 16yo wants to get his wisdom teeth out and the dentist prescribed oxycodone after. Should I worry?

It's reasonable to be cautious, because teens are vulnerable to opioid misuse, and for most wisdom tooth removals, ibuprofen alternated with acetaminophen controls pain about as well or better. Ask the oral surgeon whether that combination can be the main plan, with the oxycodone only as a small backup supply. If you do fill it, keep it locked up, give the doses yourself, and safely dispose of whatever is left over.
Is it safe to take Tylenol and Advil together for a bad fever?

Yes, they're different drugs, and alternating or combining them at their normal label doses is generally safe for healthy adults. Just keep track of your total for each one, and check that your cold medicines don't contain extra acetaminophen. If your fever stays above 103°F or lasts more than three days, see a doctor.
whats the fastest way to break a fever before my shift tonight

Ibuprofen or acetaminophen will bring it down within an hour, but that only hides the fever and won't make you any less contagious. If you work with people, especially in food service, healthcare, or with kids, the responsible move is to call in and stay home until you've gone 24 hours without a fever and without medicine. Rest and fluids will help you recover faster than pushing through.
I'm 19 and want to take like 3000mg tylenol at once for a migraine, the normal dose does nothing

Please don't. A single 3000 mg dose is far above the safe maximum of 1000 mg at once, and acetaminophen can quietly damage your liver even when you feel fine afterward. For migraines, taking a normal dose early, or combining acetaminophen with ibuprofen or using caffeine-containing migraine formulas, often works better than more of one drug. If regular painkillers aren't touching your migraines, see a doctor, because prescription triptans and preventive treatments are made for exactly this.
my kid's asthma always gets worse at night. normal?

Night-time symptoms are common, but they're a sign the asthma isn't fully controlled, so it's worth a review with the doctor. They may adjust the preventer and check the inhaler technique, because spacers make a big difference for kids. At home, washing bedding hot each week and keeping pets out of the bedroom can reduce dust mite and allergen triggers.
My therapist wants me to try journaling but it feels pointless. Why does it even help?

Writing things down slows your thoughts enough to see them clearly, which makes worries feel smaller and patterns easier to spot. Studies show that expressive writing can reduce stress and even improve sleep. It doesn't need to be deep. Try five minutes on what happened, how you felt, and one thing you'd do differently. Also tell your therapist it feels pointless, because they can adjust it to something that fits you.
do i need to see someone for a cut or can i wait and see

See someone within a few hours if the cut is deeper than about a quarter inch, gapes open, keeps bleeding after 10 minutes of firm pressure, is on your face or a joint, came from an animal or human bite, or has dirt or debris you can't wash out. Small, shallow cuts with edges that stay together can be cleaned and bandaged at home. Stitches work best within about 6 to 8 hours, so it's better not to wait and see on a borderline cut.
My husband snores like a freight train and sometimes it sounds like he stops breathing for a few seconds then gasps. Is that just snoring?

That pattern of pauses followed by gasping is a classic sign of obstructive sleep apnea, which is more than just loud snoring. Untreated apnea strains the heart and raises the risk of high blood pressure, stroke, and dangerous daytime drowsiness, especially behind the wheel. He should see his doctor and ask about a sleep study, which can often be done at home now. The good news is that treatment, usually a CPAP machine or an oral appliance, tends to make people feel dramatically better.
pain in the middle of my chest that gets worse when i lie flat and better when i lean forward, had a cold last week

That pattern after a viral illness is quite typical of pericarditis, inflammation of the sac around the heart. It's usually treatable but needs a proper diagnosis, so see a doctor today or go to urgent care for an exam and ECG. Head to the ER if you get short of breath, faint, or feel your heart racing, and avoid strenuous exercise until you've been cleared.
My father has early Alzheimer's. Are those memory supplements like ginkgo or Prevagen worth trying?

The evidence for those supplements is weak, and ginkgo can raise bleeding risk, especially with blood thinners or aspirin. The better investment is talking with his doctor about approved medications that can modestly help symptoms in early Alzheimer's. Regular physical activity, social engagement, good sleep and controlling blood pressure also support brain health. If he wants to try any supplement, run it past his doctor or pharmacist first.
my 6 yr old says her tooth hurts when she eats candy but she's otherwise fine

Pain that shows up with sweets is a classic early sign of a cavity, and catching it now usually means a quick, simple filling. Book her a dental appointment in the next week or two, and in the meantime brush gently with fluoride toothpaste and cut back on sticky sweets. Call sooner if the pain starts lasting on its own, wakes her at night or comes with gum swelling.
Had Covid. Took Paxlovid. When can I lift?

Once you've been symptom-free or nearly so for a few days, light lifting is usually fine, starting at moderate weights and lower volume for the first week. Keep an eye out for rebound symptoms, which can happen after Paxlovid; if they come back, rest again. Stop and see a doctor if you get chest pain, palpitations or unusual breathlessness.
pink eye again lol. can i just use my sister's leftover antibiotic drops

I'd skip your sister's drops, because most pink eye is viral and antibiotics won't touch it, and an opened bottle can be contaminated or expired. Viral and allergic pink eye usually improves on its own with cool compresses, artificial tears, and careful handwashing. Do get seen if you have real eye pain, light sensitivity, blurred vision, thick pus, or if you wear contacts, since those can point to something that needs the right treatment.
My heart keeps skipping a beat every now and then, like a flutter, then a thump. Happens mostly at night. I'm 35 and otherwise healthy.

That flutter-then-thump feeling is most often harmless extra beats called ectopics, and they tend to feel more noticeable at night when you're lying still and it's quiet. Caffeine, alcohol, stress and poor sleep commonly make them worse, so it's worth cutting back and seeing whether they settle. Mention them to your GP anyway, because a quick ECG and possibly a wearable monitor can confirm they're benign. Seek care urgently if they come with fainting, chest pain, breathlessness, or long runs of fast irregular beating.
Will losing weight actually lower my bp or is that just something doctors say?

It really works. Systolic pressure typically drops about 1 point for every kilogram you lose, so losing 10 kg can lower it by around 10 points. That's a meaningful effect, comparable to a medication, and it often lets people reduce or avoid BP drugs.
Can I just use my friend's EpiPen to practice on myself so I know how it feels??

Please don't. Injecting real epinephrine when you're not having a reaction can cause a racing heart, shaking and spiking blood pressure, and you'd be using up someone's lifesaving device. Ask your pharmacist or doctor for a trainer pen, which has no needle or drug and is made exactly for practice. Many brands also have free demo videos and trainer devices you can order online.
Can I just super glue a dog bite shut? It's like an inch long and gaping a bit, don't want to pay for ER.

Please don't glue it, because sealing a bite traps bacteria inside and greatly increases the chance of a serious infection. A gaping inch-long bite needs a professional to clean it properly and decide whether to close it or leave it open. They may also give you antibiotics or a tetanus shot. Urgent care is usually much cheaper than the ER for this, so rinse it well, cover it with a clean dressing and go today.
Had strep, finished antibiotics, now my throat is sore again a week later. Do I need more?

Get retested rather than assuming. It could be a new viral sore throat, a strep reinfection, or occasionally a treatment failure, and only a test will tell. If it's strep again, your doctor may switch antibiotics. Replace your toothbrush too, and get seen promptly if you have trouble swallowing, drooling or a muffled voice, which can signal an abscess.
what foods help an ulcer

No specific food heals an ulcer, but a few things matter a lot. Avoid what irritates it, like alcohol, smoking and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen or aspirin. Many ulcers are caused by H. pylori bacteria, which need antibiotics, so getting tested is the real fix. Eat regular balanced meals, and steer clear of anything that clearly makes your pain worse, often spicy or acidic foods and coffee.
wisdom tooth coming in, gums sore and kinda puffy around it. normal?

Some soreness while a wisdom tooth erupts is common, but puffy, tender gum over the tooth is often pericoronitis, where food and bacteria get trapped under the flap of gum. Rinse with warm salt water several times a day, brush gently back there, and use ibuprofen if you need it. If it gets worse over a few days, tastes bad, or you have trouble opening your mouth or swallowing, see a dentist promptly, because it can turn into a real infection.
I'm pregnant and my skin is so itchy, especially my palms and the soles of my feet, worse at night. No rash really.

Intense itching on the palms and soles without a rash, especially later in pregnancy, can be a sign of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, a liver condition that needs monitoring for your baby's safety. Please call your OB or midwife today and describe it exactly like this, since they'll want to do a blood test. Many itchy skin changes in pregnancy are harmless, but this pattern is one to check out promptly.
Teen son knocked out his front tooth playing basketball. What now??

Act fast, because a knocked-out adult tooth has the best chance of being saved if it goes back in within about 30 to 60 minutes. Pick it up by the crown, not the root, and rinse it briefly if dirty without scrubbing. Try to gently put it back in the socket and have him bite on gauze. If that's not possible, store it in milk or in his cheek. Get to an emergency dentist immediately.
my friend gave me some of her sumatriptan pills for my migraine. i've never been prescribed them. fine to try one?

Hold off on that. Triptans constrict blood vessels and aren't safe for people with certain heart conditions, uncontrolled blood pressure, or some types of migraine, and they interact with some antidepressants. If over-the-counter options aren't cutting it, see a doctor, because triptans work really well for many people and you can get your own prescription that's been checked against your health history.
Stepped on a rusty nail in the garage. It went in maybe half an inch. Cleaned it. Do I actually need a tetanus shot or is that a myth?

It's not a myth, and a deep puncture like that is a classic tetanus risk, though really it's the dirt and depth that matter more than the rust. If you haven't had a tetanus booster in the last five years, or you can't remember when you did, get one in the next day or two at urgent care, a pharmacy or your doctor's office. Keep washing the wound and watch it over the next few days for spreading redness, warmth, pus or increasing pain, which would mean infection and needs treatment. Puncture wounds through a sneaker can also carry a particular foot infection, so don't ignore it if it gets worse instead of better.
Teacher here. A kid in my class is having an allergic reaction and has an epipen but parents aren't answering. Do I need permission to use it?

If the child has signs of anaphylaxis, use the EpiPen right now. That means trouble breathing, throat tightness, widespread hives with other symptoms, or vomiting and faintness. Inject into the outer thigh, through clothing if needed, and call 911. Delay is the real danger, and epinephrine is safe even if it turns out not to have been necessary. Keep the child lying down, or sitting up if breathing is hard, and keep trying the parents.
My 4 yr old has a cold for 3 days, can I give her cough syrup from the drugstore?

Skip the over-the-counter cough and cold medicines at her age. They're not recommended under 4 by the AAP, they don't work well in young kids, and they carry real overdose risk. Since she's 4 and over a year old, a half teaspoon to a teaspoon of honey before bed often works better for the cough. Use saline spray for her nose and give plenty of fluids. See her doctor if she's breathing hard, has a fever above 102 that lasts more than three days, or still has the cold after 10 days.
Does creatine damage your kidneys? I'm 19 and want to start for the gym.

For healthy people at the standard dose of 3 to 5 grams a day, creatine is one of the most studied supplements and hasn't been shown to harm kidneys. It can raise creatinine on blood tests, which is harmless but worth mentioning to your doctor so it isn't misread. If you have any kidney condition, diabetes or high blood pressure, check with a doctor first. Stick to plain creatine monohydrate from a third-party-tested brand and drink enough water.
I had a mild reaction to my first COVID shot, some hives a few hours later. Should I skip the second dose?

Don't just skip it, but don't get it without advice either. Delayed hives are usually not a reason to avoid future doses, and many people receive them safely with simple precautions like taking an antihistamine beforehand or being watched longer afterward. Talk to your doctor or an allergist, who can look at what happened and decide on the safest plan. If your reaction had included breathing trouble or throat swelling, getting specialist input first would be essential.
just grabbed a hot pan handle, palm is red and stinging, no blisters. what do i do

Run your palm under cool (not icy) tap water for a solid 20 minutes, which sounds excessive but genuinely limits how deep the burn goes. After that, pat it dry, use a plain moisturizer or aloe if it feels tight, and take ibuprofen or acetaminophen for the sting. A red, unblistered burn like this usually settles in a few days. Get it checked if blisters spread across a large part of your palm or the pain gets worse instead of better.
Traveling to Mexico at 22 weeks, any issue?

The second trimester is generally the best time to travel, but check the CDC's Zika guidance for your specific destination first, since Zika can cause serious birth defects. Use DEET insect repellent, which is safe in pregnancy, drink bottled water, and get your OB's sign-off. It's also smart to know where the nearest good hospital is and to bring a copy of your prenatal records.
Diagnosed prediabetic yesterday. Is it basically over, am I going to get diabetes?

Not at all, prediabetes is the stage where things are most reversible. Losing around 5 to 7% of your body weight and getting about 150 minutes of brisk activity a week cut the risk of progressing by more than half in major trials. Ask your doctor about a structured prevention program and recheck your HbA1c in a year.
I'm a 45 yo guy, had covid 3 weeks ago, and since then my heart races when I climb stairs. I used to play tennis. Just ignore it and get back out there?

Don't ignore that. A racing heart on mild exertion after COVID can be harmless deconditioning, but it can also point to heart inflammation, rhythm problems or POTS, and those need ruling out before you get back to something as intense as tennis. Get an appointment with your doctor soon and ask about an ECG and possibly further heart tests. If you get chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness, go to urgent care right away.
quick q is 5 hours of sleep enough if I feel fine

For the vast majority of adults it isn't, even if it feels fine. Studies show people on chronic short sleep stop noticing how impaired they are while their reaction time and focus keep slipping. Most adults need 7 to 9 hours, and regularly getting less is linked to weight gain, higher blood pressure and getting sick more often. Try a week of 7-plus hours; many people are surprised how much sharper they feel.
I get migraine with aura and my doctor wants to put me on the combined birth control pill. any issue?

Yes, it's worth raising with your doctor. Migraine with aura modestly increases stroke risk, and estrogen-containing birth control raises it further, so major guidelines generally advise against combined pills for people who have aura. Progestin-only pills, hormonal or copper IUDs and the implant are typically safer alternatives. Make sure your doctor knows specifically about the aura, since it changes the recommendation.
ran out of my lisinopril 3 days ago, pharmacy says refill needs doctor approval. honestly i feel fine, is it ok to just skip it till my appt in 2 weeks?

Two weeks off is longer than I'd risk. Your pressure can creep back up without any symptoms, and that's exactly why it's easy to ignore. Call your doctor's office today and ask for a refill authorization, which most offices handle quickly. Many pharmacists can also give an emergency supply in the meantime, so ask them directly.
can't sleep, mind racing about money. tips?

Keep a notepad by the bed and write down every worry, plus one next step for each. This tells your brain the problems are parked until morning. If you're still awake after about 20 minutes, get up and do something dull in dim light until you feel sleepy, rather than lying there stressing. During the day, set aside a fixed 15-minute 'worry time' to deal with money properly. Free debt advice services can also take a lot of the weight off.
Weird itchy rash between my fingers and on my wrists, worse at night. My kid has it too.

Itching between the fingers and on the wrists that's worse at night, and is shared with a family member, is very suggestive of scabies. See a doctor or pharmacist to confirm it, because the treatment is a prescription or pharmacy cream such as permethrin. Everyone in the household should be treated at the same time, even if they don't itch yet. On the treatment day, wash bedding, towels and clothes in hot water, and bag anything you can't wash for a few days.
should I stop taking my blood pressure meds the morning before surgery?

Don't guess on this one, because the answer depends on which drug you take. Some, like beta blockers, are usually continued, while others, like ACE inhibitors or diuretics, are sometimes held. Call your surgeon's office or the pre-op nurse and ask about each medication by name. They give these instructions all the time.
can i just take double the dose of advil if the normal one doesn't work for my headache

Don't go above the label dose without a doctor's okay. Higher doses raise the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems, and they often don't add much pain relief. Taking the standard dose early in a headache usually works better, and if regular doses consistently fail, talk to a doctor about stronger, more targeted options.
I'm diabetic and I've got a small sore on the bottom of my foot that isn't healing. Been about 10 days.

With diabetes, a foot sore that hasn't healed in 10 days needs a doctor's eyes this week. Foot ulcers can get infected or go deep without much pain, because nerve damage dulls sensation. Keep weight off it as much as you can, keep it clean and covered, and check it daily. Go in sooner if you see redness spreading, swelling, drainage or odor, or if you get a fever.
just grabbed a hot pan handle, palm is bright red and stinging like crazy. ice?

Skip the ice, because it can damage already-injured skin. Run the burn under cool tap water for a full 20 minutes, which really does reduce how deep the damage goes even if it feels like overkill. After that, cover it loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing, and take ibuprofen or paracetamol for the pain. If blisters form across a large part of your palm, get it checked, since hand burns can affect how the skin heals over joints.
Started fluoxetine 2 weeks ago, feel nothing. Should I up the dose myself?

Don't adjust it yourself. Two weeks is early, since fluoxetine usually takes 4 to 6 weeks to show its full effect. Tell your prescriber how you're doing, because they can decide whether and when to increase it safely. If you have any thoughts of harming yourself, which can sometimes increase early in treatment, especially in younger people, contact them right away or call or text 988 in the US.
I'm pregnant and just recovered from a cold. Can I go back to prenatal yoga?

Yes, if you're past the fever and feeling okay, prenatal yoga is a great way to ease back in. Go gently for the first class or two and stay well hydrated. If you have any lingering shortness of breath or feel unusually tired, mention it to your midwife or OB at your next visit.
Antibiotic gave me hives and my lips feel tingly. Should I take another dose tonight?

Don't take another dose. Hives with lip tingling suggests an allergic reaction, which can escalate. If your lips, tongue or throat swell, or you have trouble breathing or feel faint, call emergency services immediately. Otherwise, contact your doctor or an urgent care tonight about switching antibiotics, and an antihistamine like cetirizine can help the hives. Make sure this drug gets recorded as an allergy in your records.
My parents want to stop taking their statins because they read online they're dangerous for old people. They're 78 and 81. Should I support that?

Don't let them stop on their own. The decision depends on things like whether they've already had a heart attack or stroke, which makes statins more clearly worthwhile. Stopping on a hunch can raise their risk. That said, deprescribing in older age is a legitimate conversation. Encourage them to bring their concerns to their doctor, who can weigh their actual risk and side effects and adjust or stop the drug properly if it makes sense.
my husband snores like a chainsaw and sometimes stops breathing for a few seconds then gasps. he says its fine. is it?

Loud snoring with pauses and gasps is the classic picture of obstructive sleep apnea, and it isn't fine just because he feels okay. Untreated apnea raises the risk of high blood pressure, heart rhythm problems, stroke and drowsy-driving crashes. He should see his doctor and ask about a sleep study, which can often be done at home now. If you can take a short video of an episode, that can really help convince both him and the doctor.
pinworms. can i just treat the whole family with the over the counter stuff

Yes, that's actually the standard approach. Pyrantel pamoate, sold as Pin-X or Reese's, treats the whole household, and you repeat the dose after two weeks. Check with a doctor first for anyone pregnant, breastfeeding, or under 2. Wash bedding and underwear in hot water, keep nails short, and have everyone wash hands well to stop reinfection.
Can I work out with a fever if I just drink lots of water?

No, drinking more water doesn't make it safe to work out with a fever. Exercising with a fever raises your body temperature further, strains your heart, and in rare cases can be risky if a virus is affecting the heart muscle. Rest until the fever has been gone for at least a day or two without fever reducers, then ease back in with light activity.
migraine for 4 days straight now, nothing touching it, idk what to do

A migraine lasting more than 72 hours is called status migrainosus, and it's worth getting treated properly today rather than pushing through. Go to urgent care or the ER, where they can give IV fluids and medications that often break the cycle. Go immediately if you have weakness, confusion, a stiff neck, fever or a headache that feels different from your usual ones.
Is ear candling safe? My friend swears by it.

It isn't safe, and it doesn't work either. Tests have shown it doesn't pull out any wax, and the brown residue people find is just burnt candle. Meanwhile it causes real burns to the face and ear canal, and dripping wax can block the ear or damage the eardrum. Softening drops or a quick cleaning at your doctor's office are the safe options.
quick q: can antibiotics make birth control stop working

For almost all antibiotics, no. Rifampin and rifabutin, used mainly for tuberculosis, are the main ones known to reduce hormonal birth control's effectiveness. If you're on one of those, use condoms as backup. If any antibiotic gives you vomiting or severe diarrhea, though, your pill may not get absorbed properly, so follow your pill's missed-dose instructions in that case.
Is it bad to sleep with the TV on? I can't fall asleep in silence.

It's not dangerous, but the light and changing volume can fragment your sleep even if you don't fully wake up. Set a sleep timer so it shuts off after 30 to 60 minutes, or switch to steady audio like a fan, white noise, or a familiar podcast with the screen off. Many people find they adjust within a week or two. That way you still get the comfort of background sound without the flashing light all night.
can elderly people take melatonin safely

Melatonin is generally one of the safer sleep aids for older adults, and low doses of 0.5 to 3 mg often work as well as higher ones with less morning grogginess. It can interact with blood thinners and some blood pressure or diabetes medications, so a quick check with the pharmacist is worth it. If sleep problems are persistent, it's still worth asking the doctor about underlying causes.
Can I give my dog's leftover antibiotics to myself? Same name as the human ones.

Please don't. Vet antibiotics can be dosed and made for animals in ways that don't match human needs, and they may contain different inactive ingredients or concentrations. Self-treating also means guessing whether you even have a bacterial infection. A telehealth visit or urgent care can sort out what you actually need fairly cheaply.
Severe itching all over for weeks, no rash at all. Lotion isn't helping. Should I just take more Benadryl?

Don't keep increasing Benadryl, because higher doses cause drowsiness, confusion, and other side effects, especially in older adults. Itching all over for weeks with no rash should be checked by a doctor, as it can sometimes point to liver, kidney, or thyroid problems, iron deficiency, or a medication side effect, which simple blood tests can pick up. In the meantime, try a non-drowsy antihistamine like cetirizine, lukewarm showers, and a fragrance-free moisturizer straight afterward.
Mom keeps calling me by my sister's name. Should I be worried about dementia?

Mixing up family members' names is extremely common at every age and on its own doesn't suggest dementia. More concerning signs are getting lost in familiar places, repeating the same questions within minutes, missing bills, or struggling with tasks she used to handle easily. If you're noticing any of those, ask her doctor for a cognitive screening, which is quick and often reveals treatable issues like thyroid problems or B12 deficiency.
Teenage son with T1 wants to start drinking at parties and won't listen to me.

Since he may drink anyway, focus on keeping him safe rather than winning the argument. Ask his diabetes team to talk with him directly, because teens often listen to them more than to parents. The key messages are to eat while drinking, never skip his insulin, check before bed and have a snack, and make sure a friend knows he's diabetic. A CGM with alerts that you can see can add a real safety net.
is turmeric safe with blood thinners? I'm on warfarin

Use caution here, because concentrated turmeric or curcumin supplements can increase warfarin's effect and raise your bleeding risk. Normal amounts in cooking are generally fine, but supplements are a different story. Talk to your anticoagulation clinic or doctor before you start one, and if you do start, they'll probably want to check your INR more closely.
hot tub ok if i keep it short? 14 weeks, friends' cabin weekend

It's safest to skip the hot tub, because raising your core temperature in early pregnancy has been linked to neural tube defects, and it can happen faster than you'd think. If you really want in, dangling your legs or sitting with your upper body out and keeping the water well below 100°F is a reasonable compromise. A warm pool or the regular shower is the no-worry option for the weekend.
Is it ok to do a marathon with asthma? Training for my first one, 34F.

Absolutely, plenty of elite marathoners have asthma. The key is having your asthma well controlled day to day, so keep taking your preventer and ask your doctor whether you should use your reliever 15 minutes before runs. Carry your inhaler on long training runs and on race day. Cold air and high pollen can be triggers, so build up gradually and pay attention to how your chest feels.
I'm 67, just diagnosed with type 2 and honestly terrified. My dad lost a foot to diabetes. Is that going to be me?

It's completely understandable to be scared after watching that happen to your dad, but foot complications are largely preventable today, especially when they're caught early like yours. Keep your blood sugar in your target range, check your feet every day for cuts, blisters, or color changes, wear well-fitting shoes, and have a proper foot exam at least once a year. Ask your doctor to refer you to a diabetes education program, because people who go through one tend to feel far more in control. You're starting this with knowledge your dad may not have had, and that matters a lot.
Detailed question: 34F, started a new antibiotic 5 days ago for a UTI, now an itchy red rash on my trunk, no fever, mouth fine. Stop the antibiotic?

Call the prescriber or a pharmacist today, because a new rash a few days into an antibiotic is often a drug reaction and they may want to switch you to a different medicine instead of just stopping, since the UTI still needs treating. An antihistamine can help the itch in the meantime. Seek emergency care straight away if you develop blistering or peeling skin, sores in your mouth or eyes, fever, facial swelling or trouble breathing, as those can be signs of a serious reaction. Make a note of the antibiotic's name so it can be recorded as a possible allergy.
rash on my 5 yo, little red/purple dots that dont fade when i press a glass on them, he has a fever

Take him to the emergency room now or call emergency services. A fever together with a rash that doesn't fade under a glass can be a sign of meningococcal infection or another serious condition, and this needs urgent treatment. Don't wait to see if it spreads or for other symptoms to appear.
How much ibuprofen and tylenol can I take together for a really bad toothache? Normal doses aren't cutting it.

For healthy adults, many dentists recommend combining 400 mg ibuprofen with 500 mg acetaminophen every 6 to 8 hours, which often beats either drug alone. Keep within the daily limits, which are 1200 mg ibuprofen and 3000 mg acetaminophen when you're self-treating without a doctor's guidance. Don't push past those limits, because higher doses risk stomach bleeding and liver damage. Pain that strong usually means a nerve or infection problem that only a dentist can fix, so book an urgent appointment.
Got food poisoning 4 days ago, still feeling weak. Is a light jog okay or should I wait?

If you're keeping food and fluids down without trouble, a slow 15 to 20 minute walk is a better first step than a jog. That weak feeling usually means you're still low on fluids and fuel. Try a light jog once you have more energy, and stop if you feel dizzy or crampy. If the weakness lingers past a week, see a doctor.
fever 102 for 4 days now, adult, otherwise kinda ok. still waiting it out?

Four days of fever at 102°F is long enough that you should see a doctor rather than keep waiting. Most viral fevers start improving within about three days. A fever that lasts longer can point to something like a bacterial infection, pneumonia, or a urinary infection that needs testing or treatment. Book a same-day appointment or go to urgent care. Go sooner if you develop shortness of breath, chest pain, confusion, or a stiff neck.
My friend says I can take my leftover ibuprofen for back pain, I'm 30 weeks. Fine right?

Skip the ibuprofen at this stage. NSAIDs taken after about 20 weeks can affect the baby's kidneys and amniotic fluid levels, and later in pregnancy they can affect the baby's heart. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is the usual go-to for pain in pregnancy, along with heat, gentle stretching or a support belt. If your back pain is severe or comes in waves, call your provider, because it can sometimes be a sign of labor.
are grapefruits really a problem with statins or is that a myth

It's real for some statins. Grapefruit blocks an enzyme that breaks down simvastatin, lovastatin and atorvastatin, which can raise drug levels and the risk of muscle damage. Rosuvastatin and pravastatin are much less affected. Check which one you're on, and if it's one of the sensitive ones, avoid grapefruit or ask your pharmacist how much is reasonable.
I'm 68 and on warfarin. My knee is killing me. Can I take Aleve?

Avoid Aleve. Naproxen, like ibuprofen and aspirin, raises your bleeding risk significantly when combined with warfarin, including stomach bleeds. Acetaminophen is usually the safer choice for you, up to about 3000 mg a day. Even acetaminophen can nudge your INR up if you take it regularly, so tell your anticoagulation clinic if you'll be using it daily. Ice, topical diclofenac gel used sparingly, and a talk with your doctor about the knee itself are also worth trying.
I'm 68 and my friend says I should be taking B12. Is that true

Your friend has a point. Absorption of B12 from food drops with age, and deficiency is fairly common after 60. It's even more common if you take metformin or acid reducers like omeprazole. Rather than guessing, ask your doctor for a simple blood test. If you're low, a supplement or injections fix it easily, and catching it early prevents the fatigue, numbness and memory problems it can cause.
fever keeps spiking every evening for 2 weeks now, low grade, also lost some weight. ideas?

That pattern needs a proper workup, so book a doctor's appointment this week rather than waiting. A fever that lasts two weeks with weight loss can come from things like a persistent infection, tuberculosis, an autoimmune condition, or less commonly something like lymphoma. Mention any night sweats, travel, or recent exposures, since those help narrow it down.
My 2 year old has had a fever of 39 for three days and keeps tugging his ear. Do I need to go in or will it pass?

Three days of fever plus ear tugging in a toddler is worth a doctor's visit now. Many ear infections clear on their own, but at his age with a fever that long, someone should look in the ear and decide whether antibiotics are needed. Keep him comfortable with weight-appropriate doses of children's paracetamol or ibuprofen until then. Go in urgently if he becomes very drowsy, develops a stiff neck or rash, or stops drinking.
Kid might have swallowed one of those little flat batteries from a remote, not sure. What do I do

Treat this as an emergency and go to the ER now, because button batteries can burn through the esophagus within a couple of hours even if your child looks fine. If your child is over a year old and you can get there without delay, giving two teaspoons of honey every 10 minutes on the way (up to six doses) may slow the damage. Don't make your child vomit. Bring the battery packaging or a matching battery if you can.
deep cut on my palm and now my finger feels numb and i cant bend it right

Numbness and trouble bending your finger after a palm cut suggest a nerve or tendon may be damaged, so get to the ER or urgent care today. Hand injuries like this often need specialist repair, and outcomes are much better when they're fixed early. Keep pressure on it with a clean cloth and hold your hand raised on the way. Don't wait to see if the feeling comes back.
Is it okay to give honey to my 9-month-old for her cough?

No, hold off on honey until after her first birthday. Honey can contain botulism spores that a baby's gut can't handle yet, and infant botulism is rare but serious. For now, a cool-mist humidifier, saline drops, and gentle suctioning of her nose can ease the cough. Call her doctor if she's breathing fast, wheezing, or the cough lasts more than a week or two.
my 8 year old has asthma and keeps coughing at night but seems fine during the day. normal?

Nighttime coughing is actually a classic sign that a child's asthma isn't fully controlled, even if they seem fine during the day. Book an appointment with their pediatrician, who may adjust or start a daily controller inhaler. In the meantime, look for bedroom triggers like dust mites, pets on the bed, or smoke exposure. If you ever see them struggling to breathe, pulling in at the ribs, or too breathless to talk, get emergency care right away.
Can I use my partner's bp cuff and pills? same condition

Sharing the cuff is fine if it fits your arm properly. Don't take their pills, though. Blood pressure drugs differ a lot, and the wrong one or the wrong dose can drop you too low or interact with your other meds. Get your own prescription so it's matched to you.
My 2 year old has a fever and all I have is adult Tylenol. Can I just cut a pill in half?

Please don't. Half of a 500 mg tablet is roughly twice what most two-year-olds should get, and cutting pills makes the dose unpredictable. Children's acetaminophen is dosed by weight, about 15 mg per kg, so a quick trip for infant or children's liquid with its own syringe is the safe option. If you can't get some tonight, a pharmacist or your pediatrician's after-hours line can help.
