Call the doctor right away if your child is under 3 months, seems very lethargic, has trouble breathing or keeps a fever over 104°F.
woke up and half my face feels droopy and my eye won't close all the way

Facial droop needs urgent attention, so call emergency services or go to the ER right now, because it can be a stroke and time matters a lot. It might turn out to be Bell's palsy, but only a doctor can rule out a stroke, and Bell's palsy also responds best to treatment started early. Until you're seen, protect that eye from drying out with lubricating drops and keep it gently covered.
can i take pepto if i'm on a daily aspirin

It's best to check with your doctor or pharmacist first, because Pepto-Bismol contains bismuth subsalicylate, a chemical relative of aspirin. Taking the two together can raise your risk of bleeding and stomach irritation. A plain calcium carbonate antacid like Tums is usually the safer pick for heartburn or indigestion in the meantime.
found a bat in my kid's bedroom this morning, no bite marks I can see. bat's still in the house. what do i do

Treat this seriously. Bat bites can be tiny enough to miss, and a sleeping child might not notice or report one. If you can do it safely with thick gloves, trap the bat under a container without crushing its head, then call your local health department or animal control right away so it can be tested for rabies. Call your pediatrician today as well, because health guidelines usually recommend rabies shots after a bat is found in a room with a sleeping child, unless the bat tests negative.
my toddler swallowed a button battery i think?? hes acting fine

Go to the emergency room right now, even though he seems fine. A button battery stuck in the esophagus can cause serious burns within about two hours, often before any symptoms appear. If he's over 12 months old and it happened within the last 12 hours, you can give 2 teaspoons of honey every 10 minutes on the way, up to 6 doses, to help protect the tissue. Don't make him vomit, and bring the battery packaging if you have it.
my belly is swollen and hard, havent pooped in 3 days and keep throwing up

Go to the emergency room now. A swollen, hard belly with vomiting and no bowel movements can be a sign of a bowel obstruction, which needs urgent treatment. Don't eat, and don't take laxatives in the meantime. If you feel very unwell, have severe pain or feel faint, call 911.
Is it safe to take Tylenol for a headache while pregnant?

Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is generally considered the go-to pain reliever in pregnancy when used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest time. Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin unless your doctor specifically tells you otherwise, especially after 20 weeks. If the headache is severe, won't go away, or comes with vision changes or swelling in the second half of pregnancy, call your provider right away, since that can be a sign of preeclampsia.
can i exercise if my blood sugar is 290

It depends on ketones. If you have type 1, or you're on insulin, check for ketones first, and if they're moderate or high, don't exercise, because it can push you toward ketoacidosis. If ketones are negative and you feel fine, light to moderate exercise is generally okay and can help bring the number down. Stay hydrated and recheck. If you have type 2 and aren't on insulin, a walk is usually fine. But if you're seeing numbers like 290 regularly, let your doctor know.
small red dots on my legs that don't fade when I press a glass on them, I also feel feverish

Spots that don't fade under a glass combined with a fever need urgent medical attention, so go to the emergency department or call emergency services now. That combination can be a sign of a serious infection like meningococcal disease or a blood problem, and quick treatment matters. Don't wait to see if it gets better.
34F, pregnant 32 weeks, got a reading of 145/95 and a headache that won't quit. probably just stress right?

Please don't assume it's stress. High blood pressure plus a persistent headache in the third trimester can be a sign of preeclampsia, which needs prompt evaluation. Call your OB or labor and delivery unit now, or go in, especially if you have vision changes, upper belly pain, or sudden swelling. They can check your urine and bloodwork quickly, and it's much better to be checked and reassured than to wait.
cut my hand on glass, bleeding stopped but i can't fully bend my finger now

Get that seen today. Trouble bending a finger after a cut can mean a tendon or nerve was damaged, and those repairs work best when done early. Keep the cut covered and don't try to test or force the finger. Urgent care or an ER can check it and refer you to a hand specialist if needed.
how many hours of sleep do i actually need when stressed, i'm getting like 5

Most adults need seven to nine hours. Five a night will amplify stress, because sleep loss makes the brain more reactive to threats and less able to regulate mood. Keep a consistent wake time, cut caffeine after midday, and put screens away for the last half hour before bed. If stress keeps you lying awake for weeks, CBT for insomnia is the most effective treatment and your doctor can point you to it.
burned my hand on the oven rack, should I put butter on it

Skip the butter, because it traps heat and can raise infection risk. Run the burn under cool (not ice-cold) running water for a good 20 minutes, which genuinely limits the damage even if you start a few minutes late. After that, cover it loosely with a clean non-stick dressing or plastic wrap and take ibuprofen or acetaminophen for pain if you need it. If it's bigger than your palm, blistering badly, white or leathery, or on a joint, get it seen.
fever plus really bad headache and my neck hurts to bend forward. 19, college dorm

Get to an emergency department or urgent care right now. That combination can be a sign of meningitis, which spreads in dorms and can worsen within hours. Tell staff about the stiff neck right away, and have someone go with you if possible. A purple or dark rash that doesn't fade when pressed makes this even more urgent.
temp 102 and my neck is really stiff and light hurts my eyes

Go to the emergency room now. Fever with a stiff neck and light sensitivity are classic warning signs of meningitis, and that needs immediate treatment. Don't drive yourself if you feel very unwell. Call emergency services if you notice a rash or get confused.
does salt really matter that much or is that overblown

For many people it really does matter. Cutting sodium to around 1,500–2,300 mg a day can lower systolic pressure by about 5–6 points, which is similar to what some medications achieve. Most of that sodium comes from processed and restaurant food rather than the salt shaker, so reading food labels makes the biggest difference.
Is a chiropractor safe for lower back pain or a scam?

Spinal manipulation can give modest short-term relief for some uncomplicated lower back pain, about on par with exercise-based physiotherapy. It isn't a scam, but it isn't a cure either. Be wary of anyone who wants regular X-rays, sells long prepaid treatment packages, or claims to treat non-back conditions. A physiotherapist is often the better first choice because they'll give you exercises that keep helping after the appointments end.
My 4 year old has had a fever for 5 days now, it keeps coming back after the tylenol wears off. She's eating a bit. Should I keep waiting it out?

Five days is long enough that she should be seen by her doctor, ideally today. Most viral fevers settle within three days. A fever that persists can point to an ear infection, a urinary tract infection or, less commonly, something like Kawasaki disease, which needs prompt treatment. Watch especially for red eyes, cracked lips, a rash or swollen hands and feet.
Is Neosporin necessary or is Vaseline fine for a scrape?

Plain petroleum jelly works just as well for most minor scrapes and doesn't carry the allergy risk that some antibiotic ointments do. Clean the scrape well with water, put on a thin layer of Vaseline, and cover it. See someone if it gets redder, more painful, or starts oozing pus.
neck stiff, bad headache, fever. slept wrong?

A stiff neck with a fever and bad headache isn't something to chalk up to sleeping wrong. It can be a sign of meningitis, which is a medical emergency. Get seen at an emergency department now. Go especially fast if you're sensitive to light, feel confused, or notice a rash that doesn't fade when pressed.
sharp ear pain and some blood after a slap/hit to the ear. hearing muffled

That could be a ruptured eardrum, so keep the ear dry and don't put any drops or anything else in it. Most small tears heal within a few weeks, but you should see a doctor in the next day or so to confirm it and check your hearing. Go to the ER if you have severe dizziness, a lot of bleeding, or a head injury. If someone hit you on purpose and you're not safe, please reach out for help as well.
Can I take ibuprofen for chest pain? I've got a wall in my chest that hurts after shoveling snow. 58 years old.

Please don't treat this as a muscle strain yet, because shoveling snow is a well-known trigger for heart attacks in people your age. Chest pain right after that kind of heavy exertion needs to be ruled out as cardiac first. Call emergency services if the pain is ongoing, spreading, or comes with breathlessness or sweating. Get same-day medical assessment even if it's eased.
my 4 month old will only sleep on her tummy and she sleeps so much better that way. is it ok if i watch her?

Safe sleep guidelines are clear that babies should be placed on their backs for every sleep until age one, because tummy sleeping significantly raises the risk of SIDS. Even watching closely doesn't protect her, since SIDS happens silently and you'd eventually doze off too. Supervised tummy time while she's awake is great, and once she can roll both ways on her own it's fine to let her stay in the position she rolls into. If back sleeping is a constant battle, her pediatrician can help with settling strategies.
My doctor said my iron is low. Can I just double up on the iron pills so it fixes faster?

Don't double up without checking with your doctor first. Higher doses mostly bring more constipation, nausea and stomach pain without fixing things much faster. Taking too much can also be genuinely dangerous, especially if kids in the house could get into the bottle. Some research suggests taking iron every other day absorbs as well as daily dosing, so ask your doctor about that, and take it with vitamin C rather than tea, coffee or dairy to help it absorb.
I'm vegan for 3 years and never took B12. Is that a problem or is it just a myth?

It's not a myth, and after three years you should get it checked. Reliable B12 essentially only comes from animal foods, fortified foods or supplements, and body stores can take years to run down, so feeling fine now doesn't mean you're in the clear. Deficiency can cause anemia and nerve damage that isn't always fully reversible. Ask for a B12 test, possibly with methylmalonic acid, and start a supplement or fortified foods regardless.
rubbing alcohol on skin to cool fever, my grandma swears by it

Skip the alcohol. Skin absorbs it, and children can be poisoned this way. It also cools the skin so fast that it can trigger shivering, which pushes the core temperature back up. A lukewarm sponge bath, light clothing and an appropriate fever reducer are safer and work better.
Can I take melatonin every night forever?

Low-dose melatonin is fairly safe, but it isn't really meant to be a forever nightly fix. Small doses of 0.5 to 3 mg are often as effective as bigger ones and cause less grogginess. If you need something every single night to sleep, there's likely an underlying issue like stress, irregular schedules or sleep apnea worth sorting out with a doctor. CBT for insomnia is the gold-standard long-term treatment.
Is it safe to fly at 34 weeks? Just a 2 hour flight to see my parents.

Many airlines allow travel up to 36 weeks for a single pregnancy, but some ask for a doctor's letter after about 28 weeks, so check your airline's policy before you book. Talk to your midwife first as well, because a complication like preeclampsia or a twin pregnancy can change the advice. Make sure you take your pregnancy notes with you, drink plenty of water, and walk the aisle or flex your ankles often to lower the risk of a blood clot.
Does yogurt or probiotics actually help with antibiotic side effects

There's modest evidence that probiotics, particularly Saccharomyces boulardii and certain Lactobacillus strains, reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea for some people. They're low-risk for most healthy adults; just take them a couple of hours apart from your antibiotic dose. If you're immunocompromised or seriously ill, check with your doctor first. Yogurt is fine to eat, but avoid dairy around doses of drugs like doxycycline or cipro.
throbbing headache behind one eye, eye is red and blurry, seeing halos around lights

Go to an ER or urgent eye clinic now. Eye pain with redness, blurry vision and halos can be acute angle-closure glaucoma, which raises eye pressure quickly and can cause permanent vision loss within hours. If it comes with nausea or vomiting, that makes it even more urgent.
Hiking and my friend got a deep gash on his shin from a rock, we're 3 miles from the car

Press firmly on the wound with the cleanest fabric you have, and hold steady pressure for at least 10 minutes with his leg raised. If it soaks through, add more material on top rather than removing the first layer. If it's bleeding heavily and won't stop with pressure, call 911 or use a tourniquet high on the thigh if you have one. Once it's controlled, rinse it with drinking water, wrap it snugly, and head straight out to urgent care, because a deep gash likely needs cleaning and closure.
IBS flare. Cramping, alternating constipation and diarrhea. What helps that isn't a doctor visit

Peppermint oil capsules have decent evidence for easing IBS cramping, and soluble fiber like psyllium can steady things whether you're swinging toward constipation or diarrhea. Regular meals, cutting back on fatty food, caffeine and alcohol, and trying a low-FODMAP diet for a few weeks often help a lot. Stress management and exercise also make a real difference. If you've never had IBS formally diagnosed, or notice blood, weight loss or nighttime symptoms, it's worth seeing a doctor to confirm it's IBS.
punched my friend's dog off me (it attacked my dog) and now my knuckle has a cut from its tooth and its swelling. I'll just ice it

Ice is fine for comfort, but a tooth cut over a knuckle with swelling needs to be seen today. Knuckle wounds can carry bacteria into the joint or tendon, and those infections can damage hand function if they're not treated early. Wash it thoroughly, then go to urgent care or an ER, where they may give antibiotics and check for joint involvement. Also find out whether the dog's rabies shots are current.
My ferret bit me hard enough to bleed. Is that a rabies thing or no?

Ferrets can carry rabies, so this matters more than a hamster bite would, although the risk is very low if yours is vaccinated and stays indoors. Wash the bite with soap and water for several minutes and check your ferret's rabies vaccination record. Then call your doctor, who will likely advise watching the ferret for 10 days and checking whether your tetanus shot is up to date. If the ferret is unvaccinated or gets sick or dies during that time, contact your doctor or health department right away.
wheezing a bit, out of breath on stairs, no asthma history. 52. just a cold?

It might be, but new wheezing and breathlessness at 52 deserve a check-up rather than a guess. Your doctor can listen to your chest and look into causes like asthma, a chest infection or a heart problem. Book an appointment in the next few days. Go to urgent care or call emergency services if you get chest pain, can't catch your breath at rest, or your lips turn bluish.
whats the max nyquil i can take, i really need to sleep tonight

Stick to the dose on the label, which is usually 30 mL for adults, and don't take more than four doses in 24 hours. Don't double up, because NyQuil contains acetaminophen, and too much can seriously damage your liver. Watch out for taking it alongside Tylenol or another cold medicine that has acetaminophen in it too. Skip alcohol with it, and propping your head up plus using a humidifier can help you sleep better without extra medicine.
can i just take double the ibuprofen for my knee, the normal dose isn't doing anything

I wouldn't double it. Higher doses raise the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain without adding much pain relief. A better move is to stay within the label limit, which is 1,200 mg a day over the counter, and alternate or combine it with acetaminophen, since the two work differently and are safe together for most people. Add ice, elevation and a knee sleeve if there's swelling. If normal doses truly aren't touching the pain, the knee deserves an exam rather than more pills.
Feeling shaky and sweaty, no meter with me, type 2 on insulin. Eat or wait?

Eat fast sugar now, such as juice, regular soda, candy, or glucose tablets. If it's a low, waiting is dangerous, and if it turns out you weren't low, a bit of extra sugar does little harm. Wait about 15 minutes, and if you still feel shaky, take more. When you're back with your meter, check your levels, and start carrying a meter and sugar with you.
I'm 72 and tripped on the curb, scraped my shin pretty badly. Skin is kind of peeled back in a flap.

Rinse it gently with clean water and, if the skin flap is still attached, ease it back over the wound without stretching it. Then cover it with a non-stick dressing. Skin tears like this heal better when properly dressed, and shin wounds can be slow to heal as we get older, so it's worth having a doctor or nurse look at it within a day. Get seen sooner if it's bleeding heavily or you take blood thinners.
I'm 58, my dad is 84 and I think he's depressed since mom died last year. He says old people are just sad. True?

No. Grief after losing a spouse is normal, but persistent depression isn't a normal part of aging, and it's very treatable at any age. If a year later he's withdrawn, sleeping or eating poorly, or has lost interest in things, encourage a visit to his doctor and offer to go along. Ask him directly whether he's had thoughts of not wanting to live. Older men have the highest suicide risk, and if he says yes, call or text 988 together.
I've had a dull headache for 3 weeks straight. never had headaches before. I'm 58.

A new, persistent headache that starts after age 50 is worth seeing a doctor about soon, within days rather than weeks. Most of the time the cause is benign, but doctors want to rule out things like high blood pressure, medication side effects and giant cell arteritis, an artery inflammation that can threaten vision. If you develop jaw pain when chewing, scalp tenderness or any vision changes, get seen the same day.
Headache every morning when I wake up for the past few weeks, goes away after an hour or so. 52M. Wife says I snore a lot.

Morning headaches combined with heavy snoring are a common pattern in sleep apnea, where your breathing repeatedly drops during the night and lowers your oxygen. It's worth seeing your doctor and asking about a sleep study, since untreated apnea also raises the risk of high blood pressure and heart problems. Mention any daytime sleepiness, and know that new persistent headaches at your age deserve a checkup anyway.
I'm 7 months pregnant and my lower back and pelvis are in agony. What can I take?

Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is generally considered the safe choice in pregnancy at normal doses. Avoid ibuprofen and other NSAIDs at this stage, because they can affect the baby's heart and kidneys in the third trimester. A maternity support belt, warm (not hot) compresses, sleeping with a pillow between your knees, and a physio who specializes in pregnancy can all make a real difference with pelvic girdle pain. Mention it to your midwife or OB too, and call them promptly if the pain comes in rhythmic waves or you notice bleeding or leaking fluid, since that could be labor.
I'm 7 weeks pregnant and spotting a little pink when I wipe. Is this a miscarriage??

Light pink spotting in early pregnancy is common and often harmless, caused by things like implantation or a sensitive cervix, so it doesn't automatically mean a miscarriage. Call your midwife or doctor today so they can check you, possibly with an ultrasound or blood test. Go to urgent care or the ER right away if the bleeding becomes heavy like a period, you pass clots, or you have strong cramping, one-sided pain or dizziness.
I'm 72 and since my husband died last year I don't see much point in things. My kids are busy. Is this just grief?

I'm so sorry about your husband. Grief can last a long time, but feeling there isn't much point to things a year on may mean it has tipped into depression, which is common in later life and very treatable. Please tell your doctor exactly how you've been feeling, and consider a bereavement group, which many hospices and community centers run for free. It's also okay to tell your children plainly that you need more contact, since they may not realize. If the feeling ever turns into thoughts of ending your life, call a crisis line or your doctor right away.
do i really need prenatal vitamins or is a regular multivitamin fine

A prenatal is the better pick because it's built around what pregnancy needs, mainly at least 400 mcg of folic acid and more iron than most regular multis. Some regular multivitamins also have higher vitamin A, which isn't ideal in pregnancy. If you're on a budget, a basic store-brand prenatal works just as well as a fancy one. Ask your provider about adding DHA, which many prenatals don't include.
I've been taking Excedrin like 5 days a week for months bc my headaches keep coming back. whatever works right?

That pattern is a classic setup for medication overuse headache, where frequent painkillers, especially ones with caffeine like Excedrin, keep the headaches coming back. The usual threshold is about 10 or more days a month for combination pills. A doctor can help you taper safely and start a preventive treatment that cuts the number of headaches. It's worth booking that visit soon rather than pushing through on more pills.
can i alternate tylenol and motrin for my 3 year old? doc never told me

You can, but keep it simple to avoid mix-ups. Give each medicine at its own correct weight-based dose and interval: acetaminophen every 4 to 6 hours, ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours. Write down the time of each dose. Many pediatricians prefer to start with one medicine and add the other only if the fever comes back before the next dose is due.
is coffee banned now?? I need my coffee

Not banned. The general guideline is to stay under about 200 mg of caffeine a day, which is roughly one 12-oz cup of regular brewed coffee. Watch the hidden sources too, like tea, soda, chocolate and energy drinks, and coffee shop sizes, which can run way stronger than you'd expect. Going half-caf is an easy way to keep the ritual and the volume.
Quick q: does caffeine help or hurt headaches?

Both, depending on how you use it. A cup of coffee can boost painkillers and ease some headaches, but regular heavy intake leads to withdrawal headaches when you miss your usual dose. Keeping your caffeine moderate and consistent from day to day is the sweet spot.
My dad 78 has had chest tightness on and off today, says it's indigestion. Thoughts?

Treat this as possible heart trouble and call 911 now rather than waiting it out. In older adults, a heart attack often feels like indigestion or vague pressure instead of dramatic pain. Don't drive him yourself if you can avoid it, because paramedics can start treatment on the way. If he isn't allergic and no doctor has told him to avoid aspirin, the dispatcher may tell him to chew one.
should i pop the blister on my burn? its about the size of a grape and annoying

Leave it intact if you can. The blister roof is a sterile barrier that protects the healing skin underneath, and popping it raises infection risk. Cover it with a non-stick dressing to protect it from rubbing. A blister that size on a burn is also worth having a pharmacist or doctor look at, especially if it's on your hand, face, or a joint.
toothache. fastest fix?

Taking ibuprofen at the label dose, if you can safely take it, is usually the quickest relief for tooth pain because it tackles inflammation. You can add acetaminophen at its own label dose if you need more. A cold compress on your cheek and rinsing with warm salt water can take the edge off too. Book a dentist visit, since painkillers only mask whatever is causing it.
worst headache of my life came on like a thunderclap about 20 min ago, should I just sleep it off?

Please don't sleep this one off. A sudden, severe headache that peaks within a minute or so is called a thunderclap headache, and it can signal bleeding in the brain or another emergency. Call 911 or get to an emergency room right now, and don't drive yourself. It may turn out to be nothing serious, but this is exactly the situation where you want to be checked fast.
hives keep coming and going for a week. no idea why. help

Hives that come and go are often triggered by something like a recent virus, a new medication, a food, heat, or pressure on the skin, though sometimes no cause is found. A daily non-drowsy antihistamine like cetirizine or loratadine usually controls them well, and cool showers and loose clothing help with the itch. See a doctor if they last more than six weeks or keep recurring, and get emergency help right away if you notice lip or tongue swelling or trouble breathing.
Do those mental health apps actually work or are they a gimmick

Some genuinely help. Apps based on CBT or mindfulness can reduce mild anxiety and low mood, especially if you use them regularly. They work best as a supplement, not a replacement, for proper care if you're struggling a lot. Choose ones recommended by health services, and if you're not improving after a few weeks, see a professional.
My 77 year old mom has a red, hot, painful spot on her leg that's spreading. She wants to put some antibiotic cream on and wait.

A spreading red, hot, painful area sounds like cellulitis, a skin infection that needs oral antibiotics, not cream. Get her seen today at her doctor or an urgent care. Drawing a pen line around the edge of the redness helps track whether it's spreading. If she gets a fever, chills, confusion, or the redness spreads quickly, go to the ER.
50M, my doc says prediabetic. Is cinnamon or berberine enough to fix it without changing my diet?

No supplement will reverse prediabetes on its own. Berberine has some evidence for lowering blood sugar, but it causes GI side effects and interacts with several medications, so clear it with your doctor first. Cinnamon's effect is small. What reliably works is losing about 5 to 7 percent of your body weight, about 150 minutes of brisk activity a week, and cutting back on sugary drinks and refined carbs, which can cut your risk of diabetes by more than half.
Stepped on a rusty nail in the garage. It went through my shoe into my foot. How worried should I be

Wash it well with soap and running water, and check when your last tetanus shot was, because you need a booster if it's been more than 5 years for a puncture like this. Puncture wounds through shoes can also carry bacteria deep into the foot, so it's worth seeing a doctor today rather than just bandaging it. Over the next few days, watch for spreading redness, warmth, increasing pain, pus or fever, and get seen quickly if any of those show up.
I've had sudden hearing loss in my left ear since this morning, no pain, no cold. Should I wait a week?

Please don't wait, because sudden hearing loss in one ear with no obvious cause is treated as an emergency. Steroid treatment works best when started within the first few days. Get seen today by urgent care, an ER, or an ENT who can do a quick hearing test.
Honestly what's the most Tylenol I can take in a day? My back is killing me and I've been popping them all day.

For a healthy adult the ceiling is 4,000 mg in 24 hours, and many doctors suggest staying at 3,000 mg to leave a safety margin. If you drink regularly or have liver issues, keep it lower still. Add up every source, because cold medicines, sleep aids and some prescription painkillers also contain acetaminophen, and that's how people overdose without realizing it. If you think you've gone over 4,000 mg, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 now even if you feel fine, because liver damage doesn't cause symptoms right away. If your back still needs this much after a few days, get it checked.
My teeth hurt in the morning and my jaw is tired. I think I grind at night?

That pattern fits nighttime grinding (bruxism) pretty well, and stress, alcohol, caffeine, and sleep apnea can all make it worse. A dentist can check for wear or cracks and fit you with a custom night guard, which protects your teeth much better than a cheap boil-and-bite one. If you also snore or wake up unrefreshed, mention it to your doctor, because sleep apnea and grinding often go together.
can i get vaccinated while i have a cold

Yes, a mild cold, even with a low-grade fever, isn't a reason to postpone a vaccine and won't make it work any less well. The usual advice is to wait only if you have a moderate or severe illness, like a high fever or feeling genuinely unwell. If you're unsure, tell the nurse your symptoms and they'll decide on the spot.
bronchitis, coughing 10 days, can my doc just give me antibiotics to speed it up

Acute bronchitis is almost always viral, and antibiotics don't shorten it. They mostly add side effects. The cough commonly lasts 2 to 3 weeks, so day 10 is right on schedule. Honey, fluids, a humidifier and rest help, and many people find dextromethorphan useful at night. Do go back if you get a high fever, shortness of breath, chest pain, are coughing blood, or the cough passes 3 weeks. Those can point to pneumonia or something else.
Can I crush my dad's pills in applesauce? He's having trouble swallowing them

Sometimes, but check with the pharmacist first, because crushing extended-release, enteric-coated or 'XL/ER/SR' pills can release the whole dose at once or ruin the drug. Many medications come as liquids or smaller tablets, and the pharmacist can tell you which ones are safe to crush. New trouble swallowing is also worth raising with his doctor, since it can come from stroke, Parkinson's or other conditions and raises the risk of choking and pneumonia.
Neighbor's dog bit my hand. Not super deep but it broke the skin. It's probably fine right?

Wash it thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes, but then do get it seen today, because hand bites from dogs get infected surprisingly often and you may need antibiotics. A doctor will also check your tetanus status and assess rabies risk, so find out from your neighbor whether the dog's vaccinations are up to date. Don't close the wound tightly yourself, and watch for redness, swelling or pain that keeps getting worse.
I'm on blood pressure meds and feel dizzy every time I stand up. Should I just skip doses on those days?

Don't skip doses on your own, because that can make your pressure swing up and down. Dizziness on standing often means the dose is a bit too strong or you're low on fluids. Call your prescriber this week so they can adjust it. Until then, stand up slowly, stay hydrated and sit down right away if you feel lightheaded. Get help urgently if you faint or hit your head.
hamster bit me lol do i need anything

Hamster bites hurt more than they're worth worrying about. Wash it with soap and water, put on some antibiotic ointment and a bandage, and you're basically done. Rodents like hamsters almost never carry rabies, so no shots are needed, but get it looked at if it turns red, hot, or puffy over the next couple of days.
cracked my front tooth on a fork, no pain really just a chip

A small painless chip isn't an emergency, but it's worth getting it looked at in the next week or two so it can be smoothed or bonded before it chips further. Until then, avoid biting hard things with that tooth. If the edge is sharp, a bit of dental wax over it will protect your lip. Call sooner if you see pink or red in the center of the tooth, or it becomes painful or sensitive to temperature.
Kid got stung by a jellyfish at the beach, lifeguard said pee on it? really?

No, urine doesn't help and can actually make the stingers fire more. Rinse the area with seawater (not fresh water), and remove any tentacles with tweezers or a gloved hand, then soak the skin in water as hot as is comfortably tolerable for about 20 minutes to ease pain. Seek urgent care if your child has trouble breathing, a widespread rash, vomiting, or the sting covers a large area or is near the eyes.
grandma 84 is a bit confused today and warm, temp 100. she's usually sharp

New confusion in an older adult is a warning sign, especially when it comes with a fever, so she should be seen today. In elderly people, infections like UTIs, pneumonia, or sepsis often show up as confusion rather than a high temperature. Take her to urgent care or the ER, or call her doctor right away. Call emergency services if she becomes very drowsy, has trouble breathing, or can't stay awake.
Is it okay to use my mom's Xanax before my job interview tomorrow? Just one.

I'd skip it. Taking someone else's prescription is risky because you don't know how it will affect you, and it can leave you foggy, slow or oddly flat in the interview itself. Try preparing answers out loud tonight, getting decent sleep, and doing slow breathing before you walk in. Remember that some nerves actually help you perform. If anxiety regularly gets in your way, see your doctor about options that are actually prescribed for you.
i have leftover amoxicillin from last year, can i take it for my tooth infection?

Don't use leftovers, because it's probably not a full course, it may be the wrong drug or dose, and partial antibiotic courses help bacteria become resistant. Antibiotics also don't fix the source of a tooth infection, which usually needs drainage, a root canal or an extraction. See a dentist or urgent care so you get the right prescription and the actual cause treated.
Something's stuck in my eye, feels like sand, I've been rubbing it for an hour. What now

Stop rubbing, because that can scratch your cornea or drive the particle in. Rinse with clean water or saline, blinking under it, and try pulling your upper lid out over the lower lid to sweep it out. If it still feels like something's there after rinsing, or your eye is very red, watery or light-sensitive, get it checked today. You may have a scratch or an embedded fragment.
I'm 74 and I take a Benadryl every night to sleep, been doing it for years. My granddaughter says that's bad. Is she right?

She has a point. Diphenhydramine, the ingredient in Benadryl and most PM sleep aids, is strongly anticholinergic. In older adults, nightly use is linked to next-day grogginess, confusion, falls, constipation, urinary retention and possibly a higher long-term risk of dementia. It's worth talking with your doctor about tapering off and trying safer approaches such as sleep habit changes or CBT for insomnia, which works well at any age.
I'm on warfarin. My knee is killing me. Advil ok?

Avoid Advil. Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs like naproxen and aspirin raise the risk of serious bleeding when combined with warfarin, including stomach bleeds. Acetaminophen is the usual safer choice, but stay under about 2000 mg a day and tell your anticoagulation clinic, since regular use can nudge your INR up. A topical gel or an ice pack can also help, and ask your doctor about the knee if it doesn't settle.
Can taking a lot of vitamin C cure a cold faster? I'm thinking like 5g today

Unfortunately, megadosing vitamin C once you're already sick does very little, and 5 grams will mostly give you diarrhea and stomach cramps. People who take it regularly before getting sick may shorten colds slightly, but starting it mid-cold barely helps. Rest, fluids, honey for the cough and time are your best bet right now.
Can I take my wife's sumatriptan? We both get migraines.

I'd skip it. Sumatriptan narrows blood vessels, so it isn't safe for people with certain heart conditions, uncontrolled blood pressure or some types of migraine, and it can interact with antidepressants. Your doctor can check those things quickly and prescribe your own if it suits you, and in the meantime an over-the-counter painkiller taken early is the safer bet.
Constipated for 4 days. Can I take a bunch of laxatives to clear it out fast?

Don't stack laxatives, because overdoing it can cause painful cramping, dehydration and electrolyte problems. Take one product at the labeled dose, such as polyethylene glycol (Miralax), and drink plenty of water. Getting up and walking around and eating fiber-rich foods like prunes also help. If you have severe belly pain, vomiting, a swollen abdomen, or can't pass gas, that could be a blockage, so get seen urgently instead of taking more laxatives.
Can I give my kid my old leftover cefalexin pills crushed up? She has the same rash I had.

Please don't. Adult capsules aren't dosed for a child, and rashes that look alike can have totally different causes, including viral rashes, eczema or allergies that antibiotics won't help. Some rashes even get worse with the wrong treatment. Have her seen. A pediatrician can usually tell quickly what it is. If the rash comes with high fever or spots that don't fade when you press a glass on them, go to the ER right away.
My dad is 82 and on like 11 different medications from different doctors. Is that too many?

It's not automatically too many, but taking that many from several prescribers raises the risk of interactions, duplicates and side effects like dizziness or confusion. Bring every bottle, including supplements and over-the-counter drugs, to his primary doctor or pharmacist and ask for a full medication review. Doctors often find drugs that can be lowered or stopped safely. He shouldn't stop anything on his own, though, since some medications need to be tapered.
Ear thermometer says 37.2, forehead says 38.4. Which do I believe?

Neither is perfect, so recheck with a more reliable method. Forehead readings can be thrown off by sweat or a warm room, and ear readings are often low if the thermometer isn't angled correctly into the canal. For adults and older kids, an oral digital thermometer is a good tiebreaker. For babies under a year, rectal is the gold standard.
Throwing up for 2 days, can't keep water down. I'm 34, otherwise healthy. Just ride it out?

Not when you can't keep water down for two days, because the risk of dehydration is now real even if you're otherwise healthy. Try tiny sips of an electrolyte drink every five to ten minutes. If even that comes back up, or you feel dizzy, are barely peeing, or have severe belly pain, go to urgent care or the ER. They can give you IV fluids and anti-nausea medication, and you'll feel dramatically better fast.
can i use the hot tub at my friend's place, i'll keep it short

Hot tubs are best skipped during pregnancy, especially in the first trimester, because raising your core temperature above about 102°F has been linked to neural tube defects. Even short soaks can heat you up faster than you'd expect. A warm (not hot) bath, or dangling your legs in while keeping your body out, is a much safer way to relax. Pools at normal temperature are totally fine.
Can vitamin C megadoses cure my cold faster? thinking 10 grams a day

Skip the megadose. High amounts of vitamin C barely shorten a cold once you have it. At 10 grams, you're likely to get diarrhea and cramps, and in some people it raises the risk of kidney stones. Normal intake from food or a standard supplement is fine. Rest, fluids, and zinc lozenges started early have about as much evidence as anything.
I had my appendix out laparoscopically 10 days ago. When can I lift weights again?

Walking is great right away, but most surgeons recommend avoiding heavy lifting and straining your core for at least two to four weeks after laparoscopic appendix surgery to let the incisions heal and reduce the risk of a hernia. Your surgeon's specific instructions are the ones to follow, so check your discharge papers or call the office if you're unsure. When you restart, begin with light weights and avoid anything that makes you strain or hold your breath. Stop if you get pain at the incision sites.
is it true you're supposed to take probiotics with antibiotics

There's reasonable evidence that certain probiotics, such as Saccharomyces boulardii or some Lactobacillus strains, can lower the chance of antibiotic-associated diarrhea for some people. Space them a couple of hours away from your antibiotic dose. They're not essential, though, and if you develop severe watery diarrhea, especially with cramping or fever, call your doctor, since that can be C. diff rather than ordinary stomach upset.
dog bite from my neighbor's dog, small puncture, broke skin. wash and done?

Wash it thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes, but don't stop there, because dog bite punctures get infected more often than they look. See a doctor within a day, since many bites need preventive antibiotics, especially on the hands. They'll also check your tetanus status. Ask your neighbor for proof of the dog's rabies vaccination, and go in sooner if redness, swelling, or pus shows up.
can I use my old prescription steroid cream from last year on this new itchy rash? think it's allergic

It might be fine if it's a mild cream and the rash looks like the one it was prescribed for, but steroid creams can make some rashes worse, like fungal infections or scabies. Avoid using it on your face, groin or broken skin without a doctor's guidance, and check that it hasn't expired. If the rash is spreading, blistering, or not improving after a few days, get it looked at so you know what you're actually treating.
There's a red streak going up my arm from a cut on my hand I got two days ago. It's kind of warm. I'll just put Neosporin on it?

A red streak spreading from a wound can mean the infection is moving along your lymphatic vessels (lymphangitis). That needs antibiotics by mouth, not just cream. Get seen today at urgent care or by your doctor. Go to the ER if you have a fever, chills, rapid spreading or feel unwell. This usually clears up fast with the right treatment, but it can get serious if you wait.
My 8yo is complaining his knees hurt at night but he's fine in the day. Growing pains?

That pattern fits growing pains well: aching in both legs in the evening or at night, gone by morning, in a child who runs and plays normally. Gentle massage, a warm bath and a dose of child's paracetamol or ibuprofen if needed usually help. See a doctor if the pain is in only one leg, the joint is swollen, red or warm, he limps, has a fever, or the pain is present during the day too.
My dog bit me after I stepped on his paw. Should I worry about him being aggressive?

A bite after sudden pain is a normal reflex and doesn't necessarily mean he's aggressive. Still, have your vet check his paw, since pain makes dogs more likely to snap. For the bite itself, wash it well and get it checked if it's deep or on your hand. If biting happens again without a clear cause, talk to your vet or a trainer.
I think I have ADHD. Can I just buy Adderall off a guy at work?

Don't do that. Street or unprescribed pills can be counterfeit, and fake Adderall laced with meth or fentanyl has caused real deaths. Stimulants also carry heart risks and need proper dosing. A doctor or psychiatrist can assess you for ADHD properly, and if you have it, you'll get a safe, consistent prescription plus other strategies that help. Many places now offer telehealth ADHD assessments, so it's more accessible than it used to be.
my kid (6) is the pickiest eater alive, lives on pasta and crackers. do I need a multivitamin for him??

A children's multivitamin is a reasonable safety net for a very picky eater and won't hurt at the standard dose. It doesn't replace food, though. Keep offering small portions of new foods alongside ones he likes, without pressure, because exposure over time really does work. Store the vitamins locked away, since iron-containing chewables are a leading cause of poisoning in young kids. If he's dropping on his growth chart, seems tired or pale, or eats fewer than about 20 foods total, mention it to his pediatrician.
my knee clicks when i squat but doesnt hurt. problem?

Painless clicking or popping in the knee is very common and usually just gas bubbles or tendons moving over bone, so on its own it's nothing to worry about. Keep squatting with good form and keep your leg muscles strong, because strong quads and glutes support the joint well. It's worth getting checked if the clicking starts coming with pain, swelling, locking or the knee giving way.
I've had insomnia for 3 months straight. Like 3-4 hours a night. Nothing helps.

Three months of that is chronic insomnia, and it's time to see a doctor rather than keep pushing through. They can check for causes like anxiety, depression, thyroid problems, medications, or sleep apnea. Ask specifically about cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), which works better long-term than sleeping pills and is available through apps and online programs too. In the meantime, be very careful driving on so little sleep.
is it ok to sweat out a cold at the gym

Sweating doesn't flush out a cold, so there's no benefit to forcing it. If your symptoms are only above the neck, like a runny nose or mild sore throat, light exercise such as a walk is usually fine. Skip the gym if you have a fever, body aches, or chest congestion, and remember you'll be spreading germs on shared equipment. Rest now and you'll likely be back to full workouts sooner.
Water broke I think? 36 weeks, clear fluid, no contractions. Can I wait till morning? It's 2am

Call labor and delivery now rather than waiting until morning. Once your water breaks, there's a risk of infection and of the cord slipping down, so they'll want to assess you even without contractions. Note the time, color and smell of the fluid, and wear a pad, not a tampon. If the fluid is green or brown, or you feel something in your vagina, go in immediately.
just a cold, runny nose, no fever. gym ok?

Usually yes, as long as the symptoms are all above the neck, like a runny nose, sneezing or a mild sore throat. Drop the intensity a notch, wipe down equipment, and skip it if you feel worse after the first ten minutes. If the cold moves into your chest or you get a fever or body aches, rest instead.
I stepped on a rusty nail, went through my shoe. Last tetanus shot was... no idea honestly.

Wash the wound well with soap and water, then see a doctor or urgent care today for a tetanus booster. When you don't know your vaccine history, you need one for a puncture like this. Nail punctures through a shoe can also push bacteria deep into the foot, so watch for redness, warmth, swelling or pain that gets worse over the next few days, and get it checked if any of that shows up.
Can I just superglue a cut shut? I really don't want to go to the ER for this.

For a small, clean, shallow cut with edges that line up easily, a thin layer of glue over the closed skin can work, but medical skin glue is the better choice than hardware superglue. Don't use glue on deep, dirty, gaping or bite wounds, or on cuts over joints, because you can trap bacteria inside. If it's deep enough that you're seriously debating it, it's probably worth having a clinic close it properly. An urgent care visit is usually much quicker and cheaper than the ER.
Does stress cause high blood pressure permanently?

Acute stress raises your blood pressure temporarily, and it usually comes back down once the stress passes. Chronic stress can contribute to lasting hypertension, partly through poor sleep, alcohol, eating habits and inactivity. Managing stress helps, but don't assume a high reading is just stress. Confirm it with repeated home readings.
should i pop a burn blister? its annoying

Leave it intact, because the blister roof is natural protection that keeps infection out while new skin forms underneath. Cover it with a soft dressing or a hydrocolloid blister plaster to cushion it. If it pops on its own, wash it gently with soap and water, leave the skin flap in place, and cover it. See a doctor if it's large, painful, or showing signs of infection like spreading redness, pus, or warmth.
Does losing weight really help bp or is that a myth

It really helps. Roughly, every kilogram you lose can drop systolic pressure by about 1 point, and losing 5–10 kg often makes a meaningful difference. Combined with less salt and regular activity, some people reduce or avoid medication. Keep taking any prescribed meds until your doctor adjusts them, though.
I read that you can cure food allergies by eating a tiny bit more each day. Going to try this with my daughter's egg allergy, starting tonight.

Please don't start this at home on your own. What you're describing is oral immunotherapy, and it's real, but it's done under an allergist's supervision because the doses must be precisely measured and reactions, including anaphylaxis, can happen during the process. An allergist can also check whether she's already outgrowing it, which many kids do with egg, often confirmed through a supervised food challenge. Book that appointment. It's a much faster and safer path to the same goal.
Flu test came back positive. Doctor offered Tamiflu but I heard it barely works. Worth it?

It's worth considering, especially if you're within 48 hours of symptoms starting. On average it shortens the illness by about a day, which sounds modest, but it also lowers the risk of complications like pneumonia, which matters more if you're over 65, pregnant, or have conditions like asthma, diabetes or heart disease. The main side effect is nausea, which taking it with food usually helps. If you're young and healthy it's a reasonable judgment call, so talk through your risk factors with your doctor.
my husband refuses to go to the hospital, he's sweaty, gray looking and says his chest hurts but it's 'just stress'

Sweating, a gray color and chest pain together are serious warning signs of a heart attack, so call emergency services yourself right now, even if he objects. Paramedics can check him at home with an ECG, which may be easier for him to accept than a hospital trip. If he's not allergic, have him chew a regular aspirin while you wait, and if he becomes unresponsive and isn't breathing normally, start CPR.
My mother lives alone 3 hours away, she's 81 and sharp but frail. What's one thing I should set up?

Get her a medical alert device with automatic fall detection, ideally one she wears all the time, including in the shower where many falls happen. Many older adults fall and can't reach a phone, and lying on the floor for hours causes serious complications. Pair it with a daily check-in call or text routine. Also make sure a nearby neighbor or friend has a key.
hot oil from a frying pan splattered my face, few small spots near my eye. what do i do

Cool the spots right away with cool running water or a cool wet cloth for 10 to 20 minutes, keeping water out of your eye. If any oil hit your eye itself, or your eye is painful, red, watering or your vision is blurry, get to urgent care or an eye clinic immediately. Small spots on the skin usually heal well, but facial burns near the eye are worth a quick professional check if they blister.
I'm 68 and since my wife passed last year I just don't see the point in much anymore. Kids say I should see someone but I'm not one for talking.

I'm sorry about your wife, because losing a partner is one of the hardest things there is. Feeling that nothing has much point a year on can be grief that's turned into depression, which is common at your age and very treatable. Seeing your GP is a good start, and it doesn't have to mean lots of talking, since treatment can be practical and straightforward. If 'no point' ever turns into thoughts of ending your life, please tell someone or call a crisis line straight away.
Stray cat scratched me while I was trying to feed it. Should I worry about rabies from a scratch?

It's worth a call to your doctor or local health department, because a stray's vaccination status is unknown and scratches can occasionally transmit rabies if saliva was on the claws. Wash the scratch thoroughly with soap and water right away. They'll advise you based on how common rabies is in your area and whether the cat can be found and observed. Don't try to handle it again, but noting where it lives helps them decide.
What's the best mattress for back pain? Firm right?

Not necessarily. Studies actually favor medium-firm mattresses over very firm ones for people with chronic low back pain. The best mattress is one that keeps your spine fairly neutral in your usual sleeping position. Side sleepers usually need a bit more softness at the shoulders and hips, and back sleepers do well with medium-firm. If you can, test it for a few weeks with a good return policy, since comfort is highly individual.
My husband got stung and passed out briefly but he's awake now and says he's fine and won't go to the hospital

Fainting after a sting is a sign of anaphylaxis, and he needs emergency care now even though he feels better. Symptoms can come back hours later in a second wave. Call emergency services, and use an epinephrine auto-injector if one is available. Afterward, he should see an allergist about carrying epinephrine and about venom immunotherapy, which dramatically lowers the risk of future reactions.
Is it fine to do yoga while I have a mild cold?

Gentle yoga is usually fine with a mild cold and can even help you feel a bit better. Skip hot yoga and intense power flows for now, because the heat and exertion can dehydrate you. If you're stuffy, you may want to avoid long inversions. Please stay home rather than going to a class so you don't pass it on.
Pregnant, 28 weeks, anxiety through the roof. Can I keep taking my lexapro or should I just quit cold turkey to be safe for the baby?

Don't stop it suddenly. Quitting cold turkey can cause withdrawal and a relapse of anxiety, and untreated anxiety in pregnancy carries real risks for you and the baby too. Lexapro is one of the more commonly used options in pregnancy, and the decision should be made with your OB or prescriber, ideally this week. Tell them your anxiety has gotten worse, because that's important information on its own.
My 79 year old mom can't sleep. Is it ok to give her Benadryl every night?

I'd steer away from that. Diphenhydramine is on the list of drugs older adults should generally avoid, because it can cause confusion, memory problems, constipation and urinary retention, and it raises the risk of falls. Start with sleep habits: a consistent schedule, less daytime napping, and no caffeine after lunch. Also have her doctor look for causes like pain, needing to urinate at night, or a medication side effect. A low dose of melatonin is a gentler option to discuss with them.
I've been taking Benadryl every night for about 8 months to sleep. Works great. Any reason to stop?

Yes, there are good reasons to taper off. Your body builds tolerance to diphenhydramine fairly quickly, and regular long-term use of anticholinergic drugs like it has been linked to memory problems and a higher risk of dementia, especially as people get older. It can also cause next-day grogginess, constipation, and urinary issues. Talk with your doctor about why you're having trouble sleeping and how to wean off, since stopping abruptly can cause a few nights of rebound insomnia. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia is the most effective long-term fix and is worth asking about.
quick q is ibuprofen ok for my 82 yr old dad's knee pain

Often it's not the best first choice at his age. Ibuprofen raises the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney damage and high blood pressure, especially if he takes a blood thinner, a diuretic or blood pressure medication. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) is usually the safer starting point, as long as he stays within the daily limit and doesn't drink heavily. A topical diclofenac gel on the knee also works well with far less risk. Check with his pharmacist about his specific meds before he starts anything regular.
toddler had a seizure with her fever, it stopped after about a minute and she's sleepy now. do i still need to go in??

Yes, get her seen today. A first seizure with fever needs a doctor's evaluation even though most febrile seizures turn out to be harmless. Call emergency services right away if she has another seizure, has trouble breathing, has a stiff neck, or doesn't gradually become more alert. Sleepiness for a while afterward is common, but she should keep improving.
is it safe to get vaccinated while breastfeeding?

Yes. Almost all vaccines, including flu, COVID, Tdap and MMR, are safe while breastfeeding, and some of your antibodies even pass to your baby through the milk. You don't need to pump and dump or pause nursing. The rare exceptions are a couple of travel vaccines like yellow fever, which a travel clinic will weigh with you.
my dad (72) has been taking his wife's blood pressure pills because he ran out of his. they're a different brand but same thing right?

Not necessarily, and it's risky. Blood pressure drugs vary a lot in type and dose, and the wrong one can drop his pressure too low or interact with his other meds, which matters even more at 72. Have him call his pharmacy today, since they can often give an emergency supply or contact his doctor for a refill. In the meantime, he should stop taking hers.
My dermatologist wants a biopsy of a spot on my nose. Is that overkill? I don't love the idea of a needle on my face.

It's not overkill, because a biopsy is the only way to know for sure what a spot is, and the nose is a common place for basal cell skin cancer. The procedure is quick, the numbing injection is the worst part, and the small mark usually heals very well on the face. Getting an answer now means any treatment needed can be smaller and simpler. If you're nervous, tell your dermatologist, as they can walk you through it and use the gentlest technique.
can i use my hot tub? its only 102

Hot tubs are best avoided in pregnancy, especially in the first trimester. At 102°F your core temperature can rise enough within about 10 minutes to raise the risk of neural tube defects. A warm, not hot, bath is a safer way to relax. If you do get in a hot tub, keep it brief, sit with your chest out of the water, and get out if you feel too warm.
My tooth got knocked out playing hockey!! what do i do right now

Pick it up by the crown, not the root, and if it's dirty rinse it briefly with milk or water without scrubbing. Gently push it back into the socket and bite on a cloth to hold it, or if you can't, keep it in milk or tucked inside your cheek. Get to a dentist or ER within 30 to 60 minutes, because a tooth replanted quickly has the best chance of surviving.
My son got a tooth knocked clean out at soccer, it's an adult tooth. What do I do with it

Move fast, because getting the tooth back in within an hour gives it the best chance of surviving. Pick it up by the crown, not the root, and if it's dirty rinse it briefly with milk. If your son is old enough to cooperate, gently push it back into the socket and have him bite on gauze. If you can't do that, store it in cold milk or his own saliva, not water, and get to a dentist or ER immediately.
do i actually need electrolyte drinks after a 30 min jog

Nope, for a 30-minute jog water is plenty, and your next meal will replace the small amount of sodium you lost. Electrolyte drinks start to make sense for sessions longer than an hour, in serious heat, or if you're a very salty sweater. Otherwise they mostly add sugar.
can i dye my hair while pregnant

Most experts consider hair dye low-risk, because very little gets absorbed through the scalp, though many people wait until after the first trimester to be extra cautious. Do it in a well-ventilated room, and options like highlights that don't touch the scalp cut exposure even further. If you're a stylist doing it daily, gloves and good airflow matter more.
my 2 yr old swallowed maybe 5 of my iron pills. she seems totally fine. do i need to worry

Yes, act now. Call Poison Control right away (1-800-222-1222 in the US) or go to the ER. Iron poisoning in toddlers can look fine at first and then turn serious hours later, and five adult iron pills could be a dangerous dose for a child her size. Bring the bottle with you so they know the exact strength.
teenager here (16), my bp was 140/90 at sports physical. should i be worried

It's worth following up, but don't panic, because nerves, caffeine or a cuff that's too small can push up a reading. That number is high for a 16-year-old, though, so ask to have it rechecked over a few visits. Tell a parent and your doctor so they can look into it properly. Teens can have high blood pressure for specific reasons, and catching it now is a good thing.
Breastfeeding and wondering if I can keep taking my ashwagandha

I'd pause the ashwagandha while breastfeeding. There's very little safety data on it for nursing mothers, and it can affect thyroid and hormone levels. If you've been using it for stress or sleep, talk to your doctor or a lactation consultant about options with a better track record during breastfeeding.
my glaucoma drops are expensive, can i skip some days if my eyes feel fine

Please don't skip them. Glaucoma causes no symptoms while it slowly and permanently damages your vision, so feeling fine says nothing about your eye pressure. Ask your eye doctor or pharmacist about generic versions, a different drug, or manufacturer coupons, since there are often cheaper options that work just as well.
Found a site selling insulin for half the price without a prescription, from Canada I think. Legit?

Be really careful there, because a lot of sites claiming to be Canadian pharmacies sell counterfeit, expired, or improperly stored insulin, and bad insulin can put you in DKA. A legitimate pharmacy will always ask for a prescription. You can check whether a site is real through verification programs like NABP's safe.pharmacy. Before you buy, look into the manufacturer's patient assistance programs and the $35 monthly cap programs from Lilly, Novo, and Sanofi, and check whether your state has an insulin price cap. Those can often beat that site's price safely.
how long should a 3 year old be sleeping

Most 3-year-olds need about 10 to 13 hours of sleep in a 24-hour period, and that can include a nap. Many still nap for an hour or so, though some drop it around this age and need an earlier bedtime instead. A consistent wind-down routine and a dark, cool room help a lot. If he snores loudly most nights or seems to pause his breathing during sleep, mention it to his pediatrician.
my 9 month old has 102 fever but is playing and eating fine. ER?

If she's playful, eating, and peeing normally, you probably don't need the ER. Babies over 6 months can usually be managed at home with a weight-based dose of infant acetaminophen or ibuprofen and plenty of fluids. Call your pediatrician if the fever lasts more than 24 to 48 hours at this age. Go in sooner if she becomes hard to wake, refuses to drink, has fewer wet diapers, struggles to breathe, or develops a rash that doesn't fade when you press on it.
can i take ibuprofen and tylenol together for a bad toothache

Yes, that combination is safe for most healthy adults and actually works better for dental pain than either drug alone because they act differently. A common approach is 400 mg ibuprofen plus 500 to 1000 mg acetaminophen, either together or staggered, keeping acetaminophen under 3000 to 4000 mg a day and ibuprofen under 1200 mg a day without a doctor's guidance. Skip the ibuprofen if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers or take blood thinners. A toothache bad enough to need both usually means you should get to a dentist within a day or two.
I'm a runner, 28F, always tired. Friend said take iron. Just buy some?

Get a blood test first, including ferritin, iron and a full blood count. Female runners often do have low iron, but tiredness has lots of other causes, and taking iron you don't need can build up and cause harm. If you are low, your doctor can recommend the right dose. Taking it every other day with vitamin C is often absorbed better and is easier on your stomach.
can meditation replace my antidepressants? i've been meditating for a month and feel great

Feeling great is wonderful, and meditation is a genuinely good tool to keep. But feeling better is often a sign the medication is working, not that you no longer need it. Stopping on your own raises the risk of relapse and discontinuation symptoms. If you want to come off, ask your prescriber about a gradual taper, ideally during a stable, low-stress period, and keep up the meditation alongside it.
Wife accidentally took my metoprolol instead of her vitamin. She's fine so far. Do we need to do anything?

Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 in the US, or your local poison line. They'll tell you whether she can stay home based on the dose and her health, and the call is free. A single dose in a healthy adult often just causes tiredness or a lowered pulse and blood pressure, but she should avoid driving and get up slowly for the rest of the day. If she gets very dizzy, faints, has a pulse under about 50, or feels short of breath, call emergency services.
My chest has felt tight since I got over covid 2 weeks ago, and my heart pounds when I climb stairs. 38F.

That's worth checking with your doctor soon rather than waiting it out. COVID can occasionally cause inflammation of the heart muscle or its lining (myocarditis or pericarditis), and chest tightness with a pounding heart on exertion fits that possibility. Ask about an ECG and blood tests, and go easy on exercise until you've been assessed. Seek urgent care if you get chest pain at rest, fainting or worsening breathlessness.
My cat's litter box — do I really have to stop cleaning it?

Ideally, yes; hand it off to someone else if you can, because cat feces can carry toxoplasmosis, which can harm a developing baby. If you have to do it yourself, scoop daily, since the parasite takes over a day to become infectious. Wear gloves and wash your hands well afterward. Keeping your cat indoors also lowers the risk.
my 2 month old has a temp of 38.2 rectal, she seems kind of fine though. can I just give tylenol and wait till morning?

No, any fever of 38.0°C (100.4°F) or higher in a baby under 3 months needs to be seen by a doctor right away, even if she seems fine. Young infants can have serious infections that don't show obvious symptoms yet. Call your pediatrician's after-hours line now or go to the ER. Don't give acetaminophen before she's checked unless a doctor tells you to, because it can mask the fever they need to assess.
My 4 year old has a fever and I only have adult Tylenol. Can I just cut a pill in half?

Please don't. Children's acetaminophen is dosed by weight, and half an adult tablet can easily be too much for a 4-year-old. Acetaminophen overdose is dangerous for the liver. Children's liquid acetaminophen is the safe option, and many pharmacies are open late; the pharmacist can give you the exact dose for your child's weight. Call your pediatrician or an after-hours line right away if your child is very drowsy, struggling to breathe, refusing fluids, or has a fever above 104°F (40°C).

Detailed question: my father (86) has CHF, takes furosemide, and his ankles have gotten more swollen over the past 4 days. He also says he has to sleep propped up on 3 pillows now instead of 1. Anything I can do at home?

Those two changes together suggest his heart failure is worsening and fluid is building up. Call his cardiologist or doctor today rather than managing it at home. Needing more pillows to breathe at night is a classic sign of fluid in the lungs. Check whether he's gained more than two to three pounds in a day or five in a week, because they'll want to know. If he becomes breathless at rest, can't lie down at all, or has chest pain, call emergency services.
quick q - can i drink alcohol with allergy meds

It depends on the medication. With drowsy antihistamines like diphenhydramine or chlorpheniramine, alcohol strongly multiplies the sedation and can impair you badly, so skip drinking. Non-drowsy ones like fexofenadine or loratadine are lower risk, but cetirizine can still make some people sleepy with alcohol. Either way, never drink and drive on any antihistamine.
I'm diabetic and just got over a nasty virus. Anything special about restarting my workouts?

Illness often throws blood sugar off for a while, so check your glucose before and after your first few workouts. Start with shorter, gentler sessions than usual. If you take insulin or medication that can cause lows, keep a fast-acting carb with you. Make sure you're well hydrated. If you're seeing ketones or readings that are still running unusually high, get those sorted out with your care team before exercising.
is yogurt or probiotics actually useful when on antibiotics or is that a myth

There's reasonable evidence that certain probiotics, such as Saccharomyces boulardii and some Lactobacillus strains, modestly reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Ordinary yogurt is fine to eat but has less reliable doses. Take a probiotic a couple of hours apart from your antibiotic dose. If you develop severe, watery diarrhea several times a day, especially with cramps or fever, call your doctor, because that can be C. diff, which needs specific treatment.
does local honey cure pollen allergies? my mom swears by it

Unfortunately, the studies haven't shown that local honey meaningfully improves pollen allergies. The pollen causing most hay fever comes from wind-pollinated plants, not the flowers bees visit. It's harmless for adults if she enjoys it, but never give honey to babies under 1 because of botulism risk. If she wants actual desensitization, allergy shots or under-the-tongue tablets do work and are worth asking an allergist about.
my 6yo has 101 but is running around playing. medicine or no?

If they're happily playing, you don't need to give medicine. Fever is the body's way of fighting the infection, and we treat it mainly to help with discomfort. Keep offering fluids and watch how they act. Give a weight-based dose of acetaminophen or ibuprofen if they become miserable or have trouble sleeping.
how long should a kid stay home with pink eye

Many schools and daycares let kids return once they've started treatment, or once the discharge has cleared, but policies vary, so check with yours. Gunky yellow or green discharge suggests a bacterial infection, which a doctor may treat with antibiotic drops. See a doctor promptly if there's eye pain, sensitivity to light, blurry vision or swelling around the eye, or if the child is a newborn.
can I use my nasal decongestant spray for like 2 weeks straight, it's the only thing that works

Not a good idea. Sprays like oxymetazoline should only be used for about three days, because longer use causes rebound congestion that makes you more dependent on the spray. A steroid nasal spray like fluticasone or saline rinses are safer for longer stretches. If you're already stuck in the rebound cycle, a doctor or pharmacist can help you taper off.
Had a racing heart, like 180 bpm, came on out of nowhere and stopped suddenly after 10 min. I'm 22. Feel fine now. Do I need to do anything?

A sudden start and stop at that speed sounds a lot like SVT, a common rhythm problem in young people that's usually not dangerous but is very treatable. See your doctor and ask for an ECG and possibly a heart monitor so it can be caught and diagnosed. If it happens again, try bearing down hard as if straining on the toilet, which can sometimes reset it. Go to the ER if an episode lasts more than about 15 to 20 minutes, or if you get chest pain, fainting or bad breathlessness.
I keep waking up unable to move and sometimes feel like someone is in the room. Am I going crazy??

You're not going crazy; that's sleep paralysis, a common and harmless glitch where your brain wakes up before the muscle-relaxing part of dream sleep switches off. The sense of a presence in the room is a well-known part of it and comes from dream imagery spilling into wakefulness. It's often triggered by sleep deprivation, stress, irregular schedules, or sleeping on your back, so improving those usually reduces episodes. If it happens frequently or comes with sudden daytime sleep attacks or muscle weakness when you laugh, see a doctor to rule out narcolepsy.
my cat bit my hand pretty deep, two little puncture holes, it's not bleeding much. do i really need to do anything?

Yes, take this one seriously, because cat bites to the hand become infected more often than almost any other common bite. Their teeth inject bacteria like Pasteurella deep into tissue, and small holes seal over quickly and trap it. Wash it under running water with soap for several minutes, then see a doctor today, since antibiotics are usually recommended for deep cat bites on the hand. Go in urgently if you notice spreading redness, swelling or throbbing pain within the next day.
Found a tick on me in Connecticut, was probably on a day. Do I need antibiotics?

Possibly. In a high-Lyme area like Connecticut, a single dose of doxycycline within 72 hours of removal can lower your Lyme risk. Doctors generally offer it if the tick was a deer tick attached for 36 hours or more, which roughly a day may or may not reach. Call your doctor or a telehealth service today to decide. Watch the bite for a month, and get seen if you develop an expanding red rash, fever, aches or fatigue.
Got a papercut-thin but deep slice on my palm from broken glass. Might there be glass still in it?

It's possible, and glass slivers often don't show up on a quick look. Signs of retained glass include a sharp pain when you press on one spot, or a feeling that something is in there. Rinse it well under running water and look carefully with good light. Don't dig around with tweezers. If you still suspect glass, or the cut is deep on the palm, get it seen, because clinics can find and remove fragments that would otherwise cause infection.
I'm pregnant and can't sleep. Can I take unisom?

Doxylamine, the active ingredient in Unisom SleepTabs, is generally considered safe in pregnancy and is even used for morning sickness, but check with your OB or midwife before taking it. Some Unisom products contain different ingredients, so the specific product matters. Sleeping on your side with a pillow between your knees and one under your belly helps a lot, and cutting fluids a couple of hours before bed reduces bathroom trips. If you're snoring loudly or your insomnia comes with anxiety or low mood, raise that with your provider too.
I've been sick for like 3 weeks with a lingering cough after a cold. no fever. can i run or is that bad?

With no fever and feeling okay otherwise, easy running is usually fine even with a lingering cough, though you might cough more at first. Keep the pace easy and stop if you get wheezy, chest tight or very short of breath. A cough lasting three weeks or more is worth getting checked by a doctor to rule out things like post-viral asthma or a chest infection.
keto diet ok on sglt2 inhibitor? on jardiance

Be careful with that combination, because empagliflozin plus very low carb eating raises your risk of ketoacidosis, sometimes with normal-looking sugars. Talk to your doctor before starting keto, since they may suggest a moderate low-carb approach or a change in your medication. If you ever feel nauseated, get stomach pain or feel unusually tired, check your ketones and seek care urgently.
My dad (72) says one eye suddenly went dark for a few minutes then came back. He's fine now and doesn't want to bother anyone.

He needs to get checked today, ideally in an ER, even though his vision is back. Temporary vision loss in one eye, sometimes called amaurosis fugax, is often a warning sign of a clot and can come before a stroke. Getting evaluated quickly can prevent a much bigger event. If he has any weakness, facial droop, or trouble speaking, call emergency services right away.
Does doxycycline really make you burn in the sun? Going on a beach holiday

Yes, doxycycline commonly causes photosensitivity, and the sunburn can be surprisingly severe even with short exposure. Use a high-SPF broad-spectrum sunscreen and reapply often, wear a hat and cover up, and avoid midday sun as much as you can. Also take it with a full glass of water and stay upright for 30 minutes afterwards to avoid painful throat irritation.
Pregnant, 8 weeks. Is my regular multivitamin enough or do I need a prenatal?

Switch to a prenatal if you can. It's designed to provide at least 400 mcg of folic acid, which matters most in these early weeks, plus appropriate iron and iodine. Some regular multivitamins contain preformed vitamin A at levels that aren't ideal in pregnancy. Bring the bottle to your first prenatal appointment so your provider can confirm it covers what you need.
Diabetic here on metformin for 6 years, my feet tingle sometimes. Could that be a vitamin thing?

It could be. Long-term metformin is known to lower B12, and B12 deficiency causes tingling and numbness that looks a lot like diabetic neuropathy. Ask your doctor to check your B12 level, since that's easily fixed if it's low. Either way, tingling feet in diabetes deserve attention, so get a foot exam too and keep an eye on your blood sugar control.
constipated for 4 days, can i just take a bunch of laxatives to get it over with

Taking extra laxatives tends to backfire with violent cramping, diarrhea and dehydration, so stick to the label dose of one product. A gentle option like polyethylene glycol (MiraLAX) usually works within a day or two, and drinking plenty of water and walking around help it along. If you also have severe belly pain, vomiting, a swollen belly, or you can't pass gas, get seen urgently because those can signal a blockage.
is it ok to put an aspirin directly on my sore gum? my grandma swears by it

Please don't do that, because aspirin held against the gum causes a chemical burn and can leave a painful white ulcer on top of your toothache. Aspirin only works when it's swallowed and absorbed into your bloodstream. If you want something topical, a clove oil or benzocaine gel used sparingly is a safer option, and you should still have a dentist look at the tooth.
Can I superglue a cut shut instead of going to the ER? It's like an inch long on my shin, kinda gaping.

Hardware-store superglue isn't made for skin and can irritate it or seal bacteria inside, so it's not a good substitute. A gaping inch-long cut generally needs proper closure, and the window for that is roughly within 6 to 8 hours of the injury.
