Urgent care can handle this quickly and much more cheaply than the ER, often with medical-grade skin glue or a few stitches. Until you get there, clean it gently with running water and keep firm pressure on it with a clean dressing.
My dog bit a stranger at the park. The guy wants to make a big deal of it. My dog is vaccinated, can't I just give him my number and leave?

Give him your number and also your dog's rabies vaccination details, because he'll need them for his own medical care. In many places a dog bite must be reported to animal control or the health department, and your dog may need a 10-day observation period, often done at home. Cooperating and getting the vaccine records from your vet now protects both him and you. Encourage him to wash the wound and get it looked at if the skin was broken.
there's a stye on my eyelid, can I pop it like a pimple

Don't squeeze it. Popping a stye can spread the infection into the eyelid tissue. Instead, hold a warm compress on it for 10 to 15 minutes, three or four times a day, which usually brings it to a head and drains it on its own within a week. See a doctor if your eyelid gets very swollen or red, your vision changes, or it isn't improving after a week or two.
Lost about 15 pounds in 2 months without trying and my stomach feels full fast. I'm 63. Probably just aging?

No, unintentional weight loss like that, plus feeling full quickly, is not normal aging and should be checked soon. Make a doctor's appointment within the next week or so and describe exactly what you've told me. They'll likely do blood tests and may refer you for a scope. There are many possible causes, some easily treatable, but it's important not to wait.
can vaccines cause autism? my sister keeps sending me stuff

No. That claim came from a single 1998 study that was found to be fraudulent and was retracted, and its author lost his medical license. Since then, large studies covering millions of children across several countries have found no link between vaccines and autism. If it helps with your sister, your pediatrician can walk through the evidence with you both.
Pain under an old crown, comes and goes, worse when I bite. It's been about a month. Should I worry?

A month of on-and-off pain when biting under a crown deserves a dental visit soon. It can mean decay at the crown edge, a cracked tooth underneath or a nerve that's inflamed or dying. Your dentist can check with an X-ray and bite tests, and catching it early often saves the tooth.
Cut my hand on a rusty fence yesterday. Its red around the cut now. Big deal?

It could be, so check two things. First, have you had a tetanus shot in the last 5 years? If not, or if you're unsure, get a booster within the next day or two. Some redness right at the edge is normal healing. Redness that spreads, warmth, increasing pain, pus or red streaks running up your arm mean infection, and you should see a doctor today. Wash it with soap and water and keep it covered, and draw a pen line around the red area so you can tell if it's growing.
ok so my dad (70) has belly pain, hasn't pooped or farted in 2 days and now he's throwing up. he says hes fine

He needs to be seen today, ideally at an emergency department. No stool or gas, belly pain and vomiting together are classic signs of a bowel obstruction, and that can become dangerous quickly, especially at 70. Don't give him laxatives, and keep him from eating until a doctor has checked him.
my lower back has been killing me since i moved furniture saturday. bed rest till it passes?

Skip the bed rest, because staying in bed for days usually makes a strained back stiffer and slower to heal. Keep moving gently with short walks and normal light activity, and use heat or an over-the-counter anti-inflammatory like ibuprofen if it's safe for you. Most muscle strains like this improve a lot within one to two weeks. See a doctor if it's getting worse instead of better, or if pain shoots down a leg with numbness or weakness.
My son is 14 and super moody, sleeping all the time, dropped out of soccer, barely eating. Teen stuff?

Some moodiness is normal for teens, but losing interest in things he loved, along with big changes in his sleep and appetite, is a pattern that can point to depression. That's worth taking seriously. Talk with him calmly and without judgment, and book a visit with his doctor, who can screen for depression and refer him for counseling. If he ever mentions hurting himself or seems hopeless, get help right away by calling or texting 988 in the US or your local crisis line.
Had a stent put in 3 weeks ago. Can I stop the blood thinners early? They make me bruise like crazy.

Please don't stop them on your own. After a stent, those antiplatelet drugs stop a clot forming inside it, and stopping early can cause a sudden, serious heart attack. Bruising is an expected and annoying side effect. Call your cardiologist and tell them about it, since sometimes the regimen can be adjusted. Get urgent care if you have black stools, blood in your urine, vomiting blood or bleeding that won't stop.
Honestly just tell me the fastest way to get rid of a cold. I have a presentation Thursday.

There's no way to kill a cold quickly, but you can make yourself feel a lot better by Thursday. Sleep as much as you can, keep up your fluids, and use a saline rinse or decongestant spray for congestion, limiting the spray to three days to avoid rebound stuffiness. Zinc lozenges started within the first day may shorten things slightly, and ibuprofen or acetaminophen will handle aches and a sore throat. On the day, warm tea with honey helps your voice, and skip anything sedating like nighttime cold meds that morning.
Does Sudafed mess with blood pressure meds? I have hypertension and a stuffy nose.

It can. Pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine narrow blood vessels, which can push your blood pressure up and work against your medication. Saline rinses, a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, or steam are safer for congestion. Look for cold products labeled for high blood pressure, which leave out decongestants, and ask the pharmacist before you buy.
My husband has flu, I have type 1 diabetes. Anything I should do?

Call your doctor today. People with diabetes are at higher risk from flu, so they may prescribe an antiviral to help prevent it. If you're not already vaccinated, it's still worth getting the shot. Keep your distance from your husband, wash your hands often, and have him wear a mask around you. If you do get sick, follow your sick-day plan: check your glucose and ketones more often, keep taking insulin, and seek care quickly if ketones climb or you can't keep fluids down.
Can I stop my blood pressure meds now that my readings are normal? Been 3 months.

Don't stop on your own. Your readings are probably normal because the medication is working, and stopping suddenly, especially with beta blockers or clonidine, can cause a dangerous rebound spike. If you've lost weight, changed your diet or started exercising, your doctor may be able to reduce or taper the dose safely. Book a review and bring your home readings.
forehead thermometer says 99.1, am I sick?

That's within the normal range, so it doesn't count as a fever. Body temperature naturally varies from about 97 to 99.5°F over the day, and forehead readings aren't very precise. A fever usually starts at 100.4°F (38°C). If you feel unwell, recheck with an oral thermometer and pay attention to your other symptoms.
glued my fingers together with superglue lol help

Don't yank them apart, because you can tear the skin. Soak your fingers in warm soapy water for a few minutes, then gently roll or peel them apart, and acetone nail polish remover will dissolve the glue if that doesn't work, used on intact skin and away from the eyes. If glue gets in your eye or mouth, rinse with water and get medical advice rather than trying to pry anything open.
hives all over within 10 min of getting a vaccine at the pharmacy, throat feels kinda tight

Tell the pharmacist right now or call 911, because hives plus a tight throat right after a vaccine could be anaphylaxis, and that needs epinephrine immediately. Pharmacies that vaccinate keep epinephrine on hand for exactly this. Don't drive yourself anywhere or wait to see if it passes, since these reactions can worsen fast.
I accidentally gave my 2yo a double dose of his amoxicillin. Panicking.

Take a breath, because a one-time double dose of amoxicillin usually isn't dangerous. The most likely effects are an upset stomach or diarrhea. Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 in the US. It's free and fast, and they can confirm based on his weight and the exact amount. Skip the next dose only if they tell you to, otherwise go back to the normal schedule.
is it normal for old people to be tired all the time? my dad's 83 and naps constantly

Some extra napping is common with age, but constant tiredness is worth bringing up with his doctor rather than chalking up to getting old. Common treatable causes include anemia, an underactive thyroid, depression, sleep apnea, heart problems and medication side effects. A basic checkup and blood tests can sort out most of these. If the fatigue started suddenly or comes with breathlessness or weight loss, get him seen soon.
ear pain on the plane landing still there next day, muffled hearing

That's likely airplane ear, where pressure doesn't equalize, and it usually settles within a day or two. Yawning, swallowing, chewing gum, or gently blowing with your nose pinched and mouth closed can help, and a decongestant may help if you're congested. See a doctor if it lasts more than a few days or you get severe pain, fluid draining, or dizziness, since the eardrum can be injured.
is it ok to take ibuprofen for stomach cramps

Ibuprofen works well for period cramps, but it's a poor choice for cramps coming from the stomach itself because it can irritate the stomach lining and make gastritis or ulcers worse. For general tummy cramps, acetaminophen is gentler, and so is a heating pad with a little patience. If you do take ibuprofen, take it with food and don't use it daily for stomach pain without talking to a doctor.
My toddler just grabbed my hot coffee and spilled it on his chest. He's screaming. What do I do RIGHT NOW

Remove any wet clothing that isn't stuck to his skin, and run cool (not cold) water over the burn for 20 minutes while keeping the rest of him warm. Then cover it loosely with clean cling film or a clean cloth. A scald on a toddler's chest needs to be seen by a doctor today, so head to urgent care or the ER, and call 911 if it's large, blistering widely, or he seems unwell.
Feeling really overwhelmed by exams. Is pulling an all-nighter with energy drinks a good idea?

Skip the all-nighter. Sleep is when your brain consolidates what you studied, so cramming all night usually means worse recall on the day, and high-dose energy drinks can cause heart palpitations, jitters and more anxiety. You'll do better studying in focused 25 to 50 minute blocks, testing yourself instead of re-reading, and getting at least six or seven hours of sleep. If the overwhelm feels constant, your school's counseling service is free and used to exam stress.
Dad's 86 and his doctor put him on like 11 meds. That seems insane. Can I just cut out the ones that seem unimportant?

Please don't pick and choose yourself. Some drugs that seem minor, like certain blood pressure or seizure medications, can cause rebound problems if stopped suddenly. Your instinct is reasonable, though, since taking many medications raises the risk of falls and interactions in older adults. Bring every bottle, including supplements, to his doctor or a pharmacist and ask for a full medication review aimed at deprescribing what he doesn't need.
I've had a headache and double vision since this afternoon, came out of nowhere. 52, high blood pressure.

Sudden double vision with a headache, especially with high blood pressure, needs emergency evaluation tonight. It can be a stroke, a bleed, or a nerve problem that needs fast treatment. Call emergency services if you also have weakness, numbness, slurred speech or a drooping face. Don't drive yourself.
my mother is 79 and has started accusing people of stealing her stuff. is this just old age

Paranoia about theft is not normal aging. It is a fairly common early sign of dementia, where someone misplaces things and fills the gap with a theory that someone took them. It can also come from something treatable, like a urinary infection, a medication side effect, low vitamin B12 or thyroid problems, so book a doctor's visit and describe exactly what you've noticed. In the meantime, arguing rarely helps, so calmly helping her look for the missing item usually goes better.
How long after taking an antacid should I wait to take my thyroid pill?

Keep at least 4 hours between levothyroxine and antacids containing calcium, magnesium or aluminum, because they bind the hormone and reduce how much you absorb. Ideally take levothyroxine on an empty stomach with water, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast or coffee. Then save antacids, iron and calcium supplements for later in the day. Consistent timing keeps your levels steady between blood tests.
Got stung by a bee and my whole arm is swollen from wrist to elbow, no breathing issues. ER?

Large swelling around the sting site without breathing trouble is usually a big local reaction, not anaphylaxis, and is often managed at home with ice, elevation, an oral antihistamine, and ibuprofen if you can take it. Go to the ER right away, though, if you develop hives elsewhere on your body, throat or tongue swelling, wheezing, dizziness, or vomiting. Since the swelling is this large, check in with your doctor in the next day or two, and get it looked at sooner if it keeps spreading, becomes red and hot, or you get a fever.
Can I just drive myself to the ER if I think I'm having a heart attack? Ambulance is expensive.

Please don't drive yourself, because if your heart goes into a dangerous rhythm or you pass out behind the wheel, you could die or hurt someone else. Paramedics can start treatment on the way, run an ECG, and alert the hospital so the cath lab is ready, which shortens the time to get the artery open. If cost is the worry, most hospitals have financial assistance programs and bills can often be negotiated afterward, but none of that matters if you don't survive the drive. Call 911.
should I bundle up my feverish kid so he sweats it out

No. Bundling traps heat and can push his temperature higher. Dress him in light clothing with a single thin blanket, and keep the room comfortably cool. If he's shivering, a light extra layer until it passes is fine. Keep the fluids coming and use a fever reducer if he's uncomfortable.
can i go to the gym with a cold? sweating it out right?

You can't actually sweat out a virus, but light exercise is okay if your symptoms are only above the neck, like a runny nose or mild sore throat. Keep it easy, think a walk or light workout rather than heavy lifting or intervals. Skip it entirely if you have a fever, body aches or chest congestion, since hard exercise then can make you sicker and in rare cases strain the heart. Also wipe down equipment, because gyms are prime spots for spreading colds.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and craving liver pate like crazy. Fine to eat a bunch?

It's best to skip liver and pate during pregnancy. Liver is extremely high in preformed vitamin A, and too much of it is linked to birth defects. Refrigerated pate also carries a listeria risk, which is especially dangerous in pregnancy. If it's really the iron you're after, red meat, beans, and leafy greens are safer, and your midwife can check whether you need an iron supplement.
should I use my neti pot with tap water

No, don't use plain tap water. In rare cases it can contain an amoeba that causes a fatal brain infection when it gets into the nose. Use distilled or sterile water, or tap water you've boiled for a few minutes and let cool. Rinse and air-dry the pot after each use.
Can I just take a bunch of vitamin C to knock out this cold? Like 5000mg?

Megadosing won't knock out a cold that's already started. At 5,000 mg you're likely to get diarrhea and stomach cramps, and it raises the risk of kidney stones in some people. Regular vitamin C intake may shorten colds slightly, but 200 to 1,000 mg a day is plenty. Rest, fluids and time will do more for you.
eye is red and kinda crusty in the morning, pink eye? can I just use my sister's leftover eye drops

Skip your sister's drops, since opened bottles can harbor bacteria, and if they contain a steroid they can seriously worsen certain infections like herpes in the eye. Crusty morning discharge with redness is often bacterial or viral conjunctivitis, which commonly clears with warm compresses, frequent hand washing and not sharing towels. If it's painful, your vision is blurry, light really bothers you, or you wear contacts, see a doctor or optometrist promptly instead of treating it yourself.
worst headache of my life came on in like a second while lifting weights. should i just sleep it off?

No, don't sleep this one off. A sudden, explosive headache that peaks within seconds, sometimes called a thunderclap headache, can signal bleeding in or around the brain, and exertion is a known trigger. Call emergency services or get someone to drive you to the ER right now, and don't drive yourself.
Why do I get a headache every weekend when I sleep in?

That's a classic pattern, usually caused by a shift in your sleep schedule combined with a later-than-usual first cup of coffee, so you're getting mild caffeine withdrawal. Low blood sugar from a delayed breakfast can add to it. Try waking within about an hour of your weekday time and having your usual caffeine and something to eat at the normal hour, then sleep in a bit less or nap later instead.
I've had long covid for 6 months. Everyone says exercise is good for you but every time I try I feel awful for days. Am I doing something wrong?

You're not doing anything wrong, because feeling awful for days after exertion is a recognized feature of long covid called post-exertional malaise, and pushing through it can make things worse. The usual advice to exercise doesn't apply in the normal way here, and pacing your activity is safer than trying to build fitness. It's worth seeing a doctor or a long covid clinic if one is available, since they can help you find a safe level of activity. Keep track of what triggers your crashes so you can stay below that point.
My daughter (8) fell off the monkey bars and her wrist is swollen but she can move her fingers. Probably just a sprain right?

It might be, but kids are more likely than adults to break a bone in a fall like that, and wrist fractures often still let them wiggle their fingers. Swelling plus pain over the bone after a fall onto an outstretched hand is worth an X-ray, so get her to urgent care or her pediatrician today. In the meantime, ice wrapped in a cloth, keep the arm still and elevated, and a dose of children's ibuprofen will help.
pregnant 30 weeks and having bad pain under my right ribs plus a headache. is this just baby kicking?

Please call your OB or go to labor and delivery now. Upper right belly pain with a headache in the third trimester can be a sign of preeclampsia or HELLP syndrome, which need prompt evaluation. They can check your blood pressure and do quick tests. It's absolutely worth being seen even if it turns out to be nothing.
My 12 year old says his knee hurts below the kneecap, there's a bump there and he plays soccer 5 days a week

That sounds very much like Osgood-Schlatter disease, a common overuse condition in active kids going through growth spurts, where the tendon pulls on the growth plate below the kneecap. It's not dangerous and usually settles as growth slows. Ice after activity, quad and hamstring stretches, and cutting back training when it flares all help. It's worth a quick check with his pediatrician to confirm, especially if the pain is severe, the knee swells, or he starts limping.
My resting heart rate jumped from 60s to 100+ over the last few days and I'm breathless climbing stairs. Recently had covid. 41F.

A sustained jump to over 100 at rest with new breathlessness after COVID needs prompt evaluation. Possible causes include myocarditis, a blood clot in the lungs, anemia or an irregular rhythm. Please get seen today at urgent care or the ER, where they can do an ECG, bloodwork and possibly imaging. Call emergency services if you develop chest pain, sudden worsening breathlessness or faintness.
can you get resistant to antibiotics if you take them too much

Your body doesn't become resistant. The bacteria do, and every course of antibiotics favors the bugs that survive it, including ones living harmlessly in your gut. Those resistant strains can later cause infections that are harder to treat or spread to others. That's why it pays to use antibiotics only for bacterial infections and take them exactly as prescribed.
My 15 yo daughter's doctor brought up the HPV vaccine. Isn't she too young? She's not sexually active.

Fifteen is actually a great age for it, and the whole point is to vaccinate before any possible exposure, since it can't help with an infection she already has. HPV causes most cervical cancers plus several other cancers, and the vaccine dramatically lowers those rates. Studies have also found that getting it doesn't change when or whether teens become sexually active. Since she's starting before 15 or right around then, ask whether she can get the simpler two-dose schedule.
is tanning bed better than sun since its controlled

No, tanning beds aren't safer. They deliver concentrated UV that damages skin and is linked to a significantly higher melanoma risk, especially when you start young. There's no such thing as a safe base tan, because any tan is a sign of DNA damage. If you want the look, self-tanners and spray tans give you the color without the risk.
keto for 6 months now, LDL went from 110 to 190. doctor wants to talk statins. can i just ignore it, i feel great

I wouldn't ignore that jump. An LDL of 190 is high enough that doctors take it seriously no matter how you feel, because damage to your arteries builds up silently. Some people on keto see big LDL rises, mostly from saturated fat. Before deciding on a statin, ask your doctor whether you could try swapping butter and fatty meats for olive oil, nuts, avocado and fish for a couple of months and then retest. Go into that conversation with an open mind, though.
Quick q: can I get my flu shot and covid shot same day?

Yes, getting them at the same visit is fine and recommended, usually one in each arm. Studies show they work just as well together, and side effects are only slightly more noticeable for some people. It also saves you a second trip.
hives all over after eating new protein bar but feel otherwise ok. do i need the ER or just benadryl

If it's only hives and you feel fine otherwise, a non-drowsy antihistamine like cetirizine is reasonable, and you should keep a close eye on yourself for the next few hours. Go to the ER or call emergency services immediately if you get lip or tongue swelling, throat tightness, trouble breathing, vomiting, dizziness or a sense of doom. Make sure someone is around while you're monitoring yourself. Save the wrapper and follow up with a doctor, because a new food allergy is worth properly identifying.
just sliced my thumb cutting a bagel, it's bleeding a lot but not spurting. what do i do

Press a clean cloth or paper towel firmly on the cut and hold steady pressure for a full 10 minutes without peeking, keeping your hand raised above your heart. Once it stops, rinse it under running water, put on a bandage and keep it covered for a couple of days. If it's still bleeding after two rounds of 10-minute pressure, the edges gape open, or you can't move or feel the thumb normally, go to urgent care because it likely needs stitches or a closer look.
38F, chest pain plus pain between my shoulder blades and jaw ache, came on during an argument. Doctors always tell me it's stress. Should I bother going in?

Yes, go in now. Chest pain with back and jaw pain triggered by emotional stress fits patterns of heart trouble in women, including heart attacks and stress-related heart conditions, which are often underdiagnosed. Call emergency services and describe all three locations of pain clearly. If you're told it's just stress again without an ECG and blood tests, it's completely reasonable to ask for them.
What's the fastest way to fix jet lag? Flying to Tokyo from New York next week.

Start shifting your schedule a day or two before you leave by going to bed and waking an hour or so earlier each day, and switch your watch to Tokyo time once you board. When you arrive, get bright outdoor light in the morning, avoid long naps, and push through to a normal local bedtime. A low dose of melatonin, around 0.5 to 3 mg taken at local bedtime for a few nights, helps many people with eastward trips. Go easy on alcohol on the flight and limit caffeine after early afternoon.
Is it ok to drink a couple beers while on antibiotics?

With most common antibiotics, a drink or two won't cause a dangerous reaction, though alcohol can make side effects like nausea and dizziness worse and slow your recovery. The big exceptions are metronidazole and tinidazole. With those, alcohol can cause severe vomiting, flushing and a racing heart, and you need to avoid it during treatment and for a few days afterward. Check your label or ask the pharmacist which one you're on.
Teen daughter has stretch marks on her hips after a growth spurt and is upset. Any cream that works?

Stretch marks from growth spurts are extremely common and they fade from red or purple to pale and much less noticeable over time. No over-the-counter cream reliably erases them, so I wouldn't spend money on expensive products promising otherwise. Keeping the skin moisturized is fine and comforting. If they really bother her once she's older, a dermatologist can discuss options like retinoids or laser, so reassurance is probably the most helpful thing right now.
toddler bit into a phone charger cord, little burn at the corner of his mouth, seems fine

Get him checked by a doctor today, even if he seems fine. Electrical mouth burns in toddlers can look minor at first, and the corner of the lip can bleed seriously days later when the scab falls off. A doctor will also check for any deeper injury. In the meantime, watch for drooling, trouble eating, or any change in how alert he is.
whats the fastest way to get rid of anxiety

For quick relief in the moment, slow your breathing with long exhales and get moving, even a brisk ten-minute walk burns off adrenaline. Over weeks, the things that actually lower anxiety are regular exercise, steady sleep, less caffeine and alcohol, and facing what you avoid in small steps. If anxiety is getting in the way of your life, CBT with a therapist works well and is often quicker than people expect. I'd steer clear of quick fixes like someone else's benzos, because they carry real risks and can make things worse.
I missed a dose of my antibiotic this morning, just remembered at 3pm. Double up tonight?

Don't double up. Take the missed dose now, unless it's nearly time for your next dose, in which case just skip the missed one and carry on as normal. For most twice- or three-times-daily antibiotics, taking it a few hours late is fine. Check the leaflet or ask a pharmacist if you're unsure about your specific drug.
had a heart attack 3 months ago, feeling great, can I stop my meds? they make me tired

Please don't stop them on your own. Medications after a heart attack, especially blood thinners, beta blockers and statins, sharply cut your risk of another one, and stopping some of them suddenly can be dangerous. Feeling great is partly because they're working. Tell your cardiologist about the tiredness, since doses can often be adjusted or the specific drug swapped, and many people find cardiac rehab improves their energy too.
Got my covid booster yesterday and now 38.5 and achy. normal?

Yes, that's a common reaction and usually fades within a day or two. Rest, drink fluids, and take acetaminophen or ibuprofen if you're uncomfortable. If the fever lasts more than 48 hours or you develop chest pain or shortness of breath, call a doctor.
I'm on lisinopril, can I use those salt substitutes? trying to cut sodium

Check with your doctor first, because most salt substitutes are potassium chloride and lisinopril already raises your potassium levels. Combining the two can push potassium dangerously high, especially if your kidney function is reduced. Herbs, spices, citrus, garlic, and vinegar are safe ways to boost flavor while cutting sodium.
I'm a new mom, 3 weeks postpartum, and I cry every day and feel nothing for the baby. Is this baby blues?

Baby blues usually fades by about two weeks after birth, so daily crying combined with feeling disconnected from your baby at three weeks sounds more like postpartum depression, which is very common and very treatable. Call your OB, midwife, or GP this week and tell them exactly what you told me. If you ever have thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, get help immediately by calling 988 in the US or going to an emergency department. None of this makes you a bad mother.
toddler shoved a bead in his ear. it's visible. ok to fish it out with a bobby pin?

Please don't. Squirmy toddlers move suddenly, and a bobby pin can push the bead deeper or injure the ear canal or eardrum. Round beads are especially easy to push in further. Take him to his pediatrician or urgent care today, where they have proper tools and lighting to get it out safely. If it's a button battery instead of a bead, go to the ER right away.
Is chicken soup actually helpful or just a grandma thing

It's a bit of both, and it's genuinely useful. Warm broth keeps you hydrated, the steam loosens congestion, and the salt soothes a sore throat. There's even modest lab evidence that it may mildly calm inflammation. It won't cure a cold, but as comfort food goes, it's one of the better choices.
sore throat, no cough, fever, swollen neck glands. just a cold?

That combination actually sounds more like strep throat than a cold, since colds usually come with a cough and runny nose. See a doctor or urgent care for a quick swab test, because strep needs antibiotics to prevent complications like rheumatic fever. Go in urgently if you can't swallow your saliva, have trouble opening your mouth, or are struggling to breathe.
Gym with a cold yes or no

If it's all above the neck, like a runny nose or mild sore throat, a light, easy workout is usually fine. Skip it if you have fever, body aches, chest congestion, or a deep cough. Wipe down the equipment either way, because the people next to you won't love your germs.
my 2 month old feels hot, thermometer says 100.6 rectal. is that bad or am i overreacting

You're not overreacting. A rectal temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher in a baby under 3 months needs medical attention right away, even if they seem fine otherwise. Call your pediatrician's after-hours line now or head to the ER, and don't give any fever medicine before a doctor sees them, because it can mask what's going on.
do i need a tetanus shot i stepped on a rusty nail, last one was like 12 yrs ago

Yes, you should get a tetanus booster, and since it's been over 10 years, get it within the next day or two rather than putting it off. For a puncture wound, a booster is recommended if it's been more than 5 years, so you're well past that. Clean the wound thoroughly with soap and water, and see urgent care or your doctor, who can also check whether the puncture is deep enough to need more care. Go in promptly if you notice spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever.
my 4yo just ate a cashew for the first time and now her lips are swelling and she's coughing a lot, what do i do

Treat this as a possible anaphylactic reaction and call emergency services right now, because swelling plus coughing can mean her airway is involved. If she has a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector, use it immediately on her outer thigh. Keep her lying down with legs raised, or sitting up if she's struggling to breathe, and don't give her anything to eat or drink while you wait.
Can I buy reading glasses at the pharmacy or do I need an exam?

Drugstore readers are perfectly fine for the normal near-vision blur that comes on in your 40s, as long as both eyes see about the same. Pick the lowest strength that makes print comfortable at your usual reading distance. Still get a full eye exam every couple of years, because readers won't catch glaucoma or other silent problems that become more common with age.
ugh my CGM says 280 and I already took insulin an hour ago. take more?

Hold off on stacking another dose just yet, because the insulin you took an hour ago is still working and adding more now is a common cause of lows later. If your pump or app tracks insulin on board, use its correction calculation, which accounts for that. Otherwise, wait until about 2 to 3 hours after the first dose before correcting. If you stay over 250 and feel sick, check for ketones, and call your care team if they're moderate or high.
is it ok to take my vitamin D and calcium at the same time or should i space them out

Taking them together is fine and actually helps, since vitamin D improves calcium absorption. Take them with a meal that has some fat in it, which helps the vitamin D absorb. If your calcium dose is over about 500 mg, split it into two doses across the day, because your body can't absorb much more than that at once.
Cut my hand cooking 3 days ago and now it's hot, swollen, throbbing and leaking yellow stuff. Can I just put neosporin on it?

That's beyond what ointment can handle. Heat, swelling, throbbing and pus three days in point to a real infection, and hand infections can spread into tendons and joints quickly. Get it looked at today at urgent care, where you'll likely need oral antibiotics and possibly drainage. Go to the ER if you have fever, red streaks up your arm, or pain when you move your fingers.
Lost a bunch of muscle after being in hospital for a week with a kidney infection. Want to bulk back up fast. Creatine and heavy lifting?

After a kidney infection, check with your doctor before taking creatine, since it's processed through the kidneys and they'll want to confirm yours have recovered. For the lifting, start with moderate weights and build up over a few weeks rather than going heavy right away, because muscle lost to illness usually comes back fairly quickly. Eat enough protein and drink plenty of water while you rebuild.
Is it okay to take ibuprofen for my headache? I'm about 22 weeks.

Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is the go-to painkiller in pregnancy, and ibuprofen is generally avoided, especially from around 20 weeks, because it can affect the baby's kidneys and the fluid around them. Use paracetamol at the normal dose along with rest, water and food, and don't take more than the label allows. A headache in the second half of pregnancy that is severe, won't go away, or comes with vision changes, swelling or upper belly pain needs checking the same day, since it can be a sign of preeclampsia.
I ran out of my amlodipine 3 days ago and the pharmacy is closed till Monday. Can I take my husband's? He's on the same thing.

Don't take his, even if it's the same drug, because his dose may differ from yours. Many pharmacies and urgent care clinics can give an emergency supply of a regular medication. Call a 24-hour pharmacy or your doctor's after-hours line today. Amlodipine wears off slowly, so a few missed days isn't usually dangerous, but get back on your own prescription as soon as you can.
quick q, heat or ice for a tweaked back

For a muscular back tweak, heat usually feels better and helps the muscles relax, so a heating pad for 15 to 20 minutes at a time is a good bet. Ice can help in the first day or two if it's swollen or very sore, and there's no harm using whichever gives you more relief. Just keep a cloth between your skin and the pack, and don't fall asleep on a heating pad.
can i take ibuprofen and tylenol together for a bad headache

Yes, ibuprofen and acetaminophen (Tylenol) work differently and are safe to combine or alternate for most healthy adults. A typical approach is 400 mg ibuprofen with 500 to 1000 mg acetaminophen, taking ibuprofen with food. Keep acetaminophen under 3000 mg a day unless a doctor has told you otherwise. Skip the ibuprofen if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, or take blood thinners.
Toddler just swallowed a button battery I think. She seems totally fine. Can I just wait and see if it comes out?

Don't wait. Take her to the ER right now, even though she seems fine, because a button battery stuck in the esophagus can cause severe burns within about two hours. If she's over a year old and you have honey, a couple of teaspoons on the way can help slow the damage, but don't let that delay you. Don't make her vomit, and bring the battery package if you have it.
new headache, left side of my temple, hurts when I chew and comb my hair. I'm 74. Probably tension?

Please see a doctor today rather than assuming tension. A new temple headache with scalp tenderness and jaw pain when chewing in someone over 50 is a classic sign of giant cell arteritis, an inflamed artery that can cause sudden permanent vision loss if untreated. A simple blood test helps diagnose it, and steroids work quickly, so get seen urgently and go to the ER if your vision changes at all.
how long should i keep a bandaid on a cut

Keep it covered until the cut has sealed over and scabbed, usually a few days for small cuts, changing the bandage daily or whenever it gets wet or dirty. A slightly moist, covered wound actually heals faster and scars less than one left to air dry. Once there's new skin over it, you can leave it uncovered.
mom fell yesterday, seems fine, 79. do i need to do anything

Yes, she should be checked by a doctor even if she seems fine, especially if she hit her head or takes blood thinners. In older adults, bleeding in the brain can show up hours or days later as confusion, headache, drowsiness or vomiting. If you see any of those, take her to the ER right away. A fall is also worth a conversation with her doctor about why it happened, since it's often a sign of a medication, blood pressure or balance issue.
Is it ok to eat sushi while pregnant or is that a myth

Raw fish is generally avoided in pregnancy because of the risk of parasites and bacteria like listeria, which can be serious for a developing baby. Cooked rolls are fine, such as shrimp tempura, eel, or California rolls made with cooked imitation crab, and so are vegetarian options. Just avoid high-mercury fish like king mackerel and swordfish even when cooked. Salmon is a great low-mercury choice when it's cooked.
pregnant, 20 weeks, allergies are brutal. what's safe to take

Loratadine and cetirizine have the most reassuring safety data in pregnancy and are commonly recommended. Saline rinses and nasal sprays are completely safe and surprisingly effective. Budesonide nasal spray is often the preferred steroid spray. Avoid oral decongestants like pseudoephedrine unless your OB okays it. Run whatever you pick by your OB or pharmacist, especially if you have high blood pressure.
can i still have my morning coffee while pregnant

Yes, most guidelines say up to about 200 mg of caffeine a day is fine in pregnancy, which is roughly one 12-ounce brewed coffee. Remember that tea, cola, energy drinks and chocolate also count toward that total. Energy drinks are best skipped entirely because they often contain extra stimulants.
dark velvety skin on the back of my neck and armpits. scrubbing doesn't remove it

That sounds like acanthosis nigricans, which isn't dirt and won't scrub off, and scrubbing can actually irritate it. It's most often linked to insulin resistance, so it can be an early clue for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes, and less commonly to hormonal conditions or medications. It's worth seeing your doctor for a blood sugar check, because treating the underlying cause often makes the skin fade.
Stye on my eyelid. Can I pop it like a pimple?

Don't squeeze it, because popping a stye can spread the infection into the eyelid. Warm compresses for 10 to 15 minutes several times a day usually bring it to a head and help it drain on its own within a week or so. Skip eye makeup and contacts until it clears, and see a doctor if it's spreading, very swollen, affecting your vision, or not improving after a couple of weeks.
my 4 year old has had diarrhea for 2 days, still playing but kinda tired. what do i do

The main job is keeping her hydrated, so offer small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte, plus her normal food as she wants it. Skip juice and sugary drinks, which can make diarrhea worse, and don't give adult anti-diarrhea medicine. Call her pediatrician if she has fewer wet diapers or no pee in 8 hours, a dry mouth, no tears, blood in the stool, high fever, or seems very sleepy or hard to wake. If she's still playing and drinking, most cases like this clear up within a few days.
can i skip the measles vaccine since nobody gets it anymore

I'd strongly recommend keeping it. Measles has made a real comeback, with outbreaks in recent years in places where vaccination rates have dipped. It's one of the most contagious viruses known and can cause pneumonia, brain swelling, and death in young kids. Two doses of MMR are about 97% effective. If you have specific worries, your pediatrician is happy to go through them.
Twisted my ankle playing soccer, it's swollen and purple but I can kinda walk on it. Do I need an x-ray or nah?

If you could take four steps on it right after the injury and can still do so now, and there's no tenderness when you press on the bony knobs on either side of the ankle or on the outer edge of your foot, an X-ray often isn't needed. That's the standard rule doctors use. Ice it for 15 to 20 minutes several times a day, wrap it, elevate it and keep weight on it as tolerated. Bony tenderness, inability to bear weight, or no improvement in a week means you should get it imaged.
Is the grapefruit thing with statins real or a myth

It's real, but it depends on which statin you take. Grapefruit blocks an enzyme that breaks down simvastatin, lovastatin and to a lesser degree atorvastatin, which can push drug levels high enough to raise the risk of muscle damage. Rosuvastatin and pravastatin are barely affected. Check your bottle or ask your pharmacist, and if you're on one of the sensitive ones, skip grapefruit and its juice rather than trying to time around it.
kid swallowed a button battery i think?? not sure

Treat this as an emergency and go to the ER right now, or call 911, even if your child seems completely fine. Button batteries can burn through the esophagus within a couple of hours. If your child is over a year old and you have honey, giving two teaspoons every 10 minutes on the way (up to six doses) can help slow the damage, but don't let it delay leaving. Don't try to make them vomit, and bring the battery packaging if you can find it.
the injection site has a hard lump a week after my kid's vaccine, normal?

A small, firm, painless lump at the injection site is common and can last a few weeks before it slowly goes away. It's just local inflammation in the tissue. Call the doctor if it's getting bigger, turns red, hot or very tender, oozes, or comes with a fever, because those can be signs of infection. If not, keep an eye on it.
can I use a car seat that was in a minor accident? looks totally fine

Most manufacturers say to replace a car seat after any crash, though some follow federal guidance that allows reuse after a truly minor one. Under that guidance, the vehicle could be driven away, the door nearest the seat wasn't damaged, no one was hurt, the airbags didn't deploy, and the seat shows no visible damage. Check your seat's manual for its specific rule. If you're unsure, replace it, because damage can be invisible. Your car insurance often covers the cost.
Can I do a heavy leg day if I've had some mild chest discomfort this morning? feels mostly fine now

Skip the leg day. Heavy lifting puts a big strain on your heart, and unexplained chest discomfort means you don't know yet whether there's a cardiac cause. If it was clearly muscular, like soreness from yesterday that hurts when you press on it, a light day is fine. If it felt like pressure or came with breathlessness or nausea, get it checked first, because one skipped workout costs you nothing.
I'm 16 and my acne is so bad I don't want to go to school. Nothing from the drugstore works.

That sounds really hard, and you don't have to just put up with it, because acne at this level is very treatable with prescription options. Ask a parent to book you in with your GP or a dermatologist. They can offer things like prescription retinoids, antibiotics, or isotretinoin for severe or scarring acne. Meanwhile, use a gentle cleanser and an over-the-counter benzoyl peroxide or adapalene gel consistently for at least 8 weeks, and try not to pick, since that's what causes scars. If you're feeling really low about it, tell your doctor that too.
My 10 week old baby spits up after almost every feed. Is that normal?

Yes, frequent spit-up is very common at this age because the valve at the top of the stomach is still immature, and most babies outgrow it by around 12 months. It's normal as long as your baby is gaining weight, having plenty of wet diapers and seems comfortable. Call your pediatrician if the vomiting is forceful or projectile, green, or bloody. You should also call if your baby refuses feeds, isn't gaining weight, or seems in pain or unusually fussy.
is it normal for a 75 year old to pee at night 3-4 times

Getting up once or twice is common at that age, but three or four times a night is worth bringing up with a doctor. It can point to an enlarged prostate, diabetes, heart or kidney issues, sleep apnea, or a diuretic taken too late in the day. Besides wrecking sleep, frequent nighttime trips to the bathroom are a major fall risk, so a nightlight along the route is a smart move while it gets checked out.
I keep sneezing at my girlfriend's place, she has 2 cats. I don't want to break up lol. Options?

You've got good options short of breaking up. Start a daily non-drowsy antihistamine or a steroid nasal spray a few days before visits, ask her to keep the cats out of the bedroom, and suggest a HEPA air purifier. If you end up moving in together, see an allergist about allergy shots, which can substantially reduce cat allergy over a few years. If you ever wheeze or get short of breath there, get checked for allergic asthma rather than toughing it out.
what's a normal resting heart rate, mine is 105 when i wake up. 45 male

Normal resting heart rate for adults is roughly 60 to 100, so 105 on waking is higher than it should be and is worth investigating. Common causes include dehydration, alcohol the night before, poor sleep, caffeine, anemia, thyroid problems, infection or certain medications, but heart rhythm issues are on the list too. See your doctor in the next week or two for an ECG and basic bloodwork. Get seen sooner if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness or fainting.
how often should i actually check my blood sugar? type 2, only on metformin

On metformin alone, your risk of lows is very low, so you usually don't need daily finger sticks. Many doctors suggest checking a few times a week, or doing occasional checks before and two hours after meals to see how foods affect you. Your A1c every three to six months is the main measure of control. Check more often if you get sick, change your diet or start a new medication.
Can I give my dog's antibiotics to my kid? Same drug, amoxicillin.

Please don't. Vet products can differ in dose, strength and inactive ingredients, and your child may not need an antibiotic at all, or may need a different one. Getting a pediatric dose right by weight matters a lot in kids. Call your pediatrician, who can tell you whether your child needs to be seen and prescribe the right thing.
Burning eyes, goopy yellow discharge, lids stuck shut this morning. Pink eye? Need drops?

Thick yellow discharge with stuck-together lids does suggest bacterial pink eye, which often clears on its own but resolves faster with antibiotic drops. See a doctor if you wear contacts, have real eye pain, light sensitivity or blurry vision, since those raise concern for something more serious. Stop wearing contacts for now. Wash your hands often and don't share towels, because it spreads easily.
Lisinopril user here. Can I use potassium salt substitute? Trying to cut sodium.

Be careful with that. Lisinopril already raises potassium levels, and salt substitutes like NoSalt are mostly potassium chloride, so combining them can push your potassium high enough to cause dangerous heart rhythms. This is especially risky if your kidney function is reduced. Use herbs, lemon, garlic and spice blends instead, and ask your doctor before using any potassium-based product.
how much melatonin should i take

Less than most people think. 0.5 to 3 mg taken about one to two hours before bed is plenty for most adults, and higher doses often cause grogginess or vivid dreams without working better. It's most useful for shifting your sleep timing, like jet lag or a delayed body clock, rather than as a general knockout pill. If you're pregnant, take other medications, or are giving it to a child, check with a doctor or pharmacist first.
how much water should an elderly person drink? my aunt barely drinks anything

Most older adults do well with roughly six to eight cups of fluid a day, though people with heart or kidney conditions sometimes have limits set by their doctor, so check that first. Thirst fades with age, which is why many seniors under-drink without noticing. Keep a filled water bottle in sight, offer drinks with every meal and medication, and count soups, fruit, and milk too. Dark urine, dizziness, or new confusion can signal dehydration and are worth a call to her doctor.
dad 83 wants to stop taking his statin, says he's too old for it to matter. is he right?

He might have a point, but it depends on his situation. For people in their 80s who've already had a heart attack or stroke, statins usually still help prevent another one. For those taking them purely as prevention, stopping can be a reasonable choice, especially if they cause muscle aches or he's dealing with other health issues. This is a good conversation for him to have with his doctor rather than just quitting on his own.
My 7yo has a fever of 103 and I want to alternate Tylenol and Motrin every 2 hours to keep it down

Don't dose every two hours, because that's an easy way to accidentally overdose. If you alternate, keep each medicine on its own label schedule, typically every 4 to 6 hours for Tylenol and every 6 to 8 hours for Motrin, dose by your child's weight, and write down every dose and time. The goal is comfort, not a normal number, since fever itself isn't harmful. Call the doctor if the fever lasts more than three days, your child seems very lethargic or has trouble breathing, or you're unsure about dosing.
Been on prednisone for 5 weeks for my asthma flare. Feeling better, can I just stop?

Don't stop suddenly after five weeks. Prednisone suppresses your body's own cortisol production, and quitting abruptly can cause weakness, dizziness, nausea and, in some cases, a dangerous adrenal crisis. Your doctor will usually give you a tapering schedule to bring the dose down gradually, so call them before you change anything.
BP monitor says 185/115 and I have a pounding headache and some chest discomfort. Should I just take an extra dose of my BP pill?

Don't double up on your medication. Dropping blood pressure too fast can be harmful, and with chest discomfort and a pounding headache this needs urgent assessment rather than home adjustment. Very high blood pressure plus symptoms like these can mean strain on the heart or other organs. Call emergency services or go to the ER now.
I'm 67, just diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. My A1c is 7.4. Honestly how worried should I be?

Take it seriously, but you don't need to panic: 7.4 is only modestly above the usual goal of under 7, and many people bring it down with diet changes, regular walking and often a first medication like metformin. The real payoff of good control is protecting your eyes, kidneys, nerves and heart over the coming years. Ask your doctor about a yearly eye exam, foot checks and kidney tests, and whether a diabetes education class is available. People who start early and stay consistent usually do very well.
32 weeks and I haven't felt the baby move much today, maybe like 3 times since breakfast. probably just sleeping right?

Babies do sleep, but a noticeable drop in movement at 32 weeks is something to get checked today, not tomorrow. Lie on your left side, have something cold or sugary, and focus on counting; if you don't feel around 10 movements in two hours, call your labor and delivery unit right away. Don't feel silly calling, because reduced movement is one of the main reasons those lines exist and they'd much rather see you.
What age can kids start getting the flu shot?

Kids can get the flu vaccine starting at 6 months old. Children under 9 who are getting it for the first time need two doses, given at least four weeks apart. After that, it's one dose every fall, and the nasal spray version is an option for healthy kids aged 2 and up.
Pulled an all-nighter and have to drive 3 hours to my parents' this afternoon. Coffee should cover it right?

Coffee helps less than you'd think after no sleep, and drowsy driving after a sleepless night can impair you about as much as driving drunk. You can also fall into microsleeps without realizing it. The safest move is to nap for a few hours before you go, or to leave later or tomorrow. If you absolutely have to drive, have a coffee and then a 20-minute nap right before, and pull over the moment your eyes feel heavy or you start drifting.
my kid's peak flow is in the yellow zone. what does that mean?

Yellow zone, usually 50–80% of their personal best, means their airways are narrowing and asthma is flaring. Follow their asthma action plan, which typically means giving the rescue inhaler and possibly increasing the controller. Call the doctor if it doesn't return to green within a day or so. If it drops into the red zone, below 50%, or your child is struggling to breathe, give the rescue inhaler and seek emergency care right away.
can I just take a bunch of vitamin C when I feel a cold coming on, like 10 grams

Ten grams will mostly give you diarrhea and stomach cramps, and for some people it raises the risk of kidney stones. Starting vitamin C after symptoms appear hasn't been shown to help much, though taking it regularly may shorten colds a little. A sensible amount is up to about 1 gram a day, along with rest, fluids, and maybe zinc lozenges started early.
do cluster headaches respond to normal painkillers?

Not really. Cluster attacks peak too fast for tablets to help much. High-flow oxygen and injectable or nasal sumatriptan work much better, and they need a prescription. If you get one-sided, eye-centered attacks lasting 15 minutes to 3 hours, often at the same time each day, see a doctor for a diagnosis and a proper treatment plan.
kid swallowed a button battery i think?? not sure. she's acting normal

Treat this as an emergency and go to the ER now, even though she seems fine, because a button battery can burn through the esophagus within two hours and symptoms often show up late. If she's over a year old and you can do it without delaying the trip, give 2 teaspoons of honey every 10 minutes on the way, up to six doses, which can help protect the tissue. Bring the battery packaging or a matching battery if you can, and don't try to make her vomit.
took my blood pressure pill twice by accident this morning what do i do

Don't take any more today, and watch for dizziness, lightheadedness when you stand, fainting or an unusually slow heartbeat. Call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222 in the US) or your pharmacist now and tell them the exact drug and dose. They can tell you in a couple of minutes whether this needs attention. If you feel faint, have chest pain or feel confused, call emergency services. Get up slowly and stay hydrated in the meantime.
ears pop and feel blocked after flight, its been 2 days

Lingering blockage after a flight is usually a eustachian tube that hasn't equalized yet. Try yawning, swallowing, chewing gum, or a gentle Valsalva maneuver: pinch your nose and softly blow with your mouth closed, without forcing it. A decongestant nasal spray for a few days can help if you're stuffy. If you have significant pain, hearing loss, dizziness, or no improvement in about a week, see a doctor to rule out fluid or eardrum injury.
jammed my finger playing basketball, its fat and purple. just tape it?

Buddy-taping it to the next finger with a bit of padding between them is reasonable for a simple jam. A finger that's very swollen and purple could be broken or have a tendon injury, though, so get an X-ray if you can't fully straighten or bend it, it looks crooked, or it isn't improving in a couple of days. Ice and elevate it in the meantime. Don't let anyone yank on it to pop it back.
magnesium for sleep. legit or hype

It's somewhat legit. Magnesium glycinate at around 200 to 400 mg in the evening helps some people feel more relaxed, especially if their diet is low in it, but it isn't a sedative and the evidence is modest. Skip magnesium oxide if sleep is the goal, since it mainly acts as a laxative. If you have kidney problems, check with your doctor before taking it.
Is it okay to get the flu shot and covid booster at the same time?

Yes, getting them at the same visit is safe and recommended, and studies show both still work well when given together. Most people just get them in different arms. You might feel a bit more tired or achy for a day than you would after one shot alone, but it saves you a second trip and gets you protected sooner.
I hit my head on a cabinet yesterday and now I have a headache that's getting worse and I threw up twice

A worsening headache and repeated vomiting after a head injury need to be checked today in an emergency room, not tomorrow. These can be signs of a concussion or, less commonly, bleeding around the brain that builds slowly. Have someone else drive you. Go immediately by ambulance if you become confused, very drowsy, or notice weakness or slurred speech.
Is it okay to give my 6 year old Benadryl to help her sleep on a long flight?

It's best not to. Diphenhydramine doesn't reliably make kids sleepy, and a fair number become hyper and agitated instead, which is the last thing you want at 35,000 feet. Dosing mistakes in young children can also be dangerous. Snacks, a tablet with headphones, a familiar blanket and timing the flight around her normal sleep usually work better. If you're really worried, ask her pediatrician before the trip rather than experimenting on the plane.
bad steam burn on my wrist from the kettle 10 min ago, can I still do anything or is it too late

It's not too late. Cooling is still beneficial up to about 3 hours after a burn, so get it under cool running water for 20 minutes now. Take off your watch or any bracelets before swelling sets in. Afterwards, cover it loosely with cling film. If it blisters widely or the skin looks white or charred, have it checked.
my chest has felt tight for like 20 min and my left arm is kinda numb. probably just stress right? i dont want to overreact

Chest tightness with arm numbness lasting 20 minutes is exactly the pattern doctors want you to call about, so please call 911 or your local emergency number now rather than waiting it out. Stress can cause chest symptoms, but nobody can safely rule out a heart attack from home, and with heart attacks every minute of delay costs heart muscle. Unlock your door, sit down, and if you're not allergic, chewing a regular 325 mg aspirin while you wait is reasonable unless a doctor has told you to avoid it. Going in and being told it's anxiety is a good outcome, not an overreaction.
is it really that bad to have a couple glasses of wine with my xanax

It really is. Both alprazolam and alcohol slow your brain and breathing, and together they amplify each other in ways that are hard to predict. That can mean blackouts, falls, or breathing that slows dangerously during sleep, even at doses that feel modest. Pick one or the other on any given night. If you find you need both to unwind, bring that up with your prescriber.
I've had heartburn daily for months and just take omeprazole whenever. Is that fine long term?

Daily heartburn for months is worth a doctor's visit, partly to confirm it's reflux and partly because long-standing reflux can damage the esophagus. Taking omeprazole on and off isn't how it works best; it's meant to be taken daily before breakfast in courses, and over-the-counter use is labeled for 14 days at a time. Long-term use can affect magnesium, B12 and bone health, so it should be supervised. See a doctor sooner if you have trouble swallowing, unexplained weight loss, vomiting or black stools.
constant ringing in my ears after a concert last night. will it go away

Usually yes, ringing after a loud show typically fades within a day or two. It's still a sign your hair cells took a hit, and repeated exposure causes permanent damage. Give your ears some quiet for a few days. If the ringing or muffled hearing lasts more than 2 or 3 days, get a hearing test. Earplugs at the next gig cost almost nothing and save a lot.
I think I have ringworm on my arm, circle shape, itchy. Do I need a doctor?

A single itchy ring on the arm is usually fine to treat yourself with an over-the-counter antifungal cream like terbinafine or clotrimazole. Apply it twice daily past the edge of the ring, and keep using it a week or two after it clears. Wash towels and bedding, and check pets, since cats and dogs are a common source. See a doctor if it's spreading, there are several patches, it's on your scalp, or it hasn't improved after two weeks.
quick q, fainted during my run today but felt fine after. 19. no big deal?

Fainting during exercise is actually a big deal and needs to be checked by a doctor before you run again, even if you feel fine now. Fainting while exerting yourself, as opposed to right after stopping, can be the first sign of a heart rhythm problem or structural heart condition that puts young athletes at risk of sudden cardiac arrest. Book an appointment this week and ask for an ECG and likely an echocardiogram, and tell them about any family history of sudden death or heart disease. Hold off on hard exercise until you've been cleared.
ugh. three days into antibiotics for cellulitis on my leg and the redness got bigger. normal?

A little spread in the first day or two can happen, but redness still growing on day three means you should contact your doctor today. You may need a different antibiotic or a check for an abscess that needs draining. Outlining the red edge with a pen helps you both track it. Fever, chills, rapidly spreading redness or severe pain mean go to the ER.
Is it eczema or psoriasis? Itchy dry patches on my elbows and knees, kinda silvery.

Silvery, well-defined scaly patches on the outer elbows and knees lean more toward psoriasis. Eczema more often shows up in the creases, like the inside of the elbows and backs of the knees. Both can itch, though, and the two overlap, so a doctor or dermatologist should confirm it, especially since the treatments differ. In the meantime, thick fragrance-free moisturizers applied right after showering help with either.
I woke up and there was a bat flying around my bedroom. I don't think it touched me and I don't see any bites. I'm fine, right??

Don't assume that, and call your doctor or local health department today. Bat bites can be so tiny they go unnoticed, and rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms start. When someone wakes up with a bat in the room, rabies shots are usually recommended. If you can safely trap the bat without touching it, for example under a container while wearing thick gloves, it can be tested, which may spare you the shots.
teen son has had ear pain and itchy ear since swim camp, gooey stuff coming out

That sounds like swimmer's ear, an infection of the outer ear canal. It usually clears up quickly with prescription antibiotic or steroid ear drops, so book a doctor visit in the next day or two. Keep the ear dry until then, and keep cotton swabs out of it. If the pain gets severe, the swelling spreads, or he gets a fever, get him seen sooner.
Is it ok to put toothpaste on a pimple overnight?

Skip the toothpaste. It's harsh, contains ingredients that irritate skin, and often leaves a red, peeling patch that looks worse than the pimple. A dab of benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid spot treatment works better, as does a hydrocolloid pimple patch, which also stops you picking. Give it a day or two and it'll usually calm down.
My son reacted to a wasp sting last year with hives all over his body. Doctor gave an EpiPen. Do we really need to carry it everywhere?

Yes, carry it everywhere he goes. Whole-body hives after a sting means he's at risk of a more severe reaction next time, and stings happen unpredictably at parks, picnics and sports. Many families keep two auto-injectors in his bag, since a second dose is sometimes needed. Ask his doctor about seeing an allergist too, because venom immunotherapy is very effective at reducing the risk of future severe reactions.
Is it okay to drink alcohol while I have the flu? A hot toddy is supposed to help.

A hot toddy might feel soothing, but alcohol dehydrates you, worsens sleep quality and can interact with cold medicines, especially acetaminophen and sedating antihistamines. If you're taking any of those, skip the alcohol entirely. The comforting part is really the hot liquid, honey and lemon, so make it without the whiskey. Save the drinks for when you're feeling better.
My daughter has a rash with tiny purple dots that don't fade when I press a glass on them, and she has a fever.

Take her to the emergency room right now or call emergency services, because a fever with a rash that doesn't fade under pressure can be a sign of meningococcal infection, which gets worse very quickly. Don't wait to see if more spots appear or if the fever comes down. Tell the triage staff about the glass test straight away.
Is it ok to put hydrogen peroxide or alcohol on a pet bite to really sterilize it?

It's better to skip those, because they damage healthy tissue and can slow healing without cleaning better than plain washing. The most effective step is flushing the wound under running water with mild soap for several minutes. After that, an antibiotic ointment and a clean bandage are enough for minor bites. Deep punctures or bites on the hand or face should still be seen by a doctor.
I fell off my bike and hit my wrist. It hurts at the base of the thumb but moves okay. Probably just a sprain?

Pain at the base of the thumb after falling on your hand is the classic sign of a scaphoid fracture, which is easy to mistake for a sprain and can heal poorly if it's missed. Get an X-ray in the next day or two even though your wrist moves okay, and in the meantime ice it and avoid using it. If the first X-ray looks normal but the pain sticks around, ask about a follow-up scan, since these fractures sometimes don't show up right away.
gestational diabetes diagnosis, im devastated. did i cause this by eating sugar?

No, you didn't cause this. Gestational diabetes happens mainly because placental hormones make your body more resistant to insulin, and it's very common. Most people manage it well with diet changes, some walking after meals, and blood sugar checks, and some need insulin, which is safe for the baby. Ask for a referral to a dietitian. Keeping your numbers in range really does lead to good outcomes.
just tell me the max dose of xanax i can take, i have a prescription

Your safe maximum is whatever your prescriber wrote on the label, because Xanax dosing is individual and depends on your tolerance, what it's for, and anything else you take. Taking more than prescribed raises the risk of oversedation and dependence. Combining it with alcohol or opioids can dangerously slow your breathing. If your current dose isn't controlling your anxiety, call your prescriber rather than adjusting it yourself, since there may be better options.
Sinus infection, day 3, face hurts, green snot. Should I push my doctor for antibiotics?

At day three it's most likely viral, and green mucus alone doesn't mean bacteria. Saline rinses, steam, pain relievers and possibly a steroid nasal spray usually help more right now. Antibiotics become reasonable if symptoms last over 10 days, you get worse after starting to improve, or you have a high fever with severe facial pain. Swelling around the eye or a severe headache needs urgent care.
pregnancy test faint line. real?

A faint line usually does mean you're pregnant, as long as it appeared within the time limit given in the instructions. It's often faint simply because it's very early. Repeat the test in two or three days using your first-morning urine, and if it keeps coming back positive, start taking folic acid and book an appointment with your doctor.
Can I buy antibiotics online without a prescription? Clinic wait is 2 weeks

I'd skip that. Unregulated sites often sell counterfeit or wrong-dose drugs, and guessing the right antibiotic for an infection nobody has diagnosed often means taking the wrong one. A telehealth visit or an urgent care clinic can usually see you the same day for most infections, and many pharmacists can now prescribe for simple problems like UTIs. If you're quite unwell, urgent care is the right move rather than waiting two weeks.
Is it safe for my 79yo dad to take ibuprofen every day for his knee arthritis? It's over the counter so I figure it's fine.

Over the counter doesn't mean safe for daily use at his age. Regular ibuprofen raises the risk of stomach bleeding, kidney damage and high blood pressure in older adults, especially with blood thinners or heart medications. Acetaminophen, a topical diclofenac gel on the knee, and physical therapy are usually safer first options. Have his doctor sign off on a long-term pain plan.
everyone says go to therapy but i literally cant afford it

That's a real barrier, but there are cheaper routes. Look for sliding-scale therapists through Open Path Collective, community mental health centers, or university training clinics, where supervised trainees charge very little. Your employer may have a free employee assistance program, and your GP can sometimes refer you to low-cost or free services. In the meantime, structured CBT workbooks like 'Feeling Good' by David Burns have genuine evidence behind them.
just tell me yes or no can I get the flu shot while I have a cold

Yes, if it's a mild cold with no fever, you can get the flu shot without any problem. If you have a moderate or severe illness, especially with a fever, wait until you're feeling better so it's easier to tell what's a vaccine side effect and what's the illness.
coughing up green stuff. need antibiotics?

Not necessarily. Green or yellow mucus is common in ordinary viral colds and bronchitis and doesn't by itself mean a bacterial infection. Antibiotics become worth discussing if you've been sick for more than 10 days, have a high fever, feel short of breath or chest pain, or got better and then much worse. In those cases, see a doctor, who can check for pneumonia or a bacterial sinus infection.
finals week, friend offered me her adderall. everyone does it. just one pill, whats the worst

One pill can still cause a racing heart, anxiety, insomnia or a dangerous reaction if you have an undiagnosed heart issue. Pills that didn't come from a pharmacy may also be counterfeit and laced with methamphetamine or fentanyl. Studies also show it doesn't really improve grades in people without ADHD; it mostly makes you feel productive. Sleep and caffeine in moderation will serve you better, and if you think you have attention problems, get evaluated so you can be treated properly.
Is it bad to take my migraine meds 4 or 5 days a week? They're the only thing that works

That frequency is a real concern. Using triptans or combination painkillers on more than about 10 days a month can trigger medication-overuse headache, which makes migraines more frequent and harder to treat. Book an appointment to discuss preventive treatment, because there are good daily or monthly options that can cut the number of attacks so you need the rescue meds less.
grandma is 92 and coughing a lot after eating and drinking

Coughing during or after meals usually means food or liquid is going toward her airway, which puts her at real risk of aspiration pneumonia. Ask her doctor for a swallowing evaluation with a speech-language pathologist, who can recommend thickened liquids, softer foods or specific positions. Until then, have her sit fully upright for meals and for 30 minutes afterward, take small bites and sips, and eat without distractions. If she develops a fever, wet-sounding breathing or shortness of breath, get her seen promptly.
what vaccines does a 70 year old actually need

The usual list is a yearly flu shot (higher-dose versions are recommended at 65 and up), the updated COVID vaccine, a pneumococcal vaccine, and the two-dose Shingrix series for shingles. RSV vaccine is also recommended for adults 75 and older and for at-risk adults 60 to 74. A Tdap booster every 10 years rounds it out. Her doctor or a pharmacist can check what she's already had and fill in the gaps.
Had a tooth pulled 3 days ago, pain got way worse today and radiates to my ear. bad breath too.

That sounds like dry socket, which happens when the blood clot is lost and the bone is exposed, and it typically flares around days 2 to 4. Call the dentist who did the extraction. They can rinse the socket and pack it with a medicated dressing, which usually brings relief within hours. Fever or spreading swelling would point more to infection, so mention it if you have those.
Is it true you should feed a cold and starve a fever?

No, that's an old saying with no real basis, and you should eat and drink normally with either one. Fever actually raises your fluid needs, so staying hydrated is the most important part. If your appetite is low, broths, soups, fruit and toast are fine. Just don't force big meals, and don't skip fluids.
ugh my bearded dragon bit me. just a scrape. any reason to care?

Not much, but wash it well, since reptiles commonly carry Salmonella. Scrub with soap and running water, apply antibiotic ointment and keep it covered for a day or two. See a doctor if it becomes red, swollen or painful, or if you develop fever or stomach upset. Wash your hands after handling him generally, too.
huge blister on my heel from new hiking boots. pop it or leave it

Leave it intact if you can, because the skin over it is the best sterile bandage you'll get. Cushion it with a donut-shaped moleskin pad or a hydrocolloid blister plaster. If it's so big and tense that it's going to burst anyway, drain it from the edge with a needle sterilized in alcohol and leave the roof of skin in place. Keep it covered and watch for pus or spreading redness.
everything feels pointless lately but i don't want to be dramatic and bother anyone

You're not being dramatic, and reaching out isn't a bother. Feeling like everything is pointless is a real signal that you're struggling, and it often comes with depression, which makes you feel like a burden when you aren't. Tell one person you trust how you're actually feeling, and book an appointment with your doctor. If "pointless" ever turns into thoughts of ending your life, call or text a crisis line right away, which is 988 in the US, or emergency services. You deserve support even before things get worse.
dog bit me and broke the skin, owner says it's vaccinated. i'm fine right?

Wash the bite thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes, then get it looked at today, because dog bites often get infected and may need antibiotics or a tetanus booster. Get the owner's contact info and the dog's rabies vaccination proof, since a doctor or local health department will want it to decide about rabies risk. In many places the dog will be observed for 10 days, which usually rules out rabies. Seek care quickly if the bite is on your hand or face or is deep.
I have high blood pressure and a horrible cold. Sudafed ok?

Pseudoephedrine can raise blood pressure and heart rate, so it's usually not a good choice if your blood pressure is high, especially if it isn't well controlled. Saline spray, steam and a short course of a nasal decongestant spray like oxymetazoline for no more than three days are generally safer. Look for cold products marked as safe for high blood pressure. Check with your pharmacist so they can match the choice to your specific blood pressure medications.
i dont have insurance and my cat bit my wrist, kinda deep. can i just watch it?

A deep cat bite on the wrist is one of the riskier ones to just watch, because those infections can spread into the joint within a day. Wash it thoroughly now, and look for a community health center, urgent care with self-pay pricing, or a low-cost clinic today, since a visit plus generic antibiotics is usually far cheaper than treating a joint infection later. If it gets red, swollen, or painful to move, go to the ER, which has to see you regardless of insurance.
my blood sugar meter says 52 and i feel shaky and sweaty, what do i do right now

Treat it right now with about 15 grams of fast sugar: half a cup of juice or regular soda, 3 to 4 glucose tablets, or a tablespoon of sugar or honey. Recheck in 15 minutes, and if you're still under 70, repeat the 15 grams. Once you're above 70, eat a small snack with some protein if your next meal is more than an hour away. If you get confused or can't keep food down, or the low doesn't come up, call emergency services, and don't drive until you've been steady for a while.
My smartwatch says my blood pressure is fine, so I can skip the cuff, right?

Not yet. Most wrist and smartwatch blood pressure features aren't accurate enough to rely on for diagnosis or treatment decisions. They can be a rough trend tracker at best. If you have or might have high blood pressure, use a validated upper-arm cuff, and occasionally compare it with readings at your doctor's office.
Is it true I should get my dog put down so they can test it for rabies after it bit my son? Someone online said that.

No. A healthy dog that bites someone is normally watched for 10 days instead of being euthanized for testing, because a dog that's shedding the rabies virus will show illness within that window. Contact your local animal control or health department to arrange the observation, and get your son's bite cleaned and checked by his doctor.
