Euthanasia for testing is generally only considered if the animal is sick, showing neurological signs or can't be observed.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and have a pounding headache and my vision is kind of sparkly. probably just tired right?

I wouldn't assume that. A severe headache with vision changes late in pregnancy can be a sign of preeclampsia, a blood pressure condition that needs prompt treatment. Call your OB or labor and delivery unit right now, or go in to be checked, especially if you also have swelling in your face or hands or pain under your right ribs.
I forgot my birth control pill yesterday and only just remembered. What do I do?? I'm freaking out a bit

Take the missed pill right now, even if that means two pills today, then carry on with the pack as normal. For a standard combined pill, a single missed pill is usually still covered, but if you've missed two or more, use condoms for the next seven days. If you're on a progestin-only mini-pill and it's more than three hours late, the rules are stricter, so use backup for 48 hours. Your pack insert or a pharmacist can confirm the exact rules for your brand.
71yo, BP is 165/70 consistently. Doctor says it's fine because of my age. Is it?

Not necessarily. Current guidelines generally aim to bring systolic pressure down to around 130–140 in healthy older adults, because high systolic pressure raises the risk of stroke at any age. Your low diastolic number is common at your age and is part of what doctors weigh when deciding how far to lower the top number. Ask your doctor directly whether treatment would help you, and consider getting a second opinion if the answer doesn't feel reasoned.
is ear candling legit for wax

No. Studies show ear candling doesn't create suction or pull wax out, and the residue people see afterward is just candle wax. It has caused burns to the face and ear canal, and even blockages from dripping wax. If wax is actually bothering you, a few days of over-the-counter softening drops usually works, and a clinic can flush or remove stubborn wax safely.
hip hurts when I walk, 70F, been a few months. getting old I suppose

Hip pain while walking that lasts months is often osteoarthritis, and there's plenty that helps, so it's worth seeing your GP rather than just putting up with it. Physiotherapy-led strengthening, keeping active within comfort, managing weight if relevant, and using a stick in the opposite hand can all reduce pain and protect your mobility. If it gets bad enough to limit daily life, hip replacement has excellent results.
I'm 34 and I just noticed a new dark streak under my thumbnail. Didn't injure it that I know of.

A new dark streak under a nail without an injury is worth getting checked soon, especially on the thumb or big toe. Most are harmless pigment or old bruising, but nail melanoma can start this way and is easy to miss. Take a photo now so you can track any change, and book a dermatologist appointment rather than waiting it out. Mention if it's widening, has uneven colour, or the pigment is spreading onto the skin around the nail.
I'm diabetic and got a small cut on my toe trimming my nails. Can I just leave it?

Don't leave it, because with diabetes even small foot cuts can heal slowly and get infected without much pain to warn you. Wash it gently with soap and water, put on a little petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment, and cover it with a clean bandage. Check it every day. Call your doctor or podiatrist promptly if it isn't improving within a couple of days or you see redness, swelling, warmth or discharge. Many diabetics find it safer to have a podiatrist handle nail trimming going forward.
my eye got splashed with bleach while cleaning the bathroom, it stings like crazy. what do i do

Start flushing it right now with lukewarm running water from the tap or shower, holding the eyelid open, and keep going for a full 15 to 20 minutes even if it starts feeling better. Take out contact lenses if you wear them, but don't let that delay the rinsing. Bleach can injure the surface of the eye, so after flushing, get to urgent care or an ER or call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 in the US. If your vision is blurry or the pain is severe, go to the ER right away.
I'm 34, two kids under 5, and I cry in the car most days after drop-off. I love them but I feel like I'm drowning. Is this just what parenting is?

Feeling exhausted is normal with two little ones, but crying most days and feeling like you're drowning is a sign you're carrying more than you should, not just ordinary parenting. This could be depression or burnout, and both respond well to treatment, especially when caught early. Book an appointment with your GP and tell them exactly what you told me. If you have a partner or family nearby, ask for specific help this week, like one morning off.
I'm 72 and my doctor prescribed tramadol, but I also take duloxetine. The pharmacist flagged it. Should I worry?

The pharmacist was right to flag it. Tramadol and duloxetine both raise serotonin, so together they increase the risk of serotonin syndrome, and tramadol can also lower the seizure threshold. Doctors sometimes prescribe the combination deliberately at low doses, but call your doctor to confirm they're aware of it. Watch for agitation, sweating, tremor or a fast heartbeat, and seek urgent care if those appear.
Jellyfish stung my son at the beach, someone said to pee on it. Seriously?

Seriously, don't, because urine doesn't help and can actually make some stingers fire more venom. Rinse the area with seawater or vinegar, lift off any visible tentacles with tweezers or a gloved hand, then soak the area in hot water around 45°C (as hot as is comfortable without scalding) for 20 to 40 minutes to ease the pain. Get help right away if he has trouble breathing, chest pain, widespread swelling, or the sting covers a large area.
Baby hasn't moved much today, 33 weeks. I'm probably overthinking it right?

You're not overthinking it, because a reduction in your baby's movements is exactly the kind of thing maternity units want to hear about promptly. Call labor and delivery or your midwife now and don't wait until tomorrow. Drinking cold water or lying on your side is not a reliable test, and they would much rather check you and send you home reassured.
can i just take double the zyrtec if one isn't cutting it during pollen season

Don't double up on your own, because higher doses of cetirizine mostly add drowsiness without much extra relief for most people. A better move is to add a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, which works on a different part of the allergic response and is often more effective than antihistamines alone for hay fever. If you're still miserable after a week or two of consistent use, a doctor can adjust your plan or talk about allergy shots.
we have a cat, do i really have to stop doing the litter box

Yes, hand litter duty to someone else if you can, because cat feces can carry toxoplasmosis, which can harm a baby if you catch it for the first time during pregnancy. If you have to do it yourself, wear gloves, scoop daily (the parasite takes a day or more to become infectious), and wash your hands well afterward. You don't need to give up your cat, and petting and cuddling are fine. Wear gloves when gardening too, since soil can carry it.
My potassium was low on bloodwork. Can I just buy potassium pills off amazon and take a bunch?

Please don't self-treat with potassium pills. Too much potassium can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems, and the right dose depends on how low you are, your kidney function and any medications you're on. Call the doctor who ordered the bloodwork. They'll either prescribe a measured dose or recommend food changes and recheck your levels. Bananas, potatoes, beans and spinach are safe ways to add potassium in the meantime.
green snot for a week. need antibiotics right?

Not necessarily. Green or yellow mucus is just a sign of your immune system at work and happens with ordinary viral colds too. Most sinus infections clear up without antibiotics; doctors usually consider them if symptoms last more than 10 days without improving, are severe with high fever and facial pain, or get better and then worsen. Saline rinses, fluids and decongestants for a few days are your best bet for now.
Is it fine to drink apple cider vinegar for stomach pain? Saw it on TikTok

There's no good evidence that apple cider vinegar treats stomach pain, and because it's acidic it can make reflux, gastritis or ulcers worse. Drinking it straight can also erode your tooth enamel and irritate your throat. If you want a home remedy, ginger or peppermint tea has better support for nausea and cramping. If the stomach pain is recurring, it's worth finding out the cause rather than trying TikTok fixes.
Is creatine safe for teenagers? My son is 16 and plays football

Creatine monohydrate is one of the best-studied supplements, and short-term use looks safe in healthy older teens. Most pediatric groups still advise against performance supplements under 18, though, mainly because the long-term data is thin. A 16-year-old will gain far more from sleep, enough protein and consistent training than from creatine. If he's keen to try it, have him talk it over with his doctor, and stick to plain monohydrate at 3 to 5 grams a day, not pre-workout blends.
how much benadryl can i take to knock myself out, i havent slept in 2 days

Stick with the standard 25 to 50 mg dose. Taking more won't make you sleep better, and high doses of diphenhydramine can cause confusion, a racing heart, seizures and dangerous heart rhythms. Don't mix it with alcohol or other sedatives. Two days without sleep is worth a call to your doctor, and if you're feeling desperate or unsafe, call or text 988 or your local crisis line right away.
Bleeding gums when I brush and sometimes they ache. I just brush softer now so they don't bleed. good plan?

Gentle brushing is good, but bleeding gums usually mean early gum disease (gingivitis), which comes from plaque along the gumline, so avoiding those areas makes it worse. Keep brushing thoroughly with a soft brush twice a day and floss daily, and the bleeding typically settles in one to two weeks as the gums heal. Get a dental cleaning and checkup soon, and see someone sooner if the bleeding persists or comes with bruising elsewhere.
Can I still fly? I'm 35 weeks and my best friend's wedding is across the country.

Many airlines restrict travel after 36 weeks, and some want a doctor's note before that, so check your airline's rules and talk to your provider before you book. At 35 weeks there's also a real chance of going into labor far from your hospital and medical records. If your provider gives the green light, bring your prenatal records, walk the aisle often and wear compression socks to lower the clot risk.
migraine with vomiting, can't keep pills down. what now

When you can't keep tablets down, options that skip the stomach work better. Examples are sumatriptan nasal spray or injection, rizatriptan or zolmitriptan melt-on-the-tongue tablets, and anti-nausea medicine your doctor can prescribe. For now, rest in a dark room and take small sips of fluid. Go to urgent care if you can't keep any fluids down for many hours or the migraine lasts beyond three days.
My dad (78) slipped in the bathroom, he says he's fine but his hip hurts when he walks. He doesn't want to bother the doctor.

Hip pain after a fall at 78 needs to be checked today, even if he can walk. Some hip fractures still allow walking at first, and missing one can lead to serious complications. If he can't bear weight, his leg looks shorter or turned out, or he hit his head, call 911. Otherwise, take him to urgent care or the ER for an X-ray, especially if he's on blood thinners.
my lower back has been killing me since i helped my buddy move a couch on saturday. what should i do

That sounds like a classic muscle strain, and most of these settle within one to three weeks. Keep moving gently, because short walks and normal light activity heal a strained back faster than bed rest, and use ibuprofen or naproxen with food for a few days if they're safe for you. Heat for 15 to 20 minutes at a time usually feels better than ice after the first day or two. If the pain shoots down your leg below the knee, or if it isn't clearly improving after about two weeks, get it checked.
My doctor gave me azithromycin, the Z-pack, but it's only 5 days. Is that really enough??

Yes, it really is enough. Azithromycin stays in your tissues for days after the last pill, so a 5-day pack works about like a longer course of other antibiotics. Take it exactly as directed. You may keep improving after you finish. If you're not getting better by a few days after the last dose, or you're getting worse, check back with your doctor.
My dad is 78 and has had a cough with a fever for 3 days. Now he seems kind of confused. He says he's fine and doesn't want to go in.

New confusion in an older adult with a fever and cough is a warning sign and needs medical attention today, even if he insists he's fine. In older people, pneumonia or a serious infection often shows up as confusion before anything else. Take him to urgent care or the ER, and call 911 if he's breathing fast, has bluish lips, or is hard to wake. It's much better to be checked and sent home than to wait this one out.
is it bad to work out when recovering from a UTI

Light to moderate exercise is usually fine once you're on antibiotics and feeling better. Drink plenty of water, since staying hydrated helps flush the bladder. Skip hard workouts if you still have a fever, back pain or chills, which could mean the infection reached your kidneys and needs medical attention.
teen here, got braces tightened yesterday and everything aches. normal?

Totally normal, since teeth usually feel sore for two to four days after a tightening while they start shifting. Stick to soft foods like pasta, yogurt and smoothies for now. Acetaminophen or ibuprofen at the label dose for your age can help. Call your orthodontist if a wire is poking your cheek or the soreness lasts beyond a week.
quick q - how much benadryl to knock myself out, i really need to sleep tonight

The standard dose for adults is 25 to 50 mg, and going higher won't make you sleep better. It increases the risk of heart rhythm problems, confusion and a nasty hangover feeling. Benadryl also tends to work less well each night you use it, so it's fine as an occasional one-off but not a nightly fix. If sleep has been a real struggle for a while, talk to a doctor. Things like CBT for insomnia work better than any pill over the long run.
got some bleach splashed in my eye cleaning the bathroom

Rinse your eye right now under gently running lukewarm water for at least 15 to 20 minutes, holding the lid open, and take out any contact lens. Bleach can damage the eye, so after rinsing get checked at urgent care or the ER even if it feels better. You can also call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 for guidance while you flush.
burned my arm on the oven rack, should I put ice on it

Use cool running water instead, because ice can damage burned skin and cause frostbite-type injury. Keep it under the tap for about 20 minutes, then cover it loosely with a clean nonstick dressing. A painkiller like ibuprofen will help with the throbbing. Oven rack burns are usually small and superficial, but get it checked if it blisters a lot or looks white or leathery.
My son's 12 and has the flu. Can he take aspirin for the fever? It's all we have in the house.

No, don't give aspirin to anyone under 19 with flu or a viral illness, because it's linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition that affects the liver and brain. Pick up children's or regular acetaminophen or ibuprofen dosed by his weight instead. A pharmacist can help you get the dose right. Until then, fluids, light clothing and rest will help him feel more comfortable.
what's the fastest way to stop hiccups that have lasted 20 minutes

Try holding your breath for 10 to 20 seconds, then sipping ice-cold water slowly. Swallowing a teaspoon of sugar or gently pulling your knees to your chest can also reset the reflex. Twenty minutes is annoying but harmless. See a doctor only if hiccups last more than 48 hours or keep you from eating or sleeping.
I want to lose 15 lbs before a wedding in 3 weeks. Thinking water fast. Thoughts?

I'd skip the water fast. Much of the quick weight you'd lose is water and glycogen that comes right back, and fasting for days can cause dizziness, electrolyte problems and fainting, which are genuinely risky. In three weeks you can realistically lose around 4 to 6 pounds of real weight while looking and feeling noticeably better. To do that, cut back on alcohol and ultra-processed snacks, eat plenty of protein and vegetables, and walk daily. Cutting salt and alcohol in the last few days also reduces bloating a lot.
Someone online said I can get prednisone from a friend for my flared-up sciatica. Good idea?

Don't take someone else's prednisone. The research shows steroids give only modest benefit for sciatica, and the dose, duration and taper matter. They can also spike blood sugar and blood pressure, interact with other medications, and cause problems if you have conditions you haven't considered. Keep moving gently, use over-the-counter pain relievers as directed, and try heat. See your doctor, who can prescribe something appropriate, and go urgently if you develop leg weakness or bladder changes.
I have a mole on my back that my wife says looks bigger and kind of uneven at the edges now. Probably nothing, right?

A mole that is growing or developing irregular edges is exactly the kind of change that deserves a dermatologist's look soon, not a wait-and-see approach. Most changing moles turn out fine, but these are two of the classic warning signs for melanoma, which is very treatable when caught early. Have your wife snap a photo with a coin next to it for scale so you can track it, and book an appointment in the next few weeks.
Kid fell off his scooter, knee is a big scrape with gravel stuck in it. Do I need to get every bit out?

Yes, it's worth getting as much as you can out. Grit left in can cause infection and leave permanent dark marks called traumatic tattooing. Soak and rinse it under running water, then gently scrub with a soft cloth or use clean tweezers on the bigger bits. A painkiller beforehand helps. If the gravel is embedded deeply or he won't tolerate the cleaning, urgent care can numb it and clean it properly.
how much caffeine can i actually have

Most guidelines put the limit at 200 mg of caffeine a day in pregnancy, which works out to roughly one 12-ounce brewed coffee or two to three cups of tea. Remember that energy drinks, cola and chocolate also count toward the total. Staying under that limit is considered safe, so you don't have to give up your morning coffee.
My dad is 78 and has a low-grade fever and is acting confused, kind of out of it. He's usually sharp.

New confusion in an older adult with a fever needs to be evaluated today, ideally in an ER or urgent care. In elderly people, infections like a UTI, pneumonia, or sepsis often show up as confusion rather than a high temperature. Don't wait to see if it passes. If he's very drowsy, struggling to breathe, or can't stay awake, call 911.
itchy hands and feet like crazy at night, 34 wks. lotion isnt helping

Intense itching of the palms and soles in the third trimester, especially at night, can be a sign of cholestasis of pregnancy, a liver condition that needs monitoring. Call your provider soon and ask for a bile acid and liver function blood test. It's very manageable once diagnosed, but it does raise risks for the baby, so it's worth getting checked rather than just switching lotions.
I'm on sertraline and I want to try St John's wort too for an extra boost. Fine?

Don't combine them. St John's wort plus sertraline can cause serotonin syndrome, which brings agitation, sweating, tremor and a fast heart rate, and it can be serious. If you feel your sertraline isn't doing enough, tell your prescriber, because adjusting the dose or switching is much safer than adding supplements. Don't stop sertraline abruptly in the meantime.
Back pain for 6 weeks, losing weight without trying, history of breast cancer. Probably nothing right?

With your history, please don't wait this one out. Ongoing back pain combined with unexplained weight loss in someone who has had cancer needs prompt evaluation to rule out spread to the spine. Call your oncologist or doctor this week and describe exactly these symptoms. Go urgently if you develop leg weakness, numbness, or bladder or bowel changes. It may well turn out to be something benign, but this is a case where checking quickly really matters.
is it true caffeine helps headaches or is that a myth

It's real. Caffeine narrows blood vessels and boosts the effect of pain relievers, which is why it's in some headache medicines, and a cup of coffee early in a migraine helps some people. The catch is that regular heavy intake causes withdrawal headaches when you skip it, so keep it moderate and consistent.
my toddler keeps pulling at his ear and was fussy all night, low fever. ear infection?

That combination is pretty typical of an ear infection, especially if he's had a recent cold. Weight-appropriate children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen will help the pain and fever, and offering fluids and keeping him upright can make him more comfortable. Book a visit with his pediatrician to have his ears looked at, since many of these clear on their own but some need antibiotics. Seek care sooner if the fever goes above 39°C (102°F), he seems very unwell, or you see fluid draining from the ear.
Hi, I'm 68 and wear dentures. Lately there's a sore spot on my gum that won't heal. It's been about three weeks.

A denture sore spot that hasn't healed after two weeks should be looked at, so please book with your dentist soon. Often it's simply a pressure point that needs the denture adjusted. Any mouth sore lasting this long still needs a professional check to rule out anything more serious. Leaving the denture out as much as you can in the meantime will help the gum rest.
Feel like my heart is racing and bp is 90/55, I've had diarrhea all day.

That sounds like dehydration, which can lower your blood pressure and make your heart race to compensate. Sip oral rehydration solution or fluids with electrolytes steadily. Get medical care today if you can't keep fluids down, feel faint or confused, aren't urinating, or if your BP stays low or your heart keeps racing.
teenager here, my stomach hurts every morning before school but fine on weekends

That pattern often points to stress or anxiety, because your gut is closely connected to your nervous system and the pain is real even when the cause is emotional. Try eating something light for breakfast, building in some time to wind down, and thinking about whether something at school is weighing on you. Talking to a parent, school counselor or doctor is a smart move. They can rule out physical causes and help with whatever's going on.
whats a normal blood pressure

Under 120 over under 80 is considered normal for adults. From 120 to 129 systolic with a diastolic under 80 counts as elevated. Readings at 130/80 or higher on repeated measurements fall into the high blood pressure range. One reading doesn't define you, so it's the pattern over several days that matters.
quick q: yogurt or probiotics while on antibiotics, worth it?

It's reasonable and low-risk. Some probiotics, like Saccharomyces boulardii and certain Lactobacillus strains, have modest evidence for reducing antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Take them a couple of hours apart from your antibiotic dose. If you have a weakened immune system or a central line, check with your doctor first.
i think theres a metal shaving in my eye from grinding, it feels scratchy

Get to an eye doctor or urgent care today, because metal fragments from grinding can embed in the cornea and leave a rust ring within hours to a day. Don't rub the eye or dig at it. A gentle flush with clean water or saline is fine, but if the scratchy feeling persists, the fragment is likely stuck and needs removal with proper tools. Keep the eye closed on the way and wear safety glasses next time.
ugh gas pain so bad it feels like a stabbing in my chest. is that a thing?

Trapped gas can absolutely cause sharp, stabbing pain high in the belly or chest, and walking around, a heating pad, or simethicone (Gas-X) often helps it move. Chest pain can also be your heart, though. If the pain is pressure-like, spreads to your arm, jaw or back, or comes with shortness of breath, sweating or nausea, call emergency services rather than assuming it's gas.
I'm 7 months pregnant and have a bad toothache. Is it safe to go to the dentist?

Yes, dental care is safe and recommended during pregnancy, and an untreated infection is a bigger risk to you and the baby than the treatment. Local anesthetic and shielded X-rays are considered safe, so just tell the office you're pregnant. For pain in the meantime, acetaminophen is the usual choice, and you should avoid ibuprofen in the third trimester unless your OB says otherwise.
Can I put rice cereal in my 6 week old's bottle so she sleeps longer?

Please don't. Adding cereal to a bottle raises the risk of choking and overfeeding, and studies show it doesn't actually help babies sleep longer. At 6 weeks, waking at night to feed is normal and important, and solids shouldn't start until around 6 months. If she seems hungry all the time or isn't gaining weight, bring it up with her pediatrician.
hiccups and burping all day plus some stomach discomfort. weird but not terrible

That combination is usually from swallowed air or mild indigestion, often caused by eating fast, drinking carbonated drinks, chewing gum or eating a big meal. Slow down when you eat, skip fizzy drinks for a day, and try a short walk after meals. If it keeps happening for more than a couple of weeks, or you get chest pain, trouble swallowing or vomiting, see a doctor.
Spilled boiling water on my foot about an hour ago. Blisters about the size of my palm. I have work tomorrow, can I just wrap it?

A palm-sized blistering scald is bigger than I'd treat at home. Burns on the feet are also prone to infection and can make walking difficult while they heal. Run it under cool water for 20 minutes now if you haven't, since it still helps within a few hours. Then cover it loosely with cling film or a nonstick dressing and get it seen at urgent care today. A clinic can dress it properly and give you a work note if you need one.
burned my tongue on pizza lol anything to do

Sip cold water or let ice chips melt in your mouth for a few minutes, which takes the edge off. For the next day or two, stick to softer, cooler foods and skip spicy, acidic, or crunchy stuff. It usually heals within a few days on its own because mouth tissue repairs fast.
can i take ibuprofen and tylenol together for fever

Yes, they're different drugs, so you can take them together or alternate them, which often controls a stubborn fever better than either one alone. Just stick to each one's labeled dose and daily maximum. Take ibuprofen with food, and skip it if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, or you're on blood thinners. Keep track of the times you take each dose so you don't double up by accident.
Mom gets really dizzy when she stands up from the couch. She's 76 and on blood pressure meds.

That sounds like orthostatic hypotension, where blood pressure drops on standing, and blood pressure meds are a common culprit. Have her sit at the edge of the couch for a few seconds, then rise slowly and hold onto something steady. Make sure she's drinking enough. Let her doctor know soon, because a dose adjustment often fixes it, and these dizzy spells are a leading cause of falls at her age.
i'm on lithium, can i take ibuprofen for a toothache?

Check with your prescriber first, because ibuprofen and other NSAIDs can raise lithium levels into a toxic range by reducing how much your kidneys clear. Acetaminophen is the safer pick for the toothache. Book a dentist visit to deal with the cause. If you ever notice tremor, nausea, diarrhea or confusion while on lithium, get your levels checked promptly.
Lump in my armpit that hurts, came after shaving. Should I squeeze it?

Don't squeeze it, because a painful lump after shaving is usually an inflamed hair follicle or a small boil, and squeezing can push the infection deeper. Apply warm compresses for 10 to 15 minutes several times a day and take a break from shaving that side. If it grows, becomes very painful, you get a fever, or it lasts more than a week or two, see a doctor. Also see a doctor about any painless lump that sticks around, because it should be checked.
Is it ok to drink alcohol on blood pressure meds? Just a couple beers on weekends.

A couple of beers on the weekend is generally fine for most people on BP medication. Alcohol can add to the pressure-lowering effect, though, so you may feel more lightheaded than usual, especially when you stand up. Heavier drinking raises blood pressure over time and works against your meds, so keeping it moderate is the right call.
Kid swallowed one of those button batteries maybe?? not sure. she seems fine

Treat this as an emergency and go to the ER now, even though she seems fine. Button batteries can burn through the esophagus within two hours without any early symptoms. If she's over a year old and you can do it on the way, give 2 teaspoons of honey every 10 minutes to help slow the damage. Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 for guidance on the way, and bring the battery packaging if you have it.
tension headache from desk work, any tricks

Raise your screen to eye level, keep your shoulders down, and get up every 30 to 45 minutes to roll your neck and stretch. Heat on your neck and shoulders and gently massaging your temples and the base of your skull can ease a tension headache, along with water and the occasional standard dose of a pain reliever. If they're happening most days, a physiotherapist can sort out posture problems that keep feeding them.
can I use coconut oil drops for my kid's ear infection instead of going to the doctor

I wouldn't put oils in a child's ear when an infection is suspected, because if the eardrum has a hole, anything you put in can cause problems, and oil doesn't treat the infection. Many mild ear infections do clear up on their own, and children's ibuprofen or acetaminophen dosed by weight plus a warm compress outside the ear can ease the pain. See the doctor if your child is under two, has a high fever, has fluid draining, seems very unwell, or isn't improving after two to three days.
My kid's school wants a written asthma plan. Is that really necessary or just paperwork?

It's genuinely useful, because it tells staff exactly which symptoms to watch for, how many rescue puffs to give, and when to call 911, so nobody has to guess during an attack. Your child's doctor can fill one out quickly, usually on a standard green, yellow and red zone form. Also ask whether your child can carry their own inhaler or whether a spare one should be kept at school. Ten minutes of paperwork now can prevent a dangerous delay later.
is it ok to take like 5000 IU vitamin D every day? my friend does it

For many adults 5000 IU a day is above what they need, and since vitamin D is fat-soluble it can build up over months and push calcium levels too high. The usual upper limit for adults is 4000 IU unless a doctor has found a deficiency and prescribed more. The smartest move is a simple blood test for 25-hydroxy vitamin D, which tells you whether you need a supplement at all and how much.
Quick q, my kid has a honey-colored crusty sore by his nose that's spreading. Neosporin enough?

Honey-colored crusts that spread sound like impetigo, a bacterial skin infection that's very common in kids and quite contagious. It usually needs a prescription antibiotic ointment like mupirocin, or oral antibiotics if it's widespread, so call his pediatrician. Meanwhile, gently wash it with soap and water, keep his nails short, and don't share towels.
teenage daughter has a bunch of small red bumps on her upper arms that never go away, rough like sandpaper

That sounds like keratosis pilaris, a very common, harmless condition where keratin plugs the hair follicles. It often improves with age. A moisturiser containing urea, lactic acid or salicylic acid, used daily, will smooth the bumps noticeably over a few weeks. She shouldn't scrub hard or pick, since that makes the redness worse. If it's itchy, spreading or not responding, a GP can confirm it and suggest stronger options.
torn meniscus confirmed on MRI. surgeon wants to scope it. do i actually need surgery?

Not always, because for many degenerative meniscus tears in middle-aged and older adults, physical therapy works about as well as arthroscopy. Surgery makes more sense for tears from an acute injury in younger people, or when the knee locks or catches mechanically. It's completely reasonable to ask your surgeon why they recommend it for your tear specifically, whether a trial of PT first is an option, or to get a second opinion.
Can I take ibuprofen and Tylenol together for a migraine?

Yes, ibuprofen and acetaminophen work differently and can be taken together or alternated, and the combination often works better than either one alone. Stick to the label doses, which for most adults means no more than 3,000 to 4,000 mg of acetaminophen a day, counting any cold medicines that also contain it. Take ibuprofen with food. Skip it if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, or take blood thinners.
I work in finance and I'm thinking of buying modafinil online to get through the next few months. Everyone does it.

I'd advise against it. Online modafinil is unregulated, so you can't be sure what you're taking. It can also cause insomnia, anxiety, a racing heart and, rarely, serious skin reactions. Even if it works, it just masks exhaustion that comes back harder. If the workload is unsustainable, that's worth tackling directly, and if you're struggling to focus, a doctor can assess you properly.
60 y/o, had shingles, rash is healing. Can I go back to the gym?

Wait until the blisters have fully crusted over before going back, since shingles can spread the chickenpox virus to people who aren't immune. Once you're there, start with lighter workouts and avoid anything that rubs or irritates the healing area. If you have lingering nerve pain, gentle exercise is usually fine, but check with your doctor about managing it.
been feeling a pounding headache and blurry vision, home cuff says 195/120. I don't have a ride

Call emergency services now. Pressure that high with headache and vision changes can mean a hypertensive emergency that can damage your brain, eyes, or heart. Don't drive yourself. Sit down, don't take any extra pills unless a professional tells you to, and keep your door unlocked if you're alone.
is melatonin ok to take every night for stress insomnia? im 22

Low-dose melatonin is generally safe short-term, and 0.5 to 3 mg is usually plenty, since more isn't better. It's better at shifting sleep timing than at fixing stress-driven insomnia, though. For that, the most effective treatment is CBT for insomnia, which you can do through apps or books. If you're still struggling after a few weeks, see a doctor rather than relying on nightly supplements indefinitely.
Woke up with sharp chest pain that's worse lying flat and better leaning forward. Had a cold last week. 31M.

Pain that's worse lying flat and eases when you lean forward, coming after a viral illness, is a classic pattern for pericarditis, inflammation of the lining around the heart. It's usually treatable, but it needs a proper diagnosis with an ECG and exam, and occasionally the heart muscle itself is involved. Get seen today at urgent care or the ER rather than waiting it out. Avoid strenuous exercise until a doctor clears you.
can i use hydrogen peroxide to clean a cut

It's better not to. Hydrogen peroxide and rubbing alcohol damage healthy tissue and can slow healing. Rinsing well with clean running water and mild soap around the wound does the job better. Afterward, a thin layer of petroleum jelly and a bandage keep it moist and protected.
Had shingles, rash is healing. Playing tennis this weekend with friends ok?

If the blisters have fully crusted over, you're no longer contagious, and light tennis is generally fine if you feel up to it. Cover any healing areas so sweat and friction don't irritate them. Shingles can leave you more tired than you'd expect, so keep the match casual. If you've had lingering nerve pain, let your comfort guide how hard you play.
I'm 22 weeks pregnant and have 38.3 fever with body aches. Can I just rest?

Call your OB or midwife today rather than just resting. Fever in pregnancy should be evaluated, both to find the cause, like flu or a urinary infection, and because a sustained high temperature isn't great for the baby. Acetaminophen is generally the preferred fever reducer in pregnancy, while ibuprofen is usually avoided. Ask your provider to confirm before taking anything.
Worried. Hypoglycemia at 54 just now, ate juice, now at 88. Do I need to go anywhere?

You handled it well, and at 88 and climbing you usually don't need to go anywhere. Now eat a small snack with some protein and carbs, like crackers and peanut butter, so you don't drop again, and recheck in about an hour. Think about what caused it, such as a skipped meal, extra exercise or too much insulin, and tell your diabetes team if lows are happening more often. Go in if you become confused, can't keep your sugar up, or you take a long-acting sulfonylurea like glipizide, because those lows can come back.
my 9 year old had a high fever and was sick all weekend, now she's begging to go to her gymnastics class wed. ok?

If she's been fever-free for at least 24 hours without fever medicine, is eating and drinking normally and has her usual energy, Wednesday is probably fine. Let the coach know she's just recovered so they can let her take breaks. If she's still tired, pale or not eating well, one more rest day is the kinder choice.
Elderberry syrup for my kid's flu instead of Tamiflu? Prefer natural.

Elderberry isn't a substitute for Tamiflu. Evidence for it is limited, while oseltamivir is proven to shorten flu and reduce complications, especially when started within 48 hours. If your pediatrician has recommended Tamiflu, follow that, and ask whether elderberry is fine alongside it. Get care quickly if your child has trouble breathing, won't drink, seems very lethargic, or gets better and then suddenly worse.
I get stomach aches before every exam. is that real or in my head

It's real, and it's also connected to your head. The gut and brain are wired closely together, and stress hormones genuinely change gut movement and sensitivity. Slow breathing, a light familiar breakfast and less caffeine on exam days help a lot of people. If the aches happen outside stressful times too, or affect your bowels or appetite, check in with a doctor.
can I just double up my rizatriptan if the first one didn't work

Don't double up at once. With rizatriptan, the usual approach is a second dose only after at least 2 hours, and no more than the daily maximum on your prescription, which is often 30 mg for adults but may be lower if you take propranolol. If the first dose truly didn't help at all, a second often won't either. Ask your doctor about adjusting the plan or adding an anti-inflammatory.
is cracking my back bad for me? i do it like 20 times a day

Cracking your back isn't known to cause arthritis, and the pop is just gas releasing in the joint. Doing it 20 times a day suggests you're chasing a feeling of stiffness, though, and regular movement, stretching, and core strengthening usually address that better. Avoid forceful twisting or having friends crack it for you. See someone if the urge comes with real pain.
Got a red streak going up my arm from a cut on my hand. Kind of weird. Probably fine right?

That's not one to wait on, because a red streak spreading from a wound can mean the infection is traveling through your lymphatic system. Get seen today at urgent care or the ER, since this usually needs prompt antibiotics and responds well when caught early. Go straight to the ER if you have fever, chills or feel faint.
can i just use my husband's leftover antibiotic eye drops for my pink eye?

Don't use them. Most pink eye is viral and antibiotics won't help it, and drops that have been opened for a while can be contaminated. Some prescription eye drops also contain steroids, which can make certain infections, like herpes of the eye, much worse. A quick visit to a pharmacist or doctor will tell you what you actually have, and in the meantime, cool compresses and good handwashing go a long way.
after a bad sinus infection, my ears still feel blocked. can I go scuba diving on my trip next week?

I'd hold off on diving until your ears feel completely clear. Blocked ears mean you may not be able to equalize pressure, which can cause a painful ear barotrauma or even a burst eardrum underwater. Snorkeling at the surface is a safe alternative for now. If they're still blocked a few days before the trip, see a doctor, ideally one familiar with diving, to check your ears and sinuses before you go.
Mom (76) fell in the bathroom last night, says she's fine, no visible injuries. Do I need to do anything?

Yes. Even with no visible injury, an older adult who falls should be watched for the next day or two for new confusion, worsening headache, drowsiness, vomiting or pain when standing or walking, and any of those means going to the ER. This matters even more if she takes a blood thinner or hit her head, because bleeding inside the skull can show up hours later. Either way, tell her doctor about the fall, because falls often have a fixable cause like medication side effects, low blood pressure or poor vision. Grab bars and a non-slip mat in the bathroom are worth installing this week.
I fell on my belly on the ice, 29 weeks, feel okay though. Need to go in?

Yes, call labor and delivery and expect to be asked to come in, even though you feel fine. A direct blow to the belly can occasionally cause the placenta to separate without obvious symptoms at first, and they will usually monitor the baby for a few hours. If you're Rh negative, you may also need an anti-D injection.
Throbbing toothache, swollen face, and now it's hard to swallow and my voice sounds weird. I'll call the dentist Monday

Please don't wait until Monday, and go to the emergency room now. Trouble swallowing and a change in your voice along with a swollen face can mean a dental infection is spreading into your neck, which can threaten your airway and needs IV antibiotics and drainage quickly. If you have any difficulty breathing, call emergency services.
how long can a human go without sleep, asking for a game jam lol

The record is about 11 days, but please don't test it. After just 24 hours awake, your reaction time and judgment are comparable to being legally drunk, and by 48 hours you'll have microsleeps and possibly hallucinations. For a game jam, you'll ship better code by sleeping at least 4 to 6 hours a night or taking a couple of 90-minute naps. And don't drive home after a sleepless jam.
I'm a nurse doing 12 hour nights and I feel numb and irritable all the time. Is this burnout or am I depressed?

It could be either, and the two overlap a lot. Burnout usually eases when you get real time off, while depression tends to follow you into days off and holidays with low mood and loss of interest. Rotating 12-hour nights also wreck sleep, which on its own drives numbness and irritability. Talk to your GP or occupational health, because they can screen for depression and support changes to your rota, and you shouldn't wait until you're running on empty.
Detailed question: lower right molar, dull ache for 2 weeks, worse lying down at night, mild sensitivity to hot that lingers 30+ seconds. No swelling. Dentist can see me in 10 days. OK to wait?

Hot sensitivity that lingers and pain that gets worse lying down point to an inflamed nerve that probably won't recover, which often ends in a root canal. Waiting ten days without swelling is often survivable, but ask to go on the cancellation list or call other offices, because these cases can turn into an abscess. Manage it with ibuprofen at label doses and sleep with your head raised, and get seen urgently if swelling, fever or a bad taste shows up.
My husband has oxycodone left over from his surgery. My back is wrecked from moving furniture. One won't hurt right?

Please don't take it. Even one dose of someone else's opioid can be dangerous, especially combined with alcohol, sleep aids or anxiety medication, and it's not prescribed for your body or situation. For a strained back, alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen, heat, and gentle movement usually work well. See a doctor if the pain is severe or shoots down your leg. It's also worth dropping his leftover pills at a pharmacy take-back so they don't sit around the house.
When do I actually need stitches?

Get a cut seen if it's deeper than about a quarter inch or so, the edges gape apart, or it won't stop bleeding after 10 to 15 minutes of firm pressure. Go in too if it's on the face, a joint, the hands or the genitals, or if it was caused by something dirty or a bite. Aim to be seen within a few hours, since wounds are much easier to close cleanly early on.
My friend has leftover oxycodone from her surgery and offered it for my sciatica. It's just a few pills, is that okay?

I'd turn that down, since taking someone else's opioid prescription isn't safe or legal, even for a few doses. Oxycodone can interact dangerously with alcohol, sleep aids, and other medications. It also isn't very effective for sciatica compared with other approaches. A doctor can offer things that actually target nerve pain, such as specific medications, physical therapy, or sometimes a steroid injection, so it's worth booking an appointment if over-the-counter options aren't enough.
I get migraines with aura and I'm about to start the pill. Anything I should know?

Yes, tell your prescriber about the aura specifically. Combined pills containing estrogen raise stroke risk in people who get migraine with aura, so they're generally not recommended for you. Progestogen-only pills, implants and IUDs are usually safe alternatives.
Is it safe to take baking soda in water for indigestion? My grandma always did.

Half a teaspoon dissolved in a full glass of water works as an occasional antacid for most healthy adults. It's high in sodium, though, so it's a poor choice if you have high blood pressure, heart or kidney problems, or are pregnant. Never take it on a very full stomach or in large amounts, because there are rare reports of stomach rupture. If you need it regularly, a proper antacid and a doctor's look at the cause are better options.
I grind my teeth at night, my jaw hurts every morning. What do I do?

See your dentist, because a custom night guard protects your teeth and often eases the jaw pain, and they can check for damage. Stress, caffeine, alcohol and sometimes sleep apnea can drive grinding, so it's worth addressing those too. A warm compress and gentle jaw stretches in the morning help with soreness. Over-the-counter guards can be a stopgap, but a fitted one usually works much better.
18f. my lips swelled up for no reason this morning, no hives, no new food. went down after a few hours. weird?

Episodes of lip swelling like this are called angioedema. Sometimes they happen without an obvious trigger, but they're worth looking into, especially if they recur. Note anything new: medications (including NSAIDs like ibuprofen), cosmetics, lip products, or stress. See your doctor or an allergist, because some forms are hereditary and treated differently. If swelling ever involves your tongue or throat, or makes breathing or swallowing hard, call emergency services right away.
my 9yo has asthma and her inhaler is empty, the pharmacy is closed till monday. she's fine right now

Don't wait until Monday, since an asthma flare can come on fast. Call her doctor's after-hours line, which can often send an emergency refill to a 24-hour pharmacy. In many places, pharmacists can also supply an emergency inhaler. If she starts struggling to breathe, can't speak full sentences, or her lips look bluish, call emergency services immediately.
Can I fly tomorrow with a bad head cold? Big trip, nonrefundable.

You usually can, but congestion makes ear pain during descent much more likely. Take an oral decongestant about an hour before landing if it's safe for you (check with a pharmacist if you have high blood pressure or heart issues), and chew gum or swallow during descent. If you have a fever or feel genuinely ill, flying is rougher on you and riskier for those around you, so consider at least wearing a mask. Severe ear pain, or a fever that lingers after the trip, is worth getting checked.
can i use my grandma's leftover eye drops for my pink eye, they're antibiotic ones

Don't use them, even if they're antibiotic. Most pink eye is viral and antibiotics won't touch it, and an opened bottle can be expired or contaminated. Some eye drops also contain steroids, which can make certain infections like herpes much worse. If your eye has thick yellow-green discharge, real pain, or blurry vision, get it checked so you get the right treatment if you actually need one.
my heart races to like 180 out of nowhere then suddenly stops racing. happens every couple months. im 30

Sudden-on, sudden-off episodes at that rate sound a lot like supraventricular tachycardia, a common and very treatable rhythm problem, but it needs a proper diagnosis. See your doctor and ask about a heart monitor so they can catch an episode, and try to record one on a smartwatch ECG or at urgent care if it happens again. Get emergency care during an episode if you feel faint, have chest pain, get short of breath, or it doesn't stop within about 15 to 20 minutes.
Got bleach splashed in my eye cleaning the bathroom. It burns. What do I do??

Start flushing your eye right now with lukewarm running water from the tap or shower and keep going for at least 15 minutes, holding the lid open and rolling your eye around. Take out contact lenses if you're wearing them, but don't stop rinsing to search for them. Chemical splashes can damage the cornea fast, so after rinsing, go to an ER or urgent eye care even if it feels better, and call poison control if you need guidance on the way.
my tooth has been throbbing for 3 days and now my cheek is swollen and warm. can i just wait till monday for my dentist?

Facial swelling with warmth on top of a throbbing tooth usually means an abscess that's spreading, and that shouldn't wait for the weekend to pass. Call your dentist's emergency line or go to urgent care today so you can get assessed and likely started on antibiotics. Go to the ER right away if the swelling spreads toward your eye or neck, or if you get a fever, trouble swallowing or trouble breathing.
Can asthma just go away? I'm 24 and haven't needed my inhaler in two years.

Asthma can go quiet for years, particularly when it started in childhood, but the underlying tendency often remains and can return with a bad cold, allergies or smoke. Keep an in-date rescue inhaler around anyway, because an attack without one is the real risk. If you're on a daily controller, talk to your doctor before dropping it. A lung function test can also show how you're really doing.
My pet snake bit me. Not venomous, ball python. Bleeding a little from lots of tiny holes.

Ball python bites look dramatic but are usually minor. Wash it with soap and running water and check that no tiny teeth were left in the skin, since they can break off. Keep it clean and covered, and watch for signs of infection like spreading redness or pus. Reptiles commonly carry salmonella, so wash your hands well after handling. Make sure your tetanus shot is current too.
can i pop a pimple on my nose with a needle if i sterilize it first

It's better to leave it, especially on your nose. That area drains into veins near the brain, so infections there are worth avoiding, and needle-popping often pushes bacteria deeper and leaves a mark. A warm compress for 10 minutes a few times a day plus a benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid spot treatment will usually bring it down in a few days. A hydrocolloid pimple patch also helps it drain on its own if it comes to a head.
My EpiPen expired 3 months ago. I can't afford a new one right now, is it still usable in an emergency?

In a real emergency, use the expired pen if it's the only one you have. Studies show recently expired epinephrine still delivers most of its dose, which beats nothing. Then call emergency services, because you'll need monitoring either way. Don't plan around it long term, though. Ask your doctor about generic epinephrine auto-injectors, manufacturer savings programs, or the Auvi-Q and neffy patient assistance options, which can bring the cost way down.
type 1 diabetic, just over a stomach virus. anything special to watch for when I start exercising again?

Yes, after a stomach virus your blood sugar can be more unpredictable, especially if you've been eating less or been dehydrated. Check your glucose before, during and after exercise, carry fast-acting carbs, and start with short, easy sessions until your eating and insulin needs are back to normal. Make sure you're well hydrated before you start. If you have ketones or keep getting lows or highs, hold off and talk to your diabetes care team.
found a guy online selling 'homeopathic vaccine' drops for kids, cheaper and no needles. legit?

Not legit. Homeopathic "nosodes" contain essentially no active ingredient and don't produce any immunity, so a child who takes them instead of real vaccines has no protection against measles, whooping cough or anything else. They aren't approved as vaccines anywhere. Ask your pediatrician about free vaccine programs if cost is the issue, and ask about ways to make needles easier for your kid.
toddler fell off the couch and hit his head, cried right away, now playing. do i need to do anything

Crying right away and then going back to normal play is reassuring, and most couch falls like this turn out fine. Watch him closely for the next 24 hours, and you can let him nap, though check that he wakes up normally. Go to the ER if he vomits more than once, seems unusually sleepy or confused, has trouble walking, has clear fluid coming from his nose or ears, or develops a soft, squishy swelling on his head.
I keep getting fevers after my dog bit me two days ago, the bite is red and swelling

That sounds like the bite is infected, and dog bites can go downhill quickly. See a doctor today, at urgent care or the ER. You'll likely need prescription antibiotics, and they'll check whether you need a tetanus shot and whether rabies is a concern. Go to the ER if the redness is spreading fast, you see red streaks, or you feel very unwell.
I keep falling asleep at red lights on my drive home from night shift. Any tips to stay awake?

Falling asleep at red lights means you're already too impaired to be driving, so the real answer is not to push through. Take a 20-minute nap in your car or the break room before leaving, or use a rideshare or carpool on the bad days. Caffeine about 30 minutes before the drive can help, but windows down and loud music don't work. If this happens regularly, talk to your doctor about shift work disorder or possible sleep apnea, because this is a crash waiting to happen.
I'm 34 and I've had sharp pain on the lower right side of my belly since last night, it's worse when I walk. Probably gas right?

Sharp lower right pain that gets worse when you walk is the classic pattern for appendicitis, so please don't write this off as gas. Go to urgent care or the ER today, especially if you have fever, nausea or loss of appetite, or if it hurts more when you press and then let go. Don't take laxatives or use a heating pad in the meantime. If it turns out to be gas, great, but this is one where getting checked quickly really matters.
Is it okay to use hydrogen peroxide on a scrape? My mom always did.

Lots of moms did, but it's no longer recommended because peroxide damages the healthy tissue that's trying to heal. Rinse the scrape well under running water with mild soap, pick out any grit, then put on a thin layer of petroleum jelly and a bandage. Keeping it moist and covered helps it heal faster and scar less than letting it dry out.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and my molar is killing me. Is it even safe to see a dentist right now??

Yes, seeing a dentist while pregnant is safe and important, and leaving a tooth infection untreated is riskier for you and the baby than treatment is. Tell them how far along you are so they can choose pregnancy-safe anesthetic, position you comfortably and use shielding if they need X-rays. For pain in the meantime acetaminophen is the usual choice, but avoid ibuprofen in the third trimester, and call your OB if you're unsure about any medication.
Is it normal for my stool to be black? I started taking iron pills last week.

Yes, iron supplements commonly turn stool dark green or black, and so does Pepto-Bismol, so this is very likely just the pills. Iron stool is usually dark and fairly formed. Black stool that is sticky, tar-like and foul-smelling, especially with dizziness, weakness or stomach pain, can mean bleeding and needs prompt medical attention.
ugh lice. can I just use the dog flea shampoo, its basically the same stuff

Please don't. Pet products are formulated and dosed for animals and can be harmful on a child's scalp. Use an over-the-counter lice treatment such as permethrin 1%, following the label exactly, and comb the hair thoroughly with a fine-toothed nit comb every few days for two weeks. If that fails, a pharmacist or doctor can recommend prescription options that work well against resistant lice.
Stepped on a rusty nail in the garage. Went in maybe half an inch. Last tetanus shot was... no idea, high school? I'm 41.

Let it bleed briefly, wash it well with soap and running water, and cover it with a clean bandage. You definitely need a tetanus booster since it's been well over 10 years, so get one today or tomorrow at urgent care, a clinic or a pharmacy that offers it. Puncture wounds also infect easily, so get seen promptly if you notice spreading redness, warmth, pus or fever over the next few days.
do those migraine glasses with the pink tint actually do anything

They help some people. FL-41 tinted lenses filter wavelengths that tend to trigger light sensitivity, and some small studies show fewer and milder attacks in light-sensitive migraine sufferers. They're cheap and harmless to try, but they're an add-on, not a replacement for proper treatment.
sliced the tip of my finger off, just a little chunk, like pea sized. bleeding wont stop

Hold firm pressure on the fingertip with a clean cloth, keep your hand raised above your heart, and don't let up for a full 10 to 15 minutes. If it's still bleeding after that, or you're unsure about bone or nail involvement, head to urgent care. If you have the piece of tissue, wrap it in damp gauze, seal it in a bag, and put that bag on ice to bring along. Small pea-sized tips often heal well on their own once the bleeding is controlled.
can i take my sleeping pill with a glass of wine just this once

Please don't, even once. Alcohol and sleeping pills both depress the brain and breathing, and together they can cause dangerous sedation, memory blackouts, falls or complex sleep behaviors like sleep-driving. If you've already had the wine, skip the pill tonight. A rough night of sleep is far safer than that combination.
is it dehydration if I get headaches during long runs

Dehydration is a common cause, but exertion itself can trigger headaches, as can low blood sugar, heat, and tight goggles or hats. Drink before and during runs, use electrolytes for anything over an hour, eat something beforehand and warm up gradually. If the headaches come on suddenly and severely, or if this is a new pattern, see a doctor, since exertional headaches occasionally have an underlying cause worth checking.
Can I get a decongestant for my cold? I have high bp but it's controlled.

Skip pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine, the decongestants in most cold pills, because they can raise your blood pressure. Saline spray, steam, and products labeled for people with high blood pressure are safer choices. Ask the pharmacist to point you to the right options.
my toddler pulled a pot handle and got hot coffee on his arm. he's screaming. area is red with a couple small blisters

Get his arm under cool running water right now and keep it there for 20 minutes, taking off any clothing or jewelry near the burn unless it's stuck. Blistering burns on small children should be checked by a doctor the same day, because their skin is thin and burns can be deeper than they look. Cover it loosely with clean plastic wrap and head to urgent care or the ER. Go to the ER for sure if the burn is larger than his palm or involves the face, hands, or genitals.
quick q are blue light glasses necessary or a scam

There's no good evidence that blue light from screens damages your eyes, and studies haven't shown that blue light glasses reduce eye strain much. Screen fatigue mostly comes from staring and blinking less, so the 20-20-20 rule helps: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Artificial tears and a well-set-up screen help too, and if strain persists, an eye exam can catch an outdated prescription.
shoulder hurts when i lift my arm above my head, been a month

Pain lifting your arm overhead that lasts a month is often rotator cuff irritation or impingement, which usually responds well to physical therapy. Avoid painful overhead movements for now but keep the shoulder moving within comfortable ranges, since total rest can lead to stiffness. See a doctor or physio if it's not improving, if it wakes you at night, or if your arm feels weak. Also see one if this started with a fall or injury, since that could be a tear.
i'm 72 and i nap for like 2 hours every afternoon, then can't sleep at night. normal?

That's a very common cycle, and a long afternoon nap is likely eating into your nighttime sleep drive. Try trimming naps to 20 to 30 minutes and taking them before about 2 or 3 pm, and get outdoor light and some activity in the morning. If you feel like you need a long nap despite a full night's sleep, mention it to your doctor. Heavy daytime sleepiness can come from sleep apnea, medications, low thyroid or other treatable issues.
worst headache of my life came on like a thunderclap about 20 min ago, should i just sleep it off??

Don't sleep this one off. A sudden, explosive headache that peaks within a minute or so can signal bleeding in the brain, and it needs emergency evaluation right now. Call 911 or get someone to drive you to the ER immediately, and don't drive yourself.
Teenager's tooth got knocked out in a hockey game, it's a permanent tooth. Coach says put it in milk?

Milk is a good call, and speed matters a lot here since the tooth has the best chance of being saved if it's back in within about an hour. Pick it up by the crown, not the root, and if it's dirty rinse it briefly in milk or saline without scrubbing. If your teen is calm, the best option is to gently push it back into the socket and have them bite on gauze. Otherwise keep it in milk, or in the cheek, and get to an emergency dentist or ER right now.
Why do my allergies get worse at night?

Lying flat lets mucus pool and congestion build. Your bedroom is also often packed with dust mites in your pillows and mattress, plus pet dander if animals sleep with you. Pollen that settles on your hair during the day can transfer to your pillow too. Showering before bed, using allergen-proof pillow and mattress covers, washing bedding hot weekly, and taking your antihistamine or nasal spray in the evening usually make a noticeable difference.
I want to lose 15 lbs in two weeks for a wedding. Thinking water fast. Thoughts?

A two-week water fast is a bad idea. You'd lose muscle and risk dizziness, fainting, electrolyte problems, and gallstones, and most of the quick weight comes back as water as soon as you eat again. Realistically, cutting back on salt, alcohol, and refined carbs, eating plenty of protein and vegetables, and sleeping well can drop a few pounds of bloat and help you look and feel noticeably better by the wedding. Fifteen pounds of actual fat in two weeks isn't achievable safely.
Can stress actually cause stomach pain or is that made up?

It's very real, because your gut and brain are tightly connected through nerves and stress hormones. Stress can speed up or slow down digestion, increase sensitivity to pain, and trigger cramps, nausea or diarrhea. Regular exercise, sleep, and techniques like slow breathing really do help. Still, if you have persistent pain, have it checked rather than assuming it's stress, especially if it wakes you at night or comes with weight loss.
Worried sick. My BP has been creeping up — 132/84, 135/86, 134/85 this month. Am I heading for a stroke??

Those numbers are mildly elevated, not alarming, and you're far from immediate stroke territory. They're a useful early warning, and this is the stage where lifestyle changes work best. Cut back on salt, move more, limit alcohol, and look at sleep and stress. Book a routine visit with your doctor to go over your overall risk, but there's no need to panic.
Fever of 101 but I have a race on Sunday that I paid for. Ibuprofen and go?

Please don't race with a fever, and masking it with ibuprofen makes things riskier, not safer. Exercising hard with a fever raises your risk of dehydration and heat illness, and if a virus is involved, it can strain your heart. Many races allow deferrals or transfers, so check that option first. If the fever is gone by Sunday, you might jog it easily, but if it isn't, sit this one out.
is it normal for my 18 month old to only say like 3 words

At 18 months, many kids have somewhere around 10 to 20 words, so 3 is on the lower end and worth bringing up with your pediatrician. It's often just a late talker. Still, an early hearing check and a speech evaluation are easy to arrange and make a real difference if help is needed. In the meantime, narrate your day, read together, and give him chances to respond. Pay attention to whether he understands simple instructions and points to show you things, since that's useful information for the doctor.
My 4 year old just grabbed the oven door and has a red mark across her palm. She's crying. What do I do right now?

Hold her hand under cool running water for 20 minutes. It feels long, but it really limits the damage. Don't use ice, butter or toothpaste. Afterward, cover it loosely with a clean non-stick dressing and give a child's dose of acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain. Because burns on a young child's palm can affect how the hand heals, call her doctor today, and go in right away if it blisters, looks white or leathery, or covers more than a small area.
can elderly people get heatstroke easily? my nana doesn't have AC and it's 95 out

Yes, older adults are especially vulnerable because their bodies regulate heat poorly and some medications make it worse. In that heat without air conditioning, get her somewhere cool for at least part of the day, like a cooling center, library or your home, since fans alone aren't enough at that temperature. Keep her drinking fluids and check on her often. Confusion, a racing pulse, hot dry skin or fainting mean calling emergency services.
Is it safe to use my friend's Ambien just for one night before a big interview?

Don't take someone else's prescription, even for one night. Zolpidem can cause next-morning grogginess, memory gaps and even sleep-walking or sleep-driving behaviors, and you don't know how your body will react before the most important morning of your week. It can also interact badly with alcohol and other medications. You're better off with a wind-down routine, a cool dark room, and the reassurance that one night of imperfect sleep rarely hurts performance as much as people fear.
My 15 year old daughter has started wearing long sleeves all the time even when it's hot and she's been really withdrawn. I'm scared she's cutting. How do I bring it up without making it worse?

Your instinct to approach this carefully is right. Pick a calm, private moment and say something like "I've noticed you seem down lately and I'm worried about you, and I love you no matter what." Lead with concern, not with demands to see her arms. If she does tell you she's self-harming, stay as calm as you can, thank her for telling you, and avoid punishment or panic, because those tend to push it underground. Either way, book her in with her doctor or a counselor soon. If there are any deep wounds, or any sign she's thinking about suicide, get urgent help the same day.
I have a cat allergy but my girlfriend has two cats. Moving in next month. Any hacks?

Plenty of people manage this well with a combination of tactics. Keep the cats out of the bedroom, run a HEPA air purifier, vacuum with a HEPA vacuum often, and wash bedding weekly in hot water. Daily antihistamines and a steroid nasal spray can help a lot. If you have asthma or your symptoms are significant, see an allergist before you move, since allergy shots can meaningfully reduce cat allergy over time.
Pain in my upper back teeth started with a cold and gets worse when I bend over. Cavity?

That pattern sounds more like a sinus problem than a cavity, because the roots of the upper back teeth sit right under the maxillary sinuses, and congestion can make several of them ache, especially when you bend forward. Steam, saline rinses, staying hydrated, and a decongestant if it's safe for you often help that kind of pain. If it hangs on after your cold clears, or it's centered on one specific tooth, see a dentist to rule out a dental cause.
Can I dye my hair while pregnant? Salon appointment Friday.

Most experts consider hair dye low-risk in pregnancy because very little gets absorbed through the scalp. Many people wait until after the first trimester to be extra cautious, and highlights are a good option because the dye barely touches the skin. Make sure the salon is well ventilated so you're not breathing strong fumes.
Are those migraine glasses with tinted lenses legit?

FL-41 tinted lenses have some decent evidence for people who are very light-sensitive, especially under fluorescent lighting and screens. They won't stop a migraine on their own, but they can cut down triggers and make attacks more bearable. They're a reasonable thing to try alongside proper treatment.
Is the left arm or right arm better for taking blood pressure?

Either arm is fine for routine checks, but it's worth comparing both arms once. If one arm is consistently higher, use that arm from then on. A gap of more than about 10–15 points between arms is worth mentioning to your doctor, because it can sometimes point to narrowed arteries.
My friend keeps saying stuff like 'it'd be easier if I wasn't here' as a joke. Should I be worried?

Yes, take it seriously, even if it's said as a joke, because people often test the waters that way. Ask them directly and privately: "When you say that, are you thinking about killing yourself?" Asking won't plant the idea, and it often comes as a relief to the person. If they say yes, stay with them and help them contact a crisis line, which is 988 in the US, or their doctor. If they have a plan or the means and you think they're in immediate danger, call emergency services. You don't need perfect words, just honest concern.
Does morning sickness this bad mean something's wrong? I can't keep water down for a day now.

Not being able to keep fluids down for 24 hours goes beyond ordinary morning sickness and may be hyperemesis gravidarum, so contact your doctor or maternity unit today. You may need IV fluids and anti-sickness medication, both of which are safe and very effective. Go in sooner if you feel dizzy, pass very little or dark urine, or vomit blood.
Can I just use my smartwatch ECG instead of going to the doctor? It says normal sinus rhythm but I keep getting chest tightness.

A smartwatch ECG is a single-lead snapshot that's decent at spotting atrial fibrillation, but it can't rule out a heart attack or blocked arteries. Chest tightness that keeps coming back needs a proper assessment no matter what the watch says. Book a doctor's appointment soon, and go to emergency care if the tightness comes on with exertion, lasts more than a few minutes, or comes with breathlessness, sweating or nausea.
Is low blood pressure ever a problem? Mine is 95/60.

If you feel fine, 95/60 is often just normal for you, and it's common in young, fit people. It becomes a concern if you get dizziness, fainting, blurry vision or fatigue, or if it's a new drop from your usual level. In those cases see a doctor to look for dehydration, medication effects or other causes.
I took one of my roommate's adderall to study and now my heart is pounding and I feel awful. what do i do

Sit somewhere calm, sip water, and don't take any more stimulants, caffeine included. Most of the time this feeling fades over a few hours as the drug wears off. If you have chest pain, a heartbeat that feels irregular or extremely fast, trouble breathing, confusion, fainting or a severe headache, call emergency services or go to the ER right away and tell them exactly what you took. If you're unsure, Poison Control (1-800-222-1222 in the US) can advise you confidentially. Having someone stay with you for the next few hours is a good idea too.
had the flu last week, fever gone 2 days ago. can i go back to my usual 10k runs tomorrow?

I'd hold off on a full 10k tomorrow, since your body is still rebuilding after a fever and jumping straight back to full distance is how people end up relapsing or feeling wrecked for a week. Start with an easy 20 to 30 minute jog or brisk walk at a pace where you can chat, and see how you feel the next day. If that goes fine, build back up over about a week, roughly doubling the time every couple of sessions. If you get chest pain, a racing heart or unusual breathlessness, stop and get checked out.
My 72 year old dad takes warfarin and just started drinking kale smoothies every day because he read it's healthy. Should I be worried?

Yes, this is worth flagging. Kale is very high in vitamin K, which directly counteracts warfarin and can make his blood less protected against clots. He doesn't necessarily have to give up greens, since warfarin is dosed around a consistent vitamin K intake, but he should tell his doctor or anticoagulation clinic now so they can recheck his INR and adjust if needed. The key is keeping his intake steady rather than starting or stopping big amounts suddenly.
My mom has been losing weight without trying, about 10 pounds in three months. She says she's just not hungry. Should I worry?

Yes, unintentional weight loss of that much in an older adult should be checked by her doctor soon. Possible causes range from depression, dental problems and medication side effects to thyroid issues or more serious illness, and most are easier to treat when caught early. Bring a note of when it started, what she's eating and any other changes like fatigue or stomach problems. In the meantime, smaller frequent meals and calorie-rich snacks can help.
Is it dangerous to take Sudafed with high blood pressure? I'm so congested

Pseudoephedrine can raise blood pressure and heart rate, so it's best avoided if your pressure isn't well controlled. Saline rinses, a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, and short-term use of an oxymetazoline spray for 3 days at most are safer ways to clear congestion. Ask a pharmacist about products made for people with high blood pressure, since many cold combos hide decongestants.
I've had back pain for 2 months, it's worse at night, and I've lost 10 pounds without trying. I'm 61. Probably stress?

Please don't put this down to stress. Back pain that's worse at night combined with unexplained weight loss at 61 is a combination doctors take seriously, because it can occasionally signal infection or cancer. Book an appointment in the next few days and mention exactly those details. It may well turn out to be something benign, but it needs proper investigation.
Is walking ok when you have a cold?

Yes, an easy walk is usually fine with a cold and can even help you feel a bit better. Keep it at a comfortable pace and dress for the weather. If you have a fever, aches, or feel wiped out, rest instead.
found a tick on me after hiking, pulled it off. now what

Clean the bite with soap and water. Note the date, and if you can, save the tick in a sealed bag in case you need it identified. If it was attached for over 36 hours in a Lyme area, a doctor may offer a single preventive dose of doxycycline if it's within 72 hours, so it's worth a call. Over the next month, watch for an expanding red rash, fever, aches or fatigue, and see a doctor if any appear.
Do I need a hep B shot? I'm 28, got a new job at a dental office.

Yes, if you don't already have documented hepatitis B vaccination, you should get it, since dental work involves regular exposure to blood and needles. Your employer is generally required to offer it to you at no cost, so ask HR or the office manager. Healthcare workers are also usually tested afterward to confirm the vaccine took.
burned my tongue on pizza lol anything help

Sip cold water or let an ice chip melt on your tongue for a few minutes to ease the sting. Avoid hot, spicy, acidic or crunchy foods for a day or two while it heals. Tongue burns usually settle within a few days because the mouth heals fast. If it blisters badly or still hurts after a week, have a dentist or doctor take a look.
insulin is so expensive. can I stretch it by taking half doses?

Please don't ration insulin. Underdosing can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis, which can become life-threatening within a day or two, especially with type 1. Instead, look into manufacturer assistance programs and the $35 monthly caps many insurers and manufacturers now offer. Also ask your doctor about cheaper human insulins like NPH and regular, which are sold for around $25 at Walmart. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about the cost problem directly, because they deal with this constantly and often have fast solutions.
my inhaler ran out and the pharmacy is closed till monday. can i just use my friend's albuterol?

In a pinch, using a friend's albuterol is far safer than going without if you're wheezing, since it's the same medication most rescue inhalers contain. Check that it's actually albuterol (salbutamol) and not a steroid or combination inhaler, and use a fresh spacer or wipe the mouthpiece. Many pharmacies can also give an emergency supply without a new prescription, and urgent care can write one today. If your breathing gets worse despite the inhaler, or you can't speak in full sentences, go to the ER rather than waiting for Monday.
