Mole on my back changed shape and got darker in the last couple months. Probably nothing right?

A mole that's changing in shape or color is exactly the kind dermatologists want to see, so don't wait and hope it's nothing. Most changing moles turn out benign, but change is one of the main warning signs of melanoma, and melanoma caught early is very treatable. Book a dermatologist or GP appointment in the next couple of weeks and mention that it's changed. Taking a photo now with a ruler next to it will help them compare.
sleep 12 hrs on weekends to catch up. fine?

Sleeping in helps you pay back some sleep debt, but sleeping 12 hours shifts your body clock and makes Sunday night and Monday morning harder. It also doesn't fully undo the effects of weekday short sleep. A better approach is getting more sleep during the week and keeping weekend sleep-ins to an hour or two. If you regularly need 12 hours to feel human, mention it to a doctor.
teething baby, can i rub a little whiskey on gums like my grandma did

Skip the whiskey, because even small amounts of alcohol can be harmful to a baby, and it isn't worth the risk. Also avoid benzocaine gels like Orajel, since the FDA warns they can cause a dangerous blood disorder in young children. A chilled (not frozen) teething ring, a cold washcloth or gently rubbing her gums with a clean finger work well. If she's very miserable and over 6 months, ask the pediatrician about a dose of acetaminophen or ibuprofen.
nosebleed won't stop, been like 10 min

Sit up, lean forward, not back, and pinch the soft part of your nose just below the bony bridge firmly for a full 10 to 15 minutes without letting go to check. Spit out any blood that runs into your mouth instead of swallowing it, and a cold pack on the bridge can help. If it's still going after 20 to 30 minutes of proper pressure, it's very heavy, it started after a hit to the head, or you're on blood thinners, go to urgent care or the ER.
I have a mole on my back that my wife says looks bigger and darker than last year. It doesn't hurt. Probably nothing right?

Pain isn't the warning sign here. A mole that's growing or darkening is exactly the kind of change dermatologists want to see, because change is one of the main red flags for melanoma. Most changing moles turn out to be benign, but you can't tell by looking. Book a dermatology or GP appointment in the next few weeks, and have your wife take a photo with a coin next to it so you have a size reference.
Can I mix Sudafed and my blood pressure meds?

Be careful there. Sudafed (pseudoephedrine) can raise blood pressure and interact with some BP meds, so check with your pharmacist or doctor before taking it. Saline sprays, rinses, and a steroid nasal spray are safer options for congestion. Coricidin HBP is made for people with high blood pressure, but it treats symptoms rather than congestion.
Can I just use super glue to stick my crown back on? It fell off and the dentist is booked for 2 weeks

Don't use super glue, because it isn't safe in your mouth, can damage the tooth and crown, and can make it impossible for the dentist to recement the crown properly. Pharmacies sell temporary dental cement made for exactly this, and you can use it to hold the crown in place after cleaning both the crown and the tooth. Call the office back and tell them the crown came off, since many will squeeze you in sooner, especially if the tooth is sensitive or you can't get the crown to seat.
I'm 67 and my doctor wants me to get the shingles vaccine but I already had shingles in my 40s. Seems pointless?

It's not pointless. Shingles can come back, and a previous episode doesn't give reliable long-term protection, especially as immunity weakens with age. Shingrix is recommended for adults 50 and older whether or not you've had shingles. It's two doses given two to six months apart, and it also cuts your risk of long-lasting nerve pain after an outbreak. Go ahead and get it.
Ashwagandha for stress, any downsides? I have hashimoto's

Ashwagandha can raise thyroid hormone levels, which matters with Hashimoto's, especially if you're on levothyroxine. It can also stimulate the immune system, and there are rare reports of liver injury. Talk to your endocrinologist before trying it, and if you do start, get your thyroid levels rechecked within a couple of months. For stress, regular exercise and good sleep are safer first steps.
My teen son had a concussion along with a bad flu at the same time. He's itching to get back to lacrosse.

He should not return to lacrosse until a doctor has cleared him from the concussion. That usually means following a stepwise return-to-play protocol, and only once he's symptom-free. Having the flu on top of it is another reason to give him extra recovery time. A second hit before the brain has healed can be very serious, so it's worth the wait even if he's frustrated.
Scabies in our house. Can I just treat the kid who has it?

Everyone in the household and any close contacts should be treated at the same time, even if they have no symptoms. Scabies can take weeks to cause itching, and treating just one person lets it bounce back. Your doctor will usually prescribe permethrin cream applied neck-down and repeated in a week. Wash bedding, towels and recently worn clothes in hot water, and bag anything unwashable for at least 3 days. Itching can linger a couple of weeks after successful treatment, so that alone doesn't mean it failed.
My 8 year old says her tummy hurts every school morning but she's fine on weekends.

Stomach aches that show up on school mornings and vanish on weekends often point to stress or anxiety, which can cause real physical pain in kids. They can also be about rushed breakfasts or constipation. Gently ask about friends, teachers and anything that's worrying her, and mention the pattern to her pediatrician to rule out medical causes. Get checked sooner if she has weight loss, vomiting, fever, pain that wakes her at night, or blood in her stool.
what does a heart attack actually feel like? want to know what to look for

Most often it feels like pressure, squeezing or heaviness in the center of the chest that lasts more than a few minutes or comes and goes. It can spread to the arm, jaw, neck, back or upper stomach. Shortness of breath, cold sweat, nausea and lightheadedness are common companions. Women, older people and diabetics more often get vague symptoms like fatigue or breathlessness without much pain. If you suspect one, call emergency services rather than driving yourself.
best sleep position for lower back pain?

Side sleeping with a pillow between your knees keeps your hips and spine aligned, and most people with lower back pain find it the most comfortable. If you sleep on your back, a pillow under your knees takes strain off your lower back. Stomach sleeping tends to make back pain worse. If the pain is severe, getting worse, or comes with numbness, leg weakness, or bladder changes, see a doctor promptly.
how much ibuprofen can i take for tooth pain, the 200s aren't doing anything. like 6 at once?

Don't take six at once. For most healthy adults, the over-the-counter maximum is 400 mg (two tablets) every 4 to 6 hours, up to 1200 mg a day, and a doctor or dentist may sometimes advise higher doses. Adding acetaminophen on top often helps far more than piling on ibuprofen. If pain is breaking through that, the tooth probably needs treatment soon, so call a dentist.
headache after hitting my head on a cabinet yesterday, no big deal right

A mild headache after a minor bump is common and usually settles within a day or two with rest and acetaminophen. Get checked urgently if it's getting worse, or if you have repeated vomiting, confusion, unusual drowsiness, weakness, slurred speech or one pupil larger than the other. If you're over 65 or on blood thinners, get evaluated today even if you feel okay, because slow bleeds can hide at first.
dog scratched my eye a few hours ago, it's watering and I can't keep it open

Get it checked today at urgent care or by an eye doctor. Struggling to keep the eye open usually means a corneal scratch, and animal scratches carry a real risk of infection. You'll likely need antibiotic drops and a quick stain test to see how deep it is. Don't rub it or patch it tight, and take out any contact lens until you've been seen.
cat litter. do i actually have to stop or is that a myth

It's not a myth. Cat feces can carry toxoplasmosis, which can harm a developing baby, so it's best to hand litter duty to someone else. If you have to do it yourself, wear gloves, change it daily since the parasite needs a day or more to become infectious, and wash your hands well afterward. You don't need to get rid of your cat, and also wear gloves when gardening.
Allergic to dust mites. Worth buying those mattress covers?

Yes, allergen-proof zippered covers for your mattress and pillows are worth buying, because your bed is where you get the most dust mite exposure. Pair them with washing your bedding weekly in hot water, at least 130°F, and keeping your bedroom humidity below about 50%. Covers alone won't fix everything, but combined with those steps they make a real difference for a lot of people.
my teen burned her forearm with a curling iron, small blister, how should we care for it daily

Wash it gently once a day with mild soap and water, pat it dry, apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly, and cover it with a non-stick dressing. Leave the blister intact, and if it breaks on its own, keep the skin flap in place as a natural dressing. It should heal in one to two weeks. Have it checked if it gets more red, swollen, or oozy, or if it isn't improving.
my 4 year old just ate a cashew for the first time and now his lips are puffy and he's coughing a lot. is benadryl enough?

Lip swelling plus coughing after a nut can be the start of anaphylaxis, so call 911 (or your local emergency number) now rather than waiting to see if Benadryl works. If he has a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector, use it immediately. Antihistamines can ease hives but they won't stop airway swelling or a drop in blood pressure. Keep him sitting up if he's struggling to breathe, or lying down with legs raised if he seems faint or floppy.
found a tick on my leg, got it out, now there's a red circle around the spot like 3 inches wide a week later

An expanding red ring around a tick bite days later is the classic sign of Lyme disease (erythema migrans). See a doctor in the next day or two. It's usually diagnosed on sight and treated with a course of antibiotics like doxycycline, which works very well at this stage. Don't wait for flu-like symptoms to show up. Snap a photo in case the rash fades before your appointment.
how much melatonin should an adult take? the bottle says 10mg

Less than you'd think. Studies suggest 0.5 to 3 mg works about as well as higher doses, with less morning grogginess and fewer vivid dreams. Take it 30 to 60 minutes before your target bedtime. It's best for short-term use like jet lag or shifting your sleep schedule. If you need something every night to sleep, it's worth talking to a doctor about what's going on.
Got a fever of 101 after my baby's 2 month shots. Do I give tylenol? She's 9 weeks.

Call her pediatrician or the after-hours nurse line now before giving anything, because any fever in a baby this young needs a professional's input even right after vaccines. A low-grade temperature can be a normal vaccine reaction, but they'll want to check whether it's something else and will tell you the right acetaminophen dose for her weight if it's appropriate. If she's very sleepy, hard to wake, feeding poorly, or the fever climbs, go to the ER.
how long can someone go without pooping before its a problem

Normal ranges anywhere from three times a day to three times a week, so missing a day or two usually isn't a concern. After three or four days without a bowel movement, try more water, fiber, movement or a gentle over-the-counter option like polyethylene glycol. See a doctor promptly if you're vomiting, your belly is swollen or very painful, or you can't pass gas, because those can signal a blockage.
Quick q: son has a splinter deep in his foot, should I dig it out with a needle?

If you can see the end of it, sterilize some tweezers or a needle with rubbing alcohol, wash the area well and gently ease it out along the direction it went in. If it's deep, broken off, made of glass or metal, or he won't hold still, don't keep digging, because a doctor can remove it cleanly. Watch over the next few days for spreading redness, pus or worsening pain, which suggest infection. Also make sure his tetanus shots are up to date.
Is it safe to take my wife's nitroglycerin? I'm having chest pressure and she has a prescription.

Don't take her nitroglycerin; call 911 instead. Nitroglycerin can drop your blood pressure dangerously, especially if you've taken an erectile dysfunction drug like sildenafil or tadalafil recently, or if you're having a certain type of heart attack, and it also masks symptoms without fixing the underlying problem. Paramedics can give it safely after checking your blood pressure and ECG. While you wait, chewing a regular aspirin is reasonable if you're not allergic and haven't been told to avoid it.
My toddler's eye looks kind of white in photos with flash, like the other eye glows red but this one doesn't. Weird angle?

It might be the angle, but a white reflection in one pupil shouldn't be brushed off. It can signal cataract, a retinal problem, or rarely a childhood eye cancer called retinoblastoma. Show the photos to your pediatrician and ask for an eye exam soon. Early checks make a real difference here.
Do collagen supplements actually do anything for skin?

Some small studies show modest improvements in skin hydration and elasticity, though many were funded by manufacturers. Your body breaks collagen down into amino acids like any other protein, so the effect is limited. It's safe to try if you're curious. For your skin, sunscreen, not smoking and enough overall protein will do far more.
what's the max dose of tylenol in a day, I've been taking a lot plus nyquil

Check your NyQuil label, because it almost certainly contains acetaminophen too, and doubling up is how people accidentally overdose. For most healthy adults, keep the total from all sources at or under 3,000 mg a day, and lower if you drink alcohol or have liver problems. If you think you've gone over 4,000 mg in a day, call poison control at 1-800-222-1222 now. Liver damage often causes no symptoms at first, and treatment works best when it's given early.
Is microdosing psilocybin a good way to treat my depression? Lots of people online swear by it.

The online buzz is ahead of the science. Controlled trials of microdosing have mostly found effects similar to placebo, and the promising psilocybin research uses larger, supervised doses inside clinical studies. Illegal mushrooms also vary in strength, and psilocybin can interact with antidepressants or trigger problems in people with a personal or family history of psychosis or bipolar disorder. If you're interested in that route, ask your doctor about legitimate clinical trials, and keep the treatments with strong evidence, therapy and medication, on the table.
hit my head on a cabinet hard yesterday, headache today and kind of nauseous. fine?

Probably a mild concussion, but a headache plus nausea after a hard knock is worth having checked, so see a doctor or urgent care today. Go to the ER right away if the headache gets steadily worse, if you vomit repeatedly, or if you get confused, very drowsy, have slurred speech or have weakness on one side. Avoid alcohol, rest your brain from screens, and stick to acetaminophen rather than ibuprofen until you've been evaluated.
I've had a cough for 5 weeks after a cold. Everything else went away. Normal?

A lingering cough after a cold is common and can last three to eight weeks as your airways heal, so it's not automatically a worry. Still, five weeks is long enough that it's worth getting checked, especially if it's getting worse rather than slowly better. A doctor can look at things like post-viral asthma, postnasal drip, reflux or whooping cough. Go sooner if you're coughing up blood, losing weight, short of breath or having night sweats.
my back tooth has been throbbing for 3 days and now my cheek is swelling up. can i just wait til monday for my dentist?

Facial swelling with a throbbing tooth usually means an infection that's spreading beyond the tooth, so don't sit on this until Monday. Call your dentist's emergency line or go to an urgent care today, since you likely need antibiotics and a plan for draining or treating the tooth. If the swelling moves toward your eye or neck, or you develop a fever or trouble swallowing or breathing, go straight to the ER.
dog bite from my neighbor's dog, broke the skin a bit. washed it. good enough?

Washing it well with soap and water was the right first step. Dog bites that break the skin should still be seen by a doctor within a day, because they get infected easily and you may need antibiotics or a tetanus booster. Also confirm the dog is up to date on its rabies vaccine. Watch for redness, swelling, warmth or pus.
is it bad to keep a warm compress on my swollen face from a tooth abscess? feels nice

It's best to avoid heat on an abscess, because warmth can draw the infection outward and encourage it to spread. A cold compress for 15 to 20 minutes at a time is the safer choice for pain and swelling. Most importantly, see a dentist or urgent care promptly. Facial swelling from a tooth needs treatment, and you should go to the ER if it spreads or you develop a fever.
My 7 year old got stung by a bee and now his lips are swelling and he's coughing

Call 911 now, because swelling lips and coughing after a sting can be anaphylaxis, which can quickly close the airway. If he has an epinephrine auto-injector, use it in his outer thigh right away. Keep him lying down with his legs raised, or sitting up if that makes breathing easier. After this, he'll need to see an allergist and will likely be prescribed an EpiPen to carry with him.
I'm 68 and on blood thinners. Need a tooth out. Should I just stop my warfarin a few days before?

Don't stop warfarin on your own, because doing so raises your risk of a stroke or clot, which is far more dangerous than some extra bleeding at the dentist. Tell your dentist you're on it, and they'll usually coordinate with the doctor who prescribes it and check your INR shortly before the procedure. Most simple extractions can be done safely without stopping warfarin, using local measures to control bleeding, but that decision belongs to your care team.
can i take advil and tylenol at the same time or is that dumb

Not dumb at all. Ibuprofen and acetaminophen work differently, so you can take them together or stagger them a few hours apart for stronger pain relief, and that's a common, safe combo for most healthy adults. Keep each one within its own label limit, which means no more than 1,200 mg of over-the-counter ibuprofen and 3,000 to 4,000 mg of acetaminophen a day. Skip the ibuprofen if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers or take blood thinners.
my 2 year old has a cough and stuffy nose, is it ok to give her some of my adult cough syrup but just less of it?

Please don't. Over-the-counter cough and cold medicines aren't recommended for children under 4 at all, and guessing a smaller dose of an adult product is a common way kids get accidentally overdosed. For a toddler, saline drops with gentle suction, a cool-mist humidifier and plenty of fluids are the safe go-to options. Call her pediatrician if she's breathing fast or working hard to breathe, has a fever over 102°F lasting more than a couple of days, or seems unusually sleepy or isn't drinking.
cut is red and warm around the edges 3 days later, kinda throbbing. normal?

A little redness at the very edge can be normal healing, but spreading redness, warmth and throbbing at day three point toward infection. Draw a pen line around the edge of the redness so you can tell if it's growing. Arrange to see a doctor or urgent care today, especially if it's spreading or there's pus, because you may need antibiotics. Red streaks running up from the wound, fever, or feeling unwell mean you should go in right away.
sharp stabbing pain in chest for like 2 seconds then gone. happens sometimes. 19M

Brief, sharp, pinpoint pains lasting a couple of seconds are very common in young people and are often precordial catch syndrome, which is harmless and tends to happen at rest or when slouching. It isn't how heart attacks typically behave. Still see a doctor if the pains get longer or more frequent, or come with exertion, palpitations, fainting or breathlessness.
Can I drink alcohol on antibiotics? Wedding this weekend.

With most common antibiotics, like amoxicillin or doxycycline, a couple of drinks won't cause a dangerous reaction, though alcohol can slow your recovery and worsen side effects like an upset stomach. The big exceptions are metronidazole and tinidazole. Drinking on those can cause severe vomiting, flushing and a racing heart, and you need to stay off alcohol until 72 hours after your last dose. Check the name on your bottle, and if it's one of those, stick to soda at the wedding.
I'm 31 weeks pregnant and my OB wants me to get Tdap. I already had it two years ago, why again??

Tdap is recommended in every pregnancy, ideally between 27 and 36 weeks, because the goal is to pass fresh antibodies to your baby before birth. Whooping cough can be life-threatening for newborns, and your antibody levels fade fast enough that a shot from two years ago won't give your baby much protection. Getting it now is safe and is the best way to protect your baby until they're old enough for their own vaccines.
Coughing up green stuff and have a temp but feel ok. Quick run?

Skip the run today. A fever along with a productive cough means your body is fighting a chest infection, and running hard can make you feel worse and drag out your recovery. Rest and drink plenty of fluids. See a doctor if the fever lasts more than a few days or you develop chest pain or shortness of breath.
Doctor prescribed me a statin and aspirin after a minor heart scare, but I feel fine now so I want to stop them. Okay?

Please don't stop them on your own. Feeling fine is exactly what these medications are meant to help you keep doing, and they cut your risk of a future heart attack or stroke. Stopping aspirin suddenly after a cardiac event can even briefly raise your risk. If side effects or the idea of long-term pills are bothering you, talk to your doctor, because there are often alternatives or dose changes that work well.
chest feels tight after starting a new workout program. 35, healthy. push through it?

Don't push through chest tightness, even if you're healthy, because a sore chest muscle and a heart warning sign can feel similar. If it's tender to press on, changes with arm movement and comes the day after lifting, it's probably muscular, but tightness during exertion that eases with rest needs a doctor's visit before your next hard session. Stop immediately and get help if it comes with breathlessness, dizziness, sweating or pain spreading to your arm or jaw.
My 8 yo's inhaler ran out and the pharmacy is closed. He's wheezing a bit. Can he use my old one from 2 years ago?

An expired albuterol inhaler usually still delivers some medicine, and in a pinch it's better than nothing for mild wheezing, so it's reasonable to use it for him. Give the dose his doctor prescribed, shake it well, and use a spacer if you have one. Watch him closely. If he's working hard to breathe, the skin between his ribs pulls in when he breathes, he can't speak in full sentences, his lips look bluish, or the inhaler isn't helping, go to the ER or call emergency services. Call his doctor's after-hours line tonight to get a refill sorted.
I have some leftover amoxicillin from last year. Should I just take it for this cold so it doesn't turn into something worse?

Skip it. Colds are viral, so antibiotics won't shorten this one or prevent complications, and a partial leftover course can cause side effects and help breed resistant bacteria. Rest, fluids and symptom relief are the right move. If you develop a high fever, symptoms beyond 10 days, or a sudden turn for the worse, see a doctor, who can decide whether you actually need an antibiotic and which one.
My doc wants me to get a stress test for chest pain I get when exercising. Can I just keep running and see if it goes away?

Chest pain that comes on with exercise is exactly the kind that needs a stress test, so don't keep training through it. Exertional chest pain can mean an artery isn't delivering enough blood under load, and pushing through it raises the risk of a heart attack or dangerous rhythm. Hold off on strenuous exercise until the test is done, and get the appointment scheduled as soon as you can. If the pain starts happening at rest, lasts more than a few minutes, or gets more frequent, go to the ER instead of waiting.
toddler ate a crayon. like half of one. freaking out

Take a breath, because standard children's crayons are non-toxic wax and half of one will almost certainly just pass through without trouble. Check his mouth for any leftover pieces and watch for coughing, gagging, or trouble swallowing, since choking is the real concern, not poisoning. If you want extra reassurance, Poison Control (1-800-222-1222 in the US) is free and happy to take exactly this kind of call.
lost my vaccine records. do i need to redo everything?

Not necessarily, so try tracking them down first through your state immunization registry, old doctors, your school or college, or your parents' records. If you can't find them, your doctor can order blood tests to check immunity to things like measles and hepatitis B, or simply give you certain vaccines again. Getting an extra dose of most vaccines is safe, so being re-vaccinated is a reasonable fallback.
Is it okay for my asthmatic daughter (12) to get the flu shot or will it trigger an attack?

She should definitely get it. Kids with asthma are at higher risk of severe flu complications, and the flu shot doesn't trigger asthma attacks. The one thing to note is that the nasal spray version, FluMist, usually isn't recommended for kids with active asthma or recent wheezing, so ask for the injection.
My boss emails at 11pm and I feel like I have to answer or I'll get fired. Stress is killing me. Advice?

Answering at 11pm trains everyone to expect it, so try a small boundary first. Reply at 8am with a quick 'Saw this, on it this morning,' which most bosses accept without blinking. Turn off email notifications after a set hour so your brain can actually switch off. If you're genuinely afraid of being fired for not replying instantly, a direct conversation about expectations, or checking your workplace policies, is worth it. Constant stress like this is also worth raising with your doctor if it's hitting your sleep or health.
Pregnant, 28 weeks. My OB wants me to get Tdap but I'm nervous about putting anything in my body right now. Is it really necessary?

It's a very reasonable thing to ask, and Tdap during pregnancy is one of the best-studied and most strongly recommended vaccines, ideally given between 27 and 36 weeks. The antibodies you make pass across the placenta and protect your baby from whooping cough during the first couple of months, before they can be vaccinated themselves and when pertussis is most dangerous. Side effects are usually limited to a sore arm, and large studies haven't found harm to the baby. Getting it now, at 28 weeks, is right in the ideal window.
pinkeye in my 4 yr old. can I use leftover drops from when my husband had it?

Better not, because his drops might be the wrong medication, could be expired or contaminated, and a dropper that touched an infected eye can spread germs. A lot of pinkeye in kids is viral and clears on its own, so warm compresses, gentle wiping from the inner corner outward, and lots of handwashing may be all she needs. Call her doctor if there's thick yellow-green discharge, eye pain, light sensitivity, or swelling around the eye, since those may need a proper prescription or a closer look.
Pregnant, 20 weeks, and I think I have a UTI. Should I just drink cranberry juice?

Call your OB or midwife today rather than trying to manage it yourself. UTIs in pregnancy are more likely to travel up to the kidneys and can raise the risk of preterm labor. There are antibiotics that are safe at your stage. Cranberry juice won't treat an active infection. If you have fever, back pain, vomiting or contractions, go to labor and delivery or the ER.
post-flu, feeling 80%. better to wait until 100% to exercise or start now?

At 80% you can start with easy activity, like walking, gentle cycling or light stretching. Moving a little often helps you recover. Keep the intensity low and the sessions short, and save hard workouts until you're closer to full strength. If any session leaves you feeling worse the next day, back off a bit.
throat feels tight and itchy after eating shrimp for the first time. i took benadryl, can i just sleep it off?

Don't sleep this off. A tight throat after a new food can be the start of anaphylaxis, and Benadryl can't stop that. Call 911 or get to an ER now, and if anyone near you has an epinephrine auto-injector, use it. Stay with someone who can watch you rather than lying down alone.
how much ibuprofen can I take for fever, I'm an adult, like 4 pills at once ok?

Four 200 mg pills, or 800 mg, is more than you should take without a doctor's guidance. The over-the-counter dose for adults is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours, with no more than 1,200 mg in a day unless a doctor says otherwise. Take it with food, and skip it if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, or are on blood thinners. A higher dose won't bring the fever down any faster.
my dad is 81 and keeps forgetting whether he took his pills so sometimes he takes them twice. how do i stop this

Get him a weekly pill organizer with separate morning and evening compartments, and fill it yourself or have the pharmacy pre-pack his meds in dated blister packs, which many pharmacies do for free. That way an empty slot tells him the dose is already taken. Ask his pharmacist which of his medications are risky if doubled, since things like blood thinners, diabetes pills or blood pressure drugs can cause real harm. If the forgetting is new or getting worse, mention it to his doctor too.
Diabetic on metformin. Doctor wants a CT with contrast. Anything I should know?

Your doctor will usually have you pause metformin at the time of the scan and for 48 hours after if your kidney function is reduced. With normal kidneys, many places don't require a pause, so ask the radiology team to confirm based on your recent labs. Stay well hydrated, and restart metformin once they confirm your kidney function is fine.
breastfeeding, can I still take my melatonin

Melatonin passes into breast milk, and there's very little research on supplement doses during breastfeeding, so check with your doctor or pediatrician first. If they're okay with it, the lowest dose, around 0.5 to 1 mg, is the safer approach. Meanwhile, keeping lights dim during night feeds and sleeping when the baby naps can help a lot.
Is it okay to use hydrogen peroxide on a cut? That's what my mom always did.

Hydrogen peroxide actually harms healthy healing cells, so it can slow down recovery. Plain running water and mild soap around the wound are the best way to clean it. After that, a thin layer of petroleum jelly and a plaster keep it moist, which helps it heal faster with less scarring.
My 8 month old has dry red patches on her cheeks and the creases of her elbows. She keeps rubbing her face on the sheets. What can I do?

That pattern sounds a lot like infant eczema, which is very common at this age. Use lukewarm, short baths with a fragrance-free cleanser, then pat her dry and apply a thick fragrance-free moisturizer or ointment all over within a few minutes while her skin is still damp. Dress her in soft cotton and keep her nails short so the rubbing does less damage. See her doctor if the patches don't improve within a week or two, or sooner if they ooze, crust over or keep her from sleeping, because she may need a mild prescription cream.
can i do a light hike 3 days after norovirus

Possibly, if you're eating and drinking normally and no longer having symptoms. Keep it short and easy, and bring plenty of water and some snacks. Norovirus leaves many people weaker than they expect, so choose a route you can easily cut short. Stay home if you're still lightheaded or not eating much.
can i drink a beer after taking my allergy pill

With non-drowsy antihistamines like loratadine or fexofenadine, one beer is usually fine for most people. With older ones like diphenhydramine or chlorpheniramine, or even cetirizine for some people, alcohol stacks the sedation, so skip it or keep it very light. Don't drive if you're feeling at all drowsy.
I'm 45, smoker, my dad had a heart attack at 50. I get chest tightness walking uphill that goes away when I stop. Is it urgent or can it wait for my checkup in 2 months?

Don't wait two months. Chest tightness that reliably comes with exertion and fades with rest is the classic pattern of angina, and your smoking and family history make it more concerning. Call your doctor this week and say exactly that so they book you in promptly for tests like an ECG and stress test. If the tightness ever starts at rest, lasts longer than a few minutes, or gets worse, treat it as an emergency.
Stomach pain and diarrhea after a trip to Mexico, been a week. Can I just ride it out?

Mild traveler's diarrhea often clears in 3 to 5 days, but a full week means it's time to see a doctor, because a parasite or bacterial infection may need specific treatment. Keep up your fluids and electrolytes in the meantime. Don't rely on loperamide (Imodium) to plug things up if you have fever or blood in your stool. Mention where you traveled so they test for the right things.
is it ok to take like 4 extra strength tylenol at once? the pain is unbearable and 2 isn't touching it

Don't double up, because extra acetaminophen won't control the pain much better and it can seriously damage your liver. A safer and stronger option for most people is pairing your normal Tylenol dose with a normal ibuprofen dose, since the two work differently. Pain that bad means the tooth needs attention today, so call an emergency dentist rather than chasing it with more pills.
I just got out of a stressful meeting and my BP is 155/98. Freaking out a bit.

Stress can push your blood pressure up a lot in the moment, so this reading on its own isn't cause for panic. Sit quietly for 15–20 minutes, breathe slowly, and recheck. What matters is your resting readings over several days, so if those are still high, book an appointment.
Should my 79 year old father be taking a daily baby aspirin? His friend does.

Not without asking his doctor first. Current guidance has moved away from routine daily aspirin for people his age who haven't had a heart attack or stroke, because the bleeding risk often outweighs the benefit. It's very different if he already has heart disease, in which case his doctor may well recommend it. What's right for his friend isn't automatically right for him.
My grandma swears by putting butter on burns. Is that actually fine?

Skip the butter, because it holds heat in the skin and can make infection more likely. Cool running water for about 20 minutes is the best first step, and it still helps if you start within a few hours of the burn. After that, a clean nonstick dressing or a bit of aloe is all a minor burn needs. Your grandma's heart is in the right place, but the tap is the better remedy.
my toddler wakes up screaming but doesnt seem awake and doesnt remember it

That sounds like night terrors, which are common in toddlers and preschoolers and usually happen in the first few hours after falling asleep. They look scary but don't harm your child, and most kids outgrow them. Don't try to wake her. Just stay close, keep her safe, and let it pass. Overtiredness is a big trigger, so an earlier or more consistent bedtime often helps. See your pediatrician if episodes are very frequent, last a long time, involve unusual jerking or stiffening, or she seems sleepy during the day.
Is it safe to pull my own loose adult tooth? It's wiggly and hurts and I don't have insurance

Don't pull it yourself, because a loose adult tooth is usually a sign of advanced gum disease or infection, and a DIY extraction can break the root, cause heavy bleeding, or spread the infection. Look for a community health center, a dental school clinic, or a sliding-scale clinic near you, since they often do extractions cheaply. Until then, keep the area clean with gentle brushing and salt-water rinses, and use over-the-counter pain relievers as labeled.
is it bad that i take advil like 5 days a week for headaches

That's frequent enough to cause trouble. Painkillers used more than about 10 to 15 days a month can trigger medication-overuse headaches, which keep the cycle going, and daily ibuprofen also strains your stomach and kidneys. See your doctor about preventive treatment and figuring out your triggers. Cutting back with their guidance usually makes the headaches less frequent.
deep cut on knee from falling off bike, I can see like yellow fatty stuff

If you can see yellow fatty tissue, the cut has gone through the full thickness of the skin, so it needs stitches. Press a clean cloth on it, keep the leg still, and get to urgent care or an ER within the next few hours. Knee cuts also get checked to make sure the joint isn't involved, and you may need a tetanus booster depending on your last one.
is it safe to get the covid booster and flu shot same day

Yes, getting both at the same visit is safe and recommended by the CDC, and studies show both vaccines still work well when given together. You may feel a bit more tired or achy for a day than you would with one shot alone. Many people ask for one in each arm so the soreness is split up.
Is an allergy to latex a big deal? Found out at the dentist.

It can be. Latex allergy ranges from skin irritation to severe reactions, so it's worth knowing which type you have. Tell every doctor, dentist, and hospital so they use latex-free gloves and equipment. Look into cross-reactions too: some people with latex allergy also react to banana, avocado, kiwi, or chestnut. An allergist can confirm how serious it is and whether you need an epinephrine auto-injector.
My son, 5, has honey colored crusty sores around his nose that are spreading. Daycare sent him home.

Honey-coloured crusts spreading around the nose is classic impetigo, a bacterial skin infection that's very common in young kids. He needs to see his doctor, who will usually prescribe an antibiotic ointment like mupirocin, or oral antibiotics if it's widespread. Gently wash the crusts with soap and water, keep his nails short, and use separate towels so it doesn't spread through the family. He can usually go back to daycare 24 hours after starting treatment.
Back pain plus I've noticed I can't really feel when I wipe after the toilet and peeing is weird. Probably nothing?

Please go to the emergency department right now, because numbness in that area plus changes in how you pee alongside back pain are warning signs of cauda equina syndrome. In that condition, nerves at the base of the spine get compressed, and it needs an urgent scan and often surgery within hours to prevent permanent bladder, bowel and sexual problems. Don't wait to see whether it improves, and tell the staff exactly those symptoms when you arrive.
Eczema on my hands flaring because of all the handwashing at work (nurse). Lotions aren't cutting it.

Switch from lotion to a thick ointment or a barrier cream, and apply it after every wash and heavily at night under cotton gloves. Pat your hands dry fully, use alcohol rub when your hands aren't visibly dirty, since it's often gentler than repeated soap washing, and wear cotton liners under nitrile gloves if you can. Let your occupational health team or a doctor know, because a short course of prescription steroid cream can calm a flare quickly. They can also check whether a contact allergy to gloves or soap is part of the problem.
how much tylenol for a 3 year old

Children's acetaminophen is dosed by weight, not age, so check the chart on your product's box and use the syringe or cup that came with it. For a typical 3-year-old weighing about 24 to 35 pounds, that's usually 5 mL of the 160 mg/5 mL liquid every 4 to 6 hours. Don't give more than 5 doses in 24 hours. Check that no other medicines you're giving also contain acetaminophen. If you're unsure of the weight or the product strength, a pharmacist can confirm the dose in a minute.
What's the fastest way to break a fever? I have an important presentation tomorrow and need to be functional.

Ibuprofen or acetaminophen taken at the labeled dose will bring the temperature down and ease the achiness within about an hour, and you can alternate them if needed as long as you stay within each one's daily limit. Drink plenty of water and get as much sleep tonight as you can, since that's what actually helps you recover. Keep in mind that the medicine only masks the fever, so you can still be contagious. If you can present remotely or postpone, that's the kinder option for your coworkers.
Throwing up like 8 times a day, can't keep water down for over a day now. 11 weeks. Is this just bad morning sickness?

That's beyond normal morning sickness. Being unable to keep fluids down for more than a day can mean hyperemesis gravidarum and dehydration, so you should call your provider today or go to urgent care. They can give you IV fluids and anti-nausea medicine that are safe in pregnancy, and most people feel dramatically better afterward. Go in sooner if you feel dizzy, are barely peeing, or your urine is dark.
Teen daughter touched a hot curling iron, small red mark on her fingers, no blisters. Need a doctor?

A small red burn without blisters is superficial and usually fine to handle at home. Run it under cool water for 20 minutes even now, since that still helps, then use a bland moisturizer or aloe, with ibuprofen if it's sore. If blisters show up later, leave them intact and keep them covered. Have it checked if it spreads, becomes very painful, or shows signs of infection like pus or increasing redness.
My toddler has honey colored crusty sores around his nose and mouth spreading fast

Honey-colored crusts that spread quickly are textbook impetigo, a contagious bacterial skin infection common in toddlers. Get him to his doctor in the next day or so, because it usually needs a prescription antibiotic cream or, if widespread, oral antibiotics. Meanwhile, gently wash the crusts with soap and water, keep his nails short, and use separate towels. Keep him home from daycare until he's had 24 hours of treatment.
I'm 29 and pregnant, 34 weeks, and suddenly short of breath with sharp chest pain when I breathe in. Is this just the baby pushing on my lungs?

Some breathlessness is normal late in pregnancy, but sudden sharp chest pain when you breathe in is different and could be a blood clot in the lung. Pregnancy significantly raises the risk of clots. Please go to the emergency department or call your maternity unit's urgent line right now rather than waiting for your next appointment. Call emergency services if you feel faint or very breathless, or if you're coughing up blood.
Pharmacist gave me a different brand of inhaler, different shape. Do I just use it the same?

Not necessarily, because different devices can need quite different techniques. A dry-powder inhaler needs a fast, deep breath, while a puffer needs a slow one. Ask the pharmacist to show you how to use it and watch you try, which they're happy to do. Check that the active ingredient is the same as your old one too.
Do adults need a measles booster? Born in 1985, not sure what I got as a kid.

If you can't find records showing two doses of MMR, the simplest move is to just get one now, since an extra dose is safe for adults. People born after 1957 without documented immunity are advised to have at least one dose, and two if you're a healthcare worker, college student, or international traveler. A doctor can also run a blood test to check your immunity if you'd rather confirm first. Just avoid it if you're pregnant, because MMR is a live vaccine.
just tell me the max ibuprofen i can take for this fever i want it gone

For adults, the over-the-counter limit is 400 mg every 6 to 8 hours, up to 1,200 mg a day, unless a doctor tells you to take more. Going higher raises your risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems, especially when you're dehydrated from a fever. Take it with food and drink plenty of fluids. If the fever won't come down at normal doses, that's a reason to see a doctor, not to take more.
dizzy spinning when i roll over in bed, lasts like 30 seconds, otherwise fine

Brief spinning triggered by rolling over is classic BPPV, where tiny crystals in the inner ear get displaced. It's harmless and very treatable, often in one visit with a repositioning maneuver like the Epley. See a doctor or physio to confirm it and get the maneuver done properly. Seek urgent care if the dizziness comes with slurred speech, weakness, a severe headache, or trouble walking, since those point elsewhere.
I get migraines like 3 times a week now and I'm popping excedrin almost every day. is that bad?

That pattern can actually make things worse, because using painkillers like Excedrin more than about 10 days a month can trigger medication overuse headache, a rebound cycle that keeps the migraines coming. Three migraines a week is frequent enough that you're a good candidate for preventive treatment, and there are several effective options. Book an appointment with your doctor or a headache specialist and bring a rough log of your headache days and what you took.
throat feels itchy and a bit tight after shrimp at dinner 20 min ago. probably nothing right? dont want to overreact

Throat tightness after eating shrimp is a warning sign of anaphylaxis, so please call emergency services now rather than waiting it out. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector, use it right away. Sit up if breathing is hard, avoid standing up suddenly, and have someone stay with you. Going in for something that turns out mild is far better than getting there too late.
how many xanax is too many, i take 1 or 2 extra when its bad

Taking more than prescribed is risky, because Xanax builds tolerance quickly, extra doses can lead to dependence, and mixing it with alcohol or opioids can stop your breathing. Tell your prescriber that your current dose isn't covering the bad days, since they have safer options, including longer-acting medications and therapy. Don't stop suddenly either, because withdrawal can be dangerous, so any change should happen under a doctor's guidance.
water stuck in ear after swimming for 2 days, kinda itchy

Try tilting your head with that ear down and gently tugging the earlobe, then use a hairdryer on low and cool held a foot away to dry it out. Itching after swimming can be the start of swimmer's ear, so don't dig in with cotton swabs or fingers. If you develop pain when you tug your ear, swelling, or discharge, see a doctor for prescription drops, which clear it up fast.
Had a bad allergic reaction (hives, throat tight) after my first dose of a vaccine years ago. Should I get the second dose of a different one now?

Don't get any vaccine until you've talked this through with your doctor, and ideally an allergist. A reaction with throat tightness counts as serious, so it's important to identify which ingredient you might be sensitive to. Many people with a history like yours can still be vaccinated safely, sometimes with a different product or under observation in a setting prepared for allergic reactions. Bring whatever details you have about the earlier vaccine.
I'm 67 and my vision in one eye got wavy, straight lines look bent. Started a few days ago.

Straight lines that suddenly look wavy or bent can be a sign of wet macular degeneration, which progresses quickly but often responds well to treatment if it's caught early. Book an urgent appointment with an eye doctor this week, and tell them it's a new distortion so they prioritize you. If you lose central vision suddenly, go in the same day.
Honest question, is tanning beds before vacation a good idea to get a base tan so I don't burn?

Unfortunately a base tan gives you only about the protection of SPF 3 to 4, and tanning beds significantly raise your risk of melanoma and other skin cancers, especially if you start young. You'd be taking on real UV damage to avoid a little sun damage, which isn't a good trade. A better plan is broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher reapplied every two hours, a hat, and shade at midday, or a self-tanner if you want the color.
I have asthma and just caught a bad chest cold, my inhaler isn't helping as much as usual

Take that seriously, because colds are one of the most common triggers of asthma flare-ups. Contact your doctor today, since you may need a short course of steroids or a change to your controller medication, and follow your asthma action plan if you have one. Get emergency care right away if you're struggling to speak in full sentences, your lips look blue, or your rescue inhaler isn't giving relief even for a few hours.
my cat bit my hand pretty deep about an hour ago, it's a bit swollen. just wash it and forget it right?

Wash it thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes, but don't forget about it, because cat bites are deep punctures that infect more often than almost any other animal bite. Swelling within an hour is already a warning sign, so get it seen by a doctor today, since many deep cat bites need antibiotics. Hand bites are especially risky because infection can reach tendons and joints quickly.
Is it safe to take aspirin for a headache? I'm 15.

It's best for anyone under 16 to avoid aspirin because it's linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition, especially after a viral illness. Ibuprofen or acetaminophen at the dose on the package is the safer choice. If your headaches keep coming back, let a parent and your doctor know.
im 19 and my bp is 140/90 every time, my friends say im too young to worry

Your friends are wrong on this one. Consistent readings of 140/90 at 19 deserve a doctor visit, because high blood pressure in young people sometimes has a specific cause, like kidney or hormone issues, sleep apnea, stimulants or energy drinks. Get it checked properly so you know what's going on.
My itchy rash appeared after starting a new antibiotic 5 days ago. Spreading. Keep taking it?

Call the prescriber or a pharmacist today before your next dose. A spreading rash after starting an antibiotic may be a drug reaction, and they'll likely want to stop or switch it. Seek emergency care right away if you develop blistering, peeling skin, sores in your mouth or eyes, swelling of the face or lips, fever, or trouble breathing. Those can signal a severe reaction.
missed my blood pressure pill this morning, should I just take two tonight

Don't double up, because two doses at once can drop your blood pressure too far and leave you dizzy or faint. If you remember within a few hours of your usual time, take the missed pill now. If it's almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and carry on as normal. One missed dose is rarely a big deal, but call your pharmacist if you're not sure how your particular medication works.
Can I just superglue a cut shut? It's like an inch long on my shin, not too deep.

Household superglue isn't made for skin and can irritate it, so medical skin glue or adhesive closure strips are the better choice. For a clean, shallow inch-long cut, wash it well, dry the edges, and pull them together with strips or a pharmacy wound-closure product. If the edges won't stay together easily, the cut is deep, or there's dirt you can't clean out, get it closed properly within the next few hours, since stitches work best early.
My husband snores like a chainsaw and sometimes stops breathing for a few seconds then gasps. Should I worry?

Yes, that pattern is a classic sign of obstructive sleep apnea and worth getting checked. Untreated apnea raises the risk of high blood pressure, heart problems, stroke and drowsy-driving accidents. He should see his doctor and ask about a sleep study, which can often be done at home now. Treatment like CPAP usually makes a dramatic difference in how he feels during the day too.
thinking about just giving birth at home without a midwife or anyone, my body knows what to do. thoughts?

Unassisted birth carries real risks, because complications like hemorrhage, a baby who doesn't breathe right away, or cord problems can happen suddenly in low-risk pregnancies and need trained hands within minutes. If a home birth matters to you, look into a certified nurse-midwife or certified professional midwife who attends home births. They bring equipment and medication and know when to transfer to a hospital. You can still have a calm, low-intervention birth on your terms with a skilled person present.
can i skip the glucose test? i eat healthy and the drink is gross

It's worth doing, because gestational diabetes often has no symptoms and can happen to people who eat well and are a healthy weight. Left untreated, it raises the risk of a very large baby, a difficult delivery, and blood sugar problems for your newborn. If the drink is the dealbreaker, ask your provider about alternatives. Some practices allow a specific meal or a few weeks of fingerstick monitoring instead, so you may have options other than skipping it.
My 80 year old mom with dementia keeps touching her jaw and won't eat. Could it be her teeth?

It very well could be, because touching the jaw and refusing food are common ways people with dementia show mouth pain. Check her gums and any dentures for sores, swelling or a poor fit, and arrange a dental exam soon, which some dentists can do at home or in care facilities. Since she's not eating, call her doctor too if this lasts more than a day or two or she seems dehydrated.
can I drink alcohol with my migraine meds?

It depends on what you're taking, but it's usually best to skip it during an attack. Alcohol is a common migraine trigger and can worsen the hangover-like feeling afterward. It also adds stomach-bleeding risk with NSAIDs and liver strain with acetaminophen, and it can increase drowsiness with anti-nausea meds or preventives like topiramate or amitriptyline. Ask your pharmacist about your specific medication for a quick, reliable answer.
Is a heating pad or ice better for back pain?

For ordinary back pain from a strain or stiffness, heat usually helps more because it relaxes tight muscles and eases spasm. Ice can be useful in the first day or two after a clear injury if it feels better to you, so go with whichever gives more relief. Use either one for about 15 to 20 minutes with a cloth between it and your skin, and never fall asleep on a heating pad, as that's a common cause of burns.
got the flu, day 1, fever 101. do i need tamiflu or is that a waste

It's not a waste if you get it early, since antivirals like Tamiflu work best when started within 48 hours of symptoms and can shorten the illness by about a day. They matter most if you're over 65, pregnant, have asthma, diabetes, heart disease or a weakened immune system. If any of those apply, call your doctor or use a telehealth visit today. If you're otherwise healthy, rest, fluids and acetaminophen or ibuprofen for the fever are a reasonable plan too.
can i put toothpaste on pimples overnight

It's a popular trick, but toothpaste often irritates and burns the skin and can leave a red, peeling patch that looks worse than the pimple. A dab of 2.5–5% benzoyl peroxide or a salicylic acid spot treatment does the same job properly. Hydrocolloid pimple patches are also great overnight, because they flatten spots and stop you picking.
Rolled my ankle playing basketball, it's swollen but I can kind of walk. Can I just tape it and play tomorrow?

Playing on it tomorrow is a good way to turn a one-week sprain into a six-week one, so give it at least a few days. For the first 48 hours, rest it, ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time with a cloth between ice and skin, use a compression wrap, and keep it raised. If you couldn't take four steps right after the injury, or the bony knobs on either side of the ankle are tender to press, get an X-ray to rule out a fracture.
Doctor said my ferritin is 9. Can I just eat more spinach?

Spinach won't get you there. Its iron is poorly absorbed, and a ferritin of 9 means your stores are genuinely depleted, so you'll likely need a supplement your doctor recommends. Taking it every other day with some vitamin C, away from coffee, tea and calcium, improves absorption and reduces stomach upset. Also ask your doctor about finding the cause, since heavy periods or GI blood loss are common reasons for low iron.
burned my tongue on pizza, how long does it last

A scalded tongue usually feels better within a few days, since the mouth heals fast. Sip cold water, suck on ice chips, and avoid hot, spicy, acidic, or crunchy food for a day or two. If you have large blisters, signs of infection, or it isn't improving after about a week, have a dentist or doctor take a look.
Kid swallowed a coin. He's breathing fine and acting normal. Do I need to do anything?

If he's breathing, talking, eating and drinking normally with no drooling, chest pain or vomiting, most coins pass on their own within a few days. Still call your pediatrician today, because they often want an X-ray to make sure it isn't stuck in the esophagus, which can happen even when a child seems fine. Go to the ER right away if he has trouble swallowing, drools, refuses food, vomits, coughs persistently or has belly pain. Also double-check it was definitely a coin, because a button battery or magnet is a true emergency even when there are no symptoms.
is it ok to take cbd every night for sleep

The evidence for CBD and sleep is still pretty thin, and product quality varies widely. Some products contain THC or far more or less CBD than the label says. If you use it, choose third-party tested products. Check with a pharmacist first if you take other medications, since CBD can interact with blood thinners and some seizure and heart drugs. If you're relying on it every night, it's worth looking at the underlying sleep problem.
I fainted while jogging today but felt fine after a minute. 22, athlete. Coach says just hydrate.

Fainting during exercise is different from fainting after it and needs a proper cardiac evaluation before you train again. It can be a sign of an inherited heart muscle or rhythm problem, which is a known cause of sudden collapse in young athletes. See a doctor soon and ask for an ECG and likely an echocardiogram. Hold off on hard training until you're cleared.
My grandmother suddenly got really confused today, didn't know what year it was. She was totally sharp last week.

Sudden confusion in an older person is a medical problem, not normal aging, and she should be seen today. If it came on within minutes or hours, or comes with facial drooping, slurred speech or weakness on one side, call emergency services right away because it could be a stroke. If it developed over a day or two, common causes are urinary tract infections, dehydration and medication reactions, and these are very treatable. She still needs urgent care or an ER visit to check.
My 12 year old wants to start lifting weights with his older brother. He's tiny. Will it stunt his growth?

That's a myth, and supervised strength training is actually safe and beneficial for kids his age. The real risks come from poor form and trying to max out heavy weights, so have him start with bodyweight exercises or light weights and higher reps, focused on technique. If his brother is coaching, make sure he's being careful rather than competitive, and a coach or trainer who works with youth athletes can set up a good starting plan.
I've been on lisinopril for 3 months and my numbers are perfect now. Can I just stop taking it since I'm cured?

Good numbers usually mean the medication is working, not that the high blood pressure is gone. If you stop on your own, your pressure will likely climb back up, sometimes quickly. Talk to your doctor first. If you've also lost weight or changed your diet, they may be able to lower your dose or taper you off safely while monitoring your readings.
I've been on clindamycin for a week and now I have like 8 watery stools a day and cramps. Just a side effect right?

That's more than a typical side effect. Clindamycin is one of the antibiotics most linked to C. diff infection, which causes exactly this, so call your doctor today. You'll likely need a stool test and a different treatment. Don't take anti-diarrhea medicine like loperamide in the meantime, and go to the ER if you have a high fever, blood in your stool, severe abdominal pain or signs of dehydration.
Is 37.6 a fever?

Not really. Most clinicians define a fever as 38.0°C (100.4°F) or higher, so 37.6°C is at the upper end of normal or a mild elevation. Body temperature also naturally rises after exercise, hot drinks or in the late afternoon. Recheck in an hour if you feel unwell.
how much ibuprofen can i take for flu aches, like can i do 1200 at once

Don't take 1200 at once. The usual over-the-counter dose is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours, with no more than 1200 mg in a day unless a doctor tells you otherwise. Take it with food to protect your stomach. If the aches aren't controlled, you can alternate with acetaminophen rather than taking more ibuprofen, as long as you don't have liver issues.
Traveling to Ghana in 10 days, totally forgot about vaccines. Too late??

Not too late, but you need to move fast, so call a travel clinic or your doctor today. Ghana requires proof of yellow fever vaccination for entry, and that certificate only becomes valid 10 days after the shot, so you're right at the edge. You'll also likely need to discuss malaria pills, typhoid, and hepatitis A, and even a partial plan is much better than none.
I cracked my front tooth on a bottle. no pain but it looks bad. can I just superglue the piece back on??

Please don't use superglue in your mouth, because it isn't safe for oral tissue and it can damage the tooth or make proper repair harder. Keep the broken piece in milk or saliva and see a dentist within a day or two, since they can sometimes bond it back on. A crack can reach the nerve even without pain, so get it checked.
I'm 24 weeks pregnant with a pounding headache, is ibuprofen ok just this once?

Reach for acetaminophen instead. Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs are generally avoided from around 20 weeks because they can affect the baby's kidneys and amniotic fluid, and later in pregnancy a blood vessel in the baby's heart. Rest, fluids and a cool compress can help too. Since a severe headache in the second half of pregnancy can sometimes signal preeclampsia, call your OB promptly, especially if you also have vision changes, swelling or upper belly pain.
Cut my finger on a kitchen knife yesterday, today it's red around it and throbbing. Normal?

Some redness right at the edges is normal healing. Throbbing with spreading redness the next day suggests it may be getting infected. Wash it well, keep it clean and covered, and draw a pen line around the edge of the red area. If the redness moves past the line, you see red streaks or pus, or you get a fever, see a doctor today. Finger infections can spread into the tendons, so don't let this one ride.
Got diarrhea really bad on clindamycin, like 8 times today. Push through?

Don't push through this one; call your prescriber today. Frequent diarrhea on clindamycin can be C. diff, a gut infection that needs its own testing and treatment and can turn serious. Don't take Imodium unless a doctor says to, and keep drinking fluids with electrolytes. Go to urgent care or the ER if you see blood, have a fever or severe belly pain, or feel dizzy and dehydrated.
whats the fastest way to stop diarrhea, have a flight in 5 hours

Loperamide (Imodium) is the quickest option for a flight, usually 4 mg to start and then 2 mg after each loose stool, without going over the label maximum. Start sipping water or an electrolyte drink now, and keep eating light. Skip loperamide if you have a fever or blood in your stool, because then your body may need to clear an infection and slowing your gut can make things worse.
Can I drink alcohol on blood pressure medication?

Light drinking is generally fine with most blood pressure medications, but alcohol raises blood pressure over time and can boost the dizziness some drugs cause. Keep it to no more than one drink a day for women and two for men, and less is better. If you notice lightheadedness after drinking, mention it to your doctor or pharmacist.
burned my hand on a pan handle. butter or ice?

Neither. Butter traps heat and raises infection risk, and ice can damage the skin further. Run cool tap water over it for a solid 20 minutes, then cover it loosely with clean cling film or a non-stick dressing. If it blisters over an area bigger than your palm, looks white or leathery, or is on a joint, get it checked by a doctor.
is it safe to take my husband's nitroglycerin? i'm having chest tightness

Don't take someone else's nitroglycerin. It can drop your blood pressure dangerously, especially if you've taken erectile dysfunction medication or are dehydrated, and it wasn't prescribed for your situation. New chest tightness deserves a proper assessment, so call emergency services if it's ongoing or comes with breathlessness, sweating or nausea, or see a doctor today if it has already passed.
Is it true that keto cures type 2 diabetes? Thinking of stopping my metformin and going full keto

Keto can significantly lower blood sugar and some people reach remission, but please don't stop metformin on your own. If you take other glucose-lowering drugs like insulin or a sulfonylurea, cutting carbs suddenly can cause dangerous lows, and SGLT2 inhibitors combined with keto raise the risk of ketoacidosis. Tell your doctor you want to try a low-carb approach so they can adjust your medications safely and monitor your progress.
fever 3 days now, coughing, kinda short of breath walking up stairs. 45M. wait it out?

Don't wait any longer. Three days of fever plus a cough and new shortness of breath could be pneumonia, and a doctor should listen to your lungs, possibly order a chest X-ray, and check your oxygen level today. If you're short of breath at rest, have chest pain, or your lips look bluish, go to the ER.
I've been feeling exhausted for months and I think I'm low on iron. Should I just start taking iron pills?

Get a blood test first, including ferritin and a complete blood count, because fatigue has many possible causes and iron overload can damage your organs. If you do turn out to be iron deficient, your doctor will also want to find out why, especially if there's no obvious reason like heavy periods. Months of exhaustion is worth a proper checkup on its own.
can i drink baking soda water for indigestion

A small dose occasionally works as an antacid, about half a teaspoon dissolved fully in a glass of water, but it's not something to use regularly. It's high in sodium, and taking too much or taking it on a very full stomach can cause real problems, including rare stomach rupture. It's not a good option if you have high blood pressure, heart or kidney disease, or are pregnant. A standard antacid from the pharmacy is a safer bet.
52M, readings around 135/85 for a year. Doc never mentioned it. Should I care?

Yes, it's worth caring about. That's stage 1 range by current US guidelines, and a year of it is a real pattern. Your overall heart risk decides whether you need medication, so ask your doctor about it directly, ideally with a log of home readings. Cutting salt, exercising most days and limiting alcohol can realistically drop those numbers by 5 to 10 points.
My daughter (16) wants to get her ears pierced but she gets rashes from cheap earrings. Advice?

That rash is very likely a nickel allergy, so make sure the piercer uses implant-grade titanium, niobium or solid 14k-or-higher gold, and that she sticks with those metals afterward. A reputable studio that uses a needle rather than a gun is also the better choice for healing. If a rash shows up later anyway, have her switch to titanium posts and see a doctor if it oozes or doesn't settle, since an infection can look similar.
Can my 9 month old have cow's milk instead of formula now? Formula is so expensive.

Wait until 12 months to switch to cow's milk as the main drink. Before then, it can cause iron deficiency and puts strain on a baby's kidneys, while formula or breast milk give him what he needs. If cost is the problem, check whether you qualify for WIC. Store-brand formulas are also much cheaper and meet the same nutritional standards. Don't water formula down or make homemade formula, because both can be dangerous.
I need to drop 10 lbs fast now that I've finally recovered from bronchitis. Thinking two-a-days of HIIT. Good plan?

Jumping into twice-daily HIIT right after bronchitis is a fast route to setting yourself back, since your lungs and airways can stay sensitive for weeks. Start with moderate cardio like brisk walking or cycling a few times a week and build up gradually before adding any intense intervals. For weight loss, your eating habits will make a bigger difference than extreme training anyway. If you get wheezing, chest tightness or a returning cough, that's a sign to scale back.
is it fine to use my husband's prescription steroid cream on my rash

Hold off, because prescription steroid creams vary hugely in strength and the wrong one can thin the skin, especially on the face or skin folds. Steroids can also make some rashes worse, like fungal infections, which often look similar to eczema. For a mild itchy rash on the body you can try over-the-counter 1% hydrocortisone twice a day for up to a week. If the rash doesn't settle, see a doctor so you get the right diagnosis and the right strength.
I'm diabetic, 61, and feel really tired, short of breath and a bit sweaty but no chest pain. Could this be heart?

Yes, it could be, because people with diabetes and older adults often have heart attacks without classic chest pain, showing up instead as breathlessness, sweating, fatigue or nausea. That combination coming on now deserves urgent attention, so call 911 or have someone take you to the ER rather than resting it off. Check your blood sugar if you can do it quickly, since low sugar can cause sweating too, but don't let a normal reading reassure you or delay getting help.
I'm a nurse and feel feverish but we're short staffed. I'll just take Advil and go in, it's fine

I get the pressure, but working while feverish puts vulnerable patients at real risk, and Advil only hides the fever. It doesn't make you any less contagious. Call your charge nurse or occupational health, since most facilities have policies requiring febrile staff to stay home, and short staffing is their problem to solve, not yours. Rest, fluids, and a test for flu or COVID will tell you how long you need to be out.
Teen son came home with a cut on his eyebrow from a fight, it's about an inch, edges kinda apart

That one should be closed by a professional, ideally within 6 to 12 hours. The face heals well when it's closed neatly, and a gaping inch-long cut usually needs stitches, glue, or strips to avoid a noticeable scar. Hold firm pressure with a clean cloth until you get there. Also watch him for signs of a head injury, like confusion, vomiting, or a worsening headache, and ask whether he was hit hard enough to be dazed.
I'm 24, just diagnosed type 2, feeling really ashamed and kind of hopeless

That reaction is really common, but type 2 isn't a moral failing. Genetics play a huge role, and many people your age are diagnosed. The good news is that catching it early gives you real power, because changes in diet, activity and weight, plus medication if needed, can bring it under good control and sometimes into remission. Ask your doctor for a referral to diabetes education classes. They're practical, nonjudgmental and genuinely helpful.
I've had bronchitis for 2 weeks, cough is mostly gone. Can I do HIIT again?

Ease back in rather than jumping straight into HIIT. Your airways can stay irritated for a few weeks after bronchitis. Try a few moderate cardio sessions first and see how your breathing handles it, then add short intervals. If the cough flares up badly or you start wheezing, back off. If it keeps happening, check with your doctor, since lingering airway sensitivity sometimes needs treatment.
Do flu shots give you the flu? My coworker swears hers did.

No. The flu shot contains inactivated virus or just a viral protein, so it can't cause the flu. Some people get a sore arm, mild aches or a low fever for a day or two as the immune system responds, which can feel flu-ish. It also takes about two weeks to build protection, and the shot doesn't cover other viruses, so catching something around the same time is common and coincidental.
ear has been blocked and muffled since a flight 2 days ago

That's usually leftover pressure in the eustachian tube, and it often clears on its own. Try swallowing, yawning, chewing gum, or gently blowing with your nose pinched and mouth closed, and a decongestant nasal spray for a few days can help if you're stuffy. If you have significant pain, drainage, dizziness, or the muffling lasts more than a week, have a doctor check the eardrum.
Taking St John's Wort for low mood, also on birth control. Any issue?

Yes, this is an important one. St John's Wort speeds up how your body clears hormonal birth control and can make it fail, and breakthrough bleeding can be a warning sign. Use a backup method like condoms now, and talk to your doctor or pharmacist about whether to continue. It also interacts with many antidepressants, so if your low mood is persisting, a doctor can help you find a safer and more effective treatment.
I'm on sertraline and thinking about adding St John's Wort for an extra boost, natural so should be fine right?

Please don't combine those. St John's Wort raises serotonin too, and adding it to sertraline can cause serotonin syndrome, which brings agitation, a racing heart, sweating, muscle twitching and high fever, and can be serious. Being natural doesn't make it safe alongside a prescription drug. If you feel the sertraline isn't doing enough, talk to your prescriber, because a dose change or a different medication is the safe way to get that boost.
is it safe for my 87 year old grandma to take benadryl to help her sleep

It's best avoided. Diphenhydramine, the drug in Benadryl and most "PM" sleep aids, is on the list of medications older adults shouldn't take, because it can cause confusion, falls, constipation, and urinary retention. Talk to her doctor about the sleep problem itself. Pain, a medication, or a habit like long naps is often behind it. A consistent bedtime, daylight in the morning, and less caffeine after noon are safer places to start.
elderly mom getting confused suddenly over the last two days, she was sharp last week

Sudden confusion over a day or two is called delirium, and it needs medical attention today, not a wait-and-see. In older adults it's most often caused by an infection like a UTI or pneumonia, dehydration, a new medication, or low sodium, and these are usually very treatable once found. Take her to urgent care or the ER, and bring a list of her medications and a description of what she was like before. If she has trouble speaking, weakness on one side or a facial droop, call 911 instead, because that could be a stroke.
Dad's blood pressure reading at home was 185/110 but he feels fine. Can it wait till his appointment next month?

No, a reading that high shouldn't wait a month even if he feels fine. Have him rest quietly for five minutes and recheck. If it's still at or above 180/110, call his doctor today for guidance. If he has chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, vision changes, confusion or weakness, call emergency services immediately.
can i put my baby to sleep on her tummy, she sleeps so much better that way

Babies should be put down to sleep on their backs until their first birthday, because tummy sleeping significantly raises the risk of SIDS. Use a firm, flat mattress with no pillows, bumpers or loose blankets. A wearable sleep sack can help her feel snug. Once she can roll both ways on her own, it's fine to let her stay in whatever position she rolls into.
Painful blistery rash in a band on just one side of my ribs. Started with burning a few days ago. I'm 55.

A painful band of blisters on one side of the body that started with burning sounds a lot like shingles. Antiviral medication works best when started within about 72 hours of the rash appearing, so see a doctor today if you can. Keep the rash covered and avoid contact with pregnant women, newborns, and anyone with a weakened immune system until it crusts over, and get seen urgently if it's near your eye.
can i do hot yoga after being sick with a sinus infection last week

If you've finished treatment and feel mostly back to normal, it's probably fine. Still, I'd do one or two regular-temperature classes first. The heat adds a lot of dehydration and heart strain when you're not fully recovered. Hydrate well beforehand, and leave the room if you feel lightheaded.
my teen gets headaches and wants to take advil before every class basically

That's too frequent and can lead to rebound headaches, so it's worth finding the cause instead. Look at sleep, skipped breakfast, water intake, screen time and stress, and get an eye test. If the headaches keep coming most days, take your teen to their doctor so they can rule things out and set up a proper plan.
Is the HPV vaccine worth it for my 11 year old son? I thought it was a girl thing.

It's definitely for boys too, since HPV causes throat, anal, and penile cancers in men and boys can also spread it. Ages 11 to 12 is the ideal time because the immune response is stronger and only two doses are needed before age 15. It works best when given well before any possible exposure, which is why it's recommended now rather than later.
Stepped on a rusty nail in the garden. It went in maybe half an inch. Do I need a tetanus shot?

Probably yes, unless you've had a tetanus booster within the last 5 years, since a deep puncture is exactly the kind of wound that calls for one. Wash it well with soap and running water, but don't try to dig around inside it. Puncture wounds through a shoe can also carry bacteria deep into the foot, so get it seen at urgent care or by your GP today. Watch for redness, swelling or pus over the next few days.
Is it safe to get vaccines while breastfeeding?

Yes, nearly all vaccines are safe while breastfeeding, including flu, COVID, Tdap, and MMR, and you don't need to pump and dump.
