Some of the antibodies you make can even pass to your baby through your milk. The main exceptions involve certain travel vaccines like yellow fever, which needs a conversation with your doctor about the risks and benefits.
ringing in my ears after a concert last night, will it go away

Usually, yes. Ringing after a loud concert often fades within a day or two as your ears recover from the noise. Give your ears some quiet time and avoid loud noise for a few days. If it hasn't eased after about 48 hours, or your hearing feels muffled, get a hearing test soon, because sudden hearing loss responds best to early treatment. Next time, wear earplugs, since this kind of damage adds up over years.
Is it safe to keep a cat if my partner is allergic? We really want one.

It can work for some people with mild allergies, but it's a real gamble. A cat is a 15-year commitment, and rehoming is heartbreaking. Before adopting, have your partner spend extended time around cats, ideally a weekend somewhere with one, and see an allergist about testing and treatment options like immunotherapy. If your partner has asthma, be extra cautious, because cat allergen can trigger serious flare-ups. HEPA filters and a cat-free bedroom help but rarely eliminate symptoms.
fingertip got crushed in a car door, nail is purple and throbbing like crazy

That's blood trapped under the nail, and the pressure is what makes it throb so badly. Ice it and keep your hand raised for now. Then go to urgent care, where they can drain it quickly and painlessly to relieve the pressure and check for a broken fingertip bone. Don't try burning a hole through the nail at home. Go today, especially if more than a quarter of the nail is dark or the nail is loose or cut.
got a rash from a new laundry detergent, red and itchy all over my back. what do i do

This sounds like contact dermatitis, and it usually clears once you remove the trigger. Rewash your clothes and sheets in a fragrance-free, dye-free detergent, and run an extra rinse cycle. For the itch, hydrocortisone 1% cream twice a day, cool showers, and an oral antihistamine at night should help. See a doctor if it spreads, blisters heavily, or isn't improving after a week.
I have leftover amoxicillin from my last sinus infection. Can I just take it for this sore throat?

I'd skip it, because most sore throats are viral and amoxicillin won't touch them, plus a leftover partial course is the wrong dose and length even if it were bacterial. Taking random antibiotics can also mask strep and make a later test less reliable. If you have fever, swollen tonsils with white patches and no cough, get a quick strep test, otherwise warm fluids, honey and ibuprofen will carry you through.
Do those wrist BP monitors actually work or should I get an arm one?

Get an upper-arm cuff if you can, because those are generally more accurate and less sensitive to how you position your wrist. Choose a validated model, and measure your arm so you get the right cuff size, since a too-small cuff reads falsely high. Bring it to your next appointment so the clinic can check it against their equipment.
chest pain after cocaine last night, still kinda there. dont want to get in trouble

Please get seen now. Cocaine can cause heart attacks, dangerous rhythms and tears in major blood vessels, even in young healthy people, and pain that's still there the next day needs checking. ER staff are there to treat you, not report you, and telling them about the cocaine actually changes which medications are safe for you. Go to the emergency department or call an ambulance.
my migraines come with an aura. someone said I shouldn't be on the combined pill, is that true or just overcautious

It's true, not overcautious. Migraine with aura already slightly raises stroke risk, and estrogen-containing birth control raises it further. That's why guidelines generally rule out the combined pill for people with aura. Progestin-only pills, hormonal IUDs, the implant and copper IUDs are good alternatives, so talk to your prescriber about switching.
Is it ok to go to the gym with a cold? I hate missing workouts.

A common rule of thumb is the neck check: if your symptoms are above the neck, like a runny nose, mild congestion or a scratchy throat, light to moderate exercise is usually fine. If you have a fever, body aches, chest congestion or feel wiped out, skip it, because hard exercise with a fever puts real strain on your heart. Either way, wipe down equipment and consider working out at home for a few days so you don't share it with everyone at the gym.
toddler swallowed a button battery i think?? he seems fine

Go to the emergency room immediately, even if he seems fine. Swallowed button batteries can burn through the esophagus within about two hours. If he's over 12 months old and it's within 12 hours of swallowing, you can give him 2 teaspoons of honey every 10 minutes on the way, up to 6 doses, to help protect the tissue. Don't make him vomit, and bring the battery packaging if you have it.
I'm 30 weeks pregnant and my tooth is killing me. What can I take?

Acetaminophen at standard doses is the preferred pain reliever in pregnancy, while ibuprofen and other NSAIDs should generally be avoided after about 20 weeks. Warm salt water rinses can also help. Dental care is safe and important during pregnancy, including X-rays with shielding and local anesthetic, so call your dentist rather than waiting until after delivery. Let your OB know too, especially if there's any swelling or fever.
honestly just tired of everything. not suicidal just tired

Thanks for saying it, because 'tired of everything' is worth taking seriously even when it's not about wanting to die. When it lasts more than a couple of weeks, it often points to depression, burnout or a physical cause like low iron or thyroid problems. A GP visit can check both sides. In the meantime, try telling one person you trust how you're really feeling, and if things shift toward darker thoughts, reach out to a crisis line straight away.
do i really need to carry two epipens? one is annoying enough

Yes, carry two, because a single dose of epinephrine doesn't stop a severe reaction in a meaningful number of cases, and symptoms can return before help arrives. Auto-injectors can also misfire or be used incorrectly under stress. A small pouch that holds both pens makes carrying them a lot less annoying.
fishhook stuck in my finger past the barb. youtube says push it through and snip it. legit?

That push-through method is legit and works for shallow hooks in fleshy spots, if you have clean cutters and can tolerate it. Don't attempt it if the hook is near a joint, tendon, eye or face, or is deeply buried, and go to urgent care instead. Either way, wash it well afterward, and check that your tetanus shot is current within the last 5 years.
32 weeks and I haven't felt the baby move much today. Probably just sleeping right? I don't want to bother the hospital.

Please don't wait on this. A noticeable decrease in movement at 32 weeks is exactly what labor and delivery units want you to call about, any time of day or night. You're not bothering them. Lie on your left side and focus for a bit, but if movements still seem reduced, call or go in now for monitoring rather than waiting until tomorrow. Usually everything is fine, but this is one where checking quickly really matters.
How do I know if a cut needs stitches? Mine is on my eyebrow from a cabinet door.

As a rough rule, a cut needs closing if it's gaping, deeper than a few millimetres, longer than about a centimetre, or still bleeding after 10 minutes of pressure. Face cuts are worth getting closed properly for cosmetic reasons. Eyebrow cuts often bleed dramatically and usually do well with glue or strips at urgent care. Try to get it seen within a few hours, and seek care urgently if you have a headache, vomiting, or vision changes after the knock.
Can dehydration really cause a headache or is that a myth?

It's real. Even mild dehydration can bring on a headache, and it often eases within an hour or so of drinking a couple of glasses of water. It's an easy first thing to try before reaching for painkillers.
quick q, how long should i ice a sprain

Ice for about 15 to 20 minutes at a time with a cloth between the ice and your skin, and repeat every two to three hours for the first two days or so. Going longer than 20 minutes doesn't help and can cause frostbite-type skin damage. Combine it with elevation and gentle compression, then start easy movement as soon as pain allows.
pneumonia last month. still get winded climbing stairs. normal?

Some lingering breathlessness is common for several weeks after pneumonia, especially as you start moving more again. Gentle walking that you increase gradually tends to help. If it isn't steadily improving, if it's getting worse, or if you have chest pain or a cough that won't quit, see your doctor. They may want a follow-up chest X-ray to make sure the infection has fully cleared.
hi! 6 month old, 101.5 after shots this morning. normal?

Yes, a mild fever in the day or two after vaccines is a common, normal immune response. You can give infant acetaminophen dosed for her weight if she's fussy, offer plenty of feeds, and dress her lightly. Call her pediatrician if it goes above 104°F, lasts more than 48 hours, or she cries inconsolably for hours or seems unusually limp.
My dad is 87 and still insists on driving. He's gotten lost twice and clipped a mailbox. How do I handle this without a huge fight?

Getting lost and minor crashes are real warning signs, so it's worth acting now. Often the smoothest route is asking his doctor to raise it, since many older adults accept it better from a physician. A formal driving evaluation through an occupational therapist can also give an objective answer. Have practical alternatives ready, like rides from family or a ride service, because losing independence is usually what he's really fighting.
found my grandma's old fish oil pills, they expired in 2021. still ok?

I'd toss them. Fish oil goes rancid over time, and oxidized oil is less effective and may not be good for you. If they smell strongly fishy or sour when you break one open, that settles it. A fresh bottle is cheap.
My 6 year old got bitten on the cheek by our friend's dog. It's a cut maybe half an inch, bleeding a bit. She's calm now. Do we need the ER or just urgent care?

She should be seen today, and for a face bite on a child an ER or urgent care with pediatric experience is a good choice. Facial bites often need careful cleaning and sometimes stitches to heal with minimal scarring, and doctors will decide about antibiotics. In the meantime, apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth and rinse the wound with clean water. Also confirm the dog's rabies vaccination status with your friend, since the doctor will ask.
What's the fastest way to make myself throw up? Ate something sketchy.

Don't make yourself throw up; it can damage your esophagus and teeth, and it usually doesn't clear much anyway. If the food was just questionable, sip fluids, eat bland food and let your body handle it, since most mild food poisoning passes within a day or two. If you think you swallowed something toxic, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 in the US. Get medical care if you develop bloody diarrhea, a high fever, signs of dehydration, or vomiting that won't stop.
My husband snores like a chainsaw and sometimes he just stops breathing for a few seconds then gasps. Should I be worried?

Yes, that pattern of loud snoring, pauses in breathing and gasping is a classic sign of obstructive sleep apnea, and it's worth taking seriously. Untreated apnea raises the risk of high blood pressure, heart disease, stroke and drowsy-driving accidents. He should see his doctor and ask about a sleep study, which can often be done at home now. Treatment such as a CPAP machine or an oral appliance usually makes a dramatic difference, often for your sleep too.
baby is 7 weeks old and has a temp of 100.6. is that a big deal

Yes, a temperature of 100.4°F or higher in a baby under 3 months needs to be seen by a doctor right away, even if the baby seems okay. Call your pediatrician now, and if you can't reach them quickly, go to the ER. Young infants can't fight infections well and can get very sick fast, so this isn't a wait-and-see situation. Don't give any fever medicine until a doctor tells you to.
Baby has a rash all over after starting amoxicillin day 5. Stop it?

Call the prescriber or the after-hours line today before you skip or stop any doses. A blotchy rash that shows up around day 5 of amoxicillin is common and often isn't a true allergy, but a doctor needs to look at it to decide. Go to the ER right away if you see hives with swelling of the lips or face, trouble breathing, vomiting, or blistering or peeling skin.
Took one dose of cephalexin and now I have hives all over. What now

Stop taking it and call your prescriber or pharmacist now. You'll need a different antibiotic, and the reaction should be recorded as an allergy. An antihistamine like cetirizine or diphenhydramine can calm the hives. Call 911 or go to the ER immediately if you have any throat tightness, trouble breathing, swelling of your lips or tongue, wheezing, or feel faint. Those are signs of anaphylaxis.
Got some sun yesterday and now I have big blisters on my shoulders. Just aloe right?

Aloe and cool showers help, and ibuprofen eases pain and swelling. Leave the blisters intact, wear loose clothing, and drink plenty of water. Blistering means it's a second-degree burn. See a doctor if the blisters cover a large area, or if you get a fever, chills, dizziness, or signs of infection.
is a fever of 104 going to cause brain damage in my kid

Fevers from infection, even 104°F, don't cause brain damage. Temperatures that dangerous come from heatstroke, not illness. That said, a 104 fever is a good reason to call your pediatrician, and how your child is acting matters more than the number itself. Go in right away if they're very lethargic, hard to wake, struggling to breathe, have a stiff neck or rash, or aren't drinking.
ok so my throat is killing me, no cough at all, fever, swollen glands. just a cold right?

That combination, a bad sore throat with fever and swollen glands but no cough, is actually classic for strep rather than a cold. It's worth getting a quick strep test at a clinic or urgent care, because strep needs antibiotics and untreated it can occasionally cause complications. Meanwhile, ibuprofen and warm drinks or cold popsicles can ease the pain. Go in right away if you can't swallow your saliva or you're having trouble opening your mouth.
I stepped on a rusty nail in my garage. It went pretty deep through my shoe. I cleaned it, do I need to do anything else?

The big question is your tetanus shot: if your last booster was more than five years ago for a puncture like this, or you're not sure, get one within the next day or two. Deep punctures through a shoe also carry a real infection risk because bits of debris get pushed in, so it's worth having a clinician look at it, especially on the bottom of the foot. In the meantime, keep it clean and covered. Get seen promptly if it becomes red, hot, swollen, or more painful over the next few days.
I'm pregnant (28 weeks) and can't get comfortable at all. Is it true I can't sleep on my back?

In the third trimester it's best to fall asleep on your side, because lying flat on your back lets the weight of your uterus press on a major blood vessel, which can reduce blood flow. Don't panic if you wake up on your back; just roll back onto your side. A pregnancy pillow or regular pillows between your knees and behind your back can make side sleeping much more comfortable. Either side is fine, though many people find the left side most comfortable.
I'm recovering from covid but my heart rate goes to 140 just walking up the stairs. Normal?

That's worth getting checked by a doctor before you push your exercise any further. A high heart rate with minimal effort after covid can be simple deconditioning, but it can also point to heart inflammation or POTS. A doctor can do an ECG and maybe some blood tests to rule things out. Stick to gentle activity until you've been seen.
teen daughter fainted after her HPV shot. Should she skip the second dose?

Fainting after a shot is a common reaction in teens. It's caused by the needle and the stress of the moment, not by the vaccine itself, and it's no reason to skip the next dose. Tell the nurse beforehand so she can get the shot lying down and rest for about 15 minutes afterward, which makes another faint much less likely. Eating and drinking before the visit helps too.
just need a quick answer can i give my 8 month old aspirin for fever

No. Aspirin shouldn't be given to children or teenagers because it's linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare but dangerous condition affecting the liver and brain. For an 8 month old, use infant acetaminophen or infant ibuprofen, dosed by weight. If you're unsure of the dose, a pharmacist can confirm it quickly.
Cut my leg on a chainsaw, it's bleeding a lot and soaking through towels

Call emergency services now. Press hard directly on the wound with a cloth and don't let up. If blood soaks through, add more layers on top without removing the first ones, and don't stop pressing. If you have a tourniquet and the bleeding won't stop with pressure, apply it high and tight above the wound and note the time.
whats the fastest way to make a cut heal before my wedding saturday

Keep it clean, covered and lightly moist with petroleum jelly under a bandage, because moist healing is faster and scars less than letting it scab. Don't pick at it, and avoid harsh antiseptics after the first wash. Eating and sleeping well genuinely help too. If it's on a visible spot and still noticeable by Friday, a dab of concealer over a fully closed wound is fine. Just don't put makeup on an open cut.
What's the fastest way to get rid of a cold sore before my wedding Saturday

Your best bet is to start an antiviral right away, ideally prescription valacyclovir, which can shorten an outbreak if you take it early. A pharmacist, GP, or telehealth doctor can often prescribe it the same day, and over-the-counter docosanol cream is a weaker backup. Don't pick or squeeze the sore, because that spreads the virus and slows healing. By Saturday, a medicated cold sore patch can cover it smoothly under makeup without irritating it.
dog bit my lip and it's split open pretty good, bleeding a lot

Press firmly on it with a clean cloth for 10 minutes without peeking. Then head to urgent care or the ER, because a split lip from a bite usually needs a professional cleaning and possibly stitches to heal well and look right. Face bites also need careful infection prevention, so expect antibiotics, and they'll check your tetanus status too.
quick q. kid has pinkeye, can he go to school

Usually yes, once treatment has started or the gunky discharge has settled. Many schools let kids back after 24 hours on antibiotic drops for bacterial pinkeye, but check your school's specific rule. Have him wash his hands often and not share towels or pillows. See a doctor if his eye is very painful, his vision seems blurry, his eyelid is swollen and red, or it isn't improving after a few days.
What's the deal with magnesium for sleep? Which kind?

The evidence for magnesium and sleep is modest, but some people do notice they relax and fall asleep a bit more easily. Magnesium glycinate is the usual pick because it's well absorbed and gentle on the stomach. Citrate works too but can loosen your bowels. Take 200 to 350 mg in the evening, and check with your doctor first if you have kidney problems.
can i eat sushi pregnant

Sushi made with cooked fish, such as eel or shrimp, or vegetable rolls is fine, and so is sushi made from raw fish that has been properly frozen first, which is standard practice in many countries. Steer clear of high-mercury fish like swordfish, king mackerel and bigeye tuna. Avoid sushi from places where you can't be confident about freshness and hygiene, because listeria and other bacteria are a bigger risk for you right now.
do i need to take vitamin C when i have a cold

Once a cold has started, vitamin C barely changes anything. Taking it regularly beforehand may shorten colds slightly, but the effect is small. Rest, fluids and time do most of the work. Megadoses above about 2 grams a day mostly just cause diarrhea.
My son is 7 and still wets the bed most nights. My mother-in-law says I should punish him. Thoughts?

Skip the punishment. Bedwetting at 7 is common and usually comes down to a bladder or arousal system that's still maturing, not laziness or defiance, and shaming him tends to make it worse. Limiting drinks in the evening, having him pee right before bed, and using a bedwetting alarm can all help a lot. It's worth mentioning at his next checkup, and sooner if he's started wetting again after being dry, it hurts to pee, or he's drinking far more than usual.
ok so i think im allergic to my new cat. do i have to give it up??

Not necessarily, because a lot of people manage cat allergies with a combination of steps. Keep the cat out of your bedroom, run a HEPA air purifier, vacuum with a HEPA filter often, and take a daily antihistamine or steroid nasal spray. If you're wheezing, short of breath or developing asthma symptoms, though, see a doctor soon. An allergist can confirm the allergy and talk to you about allergy shots, which can reduce your sensitivity over time.
Is it ok to sleep on my back? I'm 26 weeks and it's the only comfy position

From the third trimester on, side sleeping is recommended, because lying flat on your back can compress a major vein and reduce blood flow. If you wake up on your back, don't panic; just roll onto your side. A pregnancy pillow, or a wedge behind your back, makes side sleeping much more comfortable and keeps you from rolling over.
My 10 year old had the flu last week and wants to go back to soccer practice. Fever's been gone 3 days. Okay?

If the fever has been gone for at least 24 hours without fever-reducing medicine and they're eating and acting normally, easing back into practice is generally fine. Kids often tire faster for a week or two after the flu, so let the coach know they may need breaks. If they complain of chest pain, fainting, or unusual shortness of breath, pull them out and call the doctor.
my arm is super sore after my tetanus shot yesterday, is that normal or did they hit something wrong

That's completely normal. Tetanus shots are known for causing a sore, sometimes swollen arm for two or three days, because the vaccine triggers a local immune reaction in the muscle. Keep moving the arm gently, use a cool compress, and take ibuprofen or acetaminophen if you need it. See a doctor if the redness spreads beyond a few inches, the pain gets worse after day three, or you can't lift your arm properly.
Can I give my 85yo mother some of my Ambien? She can't sleep and her doctor appointment isn't for 3 weeks.

Please don't. Ambien and similar sleeping pills significantly raise the risk of falls, confusion and next-day grogginess in older adults, and a dose meant for you could be too strong for her. Call her doctor's office now instead of waiting three weeks. They can often advise by phone, and the cause of new insomnia, like pain, depression or a medication side effect, is worth sorting out.
Food poisoning probably from sushi. When should I actually go to a doctor?

Most food poisoning clears up within one to three days with rest and steady sips of fluids. Go to a doctor if you have a fever over about 102°F (39°C), bloody diarrhea, or can't keep fluids down. You should also go if you have signs of dehydration like dizziness and very little urine, or if symptoms last more than three days. Any numbness, tingling, blurred vision or trouble swallowing after eating fish needs emergency care right away. Skip anti-diarrheal medicine if you have a fever or blood in your stool.
My 8yo got stung by a bee and now her lips look puffy and she says her throat feels weird

Call 911 now, because puffy lips and a strange feeling in her throat after a sting can be the start of anaphylaxis. If anyone has an epinephrine auto-injector, use it on her outer thigh right away. Keep her sitting up if she's struggling to breathe, or lying down with her legs raised if she feels faint. Don't drive her yourself or wait to see if it passes.
I read that beet juice lowers BP. Could I replace my amlodipine with beet juice and garlic?

I wouldn't swap them. Beet juice and garlic may lower blood pressure a few points in studies, but that's much weaker and less reliable than amlodipine. Uncontrolled pressure quietly raises your risk of stroke and heart attack. If you want to rely less on medication, talk to your doctor about a plan where you track home readings and taper only if your numbers support it.
Can I just skip my kid's MMR? Measles seems basically gone anyway.

I'd strongly advise against skipping it, because measles only seems rare where vaccination rates are high, and outbreaks keep popping up wherever they dip. Measles is extremely contagious and can cause pneumonia, brain swelling, and death, especially in young children. Two doses of MMR are about 97% effective, and it's one of the safest, best-studied vaccines we have. If you have specific worries, your pediatrician is happy to walk through them with you.
pooped and it was black and tarry. didn't eat anything weird. im 58

Black, tarry stool can mean bleeding higher up in the digestive tract, like from a stomach ulcer, so please get medical care today rather than waiting. Iron pills and Pepto-Bismol can also turn stool black, but if you haven't taken either, assume it needs checking. Go to the ER right away if you feel dizzy, faint, short of breath, or vomit anything that looks like blood or coffee grounds. Don't drive yourself if you feel lightheaded.
teen athlete fainted during basketball, seems fine now. coach says just hydrate more

Fainting during exercise, as opposed to after, is a red flag in young athletes and needs a proper heart evaluation before they play again, even if they feel fine now. Book a doctor's visit promptly and ask about an ECG and referral to a cardiologist, since conditions like cardiomyopathy or rhythm disorders can show up this way. Make sure the coach knows they're benched until cleared, and mention any family history of sudden death or fainting.
Spilled boiling water down my thigh about 20 mins ago. Big blisters forming, area is maybe the size of two hands. I don't want to go to ER for a blister.

A blistering burn bigger than about one palm is the kind that needs a doctor, so please go to urgent care or the ER today. If you haven't already, put it under cool running water now, since it still helps up to three hours after the burn. Then cover it loosely with cling film for the trip. Burns that size can get infected or scar badly without proper dressings, and they're also more painful to manage on your own than you'd expect.
cat scratch on my wrist from 2 weeks ago, now there's a swollen lump in my armpit. connected??

Quite possibly, because that pattern fits cat scratch disease, a Bartonella infection that causes swollen lymph nodes near a scratch one to three weeks later. It's often mild, but see your doctor so they can examine the node and decide whether you need antibiotics or other tests. Go sooner if you have a high fever, the lump is very painful or red, or you feel generally unwell.
My daughter's 6 months old and I'm scared to introduce eggs and peanuts. Should I just wait until she's older?

Current guidance actually favors introducing common allergens like peanut and egg around this age, because early introduction can lower the risk of developing an allergy. Use safe forms like smooth peanut butter thinned into puree and well-cooked egg, never whole nuts, and offer them at home at a time when you can watch her afterward. If she has severe eczema or an existing food allergy, talk to her pediatrician first, since they may want testing or a supervised first try.
Detailed question: I'm 34, breastfeeding a 4 month old, vegetarian, and wondering which supplements actually matter for me and the baby right now.

The big ones are B12, since vegetarians often run low and your milk levels depend on your intake, plus iodine, around 150 mcg a day, and continuing a prenatal or postnatal multivitamin. DHA from an algae-based omega-3 is worth adding since you're skipping fish. Separately, breastfed babies are usually advised to get 400 IU of vitamin D drops daily, so confirm that with your pediatrician. Your doctor can also check your iron and vitamin D levels to fine-tune things.
My 3 yo got into the dishwasher pods, might have bitten one. some foam on lips.

Wipe her mouth out with a damp cloth, have her rinse or sip a little water if she can, and call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 right now. Detergent pods are highly concentrated and can burn the mouth and throat. Call 911 or go to the ER immediately if she's coughing, drooling, having trouble breathing or swallowing, or vomiting. Don't try to make her throw up.
Taking lisinopril. Allowed to use those salt substitutes?

Be careful with them. Most salt substitutes are potassium chloride, and lisinopril already raises potassium, so together they can push it to dangerous levels that affect your heart rhythm. Ask your doctor before using one, especially if you also take a potassium-sparing diuretic or have kidney issues. Herbs, lemon and spice blends without potassium are a safer way to cut sodium.
teenager here, braces got tightened yesterday and everything aches, cant even chew

That ache after a tightening is normal and usually peaks in the first two or three days before easing off. Eat soft foods like pasta, yogurt and eggs, take ibuprofen or acetaminophen as the label says, and rinse with warm salt water if your mouth is sore. Call your orthodontist if a wire is stabbing your cheek or the pain is still bad after a week.
Lump on my eyelid, not painful, been there 3 weeks. Stye?

A painless eyelid bump that's lingered for weeks is most likely a chalazion, which is a blocked oil gland rather than an infection like a stye. Warm compresses for 10 minutes a few times a day, with gentle massage, often help it drain over several weeks. Don't squeeze or poke it. If it keeps growing, affects your vision, bleeds, or causes lash loss, have an eye doctor check it, since a few lid lumps need a closer look or minor drainage.
I'm 16 and do gymnastics. My lower back hurts when I bend backwards. Coach says push through it.

Don't push through it, because pain when arching backwards in young gymnasts is a classic sign of spondylolysis, a stress fracture in the lower spine. It heals well when caught early and rested, but can worsen if you keep training on it. Ask a parent to book you in with a doctor or sports medicine clinic, and stop backbends and arching moves until you've been checked.
my dad is 61 and says his chest feels tight and heavy and it's going into his left arm, he wants to just lie down and see if it passes

Call emergency services right now and don't let him lie down to wait it out, because chest heaviness spreading to the arm in a 61-year-old is a classic heart attack pattern. While you wait, have him chew one regular 325 mg aspirin if he isn't allergic and hasn't been told to avoid it. Keep him sitting comfortably, unlock the door for paramedics, and don't drive him yourself unless there's truly no ambulance available.
My rabbit scratched my arm pretty bad when I picked him up, like several long scratches. Rabbits are harmless right?

Pet rabbits are very low risk for rabies, but their nails can still carry bacteria, so treat this like any good scratch. Wash each scratch with soap and running water, apply antibiotic ointment and cover them. Watch for spreading redness, swelling or pus over the next few days, and check that your tetanus shot is up to date if the scratches are deep. Supporting his hindquarters when you lift him can help prevent the kicking next time.
my sister says one glass of wine a week is totally fine in pregnancy, her doctor in france said so. true?

There's no amount of alcohol that's been shown to be safe in pregnancy, which is why the major medical bodies recommend avoiding it entirely. Alcohol crosses the placenta freely, and the risk of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders isn't limited to heavy drinking. If you've already had a drink before you knew you were pregnant, don't panic, because that's very common, but stopping now is the safest choice. Alcohol-free wines and a good mocktail can help scratch the itch.
burned my hand on the oven rack, my grandma says put butter on it. yes or no

No, skip the butter, because it traps heat in the skin and can raise the risk of infection. Run cool (not ice-cold) tap water over the burn for a full 20 minutes, then cover it loosely with clean cling film or a non-stick dressing. If the burn is larger than your palm, blisters heavily, looks white or leathery, or is on your face, hands' creases or joints and isn't settling, get it checked at urgent care.
Had a lumbar puncture yesterday and now I get a massive headache whenever I stand up, goes away lying down. Normal?

That's a known complication called a post-dural puncture headache, caused by spinal fluid leaking from the puncture site. Lie flat as much as you can, stay hydrated, and caffeine can help, but call the team that did the procedure today. If it persists they can do a quick fix called a blood patch, and you should seek care urgently if you get fever, a stiff neck or confusion.
I have leftover oxycodone from my surgery last year. Can I use it for my bad back flare?

Don't use it. Opioids aren't recommended for ordinary back flares, because they work no better than other options for this kind of pain and carry real risks like dependence, drowsiness and dangerous interactions with alcohol or sleep medicines. Old pills may also not be the right dose for you now. Try heat, gentle movement and over-the-counter pain relievers instead, and see your doctor if those aren't enough. Take the leftover pills to a pharmacy take-back so they're disposed of safely.
My doctor offered me propranolol for performance anxiety before presentations. Is that a legit thing?

Yes, it's a common and legitimate use. Propranolol blocks the physical symptoms of adrenaline, like a pounding heart, shaking hands, and a shaky voice, without making you drowsy or foggy. Doctors usually suggest a test dose on a normal day first so you know how it feels. It isn't suitable if you have asthma or certain heart conditions, so make sure your doctor knows your full history.
what's the fastest way to fall asleep, I have a big exam at 8am

Put away screens, keep the room dark and cool, and try slow breathing with a longer exhale, like in for 4 and out for 6 or 8, for a few minutes. Don't take a sleeping pill you've never used before an exam, since you could feel foggy in the morning. Even if you sleep poorly, one short night won't tank your performance as much as you fear, and your adrenaline will carry you through. Set two alarms so you can stop worrying about oversleeping.
can i double my bp pill today since i forgot yesterday

No, don't double up, because that can drop your pressure too low and make you dizzy or faint. Just take today's dose as usual and carry on. If you miss doses often, a weekly pill organizer or a phone alarm really helps.
Can I give my 10 month old Benadryl so he sleeps on the flight

Please don't. Diphenhydramine isn't recommended for babies under 2 and can cause dangerous breathing problems. In some kids it backfires and causes hyperactivity instead. Feeding or offering a pacifier during takeoff and landing, keeping his usual sleep routine and bringing familiar comforts work better. If he has a cold or ear issue before the flight, check with your pediatrician.
Woke up with my lips and eyelids swollen and hives everywhere. I can breathe fine. Just take an antihistamine?

A non-drowsy antihistamine like cetirizine is reasonable for hives, but swelling of the lips and eyelids means you should get checked by a doctor today rather than wait it out. Go straight to emergency care or call emergency services if you notice any tongue or throat swelling, trouble swallowing, wheezing, hoarseness or feeling faint, because that can be anaphylaxis. Think back over anything new in the last day, such as foods, medications or products, so you can tell the doctor.
can i get the flu shot while i have a cold

With a mild cold and no fever, yes, you can get the flu shot. A minor illness doesn't make it less effective or less safe. If you're running a fever or feel properly sick, wait until you've recovered so your symptoms don't get confused with side effects. A runny nose alone isn't a reason to skip it.
can i just take some of my wife's leftover amoxicillin for this cold? i have a big week at work

Skip it, because colds are caused by viruses and amoxicillin does nothing against them, so you'd get the side effects and the antibiotic-resistance risk with zero benefit. A partial leftover course isn't the right dose for anything anyway. For the week ahead, lean on rest when you can, fluids, and ibuprofen or acetaminophen for aches. See a doctor if you're getting worse after about 10 days or you develop a high fever or facial pain.
how do i know if i need therapy or if im just being dramatic

Ask yourself whether what you're feeling is affecting your sleep, work, relationships or enjoyment of things, or whether it has lasted more than a couple of weeks. If it has, therapy is a reasonable step, not a dramatic one. You also don't need to be in crisis to go, since plenty of people use it to handle stress or patterns they want to change. The fact that you're asking is a decent sign it's worth a try.
my 2 month old feels hot, thermometer says 38.2 rectal. should i just give some tylenol and see how she does overnight?

Don't wait this one out. Any fever of 38.0°C (100.4°F) or higher in a baby under 3 months needs to be checked by a doctor right away, so call your pediatrician's after-hours line or head to the ER now. Hold off on Tylenol until a doctor has seen her, since it can mask the fever they need to assess and dosing at this age should come from them.
I'm 68 and my doctor put me on lisinopril. Now my lip swelled up out of nowhere. Coincidence?

Probably not, because lisinopril and other ACE inhibitors can cause angioedema, which is sudden swelling of the lips, face or tongue, even after months of uneventful use. If your tongue or throat swells or you have any trouble breathing or swallowing, call emergency services immediately, since antihistamines often don't stop this type of reaction. Even if the swelling is mild, call your doctor today, because you'll likely need to stop the medication and switch to a different blood pressure drug.
Can I use bleach on toenail fungus? saw it online

Don't use bleach, because it can burn the skin around the nail and doesn't penetrate the nail well enough to cure the fungus anyway. Proven options are prescription antifungal tablets like terbinafine, which work best, or medicated nail solutions like efinaconazole for milder cases. Ask your GP to confirm it's actually fungus, because psoriasis and nail damage can look the same. Keep the nails trimmed and your feet dry while you treat it, and expect several months before the nail grows out clear.
how much water should i drink when i have diarrhea, i feel kinda dizzy

Dizziness means you're probably already dehydrated, so oral rehydration salts or an electrolyte drink are better than plain water, taken as steady sips rather than big gulps. Aim to replace roughly a cup after each loose stool on top of your normal intake. If the dizziness doesn't improve within a few hours of drinking, you faint, or you can't keep fluids down, get seen today, because IV fluids can fix this quickly.
real quick: can i swim laps while i still have a lingering cough

If it's just a mild leftover cough with no fever and you feel good, easy laps are generally fine. Keep the pace gentle, because swimming limits your breathing pattern and a hard set can trigger coughing fits. If the cough is deep and productive, or comes with wheezing, rest a few more days.
Ran out of my inhaler. Can I use my sister's? Same color basically.

Color tells you nothing, because different inhalers can contain completely different drugs, and some don't work fast enough to help an attack. If hers is an albuterol rescue inhaler, borrowing it in a pinch is far safer than going without. The real fix is calling your pharmacy today, since many pharmacists can give an emergency supply. If you're struggling to breathe right now and nothing is helping, call emergency services.
quick q - can i drink tonight after my covid shot

A drink or two is fine and won't affect how well the vaccine works. I'd just go easy, since alcohol can make the tiredness, headache, or achiness some people get after the shot feel worse, and it dehydrates you. If you start feeling crummy, water and rest are the better call tonight.
can i double up my blood pressure pill since i forgot it this morning and its night now

Don't double up, because two doses close together can drop your blood pressure too far and leave you dizzy or faint. If it's still well before your next scheduled dose, you can usually take the missed one now. If you're close to tomorrow's dose, skip it and carry on as normal. Missing a single day is rarely dangerous, and a weekly pill organizer or phone alarm makes it less likely to happen again.
Whats the deal with collagen powder, worth it?

There's modest evidence that collagen peptides can slightly improve skin elasticity and possibly joint comfort, but the effects are small and some of the studies are industry-funded. Your body breaks collagen down into amino acids anyway, so getting enough protein overall matters more. If you enjoy it and the cost doesn't bother you, it's harmless for most people, so just treat it as a nice extra rather than a must-have.
Thinking about taking melatonin every night long term, any issues?

Melatonin is fairly low-risk, but most people take far more than they need. A dose of 0.5 to 3 mg about an hour before bed usually works as well as the 10 mg gummies, with less grogginess the next day. Long-term data is limited, though, and if you need something every night to fall asleep, that's worth bringing up with a doctor. Insomnia often has a fixable cause, and CBT-I, a short form of therapy for insomnia, works better than any pill in the long run.
I'm 72, recovering from shingles. The rash is healing but I'm tired all the time. Can I resume my water aerobics class?

Wait until every blister has fully crusted over before getting in a shared pool, because until then you can spread the virus. Fatigue after shingles is common, so start with a shorter or gentler session and see how you feel. If you have lingering nerve pain, the warm water may actually feel good. Let your doctor know if the exhaustion doesn't start lifting within a few weeks.
Stomach hurts. Fix?

Depends on the kind of pain, but for mild, crampy discomfort you can try sipping water, applying a heating pad, eating something bland or skipping a meal, and avoiding alcohol, coffee and greasy food for now. If you think it's gas, a short walk often helps. Get seen quickly if the pain is severe, settles in one spot (especially lower right), lasts more than a day, or comes with fever, vomiting, blood or a hard, swollen belly.
Teenager with asthma wants to try out for track. Should we avoid it?

No need to avoid it, since plenty of elite athletes have asthma. Make sure their asthma is well controlled day to day, and ask the doctor about taking two puffs of the rescue inhaler about 15 minutes before running, which prevents exercise-induced symptoms for many people. A good warm-up helps too. Your teen should keep the inhaler with them at practice, and the coach should know about it.
Is it fine to replace two meals a day with protein shakes long term?

It can work short term for convenience, but over the long haul you miss the fiber, phytonutrients and variety of real food, and it's hard to sustain. A better plan is to use one shake as a meal or snack and keep the other meals built around vegetables, whole grains and protein. If you're doing this for weight loss or a medical reason, a dietitian can make sure you aren't missing anything.
Burning in the middle of my chest after big meals, worse lying down. 31, no heart issues. Heartburn?

That pattern fits heartburn (acid reflux) well: burning behind the breastbone after large meals that gets worse when you lie down. Smaller meals, not eating within three hours of bed, raising the head of your bed and an antacid or short course of an over-the-counter acid reducer usually help. See a doctor if it lasts more than a few weeks or you have trouble swallowing or weight loss. Get urgent help if a chest pain feels different, like pressure, or comes with exertion, sweating or breathlessness.
quick q - is chest pain on the right side less serious than left?

Not reliably. Heart pain is often central or felt across the chest, and it can show up on the right side, in the arm, the jaw or the back. Right-sided pain also has its own serious causes, like a lung clot or collapsed lung. What matters more is how the pain behaves: pressure, exertion-related pain, breathlessness, sweating or nausea all deserve urgent attention whichever side it's on.
My grandmother swears by putting butter on burns. My son (7) touched the oven door. Should I?

Please don't use butter. It traps heat in the skin and raises the risk of infection. Hold his hand under cool running water for 20 minutes, then cover it loosely with cling film or a clean dressing and give a child's dose of paracetamol or ibuprofen if he's sore. If the burn is bigger than his palm, has blisters, or looks white or leathery, take him to urgent care, because children's burns are worth having assessed.
can I take zinc on an empty stomach

You can, but zinc on an empty stomach is notorious for causing nausea, so taking it with food is usually more comfortable. Keep long-term doses at or below about 40 mg a day for adults. Higher amounts over weeks can cause a copper deficiency.
had the flu last week, fever gone 2 days ago. can i hit leg day tomorrow?

Give it a few more days. Your body is still repairing itself, and heavy lifting this soon often brings back fatigue or drags out the recovery. Start with a light session at about half your usual weight once you've had three or four fever-free days, then build back over a week or so.
My teenage son says his head hurts every morning and he's been throwing up when he wakes. He seems fine by afternoon.

Please get him to his doctor promptly, within the next few days. Headaches that are worst on waking and come with morning vomiting can be a sign of increased pressure inside the skull, which needs to be ruled out. It may well be something simpler, like a sleep issue or a sinus problem, but this pattern deserves a proper exam. Go to the ER sooner if he develops vision changes, confusion, clumsiness or severe pain.
I took my antihistamine and also a nighttime cold medicine. Now I'm super drowsy. Did I mess up?

Probably yes. Many nighttime cold medicines already contain an antihistamine like diphenhydramine or doxylamine, so you likely doubled up. Don't drive or take anything else sedating, and have someone check on you. If you have trouble staying awake, confusion, a racing heart, or trouble urinating, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 in the US or seek care. Going forward, check active ingredients so you avoid overlap.
Ciprofloxacin and my morning multivitamin, any issue?

Yes, the minerals in multivitamins, like calcium, iron, magnesium and zinc, bind cipro and can stop much of it from being absorbed. Take cipro at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after the multivitamin. The same goes for antacids and calcium-fortified foods. Taking the vitamin at night and the cipro in the morning usually solves it.
Dentist gave me tramadol after an extraction. I'm on sertraline 100mg. Fine to take both?

That combination carries real risk, because tramadol raises serotonin and lowers the seizure threshold, and together with sertraline it can trigger serotonin syndrome. Call your dentist or pharmacist before taking it and make sure they know about the sertraline, since dentists don't always have your full med list. For dental pain, alternating ibuprofen and acetaminophen often works as well as or better than tramadol, if those are safe for you.
I take levothyroxine and just started an iron supplement. Any problem taking them together in the morning?

Yes. Iron binds to levothyroxine and can noticeably lower how much you absorb, so space them at least four hours apart. A simple routine is levothyroxine on an empty stomach first thing with water, then iron with lunch or dinner. Calcium and antacids behave the same way. Your doctor may recheck your TSH in a couple of months to make sure your dose is still right.
I live 3 hours from my parents. Mom (80) is caring for Dad who has Parkinson's and she sounds exhausted on the phone. What can I do from afar?

Caregiver burnout is real and can affect her health too, so you're right to step in. From a distance you can call their local Area Agency on Aging to find in-home aides, respite care, adult day programs and meal delivery. You can also take over tasks like managing prescriptions, scheduling appointments or handling bills online. Encourage her to bring up her own exhaustion with her doctor, and plan a visit where you can see firsthand how things are going.
Is it ok to take NyQuil and have a couple beers to help me sleep with this cold?

Skip the beers tonight. NyQuil already contains a sedating antihistamine, and some versions also contain alcohol, so adding drinks can make you dangerously drowsy and slow your breathing. The acetaminophen in it is also harder on your liver when combined with alcohol. NyQuil on its own plus a hot shower and an extra pillow to prop your head up should get you to sleep.
Ugh, I keep getting sick every time I start training hard again. What am I doing wrong?

You're probably ramping up too fast, often while also skimping on sleep or food. Very hard training can temporarily dampen your immune defenses, especially when recovery is poor. Increase your training more gradually, aim for seven to nine hours of sleep, and eat enough to fuel your workouts. If you keep getting infections even after that, have your doctor check for things like low iron or vitamin D.
Mom's 73 and hasn't had a shingles shot. Worth it at her age?

Yes. Shingles risk and the chance of lasting nerve pain both rise with age, so she's right in the group that benefits most. The recommended vaccine, Shingrix, is two doses a few months apart. Her doctor or a pharmacy can give it, and it's often covered. While she's there, ask about the flu, pneumonia, COVID, and RSV vaccines too.
My dog's on gabapentin. Can I take some of hers for my nerve pain? Same drug right?

It's the same molecule, but don't take it. Some liquid gabapentin can contain xylitol, the dose isn't matched to you, and gabapentin can interact with other sedatives or opioids and cause dangerous drowsiness. Nerve pain is very treatable, so see your doctor, who can prescribe the right drug at a dose that's safe for you.
My toenail is thick and yellow. Can I just soak it in bleach to kill the fungus?

Skip the bleach. It can burn and irritate your skin and won't reach the fungus living under and inside the nail anyway. Nail fungus is stubborn, and the most effective treatment is usually a prescription, either a medicated nail solution or oral terbinafine. Your doctor can confirm it's fungal first, since psoriasis and injury can look similar. If you have diabetes or poor circulation, get it looked at sooner rather than later.
Is it fine to let my 8 month old sleep on her tummy? She rolls over herself anyway.

Once she can roll both ways on her own, it's fine to let her stay on her tummy if she rolls there, but still put her down on her back at the start of every sleep. The bigger safety factor now is the crib itself: a firm, flat mattress with a fitted sheet and nothing else, meaning no pillows, bumpers, blankets, or stuffed animals. That setup lowers the risk of SIDS and suffocation even when she moves around.
I keep forgetting to check my sugar. Is checking like once a week enough? Type 2, on metformin only.

On metformin alone, you may not need daily checks, because it rarely causes lows and plenty of people in your situation test only occasionally or rely on A1c. But the right frequency depends on how controlled you are, so ask your doctor what's useful for you. Checking now and then after meals can show what foods spike you. If remembering is the issue, tie it to a routine like right after brushing your teeth.
Can I stop my antidepressants now that I feel better? Been on sertraline 8 months.

Feeling better is great, but don't stop suddenly. Coming off sertraline abruptly can cause dizziness, "brain zaps", irritability and flu-like symptoms, and stopping too soon raises the risk of the depression coming back. Most guidance suggests staying on for at least six to twelve months after you start feeling well. Talk to your prescriber about whether now is a good time and about a gradual taper over several weeks. Choose a stable period of your life to do it, not the middle of a big change.
I'm a nurse, constantly lifting patients, and my back is starting to hurt most shifts. Any advice beyond 'lift with your legs'?

Use lift equipment and slide sheets every time they're available, and ask for a second person rather than muscling transfers alone, because staff injuries pile up when people skip these under time pressure. Strengthening your core and glutes outside work makes a real difference. So does getting close to the patient and avoiding twisting while you bear load. Since it's hurting most shifts, see occupational health or a physio now, before a minor strain turns into a lasting problem.
Sudden headache plus my face drooped on one side for a minute, now fine

Call emergency services now, even though it's passed. Facial drooping with a headache can be a stroke or a transient ischemic attack (TIA), which often comes before a major stroke. Fast assessment can prevent serious damage, so don't wait or drive yourself.
toothache gone after a week of agony. guess it fixed itself?

Unfortunately, sudden relief after a bad toothache often means the nerve inside the tooth has died, not that the problem has healed. Bacteria can keep spreading and form an abscess later, sometimes with little warning. Get it checked by a dentist even though it feels fine now, since a root canal at this stage can still save the tooth.
how long should a kid stay home from school after a fever

The usual rule is that your child should be fever-free for 24 hours without any fever-reducing medicine before going back. They should also be eating and acting reasonably like themselves. If a dose of ibuprofen in the morning is what's keeping the fever away, they aren't ready yet. Some schools have their own rules, so check your school's policy too.
What's a normal blood pressure for an 80 year old? my moms home monitor says 150/85

For most older adults, doctors aim for under about 130 to 140 systolic, though targets are individualized based on health and fall risk. A reading of 150/85 isn't an emergency on its own, but if it's consistently that high, her doctor should know. Have her take readings at the same time daily after sitting quietly for five minutes and keep a log for her next appointment. Readings above 180/120, or high pressure with headache, chest pain or vision changes, need urgent care.
Red, hot, swollen patch on my shin that's getting bigger since yesterday and I feel feverish

That combination sounds like cellulitis, a bacterial skin infection that needs antibiotics, so please see a doctor today. Draw a pen line around the edge of the redness so you and the doctor can tell whether it's spreading. Go to the emergency department right away if it spreads quickly, you get red streaks, a high fever or chills, or you feel confused or very unwell. Keep the leg raised in the meantime.
think i dislocated my finger, it's sideways. youtube says i can pop it back in myself

Resist the urge. A finger that's bent sideways could be fractured as well as dislocated, and forcing it back can damage the joint, tendons or blood vessels. Splint it as it lies, ice it, and get to urgent care for an X-ray and proper reduction today. Going promptly makes it easier to fix.
can i just take two benadryl every night to sleep

Occasional use is fine for most healthy adults, but nightly Benadryl isn't a good plan. Your body builds tolerance quickly, it often causes a next-day hangover, and long-term regular use of anticholinergic drugs like diphenhydramine has been linked to memory problems, especially as people get older. Chronic trouble sleeping usually responds better to fixing the underlying cause or to CBT for insomnia, which has strong evidence behind it. Bring it up with your doctor if you can't sleep without something.
Arthritis in my hands is bad in the mornings. 61F. Any tips beyond painkillers?

Soaking your hands in warm water or using paraffin wax baths in the morning, followed by gentle finger and wrist exercises, can loosen stiffness noticeably. Wide-grip utensils, jar openers and compression gloves take strain off sore joints, and topical anti-inflammatory gels are a good option with fewer side effects than tablets. One thing worth checking with your doctor: morning stiffness lasting more than about an hour, especially with swelling in several joints, can point to rheumatoid arthritis, which benefits from early treatment.
My dad (78) gets dizzy every time he stands up since they added a new BP med. Is that normal?

It's common, but it shouldn't be brushed off, because dizziness on standing in someone his age raises the risk of falls. This is likely orthostatic hypotension from the new medication, and his doctor may need to adjust the dose or the timing. In the meantime, have him stand up slowly and sit on the edge of the bed for a minute first, and call his doctor this week. If he faints or falls, get him seen promptly.
got a fever after coming back from ghana last week, probably just a cold right

Don't assume it's a cold. A fever after travel to West Africa needs to be checked for malaria, which can turn serious quickly. See a doctor today, whether that's urgent care or the ER, and tell them exactly where you traveled and when. This is true even if you took antimalarial pills, since they don't give 100% protection. A simple blood test can rule it in or out.
pregnant, 28 weeks. midwife mentioned Tdap. is it actually safe for the baby?

Yes, Tdap is recommended in every pregnancy, ideally between 27 and 36 weeks, so you're right in the window. It's well studied in pregnancy, and the antibodies you make cross the placenta and protect your newborn from whooping cough before they're old enough for their own shots. Whooping cough can be life-threatening in young babies, so this is one of the most useful things you can do for them right now.
found a tick on my 5yo's scalp, I pulled it off. do I need to do anything else

Clean the spot with soap and water or rubbing alcohol, and if you can, save the tick in a sealed bag or photograph it in case you need to identify it later. Watch the area and her overall health for the next month, especially for an expanding red rash, fever, headache, or achy joints. Call her pediatrician if any of those show up, or now if the tick looked engorged and you live in an area where Lyme is common, since a preventive antibiotic dose is sometimes recommended.
night shift nurse, how do I sleep during the day??

Make your bedroom a cave with blackout curtains, earplugs or white noise, and a cool temperature, and silence your phone. Wear sunglasses on the drive home to cut morning light, and try to keep a similar sleep window even on days off. Avoid caffeine in the last four to six hours before you plan to sleep. If you're still exhausted or drowsy driving despite this, talk to your doctor about shift work sleep disorder, since there are real treatment options.
Can I take Sudafed with my ADHD meds (Adderall)?

Best to avoid it. Pseudoephedrine and Adderall are both stimulants, and together they can push your heart rate and blood pressure up and make you jittery or anxious. For congestion, saline rinses, a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, or a short course of oxymetazoline spray for no more than three days are gentler options. A pharmacist can point you to something safe for your exact combination.
can kids take melatonin? my 7 year old won't fall asleep and I'm exhausted

Melatonin is sometimes used for kids, but it's best to run it by the pediatrician first, because doses in store products vary a lot and it's not meant as a long-term fix. In many cases a consistent bedtime routine works as well or better: no screens for an hour before bed, a dark, cool room, and the same wake-up time every day. If he's still struggling after a few weeks of that, the doctor can check for things like anxiety or snoring that might be keeping him up.
Ear has been ringing since a concert last night. Will it go away?

Ringing after a loud concert is common and often fades within a day or two as your ears recover, so give them quiet time and avoid more loud noise for now. It's a warning sign that the volume was damaging, and repeated exposure can make tinnitus and hearing loss permanent, so foam or musician's earplugs are worth bringing next time. If it hasn't settled after a few days, or you notice muffled hearing, get a hearing check soon, because sudden hearing loss responds best to early treatment.
Out with tonsillitis for a week. Fever gone since Monday. Swim training Thursday too soon?

If your fever has been gone since Monday and you're eating and drinking normally, an easy swim on Thursday is usually reasonable. Keep it shorter and lighter than your usual session, and take it as a sign to back off if you feel unusually tired or your throat flares up. Make sure you finish any antibiotics you were prescribed.
I've been taking Afrin for 2 weeks straight and now I can't breathe without it. Help

That's rebound congestion, which is common when you use decongestant sprays past about three days. The fix is to stop. It's easiest to quit one nostril at a time over a few days, or switch to a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone, which helps the swelling settle without the rebound. It usually clears within a week or two. If you're still badly blocked after that, see a doctor to check for an underlying sinus issue.
I have leftover amoxicillin from last year. Should I take it for my abscessed tooth?

Hold off, because a leftover partial course probably isn't the right drug, dose or length for this infection, and stopping short can make it harder to treat. Antibiotics alone also don't cure an abscess, which usually needs drainage, a root canal or an extraction. Get seen by a dentist or urgent care today so they can prescribe properly. Go to the ER if swelling spreads or you feel feverish and unwell.
I have type 2 diabetes and caught the flu. Anything I should do differently?

Yes. Call your doctor early, because diabetes raises your risk of flu complications and you're a good candidate for antiviral treatment within the first 48 hours. Illness often pushes blood sugar up, so check it more often, keep taking your diabetes meds unless your doctor says otherwise, and drink plenty of fluids. Many cough syrups are sugary, so choose sugar-free versions. Seek care urgently if your sugars stay very high, you're vomiting and can't keep fluids down, or you feel confused or very short of breath.
why do I jerk awake right when I'm falling asleep

Those are hypnic jerks, and they're very common and harmless. They're more frequent when you're overtired, stressed, or have had caffeine or nicotine late in the day. Cutting caffeine after early afternoon and keeping a regular sleep schedule usually reduces them. If you're having frequent repetitive leg movements through the night, or an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, that's different and worth asking a doctor about.
creatine bad for kidneys?

In healthy people, creatine at the standard 3 to 5 grams a day hasn't been shown to harm the kidneys, and it's one of the best-studied supplements there is. It can raise your creatinine on blood tests, so tell your doctor you take it so they don't misread the results. If you already have kidney disease, skip it unless your nephrologist says otherwise.
teen son has had a cold, now says his chest hurts when he breathes deep and he's got a fever of 103. give him advil and wait?

Advil is fine for comfort, but don't just wait. Chest pain on deep breaths with a 103°F fever after a cold can point to pneumonia, so he should be seen today by his doctor or at urgent care. Head to the ER if he's breathing fast, can't catch his breath, or his lips look bluish.
My 8 year old has type 1 and wants to go to a sleepover. I'm terrified. Is this a bad idea?

It's not a bad idea, and with some planning kids with type 1 do sleepovers all the time. Give the host parent a simple written plan covering target ranges, how to treat a low with juice or glucose tabs, and when to call you. Pack extra supplies and glucagon, and show them how to use it. If your child wears a CGM with remote monitoring, you can watch overnight from home, which makes a huge difference to everyone's peace of mind.
Burned my hand on the oven, about the size of a coin, it's red and blistered. Butter?

No butter, because it traps heat and raises infection risk. Run the burn under cool, not ice-cold, water for a good 20 minutes. Then cover it loosely with a clean non-stick dressing, and leave the blister intact. Ibuprofen or paracetamol will help with the pain. Get it seen if it's on a joint, gets more painful, red or pus-filled, or looks white or leathery, which suggests a deeper burn.
Hi, I'm 19 and I think I might be pregnant but I can't tell my parents. What do I do first?

Start with a home pregnancy test using your first morning pee. They're cheap at any pharmacy and pretty accurate if your period is late. If it's positive, a Planned Parenthood or community health clinic can confirm it confidentially and talk through all your options without judgment, and in many places they can see you even without your parents involved. You don't have to figure this out alone, so if there's a trusted adult, friend or counselor you can lean on, reach out to them.
I'm 67 and just got over pneumonia. My doctor cleared me to go home two weeks ago. When can I start my water aerobics class again?

Pneumonia takes more out of you than people expect, especially in your sixties, so it's smart to ask before diving back in. Many people can return to gentle activity like water aerobics somewhere around four to six weeks after pneumonia, but it really depends on how your breathing and energy are now. Ask your doctor at your follow-up, or call the office and ask directly. When you go back, start with half a class or take it easy and stop if you get short of breath. Walking at home in the meantime is a great way to rebuild stamina.
quick q is it fine to use my husband's hydrocortisone cream on my face for a rash

A short course of over-the-counter 1% hydrocortisone on the face is generally okay, for a few days and no more than about a week. Stronger prescription steroids are a different story, so check the label first, because using those on facial skin can thin it and cause rebound redness or perioral dermatitis. Keep it away from your eyes. If the rash isn't clearly better after a week, see a doctor rather than continuing.
Is it fine to take my antibiotic with milk? It upsets my stomach

That depends on the drug. Doxycycline, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin all bind to calcium, so milk, yogurt, antacids and iron supplements can stop them from absorbing. Take those 2 hours before or 6 hours after dairy. Amoxicillin, cephalexin and many others are fine with food, including milk, and food often helps with nausea. Your pharmacist can confirm in ten seconds for your specific one.
Groomer here. I get small cat scratches basically daily. Anything I should actually be doing?

Make a habit of washing every scratch with soap and water as soon as you can, and keep your tetanus booster current since your exposure is constant. Wear gloves and long sleeves for difficult animals, and cover any open cuts while working. See a doctor for any scratch that gets red, swollen or pus-filled, or if you notice swollen lymph nodes, since cat scratch disease is an occupational risk for groomers.
quick q - my friend with a peanut allergy is coming over. if I bake cookies without peanuts but in my normal kitchen is that fine?

It depends on how sensitive your friend is, so the simplest thing is to ask them directly, since some people react to trace cross-contact. If you go ahead, wash all bowls, utensils and trays thoroughly with soap and water, wipe the counters, and check every ingredient label for 'may contain peanuts' warnings, especially chocolate chips and flour blends. Showing your friend the packaging is a nice touch, because people with food allergies often prefer to make the final call themselves.
I'm 62 and suddenly I'm seeing a bunch of new floaters plus little flashes of light in my right eye. Probably nothing right?

A sudden shower of new floaters with flashes needs to be checked today, not brushed off, because it can signal a retinal tear that can turn into a detachment. Call an ophthalmologist or optometrist for a same-day dilated eye exam, or go to the ER if you can't get in. If you notice a shadow or curtain spreading across your vision, go immediately, because fast treatment can save your sight.
my 2 year old has a fever and all we have is adult ibuprofen. can i just cut a pill in half?

Please don't. Half an adult tablet is still likely too much for a toddler, and children's doses are based on weight, so guessing is risky. A pharmacy can sell you children's liquid ibuprofen or acetaminophen with a measuring syringe, and the box gives the dose for your child's weight. If your child is unusually drowsy, struggling to breathe, refusing fluids, or has a fever above 104°F (40°C), call your pediatrician or an after-hours line tonight.
Quick q: shingles vaccine — I'm 52, had chickenpox as a kid, do I really need it?

Yes, and having had chickenpox is exactly why you need it, since the virus stays dormant in your nerves and can reactivate as shingles. Shingrix is recommended for everyone 50 and up as two doses given 2 to 6 months apart, and it's over 90% effective. It also lowers your risk of postherpetic neuralgia, the nerve pain that can linger for months after shingles, so it's well worth getting.
chest burns after spicy food and lying down. tums help. this is just heartburn right?

Burning after meals that gets worse lying down and goes away with Tums fits heartburn very well. Try smaller dinners, eating at least three hours before bed, and raising the head of your bed. See a doctor if you need antacids more than twice a week, have trouble swallowing, or are losing weight. Treat it as possible heart trouble and get checked urgently if the burning comes on with exertion or comes with sweating or breathlessness, especially if you're over 40 or have risk factors.
I have a mole on my back that my wife says looks bigger and darker than last year. It doesn't hurt. Probably nothing, right?

A mole that's getting bigger or darker is exactly the kind of change that deserves a look, even if it doesn't hurt, because early melanoma usually causes no pain at all. Book an appointment with your GP or a dermatologist in the next couple of weeks and mention that it has changed. Ask your wife to take a clear photo with a coin or ruler beside it so you have a baseline to compare against. Most changing moles turn out to be harmless, but this is one where checking early really matters.
I'm 16 and my acne is really bad. My friend has leftover Accutane, can I just take some of hers?

Please don't, because isotretinoin is one of the most tightly controlled skin medicines for good reason. It can cause severe birth defects, affect your mood and liver, and raise your cholesterol, which is why people on it get regular blood tests and close follow-up. A random dose without supervision is risky and won't clear your acne anyway, since it only works over a full course of months. Ask a parent to help you book a dermatologist appointment, because severe acne is very treatable and you may well qualify for a properly monitored course yourself.
My aunt has a sore on her heel that won't heal. She's diabetic and 73. Can I just put Neosporin on it?

Hold off on home treatment and get her to a doctor or podiatrist soon. A non-healing heel sore in someone with diabetes can turn into a serious infection quickly, and reduced feeling in the feet means it may be worse than it looks. Until she's seen, keep it clean, covered with a dry dressing, and keep pressure off it. If you see redness spreading, warmth, pus, a bad smell or fever, that's a same-day visit.
My dad is 78 and has had a cough for a week, now he seems kind of confused and is breathing faster. He says he's fine.

Get him seen today, ideally at an urgent care or ER rather than waiting for an appointment. In older adults, new confusion plus fast breathing after a cough can be a sign of pneumonia or a low oxygen level, even without a high fever. His saying he's fine doesn't rule that out. If his lips look bluish or he's struggling to breathe, call emergency services.
my dad (68) says his chest feels 'weird' and he's sweating a lot but insists it's nothing and doesn't want a fuss. what do I do

An odd chest feeling plus heavy sweating in a 68-year-old is a serious warning sign for a heart attack, so this is worth the fuss. Call emergency services now, even if he objects. You can tell him the paramedics will simply check him and leave if everything's fine. Keep him sitting and resting while you wait, and give him one regular aspirin to chew if he isn't allergic and isn't on blood thinners.
Can I put aloe straight from the plant on a burn?

Yes, fresh aloe gel is fine for minor first-degree burns once you've cooled the area with running water first. Just patch test a small area, since some people react to it, and avoid using it on open skin or burst blisters. For anything more than a mild redness, stick to a clean dressing.
on antibiotics for a tooth infection, friend's bday is saturday. can i drink or nah

It depends on which antibiotic. If it's amoxicillin, which is common for tooth infections, a drink or two won't cause a dangerous interaction, though alcohol can slow your recovery. If it's metronidazole, don't drink at all while you're taking it or for at least three days after the last dose, because the combination can cause pounding headaches, flushing and violent vomiting. Check the label or ask the pharmacist which one you're on.
what do i put on a minor burn after cooling it

Once you've cooled it for 20 minutes, aloe vera gel or a plain fragrance-free moisturizer helps the comfort and tightness. If it might rub, cover it with a loose non-stick dressing. Ibuprofen or acetaminophen handles the pain. Avoid toothpaste, butter, and oils, which can trap heat or irritate the skin.
I'm a nurse doing night shifts and I'm completely burnt out. I cry in my car before work. What can I even do?

Crying in your car before shifts is your body telling you this load isn't sustainable, and it's very common in healthcare right now. Protect your sleep fiercely with blackout curtains, earplugs and a consistent post-shift routine, and look into your employer's occupational health or employee assistance program, which often offers free confidential counseling. It's also worth seeing your own GP, because burnout often overlaps with depression, which is treatable. Asking about fewer nights or a different unit isn't failure, it's how people stay in nursing long-term.
Dad's 90 and has lost about 15 pounds in the last few months without trying. He says he's just not hungry.

Unintentional weight loss of that size in a few months needs a doctor's evaluation. At his age it can come from dental problems, depression, medication side effects, thyroid issues, swallowing difficulties or something more serious. While you wait for the appointment, small frequent meals, calorie-dense foods, and eating together can help keep his intake up. Write down what he's actually eating for a few days so the doctor gets a clear picture.
I take levothyroxine every morning. My new calcium supplement says take with breakfast. Conflict?

Yes, good catch. Calcium binds levothyroxine and can noticeably reduce how much you absorb, so keep them at least four hours apart. Take the thyroid pill first thing on an empty stomach as usual, and move the calcium to lunch or dinner. Iron and many multivitamins need the same separation.
I missed my birth control pill yesterday, should I take two today?

For most combined pills, yes. Take the missed pill as soon as you remember and today's pill at the usual time, even if that means two in one day. If you've missed only one pill, you're generally still protected. If you've missed two or more, or you take a progestin-only mini-pill where even a few hours late matters, use condoms for the next seven days and check your pack's leaflet or ask a pharmacist.
My dad is 72 and fell yesterday, now says his hip hurts but he can still kind of walk. He refuses to go to the doctor. Is it fine if he's walking?

Being able to walk doesn't rule out a hip fracture in someone his age. Some fractures are small or impacted enough to allow walking at first and then get worse. He really should have an X-ray today, either through urgent care or the ER, especially if the pain is in the groin or he's limping. If he digs in, try framing it as ruling something out quickly so he can get back to normal, and note that a missed fracture can mean a much longer recovery.
Is it safe to buy a mole removal cream online? Way cheaper than a dermatologist.

Those creams are a bad idea. They can burn a hole into the skin and leave a scar, and they mean the mole never gets examined, so a melanoma could be partly destroyed and missed while it keeps growing underneath. Regulators have warned against them for exactly that reason. If a mole bothers you, a doctor can check it and remove it properly, with the tissue sent to a lab. That's the safe way to have it gone.
kitchen knife slipped and i cut across my finger, now the tip feels numb

Numbness past a cut is a sign the cut may have reached a nerve, and sometimes a tendon too, which runs right alongside it. Hold pressure to stop the bleeding, bandage it, and get it seen today at urgent care or the ER instead of waiting for it to heal. Have them check whether you can bend and straighten each joint of that finger fully, since cut nerves and tendons in the hand are best repaired early. Don't put off getting it treated.
Does reading on my phone in bed really mess up sleep or is that a myth?
