It's real, though the effect is smaller than people think. Bright screens can slightly delay your body clock, and the bigger problem is that scrolling keeps your brain engaged and pushes bedtime later. Turning on night mode and lowering the brightness helps a bit. Putting the phone away 30 to 60 minutes before bed and reading a paper book or listening to something calm helps a lot more.
lost 30 lbs and my bp is now like 105/65 on my meds. should i cut the pills in half myself?

Congratulations on the weight loss, which is probably why your numbers dropped. Don't cut the pills yourself, though. Some can't be split, and some need to be tapered rather than reduced suddenly. Call your prescriber with a week of readings, since they'll likely lower your dose or stop one of the medications.
Swimmer's ear I think, outer ear hurts when I tug it. Can I just pour some hydrogen peroxide in?

Peroxide isn't great for an established infection and can irritate inflamed skin. If there's any chance your eardrum is damaged, you shouldn't put anything in at all. Pain when you tug the ear does sound like swimmer's ear, which usually clears quickly with prescription antibiotic drops. See a doctor to confirm, and keep the ear dry until then.
is it ok to use clove oil for a toothache or is that just an old wives tale

Clove oil does work as a temporary numbing agent, because it contains eugenol, which dentists also use. Dab a small amount on a cotton ball and hold it against the tooth, not the gums, since undiluted oil can irritate soft tissue. Don't give it to young children. It's a stopgap, so still get the tooth checked.
knocked out my son's adult front tooth playing soccer, what do i do RIGHT NOW

Pick the tooth up by the crown, not the root, and if it's dirty, rinse it briefly in milk or saline without scrubbing. If you can, gently push it back into the socket and have him bite on gauze, and if not, keep it in milk or in his cheek. Get to a dentist or ER immediately, because the best chance of saving it is within about an hour.
is it ok to use orajel on my 6 month old's teething gums

No, the FDA advises against benzocaine products like Orajel for babies and children under 2, because they can cause a rare but dangerous blood condition called methemoglobinemia. Instead, try a chilled (not frozen) teething ring, gently rubbing the gums with a clean finger, or a cold washcloth to chew on. If your baby is very uncomfortable, ask your pediatrician about weight-based acetaminophen dosing, and avoid teething necklaces and homeopathic teething gels.
My kid's asthma inhaler is expired by 3 months, he's wheezing. Use it or not?

Use it now. A recently expired albuterol inhaler may be a bit weaker, but it's far better than nothing during an attack. Get a refill as soon as possible. Go to the ER or call 911 if he's struggling to talk, his lips look blue, the skin between his ribs pulls in when he breathes, or the inhaler isn't helping.
6 yr old still wets the bed most nights. should I be worried

Bedwetting at 6 is common and usually just reflects a bladder and sleep system that's still maturing; it often runs in families. Avoid punishment, limit drinks in the hour or two before bed, and have him use the toilet right before sleep. Mention it to his pediatrician, especially if he was dry before and started wetting again, or if he's very thirsty, has pain when peeing, or snores heavily. Bedwetting alarms work well if it's bothering him.
my dog bit me on accident when i grabbed a toy, tiny scrape. he's had all his shots. overreacting if i dont do anything?

Not overreacting, that's pretty much fine. Give it a quick wash with soap and water and maybe dab on some ointment. Since your dog is vaccinated and the skin is barely scraped, there's no rabies concern. Just watch it for redness or swelling over the next few days.
Ate at a restaurant, I have a tree nut allergy, now my mouth is tingly but nothing else. Can I just wait it out?

With a known tree nut allergy, don't just wait, and keep your epinephrine in hand while you watch closely. If anything else develops, like throat tightness, trouble breathing, hives, vomiting or dizziness, use your epinephrine and call emergency services right away. Have someone stay with you for the next few hours rather than heading home alone, and call your allergist even if it stays mild.
do adults actually need a tetanus shot? i stepped on a rusty nail

Yes, adults need a tetanus booster every 10 years, and after a puncture wound like a nail you need one if it's been more than 5 years since your last shot or you don't know when you had it. Wash the wound well with soap and water and get to urgent care or your doctor within a day or two, since puncture wounds are prime territory for tetanus. Watch for redness, swelling, or pus over the next few days, because those signal an infection that needs treatment.
what herbal teas are safe? I want to cut caffeine

Ginger, peppermint and rooibos are generally considered fine in normal amounts and are great caffeine-free swaps, and ginger helps with nausea too. Be more cautious with large amounts of chamomile and with blends you don't recognize, and avoid teas marketed for detoxing, cleansing or weight loss. Herbs like pennyroyal, blue or black cohosh and dong quai are on the avoid list. Raspberry leaf is popular late in pregnancy, but check with your provider before starting it.
I'm 30 weeks pregnant and have burning when I pee. Can I just drink cranberry juice?

Call your OB or midwife today rather than trying to treat it at home. UTIs in pregnancy can move up to the kidneys more easily and are linked to preterm labor, so they're treated with pregnancy-safe antibiotics even when symptoms are mild. Cranberry juice won't clear an active infection. Head to labor and delivery if you have fever, back pain or contractions.
Thinking of trying ear candling for wax buildup, any good?

Skip it, because ear candling has been shown not to remove wax and can cause burns to the face and ear canal, or drip wax onto the eardrum. For buildup, a few days of over-the-counter softening drops or a little mineral oil usually loosen it so it works its way out. If you still feel blocked, a doctor or nurse can clear it safely with irrigation or suction in a few minutes.
Is it bad to take Advil every day for a week for a sinus headache?

A week of label-dose Advil is usually fine for a healthy adult, taken with food to protect your stomach. Be cautious if you have kidney problems, ulcers, high blood pressure, or take blood thinners. Saline rinses and steam often help sinus pressure more directly. If it hasn't improved after about 10 days, or you get a high fever or swelling around the eyes, see a doctor.
Kid has impetigo crusts on her face. Can she go to daycare tomorrow?

Usually not quite yet. Impetigo is very contagious, and most daycares and doctors recommend keeping kids home until they've been on antibiotic treatment for at least 24 hours. Prescribed antibiotic ointment or oral antibiotics clear it up quickly. Wash her hands often, keep her nails short, and use separate towels so it doesn't spread to the rest of the family.
ringing in ears after concert last night still there. permanent??

Most of the time, ringing after a loud concert fades within a day or two, so there's a good chance this will go away. Treat it as a warning that your ears took some damage, though, and give them quiet time for the next few days. If it's still there after about a week or your hearing seems muffled, get a hearing test. Next time, cheap foam earplugs or musician's earplugs will keep the music clear while protecting your hearing.
Is it true you should starve a fever?

No, that old saying doesn't hold up. When you have a fever, your body actually burns more energy and loses more fluid. Fluids are the priority, so drink water, broth, or electrolyte drinks steadily. Eat whatever light food you can tolerate. Losing your appetite for a day is normal, but not being able to keep fluids down is a reason to call a doctor.
I'm a line cook, burned my forearm on the fryer, it's white and doesn't really hurt in the center. Can I finish my shift?

No, get it looked at now. White, painless skin in the center of a burn is a sign of a deep burn that has damaged the nerve endings, and it may need specialist care and possibly grafting. Cool it under running water briefly, cover it with clean cling film or a non-fluffy cloth, and go to urgent care or the ER. Finishing the shift risks infection and worse damage.
toddler 102 fever but running around playing like normal. worry?

That's reassuring. How a child acts matters more than the number on the thermometer, and a playful, drinking toddler with a fever of 102°F is usually fighting off a routine virus. Keep up the fluids, and give a fever reducer only if she seems uncomfortable. Call her doctor if the fever lasts more than three days, she stops drinking or wetting diapers, or she becomes listless.
Had a tooth pulled 3 days ago, pain suddenly got way worse and my breath stinks

Pain that gets worse around day 2 to 4 after an extraction, along with bad breath or taste, is the textbook picture of dry socket. That happens when the blood clot is lost and the bone is exposed. Call the dentist who did the extraction, because they can clean the socket and place a medicated dressing that often brings relief within hours. Until then, take your pain reliever as directed, avoid straws and smoking, and rinse gently with warm salt water.
Is it true sweating out a fever at the gym helps you recover faster?

No, that's a myth, and it can actually make things worse. Exercising with a fever stresses your heart, speeds up dehydration, and in rare cases is linked to heart inflammation after viral infections. Rest, drink fluids, and wait until the fever has been gone for a day or two before you do anything strenuous.
is it ok to use my bleach based cleaning product on a small fungal patch on my foot? stronger than the cream

No, please don't put household bleach on your skin, because it can cause a chemical burn and broken skin that makes infection more likely, not less. Over-the-counter terbinafine cream is genuinely effective for athlete's foot when used daily for one to two weeks, and you should keep your feet dry and change socks often. If it keeps coming back or involves your toenails, a doctor can prescribe something stronger that's actually safe for skin.
quick q, dad 90 keeps coughing when he drinks water. big deal?

It can be. Coughing while drinking often means liquid is going toward his airway, called dysphagia, and that can lead to aspiration pneumonia, which is serious at 90. Tell his doctor soon and ask about a swallow assessment with a speech-language pathologist. In the meantime, have him sit fully upright and take small sips, and don't rush him.
I have leftover oxycodone from surgery and my friend has a migraine. Can I give her one?

Please don't. Sharing a prescription opioid is illegal, and it's risky for her. Oxycodone can cause dangerous breathing problems when mixed with alcohol, sleep aids or anxiety medication, and opioids often worsen migraines over time. She'd do better with an over-the-counter migraine combination or her own doctor's treatment. Drop your leftover pills at a pharmacy take-back point.
what's the difference between first second and third degree burns, quickly

A first-degree burn is red, painful and dry with no blisters, like a mild sunburn. A second-degree burn blisters, looks wet or shiny, and hurts a lot. A third-degree burn goes through the full skin and can look white, brown, black or leathery, and it may hurt surprisingly little because the nerves are damaged. Treat first-degree burns at home, get large second-degree burns checked, and treat any third-degree burn as an emergency.
my chest has felt tight and heavy for about 20 minutes and now my left arm is kind of achy. probably just stress right?

Don't assume it's stress. Chest heaviness that lasts 20 minutes and spreads into your arm is a classic heart attack pattern, so call emergency services right now rather than driving yourself. If you aren't allergic to aspirin and no doctor has told you to avoid it, chew one regular 325 mg aspirin while you wait. It's far better to be sent home with a stress diagnosis than to sit out a real heart attack.
can I take Tums with my cipro?

Not at the same time. Calcium, magnesium, aluminum, iron and zinc bind to ciprofloxacin and can make it far less effective. Take cipro at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids and those minerals, and keep dairy and calcium-fortified juice apart from your dose too. Doxycycline has the same issue, so check spacing with your pharmacist if you're on that instead.
Can I give my 3 year old adult cough syrup if I just use half the dose? Pharmacy's closed.

Please don't. Adult cough syrups often contain ingredients like dextromethorphan or decongestants that aren't safe for young kids at any dose, and halving doesn't make them safe. For a 3-year-old, a teaspoon of honey before bed, plenty of fluids and a cool-mist humidifier work as well as anything sold for coughs at that age. If they're struggling to breathe, wheezing or seem unusually drowsy, call your doctor's after-hours line or go to urgent care tonight.
Is the meningitis vaccine actually required for college or just a suggestion? Son leaves in 3 weeks.

Many colleges and some states require the MenACWY vaccine for students living in dorms, so check your son's school health forms now, since requirements vary. Even where it isn't required, it's recommended, with a booster at 16 for students who got their first dose earlier, because meningococcal disease spreads in close living quarters and can turn deadly within hours. Ask his doctor about the MenB vaccine too, which covers a different strain behind several college outbreaks. Three weeks is enough time to get at least the first doses in, so book the appointment this week.
quick q - is it bad to take zinc on an empty stomach

It's not harmful, but zinc on an empty stomach makes a lot of people nauseous, sometimes within minutes. Taking it with food solves that, and it still absorbs reasonably well. Keep long-term doses at or under 40 mg a day, because more than that can cause a copper deficiency over time.
Can I put an aspirin directly on my sore gum to numb it?

Don't do that, because aspirin placed against the gum can cause a chemical burn and leave you with a painful white ulcer on top of the toothache. If you can safely take aspirin, swallow it at the normal dose instead. For local relief, an over-the-counter benzocaine gel or a cold compress on the outside of your cheek works better. If the pain keeps coming back, get the tooth checked, since gum pain often points to a problem underneath.
hives all over after eating shrimp and now my lips feel kind of swollen

Swelling of the lips after a food reaction can progress to throat swelling. Treat this as urgent. If you have an epinephrine auto-injector, use it, and call emergency services right away if you have any trouble breathing, throat tightness, wheezing, dizziness or vomiting. Even if it's just lips and hives, take an antihistamine like cetirizine and get to urgent care or an ER now rather than waiting it out. Avoid shellfish until you've seen an allergist.
how long am I contagious with strep after starting antibiotics

Once you've been on antibiotics for about 12 to 24 hours and have no fever, you're generally not contagious. Most schools and workplaces let you return after 24 hours. Keep taking the full course even when you feel better, because finishing it helps prevent complications like rheumatic fever. Replace your toothbrush and don't share cups in the meantime.
My mom is 72 and diabetic and says she just feels 'off' — tired, a bit nauseous, kind of short of breath, but no chest pain. Is this a heart thing?

It could be. Older women and people with diabetes often have heart attacks without classic chest pain, showing up instead as fatigue, nausea and breathlessness. Since these symptoms are new for her, get her evaluated today, and call emergency services if they're getting worse, came on suddenly, or she's sweaty, pale or dizzy. Don't wait for chest pain to appear before taking this seriously.
Is it fine to pop a blister from new shoes? It's huge and annoying.

It's best left intact, since the skin over it is the most sterile bandage you'll get. Pad it with a blister plaster or a donut-shaped moleskin and change shoes if you can. If it's so big and tense that it's going to burst anyway, clean a needle with alcohol, prick the edge, let the fluid drain, and leave the roof of skin in place under a bandage. Watch for redness spreading, warmth, or pus, which point to infection.
Dentist said I need antibiotics before my root canal but the abscess pain is fading, can I skip the dentist and just finish the pills

Finish the pills and still keep the dental appointment. Antibiotics calm an abscess down, but they can't clear the infection out of the tooth itself. It will almost certainly flare up again, sometimes worse. The pain fading means the treatment is working, which makes this a good time to fix the source. If you get facial swelling, trouble swallowing or a fever before then, get seen urgently.
dad has diabetes, 77, his toe has a dark spot and he cant really feel it. hes not worried. am i overreacting

You're not overreacting. In someone with diabetes and reduced feeling in the feet, a dark spot on a toe can mean poor circulation or tissue damage, and foot problems can turn serious quickly. Get him to his doctor or a podiatrist within a day or two. Go sooner if there's swelling, warmth, spreading redness, a smell, or fever.
stretch marks starting, what actually works

Honestly, genetics play the biggest role, and no cream has been proven to reliably prevent stretch marks. Keeping your skin moisturized can help with itching, and gaining weight gradually may help a little. Avoid retinoid creams during pregnancy, and remember that most marks fade a lot after delivery.
teen athlete here (16). had strep throat, on antibiotics day 2. coach wants me at practice.

Strep is contagious for about the first 24 hours of antibiotics. After that, you can go back to practice if you have no fever and feel okay. Take it easy for a couple of days though, because your body's still fighting the infection. If you get a fever, chest pain or feel really wiped out, tell your coach and your parents and sit out.
My cat bit my hand about an hour ago, two small puncture wounds near my knuckle. It barely bled. Do I really need to do anything?

Yes, take this one seriously, because cat bites to the hand become infected far more often than they look like they will. The narrow teeth push bacteria deep into tissue near joints and tendons. Wash it well with soap and running water for several minutes, then see a doctor or urgent care today, since they will often prescribe preventive antibiotics for a hand bite. Go in sooner if you notice swelling, redness spreading, throbbing pain or trouble bending the finger.
can i alternate tylenol and motrin for my kid's fever

You can, but it raises the chance of dosing mistakes, and most pediatricians suggest sticking with one medicine first. If you do alternate, write down every dose and time, and stay within each medicine's limits for your child's weight. Ibuprofen isn't recommended for babies under 6 months. The goal is keeping your child comfortable, not getting to a perfectly normal number on the thermometer.
How long am I contagious with the flu? Want to go back to work Monday

Flu is most contagious in the first three to four days and can spread for up to about a week. A good rule is to go back once you've been fever-free for 24 hours without using fever reducers and you're feeling generally better. If you still have a fever on Monday, stay home. If you do return, wear a mask for a few days and wash your hands often.
Grandma takes like 9 different meds and now she's confused and falling. Could it be the pills?

It very well could be. New confusion and falls in older adults taking many medications are often caused by side effects or interactions, especially from sleep aids, antihistamines, blood pressure drugs and pain meds. Bring all her bottles, including supplements and over-the-counter products, to her doctor or pharmacist for a full medication review soon. If the confusion came on suddenly or she's hit her head, get her seen today, because infections and other urgent problems can look the same.
can a panic attack spike your blood pressure

Yes, a panic attack can push your blood pressure and heart rate up sharply for a short time, and that usually settles once you calm down. Wait until you're fully relaxed before you trust a reading. If your numbers stay high when you're calm, or panic attacks happen often, bring both up with your doctor. Both are very treatable.
teen daughter has a guinea pig bite on her thumb that's been red and oozy for 3 days

Redness and oozing three days later means it's likely infected, so she should see a doctor in the next day. She'll probably need oral antibiotics. Until then, keep it clean, wash it gently, and cover it. Take her in sooner if the redness spreads or she develops a fever.
my metoprolol ER pills are big, can I crush them to make them easier to swallow

Don't crush them. Extended-release tablets are designed to release the drug slowly, and crushing them dumps the full dose at once, which can drop your heart rate and blood pressure too far. Many metoprolol succinate tablets are scored and can be split in half along the line without chewing or crushing, so check with your pharmacist about your exact brand. If swallowing pills is a real problem, your doctor can look at other forms.
Is it safe to do a tiny bit of peanut at home to see if my kid is still allergic?

No, please don't do this at home, because even a tiny amount can trigger a severe reaction in a child with a peanut allergy. Allergists do supervised food challenges in a clinic, with emergency treatment on hand, and they often run blood or skin tests first to see whether a challenge is likely to be safe. Ask your child's doctor for a referral, since many kids do outgrow allergies and a supervised challenge is how you find out safely.
How much water should I actually drink? 8 glasses thing true?

The 8-glasses rule is a rough guideline, not science, and food and other drinks count toward your total too. Most healthy adults do fine drinking when thirsty and aiming for pale yellow urine. You'll need more in heat, during exercise, or when you're sick. If you have heart failure or kidney disease, your doctor may set a specific limit, so follow that instead.
Is it ok to drink a couple beers while on antibiotics? Wedding this weekend.

For most common antibiotics, like amoxicillin, doxycycline or cephalexin, a couple of drinks is unlikely to cause a problem, though alcohol can slow your recovery. The big exceptions are metronidazole and tinidazole, which can cause a severe reaction with flushing, vomiting and a racing heart, so avoid alcohol completely on those and for at least 72 hours afterwards. Check the label or ask the pharmacist which one you're on, and keep it to a modest amount either way.
Can I mix DayQuil and Advil?

Yes, that combination is generally fine for healthy adults. DayQuil contains acetaminophen, not ibuprofen, so the two don't double up. Stick to the label doses for both, and take the Advil with food. Skip the Advil if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, or are on blood thinners, and don't add Tylenol on top since DayQuil already has acetaminophen.
Feeling shaky, sweaty, and confused. I'm diabetic. what do i do

Those are classic signs of a low, so eat or drink 15 grams of fast sugar right now, such as half a cup of juice, regular soda or 4 glucose tabs, without waiting to check first. Recheck in 15 minutes and repeat if you're still under 70 or still feel off. Tell someone near you what's happening. If you become too confused to swallow safely, whoever is with you should call 911 or use glucagon if you have it.
keto cured my diabetes so I stopped my meds, right move?

Great that keto has improved your numbers, but stopping medication on your own is risky. Some drugs, especially insulin and SGLT2 inhibitors, can cause dangerous problems if they're stopped or combined with a very low-carb diet in the wrong way. Get an A1c and talk with your doctor about tapering safely, since many people genuinely do reduce or come off meds this way under supervision. Keep checking your sugar in the meantime so you'll catch it if things drift back up.
I'm on day 4 of a 10 day course and feel totally fine. My friend says I can stop. Can I?

Finish the course as prescribed unless your doctor tells you otherwise. For some infections, shorter courses are fine, but that's a decision for your prescriber to make for your specific infection, not something to guess at. Stopping early can let the infection rebound, sometimes in a harder-to-treat form. If side effects are the problem, call your doctor or pharmacist to discuss them.
just tell me the fastest way to get rid of a pulled muscle in my back, I have a wedding to dance at saturday

Keep moving gently rather than resting it. Apply heat a few times a day and take an over-the-counter anti-inflammatory like ibuprofen at the normal dose if it's safe for you. Light walking and easy stretches within a pain-free range will loosen it faster than lying around. Most mild strains feel much better within several days. On Saturday, just skip any big lifts or dips, and you'll probably dance fine.
Got poison ivy on my legs from hiking. Itching like crazy. What works?

Wash your skin, clothes, and shoes with soap and water to remove any remaining plant oil, then try cool compresses, calamine lotion, oatmeal baths, and over-the-counter hydrocortisone for the itch. An oral antihistamine at night can help you sleep, and try not to scratch the blisters open. If the rash is on your face, eyes, or genitals, covers a large area, or isn't improving in about a week, a doctor can prescribe stronger steroids.
I had a really bad case of COVID and now even a short walk wipes me out for two days afterward. Should I push through it to rebuild stamina?

Don't push through it. Being wiped out for a day or two after small efforts is called post-exertional malaise, and forcing yourself can make long COVID worse. Stay within the amount of activity that doesn't trigger a crash, even if that's very little for now. See your doctor, and ask about a long COVID clinic or a rehab program that uses pacing.
I have asthma and caught a cold, my chest is getting tight and my inhaler isn't helping as much

Take this seriously, because colds are a common trigger for asthma flares. Follow your asthma action plan if you have one, and call your doctor today since you may need steroids or a change in treatment. If you're needing your rescue inhaler more often than every four hours, can't speak in full sentences, or your lips look blue, go to the ER.
RSV vaccine at 72 - worth it?

Yes, it's recommended for everyone 75 and older, and for adults 60 to 74 who are at increased risk, such as those with heart or lung disease, diabetes, or weakened immunity. At 72, it's worth asking your doctor or pharmacist whether you fit that group. RSV puts a lot of older adults in the hospital, and the vaccine is currently a single dose, not a yearly shot.
Dull ache in my lower molar only when I chew on it. Not constant.

Pain only on biting often points to a cracked tooth, a high or loose filling, or early inflammation at the root tip. Chew on the other side for now and avoid very hard or chewy foods, since a crack can spread. Book a dental appointment in the next week or so, because catching a crack early can mean a simple crown instead of a root canal or extraction.
quick q, can dogs take benadryl for allergies? my lab keeps scratching

Plain diphenhydramine is commonly used in dogs, but call your vet for the dose rather than guessing. Avoid any product containing decongestants, alcohol, or xylitol, which can be dangerous for dogs. Constant scratching in labs is often caused by fleas, food allergies, environmental allergies or skin infections, and Benadryl doesn't help those much. A vet visit is worth it to find the cause and get something that actually works.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant with a pounding headache and my vision's a bit sparkly. Tylenol isn't helping.

Call your maternity unit or labor and delivery triage right now. A headache with visual changes late in pregnancy can be a sign of preeclampsia, which needs same-day blood pressure and urine checks. Don't wait to see if it settles, and if you also have upper belly pain or swelling, mention that too.
ear candling works right? my friend swears by it

It doesn't work. Studies show it creates no suction and doesn't pull out wax, and the brown residue your friend sees is just burnt candle. It can also burn your face or ear canal and drip wax onto the eardrum. If you feel blocked up, a few days of over-the-counter wax-softening drops usually does the job, and a clinic can irrigate your ears if it doesn't.
fever with a rash of tiny purple dots on my daughter's legs that don't fade when i press

Go to the ER now, or call 911. A fever with a non-blanching purple rash can be a sign of a dangerous bloodstream infection like meningococcal disease. It needs treatment immediately, so don't wait to see if it improves.
Heard apple cider vinegar shots melt belly fat. True? I do 3 a day

The evidence for that is weak, and any weight loss in studies was tiny. Three undiluted shots a day can erode your tooth enamel, irritate your throat, and in large amounts lower your potassium. If you like it, dilute one tablespoon in a big glass of water, drink it with a meal, and rinse your mouth afterward. Fat loss really comes down to overall diet, protein, sleep, and activity.
whats the fastest way to calm down during a panic attack

Slow your exhale. Breathe in for about four seconds and out for six to eight, because the long out-breath activates the body's calming response. Grounding helps too: press your feet into the floor and name five things you can see. Remind yourself that panic peaks within about ten minutes and passes, even though it feels dangerous. If you've never had one before, or you have chest pain that doesn't settle, get checked in person to rule out a heart problem.
bitten by a neighbor's dog, they say it's vaccinated. do i need rabies shots?

Usually not if the dog is healthy and up to date on vaccines. The standard approach in many places is to have the dog observed for 10 days, and if it stays healthy, no rabies treatment is needed. Ask your neighbor for the vaccination record and report the bite to your doctor or local health department, which can arrange the observation. Still clean the wound thoroughly and get it checked if it's deep or on the hand or face.
can I go to work with a 100.2 fever, I really can't miss tomorrow

Ideally, no. With a fever you're likely contagious, and most workplace and public health guidance says to stay home until you've been fever-free for 24 hours without medicine. Taking ibuprofen only hides the fever, not the infection. If you truly can't miss work, ask about working remotely, and if you have to go in, wear a mask and keep your distance.
can i buy reading glasses at the drugstore or do i need an eye exam

Drugstore readers are perfectly fine for basic age-related near-vision blur if both eyes are similar and they make text comfortable. Still, if you're over 40, an eye exam every year or two is worth it anyway, because it screens for silent problems like glaucoma that readers won't catch. Go sooner if you notice blurry distance vision, double vision, or big differences between your eyes.
rash under my boobs, red and kind of shiny, itches, worse in heat

That sounds like intertrigo, often with a yeast infection on top, which is very common in warm skin folds. Keep the area dry with a breathable cotton bra or a soft cloth tucked under the breast, and apply an over-the-counter antifungal like clotrimazole twice a day for two weeks. Dry the area thoroughly after showering. If it doesn't improve in two weeks, keeps coming back, or develops a bad smell or open sores, see your GP.
Can I take St John's Wort instead of my sertraline? I'd rather go natural.

Please don't swap them on your own. Stopping sertraline abruptly can cause withdrawal symptoms and a relapse, and combining it with St John's Wort can trigger serotonin syndrome, which is dangerous. St John's Wort also interferes with many other drugs, including birth control. If you want to come off sertraline, talk to your prescriber about a gradual taper and what alternatives might suit you.
Is it bad to take melatonin every single night? I've been doing it for like 8 months.

Melatonin is generally low-risk, but nightly use for months usually means something underneath isn't being addressed, like irregular sleep timing, anxiety or a sleep disorder. Most people do best on a low dose, around 0.5 to 3 mg, taken an hour or two before bed, and many take far more than they need. Try tapering down over a couple of weeks while keeping a fixed wake time. If you still can't sleep without it, see your doctor, because chronic insomnia responds well to proper treatment.
My doctor said I had viral myocarditis after COVID. I feel totally fine now, it's been a month. I really want to get back to CrossFit.

Please don't go back to CrossFit on your own judgment here, because myocarditis is the one post-viral situation where feeling fine is not a reliable signal. The usual guidance is to avoid competitive or intense exercise for around three to six months and get cleared with tests like an echo, ECG and sometimes a Holter monitor or exercise stress test first. Intense exercise with an inflamed heart muscle carries a real risk of dangerous arrhythmias. Book a follow-up with your cardiologist and ask specifically about a return-to-exercise plan. They can often approve gentle walking in the meantime.
My 2 year old has been constipated for 4 days and is crying when she tries to go. Can I give her an adult laxative but less of it?

Don't cut down an adult laxative, because dosing them for a toddler isn't straightforward and some aren't safe for little kids. Call her pediatrician today. Many will recommend a child-appropriate option like polyethylene glycol at a weight-based dose, along with more water, pear or prune juice, and fruits and veggies. Get seen sooner if she's vomiting, her belly is swollen or very painful, or there's blood in her stool.
back pain + fever + I had a kidney infection last year. related?

Possibly, so get seen today. Fever with back or flank pain can mean a kidney infection, which needs antibiotics promptly and can become serious if it's left untreated. Go urgently or to the ER if you're vomiting, can't keep fluids down, feel confused, or are getting much sicker.
My 6 year old fell off the monkey bars and her wrist is swollen but she can still move her fingers. Can I just ice it and wait?

Being able to wiggle her fingers doesn't rule out a fracture, and wrist breaks are very common in kids from exactly that kind of fall. Ice it and keep it supported for now, but get her seen at urgent care or her pediatrician today for an X-ray, especially if she's guarding it, it looks bent, or the swelling is significant. Kids' growth plates matter, so this is one to check rather than wait out.
rolled my ankle playing basketball, it's swollen but I can walk on it. can I just tape it and play tomorrow?

Playing on it tomorrow is how a mild sprain turns into one that keeps coming back. For the next couple of days, rest it, ice it for 15 to 20 minutes a few times a day, wrap it with light compression and keep it elevated. Once it's comfortable, start gentle movement. If you can't take four steps without serious pain, or the bony knobs on either side of the ankle are tender to press, get an X-ray to rule out a fracture.
my eye got splashed with bleach while cleaning the bathroom, it stings like crazy

Rinse it right now under lukewarm running water for at least 15 minutes, holding the eyelids open and rolling your eye around so the water reaches everywhere. Take out any contact lenses as you rinse. Bleach is alkaline and can keep damaging the eye after the sting fades, so once you've flushed it, go to urgent care or an ER to get it checked, even if it feels better.
Can I take two of my melatonin gummies instead of one if one isn't working?

Doubling a typical gummy dose is generally safe for healthy adults, but it often doesn't help because more melatonin isn't stronger, and higher doses can cause grogginess or vivid dreams the next day. Timing matters more than amount, so try taking a low dose (0.5 to 3 mg) about one to two hours before bed rather than right as you lie down. If you're on blood thinners, blood pressure medication, or diabetes medication, check with a pharmacist first, since melatonin can interact with them. If you still can't sleep after a few weeks, that's worth raising with a doctor.
what cheeses can't i eat

The main ones to avoid are soft cheeses made with unpasteurized milk, like some brie, camembert, feta, queso fresco and blue cheeses, because of the listeria risk. If the label says pasteurized, most are fine, and hard cheeses like cheddar and parmesan are safe either way. Soft cheese cooked until it's steaming hot is also fine, so baked brie is back on the menu.
Pregnant, 28 weeks, temperature 100.8. Is this something to call about or am I overreacting?

You're not overreacting, so call your OB or the labor and delivery line today. A fever in pregnancy is worth checking out, partly to find the cause and partly because a sustained high temperature isn't great for the baby. Acetaminophen is generally considered the safe choice in pregnancy for bringing the fever down, but avoid ibuprofen in the third trimester.
Is it okay to put hydrogen peroxide on a cut to clean it?

It's better to skip it, because hydrogen peroxide damages the healthy cells your body uses to heal and can actually slow recovery. Rinsing under clean running water with a little mild soap around the edges does the job well. Afterward, a thin layer of petroleum jelly and a bandage keep it moist, which helps it heal faster and scar less. Save the fizzy stuff for something other than open wounds.
My chiropractor wants me coming 3x a week for 6 months prepaid. Legit?

Be wary of that, because long prepaid plans aren't supported by evidence for most back or neck problems, and they're a common red flag for overselling. Reasonable care usually means a short trial of a few weeks with clear goals, then reassessment. If you want hands-on treatment, ask about a shorter plan or look into a physical therapist, who will also teach you exercises to manage it yourself. Also avoid forceful neck manipulation if you've ever had dizziness or vision changes with neck movement.
Ran out of my metoprolol 2 days ago, pharmacy can't refill til Monday. Big deal?

It can be. Stopping metoprolol suddenly can cause a rebound rise in heart rate and blood pressure, and in people with heart disease it can trigger chest pain. Call your pharmacy and ask for an emergency supply, since many pharmacies can dispense a few days' worth, or call your doctor's after-hours line today. If you get chest pain or palpitations, go to urgent care.
My 15 year old son has stopped seeing his friends, sleeps all day on weekends and snaps at everyone. Teen phase or something more?

Some moodiness is normal at 15, but pulling away from friends along with big sleep changes and irritability can be how depression shows up in teenagers. Find a calm moment, maybe side by side in the car, and ask how he's really doing without lecturing. Then book him in with his doctor. If he ever mentions self-harm or not wanting to be here, get help the same day.
I found my mother's blood pressure was 185/105 on her home cuff. She feels totally fine. Can it wait till Monday?

Have her rest quietly for five minutes and recheck. If it's still that high and she feels fine, call her doctor's office today or use an after-hours line rather than waiting until Monday. If she has chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, confusion, vision changes or weakness on one side, call 911 immediately. Also make sure she hasn't missed any blood pressure pills.
feeling better on day 4 of 10 of my antibiotics. ok to stop?

Finish the course unless your doctor tells you otherwise, since feeling better doesn't mean every bacterium is gone and stopping early raises the chance of a relapse. Some infections really can be treated with shorter courses, but that's a call for the prescriber, who knows what you're being treated for. If side effects are the real reason you want to stop, call them, because there's often an easy alternative.
Can I use my husband's blood pressure pills for a day? I ran out and the pharmacy's closed.

Please don't. Even if it's a similar drug, the dose or type may be different, and that can drop your pressure too low or interact with your other medications. Call an after-hours pharmacy or your doctor's on-call line, since pharmacists can often give an emergency supply. Missing a single dose of most blood pressure medications is usually manageable while you sort it out.
I found a tick on my 5yo's scalp. Got it out with tweezers. Now what

Nice work, because pulling it straight out with tweezers is exactly right. Clean the spot with soap and water and note the date. If you can, save the tick in a sealed bag in case it needs to be identified later. Over the next month, watch for an expanding red rash, fever, aches or unusual tiredness, and call her doctor if any of those show up. If the tick looked engorged or may have been attached more than a day, especially somewhere Lyme disease is common, call now to ask whether a preventive antibiotic makes sense.
is green snot = need antibiotics

No, green or yellow mucus is just a sign your immune system is working and happens with ordinary viral colds too. Antibiotics only come into play if a sinus infection lasts more than about 10 days, gets worse after starting to improve, or comes with a high fever and facial pain. Saline rinses and time handle most cases.
My dad has been saying stuff like 'you'd all be better off without me.' He's 58 and lost his job. Am I overreacting?

You're not overreacting. That phrase is a recognized warning sign of suicidal thinking, and job loss in middle-aged men is a known risk factor. Ask him directly and calmly whether he's thinking about suicide, because asking does not plant the idea and often brings relief. Help him reach his doctor or a therapist, and you can call or text 988 in the US yourself for guidance on how to support him. If he has a plan or access to means like firearms or stockpiled pills, treat it as an emergency and get help right away.
My 6 year old fell off the monkey bars and her wrist is swollen but she can move her fingers. Can I just wait and see?

Moving her fingers doesn't rule out a fracture, and wrist breaks are very common in kids after a fall onto an outstretched hand. Put a cold pack wrapped in a cloth on it, keep the arm still and supported, and get her to urgent care or her doctor today for an X-ray. Go to the ER right away if the wrist looks bent, her hand turns pale or numb, or the pain is severe.
can you take naproxen and ibuprofen at the same time? one isn't cutting it

Don't combine them. They're both NSAIDs, so taking them together doubles the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain without adding much pain relief. Pair one of them with acetaminophen instead, since it works differently and combines safely. If you're needing that much pain control regularly, see a doctor.
Migraines started when I began birth control pills, and now I'm seeing zigzag lines before them. Keep taking it?

Talk to your prescriber soon instead of just carrying on. Migraine with aura, which is what those zigzag lines are, raises stroke risk with estrogen-containing pills, and most guidelines advise against combining them. There are effective progestin-only and non-hormonal options, so switching is usually straightforward. Don't stop abruptly without a backup method if you're relying on it to prevent pregnancy.
I have COPD and my oxygen reads 89 on my home meter. normal for me is 91. Is that a big deal?

A two-point drop isn't an emergency on its own, but treat it as a signal, especially if you're also more breathless, coughing more or your mucus has changed color. Rest, follow your COPD action plan if you have one, and recheck in a little while with warm hands. Call your doctor today if it stays lower than usual or your symptoms are worsening, since early treatment can head off a flare. Get emergency care if it falls below about 88 and keeps dropping, or if you're confused, have bluish lips or can't speak in full sentences.
My eye is swollen almost shut after cutting grass, no pain, just itchy. Scary?

Itchy, puffy eyes after cutting grass are usually an allergic reaction, so rinse your eye and face with cool water and use a cold compress. An oral antihistamine or antihistamine eye drops should help within hours. See a doctor promptly if you develop pain, vision changes, fever or redness spreading across your eyelid and cheek, or if it isn't clearly improving by tomorrow, since those can point to infection.
how long can a person go without sleep before it gets dangerous? I have finals and want to pull 2 all nighters back to back

Two all-nighters in a row is a bad trade for finals. After about 24 hours awake your thinking is impaired roughly like being over the legal drink-driving limit, and by 48 hours you'll be having microsleeps and memory problems that undo the studying you stayed up for. Sleep is also when your brain consolidates what you learned. You'll do better studying hard in focused blocks, sleeping at least five or six hours, and reviewing in the morning. Whatever you do, don't drive after a night without sleep, and skip the stimulant pills.
I'm 67, do I need the pneumonia vaccine or is that just a pharma thing

Yes, it's recommended for everyone 65 and older, and it's well worth getting. Pneumococcal disease causes serious pneumonia, bloodstream infections, and meningitis, and older adults are hit hardest. These days it's often a single dose of PCV20 or PCV21, but your pharmacist or doctor can check your history and tell you exactly which one you need.
Why is my blood pressure higher at the doctor than at home?

That's called white coat hypertension, and it's very common, because nerves at the clinic push your numbers up. Home readings are often more representative, so bring a week of logged readings and your cuff to your next appointment so they can check it against theirs. Don't dismiss it entirely, though, since it can be an early sign of developing hypertension.
Postpartum 5 days and I cry constantly, is this baby blues or something worse?

Crying a lot in the first one to two weeks is very common and is usually the baby blues, which comes from hormone shifts and lack of sleep. Mention it to your midwife or health visitor now, though, and get help sooner if it lasts beyond two weeks, gets worse, or you feel hopeless or unable to cope. If you have thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, or feel confused or detached from reality, contact your doctor or emergency services right away, because these are treatable conditions and reaching out quickly matters.
I'm on chemo and spiked 100.5. Probably fine to sleep it off?

Please don't sleep it off. A fever during chemotherapy can be a sign of a serious infection while your immune defenses are low. Call your oncology team's emergency number right now, or go to the ER if you can't reach them. Neutropenic fever is treated as an emergency because early antibiotics matter a lot.
I'm 9 weeks and have some light pink spotting after sex last night, no cramps. Am I miscarrying??

Light pink spotting after sex is common in early pregnancy because the cervix has extra blood flow and bleeds easily, and on its own it doesn't mean you're miscarrying. Wear a pad and keep an eye on it, and give your provider's office a call today to let them know, since they may want to check you. Go to urgent care or the ER if the bleeding becomes as heavy as a period, you pass clots or tissue, or you develop strong cramps, shoulder pain or dizziness.
is it ok to skip metformin on days I don't eat much

Metformin doesn't usually cause lows on its own, so a light-eating day isn't normally a reason to skip it. The real reason to pause it is if you're vomiting, badly dehydrated, or very sick, and then you should check with your doctor or pharmacist about holding it temporarily. If you're often skipping doses because it upsets your stomach, ask about the extended-release version, which many people tolerate much better.
Can I take ibuprofen with my antibiotics?

For almost all common antibiotics, yes, and it's fine for pain or fever. Take it with food to protect your stomach, and avoid it if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, or are on blood thinners. If you're on something less common, like a fluoroquinolone with a history of seizures, a quick check with your pharmacist is worthwhile.
My dad has kidney disease and wants to start protein shakes to build muscle. good idea?

He should check with his nephrologist or a renal dietitian before starting. With kidney disease, extra protein can speed up kidney decline, and many shakes are also high in potassium or phosphorus, which can be dangerous for him. His care team can tell him the right protein target for his stage. A renal dietitian can help him build muscle safely, and resistance exercise is usually encouraged.
what's the deal with neosporin, should i put it on every little cut

For most small cuts, cleaning with water and keeping them covered with a bit of plain petroleum jelly works just as well as an antibiotic ointment. Neosporin is fine to use, but it causes allergic skin reactions in a fair number of people. It's best saved for scrapes in dirtier settings.
woke up and half my face droops and my ear hurts, also cant close my eye fully

Get seen today, and if you also have weakness in an arm or leg, slurred speech or confusion, call emergency services right away, because it could be a stroke. A droopy face with ear pain is often Bell's palsy or a shingles-related condition, and both respond best to medication started within the first few days. In the meantime, protect the eye that won't close with lubricating drops and tape it shut gently at night so it doesn't get damaged.
sunburn so bad i have blisters on my shoulders. aloe enough?

Blistering means a second-degree burn. Use cool showers or compresses and aloe, take ibuprofen, drink plenty of water, and don't pop the blisters. Cover any broken ones with a light non-stick dressing and keep them out of the sun until fully healed. Get medical care if the blistering covers a large area, or you have fever, chills, nausea or signs of infection.
56M, newly diagnosed hypertension and borderline diabetes. Doctor wants me on two pills. I'd rather try diet first. Reasonable?

It's a reasonable conversation to have, and lifestyle changes really can lower both blood pressure and blood sugar a lot. Whether it's safe to wait depends on how high your numbers are, though. If your blood pressure is quite elevated, the stroke and heart attack risk in the meantime is real. Ask your doctor directly whether a three-month trial of diet, exercise, and weight loss with home blood pressure monitoring is acceptable, or whether to start meds now and try to come off them later. Many doctors will agree to one of those, and you'll know you're not taking a gamble.
toothache went away on its own after a week of agony. so i'm good right?

Not necessarily, because severe pain that suddenly stops can mean the nerve inside the tooth has died. The underlying infection can keep going quietly and flare up later as an abscess. Get it checked soon while things are calm, since treatment is usually easier now than during an emergency.
2 yr old bumped head on coffee table, small goose egg, crying stopped quickly. need ER?

A quick cry, a bump on the forehead, and then back to normal is very common and usually doesn't need the ER. Ice it with a wrapped cold pack and watch him closely for the next 24 hours. Go in right away if he vomits more than once, seems unusually sleepy or hard to wake, acts confused or unsteady, lost consciousness at all, or if the swelling is on the back or side of his head rather than the forehead.
Does grapefruit really mess with statins or is that a myth? I'm 58 and love my morning grapefruit.

It's real, but it depends on which statin you take. Grapefruit blocks an enzyme that breaks down simvastatin and lovastatin, and to a lesser degree atorvastatin, so blood levels can climb high enough to raise the risk of muscle damage. Rosuvastatin and pravastatin aren't meaningfully affected. Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether yours is a problem, and if it is, they may be able to switch you so you can keep your grapefruit.
Should I give my kid aspirin for fever? It's what my mom always gave us.

Skip the aspirin. It's not recommended for anyone under 18 with a fever because of the risk of Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition that affects the liver and brain. Children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen at the dose for their weight is the safer choice.
I'm allergic to penicillin. Doc prescribed cefalexin. Is that safe??

Usually yes; the cross-reactivity between penicillin and cephalexin is low, and doctors prescribe it to penicillin-allergic patients all the time. The exception is if your penicillin reaction was severe, like throat swelling, difficulty breathing, or a blistering skin reaction. If that's your history, call the prescriber before taking it to make sure they knew. Either way, stop and seek emergency help if you get hives, swelling of the face or lips, or wheezing.
I fell off a ladder about 6 feet and landed on my back. I can move but my back hurts a lot. Should I just take some advil and lie down?

A fall from that height onto your back is enough to injure the spine, so get evaluated today rather than sleeping it off. If you have numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs, trouble controlling your bladder, or severe pain, call 911 and stay still. Otherwise, have someone drive you to urgent care or the ER. Moving around fine doesn't rule out a fracture.
do i need electrolyte drinks for my 30 min jog

Nope. For a 30-minute jog, water is plenty, and electrolyte drinks just add sugar or cost. They start to matter for runs over about an hour, hard sessions in serious heat, or if you're a heavy, salty sweater.
Doctor gave me doxycycline. Anything I should know? I'm going to the beach.

Doxycycline makes you burn much faster, so use high-SPF sunscreen, cover up and avoid midday sun. Take each dose with a full glass of water and stay upright for at least 30 minutes afterward, because it can cause painful irritation if it sits in your esophagus. Don't take it at the same time as dairy, antacids, iron or calcium, which block absorption. Space those at least two hours apart.
Can I use my mom's leftover oxycodone for my bad back? It's like 2 years old.

Don't use it. Taking someone else's opioid is risky. Opioids can cause dangerous drowsiness and slowed breathing, especially with alcohol, sleep aids or anxiety medications, and they don't work better than NSAIDs for most back pain. Stick with over-the-counter options, heat and gentle movement. If your pain is severe enough that you're reaching for that, see a doctor. Then take those old pills to a pharmacy take-back program so they're safely disposed of.
I'm 80 with osteoporosis and my back suddenly hurts badly after just bending to pick up a towel. Do I need to bother anyone?

Yes, please call your doctor today. With osteoporosis, sudden severe back pain after something as minor as bending can mean a vertebral compression fracture. These are common and very treatable, but they need an X-ray to confirm. Proper pain control can keep you mobile, and your doctor may want to review your bone treatment too. If you also have leg weakness or numbness, go to the emergency department.
how do I know if I'm ready to exercise again after being sick

A good rule is that you're ready to start easing back in when you've had no fever for at least a day without medication, you're eating and sleeping normally, and everyday activity like stairs or a walk doesn't wipe you out. Begin at around half your usual intensity and duration, and if you feel fine afterward and the next day, step it up gradually. If symptoms come back or you feel unusually drained, drop back down.
how fast can I get my blood pressure down naturally, I have a work physical in 3 days

You can't safely make a big change in three days, but you can avoid things that falsely raise your reading. Cut back on salt and alcohol, sleep well, and skip caffeine, nicotine, and decongestants the morning of the exam. Arrive early and sit quietly before the test. If you're truly hypertensive, it's better to have it found and treated than masked.
Baby (4 months) has a flat spot on the back of her head

Flat spots are common at this age because babies spend so much time on their backs, and they usually improve with repositioning. Give her plenty of supervised tummy time while she's awake. Alternate which end of the crib her head faces, and limit long stretches in car seats and swings. Keep putting her to sleep on her back. Point it out at her next checkup, since a doctor can tell whether a helmet or a neck-tightness check is needed.
Lump under my arm 5 days after my covid booster. Freaking out a little.

That's very likely a swollen lymph node, a common and harmless sign that your immune system is responding, and it usually shows up on the same side as the shot. These typically fade within a couple of weeks. If it's still there after four to six weeks, keeps growing, or you notice other new lumps, have your doctor check it. If you have a mammogram scheduled soon, mention the recent vaccine, since it can show up on the scan.
Back pain plus I've lost about 15 pounds without trying and I'm sweating at night. 58F. Probably just stress right?

I wouldn't put this down to stress. The combination of back pain, unintentional weight loss, and night sweats is a pattern doctors want to look into promptly. It can have several causes, including infection or other conditions that are far easier to treat when caught early. Please book an appointment with your doctor within the next week or so and mention all three symptoms together.
is it ok to give my kid tylenol before shots so he doesn't get a fever

It's better not to give it beforehand. Some studies suggest that pre-dosing fever reducers may slightly blunt the immune response to certain vaccines. If he gets a fever or is fussy afterward, it's fine to treat it with the correct weight-based dose. To help with the needle pain itself, numbing cream, a distraction, or holding him on your lap all work well.
My dad (78) fell in the bathroom, says he's fine but his hip hurts when he walks. He refuses to go in.

Hip pain after a fall at his age needs an X-ray. Some hip fractures still let a person walk, and missing one can lead to serious complications. Try reframing it for him: a quick check now is what keeps him independent, and a doctor visit or urgent care trip is much easier than a crisis later. If he can't put weight on that leg, or the leg looks shortened or turned outward, call 911.
hives keep showing up every few days for like 2 months now. no idea why

Hives lasting more than six weeks are called chronic hives, and often no specific trigger is ever found. A daily non-drowsy antihistamine is the usual first treatment, and doctors sometimes increase the dose beyond the label under their supervision. See a doctor or allergist to rule out underlying causes and discuss stronger options if needed, and go to the ER if you ever get lip or throat swelling or trouble breathing.
Kid cut his knee on gravel, there's little bits stuck in it. Do I need to get every bit out?

Yes, it's worth getting the grit out, because dirt left in a wound raises the risk of infection and can leave permanent dark marks in the skin. Rinse it under running water for several minutes and gently wipe with a clean wet cloth. You can lift out loose bits with tweezers cleaned in alcohol. If pieces are embedded deep, the wound is large, or he won't let you near it, a clinic can clean it properly with numbing. Afterward, cover it with petroleum jelly and a bandage.
Chef here, sliced fingertip pad clean off, maybe pea-sized. Bleeding like mad. Worth going in?

Yes, get it seen. Fingertip injuries bleed heavily, and a pea-sized loss of tissue usually heals well with proper dressing, but a clinician should check whether bone is exposed and set you up with the right care. Press firmly with a clean cloth and keep your hand raised above your heart. If you have the piece of fingertip, wrap it in damp gauze, put it in a sealed bag, and set that bag on ice to bring with you.
Are those detox teas actually doing anything? I feel lighter after

That lighter feeling is mostly from laxatives like senna and diuretic ingredients flushing out water and stool, not fat or toxins. Regular use can cause dehydration, electrolyte imbalances and dependence on laxatives to go to the bathroom. Your liver and kidneys already handle detoxing well. Water, fiber and sleep will do more for you.
Can I microdose mushrooms to fix my depression instead of meds?

The evidence for microdosing is weak, and placebo-controlled studies have mostly found effects no better than placebo. It's also illegal in most places, doses are unpredictable, and it can interact with antidepressants or trigger problems in people with a personal or family history of psychosis or bipolar disorder. If medication isn't appealing, therapy alone works well for many people, so talk to a doctor about all your options, and ask about legitimate clinical trials if psychedelic therapy interests you.
toothache + headache + ear pain on same side. connected?

They can be connected, because pain from an upper or lower back tooth often radiates to the ear, temple and jaw. Jaw joint problems or an ear infection can mimic the same pattern. Ibuprofen is a good first step. If it lasts more than a couple of days, see a dentist first, and see a doctor if there's ear discharge, hearing changes or fever.
fever 101 for two days, body aches, cough. flu?

That combination sounds a lot like flu or another respiratory virus, especially if it came on suddenly. Rest, fluids, and acetaminophen or ibuprofen for the aches are the mainstay. If you're within about 48 hours of symptom onset or you're higher risk (over 65, pregnant, asthma, diabetes, heart disease), call your doctor, because antiviral medication works best when started early. Get seen promptly if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, confusion, or a fever that comes back after improving.
I have leftover oxycodone from surgery. Can I take one for my sprained ankle?

I wouldn't. Ibuprofen or naproxen with ice and elevation usually handles a sprain better, because they also reduce swelling, and they don't carry the drowsiness or dependence risk of opioids. Leftover opioids are best disposed of at a pharmacy take-back site so they don't end up in the wrong hands. If the ankle is so painful you can't bear weight, get it X-rayed to rule out a fracture.
My eyelid has a painful red bump near the lashes. Can I pop it like a pimple?

Don't squeeze it, because that can spread the infection into the eyelid. It sounds like a stye. Warm compresses for 10 to 15 minutes, several times a day, usually help it drain by itself within a week. Skip eye makeup and contacts meanwhile. See a doctor if the whole lid swells, your vision changes, or it's not improving after a week or two.
ice on a burn yes or no, quick
No. Ice can damage the tissue further and cause a cold injury on top of the burn. Use cool running tap water for about 20 minutes instead.
My teen son wants pre-workout powder, he's 15. thoughts?

I'd steer him away from it. Most pre-workouts pack 200 to 400 mg of caffeine per scoop, plus other stimulants, which can cause a racing heart, anxiety and poor sleep in a 15-year-old. Some are also contaminated with banned substances. A banana or some toast an hour before training does the same job safely, and good sleep and regular meals matter far more for his progress.
Recovering from covid, mild case. Any red flags I should watch for when I start running again?

Yes. Stop and get checked if you notice chest pain or pressure, palpitations or a racing heart that doesn't settle, unusual breathlessness, dizziness or fainting, or a resting heart rate noticeably higher than your usual. Those can be signs of heart or lung involvement, which is uncommon but important to catch. Without those, start with a week of easy, short sessions and build up gradually.
I keep checking that the stove is off like 20 times before leaving, it's making me late for work. Just how do I stop

That pattern of repeated checking that you can't shake off sounds like it could be OCD, and the good news is it responds really well to treatment. Each check gives you brief relief, which teaches your brain to check again, so the most effective approach is a therapy called exposure and response prevention. In it you gradually practise checking once and tolerating the discomfort until it fades. A GP referral to a CBT therapist who does ERP is the best route, and it usually makes a big difference.
Wrist pain and tingling in my thumb and fingers at night, wake up shaking my hand. Carpal tunnel?

That's a very typical picture of carpal tunnel syndrome, where the median nerve gets compressed at the wrist. A wrist splint worn at night that keeps the wrist straight often helps a lot, along with cutting back on repetitive gripping. See your GP if it doesn't improve in a few weeks, or sooner if you notice weakness, clumsiness or wasting at the base of the thumb, as steroid injections or minor surgery work well and nerve damage is better caught early.
quick q - does caffeine actually help headaches or is that a myth

It's real. Caffeine narrows blood vessels and helps pain relievers absorb, which is why it's added to products like Excedrin, and a cup of coffee can take the edge off a tension headache or early migraine. The catch is that daily heavy use leads to withdrawal headaches when you skip it. Use it occasionally as a boost, not as a crutch.
my bp machine just said 182/115 and i have a pounding headache and blurry vision. should i just lie down?

Don't lie down and wait this out. A reading that high together with a severe headache and blurry vision can signal a hypertensive emergency, so call emergency services or get someone to take you to the ER right now. Don't drive yourself, and don't take extra doses of any blood pressure pills to try to bring it down on your own.
swimmer's ear remedies? going to the beach again tomorrow

If your outer ear hurts when you tug on it, see a doctor for prescription antibiotic drops, which usually clear swimmer's ear within a few days. Keep the ear dry while it heals, so skip swimming tomorrow or use a well-fitting earplug, and don't put anything into the canal. Over-the-counter drying drops are fine for preventing it, but they aren't a good treatment for an active infection, and you shouldn't use them if your eardrum might be damaged. Once it heals, tilting your head and drying your ears gently after swimming helps stop it from coming back.
i think i have ringworm on my arm. circle shape, itchy, clear-ish middle

That description fits ringworm well, which is a fungal infection, not a worm. Apply an over-the-counter antifungal cream like terbinafine or clotrimazole twice a day, and keep going for one to two weeks after it looks gone, because stopping early is the usual reason it comes back. Wash towels and check pets, since they're a common source. If it's spreading despite treatment after two weeks, or it's on your scalp, see a doctor because you may need tablets.
Is it normal for type 1 kids to have sugars all over the place during growth spurts?

Yes. Growth spurts and puberty raise insulin resistance because of growth hormone, so sugars often swing higher, especially overnight and in the morning. It usually means their doses need to go up, so check in with their diabetes team rather than guessing at changes yourself. Keep logging readings, since patterns make the adjustments easier.
There's a red area around a bug bite on my leg and it's getting bigger and hot. Should I worry?

A bite that's red, hot and spreading sounds like it could be cellulitis, a skin infection that usually needs antibiotics, so see a doctor today. Draw a line around the edge of the redness with a pen so you can tell if it's spreading. If you develop a fever, chills, red streaks running up the leg, or the area spreads fast over a few hours, go to urgent care or the ER right away.
ok so strep throat, on amoxicillin day 3, feel better. lifting heavy today?

If you've been fever-free for a day and feel genuinely better, a moderate session is reasonable, but I'd skip maxing out and keep it around 60 to 70 percent of your usual effort. Your body is still finishing the job, and heavy lifting when you're run down can bring back fatigue. Keep taking the full course of amoxicillin even though you feel better.
woke up with headache and my whole family feels sick and dizzy too, we have a gas furnace

Get everyone, including pets, out into fresh air right now and call emergency services from outside. Headaches and dizziness hitting a whole household with a fuel-burning appliance strongly suggest carbon monoxide poisoning, which can be deadly. Don't go back in until the fire service or your gas provider has checked the house, and make sure you have a working CO alarm afterwards.
I'm on blood pressure meds, which cold medicine is safe?

Avoid decongestants like pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine, because they can raise your blood pressure. Look for products labeled for high blood pressure, like Coricidin HBP, or treat symptoms individually. Saline spray works for congestion, acetaminophen for aches, and plain dextromethorphan for cough. A quick check with your pharmacist is worth it to rule out interactions with your specific medications.
Working from home on my sofa all day and my neck and shoulders are wrecked. Quick fixes?

The biggest quick fix is raising your screen to eye level, even on a stack of books, and using a separate keyboard so you're not hunching over a laptop. Sit at a table with your back supported, and get up every 30 to 45 minutes to move, roll your shoulders and do a few chin tucks. Heat on the tight muscles in the evening helps, and things usually improve within a couple of weeks once the setup changes.
my kid got stung by a bee, first time. what to watch for

Scrape the stinger out with a fingernail or card, wash the area, and use ice and an antihistamine for local swelling, which can be quite large and still be normal. Call 911 if you see hives spreading away from the sting, swelling of the face or lips, wheezing, trouble swallowing, vomiting, or dizziness. Serious reactions usually start within 30 minutes, so keep an eye on them for that window.
had the flu last week, fever broke 2 days ago. can i go back to my usual 10k runs tomorrow?

Give it a bit more time: wait until you've been fever-free for at least a few days without any fever-reducing meds, then start with an easy 20 to 30 minute jog rather than a full 10k. Flu can leave you more drained than you feel at rest, and pushing hard too soon can stretch out your recovery. If that first easy run feels fine, build back up over a week or two, and stop if you get chest pain, unusual breathlessness or a racing heart.
Been bloated every day for like 3 weeks and my jeans don't fit, I'm 58 female, no big diet changes

New, persistent bloating that lasts weeks without a clear reason deserves a doctor's visit, especially at your age. Most of the time the cause is benign, like IBS or constipation. But ongoing bloating in women over 50 is also one of the subtle signs of ovarian cancer, and that's worth ruling out. Book an appointment soon and mention how long it's lasted and any changes in appetite, urination or bowel habits.
can you be allergic to the sun? i get itchy bumps every spring when i go outside

Yes, and what you're describing sounds a lot like polymorphous light eruption, a common sun sensitivity that flares in spring when skin first gets strong sunlight again. Using broad-spectrum high-SPF sunscreen, wearing covering clothing, and gradually building up sun exposure often helps a lot. A dermatologist can confirm it and rule out other photosensitivity causes, including reactions to medications you might be taking.
I'm a teacher and I feel a cold coming on. How do I know when I'm not contagious anymore?

You're most contagious in the first two to three days of symptoms, and you can spread a cold for about a week, though less as you improve. A practical rule is to return once you've been fever-free for at least 24 hours without fever medicine and feel well enough to work. Wash your hands often and cough into your elbow in the meantime. A mask in the classroom for the first few days back is a kind move if your school allows it.
university student here, i keep getting heart palpitations when stressed. anxiety or should i worry

Stress-related palpitations are very common and usually harmless, especially if they come with anxious moments and settle down afterward. Caffeine, energy drinks and poor sleep often make them worse, so cut back there first. Still, get them checked once by a doctor, who can do a quick ECG. And seek urgent care if you have chest pain, fainting, shortness of breath, or palpitations that don't stop.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and have a headache that won't go away plus my vision is kind of sparkly. Probably just tired?

Please don't assume it's tiredness. A persistent headache with visual changes in late pregnancy is a classic warning sign of preeclampsia, which can become dangerous quickly. Call your labor and delivery unit or OB right now, or go straight to the hospital, so they can check your blood pressure and urine.
is cracking your knuckles gonna give me arthritis

No, the research doesn't support that. Studies, including one doctor who cracked the knuckles of only one hand for decades, haven't found that knuckle cracking causes arthritis. The pop is just gas releasing from the joint fluid. The one exception is if cracking hurts or your joints are swollen, which is worth getting checked.
sudden hearing loss in my right ear woke up with it, no pain. just wax probably?

It might be wax, but sudden hearing loss in one ear with no obvious cause needs to be seen within a day or two, because it can be sudden sensorineural hearing loss. That condition responds best to steroid treatment started early. See an urgent care doctor or an ENT as soon as you can and say it was sudden. Don't spend a week trying wax drops first and lose the window for treatment.
I get stomach pain and diarrhea every time I'm stressed before exams. Normal?

Very common, since the gut and brain are tightly linked, and stress can speed things up in your intestines. Regular sleep, cutting back on caffeine before exams, eating smaller plain meals, and using breathing exercises or a short walk can all ease it. If it happens a lot even outside stressful times, it might be irritable bowel syndrome, which a doctor can help you manage. Get it checked if you notice blood, weight loss or symptoms that wake you up at night.
Red streak going up my arm from a cut on my hand. Kinda hot and sore.

A red streak spreading from a wound can mean the infection is moving through your lymphatic system, and that needs to be seen today, not tomorrow. Go to urgent care or your doctor right away, since this usually needs prescription antibiotics. If you also have a fever, chills, or the streak is moving quickly, go to the emergency room.
Short version: always tired, unmotivated, can't focus. Depression or just lazy?

Laziness doesn't usually feel this bad. Ongoing tiredness, low motivation, and poor focus are classic depression symptoms, but they can also come from thyroid problems, anemia, poor sleep, or vitamin deficiencies. See your doctor for a checkup and basic blood tests. If those come back normal, ask about being screened for depression or ADHD, because both are very treatable.
lips swelling after shrimp. took benadryl. good?

Benadryl can help mild symptoms, but lip swelling after shellfish can progress to a serious reaction, and Benadryl won't stop anaphylaxis. Call 911 or get to an ER now if you notice any throat tightness, trouble swallowing or breathing, a hoarse voice, dizziness, or vomiting. If you have epinephrine, use it. Even if things settle down, don't stay alone, and see a doctor soon to confirm a shellfish allergy and get an epinephrine prescription.
my blood sugar was 52 just now, type 1, what do I do fast

Treat it right now with 15 grams of fast sugar, such as 4 glucose tablets, half a cup of juice or regular soda, or a tablespoon of honey, then recheck in 15 minutes. If you're still under 70, repeat the 15 grams. Once you're back up, eat a snack with some protein or carbs if your next meal is more than an hour away. If you feel confused or can't keep sugar down, get someone to help you or call emergency services, and make sure the people around you know where your glucagon is.
quick question is st john's wort ok for mild depression

It has some evidence for mild depression, but it interacts with a lot of medications, including the contraceptive pill, blood thinners, some heart drugs and antidepressants, sometimes dangerously. Check with a pharmacist or doctor before starting it. Never combine it with prescribed antidepressants. Exercise, daylight and talking therapy are good evidence-based options for mild depression too.
my 4 month old has a fever of 100.8 the day after her shots, is that normal or should I go to the ER?

A low-grade fever like 100.8°F within a day or two of routine infant vaccines is common and usually means her immune system is responding as expected. Keep her comfortable, offer frequent feeds, and ask her pediatrician about acetaminophen and the right dose for her weight before giving any. Go to the ER or call right away if the fever hits 104°F or higher, she's inconsolable for more than three hours, she's unusually floppy or hard to wake, or she has trouble breathing. If the fever lasts beyond 48 hours, call the pediatrician to rule out something unrelated to the shots.
My husband has a fever of 104 and he's acting confused, kind of out of it. He says he just needs sleep.

Take him to the ER now, or call emergency services if he's hard to rouse or getting worse. Confusion with a fever that high can signal a serious infection like meningitis or sepsis, and that needs urgent evaluation. Don't let him sleep it off.
i'm 7 weeks pregnant and threw up 6 times today, can't keep water down. is this just normal morning sickness?

Some vomiting is normal at 7 weeks, but not being able to keep water down is a different situation, because you can get dehydrated quickly.
