Call your midwife or doctor today, or go to urgent care if you're dizzy, peeing very little, or your urine is dark. This could be hyperemesis gravidarum, and it responds well to treatment like IV fluids and anti-nausea medication. You don't have to tough it out.
do weighted blankets actually work or is it a scam

They're not a scam, but they're not magic either; small studies suggest they can help some people feel calmer and sleep a bit better, especially those with anxiety. Most people do best with a blanket around 10 percent of their body weight. They're not safe for babies or toddlers, and people with breathing problems or limited mobility should check with a doctor first. If you're curious, try one with a good return policy.
I'm on blood thinners and my stomach hurts after taking aspirin for a headache. Big deal?

It could be, because aspirin combined with a blood thinner significantly raises the risk of stomach bleeding. Stop taking aspirin for headaches and ask your doctor or pharmacist what pain relief is safe for you, which is usually acetaminophen. Call your doctor today about the stomach pain, and go to the ER if you see black or bloody stool, vomit blood or coffee-ground-like material, or feel faint.
My 90-year-old mother wants to keep driving. She's had two fender benders this year. How do I handle this?

Two crashes in a year is a real warning sign. A good next step is asking her doctor to evaluate her vision, reaction time and cognition, or arranging a formal driving assessment through an occupational therapist. Hearing it from a neutral professional often lands better than hearing it from family. Before she gives up the keys, work out alternatives like rides, community transport or delivery services, because losing independence is usually the real fear.
Is pink eye always contagious and does it need antibiotic drops?

Most pink eye is viral or allergic, and neither responds to antibiotic drops. Viral pink eye is contagious and clears in one to two weeks with cold compresses. Thick yellow-green discharge that glues the eye shut suggests bacterial, which drops can shorten. See a doctor promptly if you wear contacts or have eye pain, light sensitivity or blurred vision, since those can signal something more serious.
My dad's sugar is 450 and he's confused and vomiting. Can I just give him his insulin and wait?

Call 911 or take him to the ER now. Confusion and vomiting with sugar that high can mean diabetic ketoacidosis or a hyperosmolar state, and both are emergencies that need IV fluids and monitored treatment. Don't try to manage this at home with extra insulin. Bring his medications and meter with you.
My 4 year old has had diarrhea since yesterday, still playing but not eating much. Do I need to worry?

A kid who's still playing is reassuring, and most toddler diarrhea is a virus that clears in a few days. Hydration matters far more than food right now, so offer small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte, and let her eat bland foods whenever she wants. Call her doctor if she has fewer wet diapers or trips to pee, no tears when crying, a dry mouth, blood in the stool, a high fever, or unusual sleepiness, or if it's still going after a few more days.
Toddler hit his head on the coffee table, cried right away, now playing. Do I need to do anything?

Crying right away and then going back to normal play is a reassuring sign. Watch him closely for the next 24 hours. Take him to the ER if he vomits more than once, seems confused or unusually sleepy, is hard to wake, has trouble walking, or develops a large soft swelling. It's fine to let him nap; just check that he wakes easily and acts like himself.
What's the fastest way to get rid of a cold sore before my wedding on Saturday

Start an antiviral cream like aciclovir straight away and apply it as often as the label says, five times a day for aciclovir. Better still, ask a doctor or pharmacist today about oral antivirals like valaciclovir, which can shorten an outbreak when taken early. Keep your hands off it, and use a cold sore patch, which protects it and can be covered with makeup on the day. Avoid kissing anyone or sharing lip products until it's fully healed, and congratulations.
18 weeks pregnant, can I keep taking my usual lisinopril?

Contact your doctor or midwife today, because ACE inhibitors like lisinopril aren't recommended in pregnancy, especially after the first trimester, due to risks to the baby's kidneys. Don't just stop without a plan, since your pressure still needs controlling. They can switch you to a pregnancy-safe option like labetalol or nifedipine.
Grandpa takes simvastatin. He loves grapefruit juice every morning. Big deal?

Yes, it matters. Grapefruit blocks the enzyme that breaks down simvastatin, so blood levels can rise sharply and raise the risk of muscle damage, which shows up as unexplained muscle pain, weakness or dark urine. Orange juice is a fine swap. If he won't give up grapefruit, his doctor can switch him to a statin like rosuvastatin or pravastatin, which aren't affected.
I'm 78 and diabetic. My granddaughter's puppy nipped my shin, small break in the skin.

Diabetes and age both slow healing, and shins are a common spot for wounds to linger, so this is worth more care than usual. Wash it gently with soap and water, cover it with a clean dressing, and call your doctor today to have it looked at. They may recommend antibiotics or a tetanus booster. Check it daily, and get seen promptly if you notice redness, warmth, swelling or drainage, or if your blood sugars run higher than usual.
Teen knocked out a permanent front tooth playing hockey. Help??

Move fast, because the tooth has the best chance of surviving if it's back in within about 30 to 60 minutes. Pick it up by the crown, not the root, and rinse it briefly in milk or saline without scrubbing. If he's alert and calm, gently push it back into the socket and have him bite on gauze. Otherwise, store it in milk or inside his cheek and get to an emergency dentist or ER immediately.
Can I superglue a cut shut instead of going to urgent care? It's about an inch long on my forearm.

Household superglue isn't made for skin and can irritate it. Medical skin glue exists, but it's only right for clean, shallow cuts with edges that come together easily. If the cut is gaping, deep, or still bleeding after 10 minutes of pressure, urgent care is the right call, and they may use glue or stitches. A shallow, straight inch-long cut that closes neatly can usually be handled with butterfly strips and a bandage.
my 4 year old shoved a bead in her ear, can i get it out with tweezers?

Please don't use tweezers, because a round bead tends to slip and get pushed deeper, and a squirming four-year-old makes it easy to scratch the canal or damage the eardrum. If you can clearly see it right at the opening, tilting her head affected side down and gently shaking can sometimes let it fall out on its own. Otherwise take her to her doctor or an urgent care today, where they have the right tools and can do it safely in a minute or two.
my 8 month old has a 102 fever but is playing and drinking fine. ER?

If she's playful and drinking well, she usually doesn't need the ER for a 102°F fever at 8 months. Calling your pediatrician for advice is still a good idea. You can give infant acetaminophen or ibuprofen at the weight-based dose. Go in if she becomes listless, refuses to drink, has far fewer wet diapers, breathes hard, or the fever lasts more than 24 hours.
I've had insomnia for over a year. Pills haven't helped long term. Is there anything else?

Yes, the first-line treatment that experts actually recommend is cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), and it often works better long term than medication. It involves structured techniques like consistent wake times, temporarily restricting time in bed, and retraining your brain to link bed with sleep. You can do it with a trained therapist or through reputable digital programs. Ask your doctor for a referral, and get checked for apnea, depression or pain if those could be playing a role.
my dad (72) has bad belly pain and his belly is swollen and hard, he hasnt pooped in days and keeps vomiting

Take him to the ER right away or call an ambulance, because a swollen, hard belly with vomiting and no bowel movements in an older adult strongly suggests a bowel obstruction. That's a medical emergency, and it can get dangerous quickly. Don't give him laxatives, food or drink while you wait.
Raccoon got into our garage and my dog fought it. Dog's fine, I'm fine, but I cleaned my dog's wounds bare-handed. Concern?

Yes, call both your vet and your doctor or local health department today. Raccoons are a major rabies carrier, and its saliva on your dog's wounds could reach you through any cuts on your hands. Your dog will probably need a rabies booster and an observation period even if vaccinated. Your doctor can decide whether you need preventive shots. Wash your hands thoroughly now and use gloves for any further wound care.
Are probiotics worth it for an upset stomach?

Probiotics have decent evidence for a few specific situations, like preventing diarrhea from antibiotics and possibly easing some IBS symptoms. For a random upset stomach, the benefit is modest. If you try them, pick a product with researched strains like Saccharomyces boulardii or Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and give it a few weeks. Yogurt and kefir are cheap ways to get some of the same effect, and people with weakened immune systems should check with their doctor first.
my asthma attack eased after the inhaler, do i still need to go to the doctor?

If it was a real attack that needed several puffs, yes, see your doctor within the next day or two even though it eased. Attacks can come back within hours, and your treatment may need adjusting to stop it happening again. Go urgently if symptoms return or the reliever stops lasting at least four hours.
I'm 34, I feel burnt out constantly, and I'm thinking of quitting my job with no plan. Smart or dumb?

It can be the right call, but quitting with no plan often swaps burnout stress for money stress, which can feel just as crushing. Before you decide, see whether you can buy yourself some breathing room first: take some leave, see a doctor about medical leave if you're really depleted, or start a quiet job search while you set a firm end date. It's also worth having a doctor check whether this is burnout or depression, because depression can make every option look hopeless and follows you to the next job. If you do have enough savings to cover a few months, a planned break is a legitimate choice.
Is it normal for a cut to be a little pink around the edges after 2 days?

A thin pink rim around a healing cut is normal and is just part of the inflammation that comes with repair. What's not normal is redness that spreads outward, gets darker, feels hot, throbs more each day, or comes with pus or a fever. If you see any of those, especially a red streak tracking away from the wound, get it checked promptly because it could be an infection.
found some cinnamon pills online that say they cure diabetes, worth trying instead of meds?

No, nothing cures diabetes, and cinnamon has at best a tiny, inconsistent effect on blood sugar in studies. Swapping it in for your medication risks high sugars quietly damaging your body. If you want to take it alongside your meds, tell your doctor first, because some supplements interact with other drugs or affect the liver. Your money is better spent on test strips or a good pair of walking shoes.
my bp just read 185/120 at the pharmacy machine but i feel totally fine. can i just go home and recheck tomorrow?

Don't wait until tomorrow. Sit quietly for five minutes and recheck, and if it's still around 180/120 or higher, call your doctor's office or an urgent care line today. If you have chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, vision changes or trouble speaking, call emergency services right away. Feeling fine doesn't rule out a reading that high, so it needs a same-day conversation with a professional.
can my kid go to daycare the day after shots?

Usually yes. If they're acting like themselves, there's no reason to keep them home. Most daycares will send kids home with a fever, though, so if they're running a temperature or are really fussy, a quiet day at home is kinder for everyone. Side effects typically settle within a day or two.
My dad (68) has black tarry poop the last two days. He says he feels fine.

Black, tarry stool can mean bleeding in the upper digestive tract, so your dad should see a doctor today even though he feels fine, because slow bleeds often don't cause symptoms until they're serious. Iron pills and Pepto-Bismol can also turn stool black, so mention it if he takes either. Take him to the ER instead if he's dizzy, faint, short of breath, pale, or vomiting anything that looks like coffee grounds. Bring a list of his medications, especially blood thinners, aspirin or NSAIDs.
sudden curtain over part of my vision in one eye, no pain. probably nothing?

Treat this as an emergency. A painless shadow or curtain moving across your vision is a classic sign of retinal detachment, and it can also come from a blocked blood vessel or a stroke. Go to an ER or an emergency eye clinic today, not tomorrow. Fast treatment is often the difference between saving and losing sight in that eye.
Is it fine to let my 5 year old sit in the front seat for a short drive?

No. Kids are safest in the back seat until they're about 13, because a deploying front airbag can seriously injure a small child, even at low speeds. At 5, he should also still be in a car seat with a harness or a booster seat, depending on his size. Short trips aren't safer, since most crashes happen close to home.
What's actually the difference between a cold and flu? I can never tell

The big difference is speed and intensity. A cold creeps in gradually with a stuffy nose, sneezing and sore throat, and you can usually still function. Flu tends to hit suddenly, often within hours, with fever, body aches, chills and exhaustion that can flatten you for days. If you think it's flu and you're in a higher-risk group, call your doctor early, since antivirals work best in the first two days.
Are prenatal vitamins actually necessary or just marketing?

They're genuinely worth it, mainly for the folic acid, which significantly lowers the risk of neural tube defects. Ideally you start at least a month before conception and keep going throughout pregnancy. Look for one with 400 to 800 mcg of folic acid, plus iron and iodine. Ask your provider about separate DHA, since many prenatals don't include it.
My 6 year old has had a stomach bug for 2 days. How do I know if she's dehydrated?

The main signs to watch for are peeing less than every 8 hours, a dry mouth, no tears when crying, sunken eyes, and being unusually tired or cranky. Give her small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte instead of plain water or juice. Call her doctor if she can't keep fluids down, has blood in her vomit or stool, or if the vomiting continues past day two. Take her in urgently if she becomes very drowsy or hard to wake.
I have IBS and a flare is wrecking me. Anything that actually works fast?

For a flare, a heating pad on your belly and peppermint oil capsules (enteric-coated) are two of the quicker, better-supported options for cramping. If diarrhea is the main problem, loperamide can help, and for constipation, polyethylene glycol is gentle. Stick to simple, low-FODMAP foods for a day or two. If your flares are frequent, ask your doctor about prescription options, and get checked if you have new symptoms like bleeding, weight loss or fever, since those aren't typical of IBS.
My apple watch says AFib. I feel totally fine. Ignore it?

Don't ignore it, even though it isn't an emergency if you feel well. Atrial fibrillation often causes no symptoms but raises stroke risk, and watch alerts are accurate enough to deserve a proper ECG. Book an appointment with your doctor soon and bring the watch readings. Seek urgent care if you develop chest pain, fainting, a very fast heart rate or stroke signs like facial droop or weakness on one side.
My friend said I could take one of her Ambien, just this once. Thoughts?

I'd skip it. Zolpidem is a prescription drug for a reason: it can cause sleepwalking, sleep-driving and memory gaps, it interacts badly with alcohol and other sedatives, and the right dose depends on things like your sex and body size. It's also illegal to share. If you're struggling enough to consider it, that's a good reason to see your own doctor, who can sort out what's driving the insomnia.
My mom is 74, diabetic, and has a small sore on her foot that's been there 2 weeks. She says it's nothing.

A foot sore that hasn't healed in two weeks in someone with diabetes needs a doctor this week, not eventually. Diabetes can blunt pain and slow healing, so small wounds can quietly turn into serious infections that lead to amputation. Get her seen by her doctor or a podiatrist soon. Make it same-day or urgent care if you see spreading redness, warmth, swelling, drainage, a bad smell, or fever. Until then, keep it clean and covered, and keep her weight off it as much as possible.
I'm 67 and keep forgetting my diabetes pills. Does missing one matter much?

An occasional missed dose of something like metformin isn't dangerous. Just take the next one at the usual time and don't double up. Regular misses do add up, though, so a weekly pill organizer or a phone alarm can help a lot. Your pharmacist can also check whether a once-daily version would be simpler for you.
Elderly mom (84) isn't running much of a fever, just 99.8, but she's way more confused than usual and peeing a lot.

Get her seen today, and go to the ER if the confusion is significant or getting worse. Older adults often don't mount a high fever even with serious infections, and new confusion plus urinary changes strongly suggests a urinary tract infection that may be spreading. This kind of infection is very treatable, but it shouldn't wait.
How long should a nap be

Either keep it to about 20 minutes or go for a full 90-minute cycle. A 20-minute nap refreshes you without dropping into deep sleep, so you wake up alert. Thirty to 60 minutes often leaves you groggy. Try to nap before mid-afternoon so it doesn't wreck your nighttime sleep.
Someone's dog bit me on a hike and they took off before I could get info. Small bite on my ankle but broke the skin.

Wash it thoroughly with soap and water, then contact your doctor or local health department today. With an unknown dog whose vaccination status can't be confirmed, they'll assess whether you need rabies shots based on local rabies risk and the circumstances. Report the bite to animal control with any description of the dog and owner, since finding them could spare you the shots. Get your tetanus status checked as well.
I'm diabetic and burned my foot on a hot water bottle. It's just a blister. Ok to treat at home?

With diabetes, a foot burn deserves a doctor's look even if it seems minor, because reduced feeling and slower healing make infections and ulcers much more likely. Cool it, cover the blister with a clean non-stick dressing, and avoid walking on it more than necessary. Try to see your GP or a foot clinic in the next day or so, and sooner if it gets red, swollen or starts draining.
my mom is 80 and gets dizzy whenever she stands up. thoughts?

That sounds like orthostatic hypotension, where blood pressure drops on standing. It's common in older adults and often caused by blood pressure medications, dehydration or diabetes. Have her sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before standing, rise slowly, and drink enough fluids. Tell her doctor, since a medication adjustment often fixes it, and the fall risk is real. If she faints or has chest pain or palpitations, get her checked urgently.
Glucose test is gross, can I skip it? I feel fine.

Feeling fine doesn't rule out gestational diabetes, because it usually has no symptoms, and untreated it can lead to a very large baby and complications at delivery. The test is worth doing, typically between 24 and 28 weeks. If the drink is the problem, ask your provider whether an alternative is available; some offices offer different options.
can collagen powder fix my knee arthritis?

Don't expect it to fix it. A few small studies suggest collagen might ease joint pain modestly, but it doesn't rebuild worn cartilage. It's generally safe to try for a couple of months if you're curious. The things with strong evidence are strengthening the muscles around the knee, staying at a healthy weight and physical therapy, so ask your doctor about a PT referral.
Ankle twisted badly playing football, swollen and I can't put weight on it at all. Wait and see?

If you can't take four steps on it, get an X-ray, because that's one of the standard signs a fracture needs ruling out. Urgent care or a minor injuries unit is the right place today. Until then, keep it raised, ice it in 15 to 20 minute bursts, and use crutches or have someone help you rather than forcing weight onto it.
I'm 7 weeks pregnant and I've had cramping and some spotting since this morning. Should I just wait it out?

Light spotting and mild cramping are common in early pregnancy and often turn out fine, but it's worth calling your midwife or doctor today rather than waiting so they can decide whether you need a scan or blood test. If the bleeding becomes heavy like a period, you pass clots, or you get severe one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain or feel faint, go to the emergency department straight away because that can signal a miscarriage or an ectopic pregnancy.
I'm on chemo, my oncologist hasn't mentioned vaccines but flu season is coming. Should I just go get one at CVS?

Check with your oncology team before going, because timing around chemo cycles matters, and some vaccines like the nasal flu spray are live and off-limits for you. The regular flu shot is usually recommended for people on chemo, and they'll tell you the best day in your cycle to get it. It's also worth asking whether the people you live with should get vaccinated too, since that helps shield you.
My mom is 76 and says her chest feels tight but she insists it's just indigestion and refuses to go anywhere. What do I do??

Call 911. Chest tightness in a 76-year-old needs emergency evaluation, and women often have heart attacks that feel like indigestion. Paramedics can assess her at home, which may be easier than arguing her into a car. If she isn't allergic and no doctor has told her to avoid it, they may have her chew an aspirin, but don't let that delay the call.
I get palpitations after coffee — like skipped beats. 25M. Anything to worry about?

Occasional skipped or extra-feeling beats after caffeine are very common in healthy young people and are usually harmless premature beats. Try cutting back on coffee and energy drinks, and watch sleep, alcohol and stress, since those are frequent triggers. See a doctor if they become frequent or sustained, come with dizziness, fainting, chest pain or shortness of breath, happen during exercise, or if anyone in your family died suddenly young. A basic ECG is a cheap, easy way to put your mind at rest if they keep bothering you.
Wrist cuff or arm cuff, which is better?

An upper-arm cuff is generally more accurate and is what most doctors recommend. Wrist cuffs are very sensitive to position, so your wrist has to be exactly at heart level. Make sure the cuff is the right size for your arm, and bring it to your next appointment to check it against the office reading.
quick q - bee sting on my arm, swelling is like the size of my hand now, 1 day later. ER?

A large swelling that spreads around the sting site over a day or two is a large local reaction, and it usually doesn't need the ER. Ice it, keep the arm raised, and take an oral antihistamine plus ibuprofen for the swelling and itch. Go in right away if you get hives elsewhere, throat or tongue swelling, trouble breathing, or dizziness. See a doctor soon if it turns hot, streaky red, or keeps growing after day three, since that can mean infection.
got leftover amoxicillin from last year, think i've got a sinus infection again. just take those?

I wouldn't. Most sinus infections are viral and clear up without antibiotics. A partial leftover course also isn't enough to treat a real bacterial infection properly, and taking it can breed resistance. Saline rinses, fluids and pain relievers usually get people through. If you've had symptoms for more than 10 days, they worsen after improving, or you have a high fever or facial swelling, see a doctor.
Mom is 74 and has been really thirsty and peeing constantly. She's lost some weight without trying.

That combination of thirst, frequent urination and unexplained weight loss strongly suggests high blood sugar, and she should see her doctor in the next day or two for a blood test. If she becomes confused, very drowsy, starts vomiting or seems dehydrated, take her to the ER, because very high sugar can become dangerous in older adults. Until she's checked, steer her toward water instead of juice or soda. Diabetes is very treatable once it's diagnosed.
My stepdad, 78, keeps stopping breathing for a few seconds when he sleeps and snores like crazy. Mom just jokes about it.

That pattern sounds a lot like sleep apnea, and it's not just a snoring nuisance. Untreated, it raises the risk of high blood pressure, heart rhythm problems, stroke and daytime drowsiness that can make driving dangerous. Ask his doctor about a sleep study, many of which can now be done at home. Treatment like a CPAP machine often makes people feel noticeably sharper and more energetic.
cut my finger slicing an onion, bleeding a lot but not huge. how long do i press before i worry

Press firmly with a clean cloth for a full 10 minutes without peeking, and raise your hand above your heart. Most kitchen finger cuts stop in that time. If it's still bleeding steadily after 10 to 15 minutes of real pressure, or the cut gapes open, it probably needs stitches or glue, so head to urgent care.
is it okay to use my wife's leftover cipro for my traveler's diarrhea

Better not. Cipro carries real risks, including tendon rupture, and many traveler's diarrhea bacteria are now resistant to it, especially in South and Southeast Asia. Most cases clear in 3 to 5 days with fluids and oral rehydration salts, and loperamide can help if you have no fever or blood. See a local doctor if you have a high fever, bloody stool or signs of dehydration, or you're not improving after a few days.
is allergy season making me tired or am i just lazy lol

Probably not laziness. Allergies really do drain you, because the inflammation itself causes fatigue, and congestion wrecks your sleep quality even if you don't notice waking up. Older antihistamines like Benadryl make it worse, so switch to non-drowsy options like loratadine or fexofenadine. A daily steroid nasal spray helps with the stuffiness that ruins sleep. If you're exhausted even with your allergies controlled, get a checkup to rule out things like anemia or thyroid issues.
can i drink a glass of wine to help me sleep

Alcohol helps you fall asleep faster but makes the second half of the night worse. It suppresses REM sleep and tends to cause wake-ups, sweating and bathroom trips. A single glass with dinner is unlikely to do much harm, but using it as a nightly sleep aid backfires and can build into a dependence. Try herbal tea, a warm shower or reading instead, and finish any alcohol at least three hours before bed.
is it safe to do the oral immunotherapy thing at home with tiny bits of peanut? saw it on tiktok

No, don't try this at home. Real oral immunotherapy uses carefully measured doses that increase under an allergist's supervision, with emergency treatment ready, because reactions, including anaphylaxis, are common during the process. Doing it yourself with eyeballed amounts of peanut is genuinely dangerous. If you're interested, ask an allergist about supervised OIT or the FDA-approved peanut powder programs.
Is it safe to eat sushi when pregnant?

Cooked sushi, like eel, shrimp tempura and California rolls made with cooked crab, plus veggie rolls, are fine. Raw fish carries a small risk of parasites and listeria, so most doctors recommend skipping it until after delivery. Also steer clear of high-mercury fish like king mackerel, swordfish and bigeye tuna, raw or cooked.
my friend says i can take my leftover accutane once i stop breastfeeding but what about now, im 3 months pregnant and my acne is horrible

Please don't take isotretinoin (Accutane) while you're pregnant. It causes severe birth defects even in small amounts, which is why it's so tightly controlled. Stop it right away if you've taken any, and tell your OB. For pregnancy acne, ask your doctor or a dermatologist about safer options like azelaic acid or certain topical antibiotics. Also don't take leftover prescription meds without a fresh check, even after breastfeeding.
how long after mono can I play football? I feel fine and it's been 2 weeks

Not yet, unfortunately. Mono often swells the spleen, and a hit to the abdomen can rupture it even when you feel completely fine. The standard advice is no contact sports for at least three to four weeks from when symptoms started, and longer if your spleen is still enlarged, so you need a doctor to clear you before you play football. Light non-contact activity like walking is usually fine sooner.
Quick q - is it ok to give my 6 year old half an adult ibuprofen tablet since we ran out of the kids one?

It's safer to dose by weight with a children's product, because cutting adult tablets makes it easy to get the amount wrong. Ibuprofen for kids is usually 5 to 10 mg per kg every 6 to 8 hours. Half of a 200 mg tablet is 100 mg, which is roughly right for a child of about 10 to 20 kg. Check her weight, and if you're unsure, a pharmacist can confirm the dose in a minute over the phone. Only use plain ibuprofen, not a combination cold product.
What's a good bedtime routine? I'm 34 and my sleep is just meh.

The most powerful change is a consistent wake time every day, including weekends, followed by bright light soon after you get up. In the last hour before bed, dim the lights, put screens away, and do something calming like reading, stretching or a warm shower. Keep your bedroom cool, dark and quiet, cut caffeine after early afternoon, and keep alcohol light and early. Give it two to three weeks, and see a doctor if your sleep is still poor or you're very tired during the day.
Eyes swollen, itchy and red every spring. Can I just use redness drops like Visine every day?

Daily redness-relief drops aren't a good fit. They shrink blood vessels temporarily, but with regular use they can cause rebound redness that leaves your eyes worse. For seasonal eye allergies, antihistamine drops like ketotifen or olopatadine work much better and are safe for daily use through the season. Cool compresses and not rubbing your eyes help too. See an eye doctor if you notice pain, discharge, light sensitivity, or vision changes, since those aren't typical of allergies.
Been having nightmares since a car accident 2 months ago. Will it just pass?

Nightmares right after a frightening event are common and often fade within a few weeks. But two months of ongoing nightmares is worth getting help for, especially if you also have flashbacks, feel on edge, or avoid driving. These can be signs of post-traumatic stress, which responds well to treatment like trauma-focused therapy. Talk to your doctor or a therapist, and if you ever have thoughts of harming yourself, reach out to a crisis line or emergency services right away.
my 2 year old touched the oven door and has a red mark on her hand, she's crying but seems ok now. do i need to take her in?

Cool it under lukewarm-to-cool running water for 20 minutes if you haven't already, keeping the rest of her warm so she doesn't get chilled. Burns on young children's hands are worth having checked by a doctor or urgent care even when they look minor, because their skin is thinner and hands are a sensitive area for healing. Definitely go in if any blistering appears, the mark is larger than her palm, or she seems unusually unwell.
Can I give my 18 month old Claritin for allergies?

Loratadine is generally only labeled for kids two and older. For an 18-month-old, check with the pediatrician before giving it, both to confirm the dose and to make sure it's really allergies rather than a cold, which is much more common at that age. Saline drops and gentle suctioning are safe ways to ease a stuffy nose in the meantime. Never give adult tablets or combination cold medicines to a toddler.
My 10 year old wants to try his older brother's melatonin gummies to sleep, they're just vitamins right?

Melatonin is a hormone, not a vitamin. Gummies are poorly regulated, and their actual dose can be far higher than the label says. Short-term, low-dose use can be okay for some kids, but it's worth checking with his pediatrician before starting, especially to figure out why he's struggling to sleep. Often, a consistent bedtime, no screens in the hour before bed and a dark room work better.
My home cuff just said 182/121 and I have a pounding headache and blurry vision. Should I just lie down and recheck in an hour?

Don't wait an hour; call emergency services now. A reading that high together with a severe headache and vision changes can mean a hypertensive emergency, which can damage the brain, heart or kidneys quickly. Sit down, stay calm, and don't drive yourself or take extra blood pressure pills to bring it down fast while you wait for help.
Elderly father (82, diabetic) has a small cut on his shin that isn't healing after 2 weeks. Should I keep using antibiotic ointment?

Two weeks without healing in an 82-year-old with diabetes is worth a doctor's visit now rather than more ointment. Diabetes and age both slow healing and raise the risk of serious infection or ulcers, especially on the lower legs. Keep it clean and covered until then, and go sooner if you see spreading redness, swelling, pus, or he develops a fever.
My father (81) has diabetes and refuses to check his feet. Is it really a big deal?

It really is, because diabetes can dull feeling in the feet, so a small blister or cut can turn into a serious infection before he notices it. A quick daily look, which you or a caregiver can do, for redness, sores, swelling or color changes catches problems early. He should also have his feet examined by his doctor or a podiatrist at least once a year. Any wound that isn't healing within a few days needs prompt medical attention.
got a rash all over after my shot 20 min ago and my lips feel kinda tingly

Tingling lips plus a widespread rash right after a vaccine can be the start of an allergic reaction, so treat this as urgent. If you're still at the clinic, tell staff immediately; if you've left, call 911 now, especially if you notice any throat tightness, trouble breathing, or dizziness. Don't wait to see whether it passes, because these reactions can escalate quickly and are very treatable when caught early.
My 6 year old has a croupy barking cough at night, sounds scary. What do I do right now?

Take her into the bathroom with a hot shower running so she breathes the steam, or bundle her up and step outside into cool night air, since both often calm croup quickly. Keep her as calm as you can, because crying makes it worse. Call 911 or go to the ER if she has a high-pitched noise when breathing in while resting, struggles to breathe, drools, or looks pale or blue. Otherwise, call her doctor in the morning, since a steroid dose often helps.
I want to stop my sertraline. I feel fine now. Can I just stop tomorrow?

Don't stop it cold, because quitting sertraline abruptly can cause discontinuation symptoms like dizziness, irritability, flu-like feelings, and 'brain zaps,' and it also raises the risk of relapse. Feeling fine is great news, but it's often the medication doing its job. Talk to your prescriber about a gradual taper, which usually takes a few weeks or longer, and about whether now is a good time to come off it.
hamster bit my finger lol. bled a little. is that a big deal

Not a big deal in most cases, since pet hamsters don't carry rabies and their bites are usually small. Wash it well with soap and water, apply a bit of antibiotic ointment and cover it. Watch for redness, swelling or pus over the next few days, and check your tetanus is up to date.
Does garlic supplement work like a BP pill? Thinking of skipping my doctor visit and just doing that.

Garlic supplements may lower blood pressure by a few points, but the evidence is modest and they're no substitute for proper diagnosis and treatment. They can also raise bleeding risk if you're on blood thinners. Keep the doctor visit, and you can ask about adding garlic if you'd like to try it.
Found a bat in my bedroom this morning. No bite marks that I can see. Probably fine?

Unfortunately this is one situation where you can't assume you're fine, because bat bites can be so tiny they leave no visible mark, and bats are a leading source of human rabies. Waking up with a bat in the room counts as a possible exposure, so call your doctor or local health department today about post-exposure shots. If you can safely trap the bat without touching it, do so, since testing it might rule out rabies.
Stepped on a rusty nail at work, last tetanus shot was maybe 12 years ago. Do I really need to go in?

Yes, go in today. A puncture wound is exactly the kind of injury where tetanus is a risk, and after 12 years you're overdue for a booster. For dirty or deep wounds, the booster should be given if it's been more than five years. A clinic can also clean the wound properly and check for infection. Ideally get it done within 48 hours, but a late booster is still better than none.
I'm 28 weeks pregnant and getting short of breath and my heart feels like it's pounding. Normal?

Some breathlessness and a faster heart rate are normal in pregnancy because your blood volume rises and the baby crowds your lungs, but you should still mention it to your midwife or OB soon. Get same-day care if it's new or worsening, comes on at rest, wakes you up at night, or comes with chest pain, fainting, a cough with blood, swelling in one leg, or bad headaches and vision changes. Pregnancy raises the risk of blood clots and certain heart problems, so these symptoms are worth having checked rather than brushed off.
is it ok to drink a couple beers on amoxicillin

A couple of beers won't stop amoxicillin from working, and it doesn't cause the severe reaction some antibiotics like metronidazole do. Alcohol can still make an upset stomach worse and slow your recovery, so going light is sensible while you're sick. Just make sure you finish the whole course even once you feel better.
My 3yo fell off the couch and bumped his head, has a goose egg. He cried right away and now he's playing. Okay?

Crying right away and going back to playing are reassuring signs, and a goose egg on the forehead is common. Hold a cold pack wrapped in cloth on it for a few minutes if he'll tolerate it, and keep an eye on him for the next 24 hours. Go to the ER if he vomits more than once, becomes unusually sleepy or hard to wake, acts confused, walks unsteadily, has a seizure, or has fluid coming from his nose or ears.
My 2 year old has a barking cough like a seal and it's worse at night. She's breathing ok right now.

That sounds like croup, which is usually viral and often manageable at home. Breathing cool night air or sitting in a steamy bathroom can ease it, and keeping her calm helps a lot since crying makes it worse. Call her doctor tomorrow, because a single dose of steroid often makes a big difference. If you hear a high-pitched noise when she breathes in while she's resting, see her skin sucking in around her ribs, or she's drooling or can't swallow, go to the ER.
I've been sick with long covid for 3 months. Everyone says exercise helps but every time I try I crash for days.

That crash pattern is called post-exertional malaise, and pushing through it can make long covid worse. Talk to your doctor, and ask about a long covid clinic or a physio familiar with pacing. The usual approach is to stay well below your symptom threshold and only build very slowly, rather than following standard exercise advice.
can i lift weights after my flu shot or will it mess something up

You can work out after a flu shot without any problems, and moving your arm can actually help ease soreness. If you feel achy or run down that day, take it easy or train a bit lighter, but there's no medical reason to skip the gym.
traveling to Kenya in 10 days, totally forgot about vaccines, is it too late

It's not too late, but book a travel clinic appointment in the next day or two. Some vaccines, like hepatitis A and typhoid, still give useful protection on a short timeline. The clinic will also check whether you need yellow fever vaccination for entry and prescribe malaria pills, which matter just as much for Kenya. Bring your vaccination record if you have it.
I'm 45 and had a bad flu with chest tightness. It's cleared up mostly. Can I train for a half marathon now?

Since you had chest tightness, see a doctor before you start a training plan, to make sure your heart and lungs are fully clear. Flu occasionally causes heart inflammation, and endurance training on top of that can be dangerous. Once you're cleared, rebuild your base with easy runs for a couple of weeks before following a half marathon schedule.
threw up blood this morning, not a lot, kinda looks like coffee grounds. feel ok otherwise

Please get to an ER now, even though you feel okay. Vomit that looks like coffee grounds usually means blood that has been sitting in the stomach, which points to bleeding somewhere like an ulcer. Bleeding can pick up quickly, so don't drive yourself if you feel dizzy or faint, and call emergency services if you vomit again or get lightheaded.
can allergies cause a fever?

No, allergies don't cause a true fever, even though people call it hay fever. If you have a temperature over about 100.4°F, it's more likely a cold, flu, sinus infection or another illness. If the fever is high, lasts more than a few days or comes with facial pain and thick discolored mucus, see a doctor.
What's a normal blood pressure for a 70 year old? My dad's is 138/82.

Many guidelines call under 120/80 normal and treat 130 or above on top as stage 1 high blood pressure at any age, so your dad's reading is mildly elevated. For older adults, doctors usually aim for under 130 on top if it can be done safely, but they adjust the target based on dizziness, fall risk and other conditions. One reading doesn't diagnose anything, so a few days of home readings to bring to his doctor would show the real pattern.
I'm pregnant (9 weeks) and terrified I'm not getting enough folate because I've been too nauseous to eat properly. What do I do

If you're taking a prenatal vitamin with at least 400 micrograms of folic acid, you're covered even on days you can barely eat. The supplement is the main reason it's recommended in the first place. If you can't keep the vitamin down, try taking it at night or with a small snack, or ask your midwife or doctor about a gentler version. If you can't keep fluids down or you're losing weight, call them soon, because severe pregnancy sickness is very treatable and you shouldn't just push through it.
I got the first Shingrix shot 9 months ago and forgot the second. Do I have to restart??

No restart needed. If the gap runs longer than the recommended two to six months, you just get the second dose as soon as you can, and the series still counts. Book it this week so you get full protection.
I'm allergic to penicillin. Does that mean I can't take amoxicillin?

Yes, avoid amoxicillin, because it's in the penicillin family and can trigger the same reaction. Make sure every doctor and pharmacist knows about your allergy so they choose something else. It's also worth asking about allergy testing, because most people who were labeled penicillin-allergic as kids turn out not to be, and confirming that opens up more treatment options. Just don't test it yourself by taking a dose.
my husband suddenly has a headache, his face is drooping on one side and he's slurring. what do I do

Call 911 right now. Those are signs of a stroke, and every minute counts for treatment. Note the time the symptoms started, keep him sitting or lying down, and don't give him anything to eat, drink or take, including aspirin, until paramedics assess him.
What's the fastest way to bring down my kid's fever before school photos tomorrow lol

Ha, I get it, but if he has a fever tomorrow he really should skip school, since most schools want kids fever-free for 24 hours without medicine before they come back. Ibuprofen or acetaminophen at the right dose for his weight will make him feel better tonight, but it masks the fever without making him less contagious. Most schools offer retake days, so let him rest and catch the next round.
anyone know if its ok to sleep on my back? 27 weeks

After about 28 weeks, it's best to fall asleep on your side, because lying flat on your back can press on major blood vessels and has been linked to a higher risk of stillbirth in late pregnancy. Either side is fine, though left is often recommended. If you wake up on your back, don't panic, just roll over, and a pillow behind you can help you stay put.
My 84 yo dad is still driving and I'm honestly scared. He's had two fender benders this year.

Two crashes in a year is a real warning sign. Many families find it easier to bring in an outside expert than to confront the issue head-on. His doctor can assess his vision, reaction time and cognition, and many hospitals offer formal driving evaluations by occupational therapists. If the evaluation says he can't drive safely, a clear plan for how he'll get to groceries, appointments and friends will make the change far easier for him to accept.
how long is a cold supposed to last

Most colds peak around days two to three and are mostly gone within 7 to 10 days, though a lingering cough can hang on for two or three weeks. If you're getting worse after the first week, running a fever past day three or four, or feeling better and then suddenly worse again, that can mean a secondary infection like sinusitis or an ear infection, and it's worth seeing a doctor.
can I use superglue to fix the hinge on my glasses lol

Sure, on the frame itself that's fine. Keep it well away from the lenses and let it fully cure before the glasses go near your face, since glue fumes and drips near the eye are a real hazard. Opticians will often tighten or replace hinge screws for free, so that's worth a quick stop if the glue doesn't hold.
hypo, 2.9, shaky. what do i do quick

Take 15 to 20 grams of fast sugar right now: about 150 to 200 ml of regular soda or juice, or 4 to 5 glucose tablets. Recheck in 15 minutes and repeat if you're still below 4. Once you're back up, eat a snack with some carbs if your next meal isn't soon. If you're getting confused or can't swallow safely, someone needs to call emergency services.
steroid inhaler makes my voice hoarse, thinking of just quitting it

Before you quit, try rinsing your mouth and gargling with water after every dose, then spitting it out, and ask about using a spacer, which keeps more of the medicine in your lungs and less in your throat. Those two changes fix hoarseness for most people. If it continues, your doctor can switch you to a different inhaler or dose. Stopping your controller entirely tends to lead to flares, so adjust it rather than ditching it.
Can I take melatonin every night long term for stress insomnia?

Melatonin is fairly low-risk, but it's best for shifting your sleep timing rather than treating stress-driven insomnia, and its effect on that is usually small. Lower doses of around 0.5 to 3 mg often work as well as bigger ones. If you've needed it nightly for more than a few weeks, ask your doctor about CBT for insomnia, which is the first-line treatment and has lasting results.
ugh. sore throat, fever, no cough at all. just a cold right?

Maybe, but a sore throat with fever and no cough fits strep throat, especially if your tonsils are swollen or have white patches, or your neck glands are tender. Strep needs antibiotics to prevent complications, and a quick throat swab at a clinic or pharmacy can confirm it. It's worth getting tested rather than waiting it out.
slept in my contacts again and now my eye is red and really sore and light hurts. eh i'll just wear glasses for a day

Glasses are a good start, but redness plus real pain and light sensitivity after sleeping in contacts can be a corneal ulcer. Those can scar the cornea and threaten your sight within a day or two. Keep the lenses out and see an eye doctor today. Bring the contacts and their case with you, since they may want to culture them.
Metal shaving flew into my eye at work, I can feel it. Gonna try to get it out with a magnet

Please don't, because a magnet or fingertip can scratch the cornea or drag the fragment deeper. Metal can also leave a rust ring if it stays in for long. Gently cover the eye without pressing, avoid rubbing, and get to an eye doctor or urgent care today so they can remove it properly and check for penetration.
Anxiety attack or heart attack how do i tell the difference I have panic disorder

There's real overlap, so the honest answer is that you can't always tell from home, but there are useful clues. Panic usually peaks within about 10 minutes, often comes with tingling in the hands or face and a sense of dread, and eases as you calm down, while heart pain tends to be pressure or heaviness that persists or worsens, may spread to the arm, jaw or back, and is more likely with exertion or risk factors like age, smoking, diabetes or high blood pressure. If it feels different from your usual attacks, lasts longer, or doesn't settle with your normal coping strategies, get checked rather than assuming. It's also worth asking your doctor for a baseline cardiac workup so you can feel more confident about your typical panic symptoms.
Can I use my sister's leftover steroid cream on my rash? Same thing probably.

It's better not to. Steroid creams vary a lot in strength, and using one on the wrong rash can make some conditions much worse, such as fungal infections, scabies or rosacea. A strong one used on the face or skin folds can also thin the skin. If the rash is mild, try a fragrance-free moisturiser and over-the-counter 1% hydrocortisone for a few days. If it's spreading, not improving or you're not sure what it is, get it looked at so you're treating the right thing.
Why does my blood sugar go up in the morning even though I didn't eat anything overnight??

That's usually the dawn phenomenon. In the early morning your body releases hormones like cortisol and growth hormone that push your liver to put out glucose and make you a bit more insulin resistant. Less often, a high morning number comes from a rebound after an overnight low. Checking around 3 a.m. a few nights, or looking at CGM data, can tell the two apart. Bring the pattern to your doctor, because the fix differs, such as changing medication timing or dose, and you don't want to guess.
water broke?? maybe? some leaking at 35 weeks, no contractions. can I just sleep and see in the morning

Call labor and delivery now rather than waiting until morning. If your water has broken at 35 weeks, they'll want to assess you because of the infection risk and to check on the baby, and a quick test can confirm whether it's amniotic fluid. Note the time, the color of the fluid and the amount; green or brown fluid, or any bleeding, means go in right away.
Pulled something in my back deadlifting. How soon can I lift again? I hate losing gains.

You won't lose much in a week or two, and coming back too early is how a minor strain becomes a recurring problem. Keep walking and moving gently. Once everyday movements are pain-free, return with light weights and perfect form, then build back up over a couple of weeks. In the meantime, you can still train upper body moves that don't load your back. If pain runs down your leg or you have numbness, have it assessed before you deadlift again.
Left arm 150/90, right arm 132/84. Which one is real??

Both readings are real, and doctors generally go by the higher arm. A consistent difference of more than about 10–15 points between arms is worth mentioning to your doctor, because it can sometimes point to a narrowed artery. Recheck both arms a few times on different days with a properly sized cuff. If the gap persists, bring those numbers to your appointment.
Can I just use hydrogen peroxide on my dog bite and skip the doctor? I hate going in.

Skip the peroxide and use plenty of soap and running water instead, since peroxide can damage tissue and slow healing. Whether you can skip the doctor depends on the bite. A shallow scrape on the arm or leg from a known, vaccinated dog is usually fine at home. Get seen if it's a puncture, a gaping wound, or on the hand, face, or a joint, or if you have diabetes or a weakened immune system, because those bites get infected much more often.
is walking ok while I have covid, or should I fully rest?

Gentle walking is usually fine if your symptoms are mild and you feel up to it, and it can help with stiffness and mood. Keep it short and easy, avoid anything strenuous until you're recovered, and rest on days you feel worse. Stop and seek care if you get chest pain, struggle to breathe, or feel faint.
rabbit scratched my face pretty good. three long scratches near my eye

Wash them gently with soap and clean water, avoiding getting soap in your eye, and pat dry. Shallow scratches usually heal well with a thin layer of petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment. See a doctor today if any scratch touched your eyelid or eye, if your vision is affected, or if your eye is painful, red or watery. Watch for infection over the next few days.
Sharp pain in lower right side of belly since last night, now worse when I walk. Fever 38.2. Can I just take ibuprofen and sleep it off?

Please don't sleep this one off. Pain that settles in the lower right, gets worse with movement and comes with a fever is a classic pattern for appendicitis. Painkillers can hide how serious it is. Go to urgent care or the emergency department now, and skip food and drink until you're seen in case you need surgery.
My 6 month old has red, rough patches on her cheeks and the creases of her elbows. She keeps rubbing her face on the sheets. Is this eczema?

That pattern, dry rough patches on the cheeks and in the elbow creases plus itching, is very typical of infant eczema. The core treatment is lots of thick, fragrance-free moisturizer like plain petroleum jelly or a cream from a tub, applied at least twice a day and right after short lukewarm baths, plus soft cotton clothing and short nails. Have her pediatrician take a look to confirm it and decide whether she needs a mild prescription steroid for flares. Go sooner if the patches ooze, crust over in yellow, or she seems unwell, since eczema can get infected.
My 15 year old says she's been feeling really down for months and sometimes thinks it would be easier not to be here. I don't know what to say.

You've already done something important just by her trusting you with this. Tell her you're glad she told you and that you'll get through it together. Ask her directly whether she's thinking about hurting herself or has a plan. Asking won't plant the idea, and it tells you how urgent things are. Book an appointment with her doctor or a mental health professional this week, and lock up medications and any firearms in the house. If she's in immediate danger, call or text 988 in the US, or go to the ER.
can i mix my xanax and a glass of wine to sleep tonight, rough day

Please don't combine them. Benzodiazepines and alcohol together can dangerously slow your breathing, and that risk is highest when you're asleep and no one is watching. Pick one or neither, and if you take your Xanax as prescribed, skip the wine tonight. If rough days often mean you need help winding down, tell your prescriber so they know how you're actually using it.
tetanus shot. stepped on a rusty nail. last one was... honestly no idea, maybe high school? im 41

Get a tetanus booster today or tomorrow. For a puncture wound like this, a booster is recommended if your last one was more than five years ago, and yours almost certainly was. Clean the wound well, and urgent care or a pharmacy can give you the Tdap shot. Watch for spreading redness, pus or increasing pain, and get the wound checked if any of those show up.
My friend says I can use a nebulizer with saline only instead of my meds when I have an attack. Smart?

No. Plain saline doesn't open your airways, so during an attack you need your actual bronchodilator, like albuterol, in the nebulizer or your inhaler. Saline can loosen mucus a bit in some situations, but relying on it during an attack could let a serious episode get worse. Stick to the action plan your doctor gave you. If you don't have one, ask for one.

It's not dangerous, but it's above the ideal range. Under current US guidelines, 120–129 systolic counts as elevated, and a bottom number of 80–89 is stage 1 hypertension. At 34 this is the perfect time to act with lifestyle changes like less salt, more activity, limiting alcohol and keeping a healthy weight. Recheck it a few times at home and mention it at your next checkup.
My friend twisted her knee skiing, heard a pop, and now it's swelling up fast. She wants to ski down on it.

A pop followed by rapid swelling is a classic sign of a significant ligament tear such as an ACL, and skiing down on an unstable knee risks further damage to the cartilage and meniscus. Have her flag ski patrol to get her down on a sled. She should ice it, keep weight off it, and get evaluated at a clinic or by a sports medicine doctor within a few days, sooner if the knee buckles, locks, or the pain is severe.
I'm 36 weeks and my feet and hands suddenly got really puffy over the last day, plus I've got a headache that won't quit.

Sudden swelling of the hands and face, together with a persistent headache, can be a sign of preeclampsia, so call your maternity unit or labor and delivery triage now rather than waiting for your next appointment. They will want to check your blood pressure and urine today. Go in immediately if you also notice blurred vision, flashing lights, pain under your ribs or vomiting.
Kitten scratched my arm while playing, just a surface scratch. Anything I need to do?

For a shallow scratch, wash it with soap and water, pat it dry, and keep it clean. It's worth keeping an eye on it for a few days. If you get a swollen, tender bump near the scratch or swollen lymph nodes in your armpit, especially with a fever, see a doctor, because kittens can carry the bacteria that cause cat scratch disease.
Got over a UTI, finished antibiotics. Gym fine?

Yes, once you've finished your antibiotics and your symptoms are gone, the gym is fine. Drink plenty of water, and change out of sweaty clothes soon after your workout. If you notice burning or urgency coming back, get rechecked rather than waiting it out.
How do I know if it's covid, flu or a cold? They all feel the same

They overlap a lot, so testing is the only reliable way to tell. Generally, colds come on gradually with a stuffy nose and sore throat, while flu hits suddenly with high fever, body aches and exhaustion. COVID can look like either. Home COVID tests are easy, and combo COVID-flu tests are available too. Knowing matters most if you're at high risk, since both flu and COVID have antivirals that work best when started early.
Can a sinus infection make my upper teeth hurt? All of them on one side ache.

Yes, the roots of the upper back teeth sit right below the maxillary sinus, so sinus pressure often feels like a toothache across several teeth. Clues that it's your sinuses include pain that worsens when you bend over and congestion at the same time. If the ache settles as the sinus clears, you're fine. If it centers on one tooth or lingers afterward, see a dentist to rule out a dental problem.
do gummy vitamins count or are they just candy

They do count, but they often contain less of each nutrient than tablets, they usually skip iron, and they come with added sugar. The nutrients can also degrade over time, so the actual dose may be below what the label says. They're fine if they're the only form you'll actually take. Keep them out of reach of children, though, because kids treat them like candy.
Teen son has fever, bad headache, stiff neck and now a rash that doesn't fade when I press a glass on it. What do I do

Call emergency services or get him to the ER right now. Fever, stiff neck and a non-blanching rash together are warning signs of meningococcal infection, which can become life-threatening within hours but is very treatable with prompt antibiotics. Don't wait to see if it improves.
I'm 68 and on blood thinners (apixaban). Nicked my forearm on a cabinet corner, skin tore like a flap. Bleeding slow but won't quit.

Skin tears are common with age and blood thinners, and they heal best when handled carefully. Rinse it with clean water and gently ease the flap back into place with a damp cotton bud if you can. Then hold firm pressure for 10 to 15 minutes. Cover it with a non-stick dressing rather than an adhesive plaster stuck to the skin, because adhesive can rip it further. Since it won't stop and you're on apixaban, get it seen at urgent care or by a practice nurse today, and go sooner if the bleeding picks up.
teenager gets headaches every day after school. she's 15 and on her phone constantly

Daily after-school headaches in teens are very often down to skipped lunch, too little water, poor sleep, eye strain and hours of screen time with a hunched neck. Try regular meals, a water bottle, screen breaks and a consistent bedtime for a couple of weeks. Book an eye exam too, since uncorrected vision is a common culprit. If they persist, wake her at night, or come with vomiting or vision changes, see her doctor.
My kid (8) had a bad chest cold. School wants to know if she can do PE. She's still coughing a bit.

If she has no fever, is eating and sleeping normally, and the cough is just lingering, PE is usually fine. Let the teacher know she may need to take breaks. A cough can hang around for a couple of weeks after a cold. If she gets very short of breath, wheezes, or the cough gets worse with running, have her doctor check for asthma or another issue.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and think I have a UTI, burning and peeing constantly. Can I just do cranberry juice and water for a few days?

Please don't wait on this. Call your OB or midwife today, because UTIs in pregnancy are more likely to spread to the kidneys and can trigger preterm labor. A urine test and a pregnancy-safe antibiotic are the standard fix and work quickly. Keep drinking water, but cranberry won't treat an active infection. Go in right away if you get a fever, back or side pain, or contractions.
I'm 34 and my right eye's vision got suddenly blurry and it hurts to move it

Sudden blurry vision with pain on eye movement can be optic neuritis, inflammation of the optic nerve, and it should be checked the same day. See an eye doctor urgently or go to the ER, where they can examine the nerve and decide if you need an MRI. Getting a prompt diagnosis matters because optic neuritis can sometimes be linked to conditions like multiple sclerosis that benefit from early care.
is sweating it out in the sauna or a hard workout a good way to get over a cold faster?

No, it's a myth that you can sweat out a cold with a hard workout or sauna session. Hard exercise while you're sick can make you feel worse, and a sauna can dehydrate you, especially if you have a fever. Rest, fluids and sleep do more for recovery, and light activity like a walk is fine if you only have mild cold symptoms.
sunburn so bad i have blisters on my shoulders and feel kinda dizzy and sick

Blistering plus dizziness and nausea suggests a serious burn along with possible heat exhaustion or dehydration, so you should get checked at urgent care today. In the meantime, get out of the sun and drink water or an electrolyte drink. Take cool showers or use damp cloths, and use ibuprofen for pain if it's safe for you. Leave the blisters alone. Go to the ER instead if you get confused, faint, stop sweating or develop a high fever.
hot bath to sweat out a fever, yes or no?

No. A hot bath can push your temperature higher and leave you dehydrated or lightheaded, and "sweating it out" doesn't shorten an illness. A lukewarm shower, light clothing, fluids and a fever reducer if you're uncomfortable work better.
quick: can I put olive oil in my kid's ear for an earache

Skip it until a doctor has looked in the ear. If the eardrum is perforated or there's an ear tube, oil can get into the middle ear and cause problems. Earaches in kids are usually infections, and the immediate relief comes from children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen, dosed by weight. See a doctor if there's a fever, discharge, or pain lasting more than a day or two.
can i use my mate's leftover tramadol for my back

Don't take someone else's tramadol, because it's an opioid with real risks, including dangerous interactions with antidepressants and other drugs, seizures, and dependence, and the dose wasn't chosen for you. It's also not very effective for most back pain compared with staying active and using standard pain relievers. If over-the-counter options aren't enough, see a GP, who can prescribe something safe for your situation.
quick q can i take excedrin and tylenol together

Better not. Excedrin already contains acetaminophen, the active ingredient in Tylenol, so stacking them makes it easy to exceed the safe daily limit and risk liver damage. Pick one and follow the label, and check other cold or flu products you're taking for hidden acetaminophen too.
Is it true turmeric works as well as ibuprofen? I'd rather go natural for my knee

There's some decent evidence that curcumin helps with knee osteoarthritis pain, and a few studies found it roughly comparable to ibuprofen. The effect is modest, though, and it takes a few weeks to kick in. Choose a product formulated for absorption, like one with piperine, at around 500 to 1,000 mg of curcumin a day. Check with your doctor first if you have gallbladder issues or take blood thinners. Strengthening the muscles around your knee and losing a bit of weight, if that applies, will likely help more than either pill.
My dad's 78 and gets dizzy when he stands up. Can I just tell him to stand slower and leave it?

Standing slowly is good advice, but tell his doctor too, because dizziness on standing is a major cause of falls. It's often caused by blood pressure medication, dehydration or other drugs that can be adjusted, and sometimes points to a heart or nerve issue. Have him sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before getting up and keep fluids up. If he faints or has chest pain or palpitations, he needs urgent care.
my son has had diarrhea for 2 days, he's 5. what should he eat?

He can eat his normal food as soon as he wants to, and bland options like rice, toast, bananas, crackers, and yogurt are easy on the stomach. Fluids matter most, so offer small, frequent sips of water or an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte, and avoid juice and soda, which can make diarrhea worse. Call the doctor if he has blood in his stool, a high fever, severe belly pain, or signs of dehydration like peeing very little, a dry mouth, or unusual sleepiness.
Had the flu last week, fever broke two days ago. Can I go back to my usual 10k runs tomorrow?

Give it a bit longer and scale down when you do go back. A good rule is to wait until you've been fever-free for at least a few days without medication, then start with an easy 20 to 30 minute jog at a conversational pace. Running hard too soon after flu can drag out your recovery, and in rare cases the virus can affect the heart. If the easy runs feel fine for several days, build back toward 10k over a week or two.
Is it fine to exercise with asthma or will it make it worse

Exercise is good for people with asthma, and most can be very active once their asthma is well controlled. Warm up gradually, and if exercise tends to trigger symptoms, take your rescue inhaler about 15 minutes beforehand if your doctor agrees. Cold, dry air is a common trigger, so a scarf over your mouth can help in winter. If you're regularly getting wheezy during workouts even with these steps, talk to your doctor about adjusting your treatment.
I'm allergic to eggs. Can I still get the flu shot?

Yes, people with egg allergies can get any age-appropriate flu vaccine, including a severe allergy, and no special precautions beyond the usual are needed anymore. The amount of egg protein is tiny, and there are completely egg-free options like Flublok if you'd feel more comfortable. If you've ever had a severe reaction to a flu shot itself, tell the person giving it before they vaccinate you.
Bee sting on my arm, swelling a little. Not allergic as far as I know.

If the stinger is still in, scrape it out sideways with a fingernail or card, then wash the spot and put a cold pack on it. An oral antihistamine and hydrocortisone cream can help with swelling and itch, and some local swelling over a day or two is normal. Call 911 immediately if you get hives elsewhere, throat or lip swelling, trouble breathing, or feel faint, even with no known allergy.
I'm 45 and had chest pressure walking uphill last week but it went away when I stopped. Probably just out of shape right?

Pressure that comes on with exertion and eases with rest is exactly how angina, reduced blood flow to the heart, tends to show up, so please don't write it off as being out of shape. Book an appointment with your doctor this week and tell them precisely what you told me, because they'll likely want an ECG and possibly a stress test. Hold off on strenuous exercise until then, and call emergency services if the pressure comes on at rest or lasts more than a few minutes.
My friend texted me 'I don't think I can do this anymore, sorry for everything.' She's not answering. What do I do?

Treat this as an emergency. Call emergency services now (911 in the US, 999 in the UK, 112 in much of Europe), give them her address, and say she may be at risk of suicide. If you can safely get to her or reach someone who lives with her, do that too, but don't wait on her reply before calling for help. Afterwards you can call or text 988 in the US, or a local crisis line, for support yourself.
should i get the flu shot if i already had the flu this year

Yes, it's still worth getting. Several flu strains circulate each season, and having one type doesn't protect you from the others the vaccine covers. Just wait until you've recovered from your current illness and any fever has gone. It's safe to get after having had flu.
can i just get a numbing shot at urgent care and skip the dentist

Urgent care can help with pain control and prescribe antibiotics if there's an infection, but they can't fix the tooth itself. Numbing wears off in a few hours and the problem keeps progressing. Use urgent care as a bridge if needed, but book a dentist, since that's the only way to actually stop the pain from coming back.
Does magnesium actually help with sleep or is that TikTok nonsense

It's somewhere in between. The evidence is modest, and the clearest benefit shows up in people who are actually low in magnesium, which is fairly common. Magnesium glycinate at 200 to 400 mg in the evening is a reasonable, low-risk thing to try for a few weeks. Avoid the citrate or oxide forms if you don't want a laxative effect, and skip supplements entirely if you have kidney disease unless your doctor okays it.
Pregnant (22 weeks) and I think I have a UTI. Can I wait it out a few days?

Please don't wait. In pregnancy, UTIs are more likely to travel to the kidneys and can raise the risk of preterm labor, so call your midwife or doctor today. There are antibiotics that are safe in pregnancy, and treating early is the safer option for both of you. Go in urgently if you get fever, back pain, vomiting or contractions.
newborn sleeps better on her tummy, can I just let her?

Please don't. Babies should always be put down to sleep on their backs, on a firm flat surface with no pillows, bumpers or loose blankets, because tummy sleeping significantly raises the risk of SIDS. Many babies do settle more easily on their fronts, which is part of why it's risky. Swaddling for young babies, with arms out once she shows signs of rolling, plus white noise and a darker room can help her settle on her back. Supervised tummy time while she's awake is great.
HURRY my toddler might have eaten like 5 of my iron pills what do I do

Call Poison Control right now at 1-800-222-1222 in the US, or your local emergency number. Iron overdose is genuinely dangerous for small children, even if they seem fine at first. Don't try to make them vomit. Keep the bottle with you so you can tell them the strength and how many might be missing. If your child is vomiting, very sleepy or having trouble breathing, call 911 immediately.
how many excedrin can i take in a day, i have a deadline and my head is killing me

For adults the label limit is 2 caplets per dose and no more than 2 caplets in 24 hours, so going over that isn't worth it. Excedrin contains acetaminophen, aspirin and caffeine, so don't add Tylenol or extra coffee on top of it. Drink water, eat something and step away from the screen for ten minutes, which often helps as much as another pill would.
chest hurts when i press on it. heart attack?

Pain you can reproduce by pressing on one spot usually comes from the chest wall, like a strained muscle or inflamed rib cartilage (costochondritis), not the heart. It often follows heavy lifting, coughing or a new workout and eases with rest and an over-the-counter anti-inflammatory. Pressing on it doesn't rule out a heart problem, though, so get checked urgently if you also have shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, dizziness, pain spreading to your arm or jaw, or pain that comes on with exertion.
quick q - stomach bug yesterday, threw up a bunch. gym today ok?

Skip it today. You're almost certainly still low on fluids and electrolytes, and working out dehydrated can make you lightheaded or set off cramps. Spend today rehydrating and eating bland food, then try something light in a day or two once you're keeping meals down and feel steady.
Do I need to stop my fish oil before my colonoscopy?

Many gastroenterologists ask patients to stop fish oil about 5 to 7 days before a colonoscopy, especially if polyps might be removed, because it can slightly increase bleeding. Instructions vary, so follow your procedure center's prep sheet or call them to confirm. Also mention any blood thinners, aspirin or diabetes meds, since those need specific plans.
I've had a stuffy nose for 3 months straight. Allergies? Just keep using the nasal decongestant spray?

Stop the decongestant spray. Oxymetazoline-type sprays cause rebound congestion after a few days, and months of use can create a cycle that keeps you blocked. A steroid nasal spray is the right long-term option for allergic congestion, though it takes a week or so to fully kick in. Three months of constant stuffiness also deserves a doctor visit to check for allergies, sinus problems or structural issues.
4yo has had diarrhea for 2 days, still peeing but less. what should I watch for

The main concern with diarrhea is dehydration, so keep offering small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte, and let her eat normally if she wants to. Call her doctor if she has no urine for 8 hours or more, no tears when crying, or a dry mouth. Also call if she's unusually sleepy or limp, or if there's blood in her stool. If the diarrhea lasts past 5 to 7 days or she has a high fever, she should be seen too. Skip adult anti-diarrhea medicines like loperamide unless her doctor recommends them.
my friend says you can get the flu from the flu shot. true?

No, the flu shot can't give you the flu, because it contains either inactivated virus or just a single viral protein, and neither can cause infection. What some people get is a day of mild achiness or low fever, which is the immune system ramping up. It also takes about two weeks to build protection, so people who catch something right after the shot usually picked it up before the vaccine had a chance to kick in.
Had a really bad migraine illness/virus combo last week. Can I do HIIT today if I chug energy drinks?

Skip the energy drinks and the HIIT for today. Stacking caffeine on high-intensity exercise while you're still recovering raises your heart rate and blood pressure, and it can bring the headaches back. A moderate workout or a brisk walk is a smarter way to test how you feel. Save HIIT for when you're fully back to normal.
Still coughing two weeks after a cold. Can I run or will it make it worse?

A lingering cough after a cold is common, and easy running usually won't make it worse. Some people find cold air or hard efforts set off coughing fits, so keep the pace comfortable. If the cough lasts beyond three weeks, or you have wheezing, fever, or chest pain, see a doctor to rule out something like post-viral asthma or a chest infection.
fever and burning when i pee and my lower back on one side hurts

Fever, painful urination, and pain on one side of your back together point to a possible kidney infection, which needs antibiotics soon. Get seen today at urgent care or your doctor. Go to the ER if you're vomiting, can't keep fluids down, or feel very sick.
pink eye in my 6 year old, school wants antibiotic drops before she comes back. needed?

Often not medically. Many cases of pink eye are viral or mild bacterial infections that clear on their own in a week or so. A quick visit makes sense anyway, since a doctor can tell what kind it is and help with the school's policy. Bacterial pink eye usually has thick yellow-green discharge that glues the lids shut, and drops can speed recovery. See someone promptly if she has eye pain, sensitivity to light, blurry vision or swelling around the eye.
Can I take ibuprofen and Tylenol together for a toothache?

Yes, and for dental pain this combination often works better than either one alone. A common approach is 400 mg of ibuprofen plus 500 to 1000 mg of acetaminophen every 6 to 8 hours, staying under 3000 to 4000 mg of acetaminophen per day and taking the ibuprofen with food. Skip the ibuprofen if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers, or take blood thinners, and remember this only buys you time until a dentist finds the cause.
Been burnt out for months. Thinking about quitting my job with no backup plan. Dumb?

It's not dumb to want out, but quitting with no plan can swap job stress for money stress, which is often worse. If you can, try a middle step first, such as using your sick leave, asking about medical leave, or reducing your hours, while you line up the next thing.
