Also see your doctor, because months of burnout can overlap with depression, and getting that treated will help you make the decision with a clearer head.
toothache + now my jaw hurts and I feel kind of short of breath and sweaty. 58M. probably the tooth right?

Don't assume it's the tooth, because jaw pain with shortness of breath and sweating can be a heart attack, especially at your age. Call 911 now rather than driving yourself. If you aren't allergic and have no bleeding problems, chew a regular 325 mg aspirin while you wait. Let the ER rule out your heart first, and the tooth can be dealt with afterward.
Quick one: does alcohol help you sleep?

It helps you fall asleep faster, but it makes the rest of the night worse. Alcohol suppresses REM sleep, fragments sleep in the second half of the night, and worsens snoring and sleep apnea, so you wake up less rested. If you drink, finish at least three to four hours before bed and keep it moderate. Using a nightcap regularly to get to sleep is a habit worth breaking.
Can I take ibuprofen and Tylenol together for a bad headache?

Yes, ibuprofen and acetaminophen work differently, so combining them at normal doses is generally safe for healthy adults and often works better than either alone. Stick to the label limits for each, which means no more than 3,000 to 4,000 mg of acetaminophen a day depending on the product, and take ibuprofen with food. Skip the ibuprofen if you have kidney problems, stomach ulcers or take blood thinners, and skip the acetaminophen if you have liver disease or drink heavily.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant with a pounding headache. Advil ok?

Avoid Advil and other NSAIDs at this stage of pregnancy, because they can affect the baby's heart and amniotic fluid after about 20 weeks. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) at normal doses is the usual choice instead. A severe headache at 34 weeks also needs a call to your provider today, especially with vision changes, swelling or upper belly pain, because those can be signs of preeclampsia. If you have a blood pressure cuff, check it, and call your provider right away if it reads 140/90 or higher.
My son's ear hurts and he's 6. Do we need antibiotics?

Not always. Many ear infections in kids his age clear up on their own within two to three days, and doctors often recommend a watch-and-wait approach with pain relief like children's ibuprofen or acetaminophen dosed for his weight. Have a doctor take a look to confirm it's actually an ear infection. Get him seen sooner if he has a fever over 102, severe pain, fluid draining from the ear, or isn't better after 48 hours.
Is it true my birth control won't work while I'm on antibiotics?

For most antibiotics, that's a myth. The main exception is rifampin and similar drugs, which do reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraception, so use backup protection if you're on one of those. The other risk is vomiting or severe diarrhea from any cause, which can stop the pill from being absorbed, so follow your pill's missed-dose rules if that happens.
fever with burning when I pee and pain in my lower back on one side

That sounds like a kidney infection, which is a urinary tract infection that has spread upward. It needs antibiotics soon, so see a doctor or go to urgent care today. Go to the ER if you're vomiting and can't keep fluids down, have a very high fever, or feel faint, because kidney infections can lead to sepsis.
toddler touched the glass front of our gas fireplace, palm has some small blisters. ugh

Run his hand under cool water for 20 minutes, distracting him with a show or snack if needed, then cover the palm loosely with a nonstick dressing. Blisters on a young child's palm are worth a same-day check with your pediatrician or urgent care. Hand burns can affect movement as they heal, and toddlers' skin burns deeply. Children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen at the right dose for his weight will help with pain. A safety screen over that glass is worth getting, since those fronts stay hot long after the flame is off.
how long can a fever last before its dangerous for an adult

It depends on your other symptoms more than the clock. A fever that lasts more than three days, keeps rising above 39.4°C (103°F), or goes away and then returns should be checked by a doctor. Get care right away for a stiff neck, confusion, chest pain, trouble breathing or a spreading rash, no matter how long the fever has lasted.
got a metal sliver in my eye grinding, feels like something's there

Don't rub it, and don't try to dig it out yourself. Metal from grinding can be very hot and fast, can embed in the cornea, and leaves a rust ring if it stays in. Cover the eye loosely with a clean cup or shield and get to an eye doctor or ER today. Mention that it came from grinding, because high-speed fragments sometimes need imaging to rule out penetration.
is it ok to take zyrtec every single day for hay fever or is that bad for you

Daily cetirizine is considered safe for most adults through allergy season and even year-round, and it's one of the most commonly used long-term allergy meds. The main downside is mild drowsiness in some people, so try taking it at night if that bothers you. Some people get intense itching for a few days if they stop after months of daily use. That usually settles, and tapering off can help. If you need it constantly and still feel lousy, an allergist can check whether a steroid nasal spray or allergy shots would serve you better.
Dad's 78, diabetic, and has a cut on his foot that's been there two weeks. He says it's nothing.

A foot wound that hasn't healed in two weeks in someone with diabetes needs to be seen this week. Poor circulation and reduced feeling can let a small cut turn into a serious infection quickly. Get him to his GP or a podiatrist soon, and go sooner if you notice redness spreading, swelling, warmth, pus or a bad smell. Until then, keep it clean and covered and keep him off it as much as possible.
how much ibuprofen can i take at once for tooth pain, like 4 or 5 pills? it's really bad

Don't take 4 or 5 at once, because the usual over-the-counter maximum is 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) every 6 to 8 hours, and more than that raises your risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems. Many dentists suggest alternating or combining ibuprofen with acetaminophen at their own labeled doses, which works surprisingly well for dental pain, as long as you have no conditions that rule either one out. Pain this severe usually means the tooth needs treatment, so get an urgent dental appointment rather than trying to out-dose it.
My elderly mom fell in the kitchen, she says she's fine but she's walking with a limp and her hip hurts. She doesn't want to go to the doctor.

Hip pain and a new limp after a fall in an older person needs an X-ray, because hip fractures can be surprisingly subtle and some people can still walk on them at first. Missing one can lead to the break shifting and much bigger problems, so it really is worth pushing her on this today. If she can't bear weight, the leg looks shortened or turned outward, or she hit her head, especially if she's on blood thinners, call for an ambulance or take her to the ER. It might help to frame it as ruling something out rather than assuming the worst.
Doctor gave me doxycycline. Pharmacy label says take with full glass of water and don't lie down. Is that serious?

Yes, follow that exactly. Doxycycline can stick in the esophagus and cause painful ulcers, so take it with a full glass of water and stay upright for at least 30 minutes, which means no taking it right before bed. Avoid taking it alongside dairy, antacids or iron and calcium supplements, which block absorption. It also makes you sunburn easily, so use sunscreen.
my bp just read 182/115 at the pharmacy machine, no headache or anything, can i just go home and recheck tomorrow?

Don't wait until tomorrow on that one. Sit quietly for five minutes and recheck, and if it's still above 180/110 you should contact your doctor or an urgent care clinic today. If you get chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, vision changes, confusion or weakness on one side, call emergency services right away, because that pattern can mean organ damage is happening.
severe eye pain, blurry vision, halos around lights, headache and nausea. took ibuprofen

Go to an ER now. That combination is a classic picture of acute angle-closure glaucoma, where eye pressure spikes suddenly, and it can cause permanent vision loss within hours without treatment. Ibuprofen won't fix the underlying problem, so don't wait to see if it works.
is it ok to put my feverish kid in an ice bath to cool her down quick

No, skip the ice bath. Ice-cold water can cause shivering, which actually raises body temperature, and it's miserable for her. A lukewarm bath, light clothes, fluids, and a proper dose of children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen (if she's over 6 months) work better. The goal is to keep her comfortable, not to hit a specific number on the thermometer.
My resting heart rate is 48. Should I be worried? I run a lot.

For a regular runner, a resting rate in the high 40s is usually a sign of good fitness, not a problem. It only needs attention if you have symptoms like dizziness, fainting, unusual fatigue or breathlessness, or if it has dropped noticeably without a change in your training. If any of those apply, see your doctor for an ECG. Otherwise it's fine to keep running.
Does drinking alcohol actually affect blood pressure or is that overblown

It's real. Regular drinking, especially more than one or two drinks a day, raises blood pressure and can make medications work less well. Many people see their readings drop noticeably within a few weeks of cutting back. An occasional drink is fine for most people, but heavy or daily drinking is worth reducing.
I have type 1 and threw up 3 times today, can't keep food down. Should I skip my insulin since I'm not eating?

Don't skip your insulin, especially your basal or long-acting dose. Your body still needs insulin when you're sick, and stopping it can quickly lead to diabetic ketoacidosis. Check your blood sugar every 2 to 4 hours, check for ketones, and sip sugar-free fluids, or sugary ones if your sugar is low. Vomiting three times and not keeping anything down is reason to call your diabetes team right now. Go to the ER if you have moderate or high ketones, keep vomiting, have belly pain, or are breathing fast.
Does vitamin C actually cure colds or is that a myth

Taking vitamin C once you're already sick doesn't do much. Regular daily use might shave a little time off colds for some people, and it seems to help more in people under heavy physical stress, like marathon runners. Zinc lozenges started within a day of symptoms have somewhat better evidence for shortening a cold. Very high doses of either can upset your stomach, so there's no point megadosing.
fastest way to kill a hangover headache?

Drink plenty of water or an electrolyte drink, eat something bland, and get some rest. Ibuprofen with food usually helps more than acetaminophen here, because acetaminophen puts extra strain on a liver that's still processing alcohol. Skip "hair of the dog," since more alcohol just delays the crash.
Will cutting salt really make a difference or is that overhyped?

It really does help, especially if you're salt-sensitive, which many people with high blood pressure are. Cutting sodium to around 1,500 to 2,300 mg a day can lower systolic pressure by several points, roughly what a single medication does. Most salt comes from bread, deli meat, soups, sauces and restaurant food rather than the salt shaker, so check labels.
Can I give my 14 year old some of my sumatriptan? She gets the same migraines I do

Please don't share it. Prescription migraine drugs are dosed and screened for the individual, and teens need their own evaluation. There are triptans approved for adolescents, though, so the pediatrician can work out whether one is right for her. Until then, ibuprofen at the correct weight-based dose, a dark quiet room and early treatment are reasonable.
quick q, does coffee raise blood pressure

Yes, caffeine can bump your blood pressure up for a few hours, especially if you don't drink it regularly. For most habitual drinkers, the long-term effect is small, and a couple of cups a day is generally fine. Just avoid coffee for 30 minutes before you take a reading so you don't skew the numbers.
Can I dye my hair while pregnant?

Most experts think occasional hair dyeing is fine in pregnancy, since very little of the chemical is absorbed through the skin. Many people wait until after the first trimester to be extra cautious. Use a well-ventilated room, wear gloves, and do a patch test, because pregnancy can make your skin more reactive. Highlights or balayage that don't touch the scalp reduce exposure even further.
I've had a scaly red patch on my elbows for months. Its not really itchy. Moisturizer doesn't help

Thick, scaly red patches on the elbows that don't respond to moisturizer are very typical of psoriasis, though other conditions can look similar. It's worth seeing a doctor or dermatologist to confirm, since there are effective prescription creams and other treatments, and psoriasis can sometimes be linked to joint problems worth knowing about. Until then, a thick ointment and over-the-counter products with salicylic acid or coal tar can soften the scale.
Got some oven cleaner splashed in my eye, what do I do

Start rinsing right now with lukewarm tap water and keep going for at least 15 to 20 minutes, holding the eyelids open and letting the water run from the inner corner outward. Oven cleaner is strongly alkaline, and alkali burns can keep damaging the eye after the splash, so rinsing time matters more than anything else. Call emergency services or have someone drive you to an ER while you keep flushing, and take the product bottle with you so they know exactly what it was.
My 4 year old has a cold and won't stop coughing at night. Can I give her some of my Robitussin, just a smaller amount?

Please don't give her your Robitussin, because over-the-counter cough and cold medicines aren't recommended for children under 6. Kids' bodies handle them differently, and guessing at a smaller dose of an adult product is how accidental overdoses happen. A cool-mist humidifier in her room, extra fluids and propping her head up a little can ease a night cough. If she's struggling to breathe, wheezing, or the cough lasts more than a couple of weeks, have her pediatrician take a look.
Can I dye my hair? I'm 18 weeks and my roots are horrible.

Hair dye is considered low risk in pregnancy because very little of it is absorbed through your skin, and waiting until after the first trimester, as you have, is the usual advice. Use a well-ventilated room, do the allergy patch test, and leave the dye on no longer than the instructions say. Highlights or a balayage that keep the color off your scalp reduce your exposure even further.
Travelling to Kenya in 10 days, totally forgot about vaccines. Am I screwed?

Not screwed, but book a travel clinic appointment in the next day or two, because 10 days is still enough time for several important vaccines and for malaria prevention. Yellow fever vaccination is recommended for most travelers to Kenya and is sometimes required for entry, so check this right away; the vaccine needs about 10 days to count, and some clinics have limited supply. They'll likely also recommend hepatitis A and typhoid, and they'll check whether you're up to date on routine shots like measles and tetanus. Antimalarial medication is just as important as the vaccines, so make sure you leave with a prescription.
My 15 year old son has been staying in his room all the time and barely eats dinner with us anymore. Teenagers do that right?

Some withdrawal is normal for teens, but pulling away from the family combined with eating less deserves a closer look. Check whether he's still seeing friends, keeping up at school, and doing things he enjoys, because losing interest across the board points more toward depression than ordinary teen privacy. Have a low-pressure conversation, maybe during a drive or a walk, and if you're seeing broader changes, book an appointment with his pediatrician, who can screen for depression and refer him on if needed.
keep waking up with headaches and a dry mouth even after 8 hours. ideas?

Morning headaches with a dry mouth after a full night often point to mouth breathing or sleep apnea, especially if you snore or wake up tired. Teeth grinding, nighttime alcohol, caffeine withdrawal and a dry bedroom are other possibilities. A humidifier and avoiding evening drinks are easy things to try. If it keeps up, see your doctor and ask about a sleep study.
Day 3 after a cat bite on my wrist and now there's a red streak going up my arm. Should I wait till Monday for my GP?

Don't wait. A red streak spreading from a bite can mean the infection is moving through your lymphatic system, and this needs treatment today. Go to urgent care or the ER now, especially if you also have fever, chills or worsening swelling. A cat bite infection near the wrist can spread quickly, and you may need stronger antibiotics than a pill can provide.
I'm 72 and on blood thinners. Gums bleed and one tooth hurts. Worry?

It's worth getting checked promptly, because bleeding gums plus a painful tooth often mean gum disease or infection, and blood thinners make bleeding more noticeable. Don't stop your blood thinner on your own. Tell your dentist which medication you take, so they can plan any treatment safely with your doctor. Avoid ibuprofen and aspirin for pain unless your doctor approves, since acetaminophen is usually the safer choice with blood thinners.
My 3yo got into my purse and may have eaten a couple of my pills, she seems fine right now

Call Poison Control right now at 1-800-222-1222 (in the US), even though she seems fine. Some medicines take hours to cause symptoms, and a couple of adult pills can be dangerous for a small child. Have the pill bottle in hand so you can tell them exactly what it was and how many might be missing. If she becomes drowsy, has trouble breathing, or has a seizure, call 911 immediately.
Tiny paper cut but it's on my eyelid somehow?? it stings

Rinse it gently with clean water and leave it alone; eyelid skin heals fast and tiny cuts usually close within a day or two. Avoid rubbing or putting makeup or ointments right at the lash line. If it's near the eye itself and you notice pain in the eye, blurry vision or persistent redness, have it checked.
My doctor won't give me antibiotics for my cold. That's ridiculous, I always get better faster on them.

Your doctor is right on this one. Colds are viral, and antibiotics do nothing against viruses, so the faster recovery you've noticed is almost certainly the cold running its natural course. Taking them anyway risks diarrhea and allergic reactions and adds to antibiotic resistance. Go back if you're still getting worse after 10 days or you start feeling better and then sharply worse, since that pattern can point to a bacterial sinus infection.
I have leftover amoxicillin from my last sinus infection, can I just take that for this sore throat?

Don't take the leftovers; most sore throats are viral and antibiotics won't touch them, and a partial old course isn't the right dose or length anyway. If you have a fever, white patches on your tonsils, swollen neck glands and no cough, get a quick strep test, because strep does need a proper full course. Otherwise, warm salt-water gargles, fluids and ibuprofen or acetaminophen usually get you through in about a week. Take the leftover pills to a pharmacy take-back so they aren't tempting next time.
I'm 67 and just got over pneumonia. My daughter says I should rest another month but I miss my walking group. Who's right?

You probably don't need a full month of rest, but your daughter is right that pneumonia takes a lot out of you, especially at 67. Short, gentle walks of 10 to 15 minutes on flat ground are usually fine once your fever is gone and you're breathing comfortably at rest. Build up gradually before rejoining the group. Check with your doctor at your follow-up, especially if you still get breathless or tired easily. Most people need several weeks to get their stamina fully back.
I'm 24 and fit but got 150/95 at a pharmacy machine. Probably the machine is broken right?

Maybe, but don't write it off. Pharmacy machines can be off if the cuff doesn't fit or you've just walked in, so recheck after five quiet minutes of sitting, with your arm supported at heart level. If it stays high, see a doctor. High blood pressure in a young, fit person sometimes has a specific cause, such as a kidney or hormone problem, and those are worth finding early.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and have a bad headache and my vision is kind of sparkly. probably just tired?

Please call your OB or labor and delivery right now. A severe headache with vision changes late in pregnancy can be a sign of preeclampsia, a dangerous rise in blood pressure. They'll likely want to check your blood pressure and urine today. Don't wait it out, especially if you also have swelling in your face or hands or pain under your right ribs.
fever came back after my kid was better for 2 days with an ear infection earlier

A fever that comes back after improvement is a good reason to call the pediatrician. It can mean a secondary infection, or that the ear infection isn't clearing. Book a visit in the next day or so so they can look in the ears and check for anything else. Go in sooner if your child seems very unwell, has ear drainage, or has swelling behind the ear.
Woman, 49. Weird jaw ache, exhaustion, mild nausea for a day. No real chest pain. Am I overthinking a heart thing?

You're not overthinking it. Women often have heart attacks without dramatic chest pain, and jaw ache with unusual fatigue and nausea is a recognized pattern. Get evaluated today, either in urgent care or the emergency department, where they can do an ECG and blood tests quickly. If the symptoms suddenly get worse or you feel faint or breathless, call emergency services.
Teenage daughter got a burn from a hair straightener on her neck. Looks like a red stripe. Big deal?

Usually not, since straightener burns are typically small, superficial burns that heal within a week or two. Run cool water or hold a cool damp cloth on it for 20 minutes, then apply aloe vera or petroleum jelly and leave it uncovered or lightly covered. Have her keep it out of strong sun for a few months to reduce the chance of a dark mark. See a doctor if it blisters badly, oozes, or shows signs of infection.
Shoulder hurts when I lift my arm overhead, been 3 weeks, 50M. Should I just keep working out through it?

Pain lifting your arm overhead often points to rotator cuff irritation or impingement, and pushing through it with heavy overhead pressing usually makes it worse. Drop the movements that hurt, keep doing pain-free exercises, and add gentle rotator cuff work like band external rotations. If it isn't clearly improving in another couple of weeks, or if you have night pain or real weakness lifting the arm, see a doctor or physio, since a tear needs different handling.
Teenage son stays up till 2am and sleeps till noon on weekends. Lazy or normal?

It's mostly biology, not laziness, because teenagers' body clocks shift a couple of hours later during puberty, so they genuinely don't feel sleepy until late. They also need about 8 to 10 hours, which school schedules rarely allow, so weekend sleep-ins are partly catching up. Screens late at night make the delay worse, so charging his phone outside the bedroom and getting morning sunlight can help a lot. Try to keep weekend wake times within two hours of weekday ones so Monday mornings aren't brutal.
Can ear candling get rid of wax?

No, ear candling doesn't remove wax. Studies show the 'wax' left behind is just candle residue, and the method has caused burns, canal blockages from dripping wax, and eardrum perforations. Softening drops like mineral oil or carbamide peroxide are a safer approach. If your ear is truly blocked, a clinic can irrigate or remove the wax quickly.
What's the deal with allergy shots, are they worth it for someone in their 30s?

They're often worth it if you're dealing with significant allergies to pollen, dust mites or pets and medications aren't controlling your symptoms well. Allergy shots gradually retrain your immune system over a course of three to five years, and the benefits often last long after you stop. The main commitments are regular clinic visits and waiting about 30 minutes after each shot in case of a reaction, so ask an allergist whether you're a good candidate.
I have egg allergy. no flu shot for me right?

Actually, you can get it. Current guidance says people with any severity of egg allergy can receive any flu vaccine appropriate for their age, without special precautions beyond the usual monitoring. The amount of egg protein is tiny and reactions are very rare. If you've had a severe reaction to a previous flu shot itself, though, that's a separate question to discuss with your doctor.
My friend has some leftover Xanax and offered me a couple for my flight next week. I'm a nervous flyer. Is that fine?

I'd pass on that. Someone else's Xanax wasn't dosed for you, it's illegal to share, and it can interact badly with alcohol, sleep aids or other medications you might take on a travel day. If flying anxiety is a real problem, see your doctor before the trip, since they can prescribe something appropriate or suggest alternatives. Slow breathing with a longer exhale, noise-cancelling headphones and an aisle seat also help many people more than they'd expect.
Spotting a little at 6 weeks. Pinkish brown. Should I panic

No need to panic. Light pink or brown spotting in early pregnancy is common and often harmless, sometimes from implantation or a sensitive cervix. Still, give your provider a call today so they can decide whether you need a check or an ultrasound. Seek care right away for heavy bleeding, cramping that's getting worse, one-sided pain, shoulder pain, or feeling faint, since those can point to miscarriage or an ectopic pregnancy.
is yoga ok while getting over a cold

Gentle yoga is usually a great choice while you recover from a cold. Stick to slow flows and stretching, and skip hot yoga and heavy inversions if your head is congested, since they can make the pressure and stuffiness worse. If you have a fever, rest instead.
I have a blister on my heel from new shoes, should I pop it?

Leave it intact if you can, since the skin over it is the best protection against infection. Cover it with a donut-shaped moleskin pad or a hydrocolloid blister bandage and give those shoes a break. If it's big and painful enough that it'll burst anyway, sterilize a needle, drain it from the edge, and leave the roof of skin in place before covering it.
pollen count is huge today and i have a soccer game. any tricks?

Take a non-drowsy antihistamine like loratadine or fexofenadine about an hour before the game, and wraparound sunglasses help keep pollen out of your eyes. Afterward, shower and change clothes as soon as you can so you aren't carrying pollen around all evening. If you have asthma, bring your rescue inhaler, since pollen days can trigger wheezing during exercise.
Can I take NyQuil and Tylenol together? I feel awful.

Check the NyQuil label first, because most NyQuil formulas already contain acetaminophen, the active ingredient in Tylenol. Taking both can push you past a safe daily dose and damage your liver. Stick to one source of acetaminophen, keep your total under the limit on the label (generally no more than 3,000 to 4,000 mg a day for adults, less if you drink alcohol or have liver problems), and don't drink alcohol with either.
knee swollen and hot, no injury. 52M. just ice it?

A hot, swollen knee with no injury needs to be seen by a doctor today, not just iced. It can be gout, but it can also be a joint infection, which can damage the joint quickly and needs urgent treatment. Go to urgent care or the emergency department straight away if you also have a fever, feel unwell, or can't put weight on it.
postpartum 5 weeks, cry every day, feel nothing for the baby. normal??

Daily crying and feeling disconnected from your baby five weeks after birth goes beyond the 'baby blues', which usually fade by about two weeks, and it sounds like it could be postpartum depression. It's very common, it isn't your fault, and it doesn't make you a bad mother. Call your OB, midwife or GP this week and tell them exactly what you told me, because treatment works well and many options are safe while breastfeeding. If you have any thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, call emergency services or a crisis line right away.
is it safe for my 70 year old mom to take melatonin every night

For most older adults, low-dose melatonin is one of the safer sleep aids, and 0.5 to 3 mg is usually enough, since more doesn't work better and can cause grogginess. Run it past her pharmacist or doctor if she takes blood thinners, blood pressure meds or diabetes medication, because there are some interactions. She should steer clear of over-the-counter sleep aids containing diphenhydramine (Benadryl, ZzzQuil, the 'PM' products), which raise fall and confusion risk in older people.
My 14 year old wants to start taking creatine for football. He's healthy. Is that fine or should I say no?

Creatine is one of the best-studied supplements in adults, but there's much less research in teenagers. The American Academy of Pediatrics advises against performance supplements for kids his age. At 14, he'll get more from consistent training, enough sleep and real meals with good protein than from any powder. If he's set on it, run it by his pediatrician first. If you do go ahead, only buy third-party tested products, because sports supplements are sometimes contaminated with stimulants or steroids.
honestly I'm sick of the CGM beeping at night, can I just turn alerts off?

Alert fatigue is real, but turning off your low alert entirely is risky, especially overnight, when lows can go unnoticed. Most CGMs let you adjust the thresholds, silence high alerts, or set a schedule, so keep the urgent low alarm on and tweak the rest. If you're getting woken constantly, that's useful information to bring to your diabetes team, because your overnight basal insulin or bedtime routine may need adjusting.
I'm 67 and my lisinopril makes me cough constantly. Can I just stop taking it?

Don't just stop. Call your doctor, because that dry cough is a well-known side effect of ACE inhibitors like lisinopril and there's an easy fix. They'll usually switch you to a related drug called an ARB, such as losartan, which controls blood pressure the same way without the cough. Stopping on your own leaves your pressure unprotected until you're on something else.
my crown fell off. can i superglue it back?

Please don't use superglue, because it can irritate the tooth, trap decay underneath and make it impossible to re-cement the crown properly. Clean the crown and use a temporary dental cement from the pharmacy to hold it in place until you can see your dentist. Call them within a few days, and keep the crown safe if you can't get it to stay.
My kid swallowed maybe 5 of my iron pills. She seems fine??

Call Poison Control right now (1-800-222-1222 in the US) or emergency services, even though she seems fine. Iron is one of the most dangerous overdoses in young children, and symptoms can be delayed or seem to improve before serious problems set in. Have the bottle in hand so you can tell them the strength. Don't make her vomit unless they tell you to.
I'm 41 and just found out I'm pregnant. Is there stuff I should do differently than a younger mom?

Plenty of women over 40 have healthy pregnancies, but you'll be offered a few extra checks, so book your first appointment soon. Your doctor will likely discuss screening for chromosomal conditions, such as NIPT blood testing, keep a closer eye on your blood pressure and blood sugar, and may suggest low-dose aspirin or extra scans later on. Keep taking folic acid, and tell them about any existing health conditions or medications at that first visit.
how much salt is too much if you have high bp

Aim for less than 2,300 mg of sodium a day, and ideally closer to 1,500 mg if you have high blood pressure. Most of it comes from packaged foods, restaurant meals, bread, and deli meats rather than the salt shaker. Reading labels for a week usually shows you where your sodium is coming from.
Getting bad diarrhea on clindamycin, like 6 times a day. Normal?

Call your prescriber today rather than pushing through. Clindamycin is known for triggering C. diff, a gut infection that causes frequent watery diarrhea and can get serious. You may need a test and a different treatment. Don't take anti-diarrhea meds like loperamide until you've talked to them, and seek urgent care if you see blood, have a fever or develop severe belly pain.
how much salt is too much for high blood pressure

Most guidelines suggest keeping sodium under about 2,300 mg a day, roughly a teaspoon of salt. Aiming closer to 1,500 mg can give a bigger drop if you have high blood pressure. Most sodium comes from packaged food, bread, deli meat, sauces and restaurant meals rather than the salt shaker. Checking labels is where you'll make the biggest difference.
is it bad that my resting heart rate is 52? im a runner

For a regular runner a resting heart rate in the 50s, or even 40s, is usually a sign of good fitness, because a trained heart pumps more blood with each beat. It's only a concern if you also have dizziness, fainting, unusual fatigue, or breathlessness that doesn't fit your training. If any of those show up, get a check and an ECG.
chipped my front tooth on a fork. doesn't hurt. need to do anything?

If it's a small chip with no pain, it isn't urgent, but it's still worth booking a visit in the next week or two. A dentist can smooth it or bond it so it looks right and doesn't crack further. Come in sooner if you see pink or red in the chipped area, notice sharp sensitivity, or the edge is cutting your tongue.
how long after a dog bite do i have to get a tetanus shot

Ideally get it within 48 hours of the bite, but don't skip it if more time has passed, because a late booster is still better than none. You need one if your last tetanus shot was more than 5 years ago for a dirty or deep wound like a bite, or if you can't remember when you last had one. A pharmacy, urgent care, or your doctor can give it quickly.
I have leftover amoxicillin from last year's ear infection. My throat is killing me, can I just take those?

Skip the leftovers. Most sore throats are viral, so antibiotics won't help, and a partial old supply wouldn't be a full course anyway even if this were strep. If you have a fever, white patches on your tonsils and no cough, get a quick strep test, because that's the case where the right antibiotic actually matters. Otherwise, warm salt-water gargles, fluids and ibuprofen or acetaminophen are your best bet.
My doctor offered RSV vaccine. I'm 74, healthy. Necessary?

It's a good idea, as a single RSV vaccine dose is recommended for everyone 75 and up and for people 50 to 74 with higher risk. Even healthy older adults can end up hospitalized with RSV, since it can turn into pneumonia. If your doctor offered it, they may have a specific reason in mind, so ask, and either way it's a one-time shot with mostly mild side effects.
i want to quit my antidepressants because of weight gain. can i just skip every other day to taper

Skipping alternate days isn't a good taper. Your blood levels swing up and down, which can cause dizziness, irritability and 'brain zaps,' and with shorter-acting drugs it's especially rough. Weight gain is a real reason to change, though, and there are antidepressants less likely to cause it. Bring it up with your prescriber, who can plan a proper gradual taper or a switch.
I keep getting muscle cramps at night, 60F. potassium pills?

Hold off on potassium pills, since too much can affect your heart rhythm, especially if you take blood pressure medicine or have kidney issues. Gentle calf stretches before bed and staying hydrated help many people. Mention the cramps to your doctor too, because some medications such as diuretics and statins can cause them, and a simple blood test can check your potassium and magnesium.
Woke up at 3am with horrible pain under my right ribs after a big fatty dinner, lasted 2 hours then went away. Do I need to do anything?

That's a textbook description of a gallbladder attack, so book an appointment with your doctor soon; an ultrasound can usually confirm gallstones. Until then, keep your meals smaller and lower in fat to reduce the chance of another attack. Go to the ER if the pain lasts more than a few hours, or if you develop fever, chills, yellowing of your skin or eyes, or dark urine, because those can mean an infection or a blocked duct.
Is grapefruit really a problem with statins or is that a myth?

It's real, but it depends on the statin. Grapefruit blocks an enzyme that breaks down simvastatin, lovastatin and to a lesser degree atorvastatin, which can push blood levels up and raise the risk of muscle damage. Rosuvastatin and pravastatin are barely affected. If you love grapefruit, check which statin you're on with your pharmacist, and ask your doctor about switching if needed.
can i drink tonight after my covid shot or will it ruin it

A drink or two won't ruin your vaccine, and there's no evidence moderate alcohol makes it less effective. Heavy drinking isn't a great idea, though, because it can make the fatigue and achiness from the shot feel worse and mask how you're actually feeling. Go easy and drink plenty of water.
My daughter is 12 and super worried about her weight, she's skipping lunch. She's a normal size. What should I do?

Take this seriously but stay calm. Skipping meals because of worry about weight at 12 can be an early sign of disordered eating. Talk with her about it without commenting on her body or labeling foods as good or bad, and keep family meals regular. Book a visit with her pediatrician, who can check her growth and screen for an eating disorder, since early help works much better than waiting.
what does a heart attack actually feel like? want to know what to watch for

The classic feeling is pressure, squeezing or heaviness in the center of the chest lasting more than a few minutes or coming in waves, often spreading to the arm, jaw, neck or back. It often comes with sweating, nausea, breathlessness or lightheadedness. Women, older people and diabetics more often get subtler signs like unusual fatigue, nausea or breathlessness without obvious chest pain, and whenever you suspect one, call emergency services rather than driving yourself.
My 84 yr old mother is taking 11 different medications from 4 different doctors. Is that a problem??

It can be. With that many drugs from that many prescribers, interactions and duplicate medications are a real risk, and they're a common cause of falls and confusion in older people. Put every bottle in a bag, including supplements and over-the-counter pills, and take it to her primary doctor or pharmacist for a full medication review. Many pharmacies do this for free, and it often ends with a shorter, safer list.
My father (88) has started getting confused in the evenings, agitated, sometimes doesn't know where he is. Mornings he's mostly okay. Is this just dementia?

That pattern is often called sundowning and is common in dementia, but a sudden change in confusion in an older person needs to be checked first for a treatable cause. Urinary tract infections, dehydration, new medications, and poor sleep are frequent culprits. Get him seen by his doctor soon, and same-day if the change was abrupt. In the meantime, bright light during the day, a calm, consistent evening routine, and good lighting at dusk can take the edge off.
Can I just skip my kid's MMR and catch up later when he's older? He hates shots.

Delaying MMR leaves him unprotected during the years when measles is most dangerous, and measles is contagious enough that outbreaks still pop up regularly. The standard schedule is a first dose at 12 to 15 months and a second at 4 to 6 years, and sticking to it is the safer choice. For the needle fear, ask your pediatrician about numbing cream, distraction and comfort positioning, which make a real difference for a lot of kids.
is a gluten allergy and celiac the same thing

They're different. Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition in which gluten damages the small intestine, and even tiny amounts matter over time. A wheat allergy is an immune reaction that can cause hives, swelling, or anaphylaxis. Non-celiac gluten sensitivity is a third, milder category. Get tested for celiac before cutting out gluten, because the blood test and biopsy are unreliable once you've stopped eating it.
can i use hydrogen peroxide in my ear every day to keep it clean

Daily use isn't a good idea, because ears clean themselves and regular peroxide can irritate and dry out the canal. An occasional few drops of diluted peroxide or a wax softener is fine if wax builds up, but only if your eardrum is intact. Never use it if you have ear tubes, a perforation, or pain or drainage. For most people, washing the outer ear with a washcloth is all the cleaning needed.
36 weeks and my underwear keeps getting wet, like a small trickle. pee or water broke?

It's worth getting checked today, because a slow trickle can be amniotic fluid and not just pee or discharge. Amniotic fluid is usually clear or pale and odorless and keeps leaking even when you aren't straining, while urine smells like urine. Call labor and delivery and they can do a quick test to tell for sure. Go in right away if the fluid is green or brown, or if you notice less movement.
Tested negative for covid but feel awful. Do I trust it?

One negative rapid test early on isn't conclusive, because they often miss COVID in the first couple of days. Retest 48 hours later, and ideally again after that, before ruling it out. Either way, stay home while you feel awful and especially while you have a fever. If you're high risk, a PCR test or a flu test from a clinic can confirm it, which matters because both have time-sensitive antiviral treatments.
can stress actually cause hair loss or is that a myth

It's real. A big stressor like illness, surgery, a breakup or a crushing work period can push lots of hair follicles into their resting phase, and about two to three months later you shed noticeably more. It's called telogen effluvium, and it usually recovers on its own within six months or so once things settle. It's still worth seeing a doctor, because thyroid problems, iron deficiency and other conditions cause similar shedding and are easy to test for. Bald patches, scalp pain or redness need checking sooner.
Splashed some drain cleaner on my hand, it's tingling. Rinsed for like 30 seconds.

Thirty seconds isn't nearly enough for a chemical burn, so get back under running water now. Keep rinsing for at least 20 minutes, and longer if it still tingles, while you remove any rings or contaminated clothing. Drain cleaners are often strong alkalis that keep burning deeper, so call poison control with the product label in hand. Get seen urgently if the skin looks white, grey, blistered or the pain is escalating.
Doc put me on lisinopril 3 weeks ago and my numbers are perfect now. Can I stop taking it?

Perfect numbers usually mean the lisinopril is working, not that you no longer need it. If you stop, your pressure will most likely climb back up, sometimes within days. If you'd like to come off it eventually, talk to your doctor about it, because weight loss, exercise and cutting salt can sometimes make that possible under supervision.
Does exercise actually help depression or is that just something people say?

It really does help. Large reviews show regular exercise has a meaningful effect on mild to moderate depression, comparable in some studies to therapy or medication. Brisk walking for about 30 minutes, three to five times a week, is enough to count, and doing it outside or with other people adds extra benefit. For moderate or severe depression, treat it as a powerful add-on rather than a replacement for proper treatment.
I have migraines 15+ days a month and nothing OTC helps anymore. is this just my life now?

No, it doesn't have to be. Fifteen or more headache days a month counts as chronic migraine, and there are now good preventive treatments, including CGRP medications, Botox injections and older daily pills. Ask your doctor for a preventive plan or a referral to a neurologist or headache specialist. Frequent OTC use can also be feeding the cycle, so that's worth addressing at the same time.
ugh hangover headache, can i take tylenol

Skip Tylenol after heavy drinking, because acetaminophen combined with alcohol puts extra strain on your liver. Ibuprofen with some food is the better pick if your stomach tolerates it. Drink plenty of water or an electrolyte drink, eat something bland and rest. Time is honestly the main cure.
Cut myself on a broken glass while washing up. Deep-ish gash on the base of my thumb, can't quite bend the thumb fully now.

Trouble bending your thumb after a cut there could mean a tendon or nerve has been damaged, so please go to urgent care or the ER today. Keep firm pressure on the wound and hold your hand raised on the way. Don't try to close it yourself, because a repair done early gives the best chance of full movement coming back. Tell them it was glass, since they may want an X-ray for fragments.
I get really bad leg cramps at night. Should I just start taking potassium pills?

I wouldn't self-prescribe potassium. Too much can cause dangerous heart rhythms, especially if you take blood pressure meds or have kidney issues, and low potassium often isn't the cause of cramps anyway. Stretch your calves before bed, stay hydrated, and get potassium from foods like bananas, potatoes and beans. If the cramps are frequent or severe, ask your doctor for basic bloodwork and a review of your medications, since diuretics and statins are common culprits.
sweating it out under heavy blankets works right?

It doesn't. Bundling up traps heat and can push your temperature higher while dehydrating you. Wear light layers, use a single sheet if you're chilled, drink plenty of fluids, and take acetaminophen or ibuprofen if you're uncomfortable.
Benadryl or Claritin for my itchy eyes? I have work.

Go with Claritin, because Benadryl causes real drowsiness and can slow your reaction time even when you don't feel sleepy. For itchy eyes specifically, antihistamine eye drops like ketotifen often work faster and better than a pill. Rinsing your face and eyes with cool water when you get home also helps clear the pollen out.
My 2 year old touched the oven door and has a red mark on her fingers, she's crying but calming down. ER?

Start with cool running water on her fingers for 20 minutes, or as long as she'll tolerate it, and keep the rest of her warm. If the skin is just red and she settles, it's likely minor, and you can call your pediatrician's nurse line for reassurance. Go in if blisters appear, the skin looks white or leathery, or the burn covers more than a small area. Small children's burns can be deeper than they first look, so lean toward getting it checked.
my 15 year old wants to take her friend's adderall for finals. how bad is that really

It's genuinely risky, not just against the rules. Adderall can cause a racing heart, high blood pressure, anxiety and insomnia, and in a teen with an undiagnosed heart condition it can trigger serious problems. Studies also show it doesn't improve grades much for people without ADHD. If she's struggling with focus, a doctor's evaluation is the right route, and sleep plus spaced studying will help her more this week.
my 2 month old feels hot and the thermometer says 100.6 rectal. is that a big deal or am i overreacting

You're not overreacting. A rectal temperature of 100.4°F or higher in a baby under 3 months needs medical attention right away. Call your pediatrician's after-hours line now or go to the emergency department, even if the baby seems fine otherwise. Young infants can have serious infections with few other signs, so doctors want to check them promptly. Don't give any fever medicine before talking to a doctor, because it can mask the fever they need to assess.
cat bite on my finger from yesterday, now it's red and swollen and hurts to bend. can i wait and see?

No, get seen today, ideally now. Redness, swelling and pain bending a finger after a cat bite can mean an infection that's reaching the tendon sheath, which can spread fast and may need urgent treatment. Go to an urgent care or ER rather than waiting for a regular appointment. If you see red streaks moving up your hand or arm, or have a fever, go to the ER.
my bp just read 182/115 at the pharmacy machine, I feel fine though. should I just go home and recheck tomorrow?

Don't wait until tomorrow on a reading that high. Sit quietly for five minutes and recheck, and if it's still above 180/110, call your doctor or an urgent care line today. If you get chest pain, shortness of breath, a severe headache, vision changes, confusion, or weakness on one side, call emergency services right away. Feeling fine doesn't mean it's safe, because very high pressure often has no symptoms until it causes damage.
I'm diabetic and got a small cut on the bottom of my foot. It's not bad, I'll just keep an eye on it?

With diabetes, even a small foot cut deserves more care than "keep an eye on it," because reduced sensation and circulation let infections get going quietly. Wash it gently with soap and water, cover it with a clean dressing, change it daily, and keep pressure off it as much as you can. Check it every day, including with a mirror, for any redness, warmth, swelling, drainage or odor. It's worth a call to your doctor or podiatrist this week, and go in promptly if anything looks worse or it isn't clearly healing within a few days.
Is it ok to give my 9 month old honey for her cough? My mom swears by it.

Hold off on honey until she's past her first birthday, because it can carry botulism spores that a baby's gut can't handle yet, and infant botulism is serious. For now, a cool-mist humidifier, saline drops with gentle suction, and plenty of breast milk or formula are the safest ways to ease a cough. Once she's over 12 months, your mom's honey remedy is actually backed by decent evidence.
My mom's doctor wants her to get the shingles vaccine but she says she's too old for vaccines. She's 81.

She's actually in the age group that benefits most, because shingles becomes more common and more severe with age. Older adults are also the most likely to get the long-lasting nerve pain that can follow it. The recommended vaccine, Shingrix, is given in two doses and is highly effective in people over 70. Expect a sore arm and maybe a day of feeling tired, which is a small trade for avoiding an illness that can linger for months.
Can I just give my 85 year old father my leftover Ambien? He can't sleep and it worked great for me.

Please don't. Ambien and similar sleeping pills raise the risk of falls, confusion and nighttime wandering in people his age, and sharing prescription medication is risky because it may interact with what he already takes. Talk to his doctor about the insomnia, since poor sleep in older adults often has a treatable cause like pain, frequent urination, sleep apnea or a medication side effect. Meanwhile, a consistent schedule, daytime light exposure and cutting caffeine after noon are safe places to start.
My son got a cut on his knee at the park and now two days later it's red, hot, swollen and the redness is spreading up his leg. He's 9.

Redness that's spreading, plus heat and swelling, two days after a cut sounds like a skin infection such as cellulitis. He needs to be seen by a doctor today, because he'll likely need antibiotics. Draw a pen line around the edge of the redness so you can tell if it's moving. Go to urgent care or the ER straight away if he has a fever, red streaks running up the leg, severe pain or seems unwell.
Can antibiotics make birth control stop working?

For most common antibiotics, no. The well-established exception is rifampin, and its relatives like rifabutin, which clearly reduce hormonal contraceptive effectiveness, so use backup protection with those. Vomiting or severe diarrhea from any illness can also reduce how well the pill is absorbed. In that case, follow your pill's missed-dose guidance.
My dad (72) fell yesterday and now his back hurts a lot, he has osteoporosis. He says it's just bruised.

He should get checked today. In someone his age with osteoporosis, even a minor fall can cause a vertebral compression fracture, and those often feel like a bad bruise at first. A doctor can do an exam and an X-ray, and a fracture changes how the pain is treated and whether his bone medication needs adjusting. If he has any numbness, leg weakness or trouble walking, take him to the ER rather than waiting for an appointment.
Been taking omeprazole for 3 years without seeing a doctor. Fine?

It's worth checking in with a doctor, because omeprazole is meant for shorter courses unless a doctor decides you need it long term. Using it for years can affect absorption of B12, magnesium and calcium, and the underlying cause should be looked at. Don't stop suddenly, though, since that can cause rebound heartburn. A doctor can help you taper off or confirm it's right for you.
I've had a headache for two days, is my blood pressure the cause?

Probably not. High blood pressure usually causes no symptoms at all, and headaches typically only show up at dangerously high levels. If you have a monitor, check your pressure for peace of mind. If it's above 180/120, or the headache is sudden and severe, comes with confusion, weakness or vision changes, or is the worst you've ever had, seek urgent care.
just tell me which supplement to take to lower my risk of heart attack, I don't want statins

No supplement has evidence close to what statins have for preventing heart attacks. Fish oil, red yeast rice and the rest are either weak or poorly regulated, and red yeast rice actually contains a statin-like compound in unpredictable doses. The biggest wins outside medication are not smoking, regular exercise, a fiber-rich diet and controlling your blood pressure. Talk with your doctor about your actual risk score and your concerns about statins, because there are lower doses and alternatives that may suit you.
toddler got scratched on the cheek by grandma's cat. little red line. what do i do

Wash the scratch gently with soap and water, pat it dry, and you can apply a little petroleum jelly or antibiotic ointment. A light surface scratch like that usually heals fine on its own. Call the pediatrician if it gets swollen, warm or oozy, if a lump appears near the jaw or neck in the next couple of weeks, or if your toddler runs a fever. If the scratch is near the eye, have a doctor check it today.
Can I give my 6 year old melatonin so she goes to bed earlier? Her friend's mom does it every night.

Melatonin can help some kids, but check with her pediatrician before starting, since it's best used short-term at a low dose and isn't a substitute for good bedtime habits. Children's gummies vary widely in actual dose, and accidental overdoses in kids have risen sharply, so it should be stored like medicine. Often a consistent bedtime routine, no screens for an hour before bed, and a dark, cool room fix the problem on their own. If she regularly struggles to fall asleep despite that, her doctor can look into why.
My doctor wants me on meds for 142/90 but I'd rather try beetroot juice and garlic pills. Thoughts?

Beetroot juice and garlic may lower blood pressure a little, but the effect is modest and inconsistent, so they aren't a reliable replacement for treatment. What works better without medication is cutting sodium, regular exercise, losing weight if needed, limiting alcohol and following a DASH-style diet. Ask your doctor whether a supervised three-month lifestyle trial with home monitoring is reasonable at your numbers. Agree in advance that you'll start medication if your readings don't come down.
can i be allergic to my new cat if i never had problems with my old one

Yes, that happens fairly often. Cats produce different amounts of the main allergen protein, Fel d 1, and unneutered males tend to produce the most. Allergies can also develop at any age even if you were fine before. Keeping the cat out of your bedroom, running a HEPA filter, and washing your hands after petting can help a lot. If you're wheezing or getting chest tightness, see a doctor, because cat allergy can trigger asthma.
I've got a mole on my back that my wife says looks bigger and darker than last year. It doesn't hurt. Probably nothing right?

A mole that's growing or darkening deserves a proper look even if it doesn't hurt, because change is one of the main warning signs of melanoma and early melanomas usually aren't painful. Book an appointment with your GP or a dermatologist in the next few weeks and ask them to check it, ideally with a dermatoscope. In the meantime, have your wife take a clear photo next to a ruler so you have a baseline to compare against. Most changing moles turn out benign, but this is exactly the kind you want checked rather than guessed about.
what's a good A1c number

For most adults with diabetes, the target is under 7%, while a normal A1c without diabetes is below 5.7%. Your doctor may set a looser goal, around 7.5–8%, if you're older or prone to lows, or a tighter one if you can get there safely. The goal is good control without frequent hypoglycemia.
Had strep twice this year. Is there something I should be doing differently?

Make sure you're finishing each course fully, and swap your toothbrush once you've been on antibiotics for a day or two. It's also worth asking whether someone in your household might be a carrier who keeps passing it back. If you're getting frequent confirmed strep infections, an ENT can talk through whether a tonsillectomy is worth considering, though at twice a year most people just treat each episode as it comes.
my mom is 78 and has had the flu for 3 days and now she's kind of confused and not eating

That needs medical attention today, not a wait-and-see. New confusion in an older adult with flu can signal dehydration, pneumonia or a serious infection, and those can progress quickly at her age. Take her to urgent care or the emergency department, or call emergency services if she's hard to wake, breathing fast or her lips look bluish.
should i pop a burn blister? it's annoying

Leave it intact, because the blister roof acts as a sterile bandage over the raw skin underneath. Cover it with a loose non-stick dressing so it doesn't get rubbed. If it bursts on its own, wash it gently and leave the skin flap in place. Then apply plain petroleum jelly and keep it covered. Get it checked if the area turns increasingly red, hot, swollen or starts oozing pus.
Is it okay to keep running? I'm a marathoner and just found out I'm 8 weeks.

If you're already a seasoned runner and your pregnancy is uncomplicated, you can usually keep running. Scale back intensity and skip racing for PRs. A good rule is to stay at a pace where you can still talk. Hydrate well, avoid overheating, and stop if you feel dizzy, have bleeding, chest pain, or fluid leaking. Run your plan by your OB so they can flag anything specific to you.
can weed help with stress

It can feel relaxing in the short term, but regular use tends to worsen anxiety and sleep over time. In some people, especially younger users or those with a family history of psychosis, it can trigger paranoia or panic. Many people also find they need it just to feel normal after a while, which is a red flag. Exercise, sleep and talking to someone are better long-term tools, and if you're using it daily to cope, it's worth discussing with your doctor.
My mom is 70 and has a fever and is coughing but says it's 'just a cold' and refuses to see anyone. Should I push it?

Yes, push gently. At 70, a fever with a cough can be pneumonia or flu, and those turn serious faster than in younger people. Call her doctor today. If she's short of breath, has chest pain, seems confused, or can't keep fluids down, she needs urgent care or the ER regardless of her protests. Framing it as "just to rule out pneumonia so we can stop worrying" often gets a yes.
18 y/o, got 128/78 at a sports physical. Am I doomed lol

Not doomed at all. That's in the elevated range, and it's very commonly bumped up by nerves at a physical. Recheck it a few times when you're relaxed. If it stays up, focus on limiting energy drinks and salty snacks, staying active and getting decent sleep, and mention it at your next checkup.
how long after covid can i go back to crossfit

For a mild case, many sports medicine guidelines suggest waiting until you've been symptom-free for at least a week, then building intensity over another week or two. Start with light movement and add harder work only if you feel fine afterward. If you had a moderate or severe case, or you notice chest pain, palpitations, or unusual breathlessness, check with your doctor before going back to high intensity.
is it ok to skip my asthma controller inhaler when i feel fine? seems pointless

Feeling fine is usually a sign the controller is working, not a sign you don't need it. Inhaled steroids calm the underlying airway inflammation over weeks, and stopping them often lets symptoms and flare-ups creep back. If you've been symptom-free for months, ask your doctor about stepping down your dose. That's a common and reasonable thing to do, but it should be done deliberately rather than by quietly quitting.
best time to take calcium? also take thyroid meds

Take your calcium at least four hours away from your levothyroxine, because calcium binds to it and can noticeably cut how much you absorb. A common setup is thyroid medication first thing in the morning on an empty stomach and calcium with dinner. Your body absorbs calcium best in doses of 500 to 600 mg or less, so split it up if you take more than that.
Is honey safe for my 9 month old's cough?

No, avoid honey until after their first birthday. It can contain bacterial spores that cause infant botulism, a rare but serious illness, in babies under 12 months. For a 9-month-old, try saline drops, gentle suctioning, a cool-mist humidifier and frequent feeds to keep them hydrated. Call your pediatrician if they're breathing fast, feeding poorly or running a fever above 102°F.
Got a sunburn so bad it's blistering across my shoulders. Should I pop the blisters so they heal faster?

Leave the blisters intact. They're a sterile bandage your body made, and popping them raises the risk of infection and scarring. Use cool compresses, a plain moisturizer or aloe, and ibuprofen for pain and swelling, and drink extra water. Blistering over a large area is a second-degree burn, so see a doctor if you get fever, chills, dizziness or nausea, or if a blister area becomes increasingly red, hot or oozes pus.
What's the right dose of children's ibuprofen for a 2 year old?

Ibuprofen should be dosed by weight, not age. For children's ibuprofen at 100 mg per 5 mL, a toddler weighing roughly 24 to 35 pounds usually gets 5 mL, every 6 to 8 hours as needed, with no more than four doses in 24 hours. Always use the syringe that comes with the bottle, check the concentration on the label, and give it with some food or milk. Check with your pediatrician first if your child is under 6 months, dehydrated or vomiting a lot.
ate some kinda sketchy chicken 2 hrs ago, should i make myself throw up?

No, forcing yourself to vomit isn't recommended. It doesn't reliably remove much, and it can irritate or injure your throat and esophagus. Most people who eat slightly off food feel fine or get a short-lived upset stomach. Stay hydrated and watch for vomiting, diarrhea or fever over the next day, and seek care if you get bloody stool, can't keep fluids down or have a high fever.
I have rosacea and my face is constantly red. Is there an actual treatment or do I just live with it?

There are real treatments, so you don't have to just live with it. A doctor can prescribe creams like azelaic acid, metronidazole or ivermectin for bumps, brimonidine for daytime flushing, and oral doxycycline for flares. Laser or IPL can also cut down persistent redness and visible vessels. Daily mineral sunscreen, gentle fragrance-free skincare and noting your triggers, like alcohol, heat or spicy food, help a lot alongside treatment.
is a neti pot actually good for allergies or just hippie stuff

It actually works, because saline rinses wash pollen and mucus out of your nose and can noticeably reduce congestion. The key safety rule is to use distilled, sterile or previously boiled-and-cooled water, never straight tap water, since rare but dangerous infections have been linked to tap water rinses. Clean the pot after each use and let it dry fully.
Parrot bit my lip hard. Bled but stopped. Overreacting?

Not overreacting to check it, but this is usually manageable at home. Rinse gently with clean water, hold pressure if it bleeds again, and apply a cold compress for swelling. See a doctor if the cut goes through the edge of the lip, gapes open, or shows signs of infection like increasing swelling, warmth or pus. Lip cuts that cross the border can scar unevenly without proper stitching.
Does CBD oil work for stress? Thinking of trying it instead of my meds.

The evidence for CBD and anxiety is still early and mixed, and product quality varies a lot. So it's not a reliable replacement for medication that's working for you. Stopping some antidepressants or anti-anxiety meds suddenly can also cause withdrawal and relapse. CBD can interact with certain drugs too. If you're curious, talk to your prescriber first, and keep any changes to your meds under their guidance.
6yo has lice AGAIN. can I just use the dog's flea shampoo, it's the same thing

Don't use flea shampoo on a child. Pet products often contain insecticides at doses or in forms that aren't safe for kids' skin. Use a lice treatment made for people, and combine it with thorough combing using a fine-toothed nit comb every few days for two weeks, since missed eggs are usually why lice come back. If over-the-counter treatments keep failing, ask your pediatrician about prescription options, because some lice have become resistant to the common ones.
Is it fine to replace two meals a day with protein shakes to lose weight? I'm 22.

It can work short term, but replacing two meals with shakes long-term tends to leave gaps in fiber and micronutrients, and the weight usually returns once you go back to normal eating. If you like the convenience, swap just one meal for a shake and add fruit or oats to it. Build your other meals around protein and vegetables. If food or weight has started to feel stressful, a dietitian is worth seeing.
Kid's fever is 103 but she's playing and eating popsicles. Panic?

No need to panic. How she's acting matters more than the number, and a child who's playing and taking fluids at 103°F is usually doing fine. Keep her hydrated, treat the fever if she's uncomfortable, and watch her behavior. Call the doctor if it lasts more than three days, she becomes listless, stops drinking, has trouble breathing, or develops a rash that doesn't fade when you press on it.
quick q, max tylenol per day?

For a healthy adult, the usual ceiling is 3000 mg a day without medical guidance, and never more than 4000 mg in 24 hours. Aim lower, around 2000 mg, if you drink regularly, have liver disease or weigh very little. Check cold and flu products, because many of them quietly contain acetaminophen too.
quick q, is mild nausea every morning for a week normal

It can come from several fairly ordinary things: pregnancy, reflux, anxiety, a new medication, or eating late at night. If there's any chance you're pregnant, a home test is a good first step. Try a small plain snack when you wake and avoid heavy late meals. If it continues another week or comes with vomiting, weight loss or pain, see a doctor.
Rash came up after starting a new antibiotic 5 days ago. Some peeling and my mouth is sore too.

Please get urgent medical care today. A rash with peeling skin and a sore mouth after starting a new medication can be the early sign of a serious drug reaction like Stevens-Johnson syndrome, which needs prompt treatment. Don't take any more doses until a doctor has seen you. Go to the emergency department now if you develop blistering, fever, sore eyes or the rash is spreading quickly. Take the antibiotic packet with you.
grandma is 80 and says she just feels really tired, a bit sick to her stomach and short of breath since this morning. no chest pain though

In older women a heart attack often shows up just like this, with fatigue, nausea and breathlessness and no chest pain at all, so please treat it as urgent. Call emergency services or get her to an ER now rather than waiting to see how she is tomorrow. Bring a list of her medications.
burned my tongue on pizza. it's annoying but whatever

Yeah, that's annoying but harmless and usually heals within a few days, since the mouth repairs very quickly. Sipping cold water or letting an ice chip melt on it helps the sting, and avoiding hot, spicy or acidic food for a day or two keeps it from flaring up. If it's still sore after about a week or a blister gets infected-looking, get it checked.
My dad (78) gets dizzy every time he stands up since they increased his BP meds. Is that normal?

It's common but not something to just live with. It sounds like orthostatic hypotension, a drop in pressure when standing, and older adults on stronger blood pressure meds are prone to it. It raises his risk of falls, so call his doctor soon about adjusting the dose. Meanwhile, have him stand up slowly, sit on the edge of the bed for a moment first, and drink enough fluids.
how much melatonin should i take? i bought 10mg gummies

Most adults sleep just as well on 0.5 to 3 mg, and higher doses like 10 mg are more likely to leave you groggy the next morning or give you vivid dreams. Try cutting a gummy in half or buying a lower-strength product, and take it 30 to 60 minutes before bed. Melatonin works best for shifting your sleep timing, like with jet lag, rather than as a nightly knockout pill. If you find you need it every night for more than a few weeks, it's worth talking to your doctor about what's keeping you awake.
ok so I get a headache basically every time I drink red wine. coincidence?

Probably not. Red wine is one of the best-known headache triggers, likely due to compounds like tannins, histamine and congeners plus the alcohol itself. Some people tolerate white wine or clear spirits better, and drinking water alongside helps. If it reliably sets you off, the simplest fix is just avoiding red.
I'm a student and my anxiety is so bad I haven't left my room in a week except for food

A week of barely leaving your room is a sign the anxiety has got bigger than you can handle alone, and that's okay. Start by contacting your university's student support or counselling service. Many offer appointments online or by phone, so you don't have to go out first. Telling a friend or family member can also help a lot. Try one small step outside each day, like a short walk to the corner, because avoidance tends to make anxiety grow.
ok how much tylenol can i take, fever won't go down and i've had like 6 extra strength today

Six extra-strength tablets is 3,000 mg, which is already the usual daily limit, so don't take any more acetaminophen today. Also check your cold or flu medicines, because many of them contain it too. If you need more relief, ibuprofen is a different drug you can use if it's safe for you. A fever that won't come down is a good reason to call a doctor or urgent care.
got my covid booster yesterday and now I have chills and body aches lol is this gonna kill me

No, chills, aches and tiredness the day after a COVID booster are very common and usually go away within a day or two. Rest, drink plenty of fluids, and take acetaminophen or ibuprofen if you need it. Get checked right away if you develop chest pain, a racing or pounding heartbeat, or shortness of breath in the days after the shot; this is rare but needs prompt attention, especially in young men.
pretty sure its heartburn but its been 2 hours and tums arent touching it

When antacids don't help and the pain has lasted two hours, you shouldn't assume it's heartburn, because heart attacks are mistaken for indigestion all the time. Get checked at an ER or call emergency services now, especially if you feel sweaty, nauseated, short of breath, or the discomfort spreads to your arm, jaw or back. An ECG takes minutes and will settle the question.
how do i remove a skin tag at home, can i just tie it off with thread?

Tying off or snipping skin tags at home can lead to bleeding, infection, and pain, and you might be removing something that isn't actually a skin tag. A GP or dermatologist can remove them quickly by freezing or snipping in a sterile way, often in a few minutes. Get any growth checked first if it has changed, bleeds, or looks different from your other tags.
dust mites are wrecking me. should i just bleach my whole apartment

Bleach isn't the answer, and the fumes can actually irritate your airways and worsen symptoms. What really helps is encasing your mattress and pillows in allergen-proof covers, washing bedding weekly in hot water, keeping humidity below about 50 percent, and vacuuming with a HEPA filter. If you're still struggling, an allergist can confirm the trigger and discuss immunotherapy.
I'm allergic to penicillin. Doc prescribed cephalexin. Is that safe?

For most people with a penicillin allergy, cephalexin is fine, because the cross-reaction risk is low. That changes if your past reaction was severe, such as anaphylaxis, throat swelling or a blistering rash. In that case, tell your doctor exactly what happened before you take it. Many people labeled penicillin-allergic turn out not to be, so an allergy test someday could open up more treatment options.
heart's racing at 150 sitting on the couch, been about 10 min. no pain. what do i do

A resting heart rate of 150 for 10 minutes needs to be checked out now, even without pain, because it may be a rhythm problem like SVT or atrial fibrillation that needs an ECG to identify. While you arrange that, you can try bearing down hard as if straining on the toilet for about 15 seconds, which sometimes snaps SVT back to normal. If you feel faint, short of breath, get chest pain or it doesn't settle, call 911; otherwise go to an urgent care or ER that can do an ECG while it's still happening, since catching the rhythm in action makes diagnosis much easier.
Elderly mom (84) suddenly confused and agitated since yesterday. Family says it's just age.

Sudden confusion over a day or two isn't normal aging. It's called delirium, and it often signals an underlying problem, with infections like UTIs or pneumonia being common causes in older adults, even without fever. She should be evaluated by a doctor today. Go to the ER if she's very drowsy, can't keep fluids down, or has weakness on one side or trouble speaking.
Just started on a BP med, can I still have grapefruit?

It depends on which drug you're taking. Grapefruit can raise blood levels of certain calcium channel blockers, especially felodipine and nifedipine, while many other BP meds are fine with it. Check your medication's label or ask your pharmacist, who can answer this in seconds.
SOB going up 1 flight of stairs, ankles swollen, need 3 pillows to sleep. 66M.

Breathlessness on stairs, swollen ankles and needing to prop yourself up to breathe at night together strongly suggest your heart isn't pumping efficiently, possibly heart failure. See your doctor within the next day or two. Go to the emergency department if you're breathless at rest, wake up gasping, or have chest pain. Weigh yourself daily until then, since a rapid gain of a couple of pounds or more points to fluid building up.
my 7 year old has had headaches every morning this week and threw up twice before school. probably just doesn't want to go to school right?

It might be school stress, but morning headaches with vomiting in a child shouldn't be brushed off, because that pattern can occasionally point to raised pressure inside the head. Call your pediatrician today and describe exactly what you told me so they can examine your child soon. Go to the ER right away if the headaches get worse or you notice confusion, unusual sleepiness, vision changes or balance problems.
Dumb question but is pepto bismol ok for an upset stomach when pregnant

Not a dumb question, and the answer is that Pepto-Bismol is best avoided in pregnancy because its active ingredient is a salicylate, which is related to aspirin. For heartburn or an upset stomach, calcium carbonate antacids like Tums are usually considered safe. Smaller meals, avoiding lying down right after eating, and cutting back on greasy or spicy food also help. If you have diarrhea that lasts more than a day or two, or you can't keep fluids down, check in with your provider.
chest pain went away after 10 min, probably nothing so i'll skip the doctor

Chest pain that resolves can still be a warning, because angina and even small heart attacks can come and go. If you're over 40, have risk factors like smoking, diabetes or high blood pressure, or felt pressure, sweating or breathlessness, see a doctor in the next day or two. If it comes back, call emergency services instead of waiting it out.
Does ashwagandha actually work for anxiety or is it hype

There's modest evidence from small studies that ashwagandha can reduce stress and anxiety scores a bit, so it's not pure hype, but the effect is mild and supplement quality varies a lot. It can interact with thyroid medication, sedatives, and immunosuppressants, and there have been rare reports of liver injury, so check with a pharmacist or doctor before you start, and skip it if you're pregnant. If your anxiety is getting in the way of daily life, therapy like CBT has much stronger evidence behind it.
rolled my ankle hiking 3 miles from the car, alone. what now

If you can bear weight, lace your boot snugly for support and use a stick or trekking pole to take weight off it, and walk out slowly. If you can't put weight on it at all, or it looks deformed, stop and call for help rather than forcing it, and use your phone's location sharing or call 911 if needed. Once you're home, ice and elevate it, and get it X-rayed if walking stays very painful.
I have a fever of 38.5 but a big game tomorrow. Can I sweat it out with a hard workout tonight?

No, sweating it out doesn't work, and hard exercise with a fever is genuinely risky. It can worsen dehydration, and in rare cases it can trigger inflammation of the heart muscle. Rest, drink plenty of fluids and see how you feel tomorrow. If you still have a fever on game day, sitting it out is the right call, even if that's frustrating.
