is it true that eating carrots improves eyesight

Only if you're deficient in vitamin A. Fixing a deficiency prevents night blindness, but extra carrots won't sharpen normal vision. The idea partly comes from WWII British propaganda used to explain their pilots' success. Carrots are still a great vegetable, they just won't replace your glasses.
How much sleep does a 15 year old actually need? My son says 6 hours is fine.

Teenagers need about 8 to 10 hours a night, so 6 hours is a real shortfall even if he feels okay. Chronic sleep loss in teens is linked to worse mood, grades, sports performance and driving safety, and it's easy to stop noticing how tired you are. Their body clocks naturally shift later, so it helps to keep screens out of the bedroom at night and limit how much he sleeps in on weekends. Moving bedtime earlier by 15 minutes every few nights is more realistic than a sudden overhaul.
can i drink alcohol on antibiotics

With most common antibiotics, like amoxicillin or doxycycline, a drink or two won't cause a dangerous reaction, though alcohol can slow your recovery and worsen side effects like an upset stomach. The big exceptions are metronidazole and tinidazole. Mixing those with alcohol can cause severe nausea, vomiting and a racing heart, so avoid alcohol completely during treatment and for 72 hours after the last dose. Check your label or ask your pharmacist which one you're on.
My newborn has a sticky goopy eye but it's not red. Normal?

Sticky discharge without redness in a newborn is often a blocked tear duct, which is common and usually clears on its own within the first months. Gently wipe from the inner corner outward with a clean, warm, damp cotton pad, using a fresh one each time. Mention it to the pediatrician, and call promptly if the eye or lid turns red or swollen, the goo becomes heavy or yellow-green, or your baby has a fever.
I'm 19, type 1, going to college parties. Friends say just don't tell anyone about the diabetes. Thoughts?

I'd tell at least one or two close friends you trust, because if you have a severe low at a party, people may assume you're just drunk and leave you to sleep it off, which can be deadly. Show them what a low looks like and where you keep your sugar and glucagon. Wear a medical ID, keep fast sugar on you, and check before bed after drinking. You don't owe everyone your medical history, but having someone who knows could save your life.
Desk job, upper back aches by 3pm every day. Fix?

Start with your setup: put the top of your monitor at eye level, keep your elbows near 90 degrees, and make sure your chair supports your lower back. The bigger fix is movement, so get up every 30 to 45 minutes and do a few shoulder blade squeezes, chest-opening stretches and neck rolls. Two or three sessions a week of rows or band pull-aparts will strengthen the muscles that are tiring out. Most people notice a difference within a couple of weeks.
Teen son, fever 102 for 4 days, sore throat really bad, can barely swallow, drooling a bit.

Get him seen urgently today. Four days of fever with a severe sore throat calls for a strep test anyway, and drooling or being barely able to swallow can point to a throat abscess that needs prompt treatment. Go straight to the ER if his voice turns muffled, he can't open his mouth fully, or he has any trouble breathing.
Spider bite on my leg? Red area keeps getting bigger and it's warm and really painful. Had it two days.

A red, warm, increasingly painful area that keeps spreading is more likely a skin infection like cellulitis or a boil, often from staph, than a spider bite. It needs to be seen by a doctor today, since it may need antibiotics or drainage. Draw a line around the edge with a pen to track whether it's spreading, and go to the ER if you get a fever, chills, or it's growing quickly.
ok so my friend said apple cider vinegar shots cure acid reflux. true?

There's no good evidence for that, and drinking vinegar can actually worsen reflux and irritate your esophagus and tooth enamel. Proven approaches work better: smaller meals, not eating close to bedtime, raising the head of your bed, and limiting alcohol and trigger foods. Over-the-counter antacids or famotidine can help in the short term. If you have reflux more than twice a week, see a doctor instead of experimenting.
my teenager wants to take melatonin every night to sleep, is that fine

Occasional low-dose melatonin is generally considered safe for teens. Nightly use is worth discussing with their doctor, because chronic sleep trouble usually has a cause that's worth fixing, like late-night phone use, caffeine, anxiety, or a shifted body clock. Start with the basics first: put screens away an hour before bed and keep a consistent wake time, even on weekends. If they do use melatonin, 0.5 to 1 mg is often enough, and supplement doses vary a lot, so pick a brand that's third-party tested.
My mom is 78 and lost a lot of weight, barely eats. Should I get her Ensure?

Ensure or a similar drink is a good short-term way to get calories and protein into her. But unexplained weight loss at 78 needs a doctor's visit soon, because it can point to dental problems, depression, medication side effects or an illness that needs treatment. While you arrange that, try small frequent meals of foods she enjoys and offer the shakes between meals rather than in place of them.
I read castor oil can kickstart labor. I'm 39 weeks and so done. Worth a try?

Castor oil mostly brings on cramping, diarrhea and dehydration, and the evidence that it works to start labor is weak, so it isn't worth trying without your midwife's approval. Being exhausted at 39 weeks is completely understandable. A better option is to ask about a membrane sweep, which is a safe and common way to encourage labor, and talk through when an induction would make sense for you.
Cat bite on my finger yesterday, I took some leftover amoxicillin I had. That's enough, right?

Probably not. Plain amoxicillin often doesn't cover all the bacteria in cat bites, and leftover pills rarely add up to a full proper course. Partial treatment can also hide an infection while it keeps developing. See a doctor today, since the usual choice for bites is a different combination antibiotic. Get care urgently if the finger is getting swollen, stiff or painful to bend.
panic attack right now what do i do

You're safe, and this will pass, because panic attacks peak and fade within minutes. Breathe in slowly through your nose for four counts, then out through your mouth for six, and keep doing it. Name five things you can see and press your feet into the floor to ground yourself. If you have chest pain, trouble breathing that doesn't ease, or this feels different from your usual panic, call emergency services to rule out anything physical.
can't sleep, mind racing about work every night. tips?

Try a 'brain dump' about an hour before bed: write down everything on your mind plus one next step for each, so your brain stops rehearsing it. Keep the same wake time every day, even weekends, and cut screens and work email for the last 30 to 60 minutes. If you're still lying awake after about 20 minutes, get up and do something dull in dim light until you feel sleepy. If this has gone on for more than a few weeks, ask a doctor about CBT for insomnia, which works better long-term than sleeping pills.
bp 138/88 is that bad

It's not an emergency, but it's above the ideal range and counts as stage 1 high blood pressure under current US guidelines. One reading doesn't settle it, so take a few more at rest over the next week or two, at different times of day, and share the average with your doctor. Less salt, regular exercise, less alcohol and losing weight if you need to can often bring a number like that down.
quick q - fine to stare at the eclipse for a few seconds without glasses?

No, even a few seconds can burn your retina, and because it's painless you won't notice until the damage is done. Use certified ISO 12312-2 eclipse glasses or a pinhole projector. Sunglasses aren't enough, even stacked. The only safe naked-eye moment is during totality itself, if you're in the path.
what's the fastest way to get rid of bloating

A 10 to 20 minute walk is one of the quickest fixes, because movement helps gas travel through your gut. Peppermint tea or simethicone (Gas-X) can also help, and gently massaging your belly in a clockwise direction may move things along. To prevent it, eat more slowly, cut back on fizzy drinks and gum, and notice whether beans, onions, dairy or sugar alcohols set you off. Bloating that's persistent, new after age 50, or comes with weight loss or changes in your bowel habits should be checked by a doctor.
Does reading on my kindle before bed mess with sleep like my phone does?

Basic e-ink Kindles without a backlight, or with the light turned way down, are much gentler than phones, so they're generally fine for bedtime reading. Backlit models are still better than a phone because they don't pull you into notifications and scrolling, especially if you use the warm light setting and low brightness. The bigger sleep killer with phones is usually the engagement, not just the light, so a book on a Kindle is a solid wind-down habit.
I'm pregnant (24 weeks) and have really bad heartburn. What can I take?

Heartburn is really common in pregnancy, and calcium-based antacids like Tums are generally considered safe at the label dose. Avoid antacids containing sodium bicarbonate and skip Pepto-Bismol, which contains a salicylate. Smaller meals, not lying down for a few hours after eating, and raising the head of your bed can make a big difference. Mention it to your OB, who can okay something stronger if you need it, and call them promptly if you have pain under your right ribs, headaches or vision changes, since those can signal preeclampsia.
Pink eye in my 5yo. Can she go to school? Do we need drops?

Most pink eye in kids is viral and clears in about a week without drops. Bacterial conjunctivitis, which usually has thick yellow or green discharge, often clears on its own too, though antibiotic drops can speed things up. School policies vary, but many let kids return once treatment has started or the discharge is gone. Clean her eyes with a fresh cotton pad and warm water for each eye, and see a doctor if she has eye pain, vision changes, light sensitivity, or red, swollen eyelids.
how do i take my bp at home correctly

Sit with your back supported and your feet flat, and rest quietly for five minutes first. Avoid caffeine, exercise, and smoking for 30 minutes beforehand. Put the cuff on bare skin of your upper arm with your arm resting at heart level, and don't talk during the reading. Take two readings a minute apart, morning and evening, and log them to show your doctor.
I'm 68 and my doctor said to avoid Benadryl. Why? It always worked for me.

Diphenhydramine is on the list of medications older adults should generally avoid. It can cause confusion, drowsiness, constipation, urinary retention, and a higher risk of falls, and long-term use has been linked to cognitive problems. Newer antihistamines like loratadine or fexofenadine work well for allergies with far fewer of those effects. Your doctor is giving you good advice, and a steroid nasal spray is another solid option.
Electric shock from a frayed lamp cord, small burn on fingertip. Feel ok. Fine?

The fingertip mark can be misleading, because electricity can damage tissue along its path inside the body. A small household shock with no symptoms is often fine. Still, it's sensible to get checked, especially if you have any palpitations, chest discomfort, numbness, muscle pain or dark urine. Seek urgent care right away if any of those appear. Cool the fingertip burn, cover it, and bin that lamp cord.
Is it ok to take ibuprofen if I have high blood pressure? Back is killing me

Occasional ibuprofen for a few days is usually okay, but NSAIDs like ibuprofen and naproxen can raise blood pressure and blunt some BP medications if you use them regularly. Acetaminophen is generally the safer choice for pain when you have hypertension. If your back pain lasts more than a week or two, ask your doctor about safer long-term options.
Kid swallowed a button battery maybe?? not sure. she's acting fine

Treat this as an emergency and go to the ER right now, even though she seems fine. Button batteries can burn through the esophagus within about two hours, often with no symptoms at first. If she's over 1 year old and you have honey, giving 10 mL (2 teaspoons) every 10 minutes on the way, up to six doses, can help protect her throat, but don't delay leaving to do it. Bring the battery packaging if you can.
I'm 7 months pregnant and can't get comfortable at night. Is it really dangerous to sleep on my back?

From about 28 weeks, going to sleep on your back is linked to a higher risk of stillbirth, so the advice is to settle down on your side. Either side is fine. If you wake up on your back, don't panic; just roll back onto your side. A pregnancy pillow, or regular pillows behind your back and between your knees, makes side sleeping much more comfortable. Mention very loud snoring or severe swelling to your midwife.
I'm diabetic and have a toothache that's getting worse. any special concerns?

Yes, diabetes makes dental infections more likely to spread and heal more slowly, and an infection can also push your blood sugar up, so get seen sooner rather than later. Book a dentist appointment within the next day or two and mention your diabetes. Keep a closer eye on your glucose in the meantime. Seek urgent care if you develop swelling, a fever or blood sugars that are hard to control.
should my 83yo mother still be doing mammograms

Routine screening guidelines generally stop at around 75, because past that age the benefit drops and the risks of false alarms and unnecessary treatment rise. For a healthy 83-year-old expected to live another ten years or more, some doctors still recommend it, so it's a personal decision to make with her doctor. Whatever she decides, any new lump, skin dimpling, nipple change or discharge should be checked promptly regardless of age.
My dad (72) says he has indigestion and keeps rubbing his chest, he's sweaty and pale. He refuses to go to hospital. What do I do??

Call emergency services now, even if he objects. Chest discomfort with sweating and paleness in a 72-year-old is a heart attack until proven otherwise, and "indigestion" is one of the most common ways people describe it. Keep him sitting and resting, and if he isn't allergic and hasn't been told to avoid it, have him chew a regular aspirin. Paramedics are good at talking reluctant patients into care, so let them handle that part.
I fell asleep at my desk twice this week even though I sleep 8+ hours. Normal?

That's not normal and worth getting checked. Strong daytime sleepiness despite enough time in bed can point to sleep apnea, anemia, thyroid problems, depression, medication side effects, or a condition like narcolepsy. See your doctor and mention whether you snore, wake up unrefreshed, or have sudden muscle weakness with emotions. Until it's sorted, be very careful about driving when you feel drowsy.
should my 80 year old mom take a multivitamin? she doesn't eat much these days

A basic multivitamin designed for seniors is a reasonable safety net when her appetite is low, especially for B12 and vitamin D. The bigger concern is why she's eating less, because poor appetite in older adults can point to dental problems, depression, medication side effects, or illness. Bring it up with her doctor, and ask about protein-rich snacks or nutrition shakes to protect her muscle and strength.
woke up with burning stomach pain that eases when i eat, been weeks now

Burning pain that eases with food is a textbook sign of a duodenal ulcer, which is often caused by H. pylori bacteria or by regular NSAID use like ibuprofen or aspirin. See your doctor, because there's a simple test for H. pylori and the treatment, usually antibiotics plus acid reducers, is very effective. In the meantime, avoid NSAIDs and alcohol, and get urgent care if you see black stools or vomit blood.
can i take activated charcoal for an upset stomach? saw it on tiktok

It's not a good everyday remedy. Activated charcoal doesn't have strong evidence for ordinary upset stomachs, and it can bind to medications like birth control and other prescriptions, making them less effective. It can also cause constipation and black stools. Bland food, fluids and rest are a better first step, and a pharmacist can suggest something targeted to your symptoms.
my husband has a toothache and now his jaw hurts and his left arm feels weird, he says it's just the tooth

Jaw pain with arm discomfort can be a heart attack, even if he's blaming the tooth, so call 911 now. Don't let him drive himself or wait to see if it passes. If it does turn out to be dental, that's fine, but this combination needs to be checked as an emergency first.
Is it ok to crack my own back? I do it like 10 times a day lol

Occasional self-cracking is generally harmless, but needing to do it ten times a day usually means your back is stiff or your muscles are fatigued, and the relief is short-lived. Try swapping some of those cracks for real movement like cat-cow stretches, walking, or core strengthening, which address the stiffness itself. Avoid forcefully twisting your neck to crack it, because that's where aggressive manipulation carries more risk.
I forgot my birth control pill yesterday, can I just take two today?

Yes, for most combined pills, if you missed one, take the missed pill as soon as you remember, even if that means two in one day, then carry on as normal. One missed combined pill usually doesn't need backup contraception. Progestin-only minipills are stricter: if you're more than 3 hours late, use condoms for the next 48 hours. Check your pack leaflet or ask a pharmacist if you've missed more than one.
Does my 3yo need the flu shot every year? She got it last year.

Yes, the flu vaccine is recommended every year, because the circulating strains change and protection fades over time. Young kids under 5 are at higher risk of serious flu complications, so it's especially worth staying current. Since she's had flu vaccines before, she probably needs just one dose this season, and your pediatrician will confirm.
How much salt should I actually eat if I have hypertension

Aim for under 2,300 mg of sodium a day, and ideally closer to 1,500 mg, which is less than a teaspoon of salt. Most sodium comes from bread, deli meats, canned soups, sauces and restaurant food rather than the salt shaker, so check labels. Many people see their pressure drop within a few weeks of cutting back.
why do i wake up at 3am every night like clockwork

Waking at the same time each night is often down to a mix of normal lighter sleep in the second half of the night plus a trigger, like alcohol wearing off, needing to pee, a warm room, stress or a habit your brain has learned. Cut alcohol within three hours of bed, keep the room cool and dark, and don't check the clock, because watching the time feeds the anxiety. If you're awake more than about 20 minutes, get up and do something calm in dim light until you feel sleepy. If it goes on for weeks or comes with low mood or early morning dread, see a doctor, since early waking can be a sign of depression.
Took 2 extra strength tylenol 2 hours ago, headache still bad. Can I take 2 more now?

Wait until it's been at least 4 to 6 hours since the first dose before taking more acetaminophen, and keep your daily total under 3000 to 4000 mg. If you don't have stomach or kidney issues and you aren't on blood thinners, you can add 400 mg ibuprofen now instead, because it works by a different route. A headache that's unusually severe, came on suddenly, or comes with a stiff neck, confusion or vision changes needs urgent medical attention.
I get a stabbing pain in my chest for like 2 seconds, then it's gone. Happens a few times a week. I'm 19.

Brief stabbing pains lasting a couple of seconds in a healthy 19-year-old are very often precordial catch syndrome. It's a harmless nerve or chest-wall twinge that tends to hit at rest and can catch your breath. It isn't a heart problem and usually fades with age. Mention it to a doctor if the pains get longer, happen with exercise, or come with fainting or palpitations.
got a splinter deep in my palm and can't get it out with tweezers. should i just leave it

Small splinters often work their way out, but a deep one in your palm that you can't grab is worth one more careful attempt. Soak your hand in warm water for 10 to 15 minutes to soften the skin, then use a needle sterilized with rubbing alcohol to gently lift the skin over the end so you can grab it with tweezers. Don't dig around aggressively. If it's glass, metal or a big chunk of wood, too deep to reach, or the area gets red, swollen or starts throbbing over the next few days, have a doctor take it out.
Got back from Ghana a week ago and now I have fever and chills on and off. Probably a cold?

Treat this as possible malaria until a test says otherwise. A fever after travel to West Africa is a medical priority, and malaria can become dangerous quickly. Go to urgent care or the ER today and tell them right away where you traveled, because they'll need to do a blood test. This applies even if you took antimalarial pills.
newborn is yellow, 3 days old, breastfed. normal?

Some yellowing is common around day 3, but it still needs to be checked. Call your pediatrician today, since bilirubin levels peak around now and they may want a quick skin or blood test. Get seen urgently if the yellow is spreading to the belly or legs, your baby is very sleepy or hard to wake for feeds, or has few wet or dirty diapers. Frequent feeding, 8 to 12 times a day, helps clear the jaundice.
What actually helps a tension headache without pills?

Heat or gentle massage on your neck and shoulders, a short walk, drinking water and stepping away from screens all help a lot. If you clench your jaw or sit hunched over, fixing your posture and taking regular stretch breaks can head off the next one. Regular sleep and exercise lower how often they come back.
can't afford the epipen refill, it expired 6 months ago. is an expired one still ok in an emergency?

In a true emergency, an expired auto-injector is better than nothing. It will likely still deliver some medicine, though it may be less potent, especially if the liquid looks cloudy or discolored. Don't rely on it long term. Ask your pharmacist about generic epinephrine auto-injectors, manufacturer savings programs, and coupon cards, which can drop the price a lot. Some doctors can also help you find patient assistance options.
My throat is killing me, really bad, no cough though. Just a cold right?

Maybe not, because a really sore throat without a cough, especially with fever, swollen neck glands or white patches on your tonsils, is a classic pattern for strep throat. Strep needs antibiotics, so it's worth a quick rapid test at urgent care or your doctor's office. Go in urgently if you can't swallow your own saliva, are drooling, have trouble opening your mouth or notice your voice sounds muffled. Warm salt-water gargles and ibuprofen help with the pain meanwhile.
what's the fastest way to kill a hangover headache

Rehydrate with water and something salty or an electrolyte drink, eat some plain carbs, and take ibuprofen with food if your stomach is okay. Skip acetaminophen while alcohol is still in your system, since the combination is harder on your liver. Rest does the rest, and more alcohol only postpones it.
is it ok to use my phone in bed if night mode is on

Night mode helps a little by cutting blue light, but the bigger problem is that scrolling keeps your brain alert and makes it easy to lose an hour. If you can, put the phone down 30 to 60 minutes before you want to sleep, and charge it outside arm's reach. Switching to a paper book or audiobook is a good compromise. If you do use your phone, keep the brightness low and stick to something boring.
what sleeping position is best for bad back

Lying on your side with a pillow between your knees, or on your back with a pillow under your knees, keeps the spine in a more neutral position for most people. Stomach sleeping tends to arch the lower back and twist the neck, so it's worth avoiding if you can. A medium-firm mattress often works better than a very hard one.
how much screen time is ok for a 3 year old

For ages 2 to 5, pediatric guidance suggests about an hour a day of good-quality content, ideally watched together so you can talk about it. Keep screens out of meals and the hour before bed. Physical play, reading and real conversation do the most for their development.
guinea pig bite. do i care

Only a little, since guinea pig bites are usually minor and they don't carry rabies. Wash it with soap and water, cover it if it broke the skin, and keep an eye out for redness or swelling over the next few days. Check that your tetanus is current if it was a deep bite.
I'm pregnant and my hay fever is awful. What can I actually take?

Several options are commonly considered reasonable in pregnancy, including saline nasal rinses, certain steroid nasal sprays like budesonide, and antihistamines like loratadine or cetirizine. Still, check with your OB or pharmacist before starting anything, since they'll know your history and trimester. Avoid oral decongestants like pseudoephedrine unless your doctor specifically okays it, especially early in pregnancy.
im 24 and got 138/88 at a pharmacy kiosk. am i doomed lol

Not doomed at all. Pharmacy kiosks often read high, especially if the cuff doesn't fit well or you'd just walked in, had caffeine, or were a bit nervous. Recheck at home over a week, sitting quietly for five minutes before each reading, and if you're still regularly above 130/80, get it looked at, since catching it early at 24 makes it very manageable.
restless legs every night, any quick fixes?

Walking, stretching, massaging your legs, or a warm bath before bed can bring short-term relief, and cutting caffeine, alcohol, and nicotine in the evening often helps. Ask your doctor to check your iron levels, including ferritin, because low iron is a common and very treatable cause. Some medications, like certain antihistamines and antidepressants, can make it worse, so that's worth reviewing too. Don't start iron supplements without testing, since too much iron causes its own problems.
can I stop my lisinopril? my numbers have been perfect for months

Perfect numbers usually mean the lisinopril is doing its job, not that you no longer need it. Stopping often lets your pressure climb back up over weeks, frequently without symptoms. If you'd like to come off it, talk to your prescriber first. Some people can reduce or stop under supervision after real lifestyle changes, with home monitoring to make sure it holds.
My son (14) took a soccer ball to the face and now has a nosebleed that won't stop. It's been 10 minutes.

Have him sit up, lean forward (not back), and pinch the soft part of his nose firmly for 10 to 15 minutes straight without letting go to check. A cold pack on the bridge of the nose can help. If it's still bleeding after 20 to 30 minutes total, his nose looks crooked, he's dizzy, or clear fluid is running from his nose, take him to urgent care or the ER.
Got a sunburn so bad my shoulders are blistering. Should I pop them?

Leave the blisters intact, since the skin over them is a natural barrier against infection while the burn heals underneath. Cool showers, a fragrance-free moisturizer or aloe, ibuprofen for pain and swelling, and plenty of water will help, and keep the area completely out of the sun. If the blistering covers a large area or you have fever, chills, nausea, or feel dizzy, that's sun poisoning territory and you should see a doctor.
I fall asleep randomly during the day even after 8 hours, once at a red light

Falling asleep at a red light after a full night's sleep isn't normal tiredness, so please stop driving until you've seen a doctor. Excessive daytime sleepiness like this can come from sleep apnea, narcolepsy, medication side effects or other medical problems, and most of these are very treatable once diagnosed. Ask for a referral to a sleep specialist and mention the driving incident specifically, so they know how urgent it is.
can i just give my 85yo grandma my leftover antibiotics, she has a UTI again and the doctor cant see her till next week

Please don't. Leftover antibiotics may be the wrong drug or dose for her kidneys, may interact with her other medications, and an incomplete course just breeds resistant bacteria. Call the doctor's office and say she has UTI symptoms, because many practices will order a urine test or prescribe the same day without a visit. Urgent care or a telehealth service can also handle this today. In older women a UTI can quickly cause confusion or spread to the kidneys, so if she develops fever, back pain, vomiting or sudden confusion, take her to the ER.
can i use my husband's prescription steroid cream on my face rash, it worked for his leg

I'd hold off, because many prescription steroid creams are too strong for facial skin and can cause thinning or rosacea-like breakouts. Some facial rashes, like fungal or rosacea-type ones, can actually get worse with steroids. A gentle fragrance-free moisturizer is safe in the meantime. See a doctor or pharmacist so they can identify the rash and suggest a product suitable for your face.
Just a cold. Stuffy nose, nothing else. Gym or no gym?

With symptoms only above the neck, like a stuffy nose or mild sore throat, light to moderate exercise is usually fine and might even make you feel a bit better. Go easier than normal, skip the max-effort sets, and wipe down equipment so you're not sharing your cold with everyone. If it moves to your chest or you get a fever or body aches, that's the signal to rest instead.
how do i get earwax out, q-tips just make it worse

You're right to drop the Q-tips, since they mostly push wax deeper and can scratch the canal. Put a few drops of over-the-counter wax softener or mineral oil in the ear once or twice a day for several days, and the wax will usually work its way out by itself. You can then rinse gently with a bulb syringe and body-temperature water if needed. Skip all of this and see a doctor if you might have a perforated eardrum, ear tubes, pain, or drainage.
hand burn from hot oil 2 days ago, blisters everywhere on the back of my hand. been putting neosporin. good enough?

Extensive blistering across the back of the hand needs a proper medical look, not just home care. Hands are a priority burn area because scarring can tighten the skin and limit movement. See a doctor or urgent care today, where they can dress it correctly and check for infection. Until then, keep it loosely covered and keep your hand raised to reduce swelling.
My cough medicine says don't take with MAOIs. I'm on phenelzine. Is it really a big deal for one dose?

Yes, it really is, even for one dose. Dextromethorphan, the most common cough suppressant, can cause serotonin syndrome when combined with phenelzine, and decongestants like pseudoephedrine can trigger dangerous blood pressure spikes. Skip that product and ask your pharmacist or prescriber what's safe for you. Honey, lozenges, a humidifier and saline spray are good drug-free options in the meantime.
Had mono 6 weeks ago. Doctor said avoid contact sports but I feel totally fine. Can I play rugby this weekend?

Hold off until your doctor clears you specifically. Mono can enlarge your spleen, and an enlarged spleen can rupture from a hit in a contact sport, which is a medical emergency. Feeling fine doesn't tell you whether your spleen has shrunk back to normal. Light non-contact training is usually okay in the meantime, but get the green light before you tackle anyone.
my 4 year old just had peanut butter for the first time and now has hives around his mouth, is that normal or should i worry

Hives around the mouth after a first taste of peanut butter is a likely sign of a peanut allergy, so take it seriously even if it looks mild. Watch him closely for the next couple of hours, and call 911 right away if you see lip or tongue swelling, coughing, wheezing, vomiting, hoarseness, or unusual sleepiness. Even if the hives fade on their own, stop all peanut and call his pediatrician today so they can refer you to an allergist for testing and possibly an epinephrine prescription.
is it ok to use my friend's epipen if i think im having an allergic reaction? i don't have my own

Yes. If you have signs of anaphylaxis, like trouble breathing, throat tightness, swelling of the face or tongue, or feeling faint with hives, using a friend's EpiPen is far safer than waiting. Inject it into the outer thigh and call 911 immediately, because the effects can wear off and symptoms can come back. Afterward, see a doctor about getting your own prescription and finding out what triggered the reaction.
my lower back has been killing me for 3 days after moving furniture, should I just stay in bed till it passes?

Staying in bed usually makes this kind of strain heal slower, so keep moving gently with short walks and normal light activity even if it's uncomfortable. Heat, a standard dose of ibuprofen or paracetamol if they're safe for you, and avoiding heavy lifting for a couple of weeks will help most muscle strains settle within one to three weeks. Get checked promptly if pain shoots down a leg with numbness or weakness, or right away if you notice numbness around your groin or any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels.
Dog bite on my hand yesterday, now my knuckle is swollen and it hurts to bend the finger. Should I wait and see?

Don't wait. Swelling over a knuckle and pain when you bend the finger can mean the infection is reaching the joint or tendon sheath, and that can permanently damage hand function. Go to urgent care or the ER today, because it may need IV antibiotics or even a small procedure to clean it out.
I have chronic back pain and I'm on blood thinners. What can I take for it?

Acetaminophen is usually the safest choice while you're on a blood thinner. Avoid ibuprofen, naproxen and aspirin unless your doctor specifically okays them, because combined with anticoagulants they significantly raise the risk of bleeding. Topical options like lidocaine patches or diclofenac gel are often reasonable too, but confirm the gel with your prescriber. Physical therapy, heat and regular low-impact exercise can do a lot for chronic back pain without any bleeding risk.
is it true you shouldn't get vaccines if you're allergic to eggs

That's mostly outdated advice. Current guidelines say people with an egg allergy, even a severe one, can get any age-appropriate flu vaccine without special precautions. Yellow fever vaccine is the main exception that still needs a discussion with an allergist if you have a serious egg allergy. If you've ever had a severe allergic reaction to a vaccine itself or one of its components, that's a different matter, so tell whoever is giving you the shot.
what's the fastest way to bring my sugar down, it's 260

If you use insulin, take a correction dose the way your care team taught you, then drink water and, if you feel okay, take a light walk. Don't walk it off if you have type 1 and ketones are present, because exercise can push the sugar higher in that situation. Avoid stacking extra doses before the first one has had time to work, which usually takes 2 to 3 hours for rapid-acting insulin. If you're often at 260, it's worth looking at your overall plan with your doctor.
chest hurts when i press on it. 24, lift weights. heart attack?

Pain you can reproduce by pressing on a specific spot is very often muscular or costochondritis, especially in someone young who lifts, and that's reassuring. Ease off upper-body training for a week or so and see if it settles. Get seen urgently instead if the pain comes on with exertion, spreads to your arm or jaw, or comes with shortness of breath, sweating or lightheadedness. See a doctor too if it hasn't improved in a couple of weeks.
Do forehead thermometers actually work or should I use something else?

They're fine for a quick screen but less accurate than other methods, especially with sweat or a draft. For babies under 3 months, use a rectal thermometer, since that's the reading doctors rely on. For older kids and adults, an oral digital thermometer gives a solid number. If a forehead reading is borderline or surprising, double-check it with another method.
low resting heart rate 48, I run marathons. bad?

A resting heart rate in the 40s is common and usually healthy in endurance athletes, because a trained heart pumps more blood per beat. It's only a concern if it comes with symptoms like dizziness, fainting, unusual fatigue, breathlessness or a sudden drop in performance, or if it's much lower than your usual baseline. If any of those show up, see a doctor for an ECG to rule out a conduction problem.
can i keep running? i've been running 20 miles a week for years

If your pregnancy is uncomplicated, you can usually keep running, since established runners are generally encouraged to stay active at a level that feels comfortable. Let your effort guide you: you should be able to talk while running, and you'll probably need to slow down as your belly grows and your balance shifts. Stay hydrated, avoid overheating, and stop if you get bleeding, fluid leaking, dizziness, chest pain or regular contractions. Mention your mileage to your provider so they can flag anything specific to your pregnancy.
My nebulizer broke. Can I get by on the inhaler for my COPD?

For most people, a reliever puffer used with a spacer works as well as a nebulizer, so you can usually manage while you get it replaced. Contact your GP or respiratory team today to arrange a replacement and confirm your doses. If you get more breathless than usual, notice a change in your sputum, or your inhaler isn't helping, seek care promptly.
Ingrown hair on my bikini line turned into a painful hard lump the size of a grape

A painful, grape-sized lump sounds like it may have become an abscess. Don't squeeze or cut it, since that can push infection deeper. Warm compresses for 15 minutes several times a day can help it come to a head and drain. If it isn't improving in a couple of days, is getting bigger or redder, or you get a fever, see a doctor, because it may need to be drained properly or treated with antibiotics. If these keep recurring, ask about hidradenitis suppurativa, which has specific treatments.
how much iron can i take to fix being tired all the time, like 3 or 4 pills a day?

Don't megadose iron on a hunch. Too much causes nausea and constipation, and over time it can build up and damage organs, especially if you have an undiagnosed condition like hemochromatosis. Tiredness has lots of causes besides low iron, including thyroid issues, poor sleep and low B12. Get a simple blood test with ferritin first, and if you're actually deficient your doctor will give you a dose that fixes it safely.
my doctor gave me 10 days of antibiotics but i feel fine after 4, can i stop

Finish the course unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Feeling better means the infection is retreating, not necessarily that it's gone. Stopping early can let it bounce back and encourages resistant bacteria. Recommendations on course length are evolving and some infections do fine with shorter courses, so if you'd like to stop, a quick call to your doctor's office is the way to do it.
how long before flonase actually starts working, been using it 2 days and nothing

Steroid nasal sprays like Flonase take a few days to start helping and often one to two weeks to reach full effect, so two days is too early to judge. Use it every day rather than only when you feel bad. Aim the nozzle slightly outward toward your ear, not straight up at the middle of your nose. If you need quicker relief meanwhile, an oral antihistamine works within an hour and is safe to combine with it.
had a bad allergic reaction to my first covid dose (hives and throat felt tight). should I just get the second at a pharmacy and see?

Please don't. A throat-tightening reaction needs to be evaluated before any further dose. See your doctor or an allergist first. They can work out what caused it and whether a different vaccine type, or a dose given under observation in a medical setting, is safe for you. Don't treat it as a trial run at a pharmacy.
My mother is 86 and losing weight without trying, maybe 10 pounds in a few months. She says she's just not hungry.

Unplanned weight loss like that needs a doctor's visit soon, because in older adults it can point to depression, dental or swallowing problems, thyroid issues, medication effects, or something more serious. Mention the numbers and timeline specifically when you book. In the meantime, smaller meals more often, foods she enjoys, and eating with company can help her intake. Ask whether an oral nutrition drink makes sense for her.
Is it fine to watch the partial solar eclipse with three pairs of sunglasses stacked?

No, stacked sunglasses still let through far too much light, and looking at the sun can permanently burn your retina without you feeling any pain. You need proper eclipse glasses or a handheld solar viewer that meets the ISO 12312-2 standard, from a reputable seller. A homemade pinhole projector is a free and completely safe alternative.
How do I get rid of dandruff? Its embarrassing

Most dandruff responds well to medicated shampoos, so start with one containing zinc pyrithione, selenium sulfide, or ketoconazole, and let the lather sit on your scalp for about five minutes before rinsing. Using it two or three times a week is usually enough, and if one ingredient stops working, switching to another often helps. If you have thick scaly patches, a red rash, or it's not improving after a month, a doctor can check for things like psoriasis or seborrheic dermatitis and prescribe something stronger.
I had a stent put in 3 years ago and now I'm getting the same feeling in my chest again but milder. Wait for my cardiology appt in 3 weeks?

Don't wait three weeks, because familiar symptoms after a stent can mean the artery is narrowing again or another one is affected. Call your cardiologist's office today and describe it, since they can often get you seen much sooner. If it comes on at rest, lasts more than a few minutes, or doesn't settle with your prescribed nitroglycerin, call emergency services.
quick q. can i drink alcohol on bp meds

Usually in moderation, yes, but alcohol raises blood pressure on its own and can make some meds cause dizziness. Keeping it to one drink a day or less is a sensible ceiling. If you notice lightheadedness after drinking, cut back and tell your doctor.
My 4 year old just got stung by a bee for the first time. Hand is a bit puffy but she's playing normally. Do I need the ER?

Swelling and redness right around the sting is a normal local reaction, so if she's playing happily you can manage it at home. Scrape the stinger out if it's still in, wash the area, and use a cold compress. A weight-appropriate dose of children's antihistamine can ease itching. Call 911 right away if she develops hives elsewhere, facial or lip swelling, coughing, wheezing, vomiting or unusual sleepiness, and watch her closely for the next hour or so.
ok so i had strep, on antibiotics for 3 days, feel totally fine. basketball practice tonight?

Once you've been on antibiotics for at least a day and your fever is gone, you're usually no longer contagious, and if you feel good, a normal practice is generally fine. Go a bit easier than usual, drink plenty of water, and make sure to finish all your antibiotics even though you feel better. If you get tired fast, take breaks rather than pushing through.
Had unprotected sex 5 days ago, pregnancy test negative this morning. Am I in the clear?

Not yet. Five days is too early for a test to pick up a pregnancy, because the hormone usually isn't detectable until around the time your period is due, about two weeks after sex. Test again then, or around 21 days after the encounter for a solid answer. Some emergency contraception, like the Paragard IUD or ella, can still work up to 5 days after sex, so contact a clinic or pharmacy today if you want that option.
My grandma says to put butter on burns. Is that actually ok?

Skip the butter, because it traps heat in the skin, can make the burn deeper, and raises the risk of infection. The right move is cool running water for about 20 minutes, then a clean, loose covering like cling film or a non-fluffy dressing. Your grandma's instinct to soothe it is good, but water does that job far better.
Fish oil — worth it? I'm 45, healthy, eat fish maybe once a month.

For a healthy person, the evidence that fish oil prevents heart disease is pretty underwhelming. Eating fatty fish like salmon or sardines twice a week is the better move. If that's not realistic, 250 to 500 mg combined EPA and DHA from a reputable brand is a reasonable, low-risk option. Higher doses are mainly for people with high triglycerides, under a doctor's guidance.
I'm a runner, 45, my bp spikes to 190 during hard intervals. Normal?

Systolic pressure rising during intense exercise is normal, but readings around 190 or higher in a fit 45-year-old can point to a greater future risk of hypertension. It's worth getting your resting pressure checked and mentioning this to your doctor. They might suggest an exercise stress test. Keep training unless you get chest pain, unusual breathlessness or dizziness, and stop if you do.
Can I double my insulin dose if I'm about to eat a huge holiday dinner

Don't just double it, because that's a quick way to end up with a dangerous low, especially if the meal is delayed or you eat less than you expected. If you use mealtime insulin, dose based on your carb ratio for what you actually eat, and consider splitting the dose for a long meal or one heavy in fat. If you don't have a carb ratio yet, ask your diabetes team for one before the holiday. Check your sugar a couple of hours after eating and again before bed.
child got sand in his eye at the beach and keeps rubbing it

Stop the rubbing first, since grinding sand across the eye can scratch the cornea. Flush the eye with clean bottled water or saline while he looks in different directions, or have him blink in a cup of water, which usually washes the grains out. If he still says something's in there, his eye stays red and watery, or he can't open it comfortably after a while, have a doctor check for a scratch.
Teen son (15) has knee pain below the kneecap, plays soccer constantly. Worry?

This is very likely Osgood-Schlatter disease, a common overuse problem in active teens where the tendon pulls on a growth plate below the kneecap. It isn't dangerous, and it usually settles once he finishes growing. Ice after activity, quad and hamstring stretching, and cutting back on training load during flares are the mainstays. Have it checked if the pain is severe, he's limping, he has night pain, or the knee is swollen or locking, to rule out something else.
I've had insomnia for 8 months. I've tried everything. Tea, apps, magnesium. Nothing works and I'm losing it.

Eight months is long enough to count as chronic insomnia, and it deserves real treatment rather than more trial and error on your own. The most effective treatment is cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), which outperforms sleeping pills over the long term. Your doctor can refer you, and there are evidence-based digital programs too. It's also worth checking for things that drive insomnia, like sleep apnea, thyroid problems, restless legs, medications or depression. If you're feeling desperate or hopeless, tell your doctor that directly, because you deserve support with that too.
whats the earliest age for a kid to sit in the front seat

The standard recommendation is to keep kids in the back seat until they're 13, because front airbags are designed for adult bodies and can seriously injure a smaller child. Until then, most kids also need a booster seat until the adult belt fits properly, usually around 4'9". Proper fit means the lap belt sits low across the hips and the shoulder belt crosses the chest, not the neck.
Trying to lose 20 lbs before a wedding in 5 weeks. Thinking water fast + electrolyte pills. Thoughts?

I'd steer you away from an extended water fast. It risks fainting, gallstones, heart rhythm problems from electrolyte shifts, and rebound weight gain right before the event. A realistic, safe target is around 5 to 10 pounds in five weeks. Aim for a moderate calorie deficit, high protein, lots of vegetables, cutting alcohol and liquid calories, and daily walking. Cutting back on salt and refined carbs in the final few days will also reduce bloating, so you'll look noticeably leaner without wrecking yourself.
can I give my baby honey for her cough? she's 8 months

No, honey isn't safe before 12 months because it can cause infant botulism, which is serious. For a baby her age, a cool-mist humidifier, saline drops, and gentle suction for a stuffy nose are safe options. Call her doctor if she's breathing fast or working hard to breathe, has a fever, isn't feeding well, or the cough drags on, and get urgent care if she seems to be struggling.
I'm 34 weeks and the baby has barely moved today. She's usually super active in the evenings. Should I just wait until tomorrow?

Don't wait until tomorrow. A noticeable drop in your baby's usual movement pattern is one of the warning signs that needs checking the same day. Call your labor and delivery unit or midwife now, and they will likely ask you to come in for monitoring, which is quick and routine. It is very often fine, but this is exactly what they want you to call about, so you are not overreacting.
high blood pressure meds make me dizzy so I've been skipping them. that's fine right?

Skipping them leaves your blood pressure uncontrolled, which quietly raises your risk of stroke and heart attack, so it isn't a good trade. Dizziness is a fixable problem. Tell your doctor, because they can lower the dose, change the timing or switch you to a different drug. In the meantime, stand up slowly and stay hydrated.
I have migraines and read magnesium helps. Just take a bunch?

Magnesium does have reasonable evidence for preventing migraines, but more isn't better. The usual dose is around 400 to 600mg a day, typically as magnesium citrate or glycinate, and higher amounts mostly cause diarrhea. Check with your doctor first if you have kidney problems, and give it two to three months to judge whether it's working.
Neighbor's dog bit me. They say it's vaccinated. Do I still need to do anything?

Wash the bite thoroughly and see a doctor if the skin is broken, since infection is the more common problem even with vaccinated dogs. Ask your neighbor for proof of current rabies vaccination, and in many areas the dog will be observed for 10 days, which settles the rabies question. Report the bite to animal control if your local rules require it, and check whether you need a tetanus booster.
My dad is 78 and has had the flu for 3 days and now he seems confused and is breathing kind of fast. Is this normal flu stuff?

No, that's not normal, and he needs to be seen urgently, today. New confusion and fast breathing in an older adult with flu can signal pneumonia, low oxygen or sepsis, which can deteriorate quickly at his age. Take him to the emergency room now, or call 911 if he's struggling to breathe, has bluish lips, or is very hard to wake.
I'm 67 and have a scaly rough spot on my forehead that keeps flaking off and coming back. It's been there months.

A rough, scaly spot that keeps returning on sun-exposed skin at your age is often an actinic keratosis, a precancerous sun-damage lesion. It's worth getting checked, because a small fraction can progress to squamous cell skin cancer if left alone. A GP or dermatologist can usually confirm it by looking and treat it simply with freezing or a prescription cream. Meanwhile, use daily sunscreen and a hat, and resist picking at it.
can i skip my preventer inhaler on days i feel good

No, the preventer works by calming the inflammation in your airways over time. You feel good partly because you're taking it every day. Skipping it lets that inflammation creep back, and that's when attacks happen. If you've been symptom-free for months, ask your doctor about stepping down the dose properly rather than dropping it yourself.
Jammed my finger at volleyball. Can I just pop it back if it looks crooked?

Don't try to pull it straight yourself. A crooked finger can be a dislocation with a fracture, and yanking it can damage the joint or tendons. Ice it, splint it in the position it's in by buddy-taping it to the next finger, and get it X-rayed today. A clinician can put it back safely and check that it doesn't need a longer splint.
My 78 year old mom got scratched by her cat and her forearm is red and warm around it two days later. She says it's nothing.

Redness and warmth spreading two days after a scratch sounds like an early skin infection, and older skin and immune systems can let it worsen quickly. She should see her doctor or an urgent care today for likely antibiotics. If you can, draw a pen line around the edge of the redness so you can see whether it's spreading. If she gets a fever, chills, or confusion, take her to the ER.
My mother (75) says she's been seeing flashing lights and a curtain over part of her vision since yesterday. She wants to wait for her eye appointment next month.

She shouldn't wait. Flashing lights plus a curtain or shadow over part of the vision are classic signs of a retinal detachment, which is an emergency. Call an eye doctor today for an urgent same-day visit. If you can't reach one, go to the ER. Fast treatment often saves the sight in that eye.
I'm 7 months postpartum and I have scary intrusive thoughts about something bad happening to the baby. Am I a danger?

Intrusive thoughts like that are extremely common in new parents, and the fact that they horrify you is a strong sign you're not a danger. They can be part of postpartum anxiety or OCD, which is very treatable, so tell your GP or health visitor. Hearing about this is routine for them. If you ever feel you might act on the thoughts or feel detached from reality, seek urgent help immediately.
I've had a constant knot in my stomach and tight chest from stress for a month. Is it just stress?

Stress very commonly shows up as a tight chest and a knotted stomach, but a month of chest tightness is worth getting checked by a doctor, both for peace of mind and to rule out heart, lung or reflux causes. If the chest pain is sudden, crushing or spreads to your arm, jaw or back, or comes with breathlessness, sweating or nausea, call emergency services rather than assuming it's anxiety. Once physical causes are ruled out, slow breathing, regular exercise and therapy for the underlying stress can ease these symptoms a lot.
Can I double up on my birth control pill if I missed yesterday's?

Yes, for a combined pill, take the missed pill as soon as you remember, even if that means two today, then carry on as normal. If you've missed two or more, or you're on a progestin-only pill and you're more than 3 hours late, use condoms for the next 7 days. Consider emergency contraception if you've had unprotected sex. Your pill pack leaflet or a pharmacist can confirm the exact rule for your brand.
Woke up with a pimple-like bump on my gum above a tooth. It popped and tasted salty. What is that?

That sounds like a dental fistula, a little drainage channel from an infection at the root of a tooth, and the salty taste was pus draining out. It may feel better now that it has drained, but the infection is still there and can flare up again. Book a dentist appointment in the next few days, since it usually needs a root canal or extraction.
My 89 year old father is in a lot of pain from cancer and the hospice nurse gave morphine. I'm scared we'll overdose him or he'll get addicted. Should I give less than they said?

Giving less than prescribed usually just leaves him in pain. Hospice dosing is carefully started and adjusted, and addiction isn't a meaningful concern in end-of-life care. Give it as directed, and keep a simple log of times and doses. Call the hospice line, which is available 24/7, if he seems unusually hard to wake or his breathing changes in a way that worries you. They'd much rather you call with questions than undertreat his pain.
Ugh threw up after drinking last night, now stomach burns. Can I take pepto and Advil together?

Skip the Advil this morning, since ibuprofen on top of a stomach already irritated by alcohol and vomiting can make the burning worse. Pepto is fine at the label dose, though it can harmlessly turn your stool and tongue black. Sip water or an electrolyte drink and eat something bland like toast once you can. If you vomit blood or something that looks like coffee grounds, or you can't keep fluids down, get medical care.
I'm 45 and my doctor says I'm prediabetic. Can I actually reverse it?

Yes, often you can. Losing even 5 to 7 percent of your body weight and getting about 150 minutes of brisk activity a week cut the risk of progressing to diabetes by more than half in major studies. Cutting sugary drinks and refined carbs helps a lot, and so does good sleep. Ask about a CDC-recognized diabetes prevention program, which many insurers cover, and recheck your A1c in 6 to 12 months to track your progress.
Can I use orajel on my 6 month old who's teething? She's miserable.

Skip Orajel and other benzocaine products for babies, because the FDA warns they can cause a rare but dangerous blood condition in young children. Instead, let her chew on a chilled (not frozen) teething ring, or gently rub her gums with a clean finger. If she's still miserable, ask your pediatrician about acetaminophen dosed by weight. Mention a fever or diarrhea too, since those aren't typical of teething.
I'm 19 and my bp was 138/88 at a physical. is that weird for my age?

It's higher than expected at 19, but a single reading at a physical is often inflated by nerves, caffeine, or rushing to the appointment. Check it at home a few times over a week or two. If it keeps coming back above 130/80, follow up with your doctor, since high blood pressure in young people sometimes has a specific cause worth looking into. Cutting back on energy drinks, salt, and alcohol and staying active are good moves regardless.
My 4yo cut his lip on the coffee table, bleeding like crazy and he's screaming. It's inside the mouth.

Mouth cuts bleed heavily but usually look worse than they are. Have him sit leaning slightly forward, and press a clean cloth or gauze firmly against the cut for 10 minutes. Giving him an ice pop afterward can soothe it and help it settle. Take him to urgent care if it won't stop with pressure, the cut goes through the lip border onto the outside skin, it's gaping, or a tooth seems loose or broken.
Been vegan 3 years, never taken B12. Feel fine. Do I really need it?

Yes, you really do, because B12 deficiency develops slowly and can cause nerve damage before you notice anything. Your liver stores enough to last a few years, which is why you may feel fine right now. Ask your doctor for a B12 level check, ideally with methylmalonic acid, and start a supplement either way. A common choice is 250 mcg daily or 2,000 to 2,500 mcg once a week.
do those migraine glasses with the pink tint actually work or is it a scam

FL-41 tinted lenses, the rose-colored ones, have some modest evidence behind them for people whose migraines are triggered by light, especially fluorescent lighting and screens. They won't stop a migraine on their own and aren't magic, but plenty of light-sensitive people find them helpful. Try an inexpensive pair before paying premium prices.
hamster bit my finger, drew blood. is that a big deal or nah

Usually not a big deal. Wash it with soap and running water for a few minutes, apply antibiotic ointment and a bandage, and watch it for signs of infection like increasing redness, swelling or pus. Pet hamsters bred in captivity aren't considered a rabies risk. If it becomes infected or you develop fever, see a doctor.
I'm 67 and my hip has been aching for months, worse in the morning and after walking. Is this just age?

Age plays a role, but 'just age' isn't a diagnosis. Months of hip ache that's stiff in the morning and worse with walking often points to osteoarthritis, and that is very treatable. Strengthening exercises, physical therapy, staying active with low-impact activities like cycling or swimming, and managing weight can make a real difference. See your doctor for an exam and possibly an X-ray to confirm what's going on and talk through pain relief that's safe with your other medications.
Is it okay to use a tanning bed to clear up my psoriasis?

Tanning beds aren't a good substitute, because they mostly emit UVA, which raises skin cancer risk and doesn't help psoriasis much. The treatment that does help is medical narrowband UVB phototherapy, given in controlled doses at a dermatology clinic. Short sensible doses of natural sunlight can also help some people as long as you don't burn. Ask your doctor about phototherapy or the other options available now, including creams and newer injectable treatments.
My friend texted me saying goodbye and that she's sorry for everything. She's not answering her phone. What do I do?

Treat this as an emergency and call 911, or your local emergency number, right now, then give them her address and tell them about the text. If you're close by or know someone who is, have them go to her as well, but don't wait to hear back before calling for help. In the US you can also call 988 for guidance while help is on the way. It's always better to act and be wrong than to wait.
Work night shifts as a nurse, sleep during the day is garbage. Tips?

Treat your daytime sleep like nighttime: blackout curtains or an eye mask, earplugs or white noise, a cool room, and your phone on do-not-disturb. Wear sunglasses on the drive home to block the morning light that tells your brain it's time to be awake. Try to keep a consistent sleep block even on days off, and save caffeine for the first half of your shift. If you're still struggling or nodding off driving, talk to a doctor about shift work disorder, because there are treatments for it.
I think I broke my toe. ER or just wait it out?

Most broken small toes heal fine at home. Tape it to the next toe with a bit of padding between them, wear a stiff-soled shoe, and ice and elevate it. Big toe injuries are different, and so is any toe that looks clearly crooked, has an open wound, or turns numb, cold or blue. Those should be seen at urgent care, since they may need setting or closer care.
quick q, how do i get a splinter out

Wash the area, then clean a pair of tweezers with rubbing alcohol and pull the splinter out at the same angle it went in. If it's under the skin, use a sterilized needle to gently lift the skin over the end first. Wash it again afterward and put on a bandage. If it's very deep, under a fingernail, or the area gets red, hot and swollen over the next few days, have a doctor deal with it.
do i have to see a doctor for sleepwalking or nah

Occasional sleepwalking in adults is often triggered by stress, sleep deprivation or alcohol and isn't always serious. It is worth seeing a doctor if it's frequent, you hurt yourself, you leave the house, or it started after a new medication, since sleeping pills are a known cause. Untreated sleep apnea can also trigger it. Meanwhile, lock doors and windows, put away car keys and clear tripping hazards.
What's the actual difference between a cold and the flu?

Colds creep in gradually with a runny nose, sneezing and a sore throat, and you can usually keep functioning. Flu tends to hit suddenly with fever, chills, heavy body aches and exhaustion that can flatten you for days. Flu is more likely to cause complications like pneumonia, which is why older adults, young kids, pregnant people and anyone with chronic conditions should see a doctor early if they suspect it. A rapid test at a clinic can tell you for sure.
Can I get a cortisone shot in my knee every month? It works great.

Unfortunately, monthly isn't safe. Repeated steroid injections can speed up cartilage breakdown and weaken surrounding tissue, so most doctors limit them to roughly three or four a year in the same joint, spaced at least three months apart. Talk with your doctor about building a longer-term plan around strengthening, weight management, physio or other injection types. If it's reached the point where you need shots that often, a joint replacement may be the better option.
how much water should i drink to get rid of a dehydration headache

Sip steadily rather than chugging. A glass or two over the first half hour, then regular drinks until your urine is pale yellow, usually does it. If you've been sweating a lot or were sick, an electrolyte drink helps, and if the headache hasn't eased after a few hours of rehydrating it's probably not just dehydration.
I'm 67 and straight lines like door frames look wavy in one eye lately

Book an eye exam within the next few days and mention the wavy lines specifically. Distortion like this is a classic sign of macular degeneration, and the wet form can progress quickly but often responds well to treatment when caught early. If the distortion is getting worse fast, or you lose central vision, treat it as urgent and get seen the same day.
how much coffee is ok while pregnant

Most guidelines say to keep caffeine under about 200 mg a day, which is roughly one 12-ounce cup of regular brewed coffee. Remember that tea, soda, energy drinks and chocolate count toward that total too. Energy drinks are best avoided altogether because of their high and inconsistent caffeine levels.
My 4 month old has a fever of 100.6. Is that bad or am I overreacting?

You're not overreacting, because a fever in a baby this young deserves a call to your pediatrician today, even if she seems fairly okay. At 4 months, doctors want to hear about any temperature of 100.4°F or higher. They'll guide you based on how she's feeding, how alert she is, and whether she's peeing normally. If she's very sleepy, hard to wake, struggling to breathe or refusing feeds, go to urgent care or the ER instead of waiting for a callback.
probiotics worth it for general gut health or waste of money

For an otherwise healthy person, they're mostly a waste of money, because the evidence for general benefit is thin and strains vary a lot. There's better support for specific uses, like reducing antibiotic-related diarrhea or helping some IBS symptoms. Your gut bacteria generally respond more to a varied, fiber-rich diet, and fermented foods like yogurt or kefir are a cheaper way to experiment.
Slammed my finger in a car door, nail is black and throbbing like crazy

That's blood trapped under the nail, and the pressure is what makes it throb. Urgent care can drain it quickly through a tiny hole, and they should also check for a fracture, which is common with car door injuries. Don't drill it yourself with a hot paperclip. Ice it and keep your hand raised until you get there.
is it ok to make myself throw up if i ate something sketchy

It's not a good idea. Forcing yourself to vomit can injure your throat and esophagus and usually doesn't remove much anyway. Most dodgy meals pass with nothing worse than a rough day, so rest and stay hydrated. If you swallowed something actually poisonous or a chemical, call Poison Control or emergency services instead of trying to bring it up.
Worried. My mom has COPD and asthma, her lips look a bit blue tonight.

Blue lips can mean she isn't getting enough oxygen, so call emergency services now rather than waiting until morning. While you wait, help her sit upright, and if she has a rescue inhaler or prescribed oxygen, have her use it as directed. Don't let her lie flat, and stay with her.
Birth control and antibiotics — do I need backup?

For most antibiotics, no, because studies don't show they make the pill less effective. The clear exception is rifampin, and the related drug rifabutin, which do reduce effectiveness, so use condoms during those and for about four weeks after. If an antibiotic gives you vomiting or severe diarrhea, you might not absorb the pill properly, so follow your pill's missed-dose instructions in that case.
I'm on chemo and my temp is 38.1. My next appointment is in 3 days.

Don't wait for that appointment. A fever during chemotherapy can mean neutropenic fever, which is a medical emergency because your body has fewer defenses against infection. Call your oncology team's urgent line or go to the emergency department now. Don't take fever reducers before calling unless your team has told you to.
I keep reading inversion tables fix herniated discs. Should I buy one?

Inversion tables can give some people short-term relief, but there's no good evidence they fix a herniated disc. They also aren't safe if you have high blood pressure, glaucoma, heart disease, or are pregnant, because hanging upside down raises pressure in the head and eyes. Most disc herniations improve on their own over weeks to months with activity and physical therapy. A PT can give you targeted exercises that are likely to help more.
Dog bit my lip, it's split open. Can I just put a butterfly strip on it?

A split lip from a dog bite should be seen by a doctor rather than taped at home, because facial bites often need proper cleaning and sometimes stitches for good healing and a decent scar, especially if the cut crosses the lip border. Rinse it with clean water and apply gentle pressure to stop bleeding on the way. A doctor can also decide whether you need antibiotics or a tetanus booster.
I keep waking up at 3am and can't fall back asleep. Every night for a month. Tips?

If you're awake for more than about 20 minutes, get up and do something calm in dim light until you feel sleepy, then return to bed. That stops your brain from linking bed with lying there frustrated. Keep the same wake time every day, skip alcohol in the evening, since it commonly causes early waking, and don't check the clock. A month of this is worth raising with your doctor, because early waking can be tied to depression, anxiety, or sleep apnea, and CBT for insomnia is very effective.
got a sunburn so bad my skin is blistering and i feel kinda dizzy and chilled

Blistering plus dizziness and chills suggests sun poisoning or heat illness, so get out of the sun, drink water steadily, and get seen at urgent care today. Cool showers and ibuprofen can ease the pain, and leave the blisters alone. If you get confused, faint, vomit, or have a high fever, go to the ER.
Desk job, neck and shoulders always tight by 3pm. Quick fixes?

Raise your monitor so the top of the screen is at eye level, keep your keyboard close enough that your elbows stay by your sides, and get up for a minute or two every 30 to 45 minutes. A few chin tucks and shoulder blade squeezes during those breaks help a lot, and a warm shower or heat pack in the evening loosens things up. Regular exercise that strengthens your upper back tends to fix this more lastingly than stretching alone.
My 80 yo mom got scratched by her cat, her skin tore kind of like tissue paper. Help.

Fragile older skin tears easily and heals slowly, so gently rinse the tear with clean water or saline and, if there's a skin flap, ease it back into place with a damp gauze. Cover it with a non-stick dressing and avoid regular adhesive tape, which can tear more skin when removed. Because skin tears in older adults are prone to infection, have her doctor or nurse look at it within a day, sooner if it's large or bleeding a lot.
sudden hearing loss in one ear this morning, no pain or cold

See a doctor today or tomorrow, not next month. Sudden hearing loss in one ear without an obvious cause can be sensorineural hearing loss, and steroid treatment works best when started within the first few days. Ask for a same-day hearing test or an ENT referral, and go to the ER if you also have dizziness, a facial droop or weakness.
Is it ok for my dad to take ibuprofen every day for his knee arthritis? He's 77.

Daily ibuprofen is riskier at 77 than it sounds. It can cause stomach bleeding, raise blood pressure, and strain the kidneys, especially alongside blood thinners or certain heart medications. Acetaminophen, topical diclofenac gel on the knee, and physical therapy are generally safer starting points. Have him run his pain plan by his doctor or pharmacist, who can check it against his other meds.
Does creatine actually work or is it just gym hype

Creatine monohydrate is one of the best-studied supplements out there, and it reliably helps with strength and power during short, intense efforts like lifting and sprinting. The standard dose is 3 to 5 grams a day, with no loading phase required. It's considered safe for healthy people, but if you have kidney disease or take medications that affect the kidneys, check with your doctor first. Expect a pound or two of water weight in your muscles, which is normal.
My dad is 68 and has a new headache on one side of his head, his scalp is tender and his jaw hurts when he chews.

Get him seen by a doctor today. That combination in someone over 50 is a classic picture of giant cell arteritis, an inflamed artery that can cause sudden permanent vision loss if it isn't treated quickly. Doctors usually start steroids promptly, and if he has any vision changes at all, take him to the ER.
kid fell off monkey bars, wrist is swollen but he can move his fingers. probably just a sprain right

Maybe, but kids fracture their wrists much more often than they sprain them, because their growth plates are weaker than their ligaments. Being able to move his fingers doesn't rule out a break. Splint it gently, ice it, and get an X-ray today at urgent care or your pediatrician's office. If the wrist looks deformed or his fingers go numb or pale, go to the ER.
Can I just double up on ibuprofen for my back? The normal dose isn't touching it.

I wouldn't double it. Going above the label dose raises the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain without much extra pain relief. A safer move is to add acetaminophen (paracetamol) at its own normal dose alongside the ibuprofen, since they work differently and combine well, plus heat and gentle movement. If the standard approach still isn't touching the pain after several days, see a doctor so they can figure out what's going on and offer stronger options safely.
found a youtube video showing how to adjust your own spine with a towel and sharp twist. worth trying?

I'd skip anything involving a sharp, forceful twist done on your own, especially at the neck. Fast self-manipulation can strain joints. In the neck it has rarely been linked to artery injury and stroke. Gentle stretches, slow mobility work and heat are safer ways to loosen things up. If you're stiff all the time, a physio can show you exercises that work without the risk.
Fell on my tailbone ice skating, hurts like crazy to sit. Does it need an X-ray?

Usually not. Bruised or even cracked tailbones are treated the same way: rest, ice, anti-inflammatories like ibuprofen, and a cushion so you're not pressing on it. It can take a few weeks to settle. See a doctor if the pain is severe or getting worse, or if you have numbness, weakness in your legs, or any bladder or bowel problems, which need urgent attention.
can i stop my steroid inhaler now that summer's here and my asthma is fine

Don't stop it on your own. Your asthma probably feels fine because the controller is working, and stopping it suddenly often leads to a flare a few weeks later. If you've been well controlled for about three months, it's very reasonable to ask your doctor about stepping down to a lower dose. Some people with clearly seasonal asthma do get approved to use it only part of the year. Get that plan worked out with your doctor so you know exactly when to restart.
honestly whats the fastest way to get a stubborn 83 year old to agree to a hearing test

Make it about something he cares about rather than a defect. Try "I want to make sure I'm not missing what you say" or tie it to grandkids, TV, or his card game. Offer to get your own hearing checked at the same visit, which takes the sting out. Many pharmacies and audiologists do quick free screenings. It's worth the effort, because untreated hearing loss is linked to isolation and faster cognitive decline.
Can I fly at 30 weeks? Trip's booked for a wedding

Flying at 30 weeks is usually fine if your pregnancy is uncomplicated, but check with your OB first and ask for a note, since some airlines want one later in pregnancy. Get an aisle seat, walk and stretch regularly, stay hydrated, and consider compression socks to lower your risk of blood clots. Find out where the nearest hospital is at your destination and bring a copy of your prenatal records just in case.
Going hiking for 5 days. Type 1. What should I bring insulin-wise?

Bring at least double the insulin and supplies you'd normally use, and split them between two bags in case one gets lost or wet. Keep the insulin in an insulated pouch, like a Frio wallet, away from heat and from freezing. Hiking all day usually means you'll need less insulin, so carry plenty of fast sugar and a backup glucose meter. It's worth asking your team beforehand how to adjust your basal dose for the extra activity.
Can I use orajel on my 5 month old who's teething?

No, the FDA advises against benzocaine products like Orajel for children under 2, because they can cause a rare but dangerous blood condition called methemoglobinemia. Instead, try a chilled (not frozen) teething ring, gently rubbing her gums with a clean finger, or weight-appropriate infant acetaminophen if your pediatrician okays it. Call the pediatrician if she has a fever above 100.4°F, since teething doesn't explain that.
my teen ate like 3 bags of hot chips and now says her stomach is burning

Spicy chips like those are notorious for causing gastritis-style burning. Give her a glass of milk or some yogurt, a plain snack like bread or crackers, and maybe an antacid. It should ease over a few hours. If she has severe pain, vomiting, or blood in her vomit or stool, have a doctor see her, and it's worth gently steering her away from making it a habit.
is it bad to have a couple glasses of wine every night to unwind

Two glasses every night adds up to more than the low-risk guidelines, and alcohol actually worsens anxiety and sleep quality once it wears off, so it ends up feeding the stress you're trying to escape. If you find it hard to skip a night, that's worth paying attention to. Try a few alcohol-free nights a week and give yourself another wind-down ritual, like a walk, a shower or a herbal tea. If cutting back feels difficult, your doctor can help without judgment.
Can I still have my one glass of wine with dinner now that I'm pregnant? My mom drank and I turned out fine.

The honest answer is that no amount of alcohol has been shown to be safe in pregnancy, so the standard advice is to skip it completely.
