Plenty of people were exposed and turned out fine, but alcohol crosses the placenta and the risks, like fetal alcohol spectrum disorders, don't have a known safe threshold. A good alcohol-free wine or a fancy mocktail can keep the dinner ritual going. If you drank before you knew you were pregnant, don't panic, just mention it to your provider.
Got scratched by a stray kitten 2 weeks ago, now there's a swollen lump in my armpit on the same side. Tender. Related?

It very likely is related, because that pattern fits cat scratch disease, a Bartonella infection that often comes from kittens and causes swollen lymph nodes near the scratch. It usually clears up on its own, but a doctor should confirm the diagnosis, check for other causes and decide whether you need antibiotics. Book an appointment in the next few days. Go sooner if you develop a high fever, the lump becomes very painful or red, or you have a weakened immune system.
I keep checking that the stove is off like 10 times before I leave. Annoying but whatever right?

Checking once or twice is normal, but ten times, especially if you feel anxious until you do it, sounds like it could be OCD-type checking. These habits tend to grow over time if they're left alone. The good news is that therapy called exposure and response prevention works really well for this, so it's worth bringing up with a doctor or therapist before it starts eating more of your time.
I've had flaky itchy scalp for years, dandruff shampoo kind of helps. Anything better?

Rotate between medicated shampoos with different active ingredients, because one alone often stops working as well. Ketoconazole is especially good for the seborrheic dermatitis behind most stubborn dandruff, and selenium sulfide, zinc pyrithione or coal tar are the other options. Leave the lather on for about five minutes before rinsing, and use it two or three times a week. If you have thick silvery plaques, flaking past the hairline or patches elsewhere on your body, see a doctor, since that could be scalp psoriasis, which needs different treatment.
My teenage daughter (15) wants to start a 500 calorie a day diet she saw on TikTok. How do I push back without a fight?

Your instinct is right, because 500 calories a day is far too little for a growing 15-year-old and can affect her growth, periods, bones and mood. Try getting curious rather than forbidding it: ask what she's hoping to change and how she's feeling about her body, then suggest seeing her pediatrician or a registered dietitian together as a team. If you notice skipping meals, secrecy around food, intense exercise or rapid weight loss, raise it with her doctor soon, since eating disorders often start this way and do better when caught early.
blood sugar 32 mmol/L but i feel fine. sleep it off?

No, don't sleep on a reading that high. If you have type 1 diabetes, check your ketones now, and if they're raised or you're vomiting, go to A&E. Even without ketones, a level of 32 needs your correction dose and a call to your diabetes team or an urgent care line tonight. Feeling fine doesn't mean it's safe, because the dangerous problems can build up quietly.
my gums bleed every time I floss and now they kind of ache. should I just stop flossing so they heal?

Keep flossing, because bleeding gums are usually a sign of early gum inflammation caused by plaque, and gentle daily flossing is what clears it up. Be gentle and consistent, and the bleeding typically settles within one to two weeks. If it doesn't, or your gums are receding or teeth feel loose, see a dentist for a cleaning and check.
ate sushi last night and now got the runs and puking. how long does food poisoning last

Most food poisoning burns itself out within 24 to 48 hours. The main job is to stay hydrated with small, frequent sips of water or oral rehydration salts, and to wait until the vomiting settles before trying bland food. Seek care if you can't keep fluids down for most of a day, see blood in your stool, run a high fever, feel very weak or dizzy, or aren't improving after three days.
My husband cut his leg with a chainsaw. It's bleeding a lot through the towel, he's pale. What do I do right now

Call emergency services right now. Press down hard on the wound with the towel and don't remove it; add more cloth on top if it soaks through, and keep pressing with both hands. Have him lie down with his legs raised if possible and keep him warm. If the bleeding is spurting and won't stop with pressure, and you know how, a tight tourniquet above the wound can save his life while help arrives.
I think I'm allergic to my latex gloves at work, my hands are raw. I'm a nurse.

Switch to nitrile gloves right away and report this to your occupational health department, since latex allergy can progress from skin irritation to more serious reactions with ongoing exposure. Use a gentle emollient on your hands, and see a doctor or allergist to sort out whether this is true latex allergy or irritant dermatitis from handwashing. If you ever get hives, wheezing or swelling, treat it as urgent.
Going to Kenya in 10 days, totally forgot about vaccines. Too late?

Not too late, but book a travel clinic visit in the next day or two. Yellow fever vaccine is recommended for most of Kenya, and you may need proof of it depending on your route. It ideally needs 10 days to take effect, so you're right at the edge. A clinic can also cover typhoid, hepatitis A and malaria pills, which matter just as much as the shots, and even partial protection is far better than none.
Is it fine to keep lifting heavy deadlifts with a mildly sore lower back? Don't want to lose progress.

I'd back off the heavy pulls for now. Loading a sore back near your max is a common way to turn a minor strain into a real injury that costs you months. Drop to lighter weights with perfect form, or swap in movements that don't hurt for a week or two, and keep training everything else. You'll keep most of your progress, and you can build back up quickly once the soreness is gone.
can i just take my moms xanax before my job interview tomorrow

Don't take someone else's Xanax, especially for the first time right before something important. You don't know how you'll react to the dose, and it can make you foggy, slow or oddly flat, which is the opposite of what you want in an interview. It also interacts dangerously with alcohol and some other medications. For tomorrow, prep your answers out loud tonight, get decent sleep, go easy on the coffee, and try a few slow breaths with a long exhale right before you walk in. If interview nerves are a regular problem, a doctor can talk to you about options that are actually safe for you.
Low at 55, shaky. what do i eat fast

Have 15 grams of fast sugar right now, such as 4 glucose tabs, half a cup of juice or regular soda, or a tablespoon of sugar or honey. Recheck in 15 minutes and repeat if you're still under 70. Once you're back up, eat a small snack with protein if your next meal is more than an hour away. Skip chocolate for treating the low itself, because the fat slows absorption.
I'm 68 and get stuffy every morning. Pharmacist sold me sudafed, I have high blood pressure though, fine?

That combo is worth double-checking, because pseudoephedrine can raise blood pressure and heart rate, which matters with hypertension and at your age. A steroid nasal spray or saline rinse is usually a safer choice for daily morning stuffiness. Run it by your doctor or go back to the pharmacist and mention your blood pressure and medications.
Pimple on my nose is huge and painful and my face around it is swelling. Pop it?

Leave it alone. The area around the nose drains into veins near the brain, so squeezing an infected spot there can occasionally spread infection in dangerous ways. Spreading facial swelling around a painful bump means you should see a doctor soon, since it may need antibiotics. Warm compresses are fine until then, and go to urgent care quickly if you get a fever, eye swelling or changes in your vision.
honestly is a1c of 7.4 bad or whatever

It's not terrible, but it's above where most adults with diabetes aim to be, which is usually under 7. A 7.4 means your average blood sugar is running around 165. Over years, that range nudges up the risk of eye, kidney, and nerve damage, but it's very close to target, so small changes like a bit more walking or a medication tweak can often get you there. Ask your doctor what your personal goal is, because it can be set higher for older adults or people prone to lows.
my 4 month old has a fever of 38.2 after her shots this morning. normal?

A low-grade fever within a day or two of vaccines is common and usually harmless at this age, and 38.2°C is mild. Keep her comfortable and feeding well, and you can ask your pediatrician about the right acetaminophen dose for her weight. Call the doctor if the fever reaches 40°C or higher, lasts more than 48 hours, or if she cries inconsolably for three or more hours, seems unusually floppy or hard to wake, or has a seizure.
Is it bad to sleep with a fan on all night?

It's generally fine and many people sleep better with the cooling and white noise. Some people wake up with a dry throat, stuffy nose or stiff neck, especially if it's blowing directly on them. Pointing it away from your face and keeping it clean of dust helps. A cool room, around 16 to 19°C (60 to 67°F), is good for sleep anyway.
Can ibuprofen raise blood pressure? I take it daily for my knee.

Yes. Regular NSAIDs like ibuprofen and naproxen can raise blood pressure, cause fluid retention, and make some blood pressure medications work less well. With daily use, ask your doctor about alternatives for your knee. Acetaminophen, topical NSAID gels, or physical therapy may work for you. Have your blood pressure checked too, so you know whether it's been affected.
I'm 72 and was in hospital for 5 days with a bad infection. I feel so weak now. My daughter says rest but I want to get stronger. Who's right?

You're both partly right, because you do need rest, but staying in bed too much after a hospital stay can make you weaker, especially at 72. Short, gentle walks around the house several times a day, plus getting up from a chair a few times, is a good start. Ask your doctor whether physiotherapy could help, since a physio can give you a safe plan for rebuilding strength. If you feel dizzy, short of breath or have chest pain, stop and let your doctor know.
I read cinnamon can replace diabetes meds. Thinking of stopping my glipizide and trying that instead.

Please don't stop the glipizide, because cinnamon hasn't been shown to lower blood sugar anywhere near enough to replace medication. Stopping it could send your sugars dangerously high. If you want to cut back on medication, the approaches that genuinely work are weight loss, regular exercise, and changes to your diet, all done together with your doctor so your dose can be lowered safely as you improve. Adding some cinnamon to your food is fine, just not as a replacement.
do i need antibiotics for a fever

Not usually. Most fevers come from viruses, and antibiotics don't work on viruses. They only help when there's a bacterial infection, like strep throat, a UTI, or some cases of pneumonia, and a doctor needs to diagnose those. Taking leftover antibiotics on your own can hide the real problem and cause side effects, so get checked if you think it's more than a virus.
Is it fine to buy cheap reading glasses at the drugstore instead of getting an eye exam? I'm 45 and just started struggling with menus.

Drugstore readers are perfectly fine for normal age-related near-vision change, which is very common around 45. Still get a full eye exam if you haven't had one in a couple of years, because it also screens for silent problems like glaucoma that become more common now. Get checked sooner if one eye is worse than the other or you notice distortion.
fever 101 since yesterday, body aches, adult, otherwise healthy. what do i do

That sounds like a typical viral illness, and rest, plenty of fluids, and acetaminophen or ibuprofen at label doses should help you feel better. A fever like this usually breaks within two to three days. See a doctor if it climbs above 103°F, lasts more than three days, or comes with trouble breathing, chest pain, a stiff neck, confusion, or a rash.
Baby is 6 weeks old and has a temp of 100.6 rectal. Just some sniffles otherwise. Can it wait till morning?

No, call now. Any rectal temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher in a baby under 3 months needs prompt medical evaluation, even if they otherwise seem okay, because young infants can have serious infections that don't look serious at first. Call your pediatrician's after-hours line right away or head to the emergency department, and don't give fever medicine before talking to a doctor.
is a sauna a good way to recover after the flu

Not right after the flu. You're probably still a bit dehydrated, and the heat strains your heart and can leave you dizzy. Wait until you're fully recovered and eating and drinking normally, then start with short sessions and plenty of water. Rest, fluids and gentle walks will do more for your recovery right now.
My 2yo missed her 12 month and 15 month shots because of covid lockdown stuff and then life. Do we have to start over??

No, you don't need to start over; the vaccine schedule is designed for this, and doses already given still count. Call her pediatrician and ask for a catch-up visit, where they'll look at her record and give the missing doses, often several at once, which is safe. Getting her MMR and varicella soon is especially important since measles outbreaks have been increasing. Lots of families fell behind in that period, so no one will judge you for catching up.
Quick q: does ashwagandha actually work for stress? Thinking of starting it.

There's some modest evidence that ashwagandha can lower perceived stress and cortisol a bit, but the studies are small and the effect isn't dramatic. It isn't harmless either. There are rare reports of liver injury, it can affect thyroid levels, and it shouldn't be used in pregnancy or alongside sedatives, thyroid medication or immunosuppressants without checking with a doctor or pharmacist. If you're otherwise healthy and on no meds, a short trial of a reputable brand is reasonable. Stop it if you notice yellowing skin, dark urine or unusual fatigue.
What's the right amount of screen time for a 2 year old? Asking because we're kind of failing lol

The usual guidance is to avoid screens other than video chat before 18 to 24 months. For ages 2 to 5, aim for about an hour a day of good-quality content, ideally watched together so you can talk about it. Don't stress about perfection; small changes help, like no screens during meals or the hour before bed. Make sure screens aren't crowding out sleep, play or talking time.
got sneezy and wheezy every time I clean with this new spray. is that an allergy or what

It could be an allergy, but strong cleaning products more often cause direct irritation of the airways, and the wheezing is the part to take seriously. Stop using that spray, ventilate well, and try a milder unscented product. Since wheezing can signal asthma, see a doctor to get your breathing checked. Seek urgent care if you ever feel short of breath at rest or can't speak in full sentences.
My asthma gets worse every spring. Is there anything I can do besides suffer?

Definitely, because spring asthma is usually driven by pollen allergy, and that is very treatable. Starting a daily antihistamine and a steroid nasal spray a couple of weeks before pollen season, keeping windows closed and showering after being outdoors all help. Ask your doctor whether to step up your controller inhaler during spring. Allergy testing and immunotherapy, as shots or tablets, can also reduce the problem long term.
seeing a bunch of new floaters and like flashes of light in the corner of my eye since this afternoon. 58M, nearsighted.

A sudden shower of new floaters with flashes needs an eye exam today, especially at 58 and nearsighted. Most often it's a harmless posterior vitreous detachment, but the same symptoms can mean a retinal tear, which can progress to a detachment and permanent vision loss if it's missed. Call an ophthalmologist for a same-day dilated exam, or go to the ER if you can't get one. Go urgently if you notice a curtain or shadow creeping across your vision.
I wake up at 3am every night and can't get back to sleep. It's been two months. What is wrong with me?

Early-morning waking that lasts for months is common and very treatable, but it's worth checking for causes like stress, depression, alcohol in the evening, reflux, a full bladder or sleep apnea. If you're awake for more than about 20 minutes, get up and do something dull in dim light until you feel sleepy, rather than lying there clock-watching. Keep the same wake time every day, even after a bad night. Since it's been two months, see your doctor and ask about CBT for insomnia, which works better long-term than sleeping pills.
quick q - grandpa wants to keep driving at 91. how do i know when to make him stop

Look for concrete signs: new dents or scrapes on the car, getting lost on familiar routes, near-misses, or other drivers honking at him. Riding along with him a few times tells you a lot. If you're worried, his doctor can refer him for a formal driving assessment with an occupational therapist, which takes the decision out of the family-argument zone. Planning other ways for him to get around before he stops makes it much easier for him to accept.
can i get a massage with a herniated disc or will it make it worse

Massage is generally fine and can ease the muscle spasm that often comes with a herniated disc, as long as it's gentle. Tell the therapist about the disc and ask them to skip deep pressure directly on the spine and any forceful twisting. Stop if it sets off sharper or spreading leg pain. Treat it as a complement to exercise-based physical therapy rather than a substitute.
Quick q - can I take Benadryl to sleep every night? It works great.

It's fine now and then, but nightly use isn't a great idea. You build tolerance quickly, it often leaves a next-day hangover, and long-term regular use of anticholinergic drugs like diphenhydramine has been linked to memory problems, especially as people get older. If you need help sleeping most nights, talk to your doctor about the cause. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia works better over the long run than any sleep pill.
There's a splinter deep in my palm and I can barely see it. Should I dig for it with a needle?

You can try once with a needle and tweezers that you've cleaned with rubbing alcohol, gently lifting the skin over the end rather than digging around. Soaking your hand in warm water for 10 minutes first softens the skin and sometimes brings the splinter closer to the surface. If it's deep, made of glass or metal, or you can't get it out cleanly, have a doctor remove it, because repeated digging just invites infection.
headache behind one eye, eye is red and blurry and I see halos around lights. 61F

That combination can point to acute angle-closure glaucoma, where pressure in the eye spikes and can damage vision within hours. Go to an emergency room or an urgent eye clinic right away, especially if you also feel nauseous. This isn't one to treat at home with painkillers.
can i just take two melatonin gummies instead of one if one isn't working anymore

You can, but more melatonin usually isn't the fix, because it works as a timing signal rather than a sedative, and higher doses often cause grogginess, vivid dreams or headaches without better sleep. Many people actually do better on a low dose of 0.5 to 1 mg taken a couple of hours before bed than on 5 or 10 mg at lights-out. If it seems to have stopped working, look at caffeine, late screens and an irregular wake time first. Check with a pharmacist if you take blood thinners, seizure medication or diabetes drugs.
got bit by a raccoon trying to get it out of my garage. small bite on my calf. it was acting kinda weird

Wash the bite with soap and running water for 15 minutes, then go to urgent care or the ER today, because raccoons are a major rabies carrier and odd behavior makes it more concerning. You'll very likely need rabies post-exposure shots, which work well when started promptly. Call animal control about the raccoon and keep people and pets away from it, without trying to catch it yourself.
is it safe to use a laxative every day? I've been taking one for like 3 months

Some laxatives, like polyethylene glycol (Miralax) or fiber supplements, are generally fine for longer-term use. Stimulant laxatives like senna or bisacodyl aren't meant for daily use over months without a doctor's guidance. Either way, needing something every day for three months is worth a doctor's visit to figure out why you're constipated, since things like thyroid problems, medications or other gut issues can be behind it. In the meantime, more fiber, water and daily movement help most people.
cut my finger slicing a bagel, it's bleeding a lot but i think it's not deep. how long should i press on it

Press firmly with a clean cloth or gauze for a full 10 minutes without lifting to check, and hold your hand above heart level while you do. Most finger cuts stop in that time even if they bled dramatically at first, since fingers have a rich blood supply. If it's still soaking through after 10 to 15 minutes of steady pressure, or the edges gape open, get it looked at because it may need stitches or glue.
Diabetic here, stomach flu, can't keep food down. Should I skip my insulin since I'm not eating?

Don't stop your insulin. Illness often raises blood sugar even when you aren't eating, and skipping it can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis. Check your glucose every three to four hours, test for ketones if you can, and keep sipping fluids, using sugar-containing ones if your levels are running low. Call your diabetes team for dose guidance today, and go to the ER if you can't keep fluids down, have moderate or high ketones, or feel confused or very weak.
Back pain plus I suddenly can't feel anything around my groin and I peed myself a little. Is this just a pinched nerve?

Go to the emergency department right now and don't wait to see if it settles. Back pain with numbness in the groin or saddle area and new bladder problems can mean cauda equina syndrome, where the nerves at the bottom of the spine are being compressed. It needs urgent imaging and often surgery within hours to prevent permanent loss of bladder, bowel or leg function. Tell them exactly these symptoms when you arrive.
Can I use leftover amoxicillin from last time for this fever?

Please don't. Leftover antibiotics are rarely the right drug or a full course. Most fevers are viral anyway, and taking a partial dose can mask a bacterial infection and help create resistance. If you think you need antibiotics, see a doctor who can test you and prescribe the right one. Bring the leftovers to a pharmacy take-back program instead.
My dad is 74 and on blood thinners, fell and now his hip hurts but he refuses to go in because he can still kind of stand. Should I push?

Yes, push. Being able to stand doesn't rule out a hip fracture in older adults, and some fractures only show up on imaging. Being on blood thinners also raises his risk of internal bleeding after a fall. He should be seen today, and if he hit his head at all, that's even more reason to go now. Missing a fracture can lead to a much worse break and a longer recovery.
My dad (74) keeps saying his stomach is upset and he's sweaty and tired, no chest pain though. Should I worry?

Yes, take this seriously. In older adults, a heart attack can show up as nausea, indigestion, sweating and fatigue without classic chest pain. If these symptoms are happening right now or came on suddenly, call 911 rather than driving him. Even if they've settled, he should be checked by a doctor today.
is it bad that I need like 10 hours of sleep to feel normal? I'm 34

Some people are genuinely long sleepers, but consistently needing 10 hours to feel normal at 34 is worth checking out. It can point to poor-quality sleep from apnea, thyroid problems, anemia, depression or medication side effects. If you wake unrefreshed even after a long night, or nod off easily during the day, mention it to your doctor and ask about basic bloodwork and a sleep evaluation. If you feel great on 10 hours and fine on weekdays, it may simply be how you're built.
Cut my leg on coral while snorkeling. It's shallow. Wash with seawater and keep going?

Seawater won't clean it properly, and coral cuts are notorious for getting infected and healing slowly because they leave tiny bits of coral and bacteria behind. Get out, rinse it well with fresh water and soap, scrub gently to clear debris, then apply antibiotic ointment and keep it covered. Stay out of the ocean for a day or two if you can. If it gets red, hot, swollen or starts oozing over the next several days, see a doctor because it may need antibiotics.
Is it ok to use my mom's leftover steroid cream on my rash? It's like clobetasol something

I'd hold off, because clobetasol is one of the strongest topical steroids available and can thin skin, cause stretch marks, or make some rashes like fungal infections much worse. Using it on the face, groin, or armpits is especially risky. For a mild itchy rash, over-the-counter 1% hydrocortisone is a much safer short-term option, and if it doesn't improve in a week or you don't know what the rash is, get it checked so you're treating the right thing.
Woke up with my big toe red, hot and swollen, can barely put a sheet on it. Had a few beers last night. What is this??

That sounds a lot like gout, which classically hits the big toe overnight and is often triggered by alcohol, especially beer. See a doctor or urgent care soon so they can confirm it and start proper treatment, because early treatment shortens the attack considerably. In the meantime, rest and elevate the foot, use a cool pack, drink water, and skip alcohol. If you also have a fever or feel generally unwell, get seen promptly, since a joint infection can look similar and needs urgent care.
toddler had a seizure with her fever, it stopped after a minute and now she's sleepy. is this normal??

Febrile seizures are fairly common in toddlers and usually harmless, and being sleepy afterward is expected. Your daughter still needs to see a doctor today, especially if this is her first one, so they can find the cause of the fever. Call 911 if a seizure lasts over 5 minutes, she has trouble breathing, or she doesn't start waking up normally within an hour or so.
Severe sudden back pain, between shoulder blades, feels like tearing, I'm sweaty. Is this a muscle thing?

Please call emergency services now. Sudden, severe, tearing pain between the shoulder blades with sweating can be a sign of an aortic dissection or a heart problem, both of which need immediate treatment. Don't drive yourself, and don't wait to see whether it passes.
chest pain when i breathe in deep. sharp. started yesterday

Sharp pain that worsens with a deep breath is often from a strained chest muscle or inflamed rib cartilage, but it can also come from pleurisy, pericarditis, a collapsed lung or a blood clot in the lung. Get seen today rather than waiting it out. Go to the ER right away if you're short of breath, have a racing heart, are coughing blood, have a swollen calf, or have recently had surgery, a long flight or started birth control.
neighbor's dog nipped my 6 year old on the leg, barely broke the skin. owner says the dog is vaccinated. we good?

Wash the spot thoroughly with soap and water, apply a little antibiotic ointment, and cover it. It's still smart to ask the owner for proof of rabies vaccination, and to call your pediatrician to check whether your child is up to date on tetanus. Watch the bite over the next few days for redness, warmth, swelling, or pus, and get it seen if any of those appear.
ok to take my levothyroxine with my morning coffee and calcium?

Not together. Coffee and calcium both reduce how much levothyroxine your body absorbs. Take it with plain water on an empty stomach, wait 30 to 60 minutes before coffee or breakfast, and take calcium or iron at least 4 hours apart. Whatever routine you pick, keep it consistent so your doctor can dose you accurately.
My dad is 78 and running 38.4 with some confusion today, he's usually sharp. Probably just a cold?

I wouldn't assume that. New confusion plus fever in an older adult can signal a serious infection like pneumonia, a urinary tract infection or sepsis. Older people often show confusion before more obvious symptoms appear. He should be evaluated today, and if he's very drowsy, breathing fast or getting worse, call emergency services.
ferret bite. hurts. need anything special?

Wash it thoroughly with soap and water and cover it, then watch it closely, because ferret bites can be deep and get infected. If the ferret is a pet that's vaccinated against rabies, that's reassuring. If it isn't vaccinated or you don't know its history, call your doctor or local health department about rabies, since ferrets can carry it. Deep punctures, or a bite on the hand, are worth a doctor's look either way.
I keep checking that the stove is off like 20 times before leaving. I know it's off. It's making me late to everything.

Checking over and over even when you know it's fine is a classic OCD pattern, and the more you check, the stronger the urge usually gets. The good news is that it's very treatable with a type of CBT called exposure and response prevention. See your doctor or look for a therapist trained in ERP. In the meantime, try checking once, deliberately and slowly, then saying out loud 'the stove is off' and leaving.
quick q is it normal to cry at work like once a week

It happens to plenty of people during rough patches, but crying weekly usually means something is overloading you, whether that's the job itself, burnout, or low mood spilling over from elsewhere. If it's been going on for more than a few weeks or comes with poor sleep, trouble enjoying things, or dread about going in, talk to your doctor or a therapist. Burnout and depression are both very treatable, and it's easier to deal with them early.
What's the fastest way to get rid of a cold sore before my wedding Saturday?

Start an antiviral as soon as you feel the tingle. Ask a doctor or pharmacist today about prescription valacyclovir, which can shorten an outbreak noticeably when taken early. Over-the-counter docosanol (Abreva) helps a little if you start it right away. Don't pick at it, and keep it moisturized so it doesn't crack. A green-tinted concealer applied with a clean disposable applicator can cover it well on the day.
my teenager gets migraines and wants to use her phone in a dark room the whole time lol

The dark room part is smart, but the phone screen can make migraine pain and light sensitivity worse. Encourage her to rest with her eyes closed, try a cold pack on her forehead and take her painkiller early, since dosing at the start works much better. If the migraines are frequent or affecting school, her doctor can discuss preventive options and a teen-appropriate treatment plan.
Teen son got a concussion at football Friday. Feels fine now, game is Thursday. Can he play?

Not until a doctor clears him, even if he feels fine. Concussion protocols require a stepwise return to play over several days after symptoms resolve. A second hit before the brain has healed can cause much worse injury, and rarely fatal swelling. Most states and school leagues legally require medical clearance anyway, so get him evaluated this week and follow the graduated plan.
slept in my contacts again and now my eye is red and painful and sensitive to light

Take the lenses out now and don't put any contacts back in until this is checked. Redness with pain and light sensitivity in a contact wearer can mean a corneal ulcer, and those can damage your vision quickly if they're not treated. Try to see an eye doctor today, not next week, and bring the lenses and case with you. Don't patch the eye or use redness-relief drops in the meantime.
My extended release pills are huge, can I crush them?

Generally no. Crushing or chewing an extended-release tablet can dump the whole day's dose at once, which can be dangerous with drugs like opioids, blood pressure meds or stimulants. Some ER tablets are scored and okay to split but not crush, so check the label or ask your pharmacist. They can also tell you about smaller, liquid or sprinkle versions.
Is it ok to drink energy drinks if I sometimes get palpitations?

Energy drinks are a common trigger for palpitations because of the high caffeine and other stimulants, so cutting them out is the simplest experiment you can run. Many people find their palpitations calm down noticeably within a week or two of stopping. If they continue after that, or ever come with chest pain, dizziness or fainting, see your doctor for a heart rhythm check.
Is it true beet juice lowers blood pressure? Could I use it instead of my meds?

Beet juice can lower blood pressure a few points because of its nitrates, so it's a reasonable addition to a healthy diet. The effect is modest and inconsistent, though, and it isn't a replacement for prescribed medication. Keep taking your meds, and if you want to rely less on them, ask your doctor about a plan that combines diet changes with home monitoring.
my 4 month old has a fever of 101 after her vaccines. what do i give her

A low fever after shots is common and usually settles within a day or two, and at 4 months infant acetaminophen is the option, dosed by her weight. Call your pediatrician to confirm the right dose, and don't give ibuprofen until she's 6 months old. Offer extra feeds and keep her lightly dressed, and call the doctor right away if the fever goes above 104°F, lasts more than 48 hours, or she's unusually limp, hard to wake, or crying inconsolably for over 3 hours.
my bf gets super angry and says it's because of his stress and that i should be more understanding

Stress can explain some irritability, but it doesn't excuse anger directed at you. If you feel afraid, are walking on eggshells, or he's controlling or threatening, that's a relationship safety issue. You deserve to feel safe. Talk to someone you trust or a domestic abuse helpline, and if you're ever in immediate danger, call emergency services.
My 2 year old keeps pulling at her ear and is cranky, slight fever. Ear infection probably. Wait it out?

Waiting a day or two is reasonable for many mild ear infections, as long as she's drinking, comfortable on a weight-appropriate dose of acetaminophen or ibuprofen, and the fever is modest. Call her doctor if it isn't improving within 48 hours or the fever is over 39°C (102°F). See them sooner if you notice ear drainage, unusual sleepiness, or swelling behind the ear. Many pediatricians prefer to look at kids under 2 anyway, so a quick call is worth it.
how much water should an old person drink a day? my mom barely drinks anything

Most older adults do well with about six to eight cups of fluid a day, though people with heart failure or kidney disease may have limits set by their doctor. Thirst signals weaken with age, so she probably isn't ignoring them so much as not feeling them. Leaving a water bottle within reach, offering drinks at set times, and counting soups, fruit and tea can help a lot. Watch for dark urine, dizziness or new confusion, which can signal dehydration that needs medical attention.
I'm 45 and recently had a mild heart attack. I'm desperate to get back to tennis. When's that realistic?

Many people do get back to sports like tennis after a mild heart attack, but the timing has to come from your cardiologist, usually after some tests to check how your heart handles exertion. The best route back is a cardiac rehabilitation program, which builds up your fitness safely under supervision and makes returning to tennis much more realistic. Ask your doctor for a referral if you haven't been offered one. Until you're cleared, stick with the activity level your care team recommends.
My wrist bp monitor and the doctor's reading are totally different. Which one do I trust?

Wrist monitors are more sensitive to positioning, and they often read off unless your wrist is held exactly at heart level. Bring your monitor to your next appointment and compare it against the doctor's measurement. If the readings don't match, switching to a validated upper-arm cuff is usually the more reliable choice.
My teen got diagnosed with chlamydia and is mortified. What actually happens next?

It's very common and very treatable, usually with a week of doxycycline or a single dose of azithromycin. They should avoid sex until seven days after treatment ends and their partners are treated, otherwise they can easily get reinfected. A retest in about three months is recommended. Being matter-of-fact and supportive will make them much more likely to keep getting tested in the future.
I keep catching colds every month. Is something wrong with my immune system?

Probably not, especially if you're around young kids, work in a school or healthcare, or take public transport often. Adults typically get two to four colds a year, and parents of small children get many more. Sleep, stress and handwashing make a real difference. It's worth seeing a doctor if your infections are unusually severe, keep needing antibiotics, or come with weight loss or night sweats.
I got a tattoo 5 days ago and there's a red streak going up my arm from it.

Get seen today, because a red streak spreading from a wound can mean the infection is moving through your lymphatic system, a condition called lymphangitis. It usually responds well to antibiotics but can get serious fast if ignored. Go to urgent care now, and go to the ER if you have fever, chills or the streak is spreading quickly. You can draw a line along the edge of the redness with a pen to track whether it's growing.
I've been constipated for 4 days. Just tell me the fastest fix

Fast and safe: drink a couple of big glasses of water, take a brisk walk, and try a dose of Miralax or a glycerin suppository, which usually work within hours to a day. Prunes or prune juice are a good natural option. Don't stack several laxatives at once. Severe pain, vomiting, a swollen belly or being unable to pass gas need prompt medical attention.
can kids take melatonin, my 6 year old fights bedtime every night

Melatonin can help certain kids, but check with your pediatrician before starting it. Dosing isn't well regulated in gummies, and accidental overdoses in children have risen sharply. For bedtime battles in a typical 6-year-old, a predictable routine usually works better: a consistent bedtime, a bath, books, dim lights and no screens for an hour before bed. Keep the bottle locked away if you do get the go-ahead to use it.
how high is too high for an adult fever

For most adults, the number itself matters less than how you're doing. Head to the ER for a fever of 103°F (39.4°C) or higher that won't come down with medicine, or for any fever at 104°F (40°C) or above. Get help regardless of the number if you have a stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, trouble breathing, a spreading rash, or chest pain. A fever lasting more than three days also warrants a doctor visit.
Can I take my prescribed sleeping pill with a couple beers at a wedding? I'll be home before I take it.

Don't combine them. Alcohol and sleeping pills are both sedatives, and together they can slow your breathing dangerously and increase risks like falls, blackouts and sleepwalking. On a night you drink, skip the pill. Ask your pharmacist about your specific medication, since some can't be taken even several hours after drinking.
I have some leftover amoxicillin from last year. Can I take it for my abscessed tooth until I can see someone?

Don't self-treat with leftover antibiotics, because an old partial course is usually the wrong amount and may be the wrong drug, and it can mask an infection without curing it. An abscess needs the source dealt with by draining, a root canal, or extraction, and a dentist or doctor can prescribe the right antibiotic if you actually need one. Call today for an urgent appointment, and go to the ER if you develop fever, spreading swelling, or trouble swallowing or breathing.
I'm 67 with COPD and my daughter says I shouldn't get the flu shot because it'll make me sick. True?

The flu shot can't give you the flu, because it contains no live virus. At most you might get a sore arm or feel tired for a day. With COPD, actually catching the flu can trigger a serious flare-up or pneumonia, so the shot is one of the most protective things you can do. Ask your doctor about the pneumonia and RSV vaccines too, since both are recommended for people your age with lung disease.
toddler wakes up screaming and doesn't recognize me, then remembers nothing in the morning. scary. normal??

That sounds like night terrors, which are common in young kids, look terrifying, but are generally harmless. They usually happen in the first few hours of sleep, and the child isn't actually awake, which is why they don't remember. Don't try to wake her; just keep her safe and wait it out, since it usually passes in a few minutes. Overtiredness is a big trigger, so an earlier bedtime often helps. Check with her pediatrician if episodes are very frequent, last a long time, involve rhythmic jerking, or she seems unwell in the day.
itchy bumps in lines on my wrists and between my fingers, worse at night, my roommate has it too

That pattern of itching that's worse at night, between the fingers and shared with someone you live with sounds a lot like scabies. See a doctor or pharmacist for a prescription treatment like permethrin cream, and both you and your roommate, plus any close contacts, need to treat at the same time. Wash bedding, towels and clothes from the past few days in hot water, or seal them in a bag for 72 hours. Expect the itch to linger for a couple of weeks even after successful treatment.
Stepped on a rusty nail in the garden. It's small. Fine?

Clean it well with soap and running water and keep an eye on it, but the bigger question is your tetanus shot. If it's been more than five years since your last booster, or you're not sure, get one within the next day or two. Puncture wounds are the riskiest kind for tetanus regardless of rust. Watch for redness spreading, warmth, pus or fever over the next few days, which would mean you need to be seen for possible infection.
Do I need a tetanus shot after a dog bite? Had one maybe 6 years ago.

For a bite, which counts as a dirty wound, doctors usually recommend a booster if your last tetanus shot was more than five years ago, so at six years you likely need one. It's quick and easy to get at urgent care or a pharmacy. While you're there, have the bite itself assessed, especially if it's deep or on your hand or face.
Had appendix surgery (keyhole) 10 days ago. When can I do crunches?

Hold off on crunches and heavy core work for now. Most surgeons say to wait around four to six weeks after keyhole surgery before doing those, to protect the incision sites from hernia. Walking is great right now, and you can gradually add light activity. Ask your surgeon at your follow-up exactly when to start ab exercises again.
Quick question: humidifier or no humidifier for a stuffy kid

Yes, a cool-mist humidifier can help loosen congestion, especially overnight. Use cool mist rather than warm, because hot-water units can burn a curious kid. Empty and clean it daily so it doesn't grow mold or bacteria. Saline drops and gentle suction before sleep also help a lot for little ones.
whats the fastest way to get a cut to stop bleeding

Firm, direct pressure with a clean cloth or gauze, held continuously for 10 minutes without lifting to check, plus raising the area above your heart. If blood soaks through, add more layers on top rather than removing the first one. Bleeding that spurts, soaks through quickly, or doesn't slow after 10 to 15 minutes of real pressure needs emergency care right away.
My grandma is 80, diabetic, says she's just really tired and a bit nauseous and short of breath today. No chest pain though so it's not her heart right?

Unfortunately it could still be her heart, because elderly people and diabetics often have heart attacks without typical chest pain. Sudden fatigue, nausea and breathlessness are common presentations in exactly her situation. Please get her assessed today, and call emergency services if the breathlessness is significant, she seems confused or clammy, or symptoms are getting worse.
My wife wants me to see someone for my anger. I think I'm fine, I just snap sometimes. Thoughts?

If your wife is bringing it up, it's probably affecting her more than it feels like from your side. Snapping regularly is often a sign of stress, poor sleep, depression or burnout, especially in men, where depression often shows up as irritability rather than sadness. Seeing someone doesn't mean you're broken, and anger-management work or short-term therapy can give you practical tools fast. Going is also one of the clearest ways to show her you take the relationship seriously.
dad fell in the bathroom last night, says hes fine. hes 79. do i need to do anything

Yes, have him checked by a doctor today, even if he seems okay. Older adults can have hidden fractures or slow bleeding in the head, especially if they take blood thinners. Call emergency services right away if he develops confusion, worsening headache, vomiting, unusual drowsiness or trouble walking. Once he's cleared, add grab bars and a non-slip mat, because a first fall is a strong predictor of the next one.
I'm 16 and my acne is destroying my confidence. My friend says I should just take her leftover Accutane. Is that ok?

Please don't take her Accutane. Isotretinoin is genuinely effective, but it's prescribed with monitoring for good reasons. It causes severe birth defects, it can affect liver function and cholesterol, and it can sometimes affect mood, so doctors check bloodwork and how you're feeling along the way. Tell a parent and ask for a dermatologist referral, since there's a lot they can try. Prescription treatments like topical retinoids, antibiotics or Accutane under supervision can really clear things up.
Elderly mom (82) keeps taking Benadryl every night to sleep, says it's just for allergies. Should I worry?

Yes, it's worth addressing. Diphenhydramine is on the list of drugs older adults should generally avoid, because it can cause confusion, falls, constipation and urinary retention, and long-term nightly use has been linked to higher dementia risk. Talk to her doctor about switching to a non-sedating antihistamine like loratadine for allergies. Her sleep problems need to be addressed separately and safely.
I've been on sertraline for 3 months and feel great now. Can I just stop?

Feeling great is a good sign that it's working, but don't stop abruptly. Quitting suddenly can cause dizziness, irritability and flu-like 'brain zaps', and stopping too early raises the risk of the depression coming back. Most guidelines suggest staying on it for at least six to twelve months after you feel better, then tapering slowly. Talk to your prescriber, who can plan a gradual taper when the timing is right.
hpv vaccine for my 11 yo daughter feels too early, she's a kid

That reaction is understandable, but 11 or 12 is recommended for good reasons. The vaccine works best long before any exposure, and kids this age produce such a strong immune response that they only need two doses instead of three. It protects against cancers later in life and says nothing about her behavior now. It's also recommended for boys, for the same reasons.
My legs feel crawly and I have to move them when I lie down at night. It's driving me crazy.

That sounds a lot like restless legs syndrome, which is common and treatable. It's worth seeing your doctor and getting your iron levels checked, especially ferritin, since low iron is a frequent and fixable cause. Some medications can make it worse, including certain antihistamines and antidepressants, so bring a list of what you take. In the meantime, gentle stretching, a warm bath, and cutting back on caffeine and alcohol help some people.
got hit in the head playing soccer yesterday, headache today and kinda foggy. fine to play tomorrow right?

No, those are concussion symptoms, so sit out until a doctor has cleared you. Playing again too soon risks a second hit while your brain is still healing, which can be dangerous and drags out recovery. Get checked soon, and go to the ER if the headache gets worse or you start vomiting repeatedly, feel confused, get very drowsy or notice slurred speech.
toddler threw up 3 times today, keeping nothing down. when do i worry

Right now the key is preventing dehydration, so give tiny sips of an oral rehydration solution like Pedialyte, about a teaspoon every few minutes, rather than big gulps. Call your pediatrician today if the vomiting continues past 12 to 24 hours or your toddler can't keep even small sips down. Go to the ER right away if you see no wet diaper in 6 to 8 hours, a dry mouth, no tears, unusual sleepiness, green or bloody vomit, or a swollen, hard belly. Also seek care if the vomiting follows a head bump or they might have swallowed something.
I think I have a UTI. Burning when I pee, going constantly. Can I just drink cranberry juice and wait it out?

Cranberry juice hasn't been shown to treat an active UTI, and leaving a bacterial bladder infection alone risks it spreading to your kidneys. Most UTIs clear fast with a short antibiotic course, and many pharmacies, telehealth services and clinics can prescribe the same day. If you develop fever, back or side pain, or vomiting, get seen urgently, because those point to a kidney infection.
is it ok to have one glass of wine a week while pregnant? my mom says she drank and i turned out fine

No amount of alcohol has been shown to be safe in pregnancy, so the standard advice is to skip it entirely. Plenty of people whose mothers drank turned out fine, but alcohol crosses the placenta and the risk of fetal alcohol spectrum effects doesn't have a known safe threshold. A good alcohol-free wine or a fancy mocktail can scratch the same itch for the next few months.
pregnant and our cat scratched me. any extra concern?

A scratch itself is low risk. Wash it well with soap and water and watch for signs of infection or a swollen lymph node nearby, which you should mention to your doctor. Scratches aren't a significant toxoplasmosis risk. That comes mainly from litter, so have someone else change the litter box if possible, or wear gloves and wash your hands well.
I've had mild stomach pain and lost 15 pounds in two months without trying. Probably nothing?

Unexplained weight loss of that amount with ongoing stomach pain shouldn't be brushed off, so please book a doctor's appointment soon, ideally within the next week or two. It could turn out to be something manageable like an ulcer, celiac disease or a thyroid issue, but it needs to be checked properly. Note any other changes, like bowel habits, appetite, blood in your stool or night sweats, and mention them at the visit. Seek care sooner if the pain gets severe.
Ear hurts after swimming, outside of ear is tender when I pull on it. Do I need antibiotics pills?

That sounds like swimmer's ear, an infection of the outer ear canal, and it's usually treated with prescription antibiotic ear drops rather than pills. See a doctor or urgent care to confirm and get the drops, and keep the ear dry in the meantime. Get seen sooner if swelling spreads to your face, you have a fever, or you have diabetes or a weakened immune system.
Wheezing for 3 days, inhaler helps for like an hour then it's back. Just keep puffing?

Needing your rescue inhaler every hour or two means your asthma is out of control, and that calls for medical attention today, not just more puffs. You may need oral steroids or a change in your controller medication to calm the inflammation. Call your doctor or go to urgent care now. If you're struggling to speak, your lips look bluish or the inhaler stops helping at all, go straight to the ER.
dry cough keeps me up every night, what's best to take before bed

A spoonful of honey in warm tea or on its own before bed is surprisingly effective for nighttime cough in adults and kids over one. Dextromethorphan, as in Robitussin DM or Delsym, can help if you want medicine, and propping your head up plus running a humidifier often makes a real difference. If it goes beyond three weeks or comes with wheezing or shortness of breath, see a doctor.
ok so how many layers do i bundle my feverish kid in to sweat it out

Don't bundle them. Piling on layers traps heat and can push the fever higher. Dress your child in light, breathable clothing with a single thin blanket. If they're shivering, give a light extra layer until it passes, then take it off once they warm up. Sweating it out isn't how fevers get better, but fluids and rest help.
I have back pain AND a fever of 101 and it hurts on one side near my ribs in back. Same thing?

That combination is worth taking seriously, because fever with pain in the flank area below the ribs can mean a kidney infection, not a back problem. Watch for burning when you pee, cloudy urine, nausea or chills, though you can have a kidney infection without all of those. See a doctor today or go to urgent care, since kidney infections need antibiotics promptly. Go to the ER if you're vomiting, can't keep fluids down or feel very unwell.
I'm 41 and pregnant for the first time, what extra stuff should I be doing

Congratulations! At 41 you'll likely be offered extra screening, such as cell-free DNA testing or diagnostic tests like CVS or amniocentesis. You'll also get closer monitoring for blood pressure, gestational diabetes and baby's growth later on. Get started with prenatal care early, take a prenatal with folic acid, and ask your OB about starting low-dose aspirin around 12 weeks, which is often recommended to lower preeclampsia risk. Plenty of people your age have healthy pregnancies, and the extra attention just helps catch things early.
whats a good diet after a stomach bug

Start with fluids, especially water, broth and oral rehydration drinks, then add bland, easy foods once you can keep things down. Good options are toast, rice, bananas, applesauce, crackers, eggs, plain chicken and oatmeal. Hold off on greasy food, alcohol, heavy dairy and very spicy meals for a couple of days. Most people are back to normal eating within two to three days.
can i make myself throw up after eating something sketchy to be safe

No, forcing yourself to vomit isn't recommended because it can injure your throat and esophagus and doesn't reliably clear anything out. Most mildly off food causes either nothing or a short bout of upset stomach that passes on its own. Stay hydrated and watch for symptoms. If you think you ate something actually toxic, like a poisonous mushroom or chemical, call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222 in the US) right away.
My 4 year old has a fever of 102 and I only have adult Tylenol. Can I just cut a pill in half?

Please don't. Adult tablets are 325 to 500 mg, and half of one can easily be more than a 4-year-old should get, so the dose depends on her weight. Children's liquid acetaminophen is cheap and sold at any pharmacy or 24-hour store, and a pharmacist can tell you the exact amount by weight. In the meantime, light clothing and fluids help. Call her doctor if the fever lasts more than three days, or if she seems very lethargic or has trouble breathing.
Dog bit my hand, small puncture but it broke the skin. I washed it. That's enough right?

Washing it well was the right first move, but dog bites that break the skin should still be seen by a doctor, especially on the hand. Mouth bacteria get pushed deep into the tissue and hand infections can turn nasty fast. You'll likely be offered preventive antibiotics and possibly a tetanus booster. A doctor can also advise on rabies risk if you don't know the dog's vaccination status. Keep it uncovered or lightly covered rather than taping it shut.
Headache every morning when I wake up for the past few weeks. Goes away by lunch. 52M.

Morning headaches that fade over the day are often linked to sleep apnea, especially if you snore or wake up unrefreshed. Teeth grinding, caffeine or alcohol withdrawal overnight, and high blood pressure are other common culprits. Since this is new and has gone on for weeks at your age, see your doctor for a blood pressure check and possibly a sleep study. Go sooner if you get vomiting, weakness, or vision changes.
grandma is 80 and confused and short of breath today, says chest feels funny. probably just old age?

Sudden confusion and breathlessness in an 80-year-old are not normal aging and need urgent attention, especially with chest discomfort. Older people often have heart attacks, infections or heart failure that show up exactly this way. Call emergency services or get her to an emergency department now. Bring a list of her medications.
my 3 month old has a temp of 100.6 rectal, she seems fine otherwise. can i just give tylenol and wait till morning?

At three months, a rectal temperature of 100.4°F or higher needs a call to your pediatrician or their after-hours line tonight, even if she seems fine, because young infants can have serious infections without looking very sick. Don't give Tylenol before you've talked to them, since it can mask the fever they need to assess. If she's hard to wake, feeding poorly, breathing fast or looks mottled, go straight to the ER.
Been constipated 5 days. Can I take double the laxative dose to get it over with?

Doubling the dose usually just trades constipation for painful cramping and diarrhea, and with stimulant laxatives it can throw off your electrolytes. Take the label dose of something gentle like polyethylene glycol (MiraLAX), drink plenty of water, and give it a day or so to work. If you have severe belly pain, vomiting, a swollen belly, or you can't pass gas at all, get seen right away, since those can signal a blockage. Five days with nothing working is also worth a call to your doctor.
how long after a bee sting should i worry about a reaction

Serious allergic reactions to stings usually start within minutes and almost always within the first hour. Watch for hives away from the sting site, swelling of your face or throat, trouble breathing, dizziness or vomiting, any of which means you should call emergency services immediately. A large red swelling right around the sting that grows over a day or two is common and usually not dangerous, and ice and an antihistamine can help with that.
type 2, thinking about trying keto. good idea?

Low-carb eating can lower blood sugar quite effectively and many people with type 2 do well on it. Talk to your doctor before you start, though, because if you take insulin or a sulfonylurea like glipizide, cutting carbs can cause lows unless your doses are reduced. If you take an SGLT2 inhibitor like Jardiance, strict keto raises your risk of ketoacidosis. With the right medication adjustments, it can be a reasonable thing to try.
Can I put my 18 month old in a front facing car seat now? She hates rear facing

Keep her rear-facing for now, because rear-facing seats protect a toddler's head, neck, and spine far better in a crash, and the recommendation is to stay rear-facing until she hits the seat's maximum height or weight limit, often around age 2 to 4. Bent legs or touching the seatback are fine and aren't a safety problem. Toys that attach to the seat, a back-seat mirror, and a sunshade can make the ride a lot more tolerable for both of you.
Hep B vaccine for adults—worth it if I'm married and monogamous?

Yes, hepatitis B vaccination is now recommended for all adults up to 59, and for those 60 and up with risk factors. Sex isn't the only route, since hep B can also spread through blood, shared razors or toothbrushes, and medical or dental procedures. It's a highly effective series that protects you for life, so it's worth asking your doctor or pharmacist about.
Back pain plus I suddenly can't fully control my bladder and my inner thighs feel numb. Probably just a pinched nerve, right?

Please don't wait on this one. Go to the emergency department now. Back pain together with new bladder trouble and numbness in the groin or inner thighs can mean cauda equina syndrome, where the nerves at the base of the spine are being compressed. It needs urgent imaging and often surgery within hours to prevent permanent bladder, bowel and leg problems. It may turn out to be less serious, but this is exactly the situation where you get seen today.
Diabetic, 55. Felt super breathless and wiped out doing chores but no chest pain. Is that a heart thing?

It might be. Diabetes can dull pain signals, so heart problems sometimes show up as breathlessness and exhaustion without classic chest pain. See your doctor soon, ideally within a day or two, and ask about an ECG and further heart testing. If it happens at rest, lasts, or comes with sweating, nausea or lightheadedness, go to the emergency department right away.
My buddy says to pour hydrogen peroxide on a cat bite and suck out the germs. Legit?

Skip both of those. Sucking the wound adds mouth bacteria, and peroxide damages healthy tissue without reaching deep enough to help with a puncture. The best first aid is to wash the bite under running water with plain soap for several minutes, then cover it. Cat bites often get infected anyway, especially on the hand, so have a doctor look at it today.
should i pop the blister from my burn its huge and annoying

Leave it intact, because that blister roof is a sterile barrier protecting the raw skin underneath from infection. Cover it loosely with a nonstick dressing so it doesn't get rubbed. If it pops on its own, gently wash it with soap and water, leave the flap of skin in place, and keep it covered. A blister larger than about a quarter or one on your hand, face or a joint deserves a quick look from a doctor or nurse.
I'm pregnant (14 weeks) and have a cold. What can I take?

Acetaminophen is the go-to for aches and fever in pregnancy, taken at the lowest dose that helps. Saline nasal spray, honey in warm water, a humidifier and rest are safe and work surprisingly well. Avoid ibuprofen and decongestants like pseudoephedrine unless your OB okays them. Run any cold medicine past your pharmacist before buying it, because combination products often hide ingredients you'd want to skip.
can i outgrow a shellfish allergy that started when I was 30?

It's possible but uncommon, because shellfish allergies that start in adulthood tend to stick around for life. Don't test it yourself by eating shrimp to see what happens, since reactions can be more severe than previous ones. If you want to know where you stand, an allergist can do testing and, if appropriate, a supervised food challenge where they're ready to treat a reaction.
how much melatonin for jet lag

Low doses work best for jet lag: 0.5 to 3 mg taken around bedtime at your destination for a few nights is plenty for most adults. More isn't better and tends to cause grogginess. Pair it with getting daylight at the right times in your new time zone. If you take blood thinners, seizure medication or are pregnant, check with a pharmacist first.
My 6 year old says her tooth hurts when she eats candy. Its a baby tooth so does it even matter?

It does matter, because baby teeth hold space for the adult teeth and a cavity can still turn into a painful infection that affects the tooth underneath. Pain with sweets is a classic early cavity sign, and at that stage it's usually a quick, easy filling. Book a dental visit in the next couple of weeks, and go sooner if you notice swelling, a pimple on the gum, or pain that wakes her at night.
forgot my birth control pill yesterday

If it's a combined pill and you only missed one, take it as soon as you remember, even if that means two pills today, then carry on as normal; you're still protected. If you've missed two or more in a row, take the most recent one and use condoms for the next seven days. Emergency contraception may be worth considering if you had unprotected sex in the past few days. Progestin-only minipills have a much stricter three-hour window, so if that's what you take, use backup for two days and check your leaflet or call your pharmacist.
I just got back from a trip to Ghana two weeks ago and now I have fever and chills. Probably nothing?

Fever after travel to West Africa needs prompt medical attention because it could be malaria, which can become dangerous fast, even if you took preventive pills. See a doctor today and tell them right away where you traveled so they can test you. Don't wait to see if it passes.
I'm 70 and keep getting rough scaly spots on my forehead and hands. Just old age?

Rough, scaly spots on sun-exposed skin at your age are often actinic keratoses, which are sun damage that can occasionally turn into squamous cell skin cancer. They're very common and easily treated with freezing or prescription creams. Book a dermatology skin check to get them treated and to look over the rest of your skin. Daily sunscreen and a hat going forward will help keep new ones from forming.
how long should i keep a bandage on a cut, someone told me to let it air out

Keeping it covered actually works better for most cuts and scrapes, because a moist, protected wound heals faster and scars less than one left to dry out and scab. Change the bandage daily or whenever it gets wet or dirty, and add a thin layer of petroleum jelly each time. Once new skin has formed and it's no longer open, usually after several days to a week, you can leave it uncovered. If it gets increasingly red, swollen or oozy, have it checked.
My son got bitten by a friend's dog on the face at a birthday party. It's a few small cuts near his eye. He's 4.

Clean it gently with water, press with a clean cloth if it's bleeding, and take him to urgent care or the ER today. Face bites in young kids need a professional exam, and anything near the eye should be checked for deeper injury. Get the dog owner's contact info and the dog's rabies vaccination records, since the doctor and possibly the health department will want them.
Baby has a soft bulge near her belly button when she cries. 6 weeks old.

That sounds like an umbilical hernia, which is very common in newborns and usually closes on its own by age 3 to 5. Mention it at her next checkup so her doctor can confirm it. Skip home remedies like taping a coin over it. Get her seen urgently if the bulge becomes hard, discolored or painful, or if she starts vomiting, because those can be signs the hernia is trapped.
My 4 month old has a fever of 100.6. Can I just give her some baby Tylenol and see how she does overnight?

Giving infant acetaminophen at the weight-based dose on the package is fine for comfort at 4 months, but you should still call your pediatrician's after-hours line tonight rather than just waiting it out. A fever in a baby this young warrants a professional opinion, especially if she's feeding poorly, unusually sleepy, or hard to console. If she's under 3 months, struggling to breathe, or has a rash that doesn't fade when pressed, go straight to the ER.
my 7 year old has a headache and a fever and keeps saying his neck hurts when he looks down. probably just a bug right?

It could be a virus, but fever plus headache plus neck pain when bending the head forward is a classic warning sign of meningitis, so this needs a doctor today. Take him to urgent care or the ER now, and go straight to emergency if he gets drowsy, confused, very sensitive to light, or develops a rash that doesn't fade when you press a glass against it. It's far better to have it checked and be told it's nothing.
My 70yo dad has a UTI and is suddenly really confused and not making sense. Is that normal?

Sudden confusion in an older adult with an infection is common, but it's a sign the infection is affecting him significantly, so he needs medical attention today, not tomorrow. Take him to urgent care or the ER, especially if he has a fever, low blood pressure, fast breathing or isn't drinking. Confusion can also signal sepsis or another problem, like a stroke, so it's not something to manage at home.
I'm 58 and lately I've had heartburn almost every day, which is new for me. I've lost a bit of weight too without trying. Probably just stress right?

Stress could be part of it, but new daily heartburn after 50 combined with unexplained weight loss is a combination doctors want to look at properly, not guess about. Book an appointment soon and mention both symptoms specifically, because they may want to do an endoscopy to check your esophagus and stomach. Most of the time the cause turns out to be treatable, like an ulcer or reflux damage, but it's worth ruling out the serious stuff early.
my 2 month old feels hot, thermometer says 100.6 rectal. should i just give tylenol and see how she does overnight?

Don't wait this one out. A rectal temperature of 100.4°F or higher in a baby under 3 months needs to be checked by a doctor right away, so call your pediatrician's after-hours line now or head to the ER. Hold off on Tylenol until a doctor tells you to, because it can mask the fever they need to evaluate, and infants this young can get seriously ill quickly even when they seem okay.
I get aura before my migraines. Is the combined birth control pill okay for me?

Migraine with aura is generally a reason to avoid estrogen-containing pills, because the combination raises stroke risk. Make sure whoever prescribes your contraception knows about the aura, since progestin-only pills, implants and IUDs are usually safe alternatives. If you're already on a combined pill, don't just stop it, but see your doctor soon to switch.
I've been getting angry and punching walls when stressed. Didn't hurt anyone. Should I worry?

Yes, it's worth taking seriously. Punching walls can break your hand, and anger that comes out physically tends to escalate, even if no one has been hurt so far. Work on catching the early signs, like a tight jaw or heat in your chest, and step away to cool down before you reach that point. Anger management or a therapist can teach you skills that really work, and your doctor can check for underlying stress, depression, or substance issues that might be feeding it.
is it safe to get a massage for chronic migraines or is that woo

It's not woo, but it's not a cure either. Massage, especially of the neck and shoulders, has decent evidence for reducing tension-type headaches and can lower migraine frequency for some people by easing muscle tension and stress. It works best as an add-on to a plan from your doctor, and a licensed massage therapist is a safe bet. Just avoid forceful neck cracking or manipulation, which carries a small risk of injuring the arteries in the neck.
nosebleed won't stop, been like 5 min

Sit up and lean forward rather than back, so you don't swallow blood. Pinch the soft part of your nose firmly, just below the bony bridge, and hold continuous pressure for a full 10 to 15 minutes by the clock without peeking. A cold pack on the bridge can help. If it's still going after 20 to 30 minutes of proper pressure, or it started after a hard hit to the face, get medical help.
My 84 year old dad keeps choking a little when he eats or drinks. He laughs it off. Should I?

Don't laugh it off. Frequent coughing or choking while eating can signal a swallowing problem called dysphagia, which raises the risk of aspiration pneumonia in older adults. Ask his doctor for a referral to a speech-language pathologist, who can test his swallowing and suggest safer food textures or techniques. Until then, have him sit fully upright, take small bites and eat slowly without distractions.
do those cold patch things actually work for migraine

They can help. Cold on the forehead, temples or back of the neck numbs the area and constricts blood vessels, and many people get meaningful relief, especially when it's paired with medication taken early. They're cheap and safe, so they're worth trying. Keep a cloth between ice and your skin and limit it to about 15 to 20 minutes at a time.
I just got out of the hospital after a week with COVID pneumonia. What exercise should I do?

Start very gently: short walks around your home a few times a day, plus breathing exercises if the hospital gave you any. Ask your doctor about a referral to pulmonary rehab, which is designed for exactly this kind of recovery. Build up slowly over weeks, not days. Contact a doctor if you get worsening breathlessness, chest pain, or swelling in your legs.
took 2 energy drinks and now my heart is pounding and i feel shaky

That's a common reaction to a big caffeine and stimulant load, so stop all caffeine for the rest of the day, sip water, and sit somewhere calm while it wears off over a few hours. Slow breathing can help settle the shakiness. Get emergency care if you have chest pain, fainting, a heartbeat that feels very irregular or stays above about 150, confusion, or vomiting, since too much caffeine can trigger dangerous rhythms.
toothache woke me up at 2am, can't sleep, nothing open. help

Take ibuprofen with acetaminophen if they're safe for you, hold a cold pack on your cheek for 15 minutes at a time, and sleep with your head propped up, since lying flat can make the throbbing worse. A dab of clove oil or an OTC benzocaine gel on the area can take the edge off. Call a dentist as soon as offices open, and go to the ER now if you have facial swelling, fever, or trouble swallowing or breathing.
can I superglue a cut closed instead of getting stitches? it's on my knee, kinda gaping

Medical skin glue exists, but a gaping cut over a joint like the knee is a poor candidate, because every bend pulls it open and household superglue isn't made for wounds. Get it closed properly at urgent care, ideally within about 6 to 8 hours of the injury. They'll clean it thoroughly and decide on stitches or strips. Until then, keep pressure on it and cover it with a clean dressing.
I read vaccines cause autism. My sister won't vaccinate her twins. Is there anything to it?

No, this has been studied in millions of children across many countries and there's no link between vaccines, including MMR, and autism. The original 1998 study claiming a link was retracted after it was found to be fraudulent, and its author lost his medical license. If your sister is open to it, encourage her to bring her specific worries to a pediatrician she trusts, because a calm conversation usually works better than pressure.
do allergy shots actually work or is it a money grab

They genuinely work for many people, with solid evidence for pollen, dust mite, pet dander and insect venom allergies. They're one of the few treatments that changes the underlying allergy rather than just masking symptoms. The catch is commitment, since it usually means regular injections for three to five years and waiting in the clinic after each one in case of a reaction. If daily meds aren't controlling your symptoms, it's worth a conversation with an allergist.
Teen son has terrible acne and is getting really down about it. OTC stuff hasn't worked after like 4 months.

Four months of over-the-counter treatment without results is a good reason to see a doctor, and so is acne affecting his mood. Prescription options like topical retinoids, antibiotic combinations, or isotretinoin for severe or scarring acne work far better than what's on the shelf. Start with his GP and ask for a dermatology referral if needed. Keep an eye on his mood too, and if he seems withdrawn or hopeless, mention that at the appointment, since acne genuinely affects teens' mental health.
got my wisdom tooth out 4 days ago and the pain suddenly got way worse and my breath smells terrible

That pattern of pain getting worse around day three or four, along with bad taste or smell, sounds a lot like dry socket. Call your oral surgeon today, because they can rinse the socket and pack it with a medicated dressing that often brings relief within hours. Until then avoid straws, smoking and spitting hard, and take your pain medication as directed.
My legs feel crawly and I have to move them at night, it keeps me from falling asleep. What is this?

That sounds a lot like restless legs syndrome, which causes an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, typically in the evening or at night, that's relieved by movement. It's often linked to low iron, so ask your doctor to check your ferritin level, as iron supplements can help a lot if it's low. Caffeine, alcohol, nicotine, and some antihistamines and antidepressants can make it worse. A doctor can confirm the diagnosis and discuss treatment if it's affecting your sleep regularly.
can i take my wife's nitroglycerin? i've got chest pain and she has a prescription

Don't take her nitroglycerin, because it can drop your blood pressure dangerously, especially if you've taken anything like Viagra or Cialis recently, and it could mask what's really going on. If you're having chest pain right now, call emergency services and chew a regular aspirin if you're not allergic or on blood thinners. Paramedics can safely give nitroglycerin once they've checked you over.
just found out im pregnant, had like 4 drinks at a party last weekend before i knew. did i ruin everything

Almost certainly not, and this happens to a huge number of people before they know they're pregnant. In the first few weeks after conception, the embryo isn't yet sharing your blood supply the way it will later, and a single night of drinking is very unlikely to cause harm. The important thing is to stop drinking now and mention it at your first prenatal appointment so your provider has the full picture.
My chest hurts when I breathe in deep and I've had a fever and cough with yellow-green stuff for 4 days. Just ride it out?

Don't just ride this one out, because chest pain with deep breaths, fever and a productive cough for several days can point to pneumonia. See a doctor today, at your regular office or urgent care, so they can listen to your lungs and possibly get an X-ray. If you're short of breath at rest, your lips look blue, or you feel confused or very weak, go to the ER. Pneumonia is very treatable when caught early.
Is it ok to give my 10 month old a little honey for his cough? my mom swears by it

Not yet. Honey shouldn't be given to babies under 12 months because of the risk of infant botulism, which is rare but serious. After his first birthday it's a great option, about half a teaspoon before bed. For now, use saline drops, a cool-mist humidifier, and plenty of breast milk or formula. Call his doctor if he's breathing hard, has a fever over 102°F, or isn't feeding well.
can i double up my antibiotic to kick this infection faster

No. Doubling the dose won't clear the infection faster, and it raises your risk of side effects like diarrhea, nausea and, with some antibiotics, more serious toxicity. Antibiotics work by keeping a steady level in your body over the full course, so take them exactly as prescribed. If you're not improving after two or three days, call your doctor.
