Stomach cramps and vomiting after eating leftover rice from 2 days ago. When will this end

That sounds like food poisoning, possibly from Bacillus cereus, which grows in rice left at room temperature. It usually passes within 24 hours. Sip water or an oral rehydration drink in small amounts and hold off on food until the vomiting settles. See a doctor if you can't keep fluids down for more than a few hours, you see blood, you stop urinating, or it lasts beyond a day or two.
can i drink baking soda water for indigestion? my mom always did

Occasionally, yes. Half a teaspoon dissolved in a full glass of water is a traditional antacid that works. It's very high in sodium, though, so it's a poor choice if you have high blood pressure, heart or kidney issues, or are pregnant. Don't use it regularly or take it on an overly full stomach. For frequent indigestion, a standard antacid is safer, and if you need one often, talk to your doctor.
worst headache of my life came on in like a second while lifting weights, should i just sleep it off?

Please don't sleep this one off. A sudden, explosive headache that peaks within seconds, especially during exertion, is called a thunderclap headache and can signal bleeding in or around the brain. Call emergency services or get someone to drive you to the ER right now, and don't drive yourself.
My mom is 78, on chemo, and her cat scratched her leg. She says it's nothing. Should I push her to get it looked at?

Yes, gently push, because chemotherapy weakens the immune system and makes even small pet wounds more likely to become serious infections. Clean it well with soap and water and call her oncology team today, as they often want to know about any break in the skin. They may want to examine it or start antibiotics preventively. Any fever, redness spreading or feeling unwell should be treated as urgent.
My dad is 74, fell yesterday, says his hip hurts but he can still walk a bit so he refuses to see anyone. Am I overreacting?

You're not overreacting, because some hip fractures in older adults still allow walking at first, especially impacted fractures that can shift and worsen. He should get an X-ray today, through his doctor, urgent care, or the ER if the pain is significant. Catching a fracture early is far better than having it displace. If he's stubborn, framing it as a quick check to rule things out sometimes helps.
I've been awake for 30 hours studying. Can I just drive home quick, it's only 15 minutes

Don't drive. After 30 hours awake, your impairment is comparable to being over the legal alcohol limit, and microsleeps can hit without warning even on a short, familiar route. Get a ride, take a cab or rideshare, or nap for at least 20 to 30 minutes before you even consider it. Fifteen minutes is plenty of time to crash.
My anxiety makes my chest hurt. How do I know it's anxiety and not my heart?

You can't reliably tell them apart from the inside, which is why new or unexplained chest pain should get checked by a doctor at least once. Call emergency services right away if the pain is crushing, spreads to your arm, jaw, or back, or comes with sweating, shortness of breath, or nausea, especially if you're over 40 or have risk factors. Once a doctor has ruled out a heart problem, anxiety chest pain usually becomes much less scary, and it eases with breathing techniques and treatment for the anxiety.
whats the fastest way to lower my blood pressure before my DOT physical tomorrow

You can't safely fix your true blood pressure overnight, but you can avoid falsely raising it. Skip caffeine, nicotine, decongestants and energy drinks beforehand, sleep well, and sit quietly for a few minutes before the reading. Don't take extra or someone else's medication to scrape through, since that can make you dizzy or faint. If you're truly running high, getting it treated is what keeps your card, and your health, secure long term.
I've had a new headache for 3 weeks, I'm 67, and my scalp is tender when I brush my hair and my jaw hurts chewing

Please see a doctor today or tomorrow, not next month. A new headache after 50 with scalp tenderness and jaw pain when chewing is a classic picture of giant cell arteritis, an inflammation of the arteries that can cause sudden permanent vision loss if untreated. A blood test and prompt steroid treatment can protect your eyesight. Go to the emergency room immediately if you notice any vision changes.
knee gave out and made a loud pop during basketball, now it's swelling fast. should I just walk it off?

Don't walk this one off. A pop followed by rapid swelling is a classic sign of a ligament injury, often the ACL, or sometimes a meniscus tear. Ice it, keep it elevated, use crutches if it feels unstable, and see a doctor or sports medicine clinic within a few days for an exam and possibly an MRI. Pushing through it with an unstable knee can damage the cartilage further.
My dad (72, diabetic) has a small sore on his foot that won't heal for 3 weeks. He says it's nothing.

A sore that hasn't healed in three weeks on a diabetic foot is something, and it needs a doctor or podiatrist soon, ideally this week. Diabetes reduces both feeling and blood flow in the feet, so small wounds can become serious infections or ulcers without much pain. Go in the same day if you see redness spreading, swelling, pus, a bad smell or fever. Until he's seen, keep it clean and covered and have him stay off it as much as possible.
pregnant, 32 weeks, bp was 145/95 at my appointment and now I have swelling in my face. midwife said recheck next week but I feel off

Trust that feeling and call your midwife or labor and delivery unit today, not next week. High blood pressure plus new facial swelling at 32 weeks can be a sign of preeclampsia, and it needs prompt checking. Go in right away if you also get a severe headache, vision changes, pain under your right ribs, or sudden shortness of breath.
sliced my thumb cutting a bagel, it's kind of gaping open. butterfly strips enough or do I need stitches

If the edges gape apart when your thumb is relaxed, it's deeper than about a quarter inch, or it won't stop bleeding after 10 minutes of firm pressure, you most likely need stitches or glue. Get it seen within roughly 6 to 8 hours, since closure gets riskier the longer a wound sits open. Also go promptly if you have any numbness or trouble bending the thumb, because that can mean a nerve or tendon is involved.
how do i get a splinter out of a squirmy 5yo

Wash the area, then try a piece of tape pressed on and pulled off first, since that works surprisingly often for tiny splinters. For bigger ones, use tweezers cleaned with rubbing alcohol and pull at the same angle the splinter went in, with good light. Distract them with a show, and numb the spot with ice for a minute first. See a doctor if it's deep, under a nail, or the area gets red, swollen, or starts to ooze.
Is it normal for my 76yo mom to sleep like 11 hours a day now?

Older adults don't need more sleep than younger ones, so a jump to 11 hours is worth bringing up with her doctor rather than writing off as age. Depression, thyroid problems, anemia, heart issues, sleep apnea, and medication side effects can all cause it, and most are treatable. If it came on suddenly or she's also confused or hard to wake, get her seen promptly.
quick q - left side chest pain only when i press on a spot on my ribs, otherwise fine

Pain you can reproduce by pressing one spot on the ribs is usually musculoskeletal, often costochondritis or a muscle strain, rather than your heart. Ibuprofen, warmth and avoiding heavy lifting for a week or two usually help. See a doctor if it lingers beyond a couple of weeks, and seek care promptly if you develop breathlessness, fever, or pain with exertion.
heard you can get measles titers instead of a booster. worth it?

For most adults, it's easier to get an MMR dose than a titer test, because extra MMR doses are safe even if you're already immune, and the titer adds a blood draw and often costs more. A titer can make sense if you need proof of immunity for work or school and don't have vaccination records, or if you're planning a pregnancy and want to check rubella immunity. One important exception is pregnancy or a weakened immune system, because MMR is a live vaccine and isn't given in those cases, so talk to your doctor first if either applies.
fever 39.5 since this morning, i'm 34, can i just double up on ibuprofen to knock it out faster?

Don't double the dose. Taking more than the label amount raises the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney strain without bringing the fever down any faster. For most adults, 400 mg every 6 to 8 hours is enough, and you can alternate with acetaminophen if you need extra relief, staying within each drug's daily limit. Drink plenty of fluids, and see a doctor if the fever lasts more than three days or you develop a stiff neck, confusion or trouble breathing.
newborn sleeps better on her tummy, is that ok if i watch her

Babies should be put down on their backs for every sleep, naps included, until they're one year old, because tummy sleeping significantly raises the risk of SIDS. You can't reliably watch her every moment, and SIDS can happen silently. Use a firm, flat mattress with only a fitted sheet, and no pillows, bumpers or blankets. Supervised tummy time while she's awake is great for her development, so give her plenty of that during the day.
can i just use my old expired epipen, it's only a year past

In an emergency, use an expired auto-injector if it's the only one you have, because it likely still contains some active medicine and is much better than nothing. Call emergency services right after, since its effect may be weaker. Don't rely on it going forward, though: get a refill now, and check that the solution in the window is clear, since discolored epinephrine has degraded.
pain in my chest when i press on it, been sore since i moved furniture saturday. 40s

Pain you can reproduce by pressing on a specific spot, starting after heavy lifting, is most likely a strained muscle or irritated rib cartilage. Rest, heat or ice, and an over-the-counter anti-inflammatory if you can take one usually help it settle over one to two weeks. The catch is that being sore to the touch doesn't completely rule out a heart cause, so get checked promptly if the pain spreads to your arm, jaw or back, comes on with exertion rather than movement, or comes with shortness of breath, sweating or nausea.
My 15 year old daughter has been wearing long sleeves in summer and I found a razor blade in her room. I don't know what to do.

Those are real warning signs of self-harm, and how you approach her matters a lot, so start calmly and without anger. Tell her you noticed and that you love her, then ask how she's doing rather than demanding she promise to stop. Book an appointment with her doctor or a child and adolescent mental health service soon so she gets proper support, and check whether any wounds need medical care. If she talks about wanting to die or you think she's in immediate danger, call emergency services or a crisis line right away.
quick q, can I take my magnesium and my thyroid pill together in the morning

Better not to, because magnesium can bind to levothyroxine and reduce how much your body absorbs. Take the thyroid pill on an empty stomach with water, and keep magnesium, calcium, and iron at least four hours away from it. Moving the magnesium to the evening is the easiest fix, and it may even help you sleep.
I took my bp pill twice by accident this morning. what do i do

For most people one double dose isn't dangerous, but call your pharmacist or a poison control center to check, since it depends on the drug and dose. Over the next several hours, watch for dizziness, fainting, a very slow heartbeat or feeling faint when standing. Get up slowly and avoid driving. Skip nothing and double nothing next time; just take your usual dose tomorrow unless you're told otherwise.
Big painful burn on my hand from a pan, skin's white and doesn't hurt in the middle. Butter on it?

Skip the butter, which traps heat and raises infection risk. A white patch that doesn't hurt can mean a deep burn that has damaged the nerves, so get it seen at urgent care or the emergency department today. Hand burns can affect function and often need specialist care. On the way, run the burn under cool tap water for 20 minutes, remove any rings, and cover it loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy cloth.
I keep having intrusive thoughts about hurting my newborn. I would never do it. Am I a monster?

No, you are not a monster. Unwanted, horrifying thoughts about harm coming to a baby are very common in new parents, and the fact that they disgust and frighten you is a sign they go against everything you want. They're often part of postpartum anxiety or OCD, which are very treatable. Please mention it to your doctor, midwife or health visitor. They hear this often and won't take your baby away for having intrusive thoughts. If the thoughts ever stop feeling unwanted, or you feel disconnected from reality or confused, get help urgently, because that's a different situation.
4yo pulling at her ear and cranky, low fever 100.4, had a cold last week. should I take her in tonight?

That sounds a lot like an ear infection, which often follows a cold, and it usually doesn't need an ER visit tonight if she's drinking and acting reasonably okay between fussy spells. Give her a weight-appropriate dose of children's acetaminophen or ibuprofen for the pain, then call her pediatrician in the morning. Many mild cases clear up on their own, but the doctor should check her ear. Go in sooner if her fever goes above 102, she seems very ill, fluid drains from the ear, or there's swelling behind the ear.
cough wont go away, its been like 5 weeks now. no fever. im fine otherwise

Five weeks is long enough that it's worth getting checked, even if you feel fine otherwise. Coughs often linger a few weeks after a cold, but past three weeks doctors start looking for things like postnasal drip, asthma, acid reflux, side effects from blood pressure meds like lisinopril, or occasionally whooping cough. Most of these are easy to treat once identified. See someone sooner if you start coughing up blood, losing weight, or getting short of breath.
Warts on my fingers. Duct tape thing legit or nah

Duct tape has mixed evidence, so it's harmless to try but don't expect miracles. Over-the-counter salicylic acid is the better-proven option if you use it daily after soaking and filing the wart, and keep going for several weeks. Use a dedicated emery board, don't use it anywhere else, since warts can spread. See a doctor if they're spreading fast, painful or not budging after a few months, or straight away if you're diabetic or have poor circulation.
I've had IBS for years. New thing though: waking up at night needing to poop and there's some blood. Same old IBS?

I wouldn't put this down to IBS, because IBS classically doesn't wake people from sleep and doesn't cause bleeding. Those two new symptoms are red flags that deserve a fresh look, for things like inflammatory bowel disease or other bowel conditions. Make an appointment soon and tell your doctor specifically that the pattern has changed.
Had appendix out 3 weeks ago (laparoscopic). Feeling great. Can I deadlift?

Hold off on deadlifts for now. Even after keyhole surgery, the incision sites in your abdominal wall usually need four to six weeks before heavy lifting, and straining too early risks a hernia. Walking and light activity are great at this stage. Check with your surgeon about the exact timeline for going back to heavy weights.
what's the fastest way to kill a tension headache, I have a meeting in 20 min

Take a standard dose of ibuprofen or acetaminophen with a full glass of water right now, since they take 20 to 30 minutes to kick in. While you wait, step away from the screen, drop your shoulders and gently massage your temples and the base of your skull. A few minutes of slow breathing and a snack if you've skipped a meal can take the edge off too.
I think I'm allergic to penicillin because I got a rash as a kid. My doctor wants to test it. Is that even worth bothering?

Yes, it's genuinely worth doing, because the large majority of people labeled penicillin-allergic turn out not to be allergic when tested, especially when the reaction was a childhood rash. Carrying that label often means getting broader, more expensive or less effective antibiotics later, with more side effects. The testing is done in a controlled setting where staff can handle any reaction, so it's a low-risk way to potentially open up much better treatment options.
Baby has been spitting up a lot after every feed, she's 6 weeks. Normal?

Lots of spit-up is very common at this age because the muscle at the top of the stomach is still immature, and if she's gaining weight and seems content, it's usually just messy rather than a problem. Keeping her upright for 20 to 30 minutes after feeds and burping her more often can help. Call her doctor if the vomiting becomes forceful or projectile, is green or bloody, or she's fussy during feeds or not gaining weight, because those point to something that needs checking.
is it normal for my heart to skip a beat sometimes? i'm 24 and it happens maybe a few times a week

Occasional skipped or fluttery beats are very common in healthy young people and are usually harmless extra beats called ectopics, often triggered by caffeine, alcohol, stress or poor sleep. Cutting back on those triggers often makes them less frequent. It's still worth mentioning to your doctor at your next visit, and get seen sooner if the skips come with fainting, chest pain, shortness of breath, or long runs of racing heartbeat.
my throat feels kinda tight and scratchy after eating a new curry, im fine otherwise though. overreacting?

Throat tightness after a new food isn't something to brush off, even if everything else feels fine, because it can be an early sign of a serious reaction. Call 911 right away if it worsens, or if you notice trouble swallowing, a hoarse voice, wheezing, swelling, dizziness, or hives. If you have epinephrine, use it. Don't stay alone or go to sleep for the next few hours. Even if it fades, see a doctor about allergy testing, since curries can contain nuts, sesame, mustard, or shellfish.
What's actually considered normal blood pressure these days? I keep hearing different numbers.

Under current US guidelines, normal is below 120/80. Readings of 120–129 systolic with a diastolic under 80 count as elevated, and 130/80 or higher is stage 1 hypertension. Other countries draw some of these lines a little differently, which is part of why you hear different numbers. What matters most is the pattern across several readings taken on different days, not any single number.
I'm on chemo, can I get the nasal flu vaccine instead of the shot? Hate needles

Please stick with the injection, because the nasal spray is a live vaccine and isn't recommended for people with weakened immune systems, including during chemo. The flu shot is inactivated, so it's safe for you and especially important since flu can hit hard during treatment. Talk to your oncology team about timing, since they may want it given at a particular point in your cycle, and the needle is quick.
how do i get a splinter out

Wash the area, then use tweezers wiped with rubbing alcohol to grab the exposed end and pull it out at the same angle it went in. If it's just under the skin, a needle cleaned the same way can gently lift the surface to expose it. Wash again afterward and cover it. Leave deep splinters, ones under a fingernail, or glass and metal fragments to a doctor.
Weird itchy welts popped up all over after I ate shrimp an hour ago. Lips feel kind of tingly.

Hives plus tingly lips after shrimp could be the start of a serious allergic reaction, so take it seriously right now. If you have trouble breathing, throat tightness, a hoarse voice, swelling of your tongue, vomiting, or you feel faint, call emergency services immediately and use an epinephrine auto-injector if you have one. If it's only the welts and mild tingling, take a non-drowsy antihistamine like cetirizine and have someone stay with you while you get checked urgently. Avoid shellfish until an allergist has assessed you.
My doctor diagnosed me with mono 3 weeks ago and I feel totally fine now. I play rugby. Season starts Saturday.

Please don't play Saturday without clearance from your doctor. Mono can swell your spleen even when you feel completely well, and a hit in rugby could rupture it, which is a genuine emergency. Most guidelines say no contact sports for at least three to four weeks from when symptoms started, and often longer, with a doctor confirming it's safe. Call them this week and ask specifically about returning to contact play.
My dad is 82 and keeps forgetting whether he took his pills, so sometimes he takes them twice. Is that a big deal?

It can be, especially with blood pressure drugs, blood thinners or diabetes medication, where a double dose can cause dizziness, falls, bleeding or dangerously low blood sugar. A weekly pill organizer with morning and evening compartments solves most of this, and many pharmacies will pre-pack doses into dated blister packs for free or cheap. Mention the double-dosing to his doctor or pharmacist so they know which of his meds are the riskiest to repeat.
can i just double my sertraline dose this week? exams are killing me and i feel awful

Don't double it on your own, because jumping the dose can cause side effects like agitation, stomach upset and poor sleep, and it won't kick in fast enough to help this week anyway. Call your prescriber and tell them exams are hitting you hard, since they can adjust your dose safely if it's needed. For now, short study blocks with real breaks, regular meals and protecting your sleep will do more for exam stress than an extra pill.
Is it true you shouldn't exercise for a while after a viral infection because of heart problems? I'm a bit scared now

There's a real but uncommon risk, since some viral infections can cause inflammation of the heart muscle (myocarditis), and intense exercise during that time can be dangerous. The practical rule is to avoid hard exercise while you have a fever or body-wide symptoms and to ease back in gradually once you're better. If you have chest pain, palpitations, fainting or unusual breathlessness during or after exercise, stop and see a doctor promptly. For most people who recover normally and ramp up gradually, it's not something to lose sleep over.
hit my head on a cabinet yesterday, now headache keeps getting worse and i threw up twice. i'm 70 and on blood thinners

Go to the emergency department now. A worsening headache and vomiting after a head knock, especially at 70 and on blood thinners, can mean slow bleeding in the brain, which can develop hours or days later. Call an ambulance rather than driving, and bring your medication list.
Baby is 4 weeks old and has a bit of yellow in her eyes still, she's breastfed. Wait it out?

Jaundice that's still there at 4 weeks needs a call to her pediatrician this week. It's often harmless breast milk jaundice, but they'll want a blood test to rule out liver problems. Call sooner if her poop is pale or chalky, her pee is dark, or she's feeding poorly or very sleepy. Pale poop in particular needs checking right away.
I'm 16 and my acne is getting really bad, like painful bumps under the skin. Nothing from the drugstore is working and honestly it's making me not want to go to school.

Deep, painful bumps are a sign of cystic acne, which often doesn't respond to drugstore products and really does need a doctor or dermatologist. There are prescription treatments that work much better, and getting on them early can also prevent scarring. Try to resist picking or squeezing in the meantime, and tell a parent or your school nurse how much it's affecting you so you can get an appointment soon, because this is very treatable and you don't have to just put up with it.
what's a stye and how do i get rid of it fast

A stye is a small infected oil gland at the edge of the eyelid, and most clear up within a week. The best home treatment is a clean warm compress held on the eyelid for 10 to 15 minutes, three or four times a day, which helps it drain by itself. Don't squeeze or pop it, and skip eye makeup and contacts until it's gone. See a doctor if it lasts longer than two weeks, the swelling spreads over the eyelid, or your vision changes.
My 15 year old had mono and the doctor said no sports for a while. He's feeling great now and wants to play football this weekend. It's been 3 weeks.

Please hold him out until his doctor clears him, even though he feels fine. Mono often enlarges the spleen, and a hit in a contact sport like football can rupture it, which is a genuine emergency. Most doctors want at least three to four weeks and sometimes longer before contact sports, and they may check the spleen before giving the okay. A quick follow-up appointment is worth it before the weekend game.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant, doctor wants me to get Tdap. Is it actually safe for the baby?

Yes, Tdap is recommended during every pregnancy, ideally between 27 and 36 weeks, and it has a strong safety record for both you and the baby. The point is that your antibodies cross the placenta and protect your newborn from whooping cough during the first months, before they can be vaccinated themselves. Whooping cough is most dangerous at that age, so this is one of the best things you can do for the baby right now.
I'm on chemo and my temp is 100.5. Feel ok otherwise.

Call your oncology team's urgent line right now, even though you feel okay. A fever during chemotherapy can signal a serious infection while your white blood cell count is low, and it needs to be treated quickly. Most cancer centers want you to call for any temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher. Don't take fever reducers until they tell you to, because the medicine can hide a rising temperature.
We're doing baby-led weaning, can she have whole grapes? She's 10 months

Not whole grapes. Their size and shape make them one of the top choking hazards for young kids. Cut them lengthwise into quarters, and keep doing that until she's about 4 years old. The same goes for cherry tomatoes and blueberries for younger babies; squash or quarter them.
pulling an all-nighter for exams, how much caffeine can i safely have

Most healthy adults should stay under about 400 mg of caffeine in a day, which is roughly four regular coffees, and you should spread it out rather than slamming energy drinks. Going past that brings jitters, a racing heart and anxiety that make studying worse. An all-nighter also wrecks memory consolidation, so even a 90-minute sleep in the early morning will likely help your exam more than extra caffeine. Don't drive afterward if you've been awake all night, because the impairment is comparable to being drunk.
my kid swallowed like 6 of my iron pills what do i do

Treat this as an emergency. Call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 in the US, or your local emergency number, right now. Iron overdose in children can be serious even if they seem fine at first. Don't make them vomit, and keep the bottle with you so you can tell responders the exact strength. If your child is vomiting, drowsy or has belly pain, call emergency services immediately.
is it bad to take excedrin like every day? it's the only thing that works

Taking it daily can backfire. Using painkillers on more than about 10 to 15 days a month can cause medication-overuse headache, where the pills themselves keep the headaches going, and the caffeine adds to that cycle. Talk to your doctor about a preventive treatment and a plan to taper off safely, because many people find their headaches drop off a lot once the rebound cycle breaks.
just sliced my finger cutting onions, bleeding a lot, what do i do

Press a clean cloth or paper towel firmly on the cut and keep steady pressure for a full 10 minutes without lifting to check, with your hand raised above your heart. Most kitchen cuts stop bleeding with that. Once it stops, rinse it under running water and cover it with a bandage. If it's still bleeding after 10 to 15 minutes of solid pressure, gapes open, or you can't move or feel the fingertip normally, get it looked at today because it may need stitches.
I'm pregnant and my allergies are terrible. Is anything safe?

Yes, several options are generally considered safe in pregnancy, including saline nasal rinses and certain antihistamines like loratadine or cetirizine. Some steroid nasal sprays, such as budesonide, are also commonly recommended. Check with your OB before starting anything, and avoid oral decongestants like pseudoephedrine unless they specifically clear it, especially in the first trimester.
ok so I'm 34, desk job, neck and upper back always tight by afternoon, worse on deadline weeks. Any fixes that don't involve a new chair budget lol

You can get a lot of mileage from free changes. Raise your screen so the top is around eye level using books, keep the keyboard close so your elbows stay by your sides, and get up for a minute or two every 30 to 45 minutes. Simple chin tucks, shoulder rolls, and doorway chest stretches done a few times a day help undo the hunch. Since it flares with deadlines, stress-related muscle tension is likely part of it, so regular exercise and actual breaks matter as much as posture.
my 7 year old says her head hurts and she has a fever and her neck is stiff, she's kinda sleepy

Fever, headache, a stiff neck and unusual sleepiness together can be signs of meningitis, which needs urgent care. Take her to the emergency room now, or call 911 if she's hard to wake, confused, or has a rash that doesn't fade when you press a glass against it. Don't wait to see if the fever medicine helps first.
Can I alternate Tylenol and Motrin for my 4 year old's fever? Her fever keeps coming back.

You can, but it's often unnecessary, and alternating makes dosing mistakes much easier. If you do it, write down every dose and time, dose each medicine by her weight, and never exceed each one's daily limit. A fever that comes back as the medicine wears off is normal and isn't dangerous by itself. Call her doctor if it lasts beyond three days, she seems very lethargic or hard to wake, or she isn't drinking and peeing normally.
Is it fine to keep running? I've been running 5 miles 4x a week for years. 16 weeks now.

If your pregnancy is uncomplicated and you were already a runner, you can usually keep going, just at an effort where you can still talk comfortably. Let your body set the pace as things change, stay well hydrated, avoid overheating, and expect to slow down or switch to shorter runs later on. Stop and call your provider if you get bleeding, leaking fluid, dizziness, chest pain or regular contractions, and confirm the plan at your next visit.
Asthma plus pollen allergies. My inhaler isn't keeping up this spring. Ideas?

Allergies are likely driving your asthma, so treating the allergy side often helps your breathing too. A daily steroid nasal spray and a non-drowsy antihistamine are good starting points. Keeping windows closed and checking pollen counts also helps. If you're using your rescue inhaler more than twice a week or waking up at night, your asthma isn't controlled, so see your doctor soon about adjusting your treatment. Get emergency care if your inhaler stops helping or you're struggling to speak in full sentences.
Can I keep running? I'm a regular runner, 15 weeks pregnant, no complications.

Yes, if you were running regularly before pregnancy and things are going smoothly, you can usually keep running, just ease the pace so you can still hold a conversation. Drink plenty of water, avoid overheating, and stop if you get bleeding, fluid leaking, dizziness, chest pain or calf pain. Many runners switch to lower-impact exercise later on as their balance and pelvic floor change, so mention your routine to your midwife.
swallowed a small battery?? my son (4) maybe. not sure.

Go to the emergency room right now, even if you're only unsure and he seems fine, because button batteries can burn through the esophagus in as little as two hours. Don't make him vomit, and don't give him food or drink. If he's over a year old and you have honey, giving 2 teaspoons every 10 minutes on the way can slow the damage, but don't delay leaving to do it. Bring the battery packaging or a matching battery if you can, and you can call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 on the way.
whats the max nyquil i can take, need to knock this flu out and sleep

Stick to the dose on the label, which for most adult NyQuil liquid is 30 mL every 6 hours, no more than 4 doses in 24 hours. It contains acetaminophen, so don't take any other Tylenol or acetaminophen-containing product with it, because doubling up is a common way people accidentally damage their liver. Don't drink alcohol with it either. Taking more won't knock the flu out faster, so pair it with fluids and rest instead.
Sex during pregnancy - safe? husband is weirdly nervous

For a normal pregnancy, sex is safe all the way through, because the baby is well protected by the amniotic sac, the uterine muscle and the cervical mucus plug. Your provider will tell you to avoid it if you have something like placenta previa, unexplained bleeding, leaking fluid or a risk of preterm labor. Some light cramping or a little spotting afterward can be normal, but heavy bleeding or pain isn't. As your belly grows, side-lying positions tend to be more comfortable.
Had a heart attack 3 months ago. Getting mild chest pressure again on walks. Wait for my appointment next month?

Don't wait a month; call your cardiologist's office today and tell them you're having chest pressure on exertion again. After a heart attack or stent, returning angina can mean a narrowing or a problem with the stent, and they'll likely want to see you sooner or adjust your treatment. Use your nitroglycerin as prescribed if you have it, and call 911 if the pressure doesn't go away within a few minutes of resting or after one nitro dose, or if it starts happening at rest.
what's the fastest way to fix sciatica? I've got a wedding in 5 days

There's no instant fix, but keeping moving with gentle walking, avoiding long stretches of sitting, and doing some easy nerve-friendly stretches usually helps more than resting. Over-the-counter pain relief taken regularly, plus heat on the lower back, can make the next five days much more manageable. A GP or physio can check it and may offer stronger short-term options. Get seen urgently if your leg becomes weak, if you get foot drop, or if you have any numbness in the groin or bladder changes.
ugh just tell me the fastest way to lose 15 lbs in 2 weeks, fat burner pills ok?

Skip the fat burners. Many are loaded with stimulants or unlisted ingredients that have caused heart rhythm problems and liver injury, and the FDA regularly finds hidden drugs in them. Most of what you'd lose in two weeks is water anyway, and losing that fast usually rebounds. A modest calorie deficit, plenty of protein and vegetables, and cutting back on alcohol and sugary drinks will get you real progress you can keep.
dog bit me, small puncture, it's my own dog and he's vaccinated. wash and forget?

Rabies isn't really the worry with your own vaccinated dog, but dog bites still get infected more often than other wounds, especially punctures and bites on the hand. Wash it thoroughly with soap and running water for several minutes, apply an antibiotic ointment, and leave it uncovered or loosely covered rather than taping it shut. Make sure your tetanus shot is current. See a doctor if it's on your hand, face or a joint, if it's deep, or if you get redness, swelling, warmth or pus over the next couple of days, since antibiotics are often needed for those.
rolled my ankle playing basketball. swollen. how long til i can play again

For a typical mild sprain, expect about one to three weeks. Spend the first couple of days on rest, ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time, compression, and keeping it elevated, then start gentle movement once walking doesn't hurt much. Go back to playing only when you can hop and cut on it without pain, ideally wearing a brace for a while. If you couldn't take four steps right after the injury or the bony bumps on either side of the ankle are tender to press, get an X-ray first.
Dr gave me tramadol for my knee but I'm already on Zoloft. Pharmacist didn't say anything, should I worry?

It's worth flagging, because tramadol plus sertraline raises the risk of serotonin syndrome and lowers the seizure threshold. Doctors do sometimes prescribe them together on purpose, but they should know you're taking both. Call the prescriber or pharmacist and confirm they know about the Zoloft. If you get agitation, shaking, a racing heart, heavy sweating or muscle stiffness, get medical help right away.
My grandmother's skin tore just from bumping a door. She's 92. Can I just put a band-aid on it?

Skip the regular band-aid, because pulling off the adhesive can tear fragile skin even more. Rinse it gently with clean water or saline, ease any skin flap back into place if you can, and cover it with a non-stick dressing held by a light wrap. Have her doctor or a nurse look at it if it's large, deep, or won't stop bleeding, especially if she's on a blood thinner. Watch for redness, warmth, or pus over the next few days.
I just got out of the hospital after a bad case of sepsis from a kidney infection. I'm 32 and used to be super active. Can I start running again next week to get my strength back?

Running next week is almost certainly too soon after sepsis, which takes a huge toll on muscles, the heart and energy levels, even in fit young people, and recovery often takes months. Start with short daily walks and simple strength work like chair squats, and build very gradually. Ask your discharge team or GP for a follow-up and a referral to physiotherapy, since a guided plan will get you back to running faster and more safely than forcing it now.
can i take sudafed with high blood pressure

It's best to avoid it. Pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine constrict blood vessels and can raise your pressure, especially if it isn't well controlled. Saline spray, a steroid nasal spray, or an antihistamine without a decongestant are usually safer choices. A pharmacist can quickly check an option against your other meds.
do antibiotics work on the flu

No, flu is a virus and antibiotics only kill bacteria. There are antiviral drugs like oseltamivir that work best if started within 48 hours, and they're especially worth it if you're older, pregnant, or have a condition like asthma or diabetes. Otherwise it's rest, fluids and fever reducers, and see a doctor if you get short of breath or start improving and then suddenly get worse.
Can I just double my amlodipine today since my reading was high? Ran out of patience waiting for it to work.

Don't double it on your own. Amlodipine builds up gradually and takes a week or two to reach its full effect, and an extra dose mainly raises your risk of swollen ankles, dizziness and low blood pressure. One high reading isn't a reason to change your dose. Keep a log for your doctor, unless you get chest pain, a severe headache or vision changes, which need urgent care.
whats the max fish oil I can take

For most people, up to about 3 grams a day of combined EPA and DHA from supplements is considered safe. Check the label for EPA plus DHA, not the total oil amount. Higher doses can increase bleeding risk, so talk to your doctor before going above that or if you take blood thinners like warfarin or Eliquis. If you get fishy burps, try taking it with meals or freezing the capsules.
I've been bloated constantly for like 2 months and my pants don't fit even tho I haven't gained weight. Female, 52.

Persistent bloating that's new, lasts for weeks, and changes how your clothes fit is worth bringing to your doctor soon, not just something to manage with diet. In women over 50, ongoing bloating can sometimes be an early sign of ovarian problems. Usually it turns out to be something benign, but it's easy to check with an exam and possibly an ultrasound. Mention any feeling of fullness after small meals, pelvic pain or changes in urination too.
toddler has a barking cough like a seal at night, sounds awful. what is that

That sounds like croup, a common viral infection that swells the airway in young kids and is usually worse at night. Taking her into cool night air or sitting in a steamy bathroom for a bit often calms it, and keeping her calm helps because crying makes breathing harder. Call her doctor tomorrow, since a single dose of steroid medicine often helps a lot. Call 911 or go to the ER if she makes a high-pitched noise when breathing in while at rest, drools, struggles to breathe, or her lips look blue.
I'm on blood thinners (warfarin) and got a bad headache out of nowhere. take some aspirin?

Don't take aspirin with warfarin, because it raises your bleeding risk significantly. More importantly, a sudden bad headache while on blood thinners needs prompt medical attention to rule out bleeding in the brain. Call your doctor now or go to the emergency room. Go right away if it's severe or comes with confusion, weakness or vomiting. Acetaminophen is the safer painkiller for you in general.
My son is 9 and gets stomach aches every school morning. Doctor says nothing physical. Is he faking?

Almost certainly not, because anxiety causes real stomach pain in children and school mornings are a classic trigger. Gently ask what's worrying him about school, which could be friends, a teacher, schoolwork or bullying, and let his teacher know too. Keep him going to school with lots of reassurance, since staying home tends to make anxiety stronger. If it continues, ask your doctor about a referral to a child psychologist.
my father in law has a cut on his shin that's not healing after 3 weeks, its getting red around it

That needs a doctor's look this week, or sooner. A wound that hasn't healed in three weeks and is spreading redness suggests infection and possibly poor circulation or diabetes, both of which are common in older adults. If the redness is spreading fast, it's hot and swollen, red streaks are moving up the leg, or he has a fever, go to urgent care or the ER today. Meanwhile, keep it clean and covered, and don't let him soak it or apply random home remedies.
is it ok to sleep on my back at 28 weeks? i keep waking up that way and freaking out

Waking up on your back isn't something to panic about, so just roll onto your side when you notice. From around 28 weeks, side sleeping is recommended because lying flat on your back for long stretches can press on major blood vessels. A pillow wedged behind your back can help keep you from rolling over. Either side is fine, though the left is often suggested.
neuropathy in my feet is killing me at night, what helps

Ask your doctor about medications made for nerve pain, like duloxetine, pregabalin or amitriptyline, because ordinary painkillers often don't work well. Bringing your blood sugar under steadier control can also slow the damage. Check your feet daily, since numb spots can hide injuries. Avoid heating pads and hot water bottles, as you could burn yourself without feeling it.
upper back pain between shoulder blades, sweaty, a bit nauseous. 58M. pulled muscle?

Call emergency services now rather than assume it's a muscle. Pain between the shoulder blades with sweating and nausea in a man your age can be a heart attack, and occasionally an aortic problem. Both are emergencies where minutes matter. Don't drive yourself, and if you're not allergic or told to avoid it, chew an aspirin while you wait.
Wiped out on my bike, road rash all over my forearm with little bits of gravel in it. It stings like hell.

Get every bit of gravel out, because embedded grit raises the infection risk and can leave a permanent tattoo-like mark. Rinse it under running water and gently scrub with soap and a soft cloth, then use clean tweezers for anything stuck. Afterward, keep it moist with petroleum jelly and a non-stick dressing, which heals faster than letting it scab. If it's large, deep, or you can't get the debris out, have urgent care clean it, and make sure your tetanus is up to date.
jaw and upper back aching, feel nauseous, 57 F. took ibuprofen, didnt help

Jaw and upper back pain with nausea in a woman in her 50s can be how a heart attack presents, since women often don't get classic crushing chest pain. Please call 911 now rather than trying more painkillers or waiting to see if it passes. If you're not allergic and haven't been told to avoid it, chew a regular 325 mg aspirin while you wait, and don't drive yourself.
dropped a dumbbell on my big toe and the nail is purple and throbbing like crazy

That's blood trapped under the nail, and the pressure is what makes it throb so badly. Ice it, elevate your foot and take ibuprofen, but don't try to drill or burn a hole in the nail yourself at home because it's easy to cause an infection. Urgent care can release the pressure in a couple of minutes, which brings near-instant relief, and they can check whether the toe bone underneath is fractured, which is common with a heavy drop. Go sooner if the toe is crooked, the skin around the nail is cut, or you have diabetes.
My husband says sex will hurt the baby. I'm 20 weeks, everything's been normal.

In an uncomplicated pregnancy, sex is safe, because your baby is well protected by the amniotic fluid, the uterus and the mucus plug. Your doctor would only tell you to avoid it in specific situations, such as placenta previa, unexplained bleeding or a risk of preterm labor. Some light spotting or mild cramping afterwards can be normal, but heavy bleeding, ongoing pain or leaking fluid should be checked.
My 6 month old has a cough and runny nose. Should I ask for antibiotics just in case?

Antibiotics won't help a cold, and giving them just in case can cause diarrhea and rashes in babies without any benefit. Saline drops, gentle suction and keeping them fed is the right approach. Call the pediatrician or go in if they have a fever of 100.4°F or higher, fast or labored breathing, fewer wet diapers, poor feeding, or seem unusually lethargic.
When can I start giving my baby water?

Around 6 months, when she starts solids, you can offer small sips of water from an open or straw cup, a few ounces a day at most. Before 6 months, breast milk or formula gives her all the fluid she needs. Extra water at that age can fill her up, and in larger amounts it can upset her sodium balance. Never dilute formula with extra water to stretch it.
neck cracks every time i turn it. bad?

Painless cracking or popping in the neck is usually just gas bubbles or tendons moving over bone, and it's generally harmless. It's worth getting checked if the cracking comes with pain, swelling, a grinding feeling, or numbness and tingling down your arms. Avoid forcefully cracking it yourself over and over, since aggressive self-manipulation can irritate the joints.
Bought antibiotics online without a prescription for a tooth infection. Is that fine to use?

I'd hold off. Online pills without a prescription can be counterfeit, the wrong strength, or the wrong drug for the job, and tooth infections usually need a dentist to drain the abscess or treat the tooth anyway. Antibiotics alone often just delay the problem. See a dentist soon, and go to the ER if you have facial swelling spreading toward your eye or neck, trouble swallowing or breathing, or a high fever.
can i use the forehead thermometer on my newborn or do i need rectal

For babies under 3 months, rectal readings are the most accurate and the ones doctors rely on. A forehead thermometer is okay for a quick check, but if it shows anything near 100.4°F, confirm with a rectal reading. Any confirmed fever at this age means calling the doctor right away.
My dad is 78 and his bp drops so low when he stands up he nearly faints. He's on 3 bp meds. What should we do?

That sounds like orthostatic hypotension, and in someone his age on three blood pressure drugs it's a real fall risk, so call his doctor this week. His medications may need adjusting, but don't stop or change any of them on your own. Until then, have him sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before standing, rise slowly, and drink enough fluids. If he actually faints or hits his head, get him seen urgently.
stomach ache. 22F. period is late.

Take a pregnancy test today, because a late period plus belly pain is worth ruling that in or out first. Seek care immediately if the test is positive and the pain is sharp or one-sided, or if you have bleeding, dizziness or shoulder pain, since that can mean an ectopic pregnancy. If the test is negative, the pain may be from stress, period-related cramping or a stomach bug. Still see a doctor if it's severe or doesn't settle.
Teething or a cold? 9 month old, runny nose and fussy, low temp 99.8.

That sounds more like a mild cold, since teething can cause fussiness and drooling but doesn't really cause a runny nose. A temp of 99.8 isn't a fever, so comfort care is fine: saline drops, gentle suction, a humidifier and plenty of feeds. Call the pediatrician if a fever reaches 100.4 or higher and lasts more than a day or two, or if the baby is breathing fast, pulling at their ears, refusing feeds or having fewer wet diapers. Trust your gut if they just seem off.
My baby has a flat spot on the back of her head. Shes 3 months. Did I do something wrong?

You didn't do anything wrong. Flat spots are really common now that babies sleep on their backs, which is still the right and safe choice. Give her plenty of supervised tummy time while she's awake, alternate which end of the crib her head is at, and switch which arm you hold her in when you feed her. Mention it at her next checkup so the doctor can measure it, because a few babies benefit from a helmet if it doesn't improve.
fever 3 weeks on and off, night sweats, lost like 10 lbs without trying

That combination needs a proper medical workup soon. Please book an appointment with your doctor this week rather than waiting. Prolonged fevers with night sweats and unexplained weight loss can come from infections like TB or from other conditions that are much easier to treat when caught early. Write down your temperatures, any recent travel, and other symptoms so the visit goes further.
My baby (3 months) has crusty yellow flakes on his scalp. Gross. How do I scrub it off?

That's almost certainly cradle cap. It's harmless and very common, and it's better loosened than scrubbed. Rub a little baby oil or mineral oil into the scalp, leave it 15 minutes, then gently brush with a soft baby brush and wash with mild baby shampoo. Don't pick or scrape, since that can irritate the skin. Mention it to your pediatrician if it spreads, looks inflamed or weepy, or doesn't improve after a few weeks.
My grandma's 80 and keeps getting chest infections. Which vaccines should she have?

At 80, the most important ones are the yearly flu shot, the current COVID vaccine, the pneumococcal vaccine to prevent pneumonia, and a one-time RSV vaccine, which is recommended for everyone 75 and older. Shingles (Shingrix) and a Tdap booster are also worth checking. Her doctor can review her record and catch her up, and since she's getting frequent chest infections, it's worth having them look into the underlying cause too.
My 8yo has had a stomach ache around his belly button that's moved to the lower right side and he doesn't want to walk. Probably gas?

Pain that starts around the belly button, moves to the lower right side and makes walking hurt is the classic pattern for appendicitis, so take him to be seen today. An ER or urgent care that can do bloodwork and imaging is the right place. Don't give him food or pain medicine beforehand, so he can be assessed properly and is ready in case he needs surgery.
my bunny scratched me while i was trimming its nails. just a red line.

That's an easy one: wash it with soap and water and let it be. Rabbit scratches rarely cause problems, though any break in the skin can get infected. Keep an eye out for spreading redness, swelling, or pus over the next few days. Wrapping your bunny in a towel, burrito-style, during nail trims helps prevent the next one.
Gas pain so bad I thought it was a heart attack. How do I tell the difference??

Gas pain tends to move around, feels crampy, and eases when you pass gas, burp or change position. Heart pain is more often a pressure or squeezing in the center of the chest, and it can spread to your arm, jaw or back and come with shortness of breath, sweating or nausea. The two can overlap, though, especially in women and people with diabetes. If you're ever unsure, call 911 rather than waiting it out.
My dad (71) has been really paranoid lately, thinks neighbours are stealing from him, and he's confused at times. He refuses to see a doctor. What can I do?

New paranoia and confusion in an older adult needs medical attention. It can come from treatable things like a urinary infection, medication side effects or thyroid problems, as well as early dementia. Try framing the visit as a routine check-up or a medication review rather than 'checking your memory.' You can also call his doctor yourself to share your concerns ahead of time. If the confusion comes on suddenly or gets dramatically worse, take him to urgent care or the ER, since that can signal delirium.
I'm 68 and since my husband died last year I just don't see the point of much anymore. My kids say I should get over it.

I'm so sorry about your husband. Grief doesn't run on a schedule, and a year is not long after losing a life partner, so you're not failing at anything. When I hear "I don't see the point of much," though, I want to check in: is that sadness, or are you having thoughts of not wanting to be alive? If it's the latter, please tell your doctor or call a crisis line, in the US that's 988. Even if it isn't, a grief counselor or bereavement group can help a lot, and your doctor can check whether this has tipped into depression, which is common at your age after a loss and very treatable.
I've been cutting my arm again after 2 years clean. I'm not suicidal, I just needed it. Please don't freak out.

I'm not freaking out, and a slip after two years doesn't erase that progress. Clean any wounds properly, and get medical care if a cut is deep, gaping or won't stop bleeding. It sounds like something has built up lately, so please tell a therapist, your doctor or someone you trust. Together you can work out what's changed. For the next urge, try strong cold sensations like holding ice, or texting a crisis line such as 988 in the US, to buy yourself some time.
My wrist hurts and tingles at night, especially my thumb and first two fingers. I type all day.

That pattern strongly suggests carpal tunnel syndrome, where the median nerve gets squeezed at the wrist. A wrist splint that keeps your wrist straight at night often helps a lot. Also adjust your keyboard setup so your wrists stay neutral, and take regular breaks. See a doctor if it persists beyond a few weeks, if you notice weakness or clumsiness in your hand, or if the base of your thumb looks thinner, because longstanding nerve compression can cause lasting damage.
got leftover amoxicillin from last year, fever and sore throat, gonna take it

Don't take it. Most sore throats with fever are viral, so antibiotics won't help, and a leftover partial course could be the wrong drug or the wrong dose. It can also make a strep test less reliable. A quick strep test at urgent care will tell you whether you actually need antibiotics.
sprained my ankle playing soccer. should I keep walking on it to keep it from stiffening?

Give it a day or two of rest first, with ice for 15 to 20 minutes every few hours, a compression wrap and the foot elevated. After that, gentle walking as pain allows helps healing more than total immobility. If you couldn't take four steps right after the injury, or there's tenderness right on the bony knobs of the ankle, get an X-ray to rule out a fracture.
Do I need to finish ALL the pills or is that a myth now?

It's evolving. Experts now recognize that many infections can be treated with shorter courses than the old standard, and taking more antibiotics than you need has downsides. That said, your prescriber picked a duration for your specific infection, and some infections, like strep or TB, really do need the full course. If you think your course is too long, ask your prescriber rather than stopping on your own.
can I buy reading glasses at the drugstore or do I need an exam

Drugstore readers are fine for simple age-related close-up blur, and they're cheap and safe to try. Pick the lowest strength that makes print comfortable at your normal reading distance. Still, if you're over 40 and haven't had a full eye exam in a couple of years, get one, because it checks for glaucoma and other problems that readers won't reveal.
dad 82 takes like 11 different pills now and seems confused lately. could it be the meds?

Quite possibly. In older adults, multiple medications are a common and very fixable cause of confusion, especially sleep aids, anticholinergics like diphenhydramine, bladder pills and some pain medicines. New confusion can also signal an infection, dehydration or a stroke, so get him seen soon, and urgently if it came on suddenly. Bring every pill bottle, including supplements, and ask his doctor or pharmacist for a full medication review.
My dad (75) refuses help, drinks more since retiring and seems depressed. How do I get through to him?

Lead with concern rather than criticism. You could tell him you've noticed he seems down and you miss him being himself, then ask how retirement is really going. Suggest a GP check-up framed around his general health, which older men often accept more easily than seeing someone about mental health. Help him find purpose and connection too, like volunteering, clubs or regular plans with you. If he ever talks about ending his life, take it seriously and get help immediately, since older men are at higher risk.
my blood sugar is 380 and i feel kinda thirsty but otherwise fine. can i just take extra insulin and sleep it off?

Don't sleep on a 380, especially if you have type 1 diabetes, because you need to know whether ketones are building up before you rest. Check your ketones now with urine strips or a blood meter, take a correction dose only as your care team has taught you, and drink water. If ketones are moderate or high, or you have nausea, vomiting, belly pain or fast breathing, go to the ER, since that can be diabetic ketoacidosis. If ketones are negative, recheck your sugar in two hours and call your diabetes team if it isn't coming down.
I think my elderly aunt is being financially taken advantage of by a 'new friend' and she seems more forgetful lately. What can I do?

Take it seriously, because memory changes make people much more vulnerable to financial exploitation. Gently talk with her, and if you're concerned, contact Adult Protective Services or the equivalent agency where you live, which handles exactly these situations. Encourage a doctor's visit to assess the forgetfulness, and alert her bank, since many banks have elder fraud teams. If she's still able to decide, help her set up a trusted power of attorney now.
Been on prednisone 40mg for 3 weeks for my asthma flare. Feel great, I'm just going to stop.

Don't stop it suddenly. After three weeks at that dose, your adrenal glands have likely dialed back their own steroid production, and quitting abruptly can cause severe fatigue, low blood pressure and in rare cases a dangerous adrenal crisis. Call your doctor for a taper plan, which usually lowers the dose over a week or two. Keep taking it as prescribed until you hear back.
sunburn so bad my shoulders blistered. aloe enough?

Aloe helps with comfort, but blistering means a second-degree burn, so treat it with more care. Use cool showers or compresses, take ibuprofen for pain and swelling, drink lots of water, and leave the blisters intact. Keep the area completely out of the sun while it heals. See a doctor if the blistering covers a large area, or if you get fever, chills, confusion or feel faint, because that points to sun poisoning or dehydration.
I'm 72 and I wake up at 4am every morning no matter what. Is something wrong with me?

Probably not, since the body clock naturally shifts earlier with age and many people in their seventies get sleepy around 8 or 9 pm and wake before dawn. If you feel rested and alert during the day, it's likely just your normal rhythm. Getting bright light in the late afternoon and early evening can nudge your clock a bit later if you'd like to sleep in. If you're waking up feeling unrested, sad, or anxious, or you're napping a lot during the day, mention it to your doctor because early waking can sometimes be tied to depression or sleep apnea.
found some old antibiotics in the cabinet, gonna take them for this stomach bug

Hold off on that, because most stomach bugs are viral and antibiotics do nothing against viruses. They can also worsen diarrhea and wreck your gut bacteria, and leftover pills are rarely the right drug or a full course anyway. Focus on fluids and rest. See a doctor if you have a high fever, bloody stools, or no improvement after a few days, and they can decide whether you actually need a specific antibiotic.
can I give my dog my ibuprofen hes limping

No. Ibuprofen is toxic to dogs even at fairly small doses and can cause stomach ulcers and kidney failure. The same goes for naproxen, and acetaminophen is risky too. Call your vet, who can prescribe a dog-safe anti-inflammatory like carprofen. Keep him resting until then, and go to an emergency vet if he can't put any weight on the leg.
I had my spleen removed years ago. Dog licked a small cut on my hand. Is that a thing to worry about?

It is worth acting on, because people without a spleen are at higher risk from Capnocytophaga, a bacterium in dog and cat saliva that can rarely cause severe infection. Wash the cut thoroughly with soap and water now, and call your doctor today, as many recommend preventive antibiotics in this situation. Seek emergency care immediately if you develop fever, chills, or feel suddenly very unwell.
quick q, does magnesium actually help sleep

The evidence is modest. Magnesium seems to help most in people who are low in it, which is more common in older adults and people with poor diets. Magnesium glycinate at around 200 to 400 mg in the evening is generally well tolerated, while the oxide form is more likely to cause loose stools. Check with your doctor first if you have kidney disease or take medications like antibiotics or blood pressure drugs, since magnesium can interact with them.
I have leftover amoxicillin from last year and my throat is killing me. Can I just take that?

Don't take it. Most sore throats are viral, so amoxicillin won't help, and a partial leftover course can't properly treat strep even if that's what you have. If you have a fever, swollen glands and no cough, get a quick strep test at a clinic or pharmacy; if it's positive you'll get a full, correct course. In the meantime, ibuprofen, warm salt-water gargles and fluids will do more for the pain.
can i take ibuprofen with asthma

Most people with asthma can take ibuprofen without problems. About 1 in 10 adults with asthma, though, are sensitive to NSAIDs like ibuprofen and aspirin, and these drugs can trigger an attack in them. That risk is higher if you also have nasal polyps or chronic sinus issues. If you've never taken it, or you've had a reaction before, acetaminophen is the safer choice, and you can check with your doctor.
I get dizzy when I roll over in bed, room spins for like 30 seconds

Brief spinning triggered by rolling over or looking up is classic BPPV, where tiny crystals in the inner ear drift out of place. It's harmless and usually very treatable with a simple head-repositioning move called the Epley maneuver, which a doctor or physical therapist can do or teach you. Get checked to confirm, and seek urgent care if the dizziness is constant, comes with slurred speech, weakness, a severe headache or double vision, since those suggest something other than an ear problem.
I'm 34 weeks pregnant and I think I have a UTI. Is it okay to just wait for my OB appointment next week?

Call your OB or the after-hours line today rather than waiting, because UTIs in pregnancy are more likely to spread to the kidneys and can trigger preterm labor. There are antibiotics that are safe at this stage, and treatment is quick. If you have fever, back pain, contractions or vomiting, go to labor and delivery now.
Got a tooth abscess, face swelling up on one side. Dentist can't see me for a week.

Facial swelling from a dental abscess shouldn't wait a week. Call back and say your face is swelling, since most dentists will fit in an emergency, or go to urgent care or an emergency dentist today for antibiotics and drainage. Go straight to the ER if the swelling spreads toward your eye or neck, or you have trouble swallowing or breathing, or a high fever, because these infections can spread quickly.
my 3 week old feels warm, 100.6 rectal. probably nothing right?

For a baby under 3 months, a rectal temperature of 100.4°F or higher is treated as an emergency, so please call your pediatrician right now or go to the ER. Young babies can have serious infections without looking very sick, and doctors need to check them quickly. Don't give fever medicine before talking to a doctor. Going in is absolutely the right call even if it turns out to be minor.
last tetanus shot was like 12 years ago, got a dirty bite from my dog while gardening. booster needed?

Yes, you're due. Boosters are recommended every 10 years, and for a dirty wound like a bite, doctors usually give one if it's been more than 5. Get it within a day or two at urgent care, a clinic or some pharmacies. While there, have them look at the bite itself, especially if it's a puncture.
Woke up and saw my roommate sleepwalking into the kitchen. Should I wake him up? I heard that's dangerous.

It's a myth that waking a sleepwalker is dangerous, though he may be confused or startled, so the best approach is to gently guide him back to bed without grabbing him. If you need to wake him, speak calmly from a short distance first. Mention it to him the next day, since sleepwalking is often triggered by sleep deprivation, alcohol, stress, or certain medications. If it happens often or he leaves the house or uses the stove, he should see a doctor and lock doors and windows at night.
Hands cracked and bleeding from washing them constantly at work (nurse). Any tips?

This is very common in healthcare. Using alcohol hand rub instead of soap and water when your hands aren't visibly dirty is actually gentler on skin. Use a thick, fragrance-free barrier cream after every wash and on every break, and at night apply an ointment like petroleum jelly under cotton gloves. If the cracks don't heal, become very itchy, or start weeping, see occupational health or a GP, since you may need a prescription steroid ointment or testing for glove allergy.
Is hydrogen peroxide good for cleaning cuts?

It fizzes satisfyingly, but peroxide damages healthy tissue and can slow healing, so it's not the best choice. Plain running tap water and mild soap around the edges clean a cut very well. After that, a thin layer of petroleum jelly and a bandage keep it moist, which helps it heal faster with less scarring.
My grandmother has a sore on her nose that keeps scabbing over and bleeding for months now. She says it's just dry skin.

A sore that won't heal, keeps bleeding and scabbing for months is a classic sign of a basal cell carcinoma or another skin cancer, especially on sun-exposed skin like the nose in an older person. These are very treatable, particularly when caught early, but they keep growing if ignored. Encourage her to see her GP or a dermatologist soon so it can be checked and biopsied if needed. You could offer to go with her, which often makes it easier to actually book the appointment.
my 2 year old will only eat pasta and bananas. should i give him a kids multivitamin??

Picky eating at two is very normal, and most toddlers get more nutrition than parents fear. A children's multivitamin made for his age is a reasonable safety net, but store it out of reach. Gummy vitamins look like candy, and iron overdose is dangerous for small kids. Keep offering small portions of other foods alongside the ones he likes without pressure, and mention it at his next checkup so his pediatrician can check his growth and iron.
quick q - can i give my 2 year old my gummy vitamins if i cut them in half

I'd skip that and buy a children's formula instead. Adult gummies are dosed for adult bodies, and iron in particular is a leading cause of poisoning in young kids, so halving one isn't a reliable fix. Pediatric vitamins are dosed for their age, and many toddlers who eat a varied diet don't need one at all, so it's worth asking your pediatrician. Whatever you choose, keep all gummy vitamins up high, since kids treat them like candy.
dog scratch on my arm, barely broke skin. neosporin and move on?

For a shallow scratch from a known, vaccinated dog, that's basically right. Wash it well with soap and water first, then apply the ointment and a bandage if it's somewhere it'll get dirty. Keep an eye on it for a couple of days, and see a doctor if it gets increasingly red, warm, swollen or starts draining pus. Also check that you've had a tetanus shot within the last 10 years.
Taking melatonin 10mg every night for a year, is that bad?

That's a high dose. Most people do as well or better on 0.5 to 3 mg, and higher doses can cause morning grogginess and vivid dreams. Long-term safety data is limited, so try tapering down over a couple of weeks. If you still can't sleep without it after a year, talk to your doctor about a possible underlying issue like insomnia or sleep apnea. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) works better long-term than any pill.
I'm 72 and have a small pearly bump on my nose that bleeds sometimes and never heals. My daughter is nagging me to see someone.

Your daughter's right, and it's worth booking that appointment soon. A pearly bump that bleeds and won't heal is a classic sign of basal cell carcinoma, a very common skin cancer in people with lots of past sun exposure. It grows slowly and rarely spreads, but it can damage the nose if it's left alone. It's very curable when treated early, often with a simple minor procedure.
my dad (78) seems confused suddenly, family says it's probably just a UTI and to give it a few days. thoughts?

Sudden confusion in an older adult needs to be checked today, not in a few days. A UTI is a common cause, but so are other infections, dehydration, medication problems and stroke. If it is an infection, it can progress to sepsis surprisingly fast at his age. Take him to urgent care or his doctor today. Go to the ER if he's very drowsy, has a fever, can't stand, or has facial drooping, slurred speech or weakness on one side.
quick: ibuprofen for 5 month old ok?

No, ibuprofen isn't recommended under 6 months old. Use infant acetaminophen instead, dosed by weight. Check with your pediatrician first if your baby is under 3 months or if this is the first time you're giving medicine for a fever.
Teen son with asthma started vaping. He says it's fine because it's not cigarettes. What do I tell him?

Tell him straight: vaping irritates and inflames the airways, and in people with asthma it's linked to more symptoms and more attacks, so it's not a safe alternative. The aerosol contains chemicals and fine particles that go right into already sensitive lungs, and the nicotine is just as addictive. Have his doctor talk to him too, since teens often hear it better from someone other than a parent. Resources like the free This is Quitting text program can help if he wants to stop.
Can I put an aspirin directly on my sore gum? My grandma swears by it.

Skip that one, because aspirin held against the gum is acidic enough to cause a painful chemical burn on the tissue. If you want aspirin's pain relief, swallow it as directed on the label instead. Ibuprofen often works even better for dental pain if it's safe for you, and a cold compress on the outside of your cheek can help too.
I get nosebleeds sometimes, my friend says that means my blood pressure is high. true?

Not usually. Most nosebleeds come from dry air, nose-picking, allergies or colds, and high blood pressure rarely causes them by itself. Checking your pressure is still a good idea. See a doctor if your nosebleeds are frequent or heavy, last longer than 20 minutes, or happen while you're on blood thinners.
My husband had a mild heart issue with his covid infection, myocarditis they said. He wants to go play pickup basketball. Is it safe?

Not until a cardiologist clears him. Myocarditis is a serious reason to avoid intense exercise, and the usual guidance is to stay off strenuous activity for about 3 to 6 months. Exercising too early can trigger dangerous heart rhythms. Make sure he has follow-up testing and gets the all-clear before any competitive sport, even a casual pickup game.
My 8 year old has asthma and her rescue inhaler isn't helping much tonight, she's breathing fast and her ribs are sucking in. Wait till morning?

No, don't wait. Fast breathing with the skin pulling in between or under her ribs means she's working hard to breathe, and that needs emergency care tonight. Call 911 or go to the ER now. Follow her asthma action plan for rescue puffs on the way, keep her sitting upright and calm, and bring her inhalers with you.
Big painful red lump in my armpit, kinda squishy. Boil? Can I lance it with a needle?

Please don't lance it yourself, because you risk pushing the infection deeper or spreading it. Warm compresses several times a day can help a small boil drain on its own. A large, squishy, painful lump often needs a doctor to drain it properly, and sometimes antibiotics, so get it seen if it's bigger than about a centimeter or isn't improving in a few days. Go sooner if you have a fever or spreading redness.
how long should i keep a bandage on a scrape

Keep it covered with a bandage and a thin layer of petroleum jelly until new skin has formed, usually several days to a week. Moist, covered wounds heal faster and scar less than ones left to scab in the open. Change the dressing daily or whenever it gets wet or dirty.
pulled a muscle in my back lifting a couch. heat or ice? i just want to go to the gym tomorrow

Ice in 15 to 20 minute stretches helps in the first day or two, and heat feels better after that for loosening tight muscles. Gentle walking speeds recovery more than bed rest, but skip lifting at the gym for at least a few days until moving is close to pain-free. See a doctor right away if you get numbness in the groin or legs, leg weakness, or trouble controlling your bladder or bowels.
how do i know if its anxiety or just stress

Stress usually has a clear cause, like a deadline or a move, and eases once that pressure passes. Anxiety tends to hang around without an obvious trigger or out of proportion to it, with persistent worry, restlessness, a tight chest or trouble sleeping lasting weeks. A good rule of thumb is that if it's been going on most days for a couple of weeks or more, or it's getting in the way of work, sleep or relationships, it's worth talking to a doctor or therapist. Either way, it's very treatable.
is it normal to cry at work like once a week lol

Lots of people cry at work occasionally, but once a week on a regular basis usually means something is wearing you down, whether that's the job itself, burnout, or something like depression creeping in. It's worth asking yourself whether it's tied to specific triggers like a certain manager or task, or whether you feel low and tearful more generally, outside work too. If it's the general kind, or it's been going on for more than a couple of weeks, talk to your doctor or a therapist. That isn't an overreaction, and it's very treatable.
I'm 30 weeks pregnant and have a fever of 100.8. Should I just tough it out?

Don't tough it out. Call your OB or midwife today, because a fever in pregnancy should be checked to find the cause and protect the baby. Acetaminophen is generally considered the safe choice for bringing the fever down in pregnancy, but avoid ibuprofen in the third trimester. Go in urgently if you have abdominal pain, contractions, fluid leaking, or reduced fetal movement.
UTI symptoms again. 3rd time this year. Can I just buy antibiotics online without a prescription?

Skip the no-prescription websites; you can't verify what's in those pills, and three UTIs in a year needs a proper look anyway. A doctor can run a urine culture to identify the bug and the right antibiotic, and may check for an underlying cause or talk about prevention options. Many pharmacies and telehealth services can now prescribe for uncomplicated UTIs quickly and legitimately. If you get fever, back or side pain, or vomiting, get seen the same day, because that can mean a kidney infection.
My dog was prescribed amoxicillin. I have a sinus infection. Same drug, right?

Please don't take the dog's medication. Vet doses and formulations aren't designed for humans, and some contain ingredients that aren't safe for people. Most sinus infections are viral and clear up in 7 to 10 days with saline rinses and decongestants anyway. See a doctor if it lasts more than 10 days, you get severe facial pain with high fever, or you start improving and then get worse.
pretty sure I broke my toe, the internet says they don't do anything for it so I'm not going in?

For the smaller toes that's often true: buddy-taping to the next toe, a stiff-soled shoe, and ice usually do the job. Get it checked if it's your big toe, it looks clearly bent or out of place, there's a wound near it, or you can't walk on it after a few days. Those can need setting or more support. If you have diabetes or poor circulation in your feet, have it looked at regardless.
Teen son wants colored contact lenses from a costume shop for Halloween. Any harm?

Yes, there's real risk here. Contacts without a prescription, including costume ones, can cause scratches and serious infections that sometimes lead to permanent vision loss. Decorative lenses are legally medical devices in the US for exactly that reason. If he wants the look, take him to an eye doctor for a fitting and buy prescription-grade colored lenses from a legitimate seller. Make sure he follows the cleaning and wearing instructions and never sleeps in them.
quick q can i take two different antacids at once

Generally don't stack them, because many antacids share the same ingredients, like calcium carbonate, magnesium or aluminum, and doubling up can push you past safe limits. Pick one and follow the label dose. If one dose doesn't touch the heartburn, that's a sign to talk to a pharmacist about something like an H2 blocker rather than to pile on more antacid.
I've been waking up at 3am every night for two weeks and can't get back to sleep. I'm 52 and honestly exhausted. What is going on?
