Early-morning waking that sticks around is very common in midlife, and the usual culprits are stress or low mood, alcohol in the evening, hot flashes, needing to pee, or untreated sleep apnea. If you're awake for more than 20 minutes or so, get up and do something dull in dim light until you feel sleepy, and keep your wake time fixed even after a bad night. Two weeks of this is worth mentioning to your doctor, especially if your mood has dipped, you snore, or you wake gasping. Early waking can be a key sign of depression, and that is very treatable.
ok so ive been taking ibuprofen 800mg 3x a day for like 2 months for my knee. fine?

That's a prescription-level dose for a long stretch, and it raises your risk of stomach ulcers, bleeding, kidney strain and higher blood pressure. Check in with a doctor soon to look at the knee and decide whether you need stomach protection or a different plan. Black or tarry stools, vomiting blood, or bad stomach pain need urgent care. Physical therapy, topical diclofenac gel and weight management often let people cut way back on pills.
Do I need a measles booster as an adult? Born 1985, not sure I got 2 doses.

If you can't confirm two doses, the simple fix is to get one or two MMR doses now. An extra dose is safe even if you were already vaccinated. Alternatively, a blood test can check your immunity. This matters most if you travel, work in healthcare or plan a pregnancy. Note that MMR shouldn't be given during pregnancy.
can i take two benadryl every night to sleep? it works great

Nightly diphenhydramine isn't a good long-term plan. Your body builds tolerance within a week or two, it often leaves a next-day hangover, and regular use of this type of anticholinergic drug has been linked to memory problems, especially as you get older. Use it only for an occasional rough night, and if you need help most nights, talk to your doctor about what's driving the insomnia. CBT for insomnia works better than any pill over time.
I'm anxious all the time and get chest tightness. Doc already checked my heart last year and it was fine. Do I need to go to ER every time?

If your heart checked out and the tightness matches your usual anxiety pattern, short-lived, at rest and easing as you calm down, you don't need the ER every time. Treating the anxiety itself with therapy or medication can really reduce these episodes. Go in if the pain feels different from usual, comes with exertion, lasts more than about 15 minutes, or comes with sweating, fainting or pain spreading to your arm or jaw. A clean result from last year doesn't rule out something new, so let your doctor know if your pattern changes.
just grabbed a hot pan handle, palm is bright red and stinging, no blisters. what do i do

Run your palm under cool (not ice-cold) tap water for a solid 20 minutes, which genuinely limits how deep the burn goes even if it feels like overkill. After that, keep it clean, use a plain moisturizer or aloe if it feels tight, and take ibuprofen or acetaminophen for the sting. Red skin without blisters is a superficial burn and should settle in a few days. Get it looked at if blisters cover a large part of your palm, because hands heal better with proper care.
Taking sertraline 50mg. Doctor wants me on it but I read St John's wort is natural and works the same. Can I take both?

Don't combine them. St John's wort with sertraline can cause serotonin syndrome, which shows up as agitation, fever, rapid heartbeat and muscle twitching and can be dangerous. St John's wort also interferes with many other medications, including birth control. If you'd rather try a different approach, talk it over with your doctor instead of switching or mixing on your own.
Is it true local honey cures pollen allergies?

Unfortunately the evidence doesn't support it, mostly because the pollen that triggers hay fever comes from wind-pollinated plants like grasses and trees, not the flowers bees visit. Honey is fine to enjoy, but it isn't a substitute for treatments that actually work, like steroid nasal sprays, antihistamines or allergy immunotherapy. Never give honey to babies under one year old because of the botulism risk.
Is it fine to keep taking my sertraline now that I'm pregnant?

Don't stop sertraline suddenly, because quitting abruptly can bring withdrawal effects and a relapse, and untreated depression carries its own risks for you and your baby. Sertraline is one of the most widely used and best-studied antidepressants in pregnancy. Tell the doctor who prescribes it about the pregnancy soon so they can confirm the plan and let your maternity team know.
my jaw and teeth ache every morning when I wake up. whats going on

Morning jaw and tooth aching is a classic sign of grinding or clenching at night. It's often linked to stress and sometimes to sleep problems like sleep apnea. A dentist can confirm it by looking for wear and can make a custom night guard that protects your teeth. Mention any snoring or daytime tiredness too, since that's worth checking.
I keep waking up with a racing heart and sweating at night. Like totally drenched.

That combination deserves a doctor's visit soon rather than a wait-and-see approach. Night sweats and a racing heart can come from things like anxiety, menopause, low blood sugar, thyroid problems, sleep apnea, medications or infections, and occasionally from more serious conditions. Make a note of how often it happens, plus any weight loss, fever or other symptoms, and bring it to your appointment. If you ever have chest pain, fainting or trouble breathing, get emergency care right away.
feeling really down and kind of hopeless lately, 6 months pregnant. is this just hormones

Hormones play a part, but feeling persistently down or hopeless during pregnancy can be prenatal depression, which is common, real and treatable, so it's worth telling your provider at your next visit or sooner. Talk therapy helps a lot, and there are medication options considered reasonable in pregnancy if needed. If you ever have thoughts of harming yourself, call or text 988 or go to an ER right away.
my stomach hurts after i eat pizza every time, is that normal or am i just getting old lol

It's common, and age can play a part because digestion slows and reflux gets easier to trigger, but pizza is a triple threat of grease, cheese and acidic tomato sauce. Try a smaller portion, avoid lying down for a couple of hours afterward, and see whether it's the dairy by trying it with less cheese. If the pain happens with lots of foods, wakes you at night or comes with weight loss, get it checked by a doctor.
dog bite on my calf, neighbor's dog, he says it's vaccinated. just a scrape. fine to ignore?

A shallow scrape from a known, vaccinated dog is usually low risk, but don't just ignore it. Wash it with soap and water, apply a thin layer of antibiotic ointment and cover it. Ask your neighbor for proof of the rabies vaccination, and make sure your own tetanus shot is current, which generally means within 5 years for a bite wound. Watch it for redness, warmth, pus or fever over the next few days, and get it checked if any of those show up.
sliced my finger cutting an onion, bleeding a fair bit. how long do i press on it

Press firmly with a clean cloth or paper towel for a full 10 minutes without lifting it to peek, and hold your hand up above heart level. Most kitchen cuts stop bleeding in that time. Once it has stopped, rinse it under running water, then put a bandage on it. If it is still bleeding steadily after 10 to 15 minutes of real pressure, or the edges gape open, it probably needs stitches or glue.
Sunburn so bad I have blisters and chills. Just aloe and sleep it off?

Blistering sunburn with chills is more than a normal burn. It can be sun poisoning or heat illness, so call a doctor or get to urgent care, especially if you also have a fever, headache, confusion, or nausea. Until then, drink plenty of water, take ibuprofen, keep cool, and don't pop the blisters. Aloe is fine for comfort, but it won't treat the dehydration and inflammation that are causing the chills.
i'm 55 and get indigestion-like burning in my chest when i shovel snow. fine otherwise

Burning that shows up specifically with exertion like shoveling is a classic way angina disguises itself as indigestion, and snow shoveling is a well-known heart attack trigger. Stop shoveling, have someone else do it or use a service, and book a doctor's appointment soon for an ECG and possibly a stress test. If the burning comes on at rest or lasts more than a few minutes, call emergency services.
I'm 58 and just recovered from COVID about two weeks ago. I used to walk 5 miles a day. How should I ease back in?

Start with 10 to 15 minutes of easy walking and add a little each day, as long as you feel fine the next morning. If you get chest pain, a racing or irregular heartbeat, unusual breathlessness, or dizziness, stop and see your doctor, because COVID can occasionally affect the heart. Most people your age who build up gradually over two to four weeks get back to their old distance without trouble.
is it ok to take my vitamin D with coffee in the morning or does that mess with absorption

Coffee doesn't meaningfully block vitamin D, so that part is fine. The bigger factor is fat, because vitamin D is fat-soluble and absorbs noticeably better with a meal containing some fat. If your morning is just black coffee, try moving the pill to breakfast or lunch.
quick q - can i take ibuprofen if i have asthma

Most people with asthma can take ibuprofen without trouble. But around 5 to 10 percent of adults with asthma react to NSAIDs like ibuprofen and aspirin with a flare, and the risk is higher if you also have nasal polyps or chronic sinus problems. If you've taken it before with no breathing issues, you're very likely fine. If you've never tried it or aren't sure, acetaminophen is the safer pick, and you can ask your doctor about it at your next visit.
do air purifiers actually help with dust allergies or is it a scam

A true HEPA purifier does help with airborne allergens like pet dander and pollen, and it helps somewhat with dust. Dust mite allergen is heavy, though, and mostly settles into bedding and carpets rather than floating in the air. For mites, you'll get bigger wins from allergen-proof mattress and pillow covers, weekly hot-water washing of bedding, and keeping humidity below 50 percent. If you buy a purifier, put it in your bedroom and size it to the room.
my asthma attack isn't stopping after 4 puffs of albuterol what now

Call emergency services now. An attack that doesn't respond to your rescue inhaler needs urgent treatment. While you wait, sit upright, stay as calm as you can, and keep taking puffs of albuterol, 1 puff every 30 to 60 seconds up to 10 puffs, if your asthma action plan says to. Don't drive yourself.
how do i know if a cut needs stitches

The main signs are a cut that gapes open, is deeper than about a quarter inch, or is longer than half an inch. Other signs are fat or tissue showing, edges that won't stay together, or bleeding that won't stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure. Cuts on the face, over joints, or on the hands are also worth having looked at, since they affect healing, movement and scarring. Stitches work best within roughly 6 to 8 hours, so don't sit on it overnight if you're unsure.
I'm 68 and since my wife died last year I just don't see the point in much. My kids say I should 'see someone.' I'm not crazy.

Seeing someone doesn't mean you're crazy. Grief this heavy is one of the hardest things a person goes through, and a year of losing your sense of purpose is exactly what grief counselors and doctors help with. Prolonged grief and depression are common after losing a spouse, especially later in life, and they respond well to support. Your GP is a good place to start, and many hospices also run free bereavement groups for people in your situation.
Quick q — does coffee raise blood pressure?

Yes, a little and for a short time. Caffeine can bump your reading up by roughly 5–10 points for a few hours, especially if you don't drink it often. Regular moderate coffee intake doesn't seem to cause lasting hypertension in most people. Avoid caffeine for 30 minutes before you take a reading so the number reflects your usual pressure.
Is it okay to use Q-tips to clean inside my ears every day? Feels so good.

It feels good, but it does more harm than good. Swabs push wax deeper and pack it against the eardrum, and they can scratch the canal or even puncture the eardrum. Your ears clean themselves, so just wipe the outer ear with a washcloth. If you ever feel blocked, use softening drops rather than digging.
I'm 58, postmenopausal. Do I need a calcium supplement or is food enough?

Many women your age can get enough from food if they're intentional about it. The target is about 1,200 mg a day, so a few servings of dairy, fortified plant milk, canned salmon with bones or tofu made with calcium can cover a lot. If you fall short, supplement only the gap, usually 500 mg or less at a time, rather than piling on a big dose. Vitamin D matters just as much, and it's worth asking your doctor about a bone density scan if you haven't had one.
My doctor says I need to stop my beta blocker before allergy testing?? that seems backwards, can I just skip telling them I'm on it

Please don't hide it. Beta blockers matter here because they can make allergic reactions harder to treat and can blunt the effect of epinephrine, which is exactly what testing teams rely on if something goes wrong. Tell the allergist, and let them work with your prescribing doctor. Don't stop the beta blocker on your own either, since abruptly stopping can be risky for your heart. They'll find a safe plan, whether that's a supervised pause or a different testing method.
My tooth only hurts when I drink something cold, then it goes away in a second or two. Should I worry?

A brief zing from cold that fades quickly is usually sensitivity from exposed dentin, often caused by gum recession, worn enamel or brushing too hard. A sensitivity toothpaste used twice daily for a few weeks often helps a lot. Mention it at your next checkup. Book sooner if the pain starts lingering after the cold is gone or begins happening on its own, since that can mean the nerve is involved.
is it safe to give my 18 month old benadryl so he sleeps on the plane? he also has a bit of a runny nose from allergies

I'd skip it, because diphenhydramine isn't recommended for young children and in some toddlers it causes agitation instead of sleep, which is the last thing you want at 30,000 feet. For his allergy symptoms, ask his pediatrician about a child-appropriate option and dose before the trip. For the flight itself, feeding or a pacifier during takeoff and landing, plus familiar comfort items, tends to work better than medication.
grandpa (81) says his stomach hurts and he hasn't pooped in 5 days and he's been vomiting

At his age, belly pain with no bowel movement for five days and vomiting could mean a bowel obstruction, which is an emergency. Please take him to the ER now rather than trying laxatives or enemas at home. Bring a list of his medications, since some of them commonly cause severe constipation in older adults. Don't let him eat in the meantime.
My kid's ferret bit her and it won't stop bleeding after 15 minutes of pressure.

Bleeding that hasn't stopped after 15 minutes of firm, steady pressure needs medical attention now, so head to urgent care or the emergency department. Keep firm pressure on it with a clean cloth and raise the area above heart level on the way, without lifting the cloth to check. They'll also clean the wound properly and check on infection risk and her vaccinations.
Shingrix knocked me flat last time. Can I just skip the second dose?

I'd still get the second dose, because one dose gives noticeably weaker and shorter-lasting protection than two. The rough day or two you had is a sign of a strong immune response, and the second dose often feels about the same or milder. Schedule it before a quiet day, stay hydrated, and keep acetaminophen or ibuprofen on hand.
I've been feeling on top of the world, barely sleeping and starting loads of projects. My wife says I'm acting weird. Seems fine to me?

Feeling amazing while barely sleeping, with racing ideas and lots of new projects, can be a sign of hypomania or mania, especially if people close to you notice a change. It often feels great from the inside, which is exactly why others notice first. Please see your doctor soon and bring your wife along so you get an outside view. Hold off on big financial or life decisions until you've been checked.
My grandma (82) says the straight lines in her crossword look wavy in one eye. Should I worry?

Yes, take that seriously and get her an appointment with an eye doctor within a few days. Wavy straight lines in one eye is a classic sign of macular degeneration, possibly the wet form. Wet macular degeneration can be treated with injections that preserve vision, but only if it's caught early. If her vision drops suddenly, call the eye doctor right away.
I found some leftover Xanax from my mom's prescription. Is it ok to take one before my job interview tomorrow?

Skip it. Taking someone else's prescription is risky, because you don't know how a benzodiazepine will hit you. It can make you drowsy, foggy or flat, which is the opposite of what you want in an interview. For tomorrow, try slow breathing before you go in, a short brisk walk, and a quick run-through of your top three talking points. If anxiety regularly gets in your way, see a doctor about options that are actually meant for you.
I'm on warfarin. Bad headache. Can I take ibuprofen?

Skip the ibuprofen. NSAIDs like ibuprofen, naproxen and aspirin significantly raise bleeding risk with warfarin, including stomach bleeds. Acetaminophen is the usual choice, at regular doses and not for days on end, since heavy use can bump your INR. If this headache is sudden, severe or the worst you've had, or comes after any bump to the head, get emergency care right away, because bleeding in the brain is a real concern on blood thinners.
back hurts, should i stay in bed till it's better

Bed rest actually tends to slow recovery for most back pain. Staying gently active, with walking, normal daily tasks and avoiding only what really spikes the pain, gets most people better faster. Lie down for comfort when you need to, but get up and move regularly. If the pain follows a significant fall, comes with fever, numbness, leg weakness or bladder changes, or keeps you awake every night, get seen.
My midwife said my blood pressure was 142/92. I feel totally fine. Do I need to do anything before my next appointment in 2 weeks?

That reading is in the high range for pregnancy, so it's worth asking your midwife directly whether she wants it rechecked sooner than two weeks, because feeling fine doesn't rule out preeclampsia. A home blood pressure cuff is a smart buy so you can track it. Call right away or go to labor and delivery if you get a bad headache, vision changes like spots or blurring, pain under your right ribs, or sudden swelling in your face or hands.
Is it safe to give my 4 year old adult tylenol cut in half for a headache

Use the children's liquid instead. Halving adult tablets can give a 4-year-old far more than the safe dose, and acetaminophen overdose can damage the liver. Dose children's acetaminophen by weight using the syringe that comes with it, and call the pediatrician if headaches are frequent or come with fever, vomiting or unusual sleepiness.
My 70 year old dad has started acting out his dreams, punching and yelling in his sleep. He fell out of bed last week. What's going on?

Physically acting out dreams like that can be REM sleep behavior disorder, and it's worth getting him evaluated by a doctor or sleep specialist soon. It's treatable, and in older adults it can sometimes be an early sign of neurological conditions like Parkinson's, so early follow-up matters. In the meantime, make the bedroom safer by moving the bed away from sharp furniture, padding the floor, and moving anything breakable out of reach. A bed partner may need to sleep separately for safety until it's under control.
is napping bad

Not at all, as long as it's short and early. A 20 to 30 minute nap before about 3 pm can boost alertness without messing up your night. Longer or later naps tend to leave you groggy and make it harder to fall asleep at bedtime. If you need long naps every day despite sleeping enough at night, that's worth mentioning to a doctor.
my stomach hurts after i eat pizza, every single time. whats going on

Pizza packs a lot of fat, tomato acid and cheese into one meal, so the usual suspects are acid reflux, slow fat digestion, or lactose intolerance if you also get bloating or loose stools. Try a smaller portion, thinner crust with less cheese, and don't lie down for a couple of hours after eating. If it keeps happening even with lighter versions, or the pain sits in your upper right belly, mention it to a doctor because gallbladder trouble can show up exactly this way.
is it bad to sleep with the tv on

It's not dangerous, but it usually makes your sleep worse because the changing light and sound keep pulling your brain toward lighter sleep stages even when you don't fully wake up. If you need background noise to drift off, a fan, white noise machine, or a sleep timer on the TV that shuts it off after 30 minutes is a better compromise. Keeping the room dark tends to make a noticeable difference in how rested you feel.
Shingles finally cleared. Hit the pool?

Once the blisters have fully scabbed over and healed, swimming is generally fine and you're not contagious anymore. If you still have any open or weeping spots, wait until they're healed to avoid irritation or infection. Start with a shorter swim than usual since shingles can leave you more tired than you expect.
ear feels plugged since flight 3 days ago, yawning doesn't help

Try the Valsalva maneuver: pinch your nose, close your mouth, and blow very gently until you feel a pop. Don't force it. A decongestant nasal spray for a couple of days or an oral decongestant can help open the eustachian tube, as long as you don't have high blood pressure or another reason to avoid them. If the ear still feels blocked after about a week, or it starts hurting, drains fluid, or your hearing drops noticeably, have a doctor look at it.
Teenager here, got a tattoo 4 days ago and it's puffy, warm and leaking yellowish stuff. normal?

Some redness and clear or slightly cloudy ooze is normal in the first few days. Thick yellow pus, growing warmth and puffiness, and pain that's getting worse instead of better sound like an infection. Tell a parent and get it seen by a doctor or urgent care soon, since it may need antibiotics. Keep it clean with gentle soap and water, don't pick at it, and go in right away if you get a fever or red streaks spreading from the tattoo.
sliced my thumb cutting a bagel, bleeding a lot but i think it's fine. do i need stitches?

Press a clean cloth firmly on it for a full 10 minutes without peeking, and keep your hand raised above your heart. If it's still bleeding after that, the edges gape open, it's deeper than about a quarter inch, or you can see fat or anything whitish, get it stitched, ideally within 6 to 8 hours. If it closes up neatly, wash it with soap and water and cover it with a bandage.
My daughter (7) is going to a sleepover and she has a tree nut allergy. What do I need to tell the other parents?

Tell them exactly which nuts she reacts to and remind them to check labels for "may contain" warnings, especially on snacks, granola, baked goods and pesto. Hand them her epinephrine auto-injector and show them how to use it. Be clear that if she has trouble breathing, throat tightness, repeated vomiting, or widespread hives, they should use it right away and call 911. A written action plan from her allergist with your phone number on it makes this much easier for them.
Does coffee raise blood pressure?

Yes, caffeine can bump your blood pressure up for an hour or two, sometimes by 5–10 points, especially if you don't drink it often. Regular drinkers tend to develop some tolerance, so moderate coffee isn't usually a long-term problem for most people. Just avoid measuring your blood pressure within 30 minutes of a cup, or the reading will be misleading.
my back tooth has been throbbing for 3 days and now my cheek is kind of swollen. can i just wait it out till my appointment next week?

Don't wait a week on this one, because facial swelling with a throbbing tooth usually means an infection that's spreading beyond the tooth. Call your dentist today and ask for an urgent slot, or go to urgent care if they can't fit you in, since you'll likely need drainage and possibly antibiotics. If the swelling moves toward your eye or down your neck, or you get a fever or trouble swallowing or breathing, go to the emergency room right away.
Is beet juice actually enough to replace my blood pressure meds? Read it works as well as pills.

Beet juice can lower blood pressure a little because of its nitrates, but the effect is modest and inconsistent, nowhere near a reliable replacement for prescribed medication. Drinking it alongside your meds is fine for most people. If you want to cut back or come off medication, work that out with your doctor, who can taper you safely while watching your readings.
Stomach bug yesterday, threw up like 5 times. I feel okay today. Leg day?

I'd skip leg day today, because after a bout of vomiting you're probably still low on fluids and electrolytes, and heavy lifting while depleted can make you dizzy or crampy. Focus on drinking fluids and eating normally again today, and maybe take an easy walk. Give it a day or two until you're eating and drinking well, then go back with lighter weights than usual.
missed my baby's 2 month shots by 3 weeks, did we mess everything up?

Not at all. Just book them as soon as you can, and the schedule continues from there with no restart needed. Delays are common and pediatricians catch kids up all the time. Getting in soon closes the window where your baby is unprotected against things like whooping cough.
can I put an aspirin directly on my gum where the tooth hurts? my grandma swears by it

Skip that one, because aspirin held against the gum is acidic enough to cause a painful chemical burn on the tissue without doing much for the tooth. Swallowing it is how it actually works, so take it or ibuprofen by mouth at the dose on the label. Then get the tooth checked, since the pain is coming from something a dentist needs to fix.
I got bitten by my own dog during a fight between him and another dog. It's on my forearm, kind of gaping. I'd rather not pay for a doctor visit, can I just tape it shut?

Don't tape a gaping bite closed yourself, because sealing in bacteria can lead to a nasty infection or abscess. A wound that's gaping needs professional cleaning, and a doctor will decide whether it's safe to close and whether you need antibiotics or a tetanus booster. Urgent care is usually much cheaper than an ER for this. Go today, ideally within a few hours, and keep pressure on it with a clean cloth until then.
My feet and hands got really puffy overnight and I've had a bad headache. 34 weeks. Just pregnancy stuff?

Sudden swelling in your hands and face along with a headache at 34 weeks needs to be checked today, not brushed off. That combination can be a sign of preeclampsia, a blood pressure condition that can get serious fast. Call your provider or labor and delivery now. If you have vision changes, pain under your right ribs, or shortness of breath, go straight in. A quick blood pressure check and urine test will sort it out.
do air purifiers actually help allergies or is it marketing

A true HEPA air purifier sized for the room does help with airborne allergens like pet dander, smoke and some pollen, especially in a bedroom where you spend hours. It does little for dust mites, because they settle in bedding rather than staying airborne, so wash sheets hot weekly and use mite-proof covers. Skip ionizers and ozone-generating purifiers, which can irritate your lungs.
what spf do i actually need

Use a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every day, and go for SPF 50 if you're fair, spending long periods outside or near water or snow. Most people apply far too little, so use about a teaspoon for your face and neck and a shot-glass amount for your body. Reapply every two hours, or after swimming or heavy sweating. A hat and shade still matter for strong midday sun.
